Come hither, O well-praised Indra, to the prayers of Mānyasya the poet. May we know the help at dawn as we praise — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.
If, O Indra, you indeed have that readiness to hear by which you have been the helper of praisers — do not burn up our desire when it is growing great; may we attain all the things you have, with the life-span.
Truly no king, O Indra, has deceived us — those who are now making sisters in the womb. Even the waters, easily flowing, have gone for him; Indra has come with friendship and with birds.
Indra, the hero, conquers in battles with men; he hears the call of the poet who implores. He brings the chariot near to the worshipper — if the raised songs should come of themselves.
Thus Indra with men, through desire for good fame, becomes a bold helper against those who are hostile. In the encounter of courses he is praised with voice; the all-achieving glory of the sacrificer is proclaimed.

title: Rigveda
text:
Through you, O Maghavan Indra, may we overpower the enemies who think themselves great. Be you our protector; be you also for our increase — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.
I have grown weary through many autumns, through nights and days that make the dawns old. Old age diminishes the beauty of bodies — even so now the wives should have gone to their bull-husbands.
Even those former ones who were watchers of ṛta, who declared the sacred truths together with the gods — even those came down, for they never reached the end. Now too the wives have come together with their bull-husbands.
Not in vain does the weary one whom the gods help — we two shall win all contests. Here let us win the hundred-guided race as the pair of us, united as a couple, have rushed forward together.
The desire of the roaring, pressing one has come to me — born here, from here, or from wherever. Lopāmudrā draws the bull downward; the rash one sucks the wise man as he sleeps.
This soma now drunk close by and deep in the heart I invoke. Whatever transgression we have committed, may that be forgiven by him — for mortal man has many desires.
Agastya, digging with his tools, desiring offspring, progeny and strength — the mighty seer has nourished both castes, and has gone to the gods with true prayers fulfilled.
Your realms, your well-yoked horses, your chariot — when it flies around the seas for you two — with golden rims sprinkling you, drinking the honey, you two follow the dawns.
You two go beyond the stallion when you go to the manly one whose wings spread wide, worthy of reverence. When the sister who is praised by all brings you two, O honey-drinkers, for the prize and the refreshment.
You two placed the milk in the cow Uśriyā, the ripe within the raw, the ancient one. When among the trees the truthful-dripping one calls upon you two — as a clear, unwinding one — the oblation-bearer worships.

title: Rigveda
text:
You two have indeed chosen the honey-sweet warm drink for Atri, like waters for the flood to approach. That, O Aśvins, O heroes, seeking cattle — like chariot wheels your praises return with honey.
I would turn toward you two for your gift, O wondrous Aśvins, like a worn old man aided by Tugra's son. The great earth follows the waters of you two; worn out, your eye, O worshipful ones, has suffered from distress.
When you two set down your teams and let loose the mighty lady of intelligence with your own powers, O generous givers — then the sun-lord comes forward and backward like the wind; the good-vowed one obtains a great prize.
We too, being truly your praisers, proclaim you to be true; the chanter is well-placed. And indeed, O blameless Aśvins, you two drink; for you two bulls drink right up to the god.
Indeed you two Aśvins for days in the winning of the stream of Virudra — Agastya, praised among men as a hero among heroes, has illuminated you like a Kārādhunī with thousands.
When you two carry forward with the greatness of the chariot, when you two race like the Hotā of Manu — grant good horses to the sun-lords and wealth; may we be winners of riches, O Nāsatyas.
That chariot of yours, O Aśvins, we would invoke today anew with praises for our welfare — it whose rim is unhurt, going around heaven: may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.
O most beloved, you who officiate as adhvaryus among wealth and treasure, when you lift the waters — this sacrifice has made your glory known, O you who hold riches, O guides of the people.
May your bright, milk-drinking steeds, swift as the wind, those heavenly coursers with backs unsaddled — thought-swift, vigorous bulls — bearing heavenly sovereignty, bring you Aśvins hither.
May your chariot, like a rushing river, with a yoke that glides forward, come hither for our welfare. It is swifter than thought, carrying the vigorous bull — that adorable, zealous one who presses forward first.

title: Rigveda
text:
Born here and there, both have called out together with sinless body and with their own names. One of you is the conquering hero, patron of the bountiful sacrifice; the other, fortunate son of heaven, is glorified in the chariot race.
Your Kakuha mare, tawny in hue, has gone forward following the steeds to your dwelling-places. The bay horses of one of you are fattened with prizes; the sky-regions resound, O Aśvins, with your songs of victory.
Like a vigorous bull in autumn, your chariot has sped forth, seeking refreshment, traversing many food-offerings laden with honey. With like prizes the streams have come to us like rivers flowing upward, fattening the other.
A firm and wise hymn has been sent forth to you, O Aśvins, flowing in three streams through the sacrifice. O you who are praised, protect the supplicant — whether in the course of the journey or at rest, hear my call.
Moreover, that bright, radiant hymn of yours fills men at the triple sacrificial seat. The rain-cloud, O vigorous ones, has swelled for you both, like a cow's milk, pouring forth for the worshipper of Manu.
The full-purposed worshipper praises you two, O Aśvins, like Pūṣan, like Agni at the dawns, bearing oblations. As I call to you, singing your praises, seeking wide space — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
This course has now appeared — come, O wise ones, adorn the vigorous chariot, rejoice! O you who impel thought, you who are zealous, who possess the riches of Viśpalā, O sons of heaven — you of good deeds and pure vows.
For you are the most Indra-like, the most zealous, the most Marut-like, O wonder-workers, the most skilled in deeds, the best of charioteers. You drive a chariot laden full of honey; with that chariot, O Aśvins, come to the worshipper.
What do you do here, O wonder-workers? What person who offers no oblations is glorified in your presence? You shall pass beyond the niggard Paṇi; restore the life-breath to the sage, and make light for the eloquent singer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Crush on all sides the hounds that bark and snap; strike them down, O Aśvins — you have discovered those things. Make every hymn of the praiser yield riches; both of you, O Nāsatyas, uphold my praise.
You made a raft for Tugra's son upon the rivers — a self-propelled raft with wings. With that raft, guided by divine thought, you flew well, soaring over the great waves.
The son of Tugra had been cast down into the waters, cast into darkness that offers no foothold. Four ships favored by Jaṭhala, driven by the Aśvins, carried him across.
What tree stood firm in the midst of the ocean, to which Taugra's son clung without hold? Just as the feathers of a flying bird, the Aśvins carried him upward — to Bhujyu for his glory.
May that, O heroes, O Nāsatyas, follow you — what the sages of inspired mind have uttered in praise of you. From this soma-session today, may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
Harness that steed which is swifter than thought — the three-felied, three-wheeled chariot of the vigorous pair — by which you come near to the house of the good man; you fly with the three-fold element, like a bird with wings.
Your well-wheeled chariot rolls on toward the earth; when you stand, O wise ones, at the refreshments offered — let beauty attend beauty: may this hymn be with you, and may you Aśvins accompany Uṣas, the daughter of heaven.
Mount the well-wheeled chariot that rolls according to your ordinances, that bears the oblation. By which, O heroes, O Nāsatyas, you travel the path for nourishment, for offspring, and for the soul's own sake.
May neither wolf nor she-wolf attack you; do not turn away from us, and do not abandon us. This is the share laid up for you; this is the hymn, O wonder-workers — these are the honey-filled treasures deposited for you.

title: Rigveda
text:
Gotama, Purumīḷha, Atri — the oblation-bearer calls on you two, O wonder-workers, for help. Like one going straight toward a pointed direction, come near to my call, O Nāsatyas.
We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn of praise has been established for you, O Aśvins. Come here by the god-travelled paths — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
I, the carrier, invoke you both today and again at the dawning of Uṣas with praises. O Nāsatyas, wherever you may be, O noble sons of heaven, come to the generous giver.
O vigorous pair, do rejoice among us; strike down the stingy Paṇis in your exhilaration. Be heard by me — O heroes, discerning ones, be sought out with the ear through the utterances of my thoughts.
For glory, like Pūṣan and the arrow-maker among the gods, O Nāsatyas, bring the marriage of Sūryā. Your Kakuha mare, born of the waters, is celebrated — like the ancient yokes of mighty Varuṇa.
May that sweet gift of yours be for us; impel the hymn of the praiser who deserves honor. While the peoples rejoice, O munificent ones renowned in glory, may they rejoice in heroic strength through you.
This hymn has been made for you, O Aśvins, O bountiful ones, with songs of praise and well-wrought verses. Come, rejoicing, O Nāsatyas, to the path for offspring and for the self — for Agastya's sake.
We have crossed to the far shore of this darkness; the hymn of praise has been established for you, O Aśvins. Come here by the god-travelled paths — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
Which of the two is the earlier and which the later of these two? How were they born? Who among the wise truly knows? They bear all of creation within themselves by name; the two days revolve like wheels.
The two ever-moving ones carry the many and support the moving — the footed embryo held by the footless. Like a son forever in the lap of his parents — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.

title: Rigveda
text:
I invoke the faultless, unopposed gift of Aditi, radiant and inexhaustible, worthy of reverence. May both the great ones engender that for the singer — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
May we be near the two divine daughters, the pair of worlds that are heated without distress, filled with refreshment. Both belong to the gods, both on both types of days — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
The two young women, sisters and kindred, come together, meeting in the lap of their father; sniffing toward the navel of the world — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
I invoke the two vast, great, ordinance-firm dwelling-places, mothers of the gods, for their divine aid. They who sustain the immortal in good aspect — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
The wide and broad, the many-folded ones with distant ends — I address them with reverence at this sacrifice. They who sustain good fortune, who are easy to approach — O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
Whatever sin we have committed against the gods, against a comrade or against the house-lord ever-faithful — may this prayer of ours be the atonement for them. O Heaven and Earth, protect us from calamity.
May both manly praises strengthen me; may both accompany me with protection and support. Among many a noble lord, may the gods rejoice in the liberal giver — and may we press forward with vigor, O gods.
I, of good understanding, spoke to Heaven and Earth first, so that they might hear this truth. May father and mother protect us from blame and from ill-going near at hand, with their aids.
O Heaven and Earth, O Father and Mother — may what I address to you here be true. May we be foremost among the gods with their aids — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let divine Savitṛ, the universal lord, come to us at the festival with praises and fine speech, so that you, O youthful ones, may delight in us with inspired thought at the gathering of all the world.
May all the gods come to us with all the horses — Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa together in accord, so that all may prosper us, making us triumphant over the unstable one, like strength.
Together with Turvaṇi I praise Agni, your dearest guest, with hymns. May glorious Varuṇa be ours, and may the patron, praised of foes, conduct us to refreshments.
I come near to them both with reverence, desiring conquest — Dawn and Night, like an easily milked cow. On the same day I measure out the hymn, the milk flowing from their one udder in different forms.
May Ahir Budhnya bring us joy, and may the river Sindhu come like a suckling nursing her young — the river by which we impel the offspring of the waters, the vigorous steed, swift as thought, whom they carry.
May Tvaṣṭṛ too come toward us together with the patrons at the gathering, united in purpose. May Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, who fills all peoples, the most mighty of men, come to us here.
Also our thoughts, harnessed like horses, lick the young one like cows licking a calf. Hymns praise him as wives praise their husband — him, the most fragrant among men.
May the Maruts too, with swelling armies, together with the two worlds, sit down among us in one accord — they whose steeds are dappled, rolling like rivers, consuming enemies, yoked as with Mitra, like gods.
Truly now their greatness shines forth; the draft animals are harnessed with excellent harnessing. And when on a fair day their armies scatter the arrow of destruction, they sprinkle all the desert.
Send forth the Aśvins for protection; send forth Pūṣan — for they are truly self-strong. May I turn to the gods — non-hostile Viṣṇu, Vāta, Ṛbhukṣan — seeking their benevolence.

title: Rigveda
text:
May this thought of ours for you, O adorable ones, be life-giving and settled among you — this thought of one who strives after wealth among the gods. May we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
Now I shall praise the food — great, law-sustaining, vigorous — by whose strength Trita crushed the many-jointed Vṛtra with force.
O sweet food, O honeyed food — we have chosen you. Be our protector.
Come to us, O food; approach with auspicious aids, bringing bliss. Be a friend free of hatred, charming, without duplicity.
Your savors, O food, are spread out through the realms, resting there like winds in the sky.
Yours, O food, are they who give; yours, O food, is the sweetest. The savors, swelling in taste, surge forward like those with great necks.
In you, O food, the mind of the great gods is established. With your lovely banner, one has slain Ahi with your aid.
When you, O food, went to the Vivasvat of the mountains, even there, O sweet food, come to us sufficiently for nourishment.
When we partake of the essence of the waters and plants, O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.
When we partake of you, O Soma, whether mixed with milk or mixed with barley, O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.
Be porridge, O herb; be fat in the kidneys of the charioteer. O Vātāpe, become fat indeed.
You, O food, we have refined with our words, as cows press out what is to be offered. For the gods you are a shared feast; for us too you are a shared feast.
Kindled today you reign as god among the gods, winning thousands. O Agni, wise seer and messenger, carry the oblations.
By Tanūnapāt, the sacrifice is anointed with honey as the truth-seeker proceeds; he bestows thousandfold refreshments.
You who are praised and worthy of hymns, being invoked, bring the worshipful gods hither. O Agni, you are the winner of thousands.

title: Rigveda
text:
With might they have strewn the eastward-facing sacred grass, that has a thousand heroes — there where the Ādityas reign.
She who is the virāj, she who is the samrāj, the pervasive and the powerful, the many and the yet more numerous — from the doors the streams of ghee have flowed.
Well-decked and well-adorned, they two shine in beauty. May the two Dawns sit down here.
For the first two are the divine priestly callers, the poets of fair speech. May they sacrifice this sacrifice of ours.
Bhāratī, Iḷā, and Sarasvatī — all of you I address here. May those three spur us on to glory.
For Tvaṣṭṛ is the lord of all forms; he has assembled all cattle. Sacrifice their increase for us.
O Vanaspati, release the offering silently for the gods. Let Agni taste the oblations.
Agni goes before the gods and is anointed with the Gāyatrī metre; he shines bright in the svāhā oblations.
O Agni, lead us by the good path to wealth, O god who knows all the ways. Ward off from us the sin that lurks and misleads — we would render to you the most frequent utterance of homage.
O Agni, as one renewed, carry us across all difficulties with well-being; and the wide, broad earth be for us spacious. Be a source of peace and healing for our children and our progeny.
O Agni, ward off from us the disease; peoples without fire have afflicted us. O god, O adorable one, restore the earth to us for well-being together with all the immortals.
Protect us, O Agni, with unceasing guards; and shining bright in the beloved home — may your praiser know no fear now or in future, O youngest and most powerful.
Do not abandon us, O Agni, to the ill-intentioned foe, to the adversary or to misfortune. Do not hand us over to him who bites, who stings, who intoxicates, who harms, O powerful one.
Truly one like you, O Agni born of truth, being praised, stretches out protection for his body against all who would harm or lead astray — for you, O god, are the guardian against what comes upon us crookedly.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, knowing both classes of mortals, you seek them both at the hour of setting forth. At the time of arrival you are to be instructed by Manu — purified and burnished by those who desire, the bird of heaven.
We have spoken these set hymns in this Agni of Māna's son, the powerful one. May we win a thousand with the ṛṣis — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.
Increase Bṛhaspati with new hymns — he who is unopposed, vigorous, sweet-tongued. He is the singer of songs, of brilliant radiance, whose new praises the gods and mortals listen to.
The timely words attend on him, as a rush of men seeking the gods has been let loose. For Bṛhaspati straightway opened the highest realms; Mātariśvan joined together in the rite.
He sends forth praise and the rising of homage and sound, like Savitṛ extending his arms. By his power, the terrible one who is to be slain in battle, like a fearsome beast, without demonic protection — yet mighty.
His praise flies through heaven and earth; the discerning bearer of the divine strikes like a racehorse. The arrows of the deer — these fly here; Bṛhaspati's magical powers against enemies flash toward the sky.
The evil Pajras who think of you as a godless one — they wickedly live off what is good. You do not grant a boon to the deceitful one, O Bṛhaspati; you punish the despiser.
Like a path to good pasture, easy to travel; like Mitra fully satisfied, hard to lead astray — those who are unopposed and look upon us have stood forth, opening what was veiled.
To whom praises converge like rivers flowing to the ocean with wheel-like banks — he, Bṛhaspati, the eager one, beholds both things from within: what is beyond and what are the waters.
Thus has Bṛhaspati, great, mightily born, mighty, vigorous, been placed as the divine bull. May he, when praised, grant us abundance of heroes and cattle — may we know the winning path and the life-giving community.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Kaṅkata, and the one that is not Kaṅkata, and then the true Kaṅkata — saying 'two' and 'scorching,' the unseen ones have clung fast.
Coming, she slays the unseen ones; going away, she slays them too. Crushing down, she slays them; grinding, she grinds them.
Śara grasses, Kuśara grasses, Darbha grasses, and also the Sairya and Mauñja reeds — all the hostile unseen ones have together clung fast.
The cows have settled in the cowpen; the wild animals have lain down; the banners of the peoples have been lowered — the unseen ones have clung fast.
Those there have been seen at dusk, like thieves. O unseen ones, seen-by-all — you have been caught awake.
Heaven is your father, Earth your mother, Soma your brother, Aditi your sister. O unseen ones, seen-by-all — stay still and be at peace.
Those in the shoulders, those in the limbs, those needle-like, those that are called Kaṅkata — O unseen ones, whatever you are here, all together perish.
The sun rises in the east, seen by all, the slayer of the unseen. Crushing all the unseen ones and all the sorceries.
That sun has flown up, consuming all the many things; the Āditya from the mountains, seen by all, the slayer of the unseen.
I fasten the poison to the sun, to the leather flask in the house of the soma-presser. It shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.
The little iyattika bird, together with the śakuntikā bird, has eaten your poison. It shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.
Thrice seven viṣpuliṅkā birds have sucked up the flower of the poison. They shall not now die, nor shall we die — far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.

title: Rigveda
text:
Of the nine, and of the ninety, of the festering poisons — I have seized the names of all of them. Far from it is the yoking. The golden one has made you sweet, O honey; the bee has made you honey.
Thrice seven peahens, the seven unmarried sisters — they have carried off your poison like water-carrying women carrying pots.
This little kuṣumbhaka — I split open the taka with a stone. From it the poison has flowed back, flowing away along the valleys.
The kuṣumbhaka, rolling down from the mountain, declared: 'The poison of the scorpion is without power — without power is your poison, O scorpion.'
You, O Agni, are born from the heavens; you, the swiftly blazing one, from the waters; you from the rock; you from the forests; you from the plants; you, O lord of men, are born pure.
Yours, O Agni, is the Hotṛ-office; yours the seasonal Potṛ-office; yours the Neṣṭṛ-office; you, engaged in the rite, are the Āgnīdhra. Yours is the Praśāstṛ-function; you perform the Adhvaryu duties; and you are both the Brahman-priest and the master of our house.
You, O Agni, are Indra, the bull of the righteous; you are Viṣṇu of the wide stride, worthy of reverence. You are Brahmā, the finder of wealth, O lord of prayer; you, the upholder, preside with abundant wisdom.
You, O Agni, are King Varuṇa who holds firm his ordinances; you become Mitra, the wonderful, worthy of praise. You are Aryaman, the lord of the righteous, at whose table all share; you are Aṁśa, O god, the apportioner at the assembly.
You, O Agni, are Tvaṣṭṛ granting heroic offspring to the worshiper; yours are the wives of the gods — of Mitra's greatness is the kinship. You swiftly hasten to bestow wealth in fine horses; you are the host of men, O Purūvasu, rich in many goods.
You, O Agni, are Rudra, the mighty Asura of the great sky; you command the troop of the Maruts, the nourishing ones. You travel with the ruddy winds as your auspicious companions; you are Pūṣan who guards the worshiper by your very nature.

title: Rigveda
text:
You, O Agni, are the giver of wealth to the one who worships fitly; you are the god Savitṛ, the bestower of treasures. You are Bhaga, O lord of men, and you command wealth; you are the guardian in the house of whoever has honored you.
You, O Agni, the tribes worship as the lord of the house in their home; the peoples adore you as their king who bestows favor well. You preside over all things, O bright-faced one; you face a thousand hundreds and tens.
You, O Agni, do men worship as a father with oblations; they seek you as a brother for their comfort, you who shine in your body. You become a son to one who has honored you; you, a kind and unchecked friend, are their protector.
You, O Agni, are the Ṛbhu at the summit, worthy of homage; you command the wealth of nourishing sustenance. You shine forth, O Dakṣa, for the giving of gifts; you are the all-directing one, the extender of the sacrifice.
You, O Agni, are Aditi to the worshiper, O god; you as Bhāratī, the invocation-goddess, grow through praise. You are Iḷā of the hundred winters, skilled in action; you are Sarasvatī, O lord of wealth, the slayer of Vṛtra.
You, O Agni, well-nourished, are the most exalted bird; in your desirable color is the beauty of sight. You are the great, forward-advancing food-strength; you are the abundant, all-pervading, wide wealth.
You, O Agni, have the Ādityas made their mouth; the pure ones have made you their tongue, O seer. The gift-seekers follow you at the sacrifices; in you the gods eat the offered oblation.
In you, O Agni, all the immortal, un-treacherous gods eat the offered oblation with open mouth. Through you mortals relish the libation; you, the pure one, were born as the embryo of the plants.
You are with them all and you face them all, O Agni, well-born; and you, O god, are far-surpassing. For here, in your greatness, the strengthening force pervades, and both the world-halves, heaven and earth, follow you.

title: Rigveda
text:
The generous lords who send forth for the praisers the gift headed by cattle and adorned with horses — O Agni, lead both us and them to better fortune. May we speak great words at the assembly, possessed of heroes.
Make Jātavedas grow through the sacrifice; worship Agni with oblation, with your whole being, with hymn — him the enkindled, the one of good cheer, whose men are noble, the heavenly Hotṛ, enthroned at the forepost in the assemblies.
Toward you the nights and dawns have lowed, O Agni, like milch-cows toward their calves at their resting-places. Like heaven's hub you illumine the generations of men; you shine through the nights, O much-desired one, ever watchful.
Him of wondrous deeds the gods have set down as the hub at the base of the atmospheric realm, the charioteer between heaven and earth — Agni bright-flaming as a car worthy of knowledge, praiseworthy among settlements like Mitra.
Him sprinkling in the atmosphere, in his own house, shining like the moon, bright-gleaming, in the curve they have placed — the offspring of the speckled one who illumines with his eyes, like a guardian at the ford, following both peoples.
Let that Hotṛ encompass the whole sacrifice; him too men adorn with oblations and song. Golden-jawed, he roars as he grows among the kindlings, illumining the two world-halves as heaven does with stars.
Enkindled, bringing wealth, shine for us as an auspicious boon; bestow and cause wealth to blaze among us. Make the two world-halves favorable to us, O Agni; be pleased with the oblations of man, O god.
Give us, O Agni, the great gift worth thousands; increase like a door that yields strength, O widely famed one. Make heaven and earth favorable to us through prayer; shine brightly like the sun at the dawns.
Enkindled, following the pleasant nights in order, may he shine like the sun with his red-gleaming light. Agni with his invocations is the well-sacrificing one of men, the king of the peoples, the beloved guest for the mortal.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thus among the immortals, O primal Agni, has our thought been nourished in the great heavens, among human beings — like a milch-cow yielding for the singer at the assemblies, of herself driving forth the hundredfold, manifold vigor.
May we, O Agni, illumine the peoples — whether through a swift horse or through heroic strength or through prayer. May our glory above the five peoples shine high and unassailable like the unconquerable sun.
Be aware of us — you, the powerful, the praiseworthy, in whom the well-born generous ones are active — the sacrifice, O Agni, which the vigorous ones approach, shining perpetually on their offspring in their own house.
May we both — the praisers and the generous, O Jātavedas, O Agni — abide in your shelter. Grant us the abundant, many-gleaming wealth of cattle, with offspring and good progeny.
The generous lords who send forth for the praisers the gift headed by cattle and adorned with horses — O Agni, lead both us and them to better fortune. May we speak great words at the assembly, possessed of heroes.
Agni, enkindled, set in the earth, has stood facing all the worlds. The Hotṛ, the purifier, from of old of good intelligence — may Agni, the god worthy of the gods, sacrifice to the gods.
Narāśaṁsa, adorning all the dwellings, radiant in his own light against the three heights of heaven — let him, sprinkling with ghee, with willing mind, moistening the oblation, anoint the gods at the head of the sacrifice.
Praised, O Agni, with mind, being worthy of us, sacrifice to the gods today, going before mankind. Bring hither the unshaken host of Maruts and Indra; men, worship the one who is seated on the sacrificial grass.
The divine sacrificial grass, growing, filled with heroes, spread out for wealth, easily borne on this altar, anointed with ghee — let the Vasus, the Viśve Devāḥ, the Ādityas, the worthy of sacrifice, sit upon it.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let the divine Doors, being called upon, spread wide, well-approached with reverences; wide-extending, let them spread out, ever-young, purifying the glorious color abounding in heroes.
Performing their good deeds, moistened as by ancient rains, Dawn and Night delight like two weavers at their work. Weaving together the stretched thread, facing each other — let them adorn the sacrifice with milk, well-yielding.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, the more knowing, sacrifice straightforwardly, the more wondrous with their hymn. Anointing one another, sacrificing to the gods in due season, at the navel of the earth, upon the three ridges.
Sarasvatī, perfecting our prayer, and Iḷā the goddess, and Bhāratī all-pervading — these three goddesses, sitting down, guard this unbroken refuge with their own nature.
Of reddish form, well-supporting, food-giving — an obedient hero desiring the gods is born. May Tvaṣṭṛ loosen the navel of progeny in us; then may the path of the gods also reach us.
The tree of the forest, releasing it, comes to the fore; Agni advances the oblation with his thoughts. Knowing its threefold anointing, may the divine slaughterer lead the oblation to the gods.
Ghee is sprinkled; ghee is his womb; he is established in ghee; ghee is his very dwelling. Bring hither in order; delight yourself; carry the oblation consecrated with Svāhā, O bull.
I call for you the brilliantly shining one, the well-lauded one, Agni the guest of the peoples, of fine gifts — he who has become beloved like Mitra, Jātavedas the god among godless folk.
Worshiping him, they placed him a second time at the dwelling-place of the waters; the Bhṛgus placed him among the peoples of Āyu. May this one, the swift-horsed Agni, the hub of the gods, encompass all the beings.
The gods placed beloved Agni among the human peoples, as they would settle a friend who would dwell among them. He illumines with flame those who desire him — he who is worthy of skill in the house of the generous worshiper.

title: Rigveda
text:
Delightful is his nourishment like a possession of one's own; the power of his advancing skill is a joy to see. He who thrusts out his tongue among the plants, tossing like a racehorse, whirling through his obstacles.
When the forest-eaters, as they marvel at my might, bend their color to the Uśij-fires — he is known in the delightful realm by his variegated brightness, he who, though aged, becomes instantly young again.
He who, like one thirsting, shines among the forests; along the path he has roared like a chariot-horse. The scorching one of black trail has become conscious, smiling like heaven with its clouds.
He who has stood up and encompassed the wide expanse — a beast going of his own will without a herdsman. Agni the flame-possessor, heating the withered plants, causing a black trembling, has not tasted the earth.
Now I recite the thought for you in the third assembly, meditating upon your former helping. Bestow on us, O Agni, the great wealth that gathers heroes, the nourishing strength, with good offspring.
Just as, O Agni, the Gṛtsamadas through you conquered in secret and overwhelmed the adversaries — possessed of heroes, overcoming hostility — bestow that same vitality from the generous ones upon the singer.
The conscious Hotṛ has been born, a father for the fathers' aid. Offering excellent wealth, may we, the vigorous, be able to attain the rein.
In him who is the leader of the sacrifice, seven cords are stretched; the Potṛ, as a man of the gods, drives the eighth — the divine one; he pervades all that.
He has indeed sustained it; verily, when the Brahman-priest has spoken the holy words after him, the wheel-rim has encompassed all poetic wisdom as the felly of a wheel.
For the pure Praśāstṛ together with the pure, knowing its fixed ordinances, was born with his power of will; he mounts up following them like branches.

title: Rigveda
text:
The milch-cows of Āyu attend the color of this Neṣṭṛ. Perhaps the sisters who have come to this — will they bring a choice gift from the three?
When the sister approaches the mother bringing ghee to where she stands, the Adhvaryu rejoices at their coming like barley at rain.
Let the seasonal priest make heaven for his own heaven-seeker; the laud and the sacrifice — we have been adequate; we have given; we have won.
As a knowing one may do what is fit for all the adorable gods — this sacrifice which we have made, O Agni, let it also be in you.
Accept for me, O Agni, this kindling-wood, accept this drawing-near; and listen to these songs.
With this, O Agni, for your worshiper — O grandson of strength, desired of horses — with this well-spoken hymn, O well-born one.
You who are pleased by song and longing for wealth, O giver of wealth — may we, reverencing you with hymns, pay you homage.
Be aware of us — O sage, O bountiful one, O lord of wealth, O giver of wealth — drive away from us all enmities.
May he give us rain from the sky; may he give us strength that meets no opposition; may he give us thousandfold refreshments.
O youngest, for the praiser who seeks your aid — come as our messenger with our hymn, O most sacrificing Hotṛ.
For, O Agni, you travel between the two births, O knowing, O seer — as a friendly messenger among the people.
You who know, fill us too; O knowing one, sacrifice in order; and sit down on this sacrificial grass.
O youngest, O Agni of the Bharata-clan, bring the most excellent, radiant wealth — O Vasu, wealth longed for by many.
Let no niggardliness of the divine or the mortal master us; carry us across that also, and across enmity.
And through you may we, like rivers in flood, wade across all enmities.
O Agni, pure, purifying, worthy of praise — you shine forth greatly; you are invoked with ladles of ghee.

title: Rigveda
text:
You, O Agni of the Bharata-clan, are ours, invoked with cows and bulls and eight-footed victims.
Whose food is dry wood, whose libation is ghee — the ancient, deserving, desirable Hotṛ, the wondrous son of strength.
As if hastening for prizes — now praise the harnessing of Agni's cars, of the most glorious, the bountiful one.
He who is of good guidance for the worshiper, the undecaying, wearing out the enemy — of beautiful aspect, invoked with oblations.
He who, in his beauty, is praised in the houses at dusk and dawn — whose ordinance is never diminished.
He who, like the sun, shines brightly with his beam, gleaming with his flame — anointed with undecaying ones all around.
After Atri — the self-ruling Agni — the praises have increased; he has assumed all glories.
With the aids of Agni, Indra, Soma, and the gods, may we, remaining unharmed, keep company and overcome those who battle against us.
The Hotṛ, perceiving, fierce, blazing, skilled, has sat down in the Hotṛ's seat — Agni, whose ordinance is undeceived, whose insight is excellent, most excellent, carrier of a thousand, pure-tongued.
You are the messenger; you are our protector across; you, O bull, are the guide to better things. Be the unwavering, shining guardian, O Agni, of our offspring and the continuation of our persons.
May we worship you in your supreme birth, O Agni; may we worship you with praises in the lower dwelling. The womb from which you have arisen — that I sacrifice to; into you when enkindled the oblations have been poured.
O Agni, sacrifice with the oblation, O most sacrificing; readily accept the gift-offering of largess. For you are the lord of riches among riches; you are the thinker of the bright word.
Neither part of your wealth diminishes, O wondrous one, being born day by day. Make the singer nourishing, O Agni; make him the lord of wealth with good offspring.

title: Rigveda
text:
Most beneficent with your array of praisers, the most sacrificing to the gods, auspicious to us — undeceived guardian and our protector across, O Agni, shine brightly and wealth-bestowing.
Agni, oft-invoked, the first, at the step of the father-like Iḷā, enkindled among mankind — clothed in beauty, the immortal, the all-wise, worthy of being cleansed, seeking glory — he is the victorious one.
May Agni of brilliant radiance hear my call with all his hymns — immortal, all-wise. The dark ones and the red carry his car; he has made a wheel bearing Dawn's overcoming — he who is all-supporting.
They generated the well-born one in the one lying open; Agni became the embryo in the manifoldly-adorned ones. Even in the rough one he dwells, enveloped by no one, the all-wise, with his great nocturnal powers.
I anoint Agni with the ghee-oblation — dwelling opposite all the worlds, broad across, great in body, widest, mighty in food, fierce to behold.
I anoint him facing all around from all sides; with a demon-free mind may he relish it. Agni of manly splendor, of desirable color, roaring without being touched in his body.
Let him be known for his share with overwhelming choice; may we, as messengers of yours, speak after the manner of Manu. I invoke Agni who is complete, with the ladle and speech — the honey-mixed one — with praise.
Hear the call, O Indra; may we not be harmed; may we be yours for the giving of wealth. For these streams, flowing like rivers, seeking riches, increase you with their strength.
Release the great waters, O Indra, those which swelled but were penned around by the serpent, O hero, the many. He who grew great with praises, he struck down even the immortal-thinking Dāsa.
In the praises, O hero, in which you have delighted, O Indra, and in the Rudra-hymns — for you these bright ones, as you rejoice in them, hasten forward like winds.

title: Rigveda
text:
Increasing your bright strength, placing the bright thunderbolt in your two arms — bright are you, O Indra, grown great, making the Dāsa-peoples subject to us with the sun.
The hidden one, the secret one, the concealed, shrouded in the waters, the magical one dwelling there — even him who had propped up the waters and the sky — you slew the serpent, O hero, with your heroic power.
Let us laud your former great deeds, O Indra, and let us laud the new ones accomplished. Let us laud the thunderbolt longing in your arms; let us laud the two bays, the banners of the sun.
Your two prize-winning bays, O Indra, have struck out the self-poured heavenly mead. The earth spread apart equally; even the mountain stood still about to quake.
The mountain lay still without swerving; bellowing with its mother-waters, it contracted. In the far distance they increased the voice, spreading out the pipe sent by Indra.
Indra has kicked out the great Vṛtra lying prone — the magical one. Both world-halves trembled in fear at the thunderbolt of this roaring bull.
The thunderbolt of this bull bellowed out — what the inhuman one can overwhelm the human. Having drunk the pressed Soma, he brought down the magic of the magical Dānava.
Drink and drink again, O Indra, O hero; may the exhilarating pressed ones exhilarate you. Let those who fill your flanks increase you; thus the pressed drink of the citizen has helped Indra.
In you, O Indra, we have become inspired seers; seeking your grace, we would gain the thought with truth. May we who seek your help hold fast to your praise; may we at once be yours for the giving of riches.
May we be of those, O Indra, who, with your help, seek your aid, increasing your strength. O god, bestow on us the wealth abounding in heroes — that most vigorous gift for which we have longed.

title: Rigveda
text:
Grant us dwelling; grant us friendship; grant us, O Indra, the Marut-host. Those who rejoice together, who are exhilarated — the winds guard the foremost leader.
Let those in whom you, exhilarated, having drunk, have been satisfied pass through, O Indra, O firm one. You have increased us well in battles as conquerors, with great hymns to the sky.
Those great conquerors of yours, or those who have sought your favor with praises — they, strewing the sacrificial grass as in a homestead, protected by you, O Indra, have truly reached the prize.
Among the mighty, O hero — rejoicing — drink the Soma at the three Kadrū vessels, O Indra. Having caused your beards to tremble with delight, come with your two bays to drink of the pressed drink.
Assume the might, O hero, with which you broke down Vṛtra, Dānu, and Aurṇavābha. You revealed the light for the Ārya; the Dasyu was made to sit on his left side, O Indra.
May we be of those who, with your help, crossing over, overcome all rivals and Dasyus for the Ārya. You have subjected to us for the friendship of Trita that Tvāṣṭra-born thing of all forms.
Growing great on the pressed, exhilarating drink of Trita, he has struck down the myriad serpents. Indra with the Aṅgirases has turned the sun like a wheel; he has cloven Vala.
Now may that bountiful right hand of yours, O Indra, yield to your singer the choicest gift. Grant aid to the praisers; let our share not be consumed. May we speak great words at the assembly, possessed of heroes.
He who, as soon as born, was the first thinker, the god who encompassed the gods with his power of will — from whose might the two world-halves trembled in fear at the greatness of his manly force — he, O people, is Indra.
He who made firm the trembling earth; he who stilled the mountains when they were enraged; he who measured out the atmosphere more widely; he who propped up the sky — he, O people, is Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who, having slain the serpent, released the seven rivers; who drove out the cows having opened Vala's lair; who begot fire between the two stones — the victorious one in battles — he, O people, is Indra.
By whom these all-moving things were made; who has placed the dark Dāsa-color below, hiding it; who, like a gambler winning, has taken up the mark and the Ārya's abundance — he, O people, is Indra.
Of whom they ask in awe "Where is he?" and they even say of him "He does not exist" — yet he diminishes the Ārya's riches like a dice-player's throw. Place faith in him — he, O people, is Indra.
He who is the encourager of the feeble, of the emaciated; of the Brahman-singer calling out in distress; of the one whose pressing-stones are yoked — the fine-jawed protector of the pressed Soma — he, O people, is Indra.
Whose are the horses in every direction, whose the cattle, whose the settlements, whose all the chariots; who begot the sun, who the dawn, who is the leader of the waters — he, O people, is Indra.
Whom the two opposing battle-cries invoke — the far and the near, both enemies — having mounted the same chariot, they call upon him separately — he, O people, is Indra.
Without whom the peoples do not conquer; whom those who fight invoke for help; who has become the measure of all; who shakes the unshakable — he, O people, is Indra.
Who slew with his weapon those who were repeatedly committing great sin, those who thought nothing of it; who yields not one measure to the arrogant; who is the slayer of the Dasyu — he, O people, is Indra.
Who found Śambara dwelling in the mountains in the fortieth autumn; who slew the serpent growing in strength, Dānu lying asleep — he, O people, is Indra.
He who, seven-rayed, the mighty bull, released the seven rivers to flow; who, thunderbolt-armed, kicked away Rauhinī as she was ascending to the sky — he, O people, is Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even heaven and earth bow down to him; even the mountains fear his might. He who drinks Soma, who is intent, whose arms hold the thunderbolt, who is thunderbolt-handed — he, O people, is Indra.
Who helps the presser, who helps the cooker, who helps the reciter, who helps the toiling one with his aid; whose growing power is prayer, whose is the Soma, whose is this bounty — he, O people, is Indra.
You truly shatter the prize even for the unwilling presser and cooker — yes, you are true. May we, always dear to you, O Indra, possessed of heroes, speak forth at the assembly.
She who is the birth-season, his mother — around her waters he was swiftly born, in whom he grows. That which became swollen, brimming with milk: the first-pressed nectar of the soma-stalk — that is praiseworthy.
Together they come, bearing milk in abundance, bearing nourishment for universal enjoyment. One road runs downward along the slopes — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.
The one speaks after, whatever he gives; the other, fashioning forms, moves by means of water. All things endure the impulse of the one — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.
They sit distributing nourishment to creatures, like wealth upon the back of one who waxes great as he comes. With unsatiated fangs he eats the father's food — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.
Then thou madest the earth to be seen by heaven — thou who, slaying the serpent of the torrents, didst open the paths. The gods begat thee, like a mighty steed, to be hymned with praises and with waters — thou art praiseworthy.
Thou who dispensest nourishment and growth, who hast milked out honey-sweetness from the moist and dry alike — thou layest up treasure in the realm of the sun; thou alone art lord of all — thou art praiseworthy.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou who, by ordinance, didst hold up the blossoming and the fertile streams at their bestowing, who didst create unequal beings blazing from heaven, the wide wide-spreading on every side — thou art praiseworthy.
Thou who didst bring down Nārmarī together with his wealth, for the slaying and for the gift of Dāsaveśa — the mouth encompassed by the strength-bestowing one, and even today, O much-doer, thou art praiseworthy.
Whose hundred, even ten, eating together at once — at the summons of one alone didst thou indeed spur them forth. Thou didst bind the Dasyus without a rope for Dabhīti's sake; thou becamest most helpful — thou art praiseworthy.
All things followed the blockings of his manly power; they gave him treasure, they assigned wealth to the effective one. Thou didst prop up six expanses, five visible ones; thou becamest the encompassing beyond — thou art praiseworthy.
Well worth proclaiming is thy heroic valour, O hero, whereby with a single will thou findest goods. The might of Jātuṣṭhira the powerful dost thou increase — all that thou hast done, together with Indra, is praiseworthy.
Thou didst clear the road of those without horses and without provisions for Turvīta and for Vayya to cross. One cast down low, a cripple, thou didst raise him up; making the blind and the lame to hear — thou art praiseworthy.
Concentrate for us that wealth for giving, O Lord of wealth; great is thy richness. Indra, with the glittering renown through the days — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
O Adhvaryus, bring soma for Indra; pour the intoxicating draught into the vessels. The hero ever desires his drink — offer it to the bull; this very thing he craves.
O Adhvaryus, he who smote Vṛtra that had wrapped the waters round, as lightning strikes a tree — bring this soma to him who wills it so; Indra is worthy of drinking this.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Adhvaryus, he who slew Dṛbhīka, who drove out the cows, who cleft Vala for you — him, Indra, wrap in somas as the midair wraps the wind, as a woman wraps in garments.
O Adhvaryus, he who slew Uraṇa gnawing with ninety and nine arms, who drove Arbuda downward low — urge that Indra on at the pressing of the soma.
O Adhvaryus, he who slew Svaśna, who slew Śuṣṇa the shriveller and Vyaṁsa, who slew Pipru, Namuci, and Rudhikrā — pour the soma for that Indra.
O Adhvaryus, he who pierced the hundred strongholds of Śambara as if they were ancient stones, who felled a hundred, a thousand of the Varcinas — O Bharatas, offer soma to him.
O Adhvaryus, he who, having slain, felled a hundred, a thousand in the lap of earth — who turned back the heroes of Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva — O Bharatas, offer soma to him.
O Adhvaryus, whatever ye men desire, bringing obedience, ye shall attain that in Indra. Bring the soma purified in the palms, O worshippers; pour it for Indra who is famed.
O Adhvaryus, bestow obedience upon him; from the wood bring up what has been purified in the wood. Delighting in what is offered by hand, he calls to you — pour the exhilarating soma for Indra.
O Adhvaryus, as the udder of a cow with milk, fill Indra the enjoyer with somas. I know his secret — this very one wishes to give more; may the adorable one take note of it.
O Adhvaryus, he who is king of heavenly wealth, of earthly wealth, of terrestrial wealth — fill him, Indra, like a belly with barley-somas; so let it be of benefit to you.
Concentrate for us that wealth for giving, O Lord of wealth; great is thy richness. Indra, with the glittering renown through the days — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Now indeed let me proclaim the great and true deeds of this great one, the acts of accomplishment of the truthful one. At the three Trikadrukas he drank of the pressed soma — in the rapture of this, Indra slew the serpent.

title: Rigveda
text:
He propped up the vast sky without a prop; he filled the two world-halves and the atmosphere. He held up the earth and spread it wide — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
He measured out the eastern regions as if they were a dwelling, with his bolt he pierced the channels of the rivers. He set them free along paths running far — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
He brought to naught those who had carried off Dabhīti's possessions; he placed all weapons into the blazing fire. He released cattle, horses, and chariots — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
He stilled the great roaring flood of Ita; he brought those who could not swim safely across. They went forward to him who had bathed in wealth — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
He let the Sindhu flow northward by his greatness; with his bolt he crushed together the cloud before the dawn. He hewed asunder the swift ones with his swift steeds — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
Knowing the concealed retreat of the maidens, he rose up manifest, having turned back. The lame stood upright, the blind looked with open eyes — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, he clove Vala; he shattered the firm fortifications of the mountain. He loosed the artificial barriers of those waters — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
Lulling Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep thou didst smite them, the Dasyus; thou didst protect Dabhīti. Even the lame one found gold here — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
For you the best among the true, I bring praise as an oblation on a kindled fire. We invoke Indra, unaging, yet making others age, well-nourished, forever young, for our help.

title: Rigveda
text:
From great Indra, what is there apart? All heroic powers are gathered in him. In his belly he carries soma, in his body great strength, in his hand the thunderbolt, on his head wisdom.
By the two world-halves thy might is not encompassed, nor by the seas, nor by the mountains thy chariot, O Indra. No one overtakes thy thunderbolt when thou fliest with thy swift horses across many leagues.
All beings bring will-power to this bold and adorable one, the bull who is incessant. Worship, O bull, with oblation — thou who art wiser; drink, Indra, the soma with bull-like brilliance.
The sack of the bull flows, a wave of honey, for the bull to eat and for the bull to drink. The two bull-like Adhvaryus, the bull-like stones press out the bull-like soma for the bull.
Bull-like is thy thunderbolt and bull-like thy chariot, thy two bay horses are bulls, bull-like are thy weapons. Of the bull-like rapture, O bull, thou art lord — satiate thyself, Indra, with the bull-like soma.
I advance toward thee with a prayer, like a boat on a field of battle, bold at the pressings. May he hearken to this our word — may we pour out Indra like a spring of wealth.
Turn back to us before the press of need, as a cow full of milk turns to her calf in the pasture. O thou of a hundred plans, even once with thy graces may we meet, as with consorts the bull-like one.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Sing to him this fresh hymn as the Aṅgirases did, as his ancient strength is stirred. When in the rapture of soma he shook loose all the fortifications of the cattle-pen surrounded by force on all sides.
Let him be praised who, for the first nutriment, measuring out his might, surpassed greatness — the hero who in battle wrapt his body around, and by his greatness adorned the sky upon his head.

title: Rigveda
text:
Then thou didst perform the first great heroic deed, when thou didst rouse the mighty impulse before this with thy prayer. Shaken loose by him standing in the chariot with his bay horses, the swift ones rush forward together and apart.
Then he who surpassed all worlds in greatness, the sovereign maker with his swift-flying power, grew great. Forthwith the carrier extended both worlds with light, sewing up the darkness he wrapped it fast.
He strengthened the eastern mountains with his might, he made the waters flow downward. He held up the earth that nourishes all; by his magic power he propped up the sky lest it fall.
The weapon which the father made ready for him with both arms, choosing it from all beings and all birth — with that thunderbolt, having struck, the loud-sounding one opened the way to lay Krivi low upon the earth.
Like an old maid staying at home with her parents, I seek blessing from thee from the common seat. Make me conspicuous, bring to me — give the bodily share by which thou wouldst magnify.
As the bountiful one we call thee, O Indra — do thou give, Indra, drinks and prizes. Guard us, Indra, with splendid aid; make us richer, O bull Indra.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
At dawn a new winning chariot was yoked, four-horsed, three-whipped, seven-reined, ten-oared — a human one winning the sun; may it be swift by sacrificial rites and prayers.
He was prepared first, the second and the third — the human priest. One is born from another's womb; another begets; he, the conquering bull, accompanies still others.
Now with a fresh well-spoken word let me yoke the two bay horses to Indra's chariot to come here. May not the many seers detain thee here, nor other sacrificers.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come, Indra, with thy two bay horses; come with four, come with six, being invoked. Come with eight, with ten — this soma has been pressed for drinking; O fair-faced one, do not despise it.
Come hither with twenty, with thirty; come yoked with forty bay horses. Come, Indra, with fifty well-horsed ones, with sixty, with seventy — here is soma for drinking.
Come hither with eighty, with ninety; come carried by a hundred bay horses. For this soma in the Śunahtra rites, O Indra, has been poured out for thine own exhilaration.
Come toward my prayer, Indra; place all thy bay horses on the yoke of thy chariot. For thou hast been invocable in many places — at this pressing, O hero, be exhilarated.
May friendship with Indra not depart from me; may his right-hand gift yield to us. Under his highest shelter, under his arm, may we be victorious at each and every contest.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Drunk for the rapture of this soma draught, of the pressed offering of the wise men — in whom Indra, waxing great since ancient times, has set his abode, and in whom men delight in prayer.
Exhilarated by this sweet honey, thunderbolt in hand, Indra cut through the serpent that had dammed the waters, when the streams advanced toward their own resting places and the offerings of the rivers moved forward.
That great Indra drove the flood of the waters toward the ocean, slaying the serpent. He begat the sun, he found the cows; with night-light he established the courses of the days.
He gave many unresisted gifts to Manu, the worshipper; Indra smites Vṛtra. He who at once became unconquerable for men in the contest for the sun.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra, being praised, released the sun for the mortal, the presser; when he brought forth the hidden treasure not given away, when Naitaśa brought him his share, willing.
He ever made Śuṣṇa, the shriveller, yield to his charioteer, the evil Kuyava to Kutsa. Indra smashed the ninety and nine strongholds of Śambara for Divo-dāsa.
Thus may we proclaim for thee, Indra, the praise, seeking renown, spurring ourselves on our own. May we attain that sevenfold prize, pressing eagerly; we bow down to the weapon slaying the ungodly one who mocks.
Thus the Gṛtsamadas, O hero, seeking shelter, have fashioned prayer for thee like guides. Delighting in prayer, Indra, they who sing thy newer hymn shall win food, strength, good dwelling, and happiness.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
We are thy offspring, Indra — know us indeed; we drive forth eagerly like a chariot seeking the prize. Wise ones meditating with prayer, seeking the grace of thee and of thy men.
Thou, Indra, with thine own aids guardest the peoples devoted to thee as their protector. Thou art the lord and shelter of the worshipper — thus planning, him who approaches thee.
May young Indra, much invoked, be to us a friendly comrade, a protector of men — he who guides with his aid the one reciting and the one who has laboured, the one cooking and the one praising.
That Indra do I praise, that one do I invoke, in whom in the past men waxed strong and prospered. He shall satisfy the desire for wealth as he advances, of the one delighting in prayer, of the new generation.
Delighting in the praises of the Aṅgirases, Indra the inspired poet drove on, spurring the way. Wresting away the dawns with the sun, when praised, he clove asunder the ancient things of the rock.

title: Rigveda
text:
Verily famed is the god Indra by name; he became the highest, most marvellous for man. Having challenged the favourite of the one reigning, the self-powerful one bore off the head of the Dāsa.
That Vṛtra-slaying Indra, breaker of strongholds, drove away the dark-wombed Dāsa women. He generated earth and waters for Manu; he altogether spurred on the glory of the sacrificer.
For that powerful Indra a gift was assigned by the gods in the battle of the flood, when he placed the thunderbolt on his two arms and, having slain the Dasyus, he drove through the iron fortresses.
Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Bring soma, dear to the adorable Indra — to the all-conqueror, the wealth-conqueror, the sky-conqueror, the all-vanquisher, the man-conqueror, the field-conqueror, the horse-conqueror, the cow-conqueror, the water-conqueror.
Proclaim homage to Indra — to the overwhelming, the utterly crushing, the desiring, the unconquerable, the enduring, the ordaining, the strongly assailing, the propelling, the hard to check, the all-overpowering.
All-overpowering, people-devouring, people-subduing, the warrior Indra who shakes, sprinkled according to his pleasure, the obstructor-slayer, the subduer, who is invoked among the peoples — may I proclaim the heroic deeds Indra has performed.
Irresistible bull, the quaking death-stroke, deep, noble, of incomparable poetic skill, driving the helpless ones, destroying, firm and broad — Indra, worshipped well, generated the dawns and the sun.
By sacrifice the skilful ones found the way; the Uśijas, wise ones, spurring forward with prayers, sitting around the cows that echo with chants, seeking protection, spurring Indra, they attained riches.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra, bestow the best of riches upon us; the wisdom of skill and good fortune for us. The increase of wealth, the uninjured state of our bodies, the good taste of speech, and the auspiciousness of our days.
The great bull was satisfied and drank at the three Trikadrukas the soma mixed with barley, pressed by Viṣṇu, as he willed — the mighty one was exhilarated to do the great deed. The great, far-reaching drop follows the true god, Indra, the true god.
Then, radiant, in battle he attacked Krivi with his might; he filled the two world-halves; by his greatness he increased. Then he placed another in his belly, and overflowed from it — the true drop follows the true god Indra, the true god.
Born at once with will-power, thou hast grown together with strength; grown great at once with heroic deeds, the overwhelmer of enemies, the all-seeing. The giver of desirable wealth to the praiser — the true drop follows the true god Indra, the true god.
That manly deed of thine, O dancer Indra, the first, primeval, proclaimed in heaven — when by the god's might thou didst let loose the vital breath, releasing the waters; all the ungodly one became subject through thy might; the hundred-minded one found strength, found refreshment.
We call thee, lord of the troops, Gaṇapati, the poet among poets, most widely famed — king supreme of prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati; hearing us, come, take thy seat with thine aids in the seat of worship.
Even the gods, O Bṛhaspati, thy far-seeing lordly ones, obtained their sacrificial share. Like mornings by the sun's great light — thou art verily the progenitor of all sacred formulas.
Driving away the slanderers and the dark ones, thou standest on the luminous chariot of cosmic order, O Bṛhaspati — terrible, crushing the enemies, slaying the Rākṣasas, cleaving the mountain cave, finding the sun.

title: Rigveda
text:
With good guidance thou leadest and protectest the man who has offered to thee; no distress overtakes him. Thou art the scorcher of those who hate sacred prayer, the source of wrath, O Bṛhaspati — great is that thy greatness.
No distress, no mishap from anywhere overwhelms him, nor do enmities, nor the deceitful — all crookedness thou drivest away from him whom thou, well-protecting, guardest, O Brahmaṇaspati.
Thou art our guardian, path-maker, far-seeing; by our prayers we worship according to thy ordinance. O Bṛhaspati, whoever places crooked intent against us — may calamity, the hateful one, afflict that man himself.
Or whosoever would harm us, though we are guiltless — a mortal, like an enemy wolf who sneaks close — O Bṛhaspati, turn him from the path; make it easy for us on this path to the divine gathering.
We call thee as protector of our bodies, as the rescuer, the advocate, who favours us. O Bṛhaspati, crush down the revilers of the gods; may the ill-intentioned not attain the highest happiness.
With thee, O Brahmaṇaspati, who makest well grow, may we receive the desirable, human good things. The enmities that are afar, the thunderings against us, the hostilities that threaten us — crush them all, the harmless ones.
With thee, O Bṛhaspati, the filling companion who conquers, may we attain the highest wellbeing. Let not the ill-spoken one who desires to harm us rule us; may we overcome with prayers, well-spoken.
Irresistible bull, going to the invocation, who burns down the enemy, who has conquered in battles — thou art the truly due debt-exactor, O Brahmaṇaspati, the tamer even of the violent and bold-rejoicing one.
He who intends to harm with ungodly mind, who powerful and imperious seeks to slay — O Bṛhaspati, let not his deadly blow reach us; lay down the wrath of the evilly-abiding proud one.

title: Rigveda
text:
He is to be called upon in battles, to be approached with reverence, the one who goes to the prizes and wins wealth upon wealth. All the attacks of the enemy who desires to harm, Bṛhaspati has driven away like chariots.
With the most keen and scorching one, scorch the Rākṣasas who have held thee in contempt, whose powers are manifest. Make that praiseworthy thing visible which is to be; O Bṛhaspati, afflict and crush the slanderers.
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the stranger's excellence, which shines luminously with wisdom among the peoples — that which blazes with power, O thou born of ṛta — bestow that brilliant wealth upon us.
O Bṛhaspati, let not thieves, those who would injure, the destructive enemies who lie in wait for prey, be against us. At the summons of the gods the woollen threads are spread upon the heart — no one beyond knows the secret.
Tvaṣṭṛ created thee, the poet, beyond all worlds, sāman by sāman. He, the debt-exactor, the exactor of debts, is Brahmaṇaspati, the slayer of wrong, the upholder of great cosmic order.
For thy glory the mountain opened wide when the cave of the cows was unsealed, O Aṅgiras. Allied with Indra, O Bṛhaspati, thou didst cause the ocean of the waters, surrounded by darkness, to stream forth.
O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou the controller of this hymn; be aware, and quicken its offspring. All that is blessed which the gods protect — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Protect this offering here, thou who art lord; with this fresh great hymn we would worship. So that the bounteous one, thy friend, praises us, O Bṛhaspati, succeed and quicken our prayer.
He who bent the bending obstacles down with his might, and shattered the devices of Śambara with wrath — Brahmaṇaspati set shaking what was immovable and entered and opened the wealth-containing mountain.

title: Rigveda
text:
That was to be done for the most divine of the gods — the firm ones unloosed and broke apart the solid strongholds. He drove the cows out; with his prayer he clove Vala; he hid the darkness and made the sunlight visible.
Brahmaṇaspati pierced with his might the rocky cave that streams with honey. All those who see the sun drank from that very one; together they poured into the welling spring abundantly.
Whatever worlds there are that have been and are yet to be — for many seasons their doors have been closed to you. Roaming without effort, each in a different direction, are the courses that Brahmaṇaspati has ordained.
Those who approached and attained to it, the supreme treasure of the Paṇis, hidden in the cave — those wise ones, looking back at the untruth, from whence they had come, rose up openly.
Those who possess cosmic order, looking back at untruth, came and stood firm on the path of the great. They by both arms fanned the fire in the stone — there is none who is a stranger; verily they abandoned him.
Brahmaṇaspati with the bow-string of cosmic order, with the swift one — where he desires, thither he reaches with his bow. His are the true arrows with which he shoots, for seeing by men; those born for the ear.
He is the leader, the guide, the domestic priest, the one well praised, the warrior — Brahmaṇaspati. He is fit to see when prayer brings the prize; it is from wealth alone that the sun burns; the heat burns in vain.
Vast, mighty, the first — of the exuberant Bṛhaspati the riches to be attained are well-known. These prizes of the admirable prize-winner — with which both peoples enjoy, the clans.
He who is all-pervading in the lower assembly and great — joyful, grown great by power. That god extended wide before the gods; Brahmaṇaspati is the encompasser of all these things.

title: Rigveda
text:
All truth is yours indeed, O bounteous pair; even the waters do not transgress your ordinance. Come to our oblation, O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati — come to our food like two prize-winners to a yoke.
The carriers, those who stand above, hear and follow; the eloquent sage brings wealth with his prayer in the assembly. He exacted the debt at will of those who hate firmly — Brahmaṇaspati is truly the prize-winner in the battle.
It happened as Brahmaṇaspati willed — the true wrath of the one about to perform the great deed. He who drove out the cows, he divided them among the heavens; like a great stream it flowed forth separately by power.
O Brahmaṇaspati, may we be always in possession of easily controlled wealth that has offspring; masters of the chariot, full of vigour. Mix the hero among heroes for us — thou who art lord and dost heed my call with thy prayer.
O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou the controller of this hymn; be aware, and quicken its offspring. All that is blessed which the gods protect — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
Kindling Agni, he shall conquer the foes who wish him ill; he who has wrought the sacred hymn, who has offered the oblation, shall flourish exceedingly. Born after born he overruns and surpasses them — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.
With heroes he shall conquer the hostile heroes; with kine he has spread wealth wide and is himself awake. His offspring and his progeny both grow and thrive — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.
Like a rushing river, mighty, he overwhelms those who rage against him; like a bull he overpowers the weaklings with his might. Like the onrush of Agni there is no turning it back — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.
For him the heavenly, inexhaustible ones stream forth; he with his warriors goes foremost among the cows. His force undiminished, he slays with might — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

title: Rigveda
text:
All rivers rush resoundingly for him; unbroken, they have bestowed many shelters upon him. In the goodwill of the gods he prospers, the blessed one — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.
Truly the honest worshipper shall conquer those who wish him ill; he who is devout shall prevail over the impious. He who is well-equipped shall win in battles the hard-to-conquer; he who sacrifices distributes the enjoyment from the non-sacrificer.
Sacrifice, O hero; send forth to those who are devoted; make your mind auspicious in the conquest of Vṛtra. Prepare the oblation so that you may be blessed — we choose the grace of Brahmaṇaspati for ourselves.
He indeed with his folk, with his clan, with his kindred, with his sons, bears off the prize-booty and wealth with his men — he who with devoted heart and oblation seeks to please Brahmaṇaspati, father of the gods.
Him who has attended Brahmaṇaspati with fat-laden oblations, Brahmaṇaspati leads forward on the eastern path. He guards from distress, protects from injury — the wide-acting, wondrous one saves him even from the narrowest strait.
These hymns, flowing like ghee, I offer with my tongue as an oblation to the Ādityas, the eternal kings. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga hear us, may Varuṇa of mighty birth, Dakṣa, and Aṁśa hear.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, of one purpose with me, accept this hymn of praise today. The Ādityas, pure, cleansed by the stream of truth, faultless, blameless, inviolate.
Those Ādityas are broad and deep, undeceived, warding off deceit, with many eyes. They see within both the crooked and the straight — all things are near even to these kings from the farthest distance.
The Ādityas sustain the moving and the standing; they are gods, guardians of all the world. Of far-reaching wisdom, protecting their divine lordship, upholders of ṛta, exacting the dues owed them.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Ādityas, may we know your aid in this matter — O Aryaman, even from fear there is comfort. Under your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I turn aside all evils as around a pit.
For easy is your path, O Aryaman, free of thorns, O Mitra; it is well-made, O Varuṇa. By that path, O Ādityas, speak favorably for us; grant us shelter hard for the wicked to assail.
May Aditi, daughter of kings, carry us across all enmities; may Aryaman do so by easy paths. May we abide under the great shelter of Mitra and Varuṇa, rich in heroes, unharmed.
They sustain three earths and likewise three heavens; three ordinances are established within their assembly. By ṛta, O Ādityas, great is your greatness — that, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, Mitra, is beautiful.
They sustain the three divine luminous realms; golden are they, pure, cleansed by truth's stream. Unsleeping, unwinking, undeceived, of wide renown — they exist for the protection of the upright mortal.
You, O Varuṇa, are king of all — both those gods who are lords of might, and mortals as well. Grant us a hundred autumns that we may see; may we obtain lives well-placed from of old.
Neither to the south is it discerned, O Ādityas, nor to the north, neither to the east nor to the west. Even from the wise and the thoughtful, O Vasus — guided by you, may I attain the fearless light.
He who has offered to the royal lords of ṛta, whom the perennial abundances make to grow — he, the wealthy one, goes foremost in the chariot, the giver of wealth, praised in the assemblies.
Pure, abounding in good pasture, undeceived, he dwells nearby, grown to old age, rich in heroes. None strikes him down, from near or far — he who is under the guidance of the Ādityas.
O Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, be gracious — whatever transgression we have committed against you. May I attain the wide, fearless light, O Indra; let not the long darkness overcome us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Both, meeting together, bestow abundance on him — the rain of heaven, which the fortunate one cherishes by name. He goes conquering both realms in battles; both parties become favorable to him.
Those snares of yours set for the treacherous, O adorable Ādityas, the meshes spread for the enemy — may we pass beyond them like swift horses in a chariot, unharmed, in the wide shelter.
May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.
This is from the seer of Āditya, the self-resplendent sovereign — may it overcome all things with its greatness. He who is the exhilarating god beyond reckoning for worship — I beg the great fame of Varuṇa.
In your ordinance may we be blessed and self-sufficient, O Varuṇa, praising you well. Like fires aging through the days, in the coming of the cow-rich Dawns.
May we be in the shelter of you, O Varuṇa, leader, rich in heroes, of wide renown. You, O gods, sons of Aditi, undeceived — govern over us for our companionship.
Āditya released these who sustain creation; the rivers flow on by Varuṇa's ṛta. They do not weary, nor do they let go — like birds they flew, swift, wheeling around.
Loosen me, as a rope, from sin; may we prosper at your spring of ṛta, O Varuṇa. Let not the thread be cut while I am weaving; let not the measure be broken before the work is done.
Drive fear away from me, O Varuṇa, O sovereign, O upholder of ṛta — seize me not! Like a calf from a rope, loosen the sin from me; for truly I cannot command even the twinkling of an eye without you.
O Varuṇa, let not your missiles that are aimed at the sinner strike us, O mighty one. Let us not depart to the far realms of light; loose our bonds, O gracious one, so that we may live.

title: Rigveda
text:
Homage to you of old, O Varuṇa, and also now — and again in days to come we shall speak, O mighty-born. For in you, as on a mountain, rest the unshaken, hard-to-attain ordinances.
Remove the debts that I myself have made, O sovereign; let me not be made to consume what another has committed. Many are the dawns not yet come to light — in those, O Varuṇa, instruct us living ones.
He who is my companion or comrade, O king, or who in a dream tells fear to the fearful like me — whether a thief who plans to betray us, or a wolf — from that one, O Varuṇa, protect us.
May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.
The Ādityas, upholders of vows, are swift-moving — keep sin far from me as one keeps a secret wrong at a distance. I, who know the good, call upon you for aid, O Varuṇa, Mitra, gods who are listening.
You, O gods, are wisdom; you are strength; you are those who ward off enmities from afar. You are the overseers; govern over us — today be gracious to us and also in the future.
What shall we do for you anew, O Vasus, or what by the ancient, intimate bond? You, O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, and Indra and the Maruts — grant us prosperity.
O gods — you indeed are they who must help; be gracious to me who am supplicating. Let not your chariot pass us by in the midst without cause; may we not toil in vain among those who depend on you, among your intimates.
I have indeed committed many transgressions — that which a father like a gambler has instructed me in. Far away be the snares, far away the evils, O gods; seize me not in it as a bird in a net.
Turn toward us today, O adorable ones — I, full of fear, would lay open my heart to you. Protect us, O gods, from the ravage of the wolf; protect us from the pit into which one falls, O adorable ones.

title: Rigveda
text:
May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.
