For Savitṛ who makes ṛta, for Indra the serpent-slayer, the waters do not rest. Day after day the ray of the waters passes on; the first flood of them rushes forth.
He who was about to bring destruction here upon Vṛtra — him his mother declared, knowing it. The roaring rivers, breaking the paths in their pleasure, flow day after day to their goal.
For he stood upright above the mid-region, and thus brought forth his weapon for Vṛtra. Clothed in mist he rushed upon him — Indra, of sharp weapons, conquered the foe.
O Bṛhaspati, pierce like a burning arrow the heroes of the wolf-doored demon. As you slew of old with boldness — even so slay our enemy, O Indra.
Hurl down the stone from heaven on high, with which, exhilarated, you crush the foe. In the gaining of offspring and of abundant progeny, let Indra make us the better half of the cows.
For you carry forth the purpose which you desire to win; you are the stimulators of the poor sacrificer. O Indra and Soma, do you two help us; in this fearful place make for us a world.
Darkness shall not oppress me, nor weariness, nor torpor; we shall not say 'press not the Soma.' He who fills me, who gives, who heeds me, who comes to me when I am pressing with kine.
O Sarasvatī, do you help us; with the Maruts, bold, conquer the enemies. Even that raging, mighty one — Indra slays the bull of the Śaṇḍikas.
He who from afar or who is about to strike us — look upon him, pierce him with your sharp weapon. O Bṛhaspati, conquer the enemies with your weapons; enclose in a ring the treacherous injurer, O king.
With our warriors, O hero, perform heroic deeds — those which are yours to do. Long may they be scattered as smoke; having slain them, bring us their riches.

title: Rigveda
text:
That host of yours, the Marutas — I who desire their goodwill implore with a hymn and homage the divine folk. That we may daily attain to wealth rich in all heroes, accompanied by offspring, worthy of praise.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect our chariot together with the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus. When the glory-hungry, exhilarated forest-dwellers flew like birds around the garment.
Thus, O gods, willingly do you carry upward our chariot, the prize-seeking one, among the clans. When the swift ones, spreading with their feet, stamped the dust on the ridge of the earth with their hoofs.
And may Indra, beholder of all peoples, the wise in purpose, together with the Marutic host of heaven — may he follow close after us with his wolf-like aids for the winning of great wealth in the contest.
And may Tvaṣṭṛ, the sustainer of existence, together with the wives of the gods in accord, spur on the chariot. Iḷā, Bhaga, Bṛhaddivu, and the two world-halves, Pūṣan, Puraṁdhi, the two Aśvins — they are the lords.
And those two blessed goddesses who behold each other in turn — Dawn and Night, quickeners of the moving world — may I, O Earth, with a fresh utterance praise you; and may all plants that are spreading spring forth from your offspring.
And we proclaim your praise as do the Uśijs — Ahir Budhnya and Aja Ekapād. Trita, Ṛbhukṣan, Savitṛ has placed his benevolence; Apāṁ Napāt, swift of impulse, has achieved his purpose through prayer.
These are those I desire from you, O adorable ones, prepared — which mortal men have fashioned anew together. Like a chariot-horse longing for the prize, O glory-seeker — today may I attain the inspired thought.
O Heaven and Earth, be my protectors in ṛta as I seek to win with speech. With whose life-span is longer — those I, who desire wealth, formerly, when praised, have set as great offerings to you both.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let not secret enemies beguile and harm us, let them not injure us with ill omens. Let not the friendship between us be sundered — knowing that, we entreat you with a mind set on goodwill.
With an unoffending mind bring hearing — the milch cow, swelling inexhaustibly. I urge you, O much-invoked one, each day, with my feet swift in motion and my prize-winning speech.
I invoke Rākā, easy to call, with excellent praise; may the blessed one hear us and awaken of herself. May she sew works together with her needle without missing; may she grant a hero, worthy of praise, the giver of a hundredfold.
O Rākā, those benevolent, well-formed thoughts of yours with which you bestow riches upon the worshipper — with those come to us today, O blessed one, well-disposed, granting thousandfold prosperity.
O Sinīvāli of broad braids, you who are the sister of the gods — accept the oblation that has been offered; O goddess, bestow offspring upon us.
She who has beautiful arms, beautiful fingers, who is kind, mother of many — for her, for the lady of the house, for Sinīvāli, offer the oblation.
She who is Guṅgū, she who is Sinīvāli, she who is Rākā, she who is Sarasvatī — I call upon Indrāṇī for help, and Varuṇānī for well-being.
O father of the Maruts, may your goodwill come to us; do not keep us away from the sight of the sun. May the hero fare well on his horse; may we be born and multiply in offspring, O Rudra.
With your most healing medicines, O Rudra, with those given by you, may I live a hundred winters. Drive far from us hatred and anguish; ward off diseases in all directions.
You are the most glorious among the born, O Rudra — the mightiest of the mighty, O you of the thunderbolt arm. Carry us beyond distress to well-being; ward off all attacks of injury.
Let us not anger you, O Rudra, with our homage; not with ill praise, O bull, not with invocation. Lift up our heroes with your medicines — I hear that you are the most excellent of healers.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who calls with oblations, him who calls with offerings — with praises I would propitiate Rudra. The tender-bellied, easy to invoke — may the brown, fine-lipped one not harm us, nor our minds.
The bull accompanied by the Maruts has cheered me up, who was supplicating, with swiftly increasing vital strength. Sinless as a shadow in the sun's warmth, I would seek the goodwill of Rudra.
Where, O Rudra, is your gracious hand — that which is healing and cooling? O you who remove divine injury — do look upon me, O bull.
To the tawny bull, the white-shining one, I utter great and glorious praise. With reverences we honor the matted one; we proclaim the terrible name of Rudra.
With his firm limbs, of many forms, the fierce and tawny one is adorned with shining gold ornaments. From Rudra who rules this wide existence, divine lordship shall never depart.
Worthily you bear the arrows and the bow; worthily you wear the neck-ornament worthy of worship, all-formed. Worthily you share out this formidable universe — there is nothing mightier than you, O Rudra.
Praise the famous one who sits in the chariot seat, the youthful — terrible and fierce like a wild beast, smiting. Be gracious when praised, O Rudra, to the singer; let your arrows strike down another, not us.
Even a child bows back to his father when Rudra approaches, to him who comes with reverence. I praise you as the great giver, the true master — you, when praised, give medicines to us.
Those pure medicines of yours, O Maruts — those most soothing, O bulls, those beneficent ones — those which Manu our father chose — the weal and joy of Rudra I desire.
May the missile of Rudra pass us by; may the great malevolence of the fierce one pass away. Loosen the rigid ones from the bountiful ones, O liberal giver; be gracious to our offspring and progeny.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even so, O tawny bull, O wise one, be such, O god, that you do not wroth and do not slay. Hearing our invocations, O Rudra, be gracious here — may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.
The Maruts, possessors of rain-streams, of bold might, are terrible as wild beasts in their strengths and shine brightly. Like fires blazing in splendor, impetuous, roaring, they have driven away the cows.
Like heavens with stars they shine, the devouring ones; like lightning from the cloud the rains flash forth. When Rudra, O Maruts of golden breastplates, engendered you as the vigorous ones from the bright udder of Pṛśni.
They anoint themselves like race-horses in the contests, hastening swiftly with the ears of the roaring stream. O golden-helmeted Maruts, gleaming and shaking, you come to the prize with the dappled mares, all of one mind.
At the prize they have borne all the worlds within them, quick givers, whether ever for Mitra. Dapple-horsed ones of inexhaustible wealth, rushing like hawks in their courses, sitting firmly in the chariot-pole.
With kindling fires, with milch cows of swelling udder, with roads without dust, with shining glances — like swans to their resting-places come, O Maruts of one accord, for the exhilaration of the honey-sweet.
Come to our sacred prayers, O Maruts of one accord, as the praise of men to the pressings. Like one who fattens the udder of a milch cow — create for the singer a thought that is shaped by the prize.
Give us that — the prize-winning one in the chariot, the food that lights up the prayer day by day. Refreshment for the praisers in the enclosures, for the poet — gain, wisdom, inviolability, irresistible might.
When the Maruts of golden breastplates yoke their horses to the chariots in their season, O good givers — like a cow to her calf they swell with abundance in their stations, bestowing great refreshment upon the people who have offered the oblation.

title: Rigveda
text:
Whatever mortal enemy sets upon us with wolf-like onslaught, O Vasus, protect us from injury. Turn the fiery wheel-weapon against him; strike him down, O Rudras, with the slaying weapon aimed at the impious.
Wondrous is that journey of yours, O Maruts, which is celebrated — when the streams milked from Pṛśni's udder. Or when the Rudra-born ones, who are to blame the newly born one, the undeceiving ones, grant Trita to old age to be aged.
Those great Maruts who pass on swiftly we invoke at the advancing of Viṣṇu's step. Golden-hued, lofty, with streaming garments, we who are devoted to prayer seek from them praiseworthy bounty.
They, the ten-fold firstborn, were the first to celebrate the sacrifice; may they impel us at the break of the Dawns. Dawn, like a dark woman, uncovers herself with the ruddy beams of the great, pure light, rich in cows.
The Rudras, with their ruddy, unanointed earth-lands, have grown strong in the seats of ṛta. Dripping moisture, with the strength of a steed rushing past, they have assumed a bright complexion, beautiful in form.
Seeking those for great shelter and for aid, we approach them indeed with homage and praise. Even as Trita turned the five sacrificial priests downward for the wheel's protection against the oppressor.
With that aid by which you convey the helpless man beyond distress, by which you free the praiser from the revilers — O Maruts, let that aid of yours turn toward us; may your benevolence come like a lowing cow.
I have been impelled forward, eager for the prize-winning eloquence; may the voice of the rivers rejoice in my hymns. Apāṁ Napāt of swift impulse — will he not render them beautiful and take pleasure in them?
This hymn well-fashioned from the heart — may we speak it; will he come to know it? Apāṁ Napāt, the lord, has by the greatness of his divine lordship generated all the worlds.

title: Rigveda
text:
Some waters come together, others flow toward them — the rivers fill the same enclosure. The pure and shining waters have stood around him, Apāṁ Napāt, who is pure and shining.
The unwearied young women, the waters, polishing him, the young one, go around him. He of shining and skillful powers shines brightly for us — kindled, clad in ghee, within the waters.
Three divine women, goddesses, place food for this god without tiring. Constructed, as it were, he has crept forward in the waters; he drinks the first milk of those who gave birth first.
Here is the birthplace of the horse and of the sun; protect the wise ones from the injury of treachery, from mingling with it. In the unripened fortresses, that which cannot be forgotten beyond — may the hostilities vanish, and all falsehoods.
In his own house whose milch cow gives freely, who has drunk up the self-rule and eats wholesome food — that Apāṁ Napāt, energizing within the waters, shines forth for the worshipper for the giving of riches.
He who shines widely within the waters with divine purity, an upholder of ṛta inexhaustible — indeed the other worlds and plants with their offspring are born as his branches.
Apāṁ Napāt has stood up in the womb of the recumbent ones, upright, wearing lightning as a garment. Carrying his greatest greatness, the golden-hued, mighty ones go around him.
Of golden form is he, of golden appearance — Apāṁ Napāt, he too is golden in color. Sitting within the golden womb, the golden givers give food to him.
That face of his, and the dear, secret name of Apāṁ Napāt, grows. He whom the young women kindle together in just this way — his food is golden-hued ghee.
For him, in the friendship of the most lowly of many, we would worship with sacrifices, with homage and oblations. I polish the ridge, I light it with tinder, I place food around it — I honor it with hymns.

title: Rigveda
text:
He, the bull, engendered the embryo in them; he as an infant sucks from them, they lick him. That Apāṁ Napāt of unfading color has entered here as if with another's body.
Stationed in this highest station, shining everywhere with unstained paths — the great waters, carrying ghee and food to Apāṁ Napāt's grandson, flow around of their own accord with their garments.
I have obtained for the people, O Agni, a good dwelling; I have also obtained excellent praise for the bountiful ones. All that is auspicious which the gods protect — may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.
Urging for you, O Vasiṣṭha, the men milked the kine and the waters with sheep-wool and pressing-stones. Drink, O Indra, the Soma that has been offered with Svāhā, consecrated with Vaṣaṭ, from the Hotṛ's station — you who as first have the sovereignty.
Mingled with the sacrifices and with the dappled mares and spears, beautiful in their anointing on the path, and dear — O sons of Bharata, having taken your seat on the sacred grass, O men of heaven, drink the Soma from the Potṛ's station.
Come near to us like a friend, easy to invoke; sit down upon the sacred grass and rejoice. Then be exhilarated, taking pleasure in the drink, O Tvaṣṭṛ, with the gods and with the divine women, in their company.
Bring hither the gods, O inspired Hotṛ — sacrifice, eager one; sit down in the three stations. Fill in return the onward-moving soma-honey; drink from the Agnīdh's station; satisfy yourself with your own share.
This is that which increases the manly strength of your body, the might placed from of old in your two arms. O bountiful one, it has been pressed for you and brought to you — you yourself, O Indra, drink to satisfaction from the Brahman's station.
Take pleasure in the sacrifice, both of you; hearken to my call. The Hotṛ, having sat down, recites the nivid following the ancient formula. Homage goes toward the two kings who turn hither — from the Praśāstr's station, drink the soma-honey.

title: Rigveda
text:
Be gladdened, O Adhvaryus, according to your pleasure from the Hotṛ's share of the soma-juice — he who desires a full vessel of the libation. Bring therefore this draught to him, the generous giver, obedient to his will: drink the soma from the Hotṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.
Him whom I invoked aforetime, that same one I invoke now — he is indeed worthy of invocation, the liberal giver who rules by his very name. Drink the sweet soma-draught set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.
Let your carriers be purified — those by which you travel, unharmed; be you firm, O Vanaspati. Bold one, having roared forth with your fierce cry, drink the soma from the Neṣṭṛ's cup, O Draviṇodas, at the (proper) seasons.
Not from the Hotṛ's cup, nor from the Potṛ's has he drunk to satiety, nor did he relish the oblation set forth from the Neṣṭṛ's cup. Let Draviṇodas drink from the fourth vessel, uncontaminated and immortal, belonging to the Son of Draviṇodas.
Harness your swift chariot, man-borne and fit for travel, hither today — here shall be your unyoking. The oblations are mingled with honey; come then, and drink the soma, O ye two whose wealth is in strength (Vājinīvasū — the Aśvins).
Be pleased, O Agni, with the kindling-wood; be pleased with the oblation; be pleased with the brahman (prayer) belonging to the people; be pleased with the hymn of praise. O Vasu, great one, with all the gods at the (proper) season, being yourself desirous, make the desirous gods drink the oblation.
Up has risen this god Savitṛ for his stimulation; the ever-constant carrier (of offerings) has taken his stand thereby. Now he distributes treasure among the gods, and has shared out (his gifts) with the fire of offering in blessing.
For the hearing of all, the god rises upright, extending his two arms with broad hands. Even the waters sink down at his ordinance; even this wind rests in its circuit.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even those (steeds) which he now unyokes with the swiftest, even the untamed course has rested. Even the paths of the water-rushing serpents have been laid down; following the ordinance of Savitṛ, (the world) has come to release.
She who weaves has again rolled up what was spread out; the wise one has laid down her skill in the midst of her work. The divine Savitṛ, Aramati (Piety), has risen up, having shaken apart the seasons.
The abodes of diverse forms pervade all of life throughout the house — such is the power, the flame of Agni. The mother has assigned the best portion to her son; Savitṛ has impelled (men to act) following his will.
Having taken his stance, eager to conquer, he (the sun) has wheeled back; the desire of all who roam about has come home. Leaving behind the ever-flowing waters in their altered state, he has come back following the divine ordinance of Savitṛ.
The share of water-dwelling (creatures) placed by you in the waters — the gazelles tracking across the desert have spread out (to their own places). No one violates the woodlands (which belong) to the various (creatures); none transgress the ordinances of the divine Savitṛ.
Where Varuṇa lies unsleeping, blinking in the watery womb — every living creature, Mārtāṇḍa (the sun-bird), has gone to the fold; Savitṛ has declared the births of those that stand (on the earth).
Whose ordinance neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra violates, nor do hostile powers — him, this divine Savitṛ, I now invoke for blessing with reverences.
Striving for Bhaga, for wise understanding, for eloquence — may Narāśaṁsa and Gnāspati protect us. May we be dear to the divine Savitṛ at the confluence of riches, at the gathering-place of wealth.
May the desirable bounty from heaven, from the waters, from the earth, given by you, come to us. That which brings blessing to the praisers, to the one who seeks refreshment — O Savitṛ, widely acclaimed, to your singer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like two pressing-stones you praise that very purpose; like a vulture toward a tree that holds a treasure. Like two chanters of brahman in the assembly, reciting the uktha-verse; like two messengers (you convey) the oblations belonging to the people in many places.
Going forth at dawn, like two chariot-warriors, like two Yamas you attain the boon together. Like two women adorning their bodies, like a husband and wife knowing (the proper) rites among the people.
Come first to us as the (two) horns (of an animal), gnawing powerfully like two hooves. Come hither at dawn like two ruddy geese (cakravākas) at the break of day, like two capable chariot-warriors.
Like a boat, carry us across; like a yoke, (uphold us) like the nave (of a wheel), like the felloe, like the circumference. Like a dog, keep our bodies from injury; like the khṛgala-bird (which warns), protect us from calamity.
Come hither like the aging (rush) of wind, like the flowing of a river, like two eyes with their sight. Most beneficent for our body, like two hands — like two feet, lead us toward (greater) well-being.
Like two lips speaking sweetness into the mouth, like two breasts, fill us (with nourishment) for life. Like two nostrils, be the guardians of our body; like two ears, be you sharp-hearing among us.
Like a hand, bestow power on us; like the earth, gather together our (scattered) spaces. These songs, O Aśvins, yearning for you — sharpen them like an axe on a whetstone.
These (words) that strengthen you, O Aśvins — the Gṛtsamadas have made (this) brahman-hymn of praise. O ye two heroes, come delighting in them; may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.
O Soma and Pūṣan, generators of riches, generators of heaven, generators of earth — the two guardians born of all existence — the gods made you the navel of immortality.

title: Rigveda
text:
These two gods as they are being born show favor; let these two conceal the undesired darknesses. Through these two — Soma and Pūṣan — Indra generated the ripe (cattle) within the raw (stones), among the ruddy cows (of dawn).
O Soma and Pūṣan, the measure of the atmosphere is the seven-wheeled chariot that pervades all space — turning in opposite directions, yoked by the mind: that chariot with five reins, O ye two bulls, you impel.
One has made his seat on high in heaven; the other (moves) above the earth in mid-air. Let those two release for us the navel of abundant bounty, the richly-nourishing pouring-forth of riches, upon us.
One has engendered all the worlds; the other moves beholding everything. O Soma and Pūṣan, strengthen my thought; through you both may we conquer all opposing hosts.
May Pūṣan, all-pervading, quicken (our) thought; may Soma, lord of riches, establish wealth. May the divine, unassailable Aditi protect (us); may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.
O Vāyu, come hither with those thousandfold chariots of yours, drawn by your team, to drink the soma.
O Vāyu, with your team come hither — this bright (soma) is poured out for you. You shall be one who goes to the house of the soma-presser.
Of the bright (soma) mixed today with milk — O Indra and Vāyu, with your teams, come hither, O ye two heroes, and drink.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of truth (ṛta) — this soma is pressed out for you both. Hear my invocation here.
The two kings without treachery are seated in the firm, highest assembly — the hall with a thousand pillars.
Those two universal sovereigns, for whom ghee is poured, the two Ādityas, lords of the gift (dānu) — they associate without deviation.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins — come hither with (gifts of) cattle, with horses. O Rudra (sons of Rudra), bring the wealth worthy of heroes.

title: Rigveda
text:
That no malicious mortal enemy from without or from within might do harm to you, O ye two whose wealth is the bull (Vṛṣaṇvasū — the Aśvins).
O Aśvins, bring us here the wealth of tawny aspect, O ye attentive ones, that finds wide space.
Indra, truly, has shaken off great terror from here; for he is the firm one, the all-seeing.
And may Indra be gracious to us; let no evil overtake us from behind; may blessedness be before us.
May Indra make (us) fearless on every side, on all quarters — the all-seeing conqueror of enemies.
O all-gods (Viśvedevāḥ), come hither; hear this invocation of mine; sit down upon this barhis-grass.
This intoxicating (soma), pungent and sweet, for you in the rites of the Śunahotras — drink this desirable (draught).
The Marut-hosts with Indra as their chief, the gods with Pūṣan as their gift-giver — all of you, hear my invocation.
O Sarasvatī, best of mothers, best of rivers, best of goddesses — we are as though without praise; O mother, make praise for us.
In you, O Sarasvatī divine, all life-forces are sheltered. Find joy in the rites of the Śunahotras; O goddess, shine upon our progeny.
Be pleased, O Sarasvatī possessed of sustenance (Vājinīvatī), with this brahman-prayer — the devotion that the Gṛtsamadas, O guardian of truth (ṛtāvari), dear to the gods, offer up to you.
We choose only you two, the two beneficent ones presiding over the sacrifice, to go forth — and Agni the bearer of oblations.
May Heaven and Earth today direct this successful, sky-touching sacrifice among the gods.
In your lap, O ye two without treachery, let the divine and holy powers sit here today for the drinking of soma.
Crying again and again, announcing (yourself) by your birth-cry, you set your voice in motion like a rower his boat. Be you of auspicious omen, O bird; may no universal misfortune find you.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let not the hawk slay you, nor the eagle; let not the armed warrior-archer find you. Crying again and again in the direction of the ancestors, speak here as an auspicious, good-word-speaking one.
Cry down (your omen) from the south upon our houses, auspicious and good-word-speaking, O bird (śakunta). Let no thief gain power over us, no wicked one; may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.
The śakunta-birds (kārus) sing circling sunwise; the birds speak in their proper season. It (the bird) utters both voices as though a sāman-singer — it reigns over the gāyatrī and the triṣṭubh in succession.
Like an Udgātṛ, O bird, you sing the sāman; like a brahman's son you recite at the soma-pressings. Like a powerful bull (going) to the nursing cows, proclaim blessings to us from every side, O bird; proclaim what is auspicious to us from all directions, O bird.
You who are speaking, O bird, speak blessings; even sitting in silence, discern well-being for us. When you speak as you fly up, like the karkarī (calling bird) — may we speak the great (word) in the assembly, endowed with good heroes.
O Agni, Soma's mighty one, you bear me — you have been made the conveyor at the sacrifice for worship. Shining toward the gods you harness the pressing-stone; for peace, O Agni, be pleased with your own body.
We have directed the sacrifice eastward; let our song increase while we honour Agni with fuel and reverence. The wise ones who have ruled the assemblies of heaven have sought a path even to the mighty one for the Gṛtsamadas.
The wise one of pure skill, kinsman of heaven by birth and of earth, has established the seat of joy. The gods found Agni, the visible one, dwelling within the waters, amid the work of the sister-streams.
The seven great rivers nurtured the blessed one, born white and ruddy in his greatness. The divine mares ran around Agni at his birth, as though around a new-born child, glorying in his beauty.

title: Rigveda
text:
Spreading his domain with bright limbs, purifying wisdom with the strainers of the seers, clothing himself in flame, measuring out the life-span of the waters — he fashions their great splendours, full and unfailing.
The mighty ones of heaven, inviolate and fireless, have wandered about not crying out, coming to rest. Here the seven voices, ever young and of one womb, have held together the single embryo.
His forms, all gathered together and all-shaped, are spread in the womb of ghee at the flowing of the sweet liquors. There the swelling cows have stood; the two great mothers of the wondrous one have met together.
Shining brown, the son of strength has blazed forth, bearing bright and vigorous forms. The streams of honey and of ghee drip down where the bull has grown through his poetic power.
By his birth he found even the udder of the father; he poured forth his streams and loosed the milk-cows. Moving in secret with his benevolent companions, through the great powers of heaven, he was no longer hidden in the cave.
He bore the embryo of both father and mother; alone he sucked the many swelling ones. The two co-wives of the gleaming bull, kindred to each other, both human — protect them for him.
In wide space the great one, unimpeded, has grown, for many glorious waters have come together in Agni. The householder has lain in the womb of Ṛta; Agni rests in the work of the kindred sister-streams.
Brown like a hawk in the encounter of the great ones, brilliant Agni, wishing to be seen, comes to his son. He who begot the ruddy cows — the great young Agni, embryo of the waters, most manly — has risen up.
The auspicious one has engendered the visible embryo of the waters and the forests and the herbs, of manifold forms. Even the gods came together in mind to honour the most admirable one, the mighty one just born.

title: Rigveda
text:
Great are the bright rays that follow brilliant Agni like lightnings; grown large as if in a cave, within his own seat, in the wide, unbounded expanse they milk for him the immortal draught.
The sacrificer praises you with oblations and eagerly praises your friendship and your favour. Grant protection to the singer together with the gods, and guard us with your domestic forces.
O Agni of excellent guidance, may those who dwell near you, holding all wealth, impelling with good seed and fame, may we prevail over the godless ones who make war.
O Agni, knowing all poetic wisdom, you have become the brilliant beacon of the gods. As the householder you have set men to face the task; you go as the charioteer after the gods, accomplishing your aim.
The immortal has sat down as king in the dwelling of mortals, accomplishing the affairs of the assembly. With face glistening with ghee, Agni has shone out broadly, knowing all things worthy of the sage.
Come to us, great one, swift-moving with your benevolent friendships, with your great aids. Grant us abundant and ample wealth, a share of fair speech and renown.
These, O Agni, are your ancient births; I have proclaimed new ones for the primordial. Great pressings have been set in motion for the bull; birth after birth the Knower-of-all-births has been established.
Birth after birth the Knower-of-all-births is established; he is kindled unceasing by the Viśvāmitras. May we be in the auspicious favour and fair benevolence of that god worthy of worship.
O mighty one, place this our sacrifice among the gods, O Agni of good resolve, bestowing gifts. Do you send forth our great nourishments, O Hotṛ; O Agni, win great wealth for us by sacrifice.
O Agni, accomplish for the worshipper Iḷā of many wonders, the ever-abiding winning of the cow. May there be for us a son and offspring rich in descendants; O Agni, may that favour of yours be upon us.

title: Rigveda
text:
For Vaiśvānara who augments the Truth, for Agni, we proclaim wisdom like clarified butter; the axe fashions both the Hotṛ of man and the praising singer, as a chariot is built with insight.
By his birth he illumined both world-halves; he became the praiseworthy son of his two mothers. Agni, the carrier of oblations, unaging, delightful in food, hard to deceive, guest of the peoples, rich in light.
By the will and skill of the prevailing one, in the ordering of things, the gods engendered Agni with their thoughts. I invoke the great, shining one with radiance and light, as one who is about to win a prize like a swift horse.
Wishing to win, we choose the chosen, the excellent prize of the joyful one, the boldly-won, song-worthy; the gift of the Bhṛgus, the zealous one, of poet's wisdom, Agni shining with his heavenly flame.
The peoples here have set Agni in the fore for their well-being, the winner of prizes and fame, they who have strewn the sacred grass; with ladles stretched out they place the brilliantly gleaming, all-divine, Rudra-like Agni, the fulfiller of sacrificial purpose and of works.
O Hotṛ of pure flame, the men who have strewn the sacred grass at sacrifices move around your dwelling. O Agni, those who seek your service attend to that which they may obtain; bestow wealth upon them.
When the working waters supported him at his birth, he filled both world-halves and the great sun. That seer, delightful in food, is led about for the sacrifice like a swift horse intent on winning the prize.
Honour the giver of oblations and performer of sacrifice; serve the Knower-of-all-births who dwells in the house. The charioteer of great Ṛta, all-pervading, Agni has become the Purohita of the gods.
The zealous, immortal ones have purified the three fuel-loads of the wide-ranging great Agni. Of these three, they gave one for the enjoyment of mortals; the other two have gone to their kindred abode.

title: Rigveda
text:
The human refreshments made the seer and lord of the clans into a hatchet-like sharpness for their aim. He goes flickering up hills and into valleys; he has maintained the embryo in these worlds.
Born knowing, he pleases those in whose bellies he dwells; the bull-like one roars magnificently like a lion. Vaiśvānara of wide radiance, immortal, distributes goods and precious things to the worshipper.
Vaiśvānara has ascended to the vault of heaven, to the back of the sky, rejoicing with holy praises. Wakeful, like the sun of old, generating wealth for the creature, he traverses the same course.
We implore the law-abiding, sacrificeable, inspired, worthy-of-praise one, whom Mātariśvan established with his celestial dwelling — the radiant Agni of golden hair, the well-illumined one, for ever-fresh well-being.
With reverence we implore the pure one, vigorous in his course, beholder of the sun, beacon stationed in the bright space of heaven, waking at dawn — Agni the summit of the sky, whom none may resist, the greatly mighty.
We always implore for wealth the joyful Hotṛ, the pure one of single purpose, the household god, worthy of praise, beholding all peoples — visible as a bright chariot for beauty, installed by Manu.
The inspired ones have placed their precious offerings for Vaiśvānara of wide radiance, for a path among the foundations. For Agni, the immortal, serves the gods, and has not violated the eternal laws.
The wondrous messenger travels between both worlds; the Hotṛ, the Purohita of man, is seated. Rich in wisdom, sent by the gods through heavenly days, Agni adorns the great abode.
The inspired ones magnify with their thoughts Agni, the beacon of sacrifices, the accomplisher of the assembly. In him upon whom the poets have joined their songs of praise, the sacrificer delights in favours.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni, the lord, father of sacrifices, the measurescape and the knowledge of those who praise — the seer of many forms has entered both worlds, a favourite of many; he is glorified with his abodes.
The gleaming Agni of gleaming chariot, whose vow is golden, Vaiśvānara who dwells in the waters and finds the light, penetrating swiftly and surrounded with mighty powers, fiery — the gods have placed the beautifully splendid one here.
Agni, along with the gods and all mortal beings, fashions by thought the sacrifice of many ornaments. The swift householder travels within, accomplishing his aims as charioteer, averting all attacks.
O Agni, thrive with excellent offspring through the life-spans; swell with strength; kindle our nourishments. Set the branches in motion, vigilant great one; you are the eager one and clear-minded of the gods and of the seers.
The men always extol with reverence and impulses to increase the lord of the clan, the great one, the guest, the guide of thoughts, the zealous one of the praisers, the insightful Knower-of-all-births of the rites.
The broadly-shining god, joyful, has become Agni of great chariot with his might, going beyond all habitations. May we adorn his vows as those who bring him many riches, with our good prayers in the house.
O Vaiśvānara, I delight in your abodes by which you became the discerning finder of light. Being born, you filled all worlds and both spheres; O Agni, you are all-encompassing of yourself.
The seer alone has emitted a great stream from the wondrous powers of Vaiśvānara through his own artistry. Agni was born magnifying both parents, heaven and earth, rich in seed.
Fuel-stave by fuel-stave, be kindly wakeful for us; flame by flame, bestow favour along with wealth. O god, bring the gods here for the sacrifice; as their friend you shall worship your friends with a good mind, O Agni.

title: Rigveda
text:
The one whom the gods — Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni — honour three times on each day: make this sweet sacrifice of ours, which Tanūnapāt and Ghee-womb have distributed, a success.
The all-chosen sacred thought goes forth to honour the Hotṛ as the first for worship. To approach the bull with homages and praise him — so summoned and most sacrificing, let him worship the gods.
Your path at the sacrifice has been made upright; the flames have departed upward, reaching the realms. Or the Hotṛ has been set down at the navel of heaven; we shall strew the sacred grass wide enough for the gods.
Choosing the seven priestly functions with the mind, driving all things forward going by the Truth, the many born of man-like appearance among the assemblies have spread out through this sacrifice.
As the two Dawns, glorying and nearby, smile with their diverse forms, may Mitra and Varuṇa, and Indra with his Maruts, or the great ones, be delighted with us.
I have set in place the two divine Hotṛs; the seven refreshments exult with their own power. Proclaiming the Truth, they speak only the Truth, meditating on the ordinance as its guardians.
Let Bhāratī with the Bhāratīs, Iḷā in accord with gods and men, Agni, and Sarasvatī together with the Sarasvatīs — let these three goddesses sit on this sacred grass.
O divine Tvaṣṭar, bestow upon us that nourishing, life-sustaining vigour, freely giving; from which a hero is born, active in work, of good skill, who works the pressing-stones and desires the gods.
O Lord of the forest, release the gods; Agni the sacrificer sets the oblation flowing. He alone as Hotṛ, truer than others, worships as one who knows the origins of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, kindled, in the same chariot as swift Indra and the gods. Let Aditi of good sons sit on the sacred grass; let the immortal gods be gladdened with Svāhā.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni, alert as the Dawns, the inspired seer, woke and became aware of the paths of the seers. Kindled with wide brilliance by the god-fearing, the conveyor has opened the doors of darkness.
Agni has indeed grown through the praises of the singers, with their songs and lauds worthy of homage. Delighting in many visions of the Truth, the messenger has shone forth together with the breaking of the Dawns.
Agni has been placed in human clans — the embryo of the waters, like Mitra, accomplishing by the Truth. The desirable and worshipful one has stood upon the ridge; the inspired one has become worthy of offerings of the prayers.
Agni becomes Mitra when kindled; the Hotṛ, the Knower-of-all-births, is Varuṇa. The vigorous householder as Adhvaryu is Mitra; he is Mitra of the rivers and of the mountains.
He guards the dear foremost step of the thievish bird; the great one guards the course of the sun. Agni, sublime, guards at the navel the seven-headed one; he guards the highest seat of the gods.
The skillful Ṛbhu has made the praiseworthy and lovely name; the god knows all the guidance-signs. He has lain on the skin of the grain, the ghee-rich step of the bird — that Agni guards without wavering.
Agni, desirous, has taken his place in the ghee-rich womb, widely extending and longed-for. Blazing, pure, sublime, and purifying, he renews the two mothers again and again.
Newly born, he has swelled with the plants when the wombs nourish with ghee. Like waters shining down a slope, Agni blazes in the lap of the parents, keeping them safe.
Praised, the great one has blazed upward, kindled with fuel, at the summit of heaven and the navel of the earth. Agni is Mitra, worthy of praise; as Mātariśvan the messenger he shall bring the gods for worship.
Sublime Agni, being the highest among the shining ones, has propped up the vault of heaven with his fuel. When Mātariśvan kindled from the Bhṛgus the hidden carrier of oblations.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, accomplish for the worshipper Iḷā of many wonders, the ever-abiding winning of the cow. May there be for us a son and offspring rich in descendants; O Agni, may that favour of yours be upon us.
The Kārus, being celebrated with thoughts, lead forward toward the divine as god-seekers. The prize-bearing, hymn-strong one goes eastward carrying oblation; the ghee-pouring one goes south to Agni.
Being born, you filled both worlds, and then left them to be enjoyed; now, O adorable one, let your seven-tongued conveyors be celebrated with your greatness of heaven and earth.
Heaven and earth, worthy of worship, set you down as Hotṛ for the house. When human tribes, desiring the gods, rich in offerings, invoke the bright flame.
The great one, fixed, has sat down firmly in his common seat, between great heaven and earth, being praised. In the lap sit the two co-wives, unaging and immortal, milk-cows of the far-ranging one who milk together.
Your vows, O Agni, are great and mighty; by your will you have stretched out both world-halves. You became the messenger at birth; you are the leader, O bull, of human beings.
Harness Ṛta's two long-maned, yoke-fitting, ghee-dripping red steeds to the chariot-pole. Then bring all the gods, O divine Jātavedas, make the sacrifice well-performed.
From heaven itself your flames shine out; you illumine many dawns as they blaze forth. When you, O Agni, glow with longing in the forests, the gods marvel at the joyful Hotṛ.
Whether gods exult in the wide atmosphere, or are in the bright space of heaven, or those of easy invocation, worthy of worship who are helpers — all like chariot horses have come to you, O Agni.
Come hither, O Agni, in the same chariot with these, or in separate chariots — for the horses are many. Bring the thirty-three gods with their wives in proper order; be gladdened.

title: Rigveda
text:
He is the Hotṛ for whom even the two broad worlds speak praise for the increase of every sacrifice. Both stand firm, fair and eastward like a rite — the two truth-containing ones in the truth of the one born of Truth.
O Agni, accomplish for the worshipper Iḷā of many wonders, the ever-abiding winning of the cow. May there be for us a son and offspring rich in descendants; O Agni, may that favour of yours be upon us.
The seven voices have climbed up and entered the two mothers of the white-backed one's stream. The two all-encircling parents travel together and pour forth long life for worship.
The divine milk-cows, the horses of the bull, sky-nourishing, bearing sweetness, have stood at their station. Around you, at rest in the seat of Ṛta, one cow walks the path.
They climbed up, becoming easily yoked; the knowing master, finder of riches. The blue-backed one kindled the stream of the desert plant; the many-formed one has made them blaze.
The vigorous ones carry the great work of Tvaṣṭar, imperishable and holding firm. Flashing through his limbs in the common seat, he has entered the two worlds as if they were one.
They know the delight of the ruddy bull; they rejoice at the command of the tawny one. Shining with the lights of heaven, brilliantly shining — their glorious, great song is Iḷā.
From the two great parents, following the call, they have led the strength. The bull has laid its sheath on the night; it has swelled following the praiser's own abode.
Seven inspired ones with five Adhvaryus guard the beloved hidden step of the bird. The ageless bulls exult going forward; the gods have followed the divine ordinances.
I have set in place the two divine Hotṛs foremost; the seven refreshments exult with their own power. Proclaiming the Truth, they speak only the Truth, meditating on the ordinance as its guardians.

title: Rigveda
text:
Many rays well-steered for the great swift steed, for the brilliant bull, are being bullish. O divine Hotṛ, more gladdening and discerning, bring the great gods and both worlds here.
Wealthy, of fair speech, with good beacons, the offering-rich ones have shone brilliantly at the Dawns. But even the sin that has been done, O Agni, do thou remit by the greatness of the earth.
O Agni, accomplish for the worshipper Iḷā of many wonders, the ever-abiding winning of the cow. May there be for us a son and offspring rich in descendants; O Agni, may that favour of yours be upon us.
God-fearing men anoint you at the sacrifice with divine sweetness, O Lord of the forest — whether you stand erect, placing wealth here, or whether your resting-place is in this your mother's lap.
Leaning in front of the kindled one, winning unaging and excellent manly strength with sacred speech — pushing poverty far from us, rise up for great good fortune.
Rise up, O Lord of the forest, upon the height of earth. Being well-trimmed, bestow vigour on the one who carries the sacrifice.
The youth, well-clad and adorned, has come; he becomes more excellent as he is born. The steadfast seers who are of good insight, who desire the gods with their mind, lead him up.
Born, he is being born in the goodly daylight of the days, growing in the contest in the assembly. The steadfast ones purify their works with wisdom; the inspired one, devoted to the gods, raises the voice.
The posts which the god-fearing men have fixed, O Lord of the forest, or which the axe has hewn — may the gods, self-luminous, established in them, bestow upon us a treasure rich in offspring.
Those cut down and set in the earth with ladles extended — may they, the accomplishers of the sacred ground, obtain for us among the gods the desired prize.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, of fair guidance, heaven and earth, the atmosphere — may the gods of one accord protect the sacrifice; may they raise high the beacon of the rite.
Like geese moving in a line, white-clad and self-luminous, they have come to us. Led up forward by the seers, the gods are going to the realm of the gods.
The self-luminous ones with their capitals, like horns among the horned, are seen on the earth. Listening to the call of the praisers, may they aid us in the winning of battles.
O Lord of the forest, grow with a hundred branches; may we grow with a thousand branches. May this whetted axe that has shaped you bring great good fortune.
We, mortals as friends, have chosen you, the divine, for our aid — Grandson of the Waters, the blessed, the clearly-blazing, the easily-victorious, the faultless.
Longing for the forests, you went and entered the mother waters; O Agni, your return cannot be forgotten — that, being far away, you were present here.
You have borne even what is sharp and bitter, and still you are well-disposed. Some go forward and forward; others sit around — those on whose friendship you depend.
He who had gone past many failures, past those who persistently hated him — the wise and guileless ones found him, established in the waters like a lion.
Mātariśvan led this Agni, who was thus hidden as though fleeing on his own, from afar — churned for the gods from the distance.
Mortals have seized you, O carrier of oblations, for the gods — O youngest, by your will you oversee all human sacrifices.
That your wondrous power is pleasing even to the simple one — when, O Agni, the animals sit around you, kindled on the dark night.
Pour the oblation to the self-performing sacrificer, the fierce one of pure flame. Attend with offerings to the swift messenger, the quick, ancient, praiseworthy, helpful deity.

title: Rigveda
text:
Three hundred, three thousand, and thirty-nine gods have served Agni. They sprinkled him with ghees and strewed the sacred grass for him; then at last they seated him as Hotṛ.
You, O Agni, the thoughtful mortals kindle at the sacrifice — the universal king of peoples, the divine one.
You, O Agni, they invoke at sacrifices as Hotṛ and seasonal priest. O guardian of the Truth, blaze in your own house.
He who pays homage to you, O Knower-of-all-births, with fuel — that man, O Agni, obtains excellent manly strength; he flourishes.
That Agni, the beacon of the rites, shall come with the gods, anointed with seven Hotṛs, to him who holds the oblation.
Carry forth to the Hotṛ's office the mighty ancient speech for Agni, who bears the lights of the seers and the seer-gift.
May our songs increase Agni, from whom the lauded one is born — the visible one, for great vigour and wealth.
O Agni, most skilled at the rite, worship the gods for the god-fearing man. The joyful Hotṛ, you shine beyond the failures.
O purifier, blaze out for us luminously; for us be there excellent heroic strength. Be the nearest to the praisers for their well-being.
The inspired, greatly-praising ones, vigilant, kindle you — the immortal carrier of oblations who grows with might.
Agni is the Hotṛ and Purohita of the rite, the all-seeing one. He knows the sacrifice in proper order.
He is the immortal carrier of oblations, the eager messenger delightful in food — Agni is set in motion by wisdom.
Agni is aware through wisdom; he is the first and foremost beacon of the sacrifice. For his boat crosses to the goal.
The gods have made Agni, the son of strength, the Knower-of-all-births praised of old, their conveyor.
Agni is the inviolable forerunner of human clans — the chariot always swift and ever new.
Agni, unimpeded, who has overcome all challengers, the will of the gods — Agni of the most widespread fame.

title: Rigveda
text:
The mortal who has sacrificed wins the gifts and the chariot-load — the abode of the one of pure flame.
We, inspired ones, may reach with our prayers all the well-placed gifts of Agni, the Knower-of-all-births.
O Agni, we shall win all desirable things in the contest; the gods have roused themselves in you.
O Indra and Agni, come with songs to the pressed soma, to the excellent one of the clouds. You who are sent by prayer — drink of this.
O Indra and Agni, the conscious sacrifice goes forward together with the singer. Drink of this pressed soma.
With the swiftness of the sacrifice I choose Indra and Agni as shelter of the seer. Let the two of them here be satisfied with the soma.
I invoke the two most effective, the slayers of Vṛtra, the two who always conquer and are never defeated — Indra and Agni, the most winning of prizes.
The singers who know the hymns, who praise with lauds, praise the two of you. I choose refreshment from Indra and Agni.
Indra and Agni shook down ninety strongholds ruled by Dāsas — together with a single deed.
The prayers go forward and around the works of Indra and Agni, following the paths of the Truth.
O Indra and Agni, your mighty common seats and gifts — what prize of the water-filling is placed within you both.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the shining spaces of heaven in the prizes. That heroic power of yours is clearly visible.
Sing forth the highest praise to the divine Agni; may the most skilled sacrificer come to us with the gods and sit on the sacred grass.
The law-abiding one whose both worlds and aids accompany his skill — those who have offerings invoke him; those seeking to win invoke him for protection.
He is the guide of these inspired ones and of their sacrifices — for it is truly so. Honour that Agni who is the giver and winner of bounty.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let Agni grant us the most beneficent shelters for our enjoyment — from which refreshing wealth comes to us from heaven, from the sky, from the waters.
The reciters kindle with his auspicious thoughts the unrivalled blazing Agni, the Hotṛ and lord of the clans.
Moreover, O priest, be beneficent to us in our lauds, O most invoked of gods. O Agni, who grows with the Maruts, most winning of thousands, blaze out auspiciously for us.
Now give us wealth thousandfold, rich in offspring and nourishment. O Agni, luminous excellent heroic strength, the highest and never wasting away.
The joyful Hotṛ has taken his place in the assemblies — the true sacrificer, the most seer-like, the wise one. Agni, son of strength, of lightning chariot, with flame as hair, has spread his might upon the earth.
I offer you this homage-speech; be pleased with it. O truthful, mighty one, it becomes visible to you. Knowing all, bring the knowing ones; sit in the midst of the sacred grass for our aid, O worthy of worship.
May the prize-winning Dawns run toward you, O Agni, along the paths of the wind. When they anoint you, the ancient one, with oblations, they two stand in the dwelling as at the chariot-pole.
Mitra and mighty Varuṇa and all the Maruts seek your favour, O Agni. When, O son of strength, you stand with your flame, extending your reach over settlements and men like the sun.
Today we have given you what you desire, approaching you with upraised hands and reverence. With your most sacrificing mind worship the gods; O inspired Agni, do so with unfaltering thought.
From you, O son of strength, the many divine aids go forth and the prizes. O Agni, give us a thousandfold treasure with truthful, guileless speech.
O divine one of skill and poetic will, what these mortals have done at the sacrifice is for you. Be the protector of all who have a good chariot; O immortal Agni, let all this be sweet to you.

title: Rigveda
text:
Blazing out with broad radiance, drive away enemies, Rākṣasas, and diseases. May I be in the great shelter of the well-sheltering one, under the guidance of Agni of easy invocation.
Be our protector at the breaking of this dawn, at the rising of the sun. Be pleased with my praise as with an ever-present offspring — O Agni well-born, be pleased with my body.
You, the man-seeing bull, illuminate many dark nights, O ruddy Agni. O wealth, you lead us and carry us beyond affliction; O youngest one, make us desire wealth.
Blaze out, O invincible bull Agni, having conquered all the foremost good fortunes. O Jātavedas, guide and first guardian of the sacrifice, of great and excellent leadership.
O singer, may you have many unbroken shelters. Blazing toward the gods, O wise one, carry our vigour forward like a prize-winning chariot; O Agni, set us in both worlds at ease.
O bull, swell and enliven the prizes; O Agni, may you keep both our worlds yielding richly. O divine one, shining brilliantly with the gods — let not the evil thought of a mortal encompass us.
O Agni, accomplish for the worshipper Iḷā of many wonders, the ever-abiding winning of the cow. May there be for us a son and offspring rich in descendants; O Agni, may that favour of yours be upon us.
This Agni rules over excellent heroic strength and great good fortune. He rules over wealth with good offspring; he rules over the slaying of the obstruction-demon, rich in cows.
O Maruts, accompany this growing one, in whom the riches-swelling powers reside, those who are hard to overcome in battles, who have always seized the enemy.
O bountiful Agni, sharpen us for wealth and excellent heroic strength — O highly luminous one, of the highest, offspring-rich, disease-free, mighty wealth.
He who has accomplished all, who has overcome all worlds, who has accomplished service among the gods — among the gods strive for, strive for excellent heroic strength, strive for the praise of men.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, do not surrender us to indigence, to lack of heroes, O son of strength; not to the grief-giver, not to reproach — avert the hatreds from us.
O blessed and highly luminous Agni, grant us strength of the prize at the great sacrifice, offspring-rich. Unite us with more abundant, bliss-bringing, and glorious wealth.
Being kindled first according to holy law, he is anointed with streams of oil — the all-desirable one; flame-haired, robed in ghee, the purifier, Agni the good sacrificer, is ready to worship the gods.
As you, O Agni, Jātavedas, wise and knowing, performed the priestly office on earth and in heaven — so with this oblation worship the gods today; extend this sacrifice in the manner of Manu.
Three are your lifetimes, O Jātavedas; three are your birth-forms at the dawns, O Agni. With those, wise one, worship and secure the favor of the gods; then be a source of welfare and healing for the worshipper.
Praising Agni of bright luster and fair aspect, we bow before you, O Jātavedas, worthy of hymns. The gods made you their messenger, the eager one, the carrier of oblations, the navel-center of immortality.
He who was your predecessor as Hotṛ priest, O Agni, more skilled at sacrifice, seated doubly, beneficent by his own nature — following his ordinance, O wise one, perform the sacrifice; then set our ceremony in the sight of the gods.
Be well-disposed toward us, O Agni, as you draw near — good as a friend to a friend, as a father. For the dwelling-places of men abound with malice; burn down those enmities that turn to face us.
Scorch our enemies with your heat, O Agni; scorch the malicious curse of the hostile one; O Vasu, wise and knowing, scorch the foolish ones — may your ageless, untiring flames spread forth against them.
O Agni, desiring it with fuel and with ghee, I offer the oblation for swiftness and for strength. As far as my power reaches, honoring with prayer, I dedicate this divine vision to win the hundredfold reward.

title: Rigveda
text:
Rise up with your flame, O son of strength, praised one; bestow great vitality upon those who toil. O Agni, may there be rich welfare among the Viśvāmitras; having polished your body many times over, we invoke your benevolence.
Bestow a jewel, O excellent winner of wealth — for you become that, O Agni, when you are kindled. In the house of the fortunate praiser you assume your splendid, clinging, crackling forms of beauty.
I choose Agni as Hotṛ at the sacrifice — keen, wise, all-knowing, faultless. May he, most skilled at worship, sacrifice for us and win the wealth and favor of the divine host, winning bounteous gifts.
I send forth to you, O Agni, a prayer rich in oblations, of splendid glory, giving gifts, gleaming with ghee. Moving rightward, he who embraces the divine host joins the sacrifice with its offerings of good things.
Protected by you, O Agni, may we with a keener mind both learn and teach from him who teaches good lordship. In the abundance of the most heroic riches, may we be your praisers and masters of wealth.
For many forces have been placed in you, O Agni; the peoples, sacrificing to the god, call on you. O youngest one, bring hither the divine troop — the heavenly host — which you worship today.
When the gods anointed you as Hotṛ at the sacrifice, seating you for the act of worship — be you then, O Agni, our ever-present guardian here; bestow renown upon our persons.
The carrier of offerings invokes with hymns at the dawning, Agni, Uṣas, the two Aśvins, and Dadhikrā. May the gods of beautiful light hear us, delighting together, desiring the sacrifice.
O Agni, you have three powerful steeds, three dwelling-places; three are your tongues, ancient, born of truth. Three also are your bodies beloved of the gods — with these, guard our songs, never faltering.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, Jātavedas, O god of your own nature, many are your names in the realm of immortality. And the ancient magical powers of all magicians that pervade all, O ridgepole-binder, have been deposited in you.
Agni is the leader of settlements as Bhaga is, the divine god who guards the seasons, who holds to truth. He, the Vṛtra-slayer, ancient, all-knowing, shall carry the singer across all difficulties.
Dadhikrā, Agni, and the divine Uṣas, Bṛhaspati and the god Savitṛ, the two Aśvins, Mitra-Varuṇa, Bhaga, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas — these I invoke here.
Place this our sacrifice among the immortals; O Jātavedas, accept these oblations. O Agni, eat first, O Hotṛ, seating yourself, the drops of marrow and of ghee.
O Pāvaka, drops full of ghee, drops of fat, trickle down for you. Following your own law, for the pleasure of the gods, bestow upon us the choicest boon.
For you, O Agni, O inspired one, the ghee-dripping drops are truly meant. You are kindled as the foremost seer; be the promoter of the sacrifice.
For you, O inexhaustible, O powerful one, the drops of fat and ghee drip down, O Agni. You whom the seers have praised, come with your great radiance; O wise one, accept these oblations.
The strongest fat, lifted out from the middle, we offer forward to you. O Vasu, the drops trickle upon your skin; receive them in a godly manner, distributing them as a god.
This is that Agni in whom Indra, bellowing, placed the pressed Soma in his belly. Winning a thousandfold prize like a racing steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas, while ever victorious.
O Agni, O adorable one, whatever brilliance you have in heaven, on earth, in the plants and in the waters, by which you have stretched out broadly through the mid-air — that fierce, far-seeing, flood-like radiance is yours.
O Agni, you strive toward the flood of heaven; you call upon the gods who are the bright ones. The waters that stand beyond the luminous realm of the sun, and those that stand below — those you address.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Agnis who dwell in strongholds, united in delight, flowing together in streams — may these guileless ones, free from malady, accept the sacrifice, the great refreshments.
O Agni, grant Iḷā of many feats and the ever-lasting winning of the cow to him who calls upon you. May there be for us a son, a male offspring; O Agni, may that good thought of yours be with us.
Churned out, well-set in the ritual place, young, a seer, the guide of the ceremony — ageless Agni glowing among the kindling sticks; here Jātavedas has been established, immortal.
The two Bharatas, Devaśravā and Devavāta, churned forth Agni, rich, of excellent skill. O Agni, look out with your great light upon the riches; be our leader day after day.
Ten fingers generated him, the primordial one, well-born, dear to his mothers. Praise Agni, the Devavāta, O Devaśravas — he who shall be the lord of peoples.
I have set you down in the choicest place on earth, on the seat of Iḷā, in the bright time of days. On the Dṛṣadvatī, the Āpayā, and the Sarasvatī, O Agni, shine forth in your riches.
O Agni, grant Iḷā of many feats and the ever-lasting winning of cattle to him who calls upon you. May there be for us a son, a male offspring; O Agni, may that good thought of yours be with us.
O Agni, overcome the hostile armies that press in upon us; drive them away. Crossing over those hard to cross, removing our enemies, place vigor in the bearer of the sacrifice.
O Agni, you are kindled together with Iḷā, you who invite the gods to the feast, immortal one. Accept indeed our ceremony.
O Agni, ever wakeful with your glory, O son of strength, invoked with oblations — this is my seat of sacred grass.
O Agni, with all the Agnis and the gods magnify our songs, those which are the devoted ones at the sacrifices.
O Agni, give to the devout worshipper wealth full of heroes and abounding in abundance; whet us to be rich in sons.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, you are the son of heaven, the far-seeing; and also, continuously, of earth, the all-knowing. O wise one, worship the gods here separately.
Agni, the knowing one, wins heroic powers; knowing, he wins strength, adorning himself for immortality. He, the abundant one, shall bring the gods here to us.
Agni shines in heaven and earth, for all peoples, divine, immortal, faultless. Abiding in prizes, of manifold splendor, with adorations.
O Agni and Indra, come here to the sacrifice in the house of the worshipper who has pressed the Soma, to the one who gives. O gods, come together without hindrance to drink the Soma.
O Agni, you are kindled together with the waters in the house, eternal, O son of strength, O Jātavedas. Magnifying the ritual stations with your protection.
Meditating upon Vaiśvānara Agni, the ever-present, the finder of heaven — we who hold oblations, desiring wealth, we the Kuśikas invoke with our hymns the good-giving, joyful god, the charioteer.
For protection we invoke that bright Agni, the Vaiśvānara, Mātariśvan, worthy of hymns — Bṛhaspati, the inspired listener, for the divine troop of man; the guest who is quickly pleased.
Neighing like a horse, Vaiśvānara is kindled by the Kuśikas age after age. May that Agni, ever wakeful among the immortals, bestow on us heroic might, good horses, and a jewel.
Let the vigorous Agnis go forward with their might; the speckled mares have been yoked to the splendid array. The great-watered, all-knowing Maruts, irresistible, shake the mountains as they drive forward.
We seek the protection of the Maruts who bear Agni's glory, who rule over all peoples, fierce and terrible. They who roar, the sons of Rudra, robed in rain, like lions with neighing resolve, good givers.
Band after band, troop after troop, with our praises we seek Agni's fierceness and the Maruts' might. They who have speckled horses, of undiminished generosity, the wise ones who come to the sacrifice at the assemblies.

title: Rigveda
text:
By birth I am Agni, Jātavedas; ghee is my eye, immortality is in my mouth. The song of praise, the three-composed measurer of the atmosphere — the undying warmth — oblation is my name.
With three purifying filters he has purified the hymn, knowing the light, following his thought in his heart. He has made the highest jewel by his own power; then heaven and earth looked around upon it.
The spring of a hundred streams, inexhaustible, the wise father of utterances, the joyfully intoxicated virile one in the lap of his two parents — O heaven and earth, fill that truth-speaking one.
The vigorous ones, aiming at heaven, with oblations, gleaming with ghee — the well-wisher goes forth to the gods.
I praise Agni the all-seeing with song, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the one who listens obediently, the one rich in devotion.
O Agni, may we be capable of your control, O divine, vigorous one; may we cross beyond our hatreds.
Agni, the purifier, being kindled at the ceremony, worthy of praise — flame-haired, we seek him.
Of broad brilliance, immortal, robed in ghee, well-offered with oblations — Agni is the carrier of the oblations of the sacrifice.
Those pressed from all sides, who stretch out the ladle, thus in their thought, those who possess the sacrifice — they have invoked Agni for protection.
The divine Hotṛ, immortal, goes ahead with his wisdom, impelling the assemblies.
The vigorous one is set among the prizes, led forward at the ceremonies; the inspired one is the accomplisher of the sacrifice.
The excellent one has acted through inspiration; he has set the embryo of all beings. Continuously the father of Dakṣa.
I set you down, the excellent one, as Iḷā of Dakṣa, made mighty, O Agni, of bright luster, eager.
The inspired ones kindle together with prizes Agni, the controller, the mover in the waters, winning at the harnessing of truth.

title: Rigveda
text:
I praise at the ceremony Agni, the grandson of strength, shining, near the day, of sage resolve.
Worthy of praise, worthy of reverence, visible through the darknesses — the bull Agni is kindled together.
The bull Agni is kindled, the divine carrier of gods like a horse; those who hold oblations praise him.
O bull, as bulls we kindle you, the virile one, O virile one; O Agni, shine out your great brightness.
O Agni, O Jātavedas, accept our oblation, the sacrificial cake, at the morning pressing; O you rich in devotion.
O Agni, the sacrificial cake cooked and prepared is indeed for you alone. Accept it, O youngest one.
O Agni, eat the sacrificial cake offered, that which passes beyond the day. You are the son of strength, established at the ceremony.
O Jātavedas, O wise one, at the midday pressing, accept here the sacrificial cake. O Agni, the wise ones at the assemblies do not diminish your due portion as the swift one.
O Agni, you desire the sacrificial cake offered at the third pressing, O son of strength. Then, with wonder, establish among the gods a ceremony that is rich in jewels, wakeful among the immortals.
O Agni, O Jātavedas, growing with the oblation — accept the sacrificial cake that passes beyond the day.
Here is the upper fire-drill, the procreative one is fashioned. Bring that lady of the folk — we shall churn Agni as in ancient times.
Jātavedas is hidden in the two fire-sticks, like an embryo well-placed in pregnant women. Agni is to be praised day after day by the watchful, oblation-bearing men.
Bring him down into the outstretched one — the wise knowing one instantly excited, has generated the virile one. The bright-streaked one whose brilliance is reddish — the son of Iḷā was born at the meeting-place.
We place you, O Jātavedas, O Agni, in the seat of Iḷā, at the navel of the earth, for the carrying of oblations.

title: Rigveda
text:
O men, churn him — the seer, the straightforward, the far-seeing, the immortal, the fair-faced; O men, generate Agni the auspicious, first banner of the sacrifice, in the east.
When they churn with their arms, he shines forth, red as a swift horse in the forests. Brilliant as the track of the two Aśvins, unrestricted in his motion, he twists around the stones, burning the grass.
Born, Agni shines, all-perceiving, vigorous, inspired, praised by the poet, good-giving. Whom the gods, praising him, the all-knowing carrier of oblations, have established at the ceremonies.
Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own realm, knowing; establish the sacrifice in the womb of the well-performed rite. You, the friend of the gods, worship the gods with oblations, O Agni; place great vitality in the worshipper.
O companions, make the smoke virile; go without stumbling toward the prize. This Agni conquers in battle, of good heroes, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus.
This is your womb fitting to the season, from which, born, you shone. Knowing it, O Agni, sit down here; then magnify our songs.
He is called Tanūnapāt the embryo, the supernatural — Narāśaṁsa he becomes when he is generated. When Mātariśvan measured him in the mother, the current of wind arose in his going.
Well churned out, churned; well established, set down — the seer. O Agni, perform the good ceremony; worship the gods for the one who desires the gods.
Mortals have generated the immortal, the unhesitating, swift one of firm jaws. The ten sisters, the maidens who move together, embrace the male that is born.
The seven-Hotṛ one shone forth from of old when he shone at the udder in the mother's lap. The joyful, well-pleased one does not close his eyes day after day — he who was born from the belly of the Asura.
Like the outgoings of the Maruts with their weapons for enemies, the firstborn of the prayer know everything. The Kuśikas have sent forth glorious prayer; each in his own house has kindled Agni.

title: Rigveda
text:
Today, as this sacrifice proceeds, we have chosen you here, O wise Hotṛ, knowing. Going firmly, firmly and most swiftly, knowing, all-wise, come to the Soma.
The Soma-pressing friends desire you; they press the Soma, they set out the offerings. They endure the curse of men — O Indra, whoever has true discernment comes from you alone.
Not even the farthest realms are far for you; come here, O lord of bay horses, with your bay steeds. The pressings are made for the steady bull; the pressing stones are set in motion as Agni blazes.
Indra of the beautiful jaw, the bountiful, the conqueror, of great vows, of manifold activity, impetuous — when you, the fierce one, are hard-pressed among mortals, where then are those heroic powers of yours, O bull?
For you alone, shaking even the unshakeable things, go about slaying the Vṛtras. Heaven, earth, and mountains stand fixed as if nailed down, obedient to your decree.
And in both the fearful realms, O much-invoked, with your glories, you alone, being the Vṛtra-slayer, have spoken firmly. Even these two boundless worlds, O Indra — that which is visible, O bountiful, is the gleam of you.
Go forth, O Indra, downward with your bay horses; let your thunderbolt go forward grinding the enemies. Strike those facing us, those following behind, those fleeing — make everything truly victorious.
The mortal for whom you, the milk-bearing one, set down even what was unshared — he enjoys what is to be enjoyed in the house. Benevolent is your good thought, O Indra, gleaming with ghee, your thousandfold gift, O much-invoked.
O much-invoked one, you crushed together Sahadānu, the dweller who has no hands, O Indra — Kuṇāru. O Indra, you slew with might Vṛtra the grower, the mocker without feet.
O Indra, you have lain down in the abode of the swift, great, boundless earth. The bull has propped up heaven and the atmosphere; may the waters, impelled by you, flow here.

title: Rigveda
text:
Vala, not a feeder, the cow-pen — before the striker, fearing, he opened it. He made the paths easy, driving out the cows; the voices blowing supported the much-invoked Indra.
The one with two — the pair rich in wealth joining together, O Indra, fills earth and sky. And from the mid-air, the joining is toward us, O hero — the chariot-lord's refreshments, the yoked prizes.
The quarters pointed out — as the sun does not diminish them — day after day, impelled by the bay-horsed one; when he reached the paths, then immediately he unharnesses his horses — that is its loosening.
Desiring to see, at the going of dawn, at the night, the great manifold army of Vivasvat — all know, when he came in his greatness, the many well-performed deeds of Indra.
A great light is placed in her flanks; the cow wanders carrying both raw and cooked. All savory food gathered in the dawn-cow, which Indra deposited in her for enjoyment.
O Indra, be firm — the treasury-keepers of the roads have arisen; instruct the singer and his companions for the sacrifice. The evil-minded ones of bad deeds, the mortals who carry swords, the enemies — may they be struck down.
The roar is heard with those who attack from below, the enemies. Cast down upon these your most burning thunderbolt. Break them off below and crush them; slay the Rakṣas, O bountiful, subdue them.
Root out the Rakṣas together with its roots, O Indra; cut it in the middle, cut the top piece off. You have made the stingy one, the owl-resembler, a target; fling the burning weapon against the prayer-hater.
For well-being, O leader with the vigorous ones, when you have sat down with the many great refreshments — may we be winners of great riches; may there be with us wealth with progeny, O Indra.
Bring us resplendent good fortune, O Indra; we reflect upon your gift abundantly. Our desire has spread out as the large cattle enclosure; fill it up, O lord of goods, among all goods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Gladden this desire with cows and horses, with bright generosity, and spread it wide. Striving toward heaven, the inspired ones have made their thoughts a chariot for Indra — thus the Kuśikas have cried out.
Break open for us the cow-pens, O lord of cattle; let the prizes and ancient winnings come together to us. You are the heavenly shaker, O bull of true vigor; O bountiful one, be a giver of cows to us.
For good fortune let us call the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the prize; the fierce one who hears, for protection in the fights, who slays the Vṛtras, the conqueror of riches.
The carrier of offerings will instruct the daughter's son, going knowing, honoring the shining of truth. Where the father, mingling the emission of the daughter, combined them with a willing mind.
He did not leave the kinswomen an empty inheritance; he made his embryo the receptacle of the progenitor. When the mothers generated the carrier of offerings, one made it, another made the well-made thing to prosper.
Agni was born trembling with his tongue at the great sacrifice of the red one's sons. The great embryo born greatly among them — great is the growth of the bay-horsed one through sacrifices.
The victorious ones came together against the opponent; they brought forth great light from the darkness. The dawns, knowing him, rose toward him; Indra alone became the lord of the cows.
The wise ones, the seven inspired ones, pressed through them even though hard, driving them eastward with their minds. They found all the paths of truth; knowing them indeed, he entered them with homage.
When Saramā found the breach in the rock — who made that ancient great flood to flow properly together? She who went first toward the lowing, knowing, leading the front of the syllables — to the cows.

title: Rigveda
text:
The most inspired one came, desiring friendship; the rock yielded its embryo to the well-performed rite. The young man winning together with the young ones, exulting — then he became Aṅgiras, praising immediately.
Hundred by hundred he is the foreguard-counterpart, he knows all births, he smites Śuṣṇa. Singing, the path of heaven desiring cows for us, the friend freed the friends from disgrace.
With a mind bent on cows they settled with their songs, making a path toward immortality. This indeed is now their rich abiding-place, by which, with truth, they aimed at the months.
Looking upon each other, they rejoiced, milking their own milk of the primordial seed. Their voice blazed through heaven and earth; at his birth they placed the final goal: heroes among the cows.
He, the Vṛtra-slayer, with those born, truly with oblations, Indra released the dawn-cows with songs. Bringing abundant ghee-rich food to him, the noble cow milked honey and sweet food.
They made a dwelling for the father too, with great flashing; the well-performed ones shone out distinctly. Propping up with a prop the two parents seated, spreading the swift, upward one.
If the great Dhiṣaṇā has stirred the instantly-growing, pervading one of the two worlds — the songs in whom are faultless, fitting together, all the powers unconquered for Indra.
I greatly desire your friendship, your powers; to the Vṛtra-slayer many teams of horses come. Great is the praise-song we have come to of the hero; O bountiful one, be well our guardian.
Knowing the great field of manifold splendor, then he set the movement going for his companions. Indra shining, together with the men, generated simultaneously the sun, the dawn, the path, and fire.
This pervading house-companion also set forth the waters all-together, of universal splendor. Purifying with the seers' filters of honey, the heavenly ones impel the arching ones by day and by night.

title: Rigveda
text:
Both treasure-keepers follow along the dark one; both are the generosity of the adorable sun. When your friends, O Indra, the straight-flying desirable ones, are to encircle your greatness.
Be lord of true words, O Vṛtra-slayer, all-living, the bull, bestower of vigor in our songs. Come to us with the bonds of friendship, the auspicious ones; great with great protections, as the swift one.
Honoring him with homage like an Aṅgiras, I make him new for the ancient gain. Go away from us the many godless treacheries; and heaven, O bountiful, establish for our winning.
Purifying mists have spread out; bring us across them for well-being. O Indra, you the charioteer, protect us from injury; speedily, ever-speedily make us victorious in cattle.
The Vṛtra-slayer, the lord of cattle, has pointed out the cows; he went among the dark ones with his reddish rays. Directing true words with truth, he opened wide all the doors from his home.
For good fortune let us call the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the prize; the fierce one who hears, for protection in the fights, who slays the Vṛtras, the conqueror of riches.
O Indra, O Soma-lord, drink this Soma — the midday pressing, which is dear to you. Puffing out your jaws, O bountiful, O Ṛjīṣin, here unharness your bay horses and rejoice.
O Indra, drink this soma mixed with milk, this bright churned drink — we have yielded it to you for your intoxication. With the prayer-created Marut troop, delighting together with the Rudras, drink your fill three times, O bull.
