The Maruts who increased your vigor and your power, O Indra, sang your might. O wielder of the thunderbolt, at the midday pressing, O fair-jawed one, drink together with the Rudras in their troop.
Indeed, those were the sweet, richly inspired troop of Indra, the Maruts who were there. By whom, as Vṛtra was set in motion, we found the vital spot of him who thought he had no vital spot.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra, accepting the pressing as Manu did, drink the Soma for perennial heroic power. O bay-horsed one, turn yourself toward us with sacrifices; you rush the waters like the swift streams.
You, O Indra, when you had slain Vṛtra, released the waters like swift racers to run. With a roaming weapon, the divine ones encompassed the un-divine one who was lying, wrapped up.
We worship with homage Indra the grown, the great, the lofty, the ageless, the ever-young. Of this adorable one whose dear ones have been intoxicated, heaven and earth have not encompassed his greatness.
The many well-performed deeds of Indra — all the gods do not diminish his ordinances. He who has sustained both earth and this heaven, the one of great wonders who begot the sun and the dawn.
O guileless one, true is that greatness of yours — that immediately upon being born you drank the Soma. Heaven did not encompass, O Indra, the strength of your might, nor the days, nor the months, nor the years.
Immediately upon being born, O Indra, you drank the Soma in the highest heaven for your intoxication. When you entered heaven and earth, then you became the primordial nourisher of the singers.
You slew the serpent lying around the flood, the ever-strengthening, most powerful, O much-born. Even heaven then did not match your greatness when you stood upon the earth with your other hip.
For the sacrifice, O Indra, has been your increaser, and dear to you is the sacrifice where Soma is pressed. Being a sacrificial god, he protects sacrifice with sacrifice; the sacrifice supported your thunderbolt for the smiting of the serpent.
With the sacrifice I have drawn Indra near for protection; I would turn him toward us for newer grace. He who has grown with the ancient hymns, who has grown with the middle ones and also with the new ones.

title: Rigveda
text:
What Dhiṣaṇā has generated has entered in — I would praise Indra before the end of the day. Where he would free us from distress — as both sides call upon the one going like a ship.
His vessel is full; like a vessel for Svāhā it has poured into a container for drinking. And the dear ones have come around together for intoxication — the Soma streams clockwise toward Indra.
No deep river, O much-invoked, no surrounding rocks have encompassed you. Thus, when impelled by friends, O Indra, you broke open even the firm, cattle-holding enclosure.
For good fortune let us call the bountiful Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the prize; the fierce one who hears, for protection in the fights, who slays the Vṛtras, the conqueror of riches.
Rushing forth eager from the lap of the mountains, like two mares let loose racing side by side, like two bright mother-cows licking their calves, Vipāś and Śutudrī speed on with their waters.
Urged by Indra, seeking your forward flow, you move toward the ocean like chariot-wheels on a road. Swelling with waves as you join together, one of you shining ones overtakes the other.
I came to the most motherly Sindhu, to broad and blessed Vipāś. Like two mothers licking a calf, they flow together along the same common channel.
Swelling with these waters, flowing along the god-made channel — the current once released in a torrent cannot be turned back. What does the inspired poet repeatedly call out to the rivers?
Yield to my Soma-blessed speech, O holy rivers, just for a moment! Desiring help, seeking the Sindhu, with great prayer the son of Kuśika called out.
Indra of the thunderbolt arm split open a way for us; he smote Vṛtra, the barrier of the rivers. Savitṛ the god with fair hands led them; in his impulsion we, the broad ones, flow on.
Ever worth proclaiming is that heroic deed of Indra — that he cleft the serpent asunder. He shattered with the bolt the barriers encircling them, and the waters rushed forth seeking their path.

title: Rigveda
text:
O singer, do not forget this word, when your cries rise up through future ages. Favor us in your hymns, O singer; do not cast us down among men. Homage to you!
Listen, O sister rivers, to the singer who has traveled to you from afar with cart and chariot. Bow down, become easy to cross — with your axles low, O rivers, fordable by their currents.
We hear your words, O singer — you who have come from afar with cart and chariot. I shall bow low to you like a woman swelling with milk, like a maiden ever yielding to the young man.
When the Bharatas, the cattle-seeking host, impelled and goaded by Indra, shall cross you, then let the current flow on, released in a rush — I choose your benevolence, O holy ones.
The Bharatas seeking cattle have crossed; the inspired one has won the benevolence of the rivers. Swell onward, nourishing and generous; fill your channels and flow swiftly!
Let the Śamyā's wave strike up for you, O waters — release the bonds! May the two sin-cleansing, guiltless cows not weary and come to grief!
Indra, the fort-cleaver, overpowered the Dāsa with his rays, winning wealth, distributing it among enemies. Impelled by prayer, waxing mighty in his body, the bountiful one filled both heaven and earth.
I send forth speech proclaiming the onset of you, the vigorous, the spirited, adorning it for immortal glory. O Indra, you are the foremost of human settlements, and you marched ahead even of the divine hosts.
Indra uncovered Vṛtra, irresistible in onslaught; he broke down the magic forms of the wily ones. He smote the broad-shouldered Vyaṁsa eagerly in the forests and made the cows of those who dwell afar manifest.
Indra, winning the sun, engendering the days, conquering battles with inspired men, his onslaught victorious — lighting up for Manu the banner of the dawns, he found light for the great contest.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra, pressing powerfully, entered with vigor, bearing many manly things as a man. He illumined these thoughts for the singer and surpassed with this brilliant color those others.
His great and many well-wrought deeds of Indra's are worthy of wonder. He crushed the wicked with the enclosure; with superior might and power he overwhelmed the Dasyus with his magic arts.
In battle, Indra, the lord of the good, the guardian of men, made wide room by his greatness for the gods. The inspired sages and seers proclaim those deeds of his in the seat of Vivasvat with their hymns.
The one who won all-subjugating, excellent, strength-giving gifts — who won the sun and the divine waters — who won this earth and heaven: the wise ones exult after Indra.
He won the swift horses, Indra won the sun, he won the cow that gives rich nourishment, he won golden treasure and enjoyment — having slain the Dasyus, he protected the Āryan color.
Indra won the herbs, he won the days and the lords of the forest, he won the atmosphere. He cleft open the Vala cave, drove away the Vivācs, and became the tamer of those who opposed him.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
Stand, O bay steeds, being yoked to the chariot! Come to us like Vāyu with his teams. Drink of the Soma poured forth for us — O Indra, svāhā! We have offered it to you for your exhilaration.
I yoke the swift bay horses, the two bays of the chariot-pole, for the much-invoked one. May they bring Indra hither to this sacrifice, swiftly, as one gathers gathered riches from all sides.
Lead the two powerful males near, O lord of self-power, and look down, O bull! Let the horses eat here, the red ones set free — eat the like-and-equal grain day by day.

title: Rigveda
text:
With sacred prayer I yoke your two swift bay companions who exult together, yoked by holy prayer. Mounting the firm and comfortable chariot, knowing all, as one who understands, come to the Soma.
May your two bull bays with resplendent backs not be detained by other sacrificers. Come past them all to us who always call — we shall make ourselves fit for you with pressed Soma draughts.
This Soma is yours — come hither! Drink of it ever and again with a glad heart. Sit down upon the sacred grass at this sacrifice and hold this Soma-drop in your belly, O Indra.
The sacred grass is strewn for you, O Indra; the Soma is pressed; the roasted grain is made ready for your bays to eat. To you, who dwell in that home, the mighty bull attended by the Maruts, the oblations are offered.
These men, the mountains, and the waters, O Indra, have mingled it sweet with milk for you. Come to it with a glad heart, O tall one, and drink, knowing your own right paths as one who understands.
Those Maruts whom you, O Indra, shared in Soma, who strengthened you and became your troop — rejoicing along with them, eager and desirous, drink this Soma with the tongue of Agni, O Indra.
O Indra, drink of the pressed Soma even with sovereign joy, or drink with the tongue of Agni, O adorable one. Or take the gift from the adhvaryus' hands, O mighty one, or enjoy the sacrifice and oblation of the hotar.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
Place this offering for the winning, O Indra, ever seeking us with your constant aids. He who is celebrated by great deeds has waxed great through magnifications at each pressing.
The Soma presses have been known from of old for Indra — the skilled one who mounts the cloud-peaks in flight. Grasp what is being poured out, O Indra; drink of the bull's Soma, shaken by the bull.

title: Rigveda
text:
Drink and grow, O Indra — indeed these pressed Somas are yours, both the first ones and these. Just as you drank the primordial Somas, O Indra, so drink now the admirable, the newer one.
Great is the drinking-vessel in the fold, overflowing; fierce power prevails, bold might. Not even the earth could contain him when the Soma draughts exhilarate him of the bay horses.
The great, the fierce one has grown for heroic power; the bull has fully readied himself with poetic wisdom. Indra is fortune; his prize-winning cows are born; his gifts and rewards are many.
When the rivers sped forth in their onward flow, the waters went like chariot-wheels to the ocean — yet from that seat Indra is yet more exalted when the milked Soma-stalk sates him.
The rivers flowing to the ocean, bearing well-pressed Soma for Indra — the hand-wielded pressing-stones milk the Soma-stalk; they purify it with a stream of sweetness through filters.
Like lake-like receptacles holding the Soma, the many pressings filled him full. When Indra first consumed the food — having slain Vṛtra — he chose the Soma.
Bring it here — let no one keep it from you! For we know you as the lord of riches. O Indra, whatever great gift of yours exists, grant that to us, O you of the bay horses.
Grant to us, O bountiful Indra, lord of the Soma-drops, wealth of all excellence in abundance. Grant us a hundred autumns to live, O Indra of the nose-ring — grant us heroes perpetually.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
For the slaying of Vṛtra, for might and for the conquest of armies, O Indra, we set you in motion.
Turn your mind and your eye hither to us, O Śatakratu; may the praisers make that for you, O Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
We seek your names, O Śatakratu, with all our songs, O Indra, in the conquest of those who hate us.
With a hundred dwelling-places of the much-praised one we magnify him — Indra, who upholds the clans.
I invoke the much-called Indra for the slaying of Vṛtra, for the winning of the prize in battles.
Be ever victorious in battles — we seek you, O Śatakratu, O Indra, for the slaying of Vṛtra.
In glorious battles, in combats, in contests for fame, O Indra, conquer those who oppose us.
Most impetuous and glorious, keep watch over the Soma for our aid, O Indra, O Śatakratu.
The Indra-powers which are yours among the five peoples, O Śatakratu — O Indra, those of yours I here choose.
Gain great fame, O Indra! Establish glory that cannot be overcome. We exalt your power on high.
Come to us from near, and also from afar, O mighty one. Whatever world is yours, O boulder-wielder, Indra, from that place come here to us.
I shall contemplate wisdom as if carving it; like a prize-winning horse well-harnessed and eager, I touch the beloved things and those beyond. Possessing good understanding, I wish to behold the seers.
Now ask of the births of the seers — the mind-firm, well-fashioning ones have carved the sky. These praises of yours, now growing, swift as mind and wind, have gone indeed upon the sacred law.
Laying down their hidden things here, they anointed both worlds together for power. They measured the wide ones with measures and held them firm; within the great pair they set the milch-cow for nourishment.
All beings adorned him as he stood firm; clothed in beauty, self-luminous he moves. Great is that name of the mighty lord; of all forms, he has stood firm in immortal things.
The elder bull brought forth a mightier; his overflows are many and primary. O sons of heaven — at the assemblies with prayers you two kings have established kingship from of old.

title: Rigveda
text:
Three, O kings, are the many seats of the assembly; you adorn them all. I who came here with mind saw among them the Gandharvas who perform vows, with wind-tossed hair.
They measured out by names the fellowship of this bull's milch-cow. The lords of might, clothed in various forms, have laid down their magical shapes here, one after another.
That golden thought of Savitṛ — no one for me has stretched it out fully as he has. Heaven and earth resound throughout with his excellent praise; like a woman, he has covered the births.
You two accomplish the ancient great one's work, so that the divine boon of well-being may be around us. All the magical ones behold the manifold deeds of the standing cow-tongued one.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
Prayer spoken from the heart goes toward Indra, the lord, shaped into praise. That which, ever-wakeful, is being proclaimed in the assembly, O Indra — know it as born of you.
Coming from heaven even as primordial ones, wakeful and being proclaimed in the assembly, clothed in bright and fair garments — this is our ancient paternal wisdom.
Even what the mother of Yama bore here — the foremost fell from the tongue, for it has stood forth. The forms born as twins go together; these burn darkness from the base of the blazing fire.
None of those fathers of ours who were fighters for the cows are to be blamed among mortals. Indra their strengthener, of great power, opened the cow-pens by his wondrous deeds.
Where as a friend, with the Navagva friends, the knowers followed the cows with the warriors — truly then Indra, together with the ten Daśagvas, found the sun dwelling in darkness.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra found the honey gathered in the dawn-cow — what had feet, what had hooves, what could bow the neck of the cow. He placed what was hidden, the secret, concealed in the waters, in his right hand, he of the right hand.
He chose the light, distinguishing it from darkness; may we be far from adversity when near. Be pleased with these songs, O drinker of Soma, O one magnified by Soma, O Indra, of the singer's many offerings.
Light shall attend the sacrifice along heaven and earth; may we be far from many misfortunes. For even of a mortal who presses on, the Vasus are easy to cross by their great power.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
O Indra, we call upon you, the bull, at the pressed Soma. Drink then of the sweet Soma-plant.
O Indra, be pleased with the pressed Soma that knows the work, O much-praised one. Drink, O bull, your fill.
O Indra, carry our devotional sacrifice forward with all the gods. Do bear it across, O praised lord of the folk.
O Indra, these pressed Soma-drops advance toward you, O lord of the good — the bright shining drops to your abode.
Hold the pressed, excellent Soma in your belly, O Indra. The drops that dwell in the sky are yours.
O you who delight in songs, drink our pressed Soma — you are anointed with streams of sweetness. The glory given by you, O Indra, is indeed ours.
The inexhaustible glories like those of a forest accompany Indra. Having drunk of the Soma, he has grown great.
Come to us from near and from far, O Vṛtra-slayer. Be pleased with these our songs.
When you are called between the far and near, O Indra, from that place come here to us.
Come hither now, O Indra, turned benevolently toward us who call, for the drinking of Soma; come, O boulder-wielder, with your two bays.

title: Rigveda
text:
Our seasonal hotar has sat down; the sacred grass is strewn in succession; in the morning the pressing-stones have been yoked.
These sacred prayers are being made, O bearer of prayer. Sit down upon the sacred grass. O hero, enjoy the sacrificial cake.
Grant us success at these pressings, at these praises, O Vṛtra-slayer, at these hymns, O Indra who delights in songs.
Prayers lick Indra the wide Soma-drinker, the lord of might, as mothers lick a calf.
Be exhilarated by the Soma-plant for bounty, for the great one himself. Do not put the praiser to shame.
We, longing for you, O Indra, bearing oblations, praise you. And you, O lord, desire us in return.
Do not release yourself away from us who love the bays — come hither! O Indra of sovereign power, be exhilarated here.
May the two mane-horses, dripping ghee, bring you hitherward on the comfortable chariot, O Indra, to sit upon the sacred grass.
Come to our pressed Soma mixed with milk, O Indra, with your two bays that desire us.
Come to that exhilaration, O Indra, to what is pressed on the sacred grass with the pressing-stones. Will you now be fully satisfied with it?
My songs thus directed go toward Indra, sent from here. For his return, for the drinking of Soma.
For the drinking of Soma we here invoke Indra with praises and with hymns. Will he now come?
O Indra, these Soma-drops are pressed — hold them in your belly, O Śatakratu, O lord of the prize-winning company.
For we know you as the winner of riches, O seer, bold in contests. So we seek your benevolence.
Drink this Soma of ours mixed with milk, and that mixed with barley, O Indra — the pressed draught with the bulls coming to it.
For you, O Indra, in your own home, I urge the Soma for drinking. Let this one delight your heart.
We the Kuśikas, seeking aid, invoke you, O ancient Indra, for the drinking of the pressed Soma.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come hither, standing in the chariot-seat — from of old the Soma-drinking awaits you. The beloved friends are here; spread out the sacred grass. These fire-bearers call you.
Come past the many human settlements, O noble one, with your two bays and blessings upon us. For these prayers, shaped into praise, call you, O Indra, taking pleasure in friendship.
Come swiftly to our sacrifice that increases through obeisance, O divine Indra, in accord with us and with your two bays. For I call you repeatedly with prayers, preceded by ghee, to the feast of sweetness.
May these two bulls, your bay companions, well-harnessed and well-limbed, bring you here. May Indra enjoying the pressing-feast with grain, as a friend may hear the songs of the friend.
Will you make me guardian of the people? Will you, O bountiful Soma-lord, make me a king? Will you make me a seer who has drunk of the pressed Soma? Will you grant me your immortal wealth?
May the great bays, being yoked, bring you hither, O Indra, to the common feast — those who gleam high twice from heaven, well-adorned, the wise ones of the bull.
O Indra, drink of the bull's Soma shaken by the bull, which the eager falcon brought to you — in whose exhilaration you shake the peoples forth, in whose exhilaration you opened the cow-pens.
May we invoke for our well-being the bountiful Indra, most manly in this battle, in the contest for the prize — him who listens, the fierce one for help in combats, who slays the obstructions and wins the wealth.
May this Soma, desirable and pressed by the bays, be yours. Enjoying it with your bays, O Indra, come to us — mount the bay chariot.
Delighting, you illumined the dawn; delighting, you made the sun shine. Knowing and discerning, O you of the bay horses, you grow great, O Indra, encompassing all glories.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra upheld the sky with the bay's brilliance, the earth with bay-colored form. Between those two the green one moves with abundant nourishment of the bays.
Born as the golden-green bull, he illumines all the luminous realm. The bay-horsed one holds the golden-green weapon — the green thunderbolt in his arms.
Indra, who loves the gleaming, bright thunderbolt enveloped with bright rays — uncovering it with his bays and the pressing-stones, he pressed the Soma and drove the cows up with his bays.
Come, O Indra, with your pleasing bays with peacock-feather manes! Let no one hold you back — like a bird past the snare, go past them as over a desert.
The eater of Vṛtra, the breaker of Vala, the destroyer of forts, the driver of waters — the charioteer standing with the two bays, roaring onward, Indra, the smasher even of the firm.
You nourish wisdom as if filling deep seas, you nourish the cows. Well-guarded, they reach the pasture as cows reach a pond, as streams a lake.
Bring us driving wealth — a share not recognized by others. Shake the ripe fruit from the tree as if with a hook, O Indra — the carrying-across wealth.
Self-willed, O Indra, you are self-ruling, aiming well, more self-glorious. Waxing great in might, O much-praised one, be the best known to fame for us.
Great are the heroic deeds of you, O Indra, the combative, the bull, the self-king, the fierce, the youthful, the strong, the vigorous, the unaging wielder of the thunderbolt, the famous, the great one.
You are great, O buffalo-bull, by your bull-like powers — O fierce one who overwhelms others, winning wealth. You alone are king of the whole world; you set the peoples to war and to settlement.
He shines forth beyond measure, radiant; beyond the gods in every direction, unrivaled. Indra surpasses by his greatness sky and earth; the Soma-drinker surpasses the vast great atmosphere.

title: Rigveda
text:
Wide, deep, fierce from birth, of universal reach, the refuge of prayers — into Indra the Somas pressed from of old flow and enter as rivers into the sea.
That Soma which the earth and heaven carry for you as a mother carries an embryo for the sake of you, O Indra — that the adhvaryus send for you, they cleanse it for you too, O bull, for the drinking.
O Indra, bull attended by the Maruts, drink the Soma for battle, drink of your own nature for exhilaration. Pour the sweet wave into your belly — you are the king from of old of the pressed Somas.
In accord, O Indra, in a troop together with the Maruts, drink the Soma, O Vṛtra-slayer, O hero, knowing all. Strike the enemies, drive back the despisers, and make us fearless on all sides.
O guardian of the seasons, drink at the proper seasons our pressed Soma, O Indra, with the gods your companions. Those Maruts whom you shared, who followed you and slew Vṛtra — they gave their might to you.
Those who strengthened you, O bountiful one, in the slaying of the serpent, who were with you in the slaying of Śambara, O bay-horsed one, who were with you in the winning of the cows, those inspired men who exult with you now — drink the Soma, O Indra, together with the Maruts.
We would here invoke for our protection the new-praising Indra attended by the Maruts — the bull who has grown great, the heavenly one of irresistible command, the all-conquering, the fierce giver of might.
Scarce born, the bull, the youthful one, was eager to bear away the pressed Soma juice; drink, as pleases thee, O potent one, the first draught of the excellent Soma blended with milk.
On that very day when thou wast born, in thy desire thou drankest the first milk of the Soma stalk that grows on the mountain; that milk, O youth, thy mother, thy genetrix, poured out for thee first in the great father's house.

title: Rigveda
text:
Coming to his mother he sought food; sharp-eyed, he beheld the udder of the Soma; driving others away he moved on, the impetuous one, manifold in aspect — he accomplished great deeds.
Fierce, the crusher of strongholds, overpowering in might, he shaped his body as he willed; Indra, having overcome Tvaṣṭṛ at his very birth, drank the Soma from his bowls.
With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.
Proclaim the greatness of Indra in whom all Soma-drinking peoples find their full desire; him of keen purpose, wrought wide by Dhiṣaṇā, the destroyer of Vṛtras, whom the gods brought to birth.
Whom none at all in battles overcomes — the self-ruler, foremost of heroes, standing in the tawny steeds; who, most powerful with his fighters and shouts, with far-extending flame cut short the life of the Dasyu.
Prevailing in battles, the rapid one, not to be overcome, he who fills both worlds with his greatness; to be invoked as Bhaga in the rite, worthy of the prayers, dear as a father, easy of invocation, the bestower of strength.
The upholder of heaven, exalted upon the back of the firmament, like a chariot of wind yoked with good steeds; he who clothes the night, the begetter of the Sun, the distributor of shares like Dhiṣaṇā distributes the prize.
With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.
Let Indra, svāhā, drink of him whose Soma is pressed — the strong bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has come hither; wide-reaching, may he satisfy us with these foods; may the oblation of thy body prosper according to desire.

title: Rigveda
text:
I yoke for thee thy two worshipful steeds for speed, through whom thou hast ever followed obedience from of old; may the bay steeds bring thee here, O fair-lipped one; drink now of this, the beautifully pressed Soma.
The singers, mixing him with milk, established Indra, easy to cross over, for supreme nourishment; thou who art gladdened, who hast drunk the Soma, O Ṛjīṣin, drive together for us the cows in manifold ways.
Gladden this desire with cows and horses and with thy brilliant gift that is extended far; the inspired Kuśikas have made their conveyances for Indra with joyous hymns of praise to thee.
With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.
The broad hymns have sung forth in praise of Indra, the bountiful, cherished by all peoples, worthy of laud; him who ever waxes strong, invoked by many, with beautiful praises — the immortal one who is lauded day by day.
My hymns approach Indra from all sides — the man of a hundred powers, the flood-like, the mighty, the winner of prizes, the breaker of strongholds, the swift, the one never missed, abiding in the dwelling, united with glory, the finder of light.
At the mine of riches the singer is celebrated; Indra, blameless, is pleased with praises and gives service; for he delights in the dwelling of Vivasvat — praise him who conquers all, who slays the assailants.
Sing forth together with hymns and lauds the hero, the foremost of men; he who is full of craft springs up to meet your strength; reverence to him who alone is lord from of old.
Many are his resting-places among mortals; the earth bears many treasures for him; the skies, the herbs, the waters, the swift streams, and the forests guard the wealth for Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
For thee are these prayers and hymns, O Indra; for thee entirely have they been established, O lord of bays — be pleased with them; be an ally for the help of the new song, O friend, O Vasu; bestow vigour upon the singers.
Indra, with thy Marut host, drink here the Soma as thou drankest of what was pressed for Śāryāta; under thy leadership, in thy protection, O hero, the wise poets who sacrifice well seek favour.
He, eagerly desiring, drink here the Soma pressed for us, O Indra, with thy friends the Maruts; when the gods adorned thee at birth for the great contest, O much-invoked, all of them.
In the rite of the waters these Maruts are his allies, the givers of gifts, who gladden Indra; may the devourer of Vṛtra drink together with them the pressed Soma of the worshipper in his own dwelling place.
This indeed has been pressed with strength, O lord of bounties; drink now of this, O thou who art praised with hymns.
Whosoever shall be with thee according to thy will at the pressing, pour thyself down upon him; let him delight in thee who art full of Soma.
Let the sacred prayer penetrate thy two flanks, O Indra, and thy head; and reach thy two arms, O hero, for the bestowal of bounty.
The offering with parched grain, the mixture with groats, the cake, together with the laud — be pleased with these of ours at dawn, O Indra.
The cake to be cooked, O Indra — be pleased with it and accept it; for thee the oblations are poured out.
Enjoy our sacrificial cake and delight in our hymns, as a bridegroom delights in maidens.
The sacrificial cake at the morning pressing — be pleased with ours, O thou who hast been praised of old; for thy will, O Indra, is great.
Make the parched grains and the sacrificial cake of the midday pressing beautiful here, O Indra; when the praiser, the singer, swift of purpose, desiring thee, approaches thee with hymns.

title: Rigveda
text:
At the third pressing the parched grains and the offered cake — exalt us, O thou who art praised by many; thee, O sage, who art accompanied by the Ṛbhus and prizes, may we approach with our prayers, bearing oblations.
We have made the groat-mixture for thee who art accompanied by Pūṣan, and the parched grain for thee who lovest the bay steeds; eat the cake with thy company of Maruts; drink the Soma, O hero, slayer of Vṛtra, thou who knowest.
Bring quickly to him the parched grains and the cake — to him who is the most heroic of men; day by day may the fitting offerings increase thee, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma, O bold one.
O Indra and Parvata, bring here with the great chariot the choicest refreshments, ye who bestow good heroes; enjoy the oblations at the rites, O gods; may ye two wax great, gladdened by our hymns and by Iḷā.
Stay well, O bountiful one, do not pass away; I will now sacrifice to thee with the beautifully pressed Soma; as a son grasps his father's skirt, so I take hold of thee, O Indra, O powerful one, with the sweetest hymn.
Let us two recite, O Adhvaryu, answer my words; let us make the chariot-offering agreeable to Indra; let Indra sit on this sacrificial grass of the sacrificer, and then let the laud be proclaimed to Indra.
The wife is the home, O bountiful one, and she is the womb — may the yoked bay steeds bring thee there; whenever we press the Soma, may Agni as messenger speed toward thee.
Depart and return, O bountiful one; O Indra, O brother, thy purpose lies in both directions — both where the great chariot is put to rest and where the prize-winning horse is unyoked.
Thou hast drunk the Soma; proceed home, O Indra; a fair wife awaits thee joyfully in thy house — where the great chariot is laid to rest and the prize horse is unyoked on the right side.

title: Rigveda
text:
These Bhoja princes of various forms, sons of heaven, heroes of the lord of might — giving gifts to Viśvāmitra, they extend their life to a thousandfold pressing.
The bountiful one assumes form after form, working his wonders about his own body; when he has come three times around heaven for a moment — he who seasons not the seasons, yet the master of holy law, by his own spells.
The great seer, god-born and god-driven, beholding men, stayed the flooded river Sindhu; when Viśvāmitra was conveying Sudās, Indra became friendly through the Kuśikas.
Like swans ye make your sound with the pressing stones, gladdened at the rite when the Soma has been pressed together with hymns; O inspired sages, seers who behold men, O Kuśikas, drink separately the sweet Soma mead.
Come near, O Kuśikas, be attentive; release the horse of Sudās for wealth; the king has slain the foe to east, to west, and to the north — now let him sacrifice in the choicest place of the earth.
I who have praised Indra — both these worlds — the sacred prayer of Viśvāmitra protects the people of Bharata.
The Viśvāmitras have offered the sacred prayer to Indra who wields the thunderbolt; may he make us rich in good bounty.
What do the cows do for thee among the Kīkaṭas? They yield no admixture of milk, nor do they heat the ritual drink; bring us the wealth of Pramaganda, O bountiful one, and subdue for us the low-branched one.
The far-spreading one, given by Jamadagni, having repelled ignorance, measured out greatly; the daughter of the Sun stretched out fame that is immortal and undecaying among the gods.
The far-spreading one quickly brought fame to these five peoples; bearing new life for the wing, which the Palastis and Jamadagnīs gave to me.
May the two oxen be firm, the axle strong; remove the ram, let not the yoke be shattered; may Indra give what is hidden in the peg-hole — O thou whose wheel-rim is uninjured, be thou with us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Place strength in our bodies, O Indra, place strength in our bulls; place strength in our immediate offspring and in our descendants for life — for thou art the giver of strength.
Wrap thyself in the heartwood of the Khadira tree; place thy strength in the trembling Śiṁśapā wood; axle, O firm one, be firmly made firm; do not slip away from this chariot of ours.
Let this forest tree neither abandon us nor injure us; may it bring us safely, with good shelter, from house to the place of unyoking.
Quicken us today, O Indra, with thy many aids, with the best of them, O bountiful one, O hero; let him who hates us fall low; and him whom we hate — let his own breath forsake him.
Even the axe splits apart; even the silk-cotton tree is cut through; even the cooking-pot, O Indra, when it rushes forward, well offered, throws off its foam.
People understand not the arrow; thinking it an animal, they lead the Lodha tree; they do not put the non-prize-winner to shame with the prize-winner, nor do they place the donkey before the horses.
These sons of Bharata, O Indra, have understood retreat, not advance; they urge the horse like a wild, not domestic one, and lead around the bowstring-impelled one in battle.
They have sung forth this strength for the great, ever-adorable one, again and again; may he hear us with his domestic hosts; may Agni, the inextinguishable one, hear us with his heavenly hosts.
Greatly do I sing in praise of great Heaven and Earth; my desire wanders knowing what it seeks; in their laud, at the assemblies, the gods who worship delight together in both of them.
Let the holy law of you two, O Heaven and Earth, be true; be ye great for our great well-being; I pay homage to Heaven and to Earth, O Agni; I seek with offerings, I approach for the treasure.
For your ancient ones have found you, O Heaven and Earth who keep holy law and speak truth; even heroes have praised you both in the assembly at the contest of heroes, O Earth, knowing you well.

title: Rigveda
text:
Who truly knows, who here could declare which path leads toward the gods? Their lowest seats are seen, those that are in the higher, secret observances.
The seer who beholds men has looked upon them both, delighting in the ample source of holy law; like a bird's two wings, they have made their dwelling separate, yet with one purpose, understanding each other.
Of the same origin yet parted, far and near, they stand in the firm, wakeful station; and the two sisters, being young maidens, utter the names of the couples.
All this origin has become clearly distinguished; bearing the great gods, they do not totter; one thing, moving yet firm, rules the universe; another moving, winged, is born in various directions.
I approach from afar the ancient thing of old, the kinship with the great father and begetter; where the gods, marvelling with their wonders, have stood apart in the wide path, between the two.
I speak this hymn to Heaven and Earth, may they with gentle bellies, with Agni as their tongue, hear it — Mitra, the young sovereign Varuṇa, the Ādityas who are wise seers, spread widely.
Savitṛ of golden hands, of good tongue, ruling in the assembly three times from heaven; and O Savitṛ, thou who hast spread thy fame among the gods — now drive toward us all-embracing totality.
The god Tvaṣṭṛ, the well-doer, of fair hands, possessed of goodness, guardian of holy law — may he set these things for our help; O Ṛbhus accompanied by Pūṣan, be ye gladdened; with upraised pressing stones ye have fashioned the sacrifice.
The Maruts, whose chariots are lightning, armed with spears, the youths of heaven, born of holy law, untiring; may Sarasvatī hear them, the worthy of worship; may Dhātṛ, the victorious, grant wealth accompanied by heroes.
Hymns and praises have come to Viṣṇu of many wonders on his path, like those of Bhaga's worshippers; the wide-striding one who is the summit — his many young mothers who bore him never fail him.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra, ruling with all his heroic powers, has filled both worlds with his greatness; the breaker of strongholds, the slayer of Vṛtra, of bold army — grasping firmly, bring us many cattle.
The two Nāsatyas are my fathers, to be asked of kin; the lovely name of the Aśvins is of the same clan; for ye two are the givers of riches to us among the wealthy; ye guard the gift, unblind and undeceived.
That lovely name of yours is great, O wise ones, whereby ye all, O gods, are present in Indra; O friend, O much-invoked, with thy beloved Ṛbhus, fashion this thought of ours for victory.
Aryaman, Aditi, the worthy of worship, the undeceived ordinances of Varuṇa — ward off from us childlessness and going away; may our path be fruitful in offspring and rich in cattle.
May the messenger of the gods, sent forth in many ways, declare our freedom from guilt in all wholeness; may Earth hear us, and Heaven, and the Waters, the Sun, and the wide atmosphere with the stars.
May the bull-like mountains hear us, those of firm abode, gladdened by Iḷā; may Aditi hear us together with the Ādityas; may the Maruts grant us excellent shelter.
May the path ever be easily traversable and full of nourishment; may the gods mingle the herbs with sweetness; O Bhaga, O Agni, fail me not in thy friendship; may I attain the abode of riches, the seat of plenty.
Savour the oblations, kindle the refreshments, measure out the glories toward us; O Agni, conquer all those enemies in battles; shine upon us graciously through all the days.
From the former dawns — when they dawned — the great imperishable was born at the station of the cow; the ordinances of the gods have now come to their fullness: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Let not the gods deceive us here, O Agni, nor the forefather who know the track; the banner stands between the two ancient dwellings: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
My desires fly apart in many directions; toward the fire-staff the ancient things shine forth; at the kindled fire let us speak only truth: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The one king, spread over many places, lies down in the resting places, sent forth along the forests; one mother carries the calf and dwells apart: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
He has occupied the earlier ones; the later has spread further within the young ones just born; the pregnant ones bring forth without having been approached: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
There lies a dweller; then the one calf with two mothers wanders unbound; these are the ordinances of Mitra and Varuṇa: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The priest with two mothers is the sovereign at the assemblies; following the first, he dwells upon the foundation; they carry forth the joys, those whose speech is joyous: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Like that of the most intimate hero in combat, all that approaches is seen face to face; the insight moves within what is settled of the cow: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The grey-haired one flashes back and forth among them as messenger; the great one moves within them with luminous splendour; bearing forms, he looks out upon us: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Viṣṇu the protector guards the highest station, bearing the beloved immortal abodes; Agni knows all these beings: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The two siblings, twin-like, have made their forms separate; of the two, one shines dark, the other differently; when the dark one and the ruddy one are sisters: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Where mother and daughter, both milch cows, milk together in unison and give suck face to face — I praise them within the seat of holy law: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Licking another's calf, she measured out; in what manner does the cow lay down her udder? By the milk of holy law does Iḷā fill it: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Clothing herself in footsteps, many-formed in shapes, she has stood erect licking the three-year-old; knowing this, I wander through the seat of holy law: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
As if laid in a footprint, wondrous, between the two — one hidden, the other manifest; that path going together yet running in different directions: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Let the cows low, those not suckled, milking together, lying down, not yet fully milked; ever becoming newer and newer as young maidens: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
When the bull bellows among some cows, he deposits seed in another herd; for he is the possessor of night, he is Bhaga, he is the king: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Let us now declare the might of horses of the hero; the gods know of it; thrice six times yoked, they carry five by five: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The god Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, of all forms, has nourished progeny; he has begotten them in manifold ways; and all these beings are his: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The great one has brought together two bowls face to face; both have been filled with his treasure; the hero is heard, finding wealth: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
Upon this earth of ours, all-sustaining, he dwells as a king who keeps his friends well-disposed; the heroes sit before in safety as if seated in shelter: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.
The herbs that restrain, O Indra, the waters and the earth bear wealth for thee; may we be thy friends, partakers of thy bounty: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Neither the deceitful nor the wise ones transgress the first, firm ordinances of the gods; neither do Heaven and Earth bowing before the altars, nor the mountains that have stood firm.
The one, moving alone, carries six burdens; the holy law, most abundant, the cows have come up to; three great ones stand above as if on swift horses; two are hidden in secret, one is visible.
The bull of triple gait, of all forms, likewise three-weaponed, prolific in many forms, of three faces, rules as one of greatness; he the seed-depositor, the bull of eternal ones.
The path of these ones was suddenly awakened; the lovely name of the Ādityas was called out; even the divine waters rested for him; going separately, they encompassed him on every side.
Three stations of the rivers, three of the wise ones, and the sovereign at the assembly has three mothers; the three holy women who keep the law, those sunk in the waters, ruling three times in the assembly from heaven.
Three times from heaven, O Savitṛ, impel the desirable things; day by day drive them thrice for us through the day; drive to us wealth of threefold nature; O Bhaga, O protector, O Dhiṣaṇā, set them for our gaining.
Savitṛ has driven three times from heaven; the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa, of fair hands; even the waters and the wide Heaven and Earth beg for the gem at the driving-forth of Savitṛ.
Three highest, hard to assail are the luminous realms; three are the heroes of the lord of might who rule; may the gods who keep holy law, the vigorous, hard to reach, be present three times in the assembly from heaven.
The discerning one has found my insight, the cow roaming freely, sent forth, without a herdsman; she who even now has milked abundantly from the overflowing — Indra and Agni are the admirers of her.
Indra and Pūṣan, both bulls, of fair hands, well pleased as from heaven, have milked what lay still; when all the gods shall delight in her, may I here attain the favour of the Vasus.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those who are the kinswomen who desire the power of the bull, reverently honouring them, knowing the embryo within — the cows calling aloud go toward the son, bearing splendid forms.
I speak forth to Heaven and Earth, both fair-thighed, with insight yoked to the pressing stones at the rite; these many-choiced, visible, worthy-of-worship gifts of thine for the sacrificer rise upward, O Manu.
That tongue of thine, honey-sweet, O Agni, wide-reaching, the wise one, called out among the gods — with it seat here all the worthy-of-worship ones for our protection; and cause them to drink the sweet drinks.
That care of thine which shines gloriously, O god, following like a stream from the mountain, which nourishes — grant that care to us, O Jātavedas, O Vasu; grant us the goodwill that belongs to all people.
The cow yielding the cherished milk of the ancient one — her son roams within the southern region. (Dawn) drives forward the luminous one with bright course; the hymn of praise has awakened the two Aśvins.
The well-yoked steeds carry (your car) toward you, O Aśvins; the prayers rise upward like the fathers (of old). Drive away from us the miserliness of the Paṇi; we have rendered your praises — come hither to us.
With well-yoked horses and a well-rolling chariot, O Dasras, hear this invocation from the stone-pressing. What is the reply, O Aśvins, that the inspired sages — born of old — give back to you?
Take heed and come, by whatever roads you travel; all peoples call upon you, O Aśvins. For these sweet drinks of the mountain-cow (Goṛjīkā) have been poured forth at dawn like gifts among friends.
O Aśvins, bountiful lords, the hymn of praise has sounded for you across many realms among the peoples. Come hither by the god-traversed paths, O Dasras — here are your stored treasures of sweet draughts.

title: Rigveda
text:
Your ancient abode, your auspicious friendship, O heroes, and your wealth (are) on the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā). Renewing these blessed bonds of fellowship, may we rejoice together with you in sweetness now, united.
O Aśvins, both skilled in good works, together with Vāyu and with your teams of horses, young and pleased together — O Nāsatyas, delighting beyond the passing of day, drink the Soma unfailingly, O gracious givers.
O Aśvins, your many refreshments have circled round you, borne on by songs, unimpeded. Your chariot born of Order, urged by the stone-presser, circles Heaven-and-Earth in a single day.
O Aśvins, come to the dwelling — the most honey-sweet Soma calls out for you; drink it. Your chariot of many a changing form gleams brightly; it has come most swiftly to the presser who has pressed the Soma.
Mitra, when he speaks, sets people in their proper order; Mitra upholds both the earth and the sky. Mitra watches over the peoples with unwinking eye — pour the oblation rich in ghee to Mitra.
Let that mortal prosper, O Mitra, O Āditya, who strives to please you in accordance with your ordinance. He is not slain, not overcome, protected by you; distress does not reach him, neither from near nor from afar.
Free from disease, rejoicing in refreshment, treading lightly across the breadth of the earth, dwelling near the ordinance of Āditya — may we be in the good grace of Mitra.
This Mitra is worthy of homage, most kind, a king of good dominion — he was born as the ordainer. May we be in the good grace and blessed benevolence of him, the sacred one.
Great is Āditya, to be approached with homage; he who orders mankind is most kind to the singer. Pour into the fire this oblation offered to Mitra, most worthy of admiration.
The protection of Mitra, upholder of peoples, of the divine, ever-gaining — (that protection is) the most brilliantly renowned glory.

title: Rigveda
text:
Mitra, by his greatness, has encompassed the sky with wide expanse; (he has encompassed) the earth with his glories.
The five peoples have submitted themselves to Mitra for his conquering strength. He sustains all the gods.
Mitra, among the gods possessing life-force, has made nourishing foods for the one who has cut the sacrificial grass, for one whose vows are accomplished.
Hither and thither, O men, the kinship with you has come by thought; the Auśijas reached those (deeds) with wisdom. By those magic skills, swiftly-changing in form, the Saudhanvanas — sons of Sudhanvan — attained their sacred share.
By those skills with which they adorned the cups; by that insight with which they freed the cow from its skin; by that mind with which they fashioned the two bay steeds — by that the Ṛbhus attained divinity.
The Ṛbhus attained the friendship of Indra; the grandsons of Manu pressed forward with their works. The Saudhanvanas ascended to immortality, having pervaded everywhere through their labors — the well-doers through well-doing.
You travel on the same chariot as Indra at the pressing; and you share in the glory of the oblation-offerers. The singer cannot match your good deeds, O Saudhanvanas, O Ṛbhus, nor your heroic acts.
O Indra, with the Ṛbhus possessing prizes, sprinkle the pressed Soma in your two hands. O bountiful one, urged by prayer in the house of the pious worshipper, take joy together with the Saudhanvana men.
O Indra, together with the Ṛbhus and the prize-winners, rejoice here in us at this pressing by your power, O much-praised one. These daily observances have been set in order for you through the ordinances of the gods and of Manu.
O Indra, together with the Ṛbhus and the prize-winners, seeking prizes, come here to the sacrificial hymn of the singer. With a hundred swift banners, O guide of thousands, come to the oblation-pouring of this sacrifice.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Uṣas, possessing prize-wealth, prize-winning, all-knowing — be pleased with the hymn of the singer, O bountiful one. O ancient goddess, ever-young, full of insight, you walk according to the eternal ordinance, O all-desired one.
O Uṣas, immortal goddess, shine forth — you who travel in a bright chariot, bringing pleasant truths. Let the well-guided steeds bear you, golden-hued, broad in splendor.
O Uṣas, facing all beings of the universe, you stand high as the banner of immortality. Moving toward the same goal, roll forward like the wheel of a new (wagon).
Gathering like threads from a spindle, O bountiful Dawn, the consort of the sun goes forth. Generating light, the fortunate one of beautiful works has spread herself from the edge of the sky to the earth.
Toward the shining goddess Uṣas bring forward your well-fashioned hymn of praise with homage. The honey-placing one has stretched her power aloft in the sky; the radiant spaces have blazed forth, delightful to behold.
The guardian of Order was awakened by the rays of the sky; the rich one has stood brilliantly on both world-halves. O Agni, you who beg, you approach lovely wealth — the far-coming, brightly shining Uṣas.
From the foundation of cosmic Order, urging on the Dawns, the bull has entered the mighty heaven-and-earth. The great magic wisdom of Mitra and Varuṇa has spread its light in many places like the moon.
These Bhṛgus, meditating upon you, have become (powerful) like missiles driven by you two. Where, O Indra and Varuṇa, is that glory of yours by which you ever bring gain to your friends?
This one, most numerous of your worshippers, rich in wealth, calls out again and again for your help. O Indra and Varuṇa, united with the Maruts, hear my invocation from heaven and earth.
May that treasure be ours, O Indra and Varuṇa; may that wealth of all heroes be ours, O Maruts. May the protective goddesses shelter us with their shelters; may Bhāratī (Sarasvatī), as Hotrā, (favor) us with her bounties.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Bṛhaspati, lord of all the gods, be pleased with our offerings. Bestow precious gifts upon the pious worshipper.
Worship Bṛhaspati the pure with hymns at the sacrifices. He has shown forth matchless strength.
Bṛhaspati the bull of the peoples, all-formed, undeceivable — him we choose as most excellent.
O Pūṣan, O radiant god, this newest excellent praise-song is recited by us for you.
Be pleased with this speech of mine that seeks the prize; promote (my) thought — as a bridegroom (desires) a maiden.
He who looks out over all the worlds and surveys them together — may that Pūṣan be our protector.
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of divine Savitṛ — may he impel our thoughts.
We, seeking the prize with (our) insight, implore the divine gift of Savitṛ (and) of Bhaga.
The inspired men, urged by prayer, worship divine Savitṛ with well-formed sacrifices and with homage.
Soma goes, knowing the way; he proceeds to the purified (dwelling) of the gods. He takes his seat in the womb of cosmic Order.
May Soma make nourishing foods, free from disease, for us — both for the two-footed and the four-footed creature.
Increasing our life-span, overwhelming our adversaries, may Soma take his seat in the common gathering-place.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pasture with ghee; O you of good wisdom, bedew the realms with sweetness.
O widely praised ones, growing great through homage, you two reign by the greatness of (your) power. With your longest (reach), O pure in vow.
Being praised by Jamadagni, sit in the womb of cosmic Order. Drink the Soma, O you who strengthen Order.
Thee, O Agni, the gods of one accord have ever sent as their divine messenger — by their will they sent thee forth. The immortal one established among mortals, the divine and all-knowing Ādeva — they generated thee, the all-wise Pracetas, the divine Pracetas.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, bring hither thy brother Varuṇa together with the gods, by thy goodwill — him who is fond of sacrifice, the eldest, who delights in sacrifice. Bring the truth-bearing Āditya, upholder of peoples, the king who upholds the tribes.
As a friend, turn thy friend hither, as a wheel on the chariot-track hastens swiftly — hasten toward us, O wondrous one. O Agni, find grace for us together with Varuṇa, among the Maruts of universal splendor. Grant bliss to our offspring and strength, O blazing one — grant us welfare, O wondrous one, grant us welfare.
Thou, O Agni, knowing the wrath of god Varuṇa, shouldst turn it away from us. Thou who art most worthy of worship, best of conveyors, ever blazing — drive away all hatreds from us.
Be thou, O Agni, our lowest and nearest aid at the break of this dawn. Worship Varuṇa on our behalf and bestow grace — come to us with clemency and be easy to invoke.
The most excellent and most wonderful vision of this blessed god among mortals — pure like clarified butter heated up, like the munificence of the inviolable cow, desirable and divine.
Threefold are those supreme, true, and desirable births of divine Agni. He comes enclosed within the limitless, blazing, bright, noble, and radiantly gleaming.
He is the messenger who pervades every dwelling, the Hotṛ with a golden chariot and a tongue of copper, with red horses, beautiful in form, of great light — ever joyous, the assembly of which is like one rich in food.
Awakening men — this bond of sacrifice — they lead him forth by great thongs. Achieving his goal among the houses of his worshiper, the divine one attained partnership with the mortal.
May Agni, knowing the way, lead us toward that treasure appointed by the gods. That which all the immortals fashioned by thought, that which Father Dyaus, the begetter, made true and watered.

title: Rigveda
text:
He was born first in the households, at the base of great heaven, in the womb of this aerial space — footless and headless, hiding at the extremities, stretching within the nest of the Bull.
First among those worthy of praise he arose from the womb of Ṛta, in the nest of the Bull — desirable, youthful, beautiful, and of great radiance. Seven beloved ones generated him for the Bull.
Here our fathers, the human ones, pressed forward seeking after Ṛta. Calling upon the Dawns, they drove up the radiant cows locked within the stone-walled pen, the well-milking ones within the cavern.
Having shattered the rock they polished it; others among them declared this to all around. Without restraint they sang in praise of the work; finding the light they shaped it with their thoughts.
With cow-seeking mind they surrounded the mountain that was hard, compact, and enclosing the cows. With divine speech the men, the Uśijas, opened up the firm cattle-pen full of kine.
They first thought of the name of the cow; they found the three-times-seven highest names of the mother. Knowing these, the companies sang after them; the glorious red Dawn-cow became manifest.
Darkness was dispelled, heaven shone; the light of the divine Dawns arose. The Sun stood upon the broad meadows, seeing the straight and the crooked among mortals.
Thereupon, awakening, they beheld each other; thereupon they held the heaven-given treasure. May all the gods in all the dwellings — O Mitra, O Varuṇa — let truth be in our thought.
I would speak praise toward blazing Agni, the Hotṛ, the all-sustaining, the most worthy of worship — whose bright udder the cows did not consume, whose pressed Soma was not drunk, like that poured around the filter.
Aditi of all the worshipable beings, guest of all human beings — may Agni, winning the favor of the gods, become gracious to us, the all-knowing Jātavedas.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who, the immortal truth-bearer, was established as the divine messenger among the gods — Agni, the Hotṛ, most worthy of worship, set among mortals to blaze magnificently, to be stirred with oblations.
Here today, O son of power, born between the two kindred, O Agni — thou goest as a lofty messenger having yoked the straight-membered, bull-like, bright horses.
Those exceeding, exhilarating, red, and ghee-dripping steeds I deem the swiftest by mind — belonging to Ṛta. Yoked with the red ones thou goest between you gods and the clans of mortals.
Bring Aryaman, Varuṇa, Mitra among these, Indra, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, and the Aśvins. O Agni, with good horses, fine chariot, and excellent gifts, do convey them to the people of good oblations.
O Agni, let our sacrifice be possessed of kine, possessed of sheep, possessed of horses, friend to heroes, ever imperishable. O mighty one, may this wealth be rich in refreshment, in offspring, long-lasting, broad-based, and fit for the assembly.
He who brings thee fuel perspiring, or scorches his head on account of thee — become thou his mighty guardian, O Agni, and protect him from every evil-doer.
He who brings thee food — even food desired — sharpening, arousing the joyous guest; the god-seeking one who kindles thee in his home — in him may wealth be steadfast and may he be a giver.
He who praises thee at evening or at dawn, or who, possessing oblations, makes thee a beloved offering — like a horse with golden trappings in its own stable, carry that worshiper beyond distress.
He who makes offering to thee, O immortal Agni, and performs service to thee with ladle extended — may he not be separated from wealth when he has striven; let no distress from the evil one encircle him.
He whose sacrifice thou, O Agni, hast enjoyed — the god bestowing well-placed boons on the mortal — may his Hotṛ-service be pleasing, O most youthful; may we be those whose worshiper prospers.

title: Rigveda
text:
O all-knowing one, discern wisdom and unwisdom, separating mortals as if separating the clean from the crooked. For our prosperity and good offspring, O god, grant us bounty and Aditi, and protect us.
The undeceivable seers have instructed the seer, holding him firmly in the houses of life. Therefore, O Agni, mayst thou — visible — see those wondrous things with thy feet and thine own noble steps.
Thou, O Agni, art a good guide to the lauding poet who presses Soma and worships — O most youthful, thou who art dear to peoples. Bring a wide and shining treasure to the striving one for his protection.
For when we have done this by thy aid, O Agni, with feet, hands, and bodies — like those who equip a chariot through the effort of both arms — the clear-minded ones, eagerly seeking, have grasped the truth.
Then may we seven inspired ones be born first from the mother Dawn, as creators of men. May we become sons of Heaven, Aṅgirases, and burst open the wealth-laden mountain while we shine.
Just as our fathers of old, O Agni, eagerly seeking Ṛta, went in purity to the inspiring thought — singing praises, shattering the earth, they drove forth the reddish cows.
Good workers of fine brilliance, desiring the gods, like iron, the gods blowing on their birth — shining, they magnified Agni and Indra, and came surrounding the vast cattle-pen.
As it looked upon the rich cattle-herd, when the mighty births of the gods appeared — even the Urvaśīs of mortals lamented, O noble one, for the upward course of life to grow.
We have become skilled workers through thy deeds; the dawns, shining forth, flowed with truth. Tending Agni, complete and widely brilliant, they polished the beautiful eye of the god.
These hymns, O Agni, O wise ordainer, we have spoken — enjoy them, O seer. Blaze up high, make us better; grant us great wealth, O thou of many gifts.

title: Rigveda
text:
Seek ye the king of the sacrifice, Rudra, the Hotṛ, the true worshiper of the two worlds — Agni of golden form, before the crash of the unconscious thunder, for our protection.
This womb we have made for thee — as a wife, desirous and well-dressed, for her husband. Sit down here facing toward us, surrounded — these offerings face thee, O thou of beautiful radiance.
Pronounce the hymn for him who listens, the inviolate, the ordainer who sees with a hero's eyes, who is gracious — praise the immortal god, whom I, like a Soma-presser with pressing-stone, seek as the honey-squeezer.
Do thou, O Agni, O most kindly one, O wise truth-perceiver, be aware of this Ṛta. When shall thy hymns be those to be rejoiced in together? When shall thy friendships be in thy house?
O Agni, how wilt thou speak to Varuṇa? How dost thou reproach Heaven for our transgression? How wilt thou speak to the bounteous Mitra and to Earth? What wilt thou say to Aryaman, what to Bhaga?
O Agni, what wilt thou say, thriving in thy seats, to Vāta the wide-spread and beautiful? What wilt thou say to the all-wandering Nāsatya? What to Rudra who smites heroes, O Agni?
What wilt thou say to great Pūṣan, the nurturer? What to Rudra of beautiful face, who gives oblations? What wilt thou announce to wide-striding Viṣṇu? What, O Agni, to great Śarva?
Being questioned, what wilt thou say to the truth-bearing troop of Maruts, what to the great, mighty Sun? Speak back to swift Aditi duly, O Jātavedas, all-knowing one of heaven.
By Ṛta seek the fixed truth, the raw and the ripe together with the honey — of the cow, O Agni. Though black, she swelled with kindred milk by the white nourisher, this one.
For even the bull, anointed with Ṛta, masculine Agni, by the milk on his back, moved without trembling as life-sustainer; the bull milked the bright udder of Pṛśni.

title: Rigveda
text:
Shattering the mountain by Ṛta, the Aṅgirases rejoiced together with the kine. The men of good fortune sat around the Dawn; the sun-world became manifest when Agni was kindled.
By Ṛta the divine, immortal, inviolate waters, with their honey-sweet floods, O Agni — like a prize horse in races, ever pressing forward to flow, they were ever ready.
Let us not always bear the deceitful man's burden; let us not injure the lodger or approach him. Let us not, O Agni, reap the debt of the dishonest brother; let us not share the cunning of a treacherous friend.
Protect us, O Agni, with thy protections, guarding us ceaselessly, O beautiful one, propitious. Kick back, smash the firm evil; slay the demon even though it has grown great.
Be gracious with these songs, O Agni — touch these prizes with hymns, O hero. And enjoy the prayers, O Aṅgiras; may thy praise, beloved of the gods, be kindled.
All these mysteries, O Agni, O ordainer, I have proclaimed to thee, the all-knowing — traditional sayings, secret words. I have sung poetic works fit for the seer, with thoughts, O inspired one, with hymns.
Make thy force broad as an extended track; go like a king powerful with his elephant. Raging along the fierce trail, be the archer — pierce the demons with thy hottest darts.
Thy circlings fly swiftly; blazing boldly, thou dost touch with thy tongue the burning things; O Agni, hurl the heat-sparks, and unconstrained, let loose firebrands in all directions.
Send forth thy scouts in all directions, swiftest one; be the unsupplanted guardian of this tribe. Whether the evil-speaker be far or near, O Agni, let no confusion dare to overpower thee.
Rise up, O Agni, spread thyself out and against them, O sharp-weaponed one — burn our enemies down. Whoever has created enmity against us, O enkindled one, burn him down below like dry tinder.

title: Rigveda
text:
Stand upright, shoot past us, make the divine powers manifest, O Agni. Bend low the firm ones of the sorcerers; crush the related and unrelated enemies.
He knows thy favor, O most youthful, who has opened a path for the advancing brahman. To him may all the bright days of wealth and glories of the noble one shine through the doors.
May he, O Agni, be fortunate and bountiful who seeks to satisfy thee with regular oblation and with hymns in his own house and lifetime; may all bright days and his sacrifice be fulfilled for him.
I sing to call down thy favor; may this song be in accord with what thou desirest. With good horses and fine chariots may we honor thee; may thou sustain sovereignty in us through the days.
Here may much come near thee of thyself, shining in the evenings day by day. Playing, may we, well-disposed, worship thee, having attained the glories of the peoples.
He who comes to thee, O Agni, with good horses and fine gold, with a wealth-laden chariot — thou art his protector, thou art his friend — he who has continuously enjoyed thy hospitality.
I break the great kinship with words; that came to me from father Gotama. Do thou mark this our speech, O Hotṛ, most youthful, of pure will, O dweller in the house.
Unsleeping, swift, auspicious, unwearied, undevoured, untired — let those guardians, O Agni, sitting together toward the same goal, protect us, O wise one.
Those guardians of Māmateya — thine, O Agni — watching, they protected from evil, keeping the blind at bay. The all-knowing one preserved them, the doers of good; the enemies, though wishing to harm, did not deceive them.
Strengthened by thee, protected by thee, may we attain prizes by thy guidance. Pacify both praises, O thou of true nature — do this henceforth, O shameless one.
With this fuel, O Agni, we would worship thee — take hold of the praise being recited. Burn the sorcerers; protect us from the demons; O great Mitra, from the blame of the treacherous slanderer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Together and in accord, how shall we make offering to Vaiśvānara, the bounteous, to Agni of great light? He has supported the bank like a prop with his undiminished, great vehicle.
Do not despise him who gave this gift to me, the mortal — the self-empowered god. Unto the simple one, the clever, immortal, all-knowing Vaiśvānara, most manly, young Agni, made it known.
Having the great, doubly strong Sāman-chant, sharp-edged, thousand-seeded, a mighty bull — knowing the hidden footprint of the cow, Agni spoke the inspiring thought to me.
Agni of sharp fangs, of excellent gifts, shall devour them with his hottest flame — those who infringe upon the domain of Varuṇa and the cherished, firm, perceiving laws of Mitra.
Like brotherless women straying, like women hostile to their husbands and of ill ways — being wicked, untruthful, and false, they have found this deep place.
O Agni, this thought of mine for the purifier, the lover — do not put it as a heavy burden. Thou hast boldly placed the great, deep, young back — nourish it with refreshment seven-fold.
May that same purifying thought, through the same will, attain to him from the same level.
What is to be uttered of this my speech? They speak of the hidden, the secret laid within. As they cover the outlet of the cows, the bird protects the dear, foremost station of its form.
This verily is the great, mighty face — that the primal cow accompanies the dawn-cows. Blazing over the station of Ṛta, the swiftly moving one perceived the swiftly flying one hidden.
Then the shining one sat beside his parents, following the beautiful secret of speckled Pṛśni. Near the supreme station of the mother-cow sat the tongue of the bull, of the blazing and exalted one.
Being questioned with reverence I speak the truth, O Jātavedas, by thy command if this be so: thou rulest over all that exists, that which is in heaven and that which is wealth upon earth.

title: Rigveda
text:
What is our wealth in this, what indeed is the treasure? Declare it to us, O all-knowing Jātavedas. The highest point of the hidden path — of that empty station we did not come to the source.
What is the boundary, what the guiding marks? How shall we swift ones reach that which is beautiful, as if a prize? When shall the divine wives of the immortal, the Dawns, be stretched out with the color of the Sun?
With dustless, trifling, obvious, trembling, unsatisfied speech — what do they say here to thee, O Agni? Let the unarmed ones sit and follow their own ways.
For the beauty of this enkindled bull, the face of good Vasu shone in the house. Clothed in brightness, of beautiful form to behold — like a dwelling with wealth he gleamed, of many gifts.
Stand erect, O Hotṛ Agni, at our sacrifice, more worthy of worship in the divine assembly. For thou dost surpass all thought, and thou dost even overcome the wisdom of the wise ordainer.
The blameless Hotṛ Agni, the joyous, all-knowing one has taken his seat among the tribes. He has raised his light on high like Savitṛ; like a post he has propped the smoke up to heaven.
Wearing the good burnished one, the gift-giving, ghee-dripping one, the divine gathering moving to the right — the well-aimed, well-fitted one anoints the new-born, rafter-like sacrifice-post.
When the sacred grass is strewn and Agni is kindled, the Adhvaryu stands erect, delighting. Agni the Hotṛ, like a herdsman, goes around thrice, moving, wearing them from of old.
The Hotṛ Agni, measured in gait, goes around of himself, joyous, speaking sweetly, truth-bearing. His flames run like prize horses; all beings tremble when he blazes forth.
Auspicious is thy appearance, O Agni of beautiful face, though thy nature is terrible and varied. Neither does the darkness veil thy blazing light, nor do the scattered sparks put any taint upon thy body.

title: Rigveda
text:
None has checked his conquest; neither father nor mother could hold him when he is desired. Then, like Mitra, well-settled and purifying, Agni shone among the human tribes.
Twice-five sisters dwelling together gave birth to Agni among the human tribes — him who wakens at dawn, sharp-toothed like Atharvan's tooth, bright, well-breathing, keen like an axe.
Thy golden-dripping, reddish steeds, O Agni, straight-going and well-going — the ruddy, bull-like, straight-membered, wondrous ones — they called to the divine gathering.
Those resistless, tireless, fierce, shining, roaming flames of thine, O Agni, march toward their goal — like hawks in service, with great noise, like the Marut-troop.
The prayer has been fashioned for thee, O enkindled one; he recites the hymn and worships, he has distributed. The Uśijas, the desiring ones, reverently placed Agni the Hotṛ of men, proclaiming the praise of life.
He was here established first by the establishers, the Hotṛ most worthy of worship at sacrifices, to be praised — him whom the Bhṛgus of Apnavāna made resound in the forests, the many-formed, the mighty one, in every tribe.
O Agni, when shall thy divine perception come hereafter in succession? Then mortals have seized upon thee, the praiseworthy one, among the tribes.
Looking upon the truth-bearing, all-knowing one as at the star-studded sky — the one who will complete all sacrifices, in every house.
The swift messenger of Vivasvat who surpasses all peoples — the descendants of Āyu, the Bhṛgavāṇas, seized the beacon, in every tribe.
Him, the perceiving Hotṛ, they have seated in unbroken succession — the joyous, purely-blazing, most worthy of worship one, with his seven stations.
Him, wrapped in eternal mothers, set in the wood, not touching the ground — the many-formed one, hidden in the secret place, well-known, and sought from somewhere.

title: Rigveda
text:
When the gods made sport in the same udder of the two companions, at the station of Ṛta — great Agni, the truth-bearer, invited with oblations by reverence, is ever the bird of the sacrifice.
Knowing the missions of the bird of the sacrifice, perceiving both extremities of the two worlds together — thou goest as messenger from of old, wearing them — more knowing are the ascents of heaven.
Thy black trail and the bright light in front — the moving flame, indeed the one form of forms; when the inciting ones establish the embryo, thou art straightway born and immediately art the messenger.
The strength of him newly born became visible when the wind blows following his flame. He sharpens his sharp tongue in the dry lands; he splits even firm foods with his jaws.
Since he grew on dry foods with the dry — young Agni makes a swift messenger of the swift.
With song I adorn the messenger, the all-knowing conveyor of oblations, the immortal, the most worthy of worship.
For he knows the treasure-trove of wealth, the great ascent to heaven; he will convey the gods hither.
He, the divine one, knows the bowing of the gods, for the truth-seeker in his house; he gives even beloved goods.
He is the Hotṛ and he perceiving the duty of the messenger, goes between, knowing the ascent to heaven.
May we be among those who have presented to Agni with gift-giving oblations — those who kindle him and make him thrive.
They, having won both wealth and heroic strength, became renowned — those who placed their service in Agni.
May riches much-desired come to us day by day; may prizes be roused to us.
He, the inspired one of the peoples, with the might of men, pierces through like an arrow.
O Agni, be gracious — thou art mighty, thou who comest to the god-seeking person who approaches the sacred grass to sit upon it.

title: Rigveda
text:
Hard to overcome among human tribes, the immortal protector — may he become the messenger of all.
He is led around the dwelling, the joyous Hotṛ, at the celestial ceremonies; and he sits down as the Potṛ.
And Agni is the divine lady's companion at the sacrifice, and the lord of the house in the home; and he sits down as the Brahman-priest.
For thou art the speaker on behalf of those performing the sacrifice, and of the people; and of the oblations of humans.
He fulfills the duty of messenger for him whose sacrifice thou hast enjoyed — to carry the mortal's oblation.
Enjoy our sacrifice, our worship, O Aṅgiras; hear our call.
May thy hard-to-conquer chariot encompass us on all sides — that with which thou protectest the worshiper.
O Agni, today let us attain through songs that will-power touching the heart, auspicious as a horse — may we thrive through thy invocations.
For, O Agni, thou hast become the charioteer of the auspicious will-power, of the good discernment, of the great truth.
With these songs be turned toward us, O Agni — like the sun-light, with all thy faces, well-disposed.
Praising thee today with these songs, O Agni, may we make offerings. Thy vigors thunder forth like those of heaven.
Thy most pleasant sight, O Agni, whether now by day or now by night, shines near like a golden ornament of beauty.
Thy body is like purified ghee, spotless, pure gold — that of thine shines like a golden ornament, O self-empowered one.
Even an established hatred thou drivest away from the mortal, O Agni — from the worshiper here in this way, O truth-bearer.
May friendships with thee as a brother be auspicious to us, O Agni, among the gods. May that be our navel, in the seat, in the same udder.
O Agni, O son of power, thy face shines auspiciously near, like that of the sun. Bright to see, it is seen even at night — undaunted, beautiful in form, the food of sight.

title: Rigveda
text:
Blow up for the singer his thought, O Agni, piercing the void with trembling, as thou art praised, O thou born mightily. What thou hast won together with all the gods, O bright one — grant us that, O greatly great one, and abundant thought.
From thee, O Agni, poems arise, from thee inspired thoughts, from thee come hymns of achievement. From thee comes wealth of varied beauty — such is the understanding for the worshiping mortal.
From thee the prize-horse, the burden-bearing, heaven-flying, victory-making one is born, of true vigor.
Thee, O immortal Agni, the mortals desiring the gods worship first among the divine — the god of the joyous tongue, yoked to enmity — with thoughts they serve the householder, the lord of the house, the blameless one.
Far from us keep ignorance, far from us distress, far from us every ill thought — so thou dost guard. Auspicious at night, O son of power, O Agni — whom even a god accompanies with welfare.
He who kindles thee, O Agni, with ladle extended, who prepares thy food thrice on the same day — may he be distinguished with glories, eminent, through thy power, O all-knowing Jātavedas.
He who brings thee fuel toiling, O great Agni, tending thy mighty face — enkindling thee, meeting evening and dawn, thriving with wealth, he is accompanied as he slays the enemies.
