Worthy of prior worship, the Maruts with their gleaming spear-points have assumed great vigour, adorned with golden ornaments on their chests; they are set in motion by well-reined, swift horses — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
You have assumed your own might as you know how; vast, great, you shine wide and far; you have measured out the mid-air (the atmosphere) with your strength — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Born together, goodly in form, growing together, these heroes have increased ever more for splendour; blazing like the rays of the sun — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Your greatness, O Maruts, is worthy of adornment, worthy of beholding like the eye of the sun; establish us also in immortality — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
You stir up the rain-laden clouds from the ocean, O Maruts; you, full of water, pour down the rain; your abundant milch-cows do not fail — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
When you yoked the dappled deer to the shafts and put on your golden mantles, you scatter all your foes, O Maruts — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Neither mountains nor rivers hinder you; wherever you have aimed, O Maruts, there you go; you encompass even heaven and earth — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Whatever is ancient, O Maruts, whatever is new, whatever is just now proclaimed, O Vasus, or is yet to be proclaimed — you are the knowers of all that — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Be gracious to us, O Maruts; do not smite us; extend abundant shelter to us; attend to our hymn of praise, to our friendship — may the chariots roll after them in glorious array.
Lead us toward better fortune, O Maruts, being praised; free us from troubles, O adorable ones; accept our oblation offered with the ladle — may we be lords of riches.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, I invoke today the bold host of the Maruts, adorned with golden ornaments and unguents, the peoples of the Maruts — even from the shining vault of heaven above.
Just as you think in your heart, so indeed have my desires come to fulfilment; those who have come closest to your invocations — strengthen them, O terrible to behold.
Like a bountiful earth struck and stirred, she comes exhilarated toward us; like a bear, O Maruts, is the impetuous force of you, mighty and wild, like a fearsome bull.
Those who cast down with their might as effortlessly as cows that are hard to yoke — with their courses they dislodge even the stone, the sky-reaching mountain, the hill.
Rise up now, being sprinkled with their praises; I call the most abundant, unprecedented gift of the Maruts as one calls a release of cattle.
Harness the tawny mares to the chariot; harness the red steeds to the chariots; harness the swift bay horses to the yoke for drawing — the best bearers to the yoke for drawing.
And that victorious tawny (steed), roaring loudly, has been set here as the visible one; let him not delay long in your courses, O Maruts — urge him forward in the chariots.
We now call hither the chariot of the Maruts, desirous of fame — the chariot on which the two worlds (heaven and earth), bearing beautiful sounds, have stood together among the Maruts.
I call hither that host of yours, glorious in the chariot, impetuous and worthy of praise — that host in which the well-born, fortunate, bounteous one is magnified together among the Maruts.
Come, O Rudras, together with Indra, in accord, on your golden chariots, for our well-being; this prayer from us reaches out to you, like a thirsty man's (longing) for a spring of water from heaven.
Bearing axes and lances, wise, with good bows, furnished with arrows and quivers — you are well-horsed, with good chariots, sons of Pṛśni, with fine weapons, O Maruts; come beauteously.

title: Rigveda
text:
You shake heaven and the mountains to give wealth to the worshipper; the forests bow down at your passage from fear; you agitate the earth, O sons of Pṛśni — when for glory you fierce ones yoked the dappled deer.
The Maruts with the lustre of the wind, clad in rain-garments, equal and well-formed like twin Yamas, with tawny horses, with reddish-brown horses, spotless, swelling in their bodies, vast as the sky in their greatness.
Adorned with many drops, gleaming with unguents, munificent, terrifying to behold, of inexhaustible bounty — well-born by nature, golden-chested, rays of heaven, they have partaken of the immortal name.
The spears on your shoulders, O Maruts, the strength and the power deposited in your arms — manly vigour on your heads, weapons in your chariots — all splendour has been wrought upon your bodies.
Grant us, O Maruts, wealth rich in cattle, rich in horses, with good chariots, with excellent heroes, brilliant in beauty; make our praise renowned, O sons of Rudra — may I partake of your divine favour.
Ho, O heroic Maruts, be gracious to us — O you of mighty gifts, immortal, knowing the cosmic order; truly renowned, wise, youthful, of mighty voice, loudly roaring.
Now indeed I praise this mighty host of the Maruts, worthy of fresh praise — those who powerfully draw swift-horsed chariots and rule as self-sovereigns over the immortal realm.
Praise, O wise man, this impetuous host, mighty, with rings of metal on their hands, intent on shaking, possessing magical powers, munificent — those unlimited in greatness, producing happiness, richly rewarding men.
May those who carry water come here today, all the Maruts who urge on the rain; this fire, O Maruts, that is kindled — come enjoy this, O wise and youthful ones.
You, the adorable ones, generate for the people the king Irya, fashioned by Vibhva; from you comes the fist-fighter, propelled by his arms; from you, O Maruts, comes he of good horses and brave heroes.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like spokes that are not the last, like days, they are born again and again, unceasing, through their greatness; sons of Pṛśni, supreme and vigorous — the Maruts have poured forth by their own will.
When you set forth, O Maruts, with your dappled horses and firm-wheeled chariots, the waters rush along, the forests bend, the she-cattle are loosened; let the bull (thunder) roar in the sky.
The earth spreads wide at their passing; as a nursing mother their might shakes the earth like its own womb; they have yoked wind-swift horses to the shaft, and the sons of Rudra have made rain their sweat.
Ho, O heroic Maruts, be gracious to us — O you of mighty gifts, immortal, knowing the cosmic order; truly renowned, wise, youthful, of mighty voice, loudly roaring.
Your swift scout has run forth to give good fortune; I bring forward with a hymn the cosmic order for heaven and earth; they bathe their horses, they cross the dust (atmosphere), they loosen themselves after their own lustre with their streams.
The earth trembles from their abode through fear; like a full ship she drifts, shaking as she goes; visible from afar, they who illumine with their flashes — these heroes have striven in the great assembly.
Like the highest horn of cattle for beauty, like the eye of the sun when the atmosphere is released — you stand like goodly, handsome race-horses; like young men, you heroes are observed for their beauty.
Who has reached the great deeds of you the great? Who your wisdom, O Maruts? Who your manliness? You make the earth tremble like a dust cloud when you carry gifts forward for good fortune.
Like tawny horses of the same kin, like heroes going forth to battle they have striven; like young men grown to full vigour, the heroes have grown; they dim the eye of the sun with their rains.

title: Rigveda
text:
They have no eldest or youngest, no middlemost; they have grown in greatness as those who spring up spontaneously; well-born by nature, sons of Pṛśni — O youthful heroes of the sky, come here to us.
Like birds they have flown in rows with might around the ridges of broad heaven; their horses, both kinds as they know, have shaken loose the water-veins of the mountain.
Let heaven measure out for our enjoyment; let the Dawns, rich in dew, strive together; these Maruts, praised, sons of the Ṛṣi Rudra, have shaken loose the heavenly treasure-chest.
I praise Agni with homages as self-sheltered; set in place here, may he discern our ritual act; as if going forth with prize-seeking chariots, may I prosper the hymn of the Maruts turning clockwise.
Who have taken their stand on the famous, well-seated dappled mares, O Rudras, O Maruts, in your chariots — even the forests, O terrible ones, bow down before you in fear; even the earth trembles; even the mountain.
Even the great, lofty mountain is afraid; even the ridge of heaven trembles at your roar; when you sport together, O Maruts with your spears, you rush along like converging waters.
Like choice thoroughbreds (raivatas), they have adorned their bodies with gold and with their own natures; surpassing in beauty, mighty in their chariots — jointly they have wrought greatness upon their bodies.
These, having neither eldest nor youngest, have grown together as brothers for good fortune; Rudra, their ever-young father of good works — Pṛśni, richly milking, is fair-days-giving for the Maruts.
Whether you are in the highest, O Maruts, or in the middlemost, or in the lowest heaven, O blessed ones — from there, O Rudras, take note of our oblation, O Agni, of the sacrifice which we perform.
And that which Agni and you, O Maruts, all-knowing, bring from beyond the highest ridges of heaven — be glad and shaking, O destroyers of foes, bestow abundance on the sacrificer who presses the soma.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, drink the soma, rejoicing with the Maruts who make beautiful, who hymn, who lend splendour to the host — with the purifiers, the all-enlivening, the life-promoting ones, O Vaiśvānara, together with your ancient banner.
Who are you, the most excellent heroes, who have come each singly from the most remote distance?
Where are your horses? Where your reins? How did you halt? How did you come? The seat on the back, the yoke of the two nostrils — how was it?
Behind them, urged on, the heroes spread their thighs, like women at the act of birth.
Go forth, O heroes, O young men of noble birth — as you are tempered by fire (in Agni's heat).
That which is connected with horses, and cattle, and riches of a hundred sheep — she who resounds, praised by Śyāvāśva, bestows the hero's arm's strength upon him.
Moreover a woman more vigorous than a man may be more wealthy — from one who is not devoted to the gods and lacks true bounty.
She who discerns the exhausted man, the thirsty man, the eager man — she turns her mind toward the gods.
And yet surely no man who is unpraised — so says the niggardly Paṇi — he alone is equal to Vairadeva (the hero's reward).
And a young exhilarated woman came running toward Śyāva's path; the two red mares have been aimed at the much-lauded Purumīḍha, at the inspired poet of long-enduring fame.
He who gave me a hundred milch-cows as Vaidadaśvi gave — their munificence is like a crossing (of the flood).
Those who carry this with their swift horses, drinking the intoxicating sweet drink — here they have established their glories.
By whose splendour the two worlds gleam as if in their chariots — like gold above in the sky.
Young is this Marut host, of impetuous chariots, unsurpassed, going beauteously, unopposed.
Who now knows where these spotless ones, born from the cosmic order, are exhilarated as they shake?

title: Rigveda
text:
You, O praiseworthy ones, are the leaders of mortal man, guiding him with your thought, the hearers at the callings for your help.
May those destroyers of foes, adorable, of manifold brilliance, turn to us with desirable riches.
O divine Ūrmī, carry this my hymn forth to Dārbhya, like a charioteer (carries) praises.
And let them say to me thus in the presence of Rathavīti who has pressed the soma: 'My desire does not go away from me.'
This Rathavīti the munificent one dwells along the cattle-rich (rivers), resting against the mountains.
By the cosmic order your firm cosmic order is covered, O Mitra-Varuṇa, where they unyoke the horses of the sun; a thousand ten (ten hundred) have stood together — that one I have seen, the best of divine forms.
That is your greatness, O Mitra-Varuṇa — the (cows) standing motionless have been milked (like waves) by the days; you two swell all the streams of the heavenly well; one wheel (of the sun) has rolled after you two.
You have upheld the earth and heaven with your greatness, O Mitra and Varuṇa, kings; you cause the plants to grow, you cause the cows to flow with milk; you who give swiftly, send forth the rain.
May the well-yoked horses bring you hither; may (the reins of) whichever chariot come hitherward; the bright garment of ghee follows after you; the rivers flow for you from ancient times.
Following and increasing the famed, vast thought, protecting it like the sacrificial grass with the yajus formula — bowing, holding firm power, within the seat of honour, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two sit in the Iḍā-offerings.
With bloodless hands, protecting well-doers, protecting mutually — whom you two protect within the Iḍā-offerings; O kings, wielding sovereignty without anger, the two of you bear the thousand-pillared (world) together.
Golden-garmented, its pillar is of iron; it gleams in the sky like a (great) horse-born; fixed in a beautiful field, in a well-tilled land — may we win the mead of the seat (of the sun).

title: Rigveda
text:
Of golden form at the shining forth of the dawn, with its iron pillar at the rising of the sun — you ascend, O Varuṇa and Mitra, the seat of honour; from there you two behold Aditi and Diti.
The greatest shelter, which none can pierce, the flawless shelter — O munificent guardians of the world, with that help us, O Mitra-Varuṇa; may we be those who desire (victory) and who conquer.
As guardians of the cosmic order you two stand on the chariot in the highest sky, possessing the laws of truth; him whom you two, Mitra-Varuṇa, protect here — for him the sweet rain swells from heaven.
You two reign as joint sovereigns of this world, O Mitra-Varuṇa, seeing the sky in the assembly; we crave rain, your bounty, and immortality; the thunders roam across heaven and earth.
Joint sovereigns, mighty, bull-like, lords of heaven, omniscient Mitra-Varuṇa, masters of the earth — you two take your stand with brilliant clouds and the roar; you cause the sky to rain by the māyā of the Asura-lord.
Your māyā is established in the sky, O Mitra-Varuṇa; the sun moves as the brilliant weapon of light; him you hide in the sky with cloud and rain; the drops of Parjanya rich in sweetness roll on.
The Maruts yoke the chariot for beauty and ease, like heroes in the quest for cattle, O Mitra-Varuṇa; the brilliant thunders roam across the regions; O joint sovereigns of heaven, sprinkle (the earth) with milk.
A speech nourishing and full of refreshing rain, brilliant and full of gleam — Parjanya speaks it well, O Mitra-Varuṇa; the Maruts clothe the clouds with their māyā; cause the pure, reddish sky to rain.
By the cosmic law, wise Mitra-Varuṇa, you guard the divine ordinances through the Asura's māyā; by the cosmic order you rule over all the world; you two fix in the sky the wondrous chariot of the sun.

title: Rigveda
text:
With a verse-hymn we call to you Varuṇa, the destroyer of foes, and Mitra — those two who have encompassed the solar hero (or: the good man of heaven) with their arms as if with an embrace.
Those two arms, with clear perception, going forward for the singer of praise — for your dear, intimate (grace) in all the dwellings I have continually called.
If now I might attain the path, might I travel the road of Mitra — in the shelter of this dear one, the unhurt, they have come together (found their union).
To you two, Mitra-Varuṇa, may I offer the highest (praise) with a hymn; for in the abode of the bountiful ones you strive in rivalry with the praisers.
Mitra with his bright flames, and Varuṇa, (come) to our common seat; in the abode of the bountiful ones and of your friends, for increase.
You two bear among those, O Varuṇa, sovereignty and great might; make wide for us for the winning of prizes, for wealth, for well-being.
For me at the shining forth of the dawn, in the divine field, with the gleaming cattle — like pressed soma, O heroes, come running with (your) hands and feet, you two bearing the worship-face (or: the face that does not worship).
He who perceives is of good insight; let him speak to us of the divine realm — he whose prayers the visible Varuṇa or Mitra delights in.
Those two are kings of greatest lustre, of most far-reaching fame; those two lords of the good who increase the cosmic order, who possess the cosmic order, in every generation.
Coming to you two for help, I invoke together the ancient (prayers) in your company; O you of good horses and clear perception, for the giving forth of prizes.
Mitra wins even from distress a broad path to dwell; for there is the good favour of Mitra who rushes forward, for the worshipper.
May we be in the shelter of Mitra, the most widely renowned; sinless, with your help, those who have Varuṇa's protection entire.

title: Rigveda
text:
You two, O Mitra, restrain this people and lead it together; do not pass over the bountiful; in your protection, let us not come to harm, of our seers — rescue (us).
Recognize these two gods of noble will, O mortal, the devourers of enemies — render homage to Varuṇa, fashioner of Order, for his great, benevolent bounty.
For those two hold sovereignty that cannot be turned aside, sovereign lordship rightly exercised; and in accordance with their ordinances, the human realm has been established — like heaven made visible.
We seek your wide chariot-track for these chariots of yours, O you two; we contemplate the excellent praise of the oblation-giver, firmly, with hymns.
For ye two, O poets of wonder, with the citadels of discernment, perceive the peoples by the banner — ye whose wisdom is purified.
That Truth is vast and lofty, the glory of the seers: these two, speeding freely, pour themselves broadly across in their courses.
When, O Mitra, with swift-eyed vision, we and the inspired ones strive toward the two of you in your vast sovereignty, abundant in paths.
Truly, so it is — O ye Ādityas, ye two gods who give accomplished worship greatly: O Varuṇa, O Mitra, O Aryaman, ye hold the most exalted sovereign power.
When, O Varuṇa and Mitra, ye take your seats upon the golden throne — sustainers of the peoples, devourers of enemies — guide your benevolence hither.
For all-knowing Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman follow all the divine ordinances as if by steps, and guard the mortal from harm.
For these three are truthful, touching the cosmic Order, possessors of Ṛta among every tribe; they are of good guidance and good gift, and even out of distress they make wide paths.
Who now among those praised by Mitra, or Varuṇa himself, is dear to your persons? This prayer seeks you two — the prayer of the Atris seeks you two.

title: Rigveda
text:
Sing forth to Mitra and Varuṇa with the voice of the inspired seer; ye two of vast dominion uphold the great Truth.
Co-sovereigns whose womb is the sacred ghee — both Mitra and Varuṇa — gods renowned among the gods.
Grant us of the earthly and the heavenly great wealth — your sovereignty among the gods is mighty.
They guard the Truth with Truth and hold swiftly the active discernment; these two gods, free of treachery, grow in greatness.
Lords of the rain-sky and of the streaming waters, lords of the bounteous stream — they occupy the lofty throne.
Three luminous realms, O Varuṇa, and three heavens and three spaces of mid-air, O Mitra, ye two sustain; waxing ever greater, ye guard the sagacity of the warrior, upholding the tireless ordinance.
Waters abundant in refreshment are your cows, O Varuṇa; rivers sweet with honey yield themselves for you, O Mitra; three bulls stand, seminal and brilliant, sowing seed for the three spheres.
At dawn I call loudly upon divine Aditi, and at midday when the sun has risen; O Mitra-Varuṇa, I entreat for wealth, for full welfare, for health and bliss for my offspring and my descendants.
You two, O Ādityas, sustain the shining space of the mid-region and likewise the heavenly and earthly realms — not even the immortal gods infringe upon your fixed and steadfast ordinances, O Mitra-Varuṇa.
For the protection of you two is indeed very great and manifold, O Varuṇa — now, O Mitra, may I win your benevolent grace.
May we who are free of treachery rightly obtain nourishment from you two for our sustenance — may we be your Rudras.
Protect us, O Rudras, with your guards, and defend us — you who give excellent protection; may we overcome the Dasyus with our bodies.
O two of wondrous power, may we not suffer with our bodies the affliction of yakṣma-disease, not by a remaining ailment nor by a spreading one.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come to us, O devourers of foes, Varuṇa and Mitra, with great might; approach this pleasing sacrifice.
For ye two, O Varuṇa and Mitra, rule as all-seeing sovereigns; as lords, cause our thoughts to overflow with fullness.
Come to us here, to the soma-presser who makes offerings, O Varuṇa and Mitra, to drink of this soma.
To Mitra and Varuṇa we call with hymns in the manner of Atri; sit ye down upon the barhis-grass for the drinking of soma.
By your ordinance ye are of steady abode, by your law making men well-yoked; sit ye down upon the barhis-grass for the drinking of soma.
May both Mitra and Varuṇa delight in our sacrifice for the attainment of our wish; may they sit upon the barhis-grass for the drinking of soma.
Whether today ye are in the far distance or near at hand, O Aśvins; whether among the many, O ye who give many boons, or come here from mid-air —
Here now, these two most manifold, bearing many marvels — I approach the two unimpeded ones for the granting of the boon; I call the two most powerful for enjoyment.
A marvelous form for form's sake ye have fashioned, and the wheel of the chariot ye have set in motion; ye two fly around the yokes and ages of men with greatness across the spaces.
That is accomplished by you, and all that is praised of you two; though born differently, ye two, free of blemish, have come together as kinsmen to us.
When Sūryā mounts your swiftly gliding chariot always — the ruddy birds around you two, and the radiant sunshine, clothe you.
For you two, O heroes, Atri perceives with a benevolent spirit; the spotless warmth that the Nāsatyas stir with their lips — he busies himself with that.
The mighty, tall steed of yours is heard in your courses, ever onward; when by his marvels the Atri turns you Aśvins back, O heroes.
O Rudras who delight in sweetness, a honey-rich stream clings to you, overflowing; when ye two carry across the ocean, the ripe food-gifts they bring to you.

title: Rigveda
text:
Truly indeed, O Aśvins, they call you two bringers of joy; in your course ye are most called upon in the course, and in the course ye are most merciful.
May these sacred utterances be most blissful and strengthening for the two Aśvins — these that we have fashioned as craftsmen fashion chariots; we have spoken the great homage.
Where abide you two gods, O Aśvins, today? — O you whose wealth is the mind of heaven; hear this, O two whose wealth is the bull: Atri sets himself to serve you two.
Where — where now are ye heard, O divine Nāsatyas in heaven? Toward which tribe do ye direct yourselves? Who accompanies you by the rivers?
Toward whom do ye travel? To whom do ye go? Toward whom do ye yoke your chariot? Whose sacred words do ye delight in? We are eager for your favour.
Even the city-dweller overwhelmed by water — from the city do ye gladden him for his city's sake, when he is held fast for seizure like a lion at the den of the deceitful.
From Cyavana, grown old, ye released the withered covering like a garment; when ye make him young again, the young wife's desire is fulfilled.
There is here a praiser of you two; we are in your sight for your glory; now that ye have been heard by me — come with your aids, O two whose wealth is swiftness.
Which among the many mortals has won you two today? Which inspired seer, O ye who carry the inspired ones? Which by sacrifices, O ye whose wealth is swiftness?
Let your chariot — the most eager of chariots — come, O Aśvins; the song of praise, desiring us greatly, comes among mortals.
May our repeated hymn be refreshing and sweet for you two; turn hither with keen minds and fly like eagles with swift wings.
O Aśvins, whenever ye would hear this call — your gifts are good and they mingle well for you; may these mixed offerings reach you well.

title: Rigveda
text:
The seer-praiser adorns with his hymn your most beloved chariot, the bull-like, the wealth-bearing; O Aśvins, sweet and honeyed — hear my call.
Come, O Aśvins, across all primordial ages; O workers of wonder, with golden track, most gracious, borne by the flood — hear my honeyed call.
Come to us, ye two Aśvins, bringing your treasures; O Rudras with the golden track, delighting in it, O ye whose wealth is the swift steed — hear my honeyed call.
On your chariot, O two whose wealth is the bull, the song of excellent praise is set; and the tall beast bears you two nourishment and wonderful forms — hear my honeyed call.
Awake in mind, swift in the chariot, ye who hear the call — with swift wings ye two Aśvins came down to Cyavana who was without deceit — hear my honeyed call.
May your steeds, O heroes, yoked by thought, dappled in form, carry you two for the drinking, together with your graces, O Aśvins — hear my honeyed call.
Come here, O Aśvins, O Nāsatyas, do not miss the mark; even through the hostile one's domain, travel around, ye inviolable — hear my honeyed call.
At this sacrifice, O inviolable lords of beauty, the praiser who seeks your aid and who lauds you — both of you Aśvins, do ye adorn him — hear my honeyed call.
Dawn has come, with gleaming cattle; Agni has been set in the proper season; your chariot has been yoked, O ye whose wealth is the bull, O workers of wonder, immortal — hear my honeyed call.
Agni blazes forth at the face of the Dawns; the god-seeking voices of the seers have risen up; come now hither with your chariot, O Aśvins, toward the gharma-vessel that has been made full.
Ye do not violate what is prepared; come now most swiftly, O Aśvins, praised here; at the approach of the day come for our protection, and be most beneficent in return to the sacrificer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come also at cow-gathering time, at the morning of the day, at midday when the sun has risen; by day and by night with most blissful protection — now the time for drinking, O Aśvins, has been extended.
This is indeed your ancient station, your home; these are the houses, O Aśvins, this the dwelling; come to us from the great heaven, from the mountain, from the waters, bringing refreshment and strength.
May we go together with the new protection of the two Aśvins, the joy-bringing, of excellent guidance; bring us wealth and heroes; O immortals, bring all good fortunes.
Worship first these two who travel at dawn — before the vulture, may the ruddy ones drink; for it is at dawn that the two Aśvins establish the sacrifice; the poets who have the first share proclaim it.
Worship the Aśvins at dawn, urge them on; at evening there is no sacrifice unaccomplished by the god-seekers; even another than us worships and is distinguished; each earlier sacrificer gains the better prize.
Of golden skin, honey-coloured, dripping ghee, bearing food-gifts, your chariot rolls forward; swift as thought, O Aśvins, racing like the wind, with it ye two pass over all adversities.
Whoever has served the two Nāsatyas most and has obtained the least in the division of food — may he nourish this man's offspring with toils; may he who shines not upward always overcome.
May we go together with the new protection of the two Aśvins, the joy-bringing, of excellent guidance; bring us wealth and heroes; O immortals, bring all good fortunes.
Come hither, O Aśvins, O Nāsatyas, do not fail to come; fly down like swans toward the pressed soma.
O Aśvins, like two antelopes, like two wild oxen following the pasture — fly down like swans toward the pressed soma.
O Aśvins, O ye whose wealth is speed, delight in the sacrifice for the granting of the boon; fly down like swans toward the pressed soma.

title: Rigveda
text:
When Atri, sliding down into the chasm, called to you, like a woman in need imploring — ye came with swiftness even rivalling a falcon, O Aśvins, with most blissful freshness.
Open wide, O lord of the forest, like the womb of a woman about to give birth; O Aśvins, hear my call and release Saptavadhri.
For the frightened, imploring seer Saptavadhri — by your miraculous arts, O Aśvins, ye split and opened the tree.
As the wind stirs the lotus-pond on every side, so let your embryo stir; let the ten-month child come forth.
As the wind stirs, as the forest stirs, as the ocean stirs — so stir and come forth, O ten-month child, together with the after-birth.
The boy who has lain ten months upon the mother — let him come forth alive, unharmed, alive, from her who is living.
Awaken us today, O Uṣas, possessor of heavenly light, to great wealth — as indeed thou hast awakened us before, O thou of true glory, of airy swiftness, nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
She who shone forth in good guidance, in the pure chariot, O daughter of heaven — that same one shine forth, and more powerfully, O thou of true glory, of airy swiftness, nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
She who has been good, the treasure-bearer — let her shine forth today, O daughter of heaven; the one who shines more powerfully, O thou of true glory, of airy swiftness, nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
They who, the priest-officants, laud thee with hymns, O Uṣas of brilliant light — with gifts, O one rich in gifts, of good glory, holding bounty, of excellent bestowal — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
Even if these your companies veil themselves for the winning of bounties, even so the worshippers around have laid up unwithering largess from those who give — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.

title: Rigveda
text:
Place, O Uṣas, rich in gifts, heroic fame among these patrons of ours — the liberal ones who have bestowed on us unwithering treasures — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
Bring to those great brilliance and fame, O Uṣas rich in gifts — the patrons who have granted us treasures in horses and in cattle — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
Bring also to us refreshments rich in cattle, O daughter of heaven; bring them together with the rays of the sun, with the bright, blazing radiances — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
Shine forth, O daughter of heaven; do not delay or thin out your works too long; lest the sun with his ray scorch thee like a thief or a foe — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
This much thou knowest, O Uṣas, or more than this thou deservest to give — thou who, O brilliantly bright one, shining for the praisers, dost not perish — nobly born, O Uṣas rich in horses and vigour.
The brilliant-coursed, the great, established in truth, possessing the cosmic Order, rosy-complexioned, shining wide — the divine Dawn, the bringer of heavenly light: the inspired seers sing to her with their thoughts.
She, the visible, awakening the people and making the paths easy to travel, goes in front; lofty-charioted, the great Uṣas who pleases all extends the light at the front of the days.
She, yoked with ruddy cattle, without stumbling has made wealth without failing; the goddess who chisels the paths for well-being, much praised, all-desired, shines forth.
She becomes the radiant one, wearing her double mantle, revealing her body in the east; she follows the path of the cosmic Order rightly, like one who knows it well; she does not confuse the directions.
She, brilliant like a pure body that has been known, as if bathed upright, has stood forth for our sight; pushing away enmities and darknesses, Uṣas, the daughter of heaven, has come with her light.

title: Rigveda
text:
She, the facing daughter of heaven, like an auspicious woman releases her activity toward men; unfolding the desirable gifts for the sacrificer, the young woman restores the light as it was before.
The inspired seers yoke the mind and yoke the thoughts of the great, inspired, omniscient one; he alone, the knower of right courses, distributes the priestly offices — great is the celebration of the god Savitṛ.
The seer-poet releases all forms; he has impelled good fortune for bipeds and quadrupeds; Savitṛ the Adorable has surveyed the vault of heaven and shines brilliantly following the path of Uṣas.
Following whose procession other gods have gone, impelled by the greatness of the god with power; he who measured out the earthly realms — that vigorous Savitṛ, the god, with his greatness.
And thou, O Savitṛ, goest to the three luminous realms, and thou art joined with the rays of the sun; thou goest around the night on both sides; and thou becomest Mitra, O god, by thy laws.
And thou alone hast command of the impulse to motion, and thou becomest Pūṣan, O god, by thy courses; and thou reignest over all this world of beings — Śyāvāśva has obtained thy praise, O Savitṛ.
We choose that boon of Savitṛ, the divine bestowal; we meditate upon the most excellent, all-sustaining, swift portion of the Bhaga.
For of this Savitṛ who is more self-resplendent, no one diminishes any dear thing, no one diminishes his self-sovereignty.
For he — Savitṛ the Bhaga — impels his treasures toward the worshipper; that brilliant portion do we seek.
Today, O god Savitṛ, impel for us good fortune with offspring; drive away the evil dream.
All adversities, O god Savitṛ, drive away; what is auspicious, that impel toward us.
At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, for the sinless Aditi, may we meditate upon all desirable things.

title: Rigveda
text:
Today with our well-spoken hymns we choose the lord of all gods, the lord of good men, Savitṛ of true impulse.
He who goes before both days — the day and the night — without faltering: the god Savitṛ of excellent intelligence.
He who makes all these beings hear by his sound, and impels them onward — that is Savitṛ.
Speak toward the mighty one with these songs; praise Parjanya with homage, seek to please him; the bull who cries aloud, who grants life swiftly, places his seed as an embryo in the plants.
He smites the trees and smites also the demons; all the world is afraid before his great weapon; even the guiltless flee before the bull's power, when Parjanya, thundering, smites the evil-doers.
Like a charioteer lashing horses with the whip, he makes visible his messengers of rain; from afar the roarings of a lion arise when Parjanya makes the rain-cloud.
The winds blow forward, lightnings fly down, plants rise up, heaven swells; nourishment is born for the whole world when Parjanya fertilises the earth with his seed.
At whose ordinance the earth bends down, at whose ordinance hoofed animals tremble, at whose ordinance the plants of all forms flourish — O Parjanya, grant us great shelter.
Grant us the rain of heaven, O Maruts; let the streams of the potent stallion flow forth; come hither with this thunder, O mighty one, O father, pouring down the waters.
Cry out, thunder, place the embryo; fly around with the water-bearing chariot; draw well the full waterbag downward; let the high places and the low become level.
Lift up the great bucket and pour it down; let the streams that have been released flow forward; drench heaven and earth with ghee; let there be good watering for the cows.
When Parjanya, crying aloud and thundering, smites the evil-doers, all this universe rejoices — whatever there is upon the earth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou hast poured down rain; now withhold it again; thou hast made the deserts crossable; thou hast generated the plants for nourishment; thou hast found wisdom also for the offspring.
Yes, truly so, O Pṛthivī — thou bearest the cleft of the mountains; thou who quickenest and settest the earth in motion with greatness, O mighty one.
The hymns of praise respond to thee at night with their refrains, O thou who movest everywhere; thou who shootest the obstacle forward like a neighing steed, O bright one.
Even the firm trees thou shakest with the earth through thy power; when thy rains rain down from the lightning of the cloud of heaven.
Sing forth the great, deep, beloved prayer to the sovereign Varuṇa who is widely heard — who spread the earth as a slaughterer does a hide, for the sun to tread on.
He stretched out the firmament through the forests, speed in the steeds, milk in the cows; in hearts he placed purposeful will, fire in the waters, the sun in heaven, Soma on the rock.
Varuṇa poured forth the cask whose opening turns downward through heaven, earth, and the mid-air; with it the king of all the world wets the earth like rain wetting the barley-crop.
He wets the earth and the broad sky whenever Varuṇa wishes to milk it; the mountains clothe themselves with cloud, the heroes — growing mighty — loosen their strength.
Of this celebrated Asura, Varuṇa — his great magical power have I now declared; he who, as if standing in the mid-air with a measuring rod, measured out the earth by means of the sun.
This great magical power of the most wise god — no one has dared to approach it; for the shining rivers, pouring their streams, do not fill the single ocean.
An Aryaman's man, O Varuṇa, or a friend of Mitra, or a comrade, or even an eternal brother, or a housemate, or a stranger, O Varuṇa — whatever wrong we have done to such, loosen thou that.

title: Rigveda
text:
As gamblers cheat — what wrong we have done as if in play, or what we have done that is a true transgression, or what we know not — loosen all that, O god, as if it were a loosened knot; then may we be dear to thee, O Varuṇa.
The mortal whom ye two, O Indra and Agni, both help in the battles — even the firm obstacles does he break through, like brilliant words, as Trita does.
That power which is hard to overcome in battles, which is praiseworthy in contests, which encompasses the five peoples — O Indra and Agni, we invoke that power of yours.
The mighty, powerful strength of those two bountiful ones — their sharp lightning — in the fists that are strong as wood, the slayer of Vṛtra seeks the cows.
In pursuit of the chariots we invoke you two, O Indra and Agni, lords of swift bounty, most knowing, most deserving of praise in song.
Both gods, growing in power through the days for the mortal, undeceived — even what is fitting do they set before him, like the two gods setting the portion for the steed.
Thus was the oblation offered to Indra and Agni — vigorous, pure as ghee pressed by stones; for those two establish great fame among the patrons and wealth for those who praise, nourishment for those who praise.
Let your great hymns go forth to Viṣṇu accompanied by the Maruts, born on the mountains — Evayāmarut; go forth to the troop that receives worship well, the joy-giver, the powerful, to him of the best aim, of roaring ordinance, of might.
They who were born great in greatness and who now of themselves, by their knowing, speak forth — Evayāmarut; by their will, O Maruts, that indomitable power of yours, their giving in greatness — these indomitable ones are like mountains.
They who are heard from the great heaven by their song, blazing brightly, of beautiful forms — Evayāmarut; of these, no enemy desires their assembly; they are like fires, they who have their own lightning, who shoot forward like the torrents of rivers.

title: Rigveda
text:
He of wide stride strode forth from the great, common seat — Evayāmarut; when he yoked himself on his own glorious, gleaming peaks, the strife-winner, the mighty one, goes accompanied by the men who increase his joy.
Like the roaring of thunder, the mighty bull shook you, the fierce, rushing, powerful one — Evayāmarut; by whom, victorious and going straight, those self-luminous ones, firm as rocks, golden, of good weapons, of impulse, do conquer.
Your greatness is boundless, O ye of increased might; may the fierce power protect — Evayāmarut; for ye are standers in the front battle line; standing there, ye protect from bonds; blazing like fires.
Those Rudras, of good sacrifice, blazing like fires, of great brilliance — may they protect, Evayāmarut; the earthly dwelling-place has spread out long and wide for them, at whose marches the great troops of those with wondrous power gather.
Without enmity, O Maruts, find a path for us; O Evayāmarut, hear the call of the singer; share ye in Viṣṇu's great energy — like a charioteer skilled in craft, drive enmities far away from us.
O worthy of worship, go to our sacrifice which is beautifully completed; O Evayāmarut, hear the call of the unharmed one; being like the greatest mountains in the sky, may ye, the all-knowing ones, be hard to seize and restrain the bonds.
For thou, O Agni, wast the first to take thought of this hymn, and becamest the wondrous Hotṛ. Thou, O bull, hast made thy strength hard to overcome, thy might for every might, to be with every might.
Then the Hotṛ, most worthy of worship, sat down in the seat of Iḷā, driving refreshment forward and being praised. Men devoted to the gods followed thee, the first, with minds fixed on great wealth.
Like a herd following one who goes with many cattle, the wakeful ones followed the wealth in thee. Agni, the shining, the visible, the great, endowed with fat, shining every day.

title: Rigveda
text:
Seeking with reverence the footstep of the god, the glory-seeking ones obtained unfading fame. They assumed the sacred names; at thy auspicious appearance they made merry.
The settlements on earth magnify thee; the riches of the people on both sides magnify thee. Thou becamest a protector to be remembered at the crossing; father and mother art thou always to human beings.
Worthy of worship, he is dear in the settlements; Agni the Hotṛ, the joyous, the most worship-worthy, has sat down. We would sit with bent knees before thee who shinest in the house, with homage.
Thee, O Agni, the new one, we implore, we who have good thoughts and seek thy grace, longing for the gods. Thou, O Agni, hast led the clans, shining with the great light of heaven.
The seer of the clans, lord of the enduring peoples, the impeller, the bull of the human tribes — him who urges forward, who drives on refreshment, the purifying, resplendent Agni, the adorable bestower of riches.
O Agni, that mortal has sacrificed and toiled, who has attained to thee with fuel and gift of oblation — whoever knows the offering round about with reverence, all desires that one obtains, aided by thee.
For thee in return we would do service greatly, for the great one, with homages, O Agni, with fuel and with oblations. O son of strength, we who know, with hymns and songs of praise, would come to thy auspicious gracious thought.
Thou who hast stretched out both world-halves with thy brilliance, and who art the rescuer that seeks fame through praises — with great, vigorous, shining prizes, O Agni, shine forth more widely upon us.
Always kindle for us, O Vasu, manly gifts; much cattle for our offspring and our descendants. May many refreshments, great, far from evil, auspicious glories of good renown be ours.
O Agni, O king, through thee the many, many riches and the abundant wealth: may I obtain thy store of goods. For many desirable things are in thee, O much-desired Agni; wealth for the worshipper is in thee, O king.

title: Rigveda
text:
For thou, O Agni, rulest over glory as Mitra over a principality. Thou, O all-beholding Vasu, nourishest fame like nourishment.
Thee verily do the tribes implore with sacrifices and with hymns. To thee comes the vigorous one, the wolf-free, cleaving through the air, all-beholding.
With united desire, the men of heaven kindle thee, the banner of sacrifice — when that human folk, longing for thy grace, offers oblation at the rite.
The mortal who prospers through thought for thee, O liberal giver, and who toils — he crosses with the help of the great heaven, even as one crosses enmity and distress.
The mortal who with fuel attains the sharpened oblation to thee — O Agni, he nourishes a dwelling full of abundance, for a hundred autumns.
Thy fearsome smoke rolls up and is spread bright in the sky. Like the sun with its brilliance, thou shinest gracefully, O Pāvaka.
Verily thou art to be praised in the settlements, thou art our beloved guest — delightful, to be cherished as a homestead, to be saved as a son.
For by wisdom in the trough thou art anointed, O Agni, a vigorous one capable of deeds — like a house with its own realm going everywhere, like a swift horse easy to call, a young one.
Thou, O Agni, dost consume even those unshaken things, like a beast in a pasture. For, O ageless one, the skillful ones cut the forests that are thy abode.
For thou goest as Hotṛ of those performing the rite, in the house of the clans. Grant prosperity, O lord of the clan; be pleased with the oblation, O Aṅgiras.
O Agni, friend-great one, tell the gods of the good will of the two world-halves toward us. Bring welfare, a good dwelling for the men of heaven; may we cross over hatreds, distresses, and evils — may we cross them, cross them with thy protection.
O Agni, he will dwell who is the guardian of Order, born of Order; he who is devoted to the gods and yearning for thee attains wide light. That mortal whom thou, O god, together with Mitra, and Varuṇa in unison, guardest from trouble with thy sharp power.

title: Rigveda
text:
He has sacrificed with sacrifices, toiled with labors, and presented gifts to Agni of the prospering gate. Thus indeed neither dishonor among the glorious, nor distress, nor arrogance overtakes that mortal.
His appearance is sinless like the sun, fearsome when his flaming thought comes. His host does not neigh; yet this forest-dweller, pleasant in any dwelling, cannot be restrained by night.
His great form moves even where sharp, blazing with its mouth like a horse tossing its jaws. Lolling his tongue as he goes, like an axe he is about to set fire to the wood, like a metal-worker he makes it run.
Like a shooter he has set himself in place, ready to shoot; he sharpens his gleam like the edge of iron. He who has a wonderful banner, the fire-stick that cannot be contained by night, like a bird swiftly alighting with swift flight of wings.
He, the great friend, covers himself against the dawns like a singer, and glitters with his flame. The ruddy immortal one who by night, the ruddy one who by day guides men — the immortal ruddy one who by day guides men.
His worshipper bellows forth newness like the sky; the bull, the glittering one, has bellowed in the plants. He who goes with glowing course like sunlight in his path fills both world-halves with wealth, making them good consorts.
He who flashes with his own energies like lightning, whether with refreshments or with united rays — or who has fashioned the troop of the Maruts, blazed like a skillful artisan, fierce and impetuous.
As thou, O Hotṛ, hast sacrificed to the gods with the sacrifices of Manu, O son of strength — so do thou today, O Agni, sacrifice to those same gods for us equally, desiring the desiring ones.
May Agni, the far-shining, worthy of praise, perceptible like the morning sky, grant us comfort who knows all things. He who is all-living, immortal among mortals, who rises at dawn, who is a guest — Jātavedas.

title: Rigveda
text:
The skies wonder at his mightiness; he wears radiances like the bright sun. He who ageless and purifying fills all things, who shatters even the ancient things of the rock.
For the praiseworthy one, the son, art thou; the fire-worshipper: Agni by birth has made food his seat. Be thou an energy-winner and grant us energy; like a king who subdues the enemy, mayst thou dwell within us without wolves.
He who keeps sharpening his teeth and consumes the obstructing food; like Vāyu he surpasses all nights as sovereign. May we overcome the adversaries of thy commanded ones — he moves around like a swift horse falling and flying.
Like the sun with its luminous rays, O Agni, thou hast stretched out both world-halves with brilliance. The brilliant night-flame guides around the darknesses; like Auśija, flying on his path of flame.
Thee we have chosen as the most joyful with rays of song — hear us greatly, O Agni. With strength, like Indra; the most manly ones fill thee as a divinity, like Vāyu, with bounty.
Now, O Agni, with the wolf-free paths of welfare, go before us for riches; lead us across distress. Bestow that blessing on the generous patrons who praise thee; may we rejoice a hundred winters with good heroes.
I call for you the youthful son of strength, the truthful of speech, youngest in thoughts — he who fills riches as the wise one, the all-desirable one, the much-desired, the blameless.
In thee are the treasures, O Hotṛ of the great banner; the adorable ones have stirred at evening and at morning. In thee as in earth all the worlds, all good fortunes, have been placed — in thee the purifying one.
Thou hast sat of old in these settlements; by wisdom thou becamest the charioteer of desirable things. From there, O Jātavedas, thou who knowest, fillest the worshipper with riches, in succession one after another.

title: Rigveda
text:
Whoever from afar attacks us, O Agni, whoever among those near, O great friend, would harm us — with thy own ageless bulls, O most burning one, burn him, thou who hast burning power.
He who has served thee with sacrifice, with fuel, with hymns and praises, O son of strength — that one among mortals shines, O immortal wise one, with wealth, with glory, with fame.
Do that swiftly when set in motion, O Agni; drive away the rivals with strength, O powerful one. What is praised by thee by days and night with words — be pleased with that, with the singer's hymn that resounds.
May we obtain that desire, O Agni, with thy help; O giver of riches, may we obtain wealth with good heroes. May we obtain vigour while winning vigour; may we obtain thine ageless and undying glory.
He who desires with a new hymn, seeking a path toward the son of strength, with sacrifice — goes to the wood-cleaving one, dark-hued by night, the shining divine Hotṛ who delights in the feast.
The youngest, the white one, the thunderer standing in the luminous sphere, resounding with ageless ones — he, the purifier, the most abundant Agni, follows all the wide and many things consuming them.
Thy flames driven by wind, O Agni, move hither and thither, the bright ones of the pure. The immensely anointed, divine, nine-fold ones overpower the forests, boldly breaking them.
Thy bright, pure, shining ones — like horses let loose — shear the earth. Then thy whirling brightness shines widely, as thou passest over the ridge of the dappled one.
Then the tongue of the bull flies forward like a thunderbolt hurled, fighting among the cows. Like the attack of a hero, the conquest of Agni — the fearsome, hard to restrain — devours the forests.
With thy radiance thou hast boldly stretched out the earthly expanses of the great piercing one. Drive away the fearful things with thy forces; wishing to win, consume the rivals.

title: Rigveda
text:
O brilliant one, O brilliant-dominioned one — the most brilliant, the giver of strength — grant us the brilliant, inspiring wealth, great, with many heroes; join to the singer who praises thee with brilliant praises.
The gods generated in the mouth the vessel: Agni Vaiśvānara, born in truth, the head of heaven, the fire-stick of earth — the wise one, the universal king, the guest of peoples.
The gods celebrated in unison the great invocation: the navel of sacrifices, the seat of riches — Vaiśvānara, the charioteer of rites, the banner of sacrifice, they generated.
From thee, O Agni, the inspired sage is born who wins prizes; from thee come heroes conquering enemies. O Vaiśvānara, O king, place in us the desirable riches.
All the immortal gods celebrate thee at thy birth, as a young child. Through thy designs, O Vaiśvānara, they came to immortality — when thou didst shine for both parents.
O Vaiśvānara, O Agni, none has ever defied those great ordinances of thine — when at birth in the lap of both parents thou didst find the banner for the courses of the days.
The ridges of heaven have been measured out by the eye of Vaiśvānara, by the banner of the immortal. On the very summit of that one, above all the worlds, seven streams have spread like branches.
He who of good insight measured out the realms of air, Vaiśvānara the wise who measured out the luminous regions of heaven — who has spread around all the worlds, the unwearied herdsman, the guardian of the immortal.
Now will I proclaim the might of the vigorous, ruddy, bountiful one in the assembly — a fresh, pure thought for Vaiśvānara; as Soma streams purified, so it flows beautifully to Agni.
Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of holy ordinances, watched over the cosmic laws. Of good understanding, Vaiśvānara measured out the mid-air and with his greatness touched the vault of heaven.

title: Rigveda
text:
The wondrous Mitra-like one propped apart the two world-halves; causing them to vibrate within, he expelled darkness with his light. He spread the two cosmic bowls apart as if they were skins; Vaiśvānara assumed universal virile power.
The great ones grasped him in the lap of the waters; the peoples stood around their praiseworthy king. Mātariśvan, as messenger of Vivasvat, brought Agni Vaiśvānara hither from the distant region.
O Agni, age after age bestow ever-fresh, glorious wealth on those who praise thee in the assembly. Like a wheel's rim, O ageless king, cut down the sinner below as fire cuts down a tree with its blaze.
O Agni, maintain among our patrons the ageless, hero-rich sovereignty. May we, O Vaiśvānara, O Agni, win the prize of hundreds and thousands by thy aid.
With thy inviolable guardians, O thou worshipped one, protect our patrons, O thou who hast three stations. Guard us who have offered, and the company of givers, O Agni Vaiśvānara; carry them forward as thou art praised.
The dark day and the bright day revolve in succession, perceived by all beings through the two realms of space. Agni Vaiśvānara, being born like a king, pierced through the darknesses with his light.
I know not the warp, I know not the woof, nor what it is they weave in contest, those going to the conflict. Whose son is he here who shall speak what needs saying — one greater speaks with one who is lesser, his father.
He indeed knows the warp, he knows the woof; he speaks what needs saying in due season — he who perceived this, guardian of immortality, moving below yet seeing beyond with another.
He is the first Hotṛ; behold this immortal light among mortals. He was born firm and settled here, the immortal one, waxing great in his own body.
The fixed light is set on high for seeing; the mind, swiftest of things, flies within it. All the gods, of one mind and purpose, go forth rightly toward that single will.

title: Rigveda
text:
My ears fly open, my eye flies open; this light which was implanted in my heart blazes forth. My mind wanders far in thought — what shall I say? What shall I now contemplate?
All the gods bowed down in fear when thou, O Agni, didst stand in the darkness. May Vaiśvānara, the immortal, guard us; may he, the immortal, guard us.
Set before you in the sacrifice, at the rite going forward, the gladsome, heavenly Agni of pure praise. First with hymns — for he, the far-shining Jātavedas, will make our sacrifices auspicious.
O brilliantly faced Hotṛ, O Agni, kindled with fire among men, we honour him with the praise-song. The thoughts purified for him flow pure like clarified butter, like a shout of power as Mamatā would offer.
He has grown fat with fame among mortals, the wise man who has offered to Agni with hymns. The bright-flaming one bestows upon him wondrous aids for the winning of a cattle-pen.
He who on being born filled the two vast worlds with his far-seen radiance, making the dark path bright — even through the mighty surge of night's darkness the purifying one was seen by his flame.
Now, O Agni, with thy many-prize-bringing aids bestow wealth upon us and upon our patrons — those who surpass others in generosity and fame and in the power of heroes over men.
O Agni, rejoicing, give delight to this sacrifice which the seated oblation-offerer presents to thee. Among the Bharadvājas thou dost receive pure praise — grant the heroes their portion of vigorous sustenance.
Drive apart the two hatreds, increase Iḷā; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in heroes.
Sacrifice, O Hotṛ, urged and best fitted to sacrifice, O Agni; urge like the impulse of the Maruts. Turn hither Mitra-Varuṇa, the Nāsatyas, and Heaven and Earth for the hotraship.
Thou art our most gladdening Hotṛ, not deceitful, a god within the assembly among mortals. With thy purifying tongue, O bearer Agni, sacrifice with thy own body.

title: Rigveda
text:
For truly the most nourishing wisdom craves in thee to proclaim the birth of gods for him who praises to sacrifice. Most inspired of the Aṅgirases, when the wise singer at the rite chants the sweet meter.
Blazing brightly, O far-shining, fully pure Agni, sacrifice across the wide two worlds. Him whom the five peoples, having offered oblations with reverence, anoint as Āyu, easy to please.
I now strew the sacred grass with reverence for Agni; the ladle rich with ghee and pure praise is put in motion. The seat is established in the dwelling on earth; the sacrifice is set in place like an eye in the sun.
Favour us, O brilliantly faced Hotṛ, O Agni kindled with the divine fires. Grasping the wealth of riches, O son of strength, may we pass beyond the fence of sin.
In the midst of the dwelling, the ruling Hotṛ on the sacred grass, Agni, who pushes forward, is to be worshipped by the two worlds. He, the son of strength and guardian of cosmic order, has stretched his flame afar like the sun.
In thee, the fully pure, the adorable — sacrifice, O king; let Heaven now worship as if fulfilling completeness. Settled in three stations, swiftly like a runner's stride, sacrifice the human offerings and rich gifts.
He whose wheel blazes most sharply in the forest, who shines like one growing strong on the path striking forward — the non-deceiving, swift one is conscious in his very self, the immortal in the lowest plants.
Thus with our powers like those of heroes, Agni Jātavedas is to be praised at home. Consuming the wooden fuel, conquering by wisdom, not a lazy bull — like a father he is to be won over by sacrifices.
His flames win admiration when he freely cleaves and courses along the broad earth. He who at once breaks loose, free-running, swifter than swift — like a debt-free wanderer he shines across the desert.

title: Rigveda
text:
So thou, O Agni, kindled with all thy fires, come to our aid against him who oppresses us. Thou seekest riches and driv'st away misfortune; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in heroes.
From thee, O blessed Agni, all blessings spread like the branches of trees. At thy swift call come riches, prizes, the conquest of adversaries, the rain of heaven, and the stream of waters worthy of praise.
Like Bhaga thou dost bestow treasure for our desire; like one going everywhere thou dost rule with wondrous brightness. O Agni, thou art like Mitra of the great cosmic order, the distributor of abundant lovely wealth, O god.
He, the true lord, slays Vṛtra with his might; O Agni, the wise one carries off the prize from the miser. He whom thou, O all-knowing one, born of cosmic order, dost spur with wealth, along with the son of the waters.
The mortal who has reached thy keen edge, O son of strength, through songs, hymns, and sacrifices — he, O god Agni, assumes all desirable things; he rules with riches.
Those of wide renown and hero-rich — for heroes, O Agni, O son of strength, grant fulfilment. Thou dost make abundant cattle by thy might, and food — to the wolf, to the gracious one, to the niggard.
O eloquent one, O son of strength, flying forth for us, O Agni, grant us offspring and progeny, and the prize for us. May we attain fulfilment with all our praises; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in heroes.
The mortal who has cherished service to Agni with his devotions — truly that ancient one will choose refreshment for his protection.
For Agni is the all-knowing, Agni is the most ordaining Ṛṣi. The peoples of Manu invoke Agni as Hotṛ in sacrifices.
For men of different kinds strive for thy aid, O Agni, for wealth from the lord. The Āyus overcome the Dasyu with their observances, pressing upon the one who holds no vows.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni gives the hero, the true lord, who overcomes in battle the waters, at whose strength the foes tremble with fear at the mere sight.
For Agni, the god knowing all, rescues the mortal from reproach. He is mighty; the wealth of him who holds Agni unchecked is unchecked in the prizes.
O great friend of Mitra, O god Agni, speak to the gods for goodwill of the two worlds. Bring welfare and happy dwelling to men under heaven; may we cross over hostilities, sins, and ill ways — may we cross them, may we cross them with thy help.
Glorify with song this your guest who wakes at dawn, the lord of all peoples. He discerns heaven by birth; the pure one perpetually consumes, like an embryo, what is immovable.
Him whom the Bhṛgus well-placed, worthy of praise with his flame upward, set in the lord of the forest as Mitra — thou, O wondrous one, being well pleased with Vītahavya, dost magnify thyself day by day with praises.
Be thou the uninjured increaser of strength, O lord, overcoming the uttermost of adversaries. O son of strength, extend wide shelter among mortals to Vītahavya and the wide-famed Bharadvāja.
Glorify with pure praises your blazing guest, the heavenly man Agni, the Hotṛ of Manu, the one of auspicious rite — like an inspired singer of celestial speech, the god who carries oblations, the messenger.
He who by the grace of his purifying, inspiring flame shone on the earth like the radiance of the dawn — pressing forward in the path of Etaśa at the battle, he who in the blaze is ageless and unsated.
Kindle fire upon fire for you with fuel, serve your dear and ever-dear guest. Seek ye with songs the immortal one; for the god among gods wins the desirable thing — the god among gods wins our service.
With fuel and with song I praise the kindled Agni, the pure, the purifying, firm in front at the rite. The inspired Hotṛ, much-desired, not deceiving, the poet — we seek with goodwill Jātavedas.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thee, O immortal Agni, age after age they have established as their messenger, the bearer of oblations, the guardian worthy of praise. Gods and mortals alike, with reverence, have settled the ever-wakeful, omnipresent lord of the people.
Adorning thyself, O Agni, following the ordinances of both sides, thou travellest as the messenger of the gods through the two spaces. When we embrace thy thought and thy benevolence, then be thou our triple-sheltering, auspicious one.
We who know little would worship him of fair face, beautiful to see, well-formed, yet knowing more than the wise. Knowing all ordinances, may he sacrifice; may Agni carry forth the oblation and declare it among the immortals.
Him thou protectest and thou ferryest across, O Agni, who has reached out to thee, the inspired one, O hero, with his devotion — or the keen edge of the sacrifice, or the arousal — him thou fillest with strength and wealth.
Protect us, O Agni, from him who would injure us; protect us, O strong one, from blame. May the nourishing drink come to thee in full abundance; may the thousandfold, coveted wealth come to thee fully.
Agni is the Hotṛ, the householder, he is the king; Jātavedas knows all births. He who is most deserving of worship among gods and among mortals — may that guardian of cosmic order sacrifice for us.
O Agni, what thou dost today for the people in the rite — O Hotṛ of pure flame, for thou art the sacrificer — thou dost sacrifice by cosmic order in thy greatness, when thou existest widely. O youngest one, bear the oblations that are thine today.
For the well-set offerings are to be seen; let the two worlds establish thee to sacrifice. Aid us, O generous one, in winning the prize, O Agni; may we cross over all misfortunes — may we cross them, may we cross them with thy help.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni of fair countenance, with all the gods, sit first on the woolly seat. Lead the nest-like, ghee-filled sacrifice rightly to Savitṛ and the sacrificer.
This is that Agni whom the inspired priests churn as Atharvan did — him whom they brought, eager and unwearied, from the dark cows.
Be born for the gods' enjoyment, for complete welfare, for prosperity. Bring hither the immortal gods, the increasers of cosmic order; touch the sacrifice among the gods.
We have kindled thee great, O Agni, O householder of men, with fuel. May our domestic rites not be impeded; sharpen us with thy keen brilliance.
Thou, O Agni, art the Hotṛ of all sacrifices, established by the gods among humankind.
Do thou at the rite worship the great ones with thy gladdening tongues; bring the gods hither and sacrifice.
For thou dost know the paths and the roads to the gods in their fullness, O Agni of good understanding at the sacrifices.
Bharata invoked thee then a second time with the swift ones for blessings; he worshipped the one worthy of worship at the sacrifices.
Thou, the many desirable things, give to Divodāsa who presses the Soma, to Bharadvāja who presents the offering.
O immortal messenger, bring hither the divine folk, hearing the perfect praise of the inspired singer.
Thee, O Agni, the mortals of devout mind invoke as the god at the sacrifices for the gods' enjoyment.
The bountiful ones set forth thy visible form and thy will; may all the desiring ones take delight in it.
Thou, the Hotṛ established by Manu, the bearer in thy mouth, who knowest most — O Agni, worship the peoples of heaven.
O Agni, come hither, praised, for the feasting, for the gift of oblations; sit down as Hotṛ on the sacred grass.
Thee, O Aṅgiras, we increase with fuel-sticks and with ghee; blaze mightily, O youngest one.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou, O god, winnest for us wide, praiseworthy, vast heroic glory, O Agni.
Thee, O Agni, Atharvan churned out from the lotus, from the head of every eulogist.
Thee, the Ṛṣi Dadhyaṅ, son of Atharvan, kindled — thee the slayer of Vṛtra, the breaker of strongholds.
Thee, the bull of the paths, the most destroyer of the Dasyu, the winner of spoils in battle after battle, Pāthya kindled.
Come now; I would speak other words to thee, O Agni. With these drops of Soma grow great.
Wherever thou dost place thy mind and the higher power, there thou makest thy seat.
No one has diminished thy abundance in the world of the half-circle dwellers, O lord. Yet thou dost win our service.
Agni of the Bharata clan has been approached — the slayer of Vṛtra, of wide perception, the true lord of Divodāsa.
For he, seeking and unconquered, bestows with his greatness all earthly riches upon the worshippers.
Thou, O Agni, like the ancient one yet made fresh, joined with new brilliance, hast spread out greatly with thy radiance.
O friends, present boldly to Agni your praise-hymn and your sacrifice; sing and chant to the ordaining one.
For he is the one who has sat for the ages of humanity as the poet-minded Hotṛ and messenger, the carrier of oblations.
Those two kings of pure vows — the Ādityas, the troop of Maruts — O treasure-giver, worship them here along with the two worlds.
Good is thy sight, O Agni; it quickens the mortal — O offspring of vigour and immortality.
Let the best by wisdom be given; today those who win thee with fair wealth — a mortal has attained pure praise.
Those aided by thee, O Agni, quickening to all life, crossing over the niggard's enmities, winning over the niggard's enmities.
May Agni go with his sharp flame against all devouring foes; may Agni win wealth for us.
Bring us hero-rich wealth, O Jātavedas, O all-seeing one; slay the demons, O one of good understanding.

title: Rigveda
text:
Protect us from distress, O Jātavedas, from him who would harm us; guard our sacred prayers, O poet.
The mortal who devotes himself to strike us from far or from near — protect us from that sin, O Agni.
Do thou, O god, drive off with thy tongue that evildoer — the mortal who seeks to kill us.
O wide-famed, mighty Agni, grant shelter to Bharadvāja, and desirable wealth.
May Agni, the seeker of wealth, smite the Vṛtras with marvellous might, kindled brightly, fed with oblations.
The father in the womb of his own father and mother, flashing forth in the imperishable syllable, settling into the womb of cosmic order.
Bring us prayer rich in offspring, O Jātavedas, O all-seeing one — O Agni, that which shines in heaven.
Towards thee, O glad one to behold, O one made strong, we who bring offerings have poured forth our songs, O Agni.
As if to the shade of the sun's heat have we come for shelter to thee, O Agni of golden appearance.
Thou who like a fierce archer, sharp-horned like a bamboo-cutter, hast broken open the strongholds, O Agni.
Him whom they bear as if a new-born child, a bracelet in the hand — the Agni of the peoples, the one of auspicious rite.
Present the god, the best knower of goods, for the gods' enjoyment, O Bharatas; let him sit down in his own seat.
Bring the beloved guest newly born into Jātavedas; let the gentle householder be brought near.
O Agni, yoke indeed those good horses of thine, O god, which bear sufficiently for zeal.
Come hither to us, bring the gods hither to the offerings for the feasting, for the drinking of Soma.
Blaze up, O Agni of the Bharatas, brilliantly, flashing forth unceasingly; shine widely and blaze, O ageless one.
The mortal who would serve the god with the feast should praise Agni at the rite, the oblation-holder; he should worship with upraised hand and reverence the Hotṛ who truly sacrifices, of the two worlds.

title: Rigveda
text:
With sacred verse we bring thee the oblation fashioned by the heart, O Agni. May these be thine — the bulls, the oxen, and the cows.
The gods kindle Agni, the foremost, the most Vṛtra-slaying; by whom the goods are brought and the demons crushed, he the prize-winner.
Drink the Soma, O fierce and bold one, in relation to which thou hast pierced open the great cow-pen, O Indra, who art praised greatly. Thou who with brave arm, O bolt-handed one, hast slain all adversarial Vṛtra with thy powers.
Drink of the Soma, he who is pressed through the strainer, swift to cross over, he of the handsome cheeks, the bull of hymns, who breaks open the cow-stall, who bears the bolt, in whose team stand the bay steeds — that Indra, win the shining prizes.
So drink as of old; let it gladden thee; hear the sacred prayer, grow great with the songs. Make the sun manifest; refresh us, O thou who desirest to fill; slay the enemies, O Indra; win the cattle.
These thy exhilarations, O self-sufficient Indra, drunk and swelling, make thee brilliant. These intoxicating ones exulted in the great, sufficient, mighty, all-pervading, overpowering one.
Gladdened, by which means thou didst set free the sun and the dawn, didst shatter the firm strongholds — the great mountain surrounding the cattle, O Indra, present — thou didst drive away the immovable from its own seat.
By thy will, by those thy deeds of wonder, thou didst with thy power set the ripe within the raw. Thou didst open the firm doors for the Dawn-cows; O thou accompanied by the Aṅgirases, thou didst release the cattle from the enclosure.
By great deeds thou hast spread the wide earth broadly; thou, lofty Indra, hast braced up the heavens. Thou hast upheld the two great, ancient, divine-born mother-worlds, the two ancient mothers, the mighty ones of cosmic order.

title: Rigveda
text:
Then all the gods before thee, O Indra, established thee alone, the mighty one, for the battle. When the godless one surged against the gods, they chose Indra here, in the winning of heaven.
Then even Heaven trembled away from thy bolt in fear at thine own wrath. When Indra smote the serpent as it surged, the all-life-long one struck it down for it to lie.
Then Tvaṣṭṛ turned for thee, O great and fierce one, the bolt of a thousand points and a hundred angles. With it thou didst squeeze together the serpent, willingly restless and roaring, O thou of the Soma-strainer.
Him whom all the Maruts together strengthened, for whom a hundred buffaloes were cooked for thee, O Indra — Pūṣan and Viṣṇu, running the three streams, poured the Vṛtra-slaying, intoxicating Soma-shoot for him.
Thou didst release the great flood, the mighty mass of the rivers hemmed in all around, the wave of the waters. Following their downward course, O Indra, thou didst set the downward-flowing waters flowing toward the ocean.
Thus may the fresh sacred prayer turn towards us for protection, Indra who has done all these things — great, fierce, ageless, strength-giving, rich in heroes, well-armed, of good bolts.
Set us, O Indra, the inspired ones, toward the prize, toward fame, toward refreshment and wealth brilliant; O Indra, set the patrons rich in men among the Bharadvājas, and be renowned as in heaven, O Indra.
May we win by this means the prize set by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in heroes.
Praise him — the much-invoked Indra, who wins with overwhelming might, unresisted; with these hymns magnify the unconquerable, the fierce one who endures, the bull of the human peoples.
He is the warrior, the champion, the maker of battle-tumult, the one who meets the foe head-on; the mightily protected, roaring with Soma-juice, raining down great dust — alone he became the overwhelming one of human races, of all peoples.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou, the untamed one, alone didst crush the Dasyus and protect the peoples for the Ārya; O Indra, is that heroic might truly in thee, or is it not? Declare it clearly at the right time.
Indeed, O most overpowering one, I hold that the might of thee, the mightily born, the swift of the swift, is real and lasting; more fierce than the fierce, more powerful than the powerful, thou who art inexhaustible hast become the conqueror of the withholding.
Let that ancient friendship be ours with thee — as when speaking thus with the Aṅgirasas thou didst smash Vala; O shaker of the unshaken, O wonder-worker, thou who settest armies in motion, thou didst unlock all the doors of his fortress.
For he, the fierce one, is to be invoked through prayers, the one who wields lordship in the great overcoming of Vṛtra; he who wins offspring and progeny, he the bolt-wielder, became the one to be stretched forth wide in the battles.
By his greatness, by his immortal name, he has surpassed the births of men and flowed beyond them; by his splendour, by his strength, by his wealth, by his heroic might, the foremost of heroes has his dwelling together with them.
He who was never confused nor spoke falsely, well-remembered by name — he chose Cumuri and Dhuni as well; Indra has crushed Pipru, Śambara, and Śuṣṇa even now for the shaking and the laying low of their fortresses.
Mount thy chariot, O Indra, with its upward-flowing, vigorous, and admirable power for the slaying of Vṛtra; take the bolt into thy right hand; delight thyself and stride forward, O giver of many gifts, in thy powers.
Like fire burning a dry forest, O Indra, burn down the demon with thy weapon — like the terrible thunderbolt; he who shattered with deep and lofty force, who drove forth the path, and crushed all sin and evil.
Come hither, O Indra, with wealth along a thousand paths, O thou of great splendour, with thy many powerful prizes; O son of might, come, O much-invoked one — even now no godless one should have power over the fruits.

title: Rigveda
text:
The greatness of the great-splendoured, ancient, vigorous one has been spread through heaven and earth; he has no enemy, no match, no firm opposing stand — the mighty one whose power through many forms none can withstand.
Let that thy deed be proclaimed today — what thou didst perform when thou gavest Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva to him; thou didst sharpen many thousands against the earth, and boldly thou didst lead Tūrvayāṇa to victory.
After thee, O slayer of Ahi, O god, all the gods then exulted — the most poetic of poets; when thou didst make wide space for the afflicted, for the mortal people, for the body, while they praised thee.
Heaven and earth and the immortal gods, O Indra, opened wide to that thy might; thou who doest all, bring into being what of thine is undone — generate a newer hymn through the sacrifices.
Great is Indra, hero-like, filling the peoples, moreover doubly strong, unassailable in his powers; toward us he has grown in heroic might — wide, broad, well-wrought; may he be so through the doers of good deeds.
The divine insight itself ordained Indra for the winning of prizes — the great, the lofty, the ageless, the youthful; him who has swelled with unconquerable might, who even straightway grows without limit.
With broad, ample forearms and many rays, measure out our glories toward us; like a herdsman turning cattle into the fold at home, O Indra, turn us toward thee in the fray.
Him, that Indra, the clever one of this power — we call him here now, eager to win the prize; even as the former praisers received him, irreproachable, blameless, unscathed.
He who holds his vow firm, who gives wealth, who is magnified by Soma — he is the great lord of pleasant and noble goods; the streams of riches have come together in him along the right path, like rivers flowing into the ocean.

title: Rigveda
text:
Bring to us the strongest might, O hero, the most powerful vigour, O thou who overcomest the fierce; give to us, O lord of bays, all the splendours and the bull-powers of humanity, for our exhilaration.
That exhilaration of thine, O unconquerable battle-winner, O Indra — bring it to us welling up; by which, aided by thee, we may think ourselves victorious in the winning of offspring and progeny.
Bring to us, O Indra, the bull-like vigour that touches wealth, that swells up, that is of keen discernment; by which, with thy aids, we may gain over the enemies in battles — both kinsmen and strangers alike.
Let thy vigour come, O bull, from behind, from above, from below, from in front; let it come together toward us from all sides — O Indra, place in us the splendour that contains the light of heaven.
With heroic aids, with the most heroic, O Indra, may we win the pleasant prize through those who have great hearing; for thou art seen as the king of both kinds of wealth — bestow on us the great, solid, mighty treasure.
Him accompanied by the Maruts, the bull who has grown mighty, the unstinting one, the divine commander Indra — the conqueror of all, fierce, the giver of overwhelming might — we invoke here for our aid with a fresh hymn.
O bolt-wielder, deliver to these heroes the folk that thinks itself ever so great and among whom I dwell; for thus we invoke thee, O hero, for the winning on earth — for offspring, for cattle, for the waters.
We, with these friendships of thine, O much-invoked, may we be the higher over enemy after enemy; smiting both kinds of Vṛtras, O hero, aided by thee, may we rejoice with great wealth.
