Who are the sons of the bounteous Rudra — and now the steady one is to carry them; for the great mother knows their greatness — verily Pṛśni, the propitious one, has placed the germ.
They who do not lag behind from birth, dwelling within, purifying themselves from blemishes — when the bright ones milked out according to their pleasure, sprinkling their own bodies with beauty.
In whom there is quick milking too with this motion, bearing the bold name of the Maruts — who are not sluggish, nor dull in their greatness — not even now shall the good giver put down the fierce ones.
Those indeed are fierce, with bold armies and strength; both heaven and earth, the well-adorned, they yoke; then among those raw-powerful ones the self-luminous heaven and earth stood like a fixed stake.

title: Rigveda
text:
May your march, O Maruts, be without fault — that which even without horse or chariot goes on; without a load, without reins, traversing the sky-dust, it goes accomplishing the road through heaven and earth.
There is no restrainer nor overtaker of him, O Maruts, whom you protect in the winning of prizes; and him whom you protect in offspring, in cattle, in children, in the waters — he will split open the pen at the due time, at last under heaven.
Bring forward the bright hymn to the swift, self-strong Maruta host for the singer; those who overcome mighty powers with might — at their rites, O Agni, the earth trembles.
Blazing like the lightning of the sacrifice, shaking the thirsty, like the tongue of fire — the Maruts, whose birth is brilliant, who cannot be overpowered, are three-fold radiances, like roaring heroes.
With my invocation I seek that growing Marutic host, of blazing brilliance, the sons of Rudra; for the host of heaven, with pure wisdom, the fierce mountains like waters have contended.
O Mitra-Varuṇa, may you both, the most eminent among all the true ones, grow through these hymns; who, like a single rein, the best rulers, hold together two unequal peoples with their own arms.
This beloved thought spreads the sacred grass forward toward you two, with a reverence; come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa, O good givers, with your irresistible shelter, your protective covering.
Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, by reason of this good praise, called with a dear reverence; you two who stand at activity, like activities you unite people — even those who hear you, you govern with your greatness.
Those two, pure of lineage, prize-winning like horses — when Aditi by cosmic order bore the germ; those two who, being born great and mighty, have shone in dreadful fashion on the mortal who is an enemy.

title: Rigveda
text:
When all the gods, rejoicing in your bounty, unanimously placed dominion in you two; since you encompass even the wide heaven and earth, the spies of yours are undeceivable and unwavering.
For you two sustain dominion day after day; you two strengthen the summit like the height of heaven; the firm star and the all-divine — of those two who adorn the earth and sky, it has been established.
You two fill the capacious womb — when those who are well-laden fill the abode; the young women untouched by wind are not diminished when the all-nourishing ones spread forth the milk.
With the tongue, O wise ones, always this praise — when your true hymn of praise is found in the rite; let your greatness be that, O you who eat the oblation of ghee; may you two remove the distress from the worshipper.
When the rivals of you two, O Mitra-Varuṇa, make away with your favourite abode established for you both — neither do the gods do this by challenge, nor mortals, those without sacrifice, the watery ones — not even their sons.
When the praisers spread abroad the voice, and some, thinking them the nivids, proclaim — then we speak true praises to you; with your greatness no one contends even among the gods.
Verily in this way, O Mitra and Varuṇa, your shelter in attack has been made without decay; when the cows kicked back the swift, bold bull and yoked the virile one for battle.
Your joint hearing rises with this sacrifice, O Indra-Varuṇa, when the kusa-strewn altar is ready for worship in the manner of Manu; he who turns to you today for sustenance, for great favour, for great bounty — may he obtain it.
For you two are the best among the gods, impetuous, the mightiest of heroes, the most powerful — thus have you been; most liberal to the generous, O you of mighty vigour, vanquishers of Vṛtra by holy order, with your entire host.

title: Rigveda
text:
Praise them both, O Indra-Varuṇa, delighting, with reverent powers and with eulogies of goodwill; one smites Vṛtra with the vajra by his might, the other, the sage, attends upon the settlement of men.
When the goddesses and the men grew strong, all the gods delighting in the praise of men — from them, O Indra-Varuṇa, in your greatness you arose; O Heaven and Earth, you both became the wide ones.
He truly is the good giver, the bounteous, the upright, O Indra, who devotes himself to you two, O Varuṇa; with nourishment shall the pious one overcome his enemies, shall win wealth and men abounding in riches.
That wealth, full of goods, full of abundance, which you two, O gods, bestow on the worshipper who performs sacrifice — may that be ours, O Indra-Varuṇa, he who shatters the curses of his foes.
And may wealth come to us — your well-guarded worshippers, O Indra-Varuṇa, protected by the gods — to whom the vigour that overcomes in battles, the fame, swiftly spreads, the far-reaching one.
Now, O Indra-Varuṇa, being praised, yoke riches for us, O gods, unto great fame; even thus praising the host of the mighty one, may we cross all adversities as a boat crosses water.
Sing now a beloved song, wide-resounding, to the great sovereign, to the divine Varuṇa; he who, vast in his greatness, of mighty ordinance, shines by his wisdom undecaying as with a flame.
O Indra-Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed draught, O you of steadfast ordinance, drink this pressed, intoxicating Soma; your chariot comes to the sacrifice day by day for the delight of the gods, for drinking.
O Indra-Varuṇa, both bulls, drink your fill of this most sweetly inebriating, vigour-giving Soma; this drink has been poured out for you two among us — be seated on this sacred grass and rejoice.
With prayer and with offering I impel you both together, O Indra-Viṣṇu, to the far end of this work; take pleasure in the sacrifice, bestow riches upon us, and lead us along unharmed paths.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra-Viṣṇu, begettors of all thoughts, bowls that hold the Soma — may the hymns recited for you two be fruitful, may the praises when sung with chants thrive.
O Indra-Viṣṇu, lords of joys, of ecstasies, come to the Soma, bringing treasure; may the devotions anoint you both with their gleams, and the praises with their recitations and hymns.
May horses that overcome the foe carry you both hither, O Indra-Viṣṇu, you who rejoice together; take pleasure in all the invocations of the prayers — hear, O you two, my devotions and my hymns.
O Indra-Viṣṇu, that is worthy of wonder for you both — in the exhilaration of Soma you two have widely stridden; you have made the wide firmament, you have spread out the realms for our living.
O Indra-Viṣṇu, grown mighty with the oblation, who press forward, who receive the offering with reverence — you who pour ghee, bestow wealth upon us; you are the oceans, the bowl that holds the Soma.
O Indra-Viṣṇu, wondrous ones, drink of this sweet Soma and fill your bellies; may the exhilarating draughts come to you both — hear my devotions, hear my call.
Both of you have conquered, neither of you is defeated, neither one of you two has ever been overcome; O Viṣṇu, when you and Indra competed, you two set that thousandfold wealth flying in three directions.
Rich in ghee, the glory of all beings, the wide and broad Heaven and Earth that yield honey, beautiful in form — by Varuṇa's ordinance the two are propped apart, the undecaying ones, rich in seed.
Inexhaustible, flowing with many streams, full of milk, the two world-halves yield ghee to the pious one of pure conduct; the two shining ones, rulers of this world — pour upon us the seed that Manu established.
The mortal who offers to you two, O Heaven and Earth, O Wisdom-goddesses, for the straight stepping — he prospers; he is born forward among offspring from your ordinance; what has been poured into you two takes many forms, sharing one law.

title: Rigveda
text:
Heaven and Earth, encompassed with ghee, glorious with ghee, mixed with ghee, swelling with ghee — the wide, the broad ones, coveted by the Hotṛ priest, set foremost — them do the sages pray to for favour, for offering.
May Heaven and Earth sprinkle sweetness upon us, dripping honey, yielding honey, whose rite is honey; bearing the sacrifice and wealth, the divine ones — may they grant us great fame, food, and heroic strength.
May Heaven and Earth, father and mother, all-knowing, of wondrous deeds, swell refreshment upon us; may the two world-halves, well-disposed, bringers of good to all, pour upon us gain, food, and wealth.
The god Savitṛ of wise counsel has stretched up his golden arms for the pressing rite; the vigorous, young, skilled one moistens his hands with ghee, in the holding apart of the firmament.
May we be in the stimulation of the god Savitṛ, in the best, in the giving of riches; you who are the abundance of all the two-footed and four-footed — at their settling and at their setting forth.
With your undeceived, auspicious guardians, O Savitṛ, protect our home today; O golden-tongued one, for a new happy fortune — guard us so that no evil-speaker may have power over us.
The god Savitṛ who belongs to the house has stood up at the onset of dusk with golden hands; iron-jawed, adorable, sweet-tongued, he bestows great riches upon the worshipper.
Savitṛ of beautiful aspect has raised his golden arms up like an announcer; he has climbed the heights of heaven, of earth, he has caused whatever is enormous to fly away and made it settle.
O Savitṛ, impel good fortune for us today, and also tomorrow, day by day impel good fortune for us; for, O god, with this prayer may we be partakers of great good fortune and its abode.
O Indra-Soma, great is that greatness of you two — you two performed the great primordial deeds; you two found the sun, you two found the light, you two smote all the darknesses and the fasteners.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra-Soma, you two clothe the dawn, you two lead up the sun together with his light; you two prop heaven with a prop, and you spread apart mother Earth widely.
O Indra-Soma, you two smote the serpent that had enclosed the waters, Vṛtra — Heaven agreed with you two in this; you two set the streams of the rivers flowing and many oceans spread wide.
O Indra-Soma, you two placed the ripe within the unripe, the essence of the cows within their flanks; you two seized that bright, shining thing inside these moving ones, it being unbound within the variegated ones.
O Indra-Soma, you two have indeed bestowed a famous aid that accompanies the offspring; you two, fierce ones, have wrapped round the manly vigour for men, the vigour victorious in battles.
He who is the rock-splitter, the first-born, the upholder of holy order, Bṛhaspati the Āṅgirasa who possesses oblations; doubly strong, having preceded the hot pressing on earth — as a father, as a bull, he roars filling Heaven and Earth.
Even for a man who was seeking a dwelling-place, Bṛhaspati made a way at the invocation of the gods; smiting the Vṛtra-foes, he shatters the strongholds, conquering enemies and foes in battles, overpowering them.
Bṛhaspati won together the good things, the great cattle-pens rich in cows — this god; desiring waters and the sun, irresistible, Bṛhaspati smites the enemy with his hymns.
O Soma-Rudra, uphold the divine lordly power; may the sacrificial offerings reach you two duly; bearing the seven treasures in every house — be auspicious to our two-footed, auspicious to our four-footed.
O Soma-Rudra, drive away in all directions the disease that has entered our house; drive dissolution and misfortune far away from us — may there be prosperity and great renown for us.
O Soma-Rudra, place all these medicines for us in our bodies; release, loosen from us whatever sin has been committed that is bound in our bodies.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Soma-Rudra, of sharp weapons, of sharp missiles, most benevolent — be gracious to us here; release us from Varuṇa's snare, guard us, being well-disposed toward us.
His countenance becomes like a thunder-cloud when the armoured warrior goes into the lap of battles; conquer you with an unwounded body — may the greatness of the armour protect you.
With the bow may we win cattle, with the bow may we win battles, with the bow may we conquer the fierce conflicts; the bow renders the enemy's desire impotent — with the bow may we win all the regions.
As if about to speak, she whispers into the ear, embracing her dear friend — the bowstring stretched upon the bow twangs like a woman at the battle, carrying one across.
These two that move forward like a woman toward the battle-ground — may they, coming together, hold him on their lap as a mother holds her son; may these two bowstring-ends pierce the enemies, shooting, scattering the foes.
Father of many, many are his sons — the quiver makes a sound when it goes down into battle; bound on the back, it conquers all conflicts and the assembled arrays when the archer is urged forward.
Standing in the chariot, the skilled charioteer leads the horses forward whithersoever he desires; praise the greatness of the reins — the lines draw back the mind from behind.
The bull-handed horses make fierce battle-cries along with the chariots, striving for victory; stepping forward with their fore-hooves, they destroy the enemies, crushing the foes without retreat.
The chariot's burden — that is its name, the oblation — where the weapon is laid, where its armour is; there may we be seated beside the mighty chariot, always well-disposed.
Sweet to sit with, fathers, strength-givers, having taken refuge in hardship, powerful and deep; with brilliant armies, mighty in arrows, unyielding, rich in real heroes, broad, overcoming hosts.

title: Rigveda
text:
Brāhmaṇas, fathers, Soma-drinkers — may Heaven and Earth be auspicious and unharming to us; may Pūṣan, increaser of holy order, guard us from evil — may no evil-speaker have power over us.
A bird's feather clothes it, the animal's tooth is hers — bound with cow's sinew she flies when launched; where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant shelter to us.
O Arrow, ward off from us; may our body become stone; may Soma speak for us, may Aditi grant us shelter.
She strikes against their backs, touches their hindquarters — O horse-whip of the discerning one, urge the horses forward in the battles.
Like a serpent with its coils it winds around the arm, the bowstring repelling the dart; the arm-guard knowing all the ways of motion — may this man guard that man on all sides.
She that is painted red, with the head of the roebuck, and whose mouth is of iron — to this divine arrow, born of the seed of Parjanya, great homage.
Released, fly forth, O shaft, sharpened by Brahman prayer; fly to the enemies, strike among them — do not leave any one of these alive.
Where the arrows fly together like boys with unbound hair — there may Brahmaṇaspati grant us shelter, may Aditi grant us shelter, grant us shelter always.
I cover your vital spots with armour; may King Soma clothe you about with immortality; may Varuṇa make broad space for you, broad and wider still — may the gods rejoice following you as you conquer.
He who desires to slay us, whether one of our own or a stranger — may all the gods confound him; the sacred prayer is my innermost armour.
Men generate the praiseworthy Agni by the friction of two fire-sticks, letting them fall from their hands — him who is visible from afar, the householder, the Atharvan.
The Vasus have kindled that Agni within, well-visible, for protection from every quarter — he who is ever capable and constant in the house.

title: Rigveda
text:
Blazing forth, O Agni, shine before our dwellings with unceasing flame, O youngest one; to you, ever and again, the prizes of the contest come.
Your fires, excellent beyond all other fires, have blazed forth brilliantly, rich in heroes — there where the well-born men are assembled together.
Grant us, O Agni, through our prayer, wealth rich in heroes, a praiseworthy progeny, O mighty one — wealth which no malevolent sorcerer can overcome.
To him, the highly capable one, the youthful woman, bearing oblations, ghee-laden, comes by night and at dawn; and Aramati, seeking wealth, comes near to him.
Burn away, O Agni, all hostilities — with those heats wherewith you burned up the Jarūtha; chase away soundlessly the disease that afflicts us.
He who kindles your flame, O Agni — O Vasiṣṭha, O bright one, shining, purifying — may you be here with us through these praises.
Those mortal men, heroes following the fathers' way, who have shared in your flame in many places — may you be here, well-disposed, with us through these same praises.
Let these heroic men, in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless sorceries — those who admire my praiseworthy prayer.
May we not sit helpless among men, O Agni; may there be no childlessness and no herolessness around you; grant us houses and homes full of progeny, O householder.
The horse-possessing sacrifice ever approaches him: grant us an abode rich in progeny and in good offspring, grown great by its own birth and its remainder.
Protect us, O Agni, from the unpleasant demon; protect us from the trickery of the evil-minded, harm-seeking one; allied with you, may we overcome those who attack us.
May that Agni surpass all other fires — where the prize-winning son, strong-handed, gathers the thousand-footed, undying syllables.
That is the Agni who protects his kindler from the assailant, who rescues the sacrificer from distress — around whom the well-born heroes gather.

title: Rigveda
text:
This is that Agni, invoked in many places, whom the lord, bearing oblations, kindles together; around whom the hotr-priest goes in the sacrificial rites.
Into you, O Agni, may we pour many oblations, sovereign and constant; we two making both the bridal pair go to the wedding feast.
These most eagerly desired oblations, O Agni — carry them as the undying one toward the gathering of gods; may the sweet-smelling ones come back to us.
Deliver us not, O Agni, to herolessness; not to ill-clad poverty; not to hunger; not to demons, O lord of ṛta; mislead us not in the house nor in the forest.
Proclaim my prayers now, O Agni; pour them forth, O god, for the generous lords; may we stand in your gift; preserve us evermore with blessings.
You, O Agni, are pleasant to invoke, gladsome to behold; shine brightly, O son of strength, with fair light; may no son ever be lost from us who cling to you; may no manly hero perish from among us.
O Agni, in these god-kindled fires, proclaim not our ill-maintenance; may no evil thought of yours, however slight, O son of strength, destroy us.
That mortal is wealthy, O Agni of fair face, who pours oblations to you, the immortal; he places in the deity a treasure of goods — to him the wise patron comes asking his wish.
O Agni, knowing the great prosperity, bring ample wealth to the patrons; whereby, O mighty one, we may rejoice with undiminished life and fine heroes.
Proclaim my prayers now, O Agni; pour them forth, O god, for the generous lords; may we stand in your gift; preserve us evermore with blessings.
Be pleased, O Agni, with our kindling-wood today; blaze high, sending forth the majestic smoke of worship; touch the back of heaven with your crests and spread out together with the rays of the sun.
We will praise with our sacrifices the greatness of Narāśaṃsa of the adorable ones — those gods, of good wisdom, pure, who are the layers of prayer, who savour both kinds of oblations.

title: Rigveda
text:
We would always magnify for the sacrifice him who is praiseworthy, the mighty, highly capable lord, the truthful messenger between heaven and earth — Agni kindled by Manu after the manner of Manu.
The worshippers, carrying the offerings, kneel and strew the sacred grass in the fire with reverence; O adhvaryu-priests, cleanse the oblation while pouring — the spotted one whose back is anointed with ghee.
Wise in prayer, desiring the gods, the worshippers have thrown open the doors at the gathering of deities, eager as charioteers; the two (Dawn and Night), like two mothers licking their young, have anointed him who is one at the assemblies.
And the two great divine women — Dawn and Night — like a good-milking cow yielding milk: may those two wealthy, often-invoked, adorable ones who sit upon the sacred grass come near for our well-being.
Two inspired crafters — so I think — at human sacrifices do we invoke you both, O Jātavedas pair, to worship; make our sacrifice stand upright among the invocations; win for us the desirable things among the gods.
May Bhāratī with the Bhāratī goddesses, Iḷā with gods and men, and Agni, and Sarasvatī with the Sarasvatī beings come hither — may the three goddesses sit upon this sacred grass.
Pour that nourishing sap upon us, O god Tvaṣṭṛ, granting freely; from which is born the heroic, capable man of action, well-skilled, who works the pressing stones and desires the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release the gods; Agni the sacrificer will prepare the oblation; he himself, the true hotr-priest, shall sacrifice as he knows the births of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, blazing, together with Indra and the swift gods on one chariot; may Aditi of fair sons be seated on the sacred grass; Svāhā! — may the immortal gods rejoice.
Together, make Agni your god, together with the Agni flames — the most adorable, the divine messenger of the sacrifice — he who among mortals is the firm upholder of ṛta, of fiery forehead, ghee-fed, the purifier.

title: Rigveda
text:
He snorts like a horse at pasture, straining forward, when he steps forth from his great enclosure; then the wind fans his flame after it, and your track is black.
When your ageless flames go forth as the new-born bull, O Agni, the reddish smoke ascends toward the sky; for you, the messenger, go to the gods.
Your blazing force has spread across the earth; when it crumples dry vegetation with its jaws, your attack goes forth like a loosed army; you separate the grain with your tongue like a wondrous being.
Him, the youngest, they groom at night and at dawn like a swift horse — the men who have sharpened him; the guest kindled in his own place blazes forth, the flame of the bull who receives the oblation.
Your face, of fair visage, is beautiful to behold when you blaze brilliantly at close range like golden ornament; your power surges like the thunder of heaven — show your brilliance, resplendent as the sun.
As we would offer to Agni with Svāhā, surrounded by ghee-laden oblations — with those unlimited great powers, O Agni, protect us with a hundred iron fortresses.
Or those unassailable gifts you have for the worshipper, or those words of praise with which you rescue him who has heroes — with those, O son of strength, O Jātavedas, protect us, our patrons and our praisers.
When like a pure axe he went forth shining, glowing with his own splendid body — he who was born, longed for, from the two mothers, the wise, purifying one for the worship of the gods.
Illuminate these auspicious things for us, O Agni; may we attain to clear-minded wisdom; may all these be for those who praise and hymn you; preserve us evermore with blessings.
Bring forth for the bright, shining one, oblation and well-purified prayer for Agni — he who, moving among them with his knowledge, goes between all divine and human generations.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let him be the wise Agni, ever young, since the youngest was born from his mother; he who draws the forests together, consuming the clean food, who eats up great quantities of food forthwith.
In the assembly and army of this god whom the mortals have grasped as the white one — he who has declared the human grip to be difficult of abode: Agni has shone forth for Āyu.
This Agni, the poet, the all-knowing among the ignorant, the immortal, has been placed among mortals; may he not lead us astray here, O mighty one; may we always be well-disposed toward you.
He who has settled into the god-made womb — for by his wisdom Agni has crossed over to the immortals — him, the all-nourishing embryo, the herbs, the trees, and the earth bear.
For Agni is master of great immortality, master of giving wealth and excellent heroism; may we not sit around you, O mighty one, without heroes, without cattle, without soma.
May we be lords of the possessions to be distributed, of the spontaneous wealth, of the eternal riches; O Agni, there is no residue born of another kind — do not lead astray the path of the mindless one.
The foreign one, though pleasant, born of another womb, is not truly to be grasped — it must be thought over with the mind; yet even he returns to his home again; may the new prize-winner come to us victorious.
Protect us, O Agni, from the assailant; protect us, O mighty one, from disgrace; may the dusty path converge toward you, and with it the thousandfold wealth worthy of longing.
Illuminate these auspicious things for us, O Agni; may we attain to clear-minded wisdom; may all these be for those who praise and hymn you; preserve us evermore with blessings.
Bring forth your song to Agni the mighty, the pillar of heaven and earth; Vaiśvānara who has grown great in the lap of all the immortals, with those who keep vigil.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni is stationed in heaven and on earth; he is the leader of rivers, the bull of the standing waters; Vaiśvānara, grown great with his excellence, shines upon the human peoples.
Out of fear of you the dark peoples came, abandoning their unequal food; O Vaiśvānara, when you shone for Pūru, blazing, bursting open the enemy cities, O Agni.
Your threefold ordinance, O Vaiśvānara, O Agni, is followed by both earth and heaven; you have stretched out both world-halves with your light, blazing with your unceasing flame.
You, O Agni, the tawny, yearning hymns follow — the rushing, ghee-laden songs — calling you lord of the peoples, charioteer of wealth, Vaiśvānara, beacon of the dawns and of the days.
The Vasus have established lordly power in you; the great Mitra-friends have enjoyed your wisdom; you drove the Dasyus from their homes, O Agni, generating broad light for the Ārya.
Being born in the highest heaven, you at once guard the path like Vāyu; striding forth to generate the worlds, O Jātavedas, you bestow on offspring.
Direct that luminous refreshment toward us, O Agni Vaiśvānara, O Jātavedas — by which you fatten the bounty, O all-desired one, and give wide fame to the mortal worshipper.
Yoke for our patrons that abundant, glorious, prize-giving wealth, O Agni; O Vaiśvānara, grant us great shelter together with the Rudras and Vasus, O Agni.
I proclaim and praise the glory of the universal king, the mighty lord, the one to be extolled among the peoples — the mighty deeds like those of Indra; worshipping, I speak praise of the wood-Agni.
The seer, the beacon, the nourisher, the light of the rock — they urge forward the auspicious sovereignty of both worlds; with songs like those of the city-breaker I seek the ancient great ordinances of Agni.
The Paṇis, the knotted ones, the mumbling, the faithless, the ungrowing, the unsacrificing — Agni has repeatedly driven those Dasyus away; he made the former the latter, the non-sacrificers.

title: Rigveda
text:
I praise that Agni, the mightiest in his deeds, who by his powers made the revelling ones in the western darkness into eastern ones — him who is lord of wealth, unbowed, who tames the attackers.
He who bent down the fortifications with his weapons, who made the dawns into consorts of the noble — that youthful Agni of Nahuṣa's people, by his powers, made the clans bring tribute.
All peoples rest in his protection, seeking his goodwill with their customs; Agni Vaiśvānara, the best of both worlds, has seated himself in the lap of the father and mother.
The god Vaiśvānara has taken the deep treasures at the rising of the sun; Agni has taken from the near sea and from the far, from heaven and from earth.
I urge forward for you even the powerful god Agni with reverences, as one urges a swift horse; be our knowing messenger of the sacrifice, O measuring one who is found among the gods through his own self.
Come, O Agni, along your own paths, joyful, enjoying the friendship of the gods; making the back of earth resound with your powers, you gladly burn up all the forests with your jaws.
The eastward-directed sacrifice, the well-laid sacred grass — Agni the invoked one pleases these, as a hotr-priest; calling upon the two all-desired mothers, O youngest, kindly one, from whom you were born.
The wise, discerning men of understanding instantly produce the expert charioteer at the sacrifice; Agni, the lord of the clans, has been placed in the house — joyous, honey-voiced, master of ṛta.
The chosen carrier has sat down, the one who has come — Agni the brahman-priest, the ordainer, who sits among men; both heaven and earth nourish him, and the hotr-priest sacrifices to him, the all-desired.
These have surpassed all with their glories — those manly ones who have fashioned the prayer and the choicest thing; who, hearkening, move the clans forward, who have meditated upon this truth of mine.

title: Rigveda
text:
Now we Vasiṣṭhas implore you, O Agni, as lord of wealth, O son of strength; carry refreshment to the praisers and the generous patrons; preserve us evermore with blessings.
The king is kindled together by the people with reverences, he whose face has been offered ghee; the men press together to propitiate him with oblations — Agni has shone at the forefront of the dawns.
He has been recognized as exceedingly great — the hotr-priest, the joyful, youthful Agni of Manu; spreading out light across the earth, with the dark-rimmed wheel he has swelled among the herbs.
With what will you clothe us in excellent praise, O Agni? What self-power will you grant when sung? When shall we be lords, O good giver, winning wealth that is hard to overcome and perfect?
This Agni of Bharata is proclaimed everywhere, shining with great brilliance like the sun; he who has stood over Pūru in battles, the divine guest, blazing, has shone forth.
Let the many invocations be real in you; be well-disposed with all your flames; even when praised, O Agni, you are heard when you are hymned; increase yourself by your own body, O well-born one.
May this word, hundredfold and thousandfold, rise up doubly great for Agni; that it may be auspicious for the praisers and the household, shining, disease-removing, demon-slaying.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas implore you, O Agni, as lord of wealth, O son of strength; carry refreshment to the praisers and the generous patrons; preserve us evermore with blessings.
The wooer has awoken from the lap of the dawns — the joyful hotr-priest, the most poetic, the purifier; he sets the beacon of both kinds of beings and the oblations for the gods, wealth for the pious.
He is the wise one who bursts open the doors of the Paṇis, purifying the richly nourishing sun-beam for us; the joyful hotr-priest, the domestic one of the clans, is seen through the darkness of the nights.

title: Rigveda
text:
The faultless seer, Aditi, Vivasvat, the well-spoken Mitra, the auspicious guest to us — Agni of brilliant radiance shines at the fore of the dawns; the embryo of the waters has entered into the plants.
The praiseworthy one for you, Jātavedas has blazed undimmed through the generations of Manu; he who shines with beautiful radiance — the cows have recognized him as he is kindled.
O Agni, go on your divine embassy, unharmed, toward the gods with the brahman-made band; sacrifice to Sarasvatī, the Maruts, the Aśvins, the waters, and all the gods for the bestowal of treasure.
Vasiṣṭha, kindling you, O Agni, strikes away Jarūtha; worship the bountiful goddess for wealth; of many kinds of ritual, O Jātavedas, grow old; preserve us evermore with blessings.
Like the lover of the dawn, he has reached his broad force, flashing, shining, blazing; the bull, the golden one, the pure, shines with his light; he who urges on prayers has stirred the eager ones.
Like the sun at the dawning of the days, he has shone forth; the prayer-devotees spread the sacrifice like a thought; Agni the god, knowing all births, runs as the messenger, devoted to the gods, the most winning.
The songs and prayers, desiring the gods, go to Agni begging for wealth — to him who is beautiful to behold, of fair visage, of good form, the bearer of oblations, the unwearying one of mankind.
O Agni, bring Indra together with the Vasus, bring the great Rudra together with the Rudras; bring Aditi with the Ādityas, she who belongs to all peoples; bring Bṛhaspati with the ṛk-singers, the all-desired one.
The clans praise at the sacrificial rites Agni the joyful hotr-priest, loved by the devout, the youngest; for he has become the lord of nights and of riches, the unwearied messenger for the worship of the gods.
Great art thou, the presiding spirit of the sacrifice; without thee the immortals do not rejoice. Come hither on the same chariot with all the gods, O Agni; sit here as Hotṛ, foremost of all.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thee, the swift messenger, do the oblation-bearing men always invoke for embassy; he upon whose sacrificial grass thou, O Agni, hast sat down with the gods — for him the days become auspicious.
Thrice in the night do they discern the treasures stored within thee for the mortal worshipper. Like Manu, O Agni, worship the gods here for us; be our messenger and protector against malediction.
Agni is lord of the great sacrifice; Agni is lord of every oblation that has been made. The Vasus indeed delight in his will; therefore the gods appointed him the bearer of oblations.
O Agni, bring hither the gods to partake of the oblation; let those whose chief is Indra rejoice here. Place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.
With great reverence we have come to the youngest, who blazes when kindled in his own dwelling, the brilliantly shining one who fills the two wide worlds, who is well-fed with oblations, turned toward all sides.
He who overpowers all evils by his greatness — Agni, Jātavedas, is praised in the house. May he guard us from sin and reproach, both us who hymn him and our bountiful patrons.
Thou art Varuṇa and also Mitra, O Agni; the Vasiṣṭhas strengthen thee with their hymns. May the readily won treasures be in thee. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.
Bring forth the prayer and meditation for Agni, the all-purifying, the thought-sustaining, the slayer of Asuras; being gladdened on the sacrificial grass, like an offering brought, for Vaiśvānara, the marshaller of thoughts.
Thou, O Agni, blazing with thy flame, hast filled both worlds at thy birth. Thou hast freed the gods from malediction, O Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, by thy greatness.
When, O Agni, thou wast born, thou surveyedst all the worlds, moving freely like a herdsman among cattle, wandering everywhere. O Vaiśvānara, find the path for the brahman. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
With fuel, with invocations of the gods, with oblations to Jātavedas the divine, to the bright-flaming one — reverently we would serve Agni with our gifts.
We would tend thee, O Agni, with fuel; we would serve thee with good praise, O adorable one; we, O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, with ghee; we, O god, with oblation, O thou of auspicious flame.
Come to us with the gods at the invocation of the gods, O Agni, delighting in the vaṣaṭ-call. May we be givers to thee, the divine. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.
Into the mouth of the bountiful, the approachable one, pour the oblation — he who is to us the nearest helper.
He who has sat down over the five tribes in house after house — the wise, the householder, the ever-young.
May Agni guard our wealth and household folk on every side, and also guard us from distress.
I have fashioned a new hymn for Agni, the falcon of the sky — will he win treasure for us?
His glories are desirable to behold, like wealth with abundance of heroes, as he blazes at the head of the sacrifice.
May Agni, the most skilled in worship, the bearer of oblations, come to this vaṣaṭ-call and be pleased with our songs.
Thee, the lord of the settlement, the brilliant one, O god, we would fix in our hearts; O Agni, thou who art invoked, bringer of good heroes.
Shine through the nights and through the days; through thee may we be possessed of good fire. Thou art rich in heroes, thou desirest us.
To thee do the inspired men come with their prayers, striving for gain — unto thee, the thousand-streamed, moving near.
Agni, the bright-flaming, the immortal, drives away the demons; the pure, the purifying one, he is worthy of praise.
May he, the lord, the offspring of strength, bring us riches; and may Bhaga grant the desirable gift.
Do thou, O Agni, grant fame with good heroes; and the god Savitṛ, Bhaga, and Diti give what is desirable.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, O god, protect us from distress, ward off the one who injures us; burn him, ageless, with thy most scorching flames.
Then the great one comes to us, unconquerable, for the protection of men; be thou a fortress with a hundred arms.
Protect us from sin, O thou undeceivable, from him who seeks to harm, at the fall of evening and of morning, by day and by night.
With this reverence I call Agni to you, the offspring of strength, the dearest, the most wakeful, the herald of the sacrifice, the messenger of all, the immortal.
He yokes the red steeds of universal bounty; he runs swiftly when well-fed with oblations. The sacrifice is well-praised and well-laid; the divine bestowal of riches comes to men.
His flame has risen up as he, the bountiful, is fed with oblations; the red smoke-columns that touch the sky rise up. The men kindle Agni together.
Thee, the most glorious, we make our messenger; bring the gods hither to the feast. O offspring of strength, grant all that mortals enjoy; give us that which we implore of thee.
Thou, O Agni, art our householder; thou art the Hotṛ at our rite; thou art the Potṛ, O thou who holdest all desirable things, O wise one; worship and seek the desirable.
Make a jewel for the sacrificer, O thou of good will; for thou art the giver of jewels. Set in order every priest at the rite, O thou of good praise, and him too who is capable.
In thee, O Agni, well fed with oblations, may the patrons be dear — the guiders, the bountiful ones among the people, who share out broad pastures and kine.
Those in whose house Iḍā with ghee-filled hands sits down at dawn — save them, O mighty one, from treachery and reproach; grant us shelter, O thou of far-famed might.
He, the carrier with his sweet tongue, the knower, with his mouth — O Agni, bring riches to us through the bountiful patrons, and set in order the gift of oblations.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those who give horse-wealth and great gifts with desire for fame — save them from sin with those who ferry across; be thou a hundred fortresses for them, O most youthful.
The god, the giver of wealth, desires a full vessel for you. Either pour it out, or fill it up; then indeed the god will hear you.
Him, the Hotṛ of the rite, the wise one, the carrier — the gods have made him so. Agni places a jewel and heroic wealth for the worshipper, for the man who gives.
O Agni, be thou well-kindled with good fuel, and let the sacrificial grass be widely strewn.
And let the willing doors open wide, and here bring hither the willing gods.
O Agni, go forward with the oblation, worship the gods; make the sacrifice proceed well, O Jātavedas.
Jātavedas will make the sacrifice proceed well; he will worship the immortal gods and gladden them.
Win all desirable things, O wise one; may our wishes be fulfilled today.
Thee they have appointed as bearer of oblations, O Agni, the gods have set thee, the offspring of strength.
May we be givers to thee, the divine; distribute for us great jewels as thou movest.
In thee, O Indra, even our fathers won all good things for the praisers; in thee are the good milch cows, in thee indeed the horses; thou art the most bountiful with wealth for the godly man.
For thou dwellest with thy wives like a king, enlightening the days as a wise seer. Adorn our hymns, O bountiful one, with kine and horses; sharpen us who strive toward thee for riches.
These joyful, god-seeking songs have come to thee here competing. May the path of thy riches come toward us; may we be in thy good favor, O Indra, in thy shelter.
Wishing to milk thee like a cow in good pasture, Vasiṣṭha has sent forth the sacred songs to thee. May Indra, the lord of cattle for me, come to us every day with good favor.

title: Rigveda
text:
Indra made the spreading waters fordable and easy to cross for Sudās; the new praiser silenced the raging Śimyu; he made the curses of the rivers into non-curses.
Turvaśa and Yakṣu were at the fore as defenders; the fish-like ones pressed close for gain; the Bhṛgus and the Druhyus rendered obedience; the friend ferried his friend across the diverging streams.
The Paktha, Bhalānas, Bhananta, Alina, Viṣāṇin, and Śiva clans came; he who led the Ārya's allies to battle against the Tṛtsus — through fighting he brought men with cattle-wealth.
The evil-minded, the senseless, dishonouring Aditi, they seized the Paruṣṇī river; he, the lord, shone forth mightily illumining the earth; the wise one like a beast lay in wait, watching.
They went toward the Paruṣṇī but not back from it; even the swift one did not reach the point of encounter. Indra, for Sudās, subdued the hasty foes, those castrated speakers in the human battle.
They went like cattle without a herdsman from the pasture, as the arranged ones toward their friend. The Pṛśnigāvas, sent by Pṛśni, obeyed; the Niyuts and Rantayas gave obedience.
The king cast down one and twenty men of the Vaikarṇa clans for the sake of fame. Like a wise one who sharpens the sacrificial grass at the altar, the heroic Indra let loose an onslaught against them.
Then the vajra-armed one, rolling down, struck the famous, mature Kavaṣa in the waters, and also the Druhyu.
Indra straightway burst asunder all their firm strongholds with might, seven cities of them; he distributed the household wealth of Ānavas to the Tṛtsu; we have overcome Pūru of foul speech in the assembly.
The Ānavas and Druhyus who fought for cattle — sixty hundreds, six thousands lay slain; sixty heroes over and above six who were eager for conflict — all the heroic deeds of Indra were accomplished.

title: Rigveda
text:
Urged on by Indra, the Tṛtsus, eager for battle, flowed downward like released waters; the ill-befriended ones, making a din with their noise, abandoned all their enjoyments for Sudās.
He drove away to the earth half of the hero who drank the cooked offering without Indra, who boasted against him; Indra, the wrathful one, measured out wrath against him; as lord he took possession of the road's course.
Even with a poor instrument he accomplished that one deed; he struck down even the lion-like one with a needle. Indra cut away the corners of the enclosure and gave all enjoyments to Sudās.
Thy perpetual enemies have yielded to thee; find subjugation even for the boasting Bheda. Whoever brings guilt upon the mortal who praises thee — smite him with the sharp thunderbolt, O Indra.
The Yamunā and the Tṛtsus aided Indra; with utmost completeness he robbed Bheda of his strength; the Ajas, Śigrus, and Yakṣus brought him tribute, horse-heads.
Thy favors and thy riches, O Indra, neither the former dawns nor the new ones can count. Thou hast struck down even Devaka who thought himself worthy; of thyself thou hast shattered great Śambara.
They who, exhilarated by thee, have rejoiced from the house — Parāśara, Śatayātu, Vasiṣṭha — they do not forget thy bountiful friendship; may auspicious days dawn for the patrons then.
Two hundred cows belonging to Devavat's grandson, two chariots with their brides from Sudās — worthy of Agni, I walk around the dwelling of Paijavanesya singing like a Hotṛ, praising the gift.
Four gifts of Paijavanesya, well-aimed, adorned with gold pendants, stand out clearly; the dun ones with broad backs from Sudās bear me and my offspring to fame in succession.
His fame, distributed head by head, fills both wide worlds; seven rivers praise him like flowing streams; in the forefront of battle he has established himself as our champion, fighting there.

title: Rigveda
text:
Follow this man, O Maruts, as ye followed Divodāsa, the father of Sudās; the heroic purpose of Paijavanesya is an imperishable, ageless lordship hard to assail, one that strives for service.
Who like a terrible bull with sharp horns, alone, shakes forth all the tribes; who art the dispenser of the wealth of the ever-constant non-worshipper toward the good Soma-presser.
Thou, O Indra, didst indeed aid Kutsa in that battle, hearkening with thy whole self; when thou didst subdue for him the Dāsa Śuṣṇa, the evil-harvesting one, bestowing favor on the son of Arjuna.
Thou, O bold one, with thy boldness didst aid Vītahavya; thou hast aided Sudās with all thy aids. Thou hast aided Paurukutsa Trasadasyu in the winning of fields and in the slaying of Vṛtra and Pūru.
With thy men's-minded heroes at the divine feast, O bay-horsed one, thou slayest many Vṛtras; thou hast lulled to sleep the Dasyu, Cumurin and Dhuni, for Dabhīta, striking well.
These are thy exploits, O holder of the vajra — that thou didst straightway burst asunder nine and ninety fortresses; in the hundredth at their settling thou didst pierce through; thou slewest Vṛtra and thou slewest Namuci.
These enjoyments of thine, O Indra, are of old for the sacrificer who gives the oblation, for Sudās. I yoke thy two powerful bay steeds, O virile one; may the sacred songs, O mighty one, gain strength.
May we not fall into this snare of thine for evil, O mighty, bay-horsed one. Save us with shelters free from wolves; may we be among thy beloved, O patron.
We, thy beloved men, O bountiful one, would rejoice as friends at the conquest, in thy shelter. Sharpen Turvaśa and Yādva for the one who is going to render the laudable thing for Atithigva.
Even now forthwith thy men declare praises, O bountiful, with well-ordered recitations; those who have outstripped the miserly Paṇis with their calls — choose us for that partnership.

title: Rigveda
text:
These praises of men, O best of men, flow toward thee from us, the givers of bounties. O Indra, be gracious to them in the slaying of Vṛtra, be a hero-companion and a protector of men.
Now, O heroic Indra, urged by the sacred word, strengthen thyself with thy whole body as thou art being praised with aid. Measure out prizes for us, measure out strength. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.
The self-sustaining one was born mighty for heroic deeds; he who is to work, the manly one, has worked the waters. He has come, the youthful one, to the seat of men with his aids; Indra is our protector even from great sin.
Indra, having grown mightily, will slay Vṛtra; the hero has now aided the praiser with his help. He will make a world for Sudās — yea, the giver of goods will be ever bountiful to the worshipper.
The warrior, unchallenged, maker of confusion, in the fight a hero, conqueror of all, from his birth invincible in this world — Indra spread apart the battle-lines with his own power and slew the whole hostile host.
Both worlds hast thou, O mighty Indra, filled with thy greatness by thy powers. Indra, the bay-horsed one, dripping with the thunderbolt, has spoken forth in his exhilarations amid the Soma drink.
The bull begat the bull for battle; the woman too gave birth to the manly one. He who is the foremost general, then, among men, the warrior seeking cattle, unwearied, that one is bold.
The man who seeks to please his terrible mind will surely not stumble nor come to harm. He who places services in Indra through sacrifices, the guardian of Ṛta, born of Ṛta, abides in riches.
When the former Indra bestowing favor on the later one — the greater one sacrificed the gift of the lesser — the immortal would sit far round about. O brilliant one, bring us the brilliant wealth.

title: Rigveda
text:
That dear man of thine who has given to thee, O Indra of the stone-thunderbolt, who has been thy friend in the fight — may we be those most gladdened by this good favor of thine; may we be in thy protection, the unhurt, at the men's feast.
This hymn of praise has cried aloud for thee, the bull; and the praise-song too, O bountiful, has called to thee. The desire for wealth has come to thy praiser; do thou, O Śakra, verily be able to help us with treasure.
Do thou, O Indra, grant to us the strength of one who strives toward thee, and those too who are bountiful and drive forward. May thy power toward thy praiser be the power of giving wealth. Do ye ever guard us with all blessings.
The divine, strength-giving soma-juice has been pressed; in this very pressing Indra has spoken from birth. We invoke thee, O Haryaśva, with sacrifices; be wakeful of our hymn in the raptures of the soma.
They who are exhilarated by soma, the loud-voiced ones, advance the sacrifice and spread the sacred grass at the assembly. The bulls who attend men, whose approach is heard from afar, are installed in the seat of glory.
Thou, O Indra, art he who set the waters flowing — the many that had been hemmed in by the serpent, O hero. From thee, as from a coursing mare in a chariot-race, all created things tremble in awe.
Terrible, attacking with his weapons, knowing all their manly deeds, Indra, exulting, shook the fortresses, and with the bolt in his hand smote them asunder with his greatness.
The sorcerers, O Indra, have not prevailed against us; nor have obeisances availed the worshipper, O most mighty. He, the Ārya, shall rout the creature of alien race. Let not the phallus-worshippers approach our sacred rite.
By thy power, O Indra, thou art present here on earth; the regions could not contain thy greatness. For thou slewest Vṛtra by thine own might and valour, and no foe has ever found the limit of thy battle-strength.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even the gods of old accorded their powers to thee for thy lordly sway and dominion. Indra distributes the prizes as he wills; they call upon Indra at the winning of the spoil.
Even the man of small praise has invoked thee for protection, O lord of abundant blessings, O Indra. Thou hast been our refuge, O thou of a hundred aids; the shelter of one like thee is a mighty shield for the suppliant.
May we ever be thy friends, O Indra, reverencing thee with offerings, victorious through thy greatness. With thy aid may they overcome in conflict the onslaughts of the foe who would oppress us.
Do thou, O Indra, grant us the strength of thy bounty, and to those who themselves exert their powers as Maghavans. May thy power as lord of wealth be with thy worshipper; do ye always guard us with blessings.
Drink the soma, O Indra; let it gladden thee — that which the stone, O Haryaśva, hath well pressed for thee; well-yoked is the bay-stallion by the arms of the presser.
That exhilaration of thine which is fitting and lovely, wherewith thou slayest the Vṛtras, O Haryaśva — may that intoxication, O Indra, overwhelm thee, O lord of abundant wealth.
Take heed, O Maghavan, to this my speech — the praise that Vasiṣṭha sings to thee. Be pleased with these prayers in the common joy of the soma feast.
Hear thou the invocation of the stone that has drunk deep; attend to the devotion of the inspired singer as he chants. Come, perform the nearest services and be our companion.
I do not disregard thy songs, knowing thine eager speed; nor do I disregard the praise of thee who art the lord of might. I ever speak thy name that is self-glorious.
For many are thy soma-pressings among men; many a sage invokes thee, thee alone. Be not far from us for long, O Maghavan.
For thee are all these soma-pressings, O hero; for thee I offer prayers that augment thee. Thou art invoked by men and art the sustainer of all.

title: Rigveda
text:
Now indeed no one can fully comprehend thy greatness, O wonderful and fierce one who deems himself such. Thy heroic might, O Indra, and thy bounty are without limit.
The seers of former times and they of the present, the inspired priests who have generated prayers for thee, O Indra — may thy auspicious friendships be with us. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Rise up, O prayers, for glory's sake; glorify Indra in the battle, O Vasiṣṭha — he who has spread out all things by his might. He shall incline his ear to my living words.
I pour forth the shout, O Indra, born among the gods; let my poured speech resound as the bright ones desire. For the span of one's own life is not perceived among men — yet do thou carry us past those very difficulties.
I yoke the chariot that seeks cattle with the two bays; they have taken their stand beside the prayers with delight. Indra in his greatness has spread apart the two worlds; he has slain the Vṛtras that stood against him.
Even the waters swelled full like cows that had not been milked; thy worshippers have striven towards the sacred order, O Indra. Come to us as Vāyu with his team; for thou by thy wisdom distributest the prizes.
May those intoxications gladden thee, O Indra, vigorous one of abundant gifts, for the singer. For thou alone among the gods dost apportion men's fates; rejoice, O hero, at this pressing.
Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas sing their hymns to Indra the bull, the wielder of the bolt. Praised thus, may he grant us wealth in heroes and in cattle. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
A seat, O Indra, has been prepared for thee in the hall of rite; come hither to it with thy escort, O thou much-invoked. Be thou our protector and increaser; grant us riches, and be exhilarated with the soma-draughts.
Thy mind has been seized, O Indra of double might; the soma is pressed, the sweet juices are poured around. This fair-fashioned devotion, whose stream of praise is freely flowing, invokes Indra with longing.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come, O Ṛjīṣin, from heaven and from earth to this sacred grass for the drinking of soma. May the bay steeds bring thee, who desirest exhilaration, towards our hymn of praise, O mighty one, for the joy of drinking.
Come to us, O Haryaśva, enjoying all our aids together, pleased with our prayer. Come, O fine-jawed Indra, striding mightily with thy stalwart steps, laying upon us the manly vigour of the bull.
This hymn has been fashioned for the great and fierce one, to be borne on the yoke-pole like a swift charger straining for the prize. This song invokes thee, O Indra, for the winning of wealth; grant us distinction above others as the sky is above heaven.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with the choicest treasure; we have sought thy great benevolence. Bestow on the Maghavans refreshment rich in heroes. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Great Indra comes, O fierce one, when in equal fury the armies clash together in battle. The lightning-bolt flies from the arms of the manly god; let not thy mind wander in all directions.
O Indra, smite down into the abyss the enemies, the mortal men who assail us. Make the hostile incitement of the plotter to be far away; bring to us the gathering of riches.
Hundredfold, O Śiprin, be thy aids to Sudās; a thousandfold may thy praises and gifts be. Strike down the weapon of the mortal foe; lay upon us splendour and treasure.
For such a one as thee, O Indra, I exist in intelligence; for such a one as thee, O hero, in the bestowal of gifts. With vigour fiercely throughout all the days, O Harivaṇ, make thy dwelling with us; neglect us not.
These praises of the Kutsa clan move toward Indra the Haryaśva seeking vigour, seeking god-sped might. Make the Vṛtras altogether easy to smite, O hero; may we as victors win the prize.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with the choicest treasure; we have sought thy great benevolence. Bestow on the Maghavans refreshment rich in heroes. Do ye always guard us with blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
Without pressed soma Indra has not been exhilarated; without prayer have the pressed libations not exhilarated Maghavan. Therefore I generate a hymn, that as he has taken pleasure therein, the hero may hear our newer song.
With hymn after hymn, with pressed soma after pressed soma, Maghavan has been exhilarated. When men of equal will and vigour, hard-pressed like sons invoking a father, call on Indra for aid.
He has done these deeds, now making others that the priests speak of at the soma-pressings. Like a single husband ruling over wives, Indra has well cleansed all the cities.
Thus they speak of him; and hear, O Indra — thou art the sole distributor, the speedy apportioner of prizes. His many aids are for mutual protection; may his auspicious blessings follow after us as beloved gifts.
Thus does Vasiṣṭha praise Indra, the bull of the tribes, at the soma-pressing, for the welfare of men. Bring thousandfold prizes near to us. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Men call on Indra with reverence, when they harness those thoughts that are to reach their goal. The hero who prostrates men, who delights in his own might — allot us our share in the cow-stall that yields cattle.
Whatever vigour is thine, O Maghavan, share it with thy friends, O much-invoked, with the heroes. For thou, O Maghavan, art the discerning one; release our bounty that is locked away, like water held back.
Indra is king of the moving world, of all peoples, over the earth, whatever there is of manifold form. From that position he gives riches to the worshipper, he who is praised stimulates bounty to flow hither.
Indra the Maghavan, when invoked together with us, shall in no way hold back the prize for giving, nor his aid. His bounteous gift — he whose south-offering has swelled to fullness — flows towards good things for the heroes and friends.

title: Rigveda
text:
Now, O Indra, grant us wide room for wealth; we would turn thy mind towards our bounty. May we go forth rich in cattle, horses, and chariots. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Come to us with the prayer, O Indra, O wise one; let thy bay steeds be turned hither and yoked. For indeed all mortals call upon thee; hear us, O thou who fillest all.
Thy greatness, O Indra, has answered our invocation when thou dost protect the prayer of the seers, O mighty one. When thou takest the bolt in thy hand, O terrible one, grim as thou art, thou wast born unconquerable by thy wisdom.
Those who call upon thee under thy guidance, O Indra, thou dost lead — just as thou dost lead together the two worlds and the men. For thou wast born for great dominion and might; the urger destroyed even the one who was not swift to urge.
With these days be gracious to us, O Indra; for the ill-friended peoples hasten away. Since the blameless one sees the falsehood directly, may deceitful Varuṇa turn away from us once and for all.
We would proclaim this Indra Maghavan for what he grants us of great wealth and bounty — he who protects the inspired singer's prayer of the one who sings. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
This soma, O Indra, is pressed for thee; come hither, O Harivaṇ who dwellest at home. Drink then of this well-pressed, lovely draught, coming to give us prizes, O Maghavan.
O Brāhmaṇ hero, be pleased with the prayer's fashioning; come swiftly hither with the bay steeds. Be exhilarated at this soma-pressing; hear these our prayers.
What adornment of thee is there with well-spoken hymns? When, O Maghavan, shall we make offering to thee? I have stretched forth all thoughts towards thee; set, O Indra, so that thou mayest hear when we invoke thee.
And indeed those men of thine have existed — the seers of former times to whom thou didst hearken. And so I keep calling upon thee, O Maghavan; thou, O Indra, art our guardian as a father.

title: Rigveda
text:
We would proclaim this Indra Maghavan for what he grants us of great wealth and bounty — he who protects the inspired singer's prayer of the one who sings. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Come to us, O divine Indra, with might, thou vigorous one; be thou the increaser of this our wealth. Come for great manly strength, O lord of men who wieldest the good bolt, come for great dominion and vigour, O hero.
The heroes call upon thee, calling thee with distinct voice in their own persons at the winning of the sun. Thou art to be called upon as a warrior among all peoples; cause the Vṛtras to yield — let them be easy to smite.
When, O Indra, thou hast shone forth in fair days illuminating, when thou dost plant the highest banner in battles — Agni takes his seat as the divine Ṛtvik-priest, inviting the gods here for the sake of blessedness.
We, and those gods too, O hero Indra, who praise thee the giver of prizes — grant to the pious patrons the highest protection, so that those born of good stock may attain to long old age.
We would proclaim this Indra Maghavan for what he grants us of great wealth and bounty — he who protects the inspired singer's prayer of the one who sings. Do ye always guard us with blessings.
Sing forth to Indra, the exhilarating hymn, O friends, to him of the bay steeds, the drinker of Soma.
Let heroic men recite the laud and the bright offering as is fit, for him of liberal gifts — we have made them for Indra, the truly bounteous.
Thou, O Indra, art the seeker of prizes; thou, O Lord of a hundred powers, art the seeker of cattle; thou art the seeker of gold, O bright one.
We who are devoted to thee, O Indra, praise thee exceedingly, O Bull; mark well this our song, O bright one.
Deliver us not to blame nor to the speech of the hostile one, nor surrender us to one who does not give; in thee too rests my purpose.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou art our wide-spreading armour and our champion in the forefront, O Vṛtra-slayer; with thee as ally I speak in reply.
Great indeed art thou, whose might, self-sustaining, follows; both the worlds, O Indra, acknowledge thee.
May the speech accompanied by the Maruts, moving together with the days, encompass thee, O Indra, reaching thee.
The Soma-drops, standing upright, have flowed to thee, the wondrous one, toward heaven; the people bow down together to thee.
Carry forward your praise to the great one, who is magnified by greatness, to the wise one; bestow your good-will; go forth, O many peoples who sustain human life.
Wise seers generate the well-fashioned prayer for Indra, far-reaching and mighty; the steadfast ones do not transgress his ordinances.
The sacred voices, ever unvanquished in wrath, have placed Indra together as king to drink in common; for the lord of bay steeds, press down and exhilarate the companions.
Let not the worshippers, nor any one, keep thee far from us; come hither from afar to our feast of exhilaration, or, being here, listen near at hand.
These hymn-makers of thine sit here with the pressed Soma as bees upon honey; the praisers desirous of wealth have set their desire in Indra, as a foot in a chariot.
Desirous of wealth, I call Indra of the bolt-hand, well-skilled, as a son calls upon a father.
These Soma-draughts mixed with curds have been pressed for Indra; come to them for exhilaration, O bolt-handed one, to drink — come home with thy bay horses.
The keen-eared one moves, hearing a call for riches; let him not now neglect our songs — he who can give thousands and hundreds in a day; no one can restrain the willing giver.
That hero, unassailable, has blazed forth with Indra amid warriors — he who presses for thee, O Vṛtra-slayer, the deep Soma-pressings and hastens hither.

title: Rigveda
text:
Be a shelter, O Maghavan, for the bountiful, when thou dost conquer the insolent; may we share the wealth of the one struck by thee — O unstrikable one, bring home riches.
Press the Soma for the Soma-drinker Indra, the wielder of the bolt; cook the offerings for our aid — truly the bounty of the liberal man delights the liberal.
Do not falter, O Soma-pressers; be skilful; strive for great riches; truly the bold man wins, lives, and prospers — the gods are not for the niggardly.
No one encompassed the chariot of Sudās to detain it; he whose helper is Indra, toward whom the Maruts come — he reaches the stall rich in cattle.
The mortal whose helper thou art, O Indra, wins the prize while pressing for prizes; be thou our helper of chariots, our helper of heroes, O champion.
The portion of him truly springs up like the wealth of a victor — Indra with his bay horses; deceivers do not harm him; he who is at the Soma-pressing bestows skill.
Place at the sacred rites the mighty, well-set, well-adorned prayer; even many pursuings do not overtake him who is engaged in work for Indra.
What mortal would dare to assail him who has thee as his wealth, O Indra? Truly, O Maghavan, by faith in thee on the appointed day in heaven, the swift steed wins the prize.
Urge the bountiful in the slaying of Vṛtra, those who give dear wealth; under thy guidance, O lord of bay steeds, may we with the inspired patrons pass through all difficulties.
The lowest wealth is thine, O Indra, and thou dost cultivate the middle sort; thou reignest over all that is highest; no one excludes thee from the cattle.
Thou art the famed giver of wealth to all, whose victories come; O much-invoked one, this whole earthly world, desiring thy aid, begs thy name.
If I, O Indra, were as great as thou art, I would seek only the praiser to maintain; I would not give wealth, O giver, for wickedness.

title: Rigveda
text:
I would indeed assist the magnanimous one day by day for wealth found somewhere; truly, O Maghavan, there is no kinsman, not even a father, more helpful than thou.
Truly the bold one wins the prize with Puraṁdhi as his ally; I bend Indra, the much-invoked, hither with a hymn, as a skilled carpenter bends a wheel-rim.
A mortal finds no wealth through ill-praise; riches do not come to the negligent; O Maghavan, good strength to thee — for one devoted to thee, a gift on the appointed day in heaven.
We praise thee exceedingly, O champion, as milch-cows that have not been milked; O Indra, the lord of this moving world, the heaven-beholder, the lord of the standing world.
No other, neither heavenly nor earthly, born or yet to be born, is like thee; we who desire horses, O Maghavan Indra, we who are swift and who seek cattle — we call on thee.
O Indra, bring thou that — the greater for the lesser, the greater to the needy; for thou, O Maghavan, art of abundant wealth from of old and art to be invoked in every battle.
Drive away the enemies, O Maghavan; make our riches easy to find; be thou our helper in the great contest, the strengthener of our friends.
O Indra, bring us resolve as a father brings it to his sons; help us, O much-invoked, in this our journey; may we living reach the light.
Let not unknown hostile powers, ill-intentioned, let not the inauspicious trample us; with thee, O champion, may we ever pass through the rushing streams.
The white-complexioned, right-tufted Vasiṣṭhas, who gladden the mind with hymns, have gladdened me; rising up I declare before the men at the sacred grass — the Vasiṣṭhas have not been far from me as helpers.
They brought Indra from afar with the pressed Soma, past Vaiśanta, past the mighty guardian; from the pressed Soma of Pāśadyumna Vāyata, Indra chose the Vasiṣṭhas.

title: Rigveda
text:
So with these he crossed the Sindhu; so with these he smote the adversary; so in the Battle of Ten Kings did Indra protect Sudās through your sacred formulas, O Vasiṣṭhas.
Through the sacred prayer of your fathers, the inexhaustible beneficent deed was performed by devoted men — you do not perish; for in the Śakvarī verses with a great cry you, the Vasiṣṭhas, placed your might in Indra.
Thirsty, beseeching, as though yearning for heaven, they shone in the Battle of Ten Kings, beset; Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he praised, and made wide space for the Tṛtsus.
The cattle-owners were like scattered staffs; the Bharatas were tiny and hemmed in; but Vasiṣṭha became their leader in the forefront, and straightway the clans of the Tṛtsus spread wide.
Three pour their seed in the worlds; three Āryan offspring head toward the light; three warmths attend the Dawn — all these the Vasiṣṭhas know fully.
Their radiance is like the shining of the sun; their greatness is deep as the ocean; their swiftness is like the wind — no one else, O Vasiṣṭhas, may follow up your praise.
They move together around the hidden thing of the heart with the thoughts of a thousand branches; weaving the enclosure stretched out by Yama, the Vasiṣṭhas sat down with the Apsarases.
When Mitra and Varuṇa saw thee flashing around the light of the lightning — that is thy one birth, O Vasiṣṭha; the other is when Agastya brought thee among the Viśas.
Thou art also the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, O Vasiṣṭha, born of Urvaśī from the mind, O brahmin; the seed that had fallen — all the gods received thee in the lotus with the divine prayer.
He, the discerner, knowing both worlds, giver of thousands and one who possesses eternally — Vasiṣṭha was born amid the Apsarases, about to weave the enclosure stretched by Yama.
Born together at the sacrifice, urged by devotion, they poured their commingled seed into a jar; thence Māna rose up in the midst; thence the seer born is called Vasiṣṭha.

title: Rigveda
text:
He bears the bearer of laud, the bearer of Sāman, and bearing the pressing-stone he speaks forth first; approach him with goodwill — Vasiṣṭha will come to you, O Pratṛdas.
Let the divine bright prayer go forth from us, well-fashioned as a swift racing-chariot.
The flowing waters hear and know the birth-place of earth and heaven.
Even the wide waters swell for him; in the battles against Vṛtras the mighty champions take thought.
Yoke the horses for him at the pole, as Indra the bolt-wielder with arms of gold.
Go forth toward the sacrifice as on a given day; urge it of yourselves, as if going on a journey.
Of yourselves urge the sacrifice in the battles; set up a standard, a hero for the people.
From his might the radiance has not faltered; the earth bears the weight as the ground.
I invoke the gods; O Agni, unchecked, completing the work with holy order, I set my thought.
Direct your divine thought; send forth your voice toward the gods.
The mighty Varuṇa of a thousand eyes looks upon the depths of these rivers.
He is the king of kingdoms, the ornament of rivers; imperishable sovereignty, life for all, belongs to him.
Protect us in all the clans; make our fame shine forth this day for the praiser.
Let the sinister lightning of enemies depart; ward off from all sides the blemish from our bodies.
Agni has protected us and our oblations with devotions; the most beloved praise has been placed for him.
Make the Child of Waters our friend in common with the gods; may he be gracious to us.
With hymns I praise the water-born serpent sitting in the dust at the base of the rivers.
Let Ahi Budhnya not place us in harm; let not the sacrifice of this one who lives by holy order fail.
And may these heroic men lay fame upon us; may noble ones go forth boldly for wealth.
Their great armies scorch the foe as the sun scorches the earth with its swift rays.

title: Rigveda
text:
When our consorts come forward to us, may Tvaṣṭar of the fair hands bestow heroic men.
May Tvaṣṭar be pleased with our praise; may Aramati, seeking wealth, abide with us.
May they, the bountiful ones, bestow wealth upon us; may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear; may there be good refuge for us with their many protections; may Tvaṣṭar of good gifts distribute riches.
May the mountains give us that wealth, may the waters, may the bountiful herbs and heaven; may earth, united with the forest-trees, may both the world-halves guard us around.
May the wide two world-halves extend for that; may the mighty Varuṇa, Indra's friend; may all the powerful Maruts follow — may we be the firm foundation of wealth to contemplate.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the herbs, and the forest-trees bestow that on us; may we be in the lap of the Maruts for shelter; protect us ever with blessings.
May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their aids; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are given, be auspicious; may Indra and Soma be gracious for our well-being; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious in the winning of prizes.
May Bhaga be auspicious to us; may our praise also be auspicious; may Puraṁdhi be auspicious; may riches also be auspicious; may the praise of truth and good governance be auspicious to us; may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious.
May Dhātṛ be auspicious to us; may the Sustainer also be auspicious; may the wide-shining one be auspicious with her offerings; may the great Rodasī be auspicious; may the mountain be auspicious; may the good invocations of the gods be auspicious.
May Agni, the radiant-faced, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa be auspicious, and the Aśvins; may the good deeds of the good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.

title: Rigveda
text:
May Dyāvāpṛthivī be auspicious at the morning invocation; may the midspace be auspicious for us to behold; may the herbs and the forest-trees be auspicious; may the victorious lord of the dust-realm be auspicious to us.
May Indra the god be auspicious with the Vasus; may Varuṇa of fair praise be auspicious with the Ādityas; may Rudra the healing one be auspicious with the Rudras; may Tvaṣṭar with the Gnās hear and be auspicious.
May Soma be auspicious to us; may the sacred prayer be auspicious; may the pressing-stones be auspicious; may the sacrifices also be auspicious; may the timbers of the stakes be auspicious; may the sacrificial ladle be auspicious and the altar be auspicious.
May the Sun of wide vision rise auspiciously for us; may the four directions be auspicious; may the firm mountains be auspicious; may the rivers and the waters be auspicious.
May Aditi be auspicious to us with her ordinances; may the Maruts who win the light be auspicious; may Viṣṇu be auspicious; may Pūṣan also be auspicious; may our prosperity be auspicious and Vāyu be auspicious.
May the god Savitṛ, protecting us, be auspicious; may the brightly shining Dawns be auspicious; may Parjanya be auspicious for our offspring; may the lord of the field, the bringer of blessing, be auspicious.
May the All-Gods be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī along with understanding be auspicious; auspicious be those who encompass us, auspicious those who give gifts; may the divine, the earthly, and the aqueous beings be auspicious.
May the lords of truth be auspicious to us; may our horses be auspicious; may the cows also be auspicious; may the Ṛbhus, the well-doing, the skilled of hand, be auspicious; may the Fathers be auspicious to us at the invocations.
May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahi Budhnya and the ocean be auspicious; may Apāṁ Napāt Pūru be auspicious; may Pṛśni, guarded by the gods, be auspicious.

title: Rigveda
text:
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus be pleased with this renewed prayer being offered; may the divine, the earthly, the cow-born ones, and all those worthy of worship hear us.
Those who among the gods are most worthy of sacrifice, the adorable ones of Manu, the immortal knowers of holy order — may they bestow on us ample room this day; protect us ever with blessings.
Let the sacred prayer go forth from the seat of holy order; the Sun has sent out his rays and released the cows; the wide earth has spread herself along her ridge; Agni has shone with his broad face.
I make this well-fashioned hymn for you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, lords of might — a newer refreshment; another of you two, the inviolable Ino, follows the path, and Mitra, as he speaks, maintains the people.
They came to rest in the path of the rushing wind; the cows — like good milch-kine — have caused to swell; born in the seat of the great heaven, the Bull has bellowed in that same udder.
He who would yoke with a song those thy two beloved bay steeds, O Indra, with the beautiful chariot — O champion, the two who give nourishment — and who by his wrath destroys the attacker, I would turn hither Aryaman of good counsel.
Both birds and the reverent ones worship his friendship in the seat of holy order; having been praised by men, he spreads forth his nourishment — this most beloved reverence to Rudra.
When, crying out together for glory, Sarasvatī the seventh, mother of streams, and those who have sounded well — the good-milking, good-streaming ones — swell up with their own milk.
May these swift Maruts, rejoicing, protect our prayer and our offspring; may the imperishable ones moving around not overlook us; may they foster our wealth fit to be yoked.
Proclaim the great Aramati; proclaim Pūṣan, the hero of the assembly; proclaim Bhaga, the protector of understanding at this winning, the prize-seeker Puraṁdhi.

title: Rigveda
text:
May this call go toward you, O Maruts; may it go toward Viṣṇu, the overseer of the pressed drink, with your aids; and may they assign strength for offspring to the singer; protect us ever with blessings.
May the unimpeded chariot, O Ṛbhukṣans, the swiftest bearer of prizes, carry you hither to be praised; at the pressings fill yourselves with the triple-ridged Soma-draughts in exhilaration, O fair-cheeked ones, with great gifts.
You, O unimpeded Ṛbhukṣans, truly place the imperishable jewel among the bountiful, the heaven-beholding ones; drink your fill with your own power at the sacrifices; distribute your gifts to us with your thoughts.
For thou, O Maghavan, hast spoken of the gift in the distribution of great and small wealth; both thy arms are full of wealth; true speech cannot be constrained when there is desire for riches.
Thou, O Indra, art the self-glorious Ṛbhukṣan; O praised one, like a good steed thou goest home; may we, the Vasiṣṭhas, be worshippers devoted to thee, composing the sacred prayer, O lord of bay horses.
Thou art the winner of the downward-rushing streams even for the worshipper, O lord of bay steeds, through those thoughts with which thou aidest; let me be joined to thy allied aids — when, O Indra, wilt thou bestow wealth upon us?
Thou art as if clothing us, O wise one; when, O Indra, hast thou heeded our speech? With thought going home, bring wealth rich in heroes; may our steed bring the prize-winning nourishment for us.
Whom even the goddess Nirṛti controls — the autumns of good nourishment reach Indra.
May gifts come to us to be praised, O Savitṛ; may wealth come at the bounty of the mountain; may the divine guardian attend us always; protect us ever with blessings.
The god Savitṛ has stretched upward the golden luster which he put on.
Rise up, O Savitṛ, O golden-handed; hear this, at the proper presentation of holy order; sending forth the wide, flat radiance, bestowing on men the food of mortals.

title: Rigveda
text:
May the god Savitṛ, praised by all, be here — he whom all the Vasus also sing; may he who deserves reverence bestow on us and his devotees his grace with the praise; may he protect the wise men with all his guardians.
Whom the divine Aditi praises, rejoicing in the stimulation of god Savitṛ; whom the sovereign Varuṇa praises; whom the Mitras and Aryaman praise together.
