Those who win against each other in rivalry, seeking the gift of heaven, the bounty-sharers of earth — may Ahi Budhnya hear us too, and may Varūtrī protect us with her single milch-kines.
Following that, may the lord of the family take thought, seeking the jewel of god Savitṛ; the mighty man repeatedly calls on Bhaga for aid; the mighty man, following Bhaga, then finds the jewel.
May those who win prizes be auspicious to us at the invocations — the swift-running ones, winners of light, in their divine succession.
Protect us prize-winners in every contest for wealth, O wise immortal knowers of holy order; drink of this mead and make yourselves exhilarated; go satisfied along the god-traveled paths.
Agni, erect, has reached good thought and wealth; the aging one goes to meet the divine succession; the two pressing-stones have found their path as of a chariot; the Hotṛ, impelled by holy order, sacrifices for us.
The sacred grass has been well spread for these; the two lords of the clan move here like a fissure; at the morning invocation of the people, at the Dawn, Vāyu and Pūṣan harnessed for well-being come hither.
Here on the earth the Vasus and the bright gods have rejoiced; in the broad midspace they have cleansed themselves; O far-going ones, make the paths hither; hear the message of this our envoy who has gone.
For they, the worshipful, the helpful at the sacrifices — all the gods are about the common station; O Agni, worship those who long for the sacrifice — the gift, the Nāsatyas, and Puraṁdhi.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, bring hither by our songs from heaven and earth: Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni; Aryaman, Aditi, and Viṣṇu of these — may Sarasvatī and the Maruts exhilarate them.
He has bestowed the oblation with the thoughts of those worthy of sacrifice; it reaches the desire of mortals, making them content; may Dhātṛ grant the inexhaustible wealth of those who sit at ease — may we conquer now with the allied gods.
Now Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, possessors of holy order, are praised through these Rodasīs by the Vasiṣṭhas; may the bright ones bestow the highest praise upon us; protect us ever with blessings.
Let the auspicious call come together at the assembly; let us set up our praise for the swift ones; whatever the god Savitṛ stimulates today, may we be among those who share in his jewels.
May Mitra grant us that, and Varuṇa, and the Rodasīs, and Indra the heaven-apportioned share, and Aryaman; may the divine Aditi show the way to wealth; and Vāyu and Bhaga, whom they yoke together.
He shall be mighty and powerful, that mortal whom ye, O speckle-horsed Maruts, protect; and Agni and Sarasvatī urge him on — the limits of his wealth are not to be passed.
For this Varuṇa is the guide of holy order; the royal Mitras and Aryaman have set the waters in their place; the divine Aditi, easily invoked, the unassailable — may they carry us past our afflictions, unharmed.
We are a branch of this bountiful god, in the forward offering of advancing Viṣṇu with oblations; for Rudra knows his mighty Rudrean greatness; may the Aśvins, possessing refreshment, find the most excellent track.
O Pūṣan, radiant, when the shelter and the bountiful givers bestow gifts — may those who are sources of joy guard our horses; may the all-encompassing wind grant us rain.
Now Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, the possessors of holy order, are praised through the Rodasīs by the Vasiṣṭhas; may the bright ones bestow the highest praise upon us; protect us ever with blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
At dawn we invoke Agni, at dawn Indra, at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa, at dawn the Aśvins; at dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, the Lord of Prayer, at dawn Soma, and also Rudra we call.
We invoke Bhaga the mighty, won at dawn, son of Aditi, who apportions — even the impoverished man, even the swift warrior, even the king, says of him: 'May I obtain Bhaga's share.'
O Bhaga, guide and leader, Bhaga of true bounty — lift up and sustain this our prayer; O Bhaga, enrich us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, make us strong with men, that we may be heroes.
May we be possessed of Bhaga now, and at the departure of day, and in its middle; and, O Bountiful One, at the rising of the sun — may we dwell in the favour of the gods.
May Bhaga alone among the gods be the possessor of fortune — through him may we be fortunate; 'thee, O Bhaga, all men everywhere invoke' — be thou, O Bhaga, our forerunner here.
The Dawns bow down together for the sacrifice, as Dadhikrāvan hastens to the lustrous track; may prize-winning steeds bring Bhaga, the finder of wealth, toward us — as horses draw a chariot.
Rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in heroes — auspicious Dawns, may they always shine for us; yielding ghee, well-nourished on every side — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
Let the Brahman-priests, the Aṅgirases, go forth; let the roaring of the celestial one advance; let the swelling milk-cows low — may the two press-stones be yoked, the ornament of the sacrifice.
Thy path, O Agni, is well-trodden and renowned; yoke thy tawny and thy red horses at the pressing; those ruddy ones who, seated in the dwelling, carry heroes — I invoke the birthplaces of the gods.
Magnifying your sacrifice with homage, the joyful Hotṛ has raised his voice in the near presence; O thou of many faces, sacrifice well to the gods — may thou attract holy Aramati to the rite.

title: Rigveda
text:
When, resting softly, the guest Agni comes to presence in the home of the prosperous hero — Agni well-pleased, well-kindled in the house, gives the desirable boon to the people who come before him.
O Agni, favour this our sacrifice; make us glorious among the Maruts and Indra; let Night and Dawn come to sit upon the sacred grass — here let me worship Mitra and Varuṇa who bring peace.
Thus Vasiṣṭha, desiring riches, has praised Agni the mighty, giver of all nourishment; may he spread out vigour, wealth, and strength among us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
Those who love the gods have sung your praise at the sacrifices, with homage to Heaven and Earth for refreshment — those whose prayers spread abroad in every direction like the boughs of a great tree.
Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift racehorse; uplift, O like-minded ones, the ghee-sprinkled ladles; spread the sacred grass well for the rite — the god-seeking flames have risen upward.
Let the gods sit upon the ridge of the sacred grass like sons coming to their mother, bearing gifts; let Viśvācī anoint the assembly — O Agni, let there be no failure in our worship of the gods.
The adorable ones rejoice with delight, milking the streams of Ṛta that yield sweetly; come hither today, O ye of one accord, to the greatest of your great riches, to where ye stand.
Thus, O Agni, honour us among the peoples; with thee, O mighty one, we are unharmed; allied with riches, rejoicing together, unscathed — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
For your aid I invoke first Dadhikrāvan, the Aśvins, Uṣas, Agni well-kindled, and Bhaga; Indra, Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sunlight.
Rousing Dadhikrāvan with homage, raising their voices as they advance upon the sacrifice, seating the divine Iḷā upon the sacred grass — O inspired poets, we invoke the well-invoked Aśvins.

title: Rigveda
text:
Being awake I address Dadhikrāvan, Agni, Uṣas, Sūrya, and the Dawn-cow; the vast yellow one, the tawny steer of the two heavens and of Varuṇa — may they drive all evil far from us.
Dadhikrāvan the prize-winner comes first to the fore of the chariots, knowing the way; in accord with Uṣas, with Sūrya, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases.
May Dadhikrāvan anoint our path for us, that we may follow the path of Ṛta; may Agni, the divine host, hear us; may all the wise and mighty ones hear.
Let the god Savitṛ come hither, rich in true gifts, filling the midair, borne by his horses; holding in his hand many heroic gifts, both bringing to rest and urging on all beings.
His two broad, outstretched, golden arms, unfailing, reach to the ends of heaven; truly his greatness is to be praised — even the Sun has followed his course of activity.
May that god Savitṛ, mighty of impulsion, the lord of riches, bestow riches upon us; spreading abroad the vast abundance, he then grants us the food allotted to mortals.
These hymns praise Savitṛ of fair tongue, full-handed, beautiful-palmed; may he bestow bright, ample sustenance upon us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
These songs for Rudra of the firm bow, the swift-arrowed god, self-nourishing, unconquered, all-enduring, wise, sharp-weaponed — sing them; let him hear us.
For with sovereign rule over earthly creatures, and with lordship over the divine, he governs; be thou, O Rudra, free from anger, our protector at our doors, come to our aid — be gracious to our offspring.
Thy lightning-bolt that has been shot and ranges abroad over the earth — may it pass us by; O thou of good sleep, thy thousand remedies exist — injure us not in our children and our offspring.
Strike us not, O Rudra, nor abandon us; let us not be caught in the snare of thee when wrathful; grant us a share at the sacred grass, in our hymn of life — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Waters, the wave which the god-loving Iḷā first fashioned for Indra's drinking — that pure, stainless, ghee-sprinkling, honey-sweet wave of yours we now claim.
May Apāṁ Napāt, swift in impulse, protect that sweetest wave of yours, O Waters — the wave in which Indra rejoices with the Vasus; may we who love the gods attain that wave of yours today.
The divine Waters, purified by a hundred streams, rejoicing with their own power, reach the realm of the gods; they do not transgress Indra's ordinances — offer the oblation, rich in ghee, to the rivers.
Those which the Sun has spread with his rays, those for whom Indra carved a path, a wave — O rivers, grant us wide space — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
O Ṛbhukṣan, O Vājas, rejoice in us — you heroes, generous ones, in the pressed Soma; may your resolves come hither toward us; may the Vibhvans turn the heroic chariot.
May we, through the Ṛbhus, be Ṛbhu-like for you; through the Vibhvans may we prevail with great strength; may Vāja protect us in the winning of prizes — yoked with Indra, may we overcome the foe.
For even they have many commandments that prevail, winning over all foes and overcoming resistance; may Indra with Vibhvan, Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and Ārya, through mutual combat, shatter the enemy's might.
Now, O gods, make wide space for us; be all of one accord for our protection; may the Vasus bestow refreshment upon us — do ye ever protect us with your blessings.
Flowing from the midst of the flood, purifying themselves, led by the ocean, never resting — those divine Waters that Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, has cleft open — may they protect me here.
Those divine Waters that flow from heaven, or those that flow in channels dug by man, or those that spring up of themselves — pure, cleansing, making their way to the ocean — may those divine Waters protect me here.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those in whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men — honey-dripping, pure, and cleansing — may those divine Waters protect me here.
Those in which King Varuṇa dwells, in which Soma dwells, in which all the gods take delight in their vigour, into which Agni Vaiśvānara has entered — may those divine Waters protect me here.
Protect me here, O Mitra and Varuṇa; let not the nesting, all-pervading one come upon me; I conceal the ill-formed, ugly thing — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.
Whatever knotty obstruction may exist in the joints, whatever may cleave around the knees and ankles — let blazing Agni drive that away from here — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.
Whatever poison exists in the silk-cotton tree, whatever is in the rivers, whatever venom arises from the plants — let all the gods press that out from here — let not the creeping evil, the sickness, find me.
Those Waters that flow downward, those that flow upward, those that flow along ridges, those that are full of water and those that are dry — flowing with milk for our good, may they be auspicious and divinely benign, unhindering of foot; may all the rivers be ungrudging of food.
With the fresh aid of the Ādityas may we obtain the most blissful shelter. In a state of sinlessness, in a state of Aditi's grace, may the swift ones — listening — establish this sacrifice.
Let the Ādityas and Aditi rejoice — Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa the most righteous. May they be guardians of our world; let them drink the Soma today for our protection.
All the Ādityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, and all the Ṛbhus — Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins being praised — do ye all protect us always with blessings.
May we be Ādityas, may we be Aditis — foremost among gods, Vasus among mortals. Winning through Mitra-Varuṇa as we win, may we become as Heaven and Earth endure.

title: Rigveda
text:
May Mitra and Varuṇa, as guardians, grant us shelter for our offspring and progeny. May we not enjoy what sin belongs to others; O Vasus, may we not commit that deed you would requite.
The swift Aṅgirasas, going toward the treasure of divine Savitṛ, approach it swiftly. That great adorable Father — may all the gods with one mind accept it for us.
With sacrifices I earnestly laud Heaven, and Earth with reverences — the two vast, adorable ones. For even the ancient seers, while singing praise, set these two great, divine-born ones in the forefront.
Honor these two primeval Parents with ever-fresh hymns in the seat of Ṛta. O Heaven and Earth, come to us with your divine host; great is your protection.
For yours are the many treasure-gifts, O Heaven and Earth, for the liberal sacrificer. Bestow upon us what shall be inexhaustible; do ye protect us always with blessings.
O Lord of the homestead, recognize us; enter graciously and be free of disease for us. Whatever we think of you, accept that; be auspicious to us for our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
O Lord of the homestead, be for us a furtherer — prospering with cattle and horses our home, O drop of Soma. May we be ageless in your friendship; as a father to his sons, accept us graciously.
O Lord of the homestead, may we join your gracious and joyful assembly that opens a path. Protect our rest and our labor; give us the best. Do ye protect us always with blessings.
O Lord of the homestead, dispeller of disease, entering all forms, be a gentle and kindly friend to us.
O white-toothed son of Saramā, tawny one, when you snarl — your fangs glitter as spear-points at your jaws while you gnaw; do sleep now.
Son of Saramā, go back again after the thief or the robber. Why do you bark at Indra's praisers and trouble us? Do sleep now.

title: Rigveda
text:
You tear the boar apart; let the boar tear you. You bark at Indra's praisers — why do you trouble us? Do sleep now.
Let the mother sleep, let the father sleep, let the dog sleep, let the lord of the clan sleep. Let all the kinsmen sleep; let all the people round about sleep.
Those who sit, those who move about, those who look upon us — their eyes we close together, just as this mansion is shut up.
The thousand-horned bull who has risen up from the ocean — with him, the mighty one, we lull the people to sleep.
Women who lie on cushions, women who lie in carriages, women who lie on couches — all the fragrant women, all of them we lull to sleep.
Who, sharing the same nest, has clearly made them known — Rudra's young men, well-horsed indeed?
For no one truly knows their births; they themselves know each other's origin.
Roaring like the wind, like eagles they strove with one another, sprinkling with their own purifying streams.
These secret things the wise man has discerned — what great udder the dappled cow, Pṛśni, bore.
May that tribe be rich in heroes with the Maruts, ever victorious, ever flourishing in manly might.
Most swift in their course, most lovely, most lustrous, mixed with splendor, mighty with their strength.
Fierce is your might, firm are your powers; verily the troop with the Maruts is strong indeed.
Bright is your breath, it shakes the mind to anger, like a sage of the bold host who trembles with power.
Turn away the lightning-bolt from us; let not your ill-will come upon us here.
I invoke your dear names, O swift ones, when the Maruts, eager, have drunk their fill.
Well-armed, impetuous, adorned with fine necklaces, they themselves adorn their own bodies.
Pure are your oblations, O Maruts, pure ones; I send forth the pure sacrifice to the pure. By Ṛta the guardians of Ṛta came to truth — pure-born, pure, and purifying.

title: Rigveda
text:
On your shoulders, O Maruts, are bracelets; on your chests, gold ornaments are pressed. Flashing like lightning with the rains, guiding your weapons according to your own nature.
Forth proceed your deepest greatnesses; spread forth your names, O you most worthy of worship. Enjoy this share worthy of a thousand, fit for the household, the home-sacrificer's portion, O Maruts.
If, O Maruts, you attend to the praise of the inspired poet rich in offerings, swiftly bestow the wealth of heroic strength — even that which some niggardly stranger has held back.
Like swift coursers striding forward, like young men of fair appearance bright as divine visions, dwelling in stately homes, bright as calves that gambol and are full of milk.
Honoring us, may the Maruts grant us bliss; favoring us, O well-formed Heaven and Earth. May your destructive weapon be far from our cattle and our men; O Vasus, bow to us with grace.
Your Hotā, seated and singing praises, constantly calls you and calls the Maruts for a joint gift. He who is guardian of those who travel — that guileless one invokes you with lauds.
These Maruts grant swift delight; these bow their force before force. These protect the praise of him who would win, and they lay heavy enmity on the malevolent.
These Maruts impel even the feeble; even the violent they welcome as Vasus. Drive away the darknesses, O bulls; bestow on us all offspring and progeny.
Let us not fall away from your gifts, O Maruts, nor be left behind in the distribution of wealth. Grant us a share in the desirable Vasu-treasure — whatever is well-born among you, O bulls.
When people clash in fury, heroes among the young herbs in the settlements — then, O Maruts, sons of Rudra, be our protectors and noble defenders in the battles.
Many are the ancestral hymns fashioned for you, O Maruts, that were recited in the past. Mighty with the Maruts is one vanquished in battle; only with the Maruts does the horse win strength.

title: Rigveda
text:
May there be a vigorous hero among us, O Maruts — one who is asura among men, the upholder. With him may we cross the waters to a good dwelling; then may we be at home in your presence.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the Waters, the plants, and the forests accept that for us. May we be in the shelter of the Maruts' lap; do ye protect us always with blessings.
Sweet is your name, O adorable Maruts; with power they exult in the sacrifices — they who make even the wide Heaven and Earth tremble and fill the fountain when they have gone forth in their might.
For the Maruts are discerners of the singer, guides of the worshipper's thought. Today, well pleased, sit on our sacred grass in the assemblies for your refreshment.
No others shine as these Maruts do, glittering with their golden ornaments, their weapons, their bodies. Adorning Heaven and Earth with all-manner shapes, they smear the same ointment for their own beauty.
Aside from us let that lightning of yours be, O Maruts, whatever offense we mortals may commit. May we not come under its stroke, O adorable ones; let your most kindly grace be ours.
Even in the fray delight us here, O Maruts, blameless, pure, and purifying. O adorable ones, protect us with your graces; send us forward with prizes for our flourishing.
Let the praised Maruts, heroes, come with all their names to our oblations. Grant us offspring of immortal kind; seize riches, cheerful bounties.
Come, O praised Maruts, with all your aids to the lords of Soma for complete protection. They who by themselves increase our hundredfold strength — do ye protect us always with blessings.
Sing praise to the troop that exults together, mighty in the dwelling of the divine. By their greatness they make Heaven and Earth tremble and reach the vault of heaven, away from Nirṛti's domain.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even your birth, O Maruts, is fearsome with its violence — dreadful, fiercely wrathful, tireless ones. They who surpass all with their greatness and strength — all that has sight of the sky fears at your passage.
Grant great vigor to the bountiful ones; the Maruts have indeed enjoyed our good praise. A pathless road does not foil the creature; lead us forward with your desirable aids.
From you, O Maruts, the inspired poet gains a hundredfold; from you the horse becomes enduring and thousandfold. From you the sovereign ruler slays Vṛtra; let that gift of yours be proclaimed, O shakers.
I seek that company of the bountiful Rudra; will the Maruts return to us again? Whatever offense was turned away, whatever was brought to light — we seek forgiveness of that from the swift ones.
In speech this goodly praise of bountiful ones goes forth; let the Maruts enjoy this hymn. Turn hatred far away from us, O bulls; do ye protect us always with blessings.
Him whom you protect here and there, O gods, and him whom you guide — to him, O Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Maruts, grant shelter.
Under your protection daily, O gods, he who sacrifices with devotion passes beyond his foes. He who offers to you for his choosing passes beyond his home and wins great refreshments.
Not even the last of you does Vasiṣṭha despise. Today, O Maruts, all of you, willingly, drink together at our Soma pressing.
Your aid fails not in battles for him to whom you, O heroes, grant it. May your ever-fresher grace turn toward us; come swiftly, you who are eager to drink.
O Maruts of impetuous bounty, do come and bring the food-draughts for drinking. These oblations are offered to you; I give them with goodwill — do not go elsewhere.
Come and sit on our sacred grass, and as helpers give us the desirable wealth. Unerring Maruts, in the sweet Soma draught, be gladdened here with Svāhā.

title: Rigveda
text:
Adorning their own bodies, like blue-backed swans they flew here. The whole troop settled around me — heroes joyful and exulting at the Soma-pressing.
He who, O Maruts, maliciously plans against us, who wishes to slay us across our thoughts, O Vasus — may he loose himself into the noose of deceit; smite him with the most burning stroke.
O Sāntapana Maruts, enjoy this oblation; under your protection, O destroyers of enemies.
O Maruts, masters of the household, come; do not be absent. Under your protection, O liberal givers.
Here and here I invoke you, O Maruts — self-strong seers, bright as the skin of the sun — to the sacrifice.
We worship the three-eyed one, fragrant, increaser of flourishing. As a cucumber is freed from its stalk, may I be released from death — not from immortality.
What sinless truth you speak today, O Sūrya, rising to Mitra and Varuṇa — may we be dear to Aditi among the gods, praising you, O Aryaman.
This Sūrya, the man-beholding, rises up for both of you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, over the earth. Guardian of all things moving and still, beholding among mortals the straight and the crooked.
He yoked the seven bay mares from his station that carry Sūrya, the bright-rayed ones. Mitra-Varuṇa seized their dwellings — he who surveys births together as if a herd.
The honey-sweet refreshments have risen for you both; Sūrya has climbed the bright ocean. For him the Ādityas clear the paths — Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa in accord.
These are indeed the punishers of abundant falsehood — Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa. These have grown strong in the house of Ṛta, benign sons of Aditi, inviolable.
These Mitra and Varuṇa, hard to deceive, rouse even the unthinking with their powers. Guiding one toward right wisdom, even through straits they lead by good paths.
These, sleepless watchers of heaven and earth, guide even the thoughtless one. Even in the desert there is a ford in the river; may they carry us across the expanse of this flood.

title: Rigveda
text:
In that auspicious shelter which Aditi guards, which Mitra and Varuṇa grant to the liberal sacrificer — therein placing offspring and progeny, may we swift ones not commit offense against the gods.
He who has been swayed by Varuṇa — let him worship away from the altar with priestly calls whatever sins he bears. May Aryaman cut the foe away; O bulls, free the world for the liberal one.
Their encounter is always fearsome; with secret power they overcome. The bulls tremble in fear of you; by the might of wisdom do you show grace to us.
He who has worshipped to win goodwill for the brahman — to win food, the highest wealth — may the bountiful lords suppress the wrath of the noble one and make a wide and well-founded abode.
O Mitra-Varuṇa, divine ones, this priestly office has been performed for you both in the sacrifices. Carry us through all difficulties; do ye protect us always with blessings.
Up goes the eye of Varuṇa, bright-faced and all-pervading — the Sun, spreading wide, who surveys all beings; he perceives the wrath that is among mortals.
For you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, that wise and far-famed one of true order sends forth his hymns; you two, of excellent power, have supported his prayers — as with creative force you fulfil the years.
From the wide earth and from the lofty and vast heaven, O Mitra-Varuṇa of liberal gifts, you have set your spies among the plants and peoples — watching unblinking from the place whence they arose.
Declare the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa — their might has filled both worlds with its greatness. The months of those who offer no sacrifice pass without heroic issue; but the one whose thought is sacrifice carries his community through.
All these worlds, O mighty bulls, are your domain; in them no wondrous portent or goblin is unseen. The wicked among men who follow deception — your secret works have not gone unobserved by you.

title: Rigveda
text:
I magnify your rite and call upon you both, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with reverences and earnest petition; may these new hymns, composed for the poem, delight you — prayers fashioned and offered to you.
This priestly service, O Mitra-Varuṇa, has been rendered to you both at the sacrifices. Carry us through all difficulties; guard us ever with blessings.
The Sun has risen on high, ascending with his broad blazing rays over all the manifold origins of humankind; shining equally across the sky he is seen — fashioned by wisdom, made excellent by his makers.
Rise, O Sūrya, before our dwellings as before, with these hymns, with these swift steeds as your paths; speak forth our guiltlessness to Mitra and Varuṇa, to Aryaman and to Agni.
May Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni — keepers of holy order — open to us a thousand refreshing streams; may the gleaming ones bestow on us the highest gift of praise, and may they, when glorified, satisfy our desire.
O Heaven-and-Earth, O Aditi, protect us — you to whom those of beautiful birth have been born, high and great ones; may we not incur the wrath of Varuṇa or Vāyu, nor of Mitra who is most dear to men.
Stretch out your arms for our life; sprinkle our pasture-land with ghee. Make us heard among our people, O you two youths — hear our call, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as I invoke you.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us wide scope for ourselves and our offspring; may all paths be easy-going for us; guard us ever with blessings.
Up rises the bountiful, all-seeing Sun, common to all mankind; the divine eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, who has spread away the darkness as if it were a skin.
Up rises the great impeller of people, the mighty banner, the flood of the Sun — seeking to set the common wheel in motion, when the bay steed is yoked and draws at the pole.
Blazing forth from the lap of the Dawns, he rises, praised by the singers; this god Savitṛ has pleased me — he who does not diminish the common ordinance.

title: Rigveda
text:
The golden ornament of heaven, the far-sighted, the swift, the brilliant, rises with his goal afar; now, driven forth by the Sun, men set out on their journeys and accomplish their tasks.
Where the immortals have fashioned his way — he follows the path like a falcon swooping down; at the rising of the Sun we honor you two, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with reverences and oblations.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us wide scope for ourselves and our offspring; may all paths be easy-going for us; guard us ever with blessings.
Dwelling in heaven above the realm of earth, may the streaming libations of ghee be offered to you both. May Mitra and Aryaman of noble birth, the good king, the good ruler Varuṇa, delight in our oblation.
Come hither, you two kings, great guardians of holy order, lords of the rivers, rulers — come to us; O Mitra-Varuṇa of swift bestowal, send down to us refreshing food and rain from heaven.
May Mitra, Varuṇa and the noble god Aryaman lead us forth by the safest paths; may none harm Sudās when he speaks — may we rejoice in nourishment, guarded by the gods.
He who fashions for you in his mind this seat of honor, who holds his thought upright and sustains it — drench him, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with ghee; you two kings, satisfy him with good dwellings.
This praise, O Varuṇa, this hymn, is dedicated to you and Mitra, pure as soma for Vāyu; protect our thoughts, grasp our minds; guard us ever with blessings.
At the rising of the Sun I call upon Mitra and upon Varuṇa of pure might with well-spoken hymns — whose lordly power is imperishable and supreme, both perceived and advancing in the journey of all.
For they are the lords of the gods, those two nobles; may they make our dwellings vigorous with strength. May we, O Mitra-Varuṇa, attain to you two — where heaven and the days nourish and delight.

title: Rigveda
text:
You two have many snares and are barriers of falsehood, hard to cross for the mortal enemy; along the path of holy order, O Mitra-Varuṇa, may we cross difficulties as if by boat across the waters.
Come, O Mitra-Varuṇa, be pleased with our oblation; sprinkle our pasture-land with ghee and with refreshing food; bestow upon the people here the best of gifts; fill us with the fair waters of heaven.
This praise, O Varuṇa, this hymn, is dedicated to you and Mitra, pure as soma for Vāyu; protect our thoughts, grasp our minds; guard us ever with blessings.
Let our mighty praise go forth to Mitra and Varuṇa, full of reverence — to the two born of great strength.
Those two gods of excellent discernment, the fathers of discernment, uphold all with their lordly greatness.
You two who guard the body and protect the person of singers — O Varuṇa, O Mitra, further our thoughts.
What blameless gift Mitra, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Bhaga send forth today at the rising of the Sun —
May that abode be well-aided; may the liberal ones, in their course, carry us beyond the trouble — those who lead us past distress.
And the self-sovereign Aditi, along with those who govern the uninjurable ordinance — those great kings are lords.
At the rising of the Sun I praise Mitra and Varuṇa, and Aryaman the destroyer of enemies.
This thought is for the golden wealth and the inviolable might; this inspired prayer is for the winning of the sacred drink.
May we be yours, O Varuṇa, yours, O Mitra, together with the generous patrons; may we hold fast nourishment and light.
Many are they, the eye of the Sun, Agni-tongued, increasers of holy order, who have governed with their thoughts the three assemblies, encompassing all things.
They who have established the year, the month, the day, the sacrifice, the night, and the sacred verse — Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman have attained to the sovereignty which none can approach; the kings have encompassed it.

title: Rigveda
text:
This we meditate upon for you today with well-spoken hymns at the rising of the Sun — that which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman bear together: you are the charioteers of holy order.
Keepers of holy order, born of holy order, increasers of holy order, awesome and haters of falsehood — in the most glorious shelter of your favor may we men and our patrons be.
Up goes that beautiful form visible from afar on the back of heaven — when the divine swift steed Etaśa carries it onward, sufficient for the sight of all.
Lord of every moving and stationary being, pervading all the realm alike — the seven bay mares in the chariot carry the Sun for the good of all.
That bright eye set in place by the gods rises high — may we see a hundred autumns; may we live a hundred autumns.
Come, O inviolable Varuṇa, and Mitra, splendidly, with your poetic powers, to drink the Soma.
With the forms of heaven, O Varuṇa and Mitra, come — you who are without deceit; drink the Soma eagerly.
Come hither, O Mitra-Varuṇa, delighting in the oblation, O lords; drink the Soma, O increasers of holy order.
To praise your chariot, O lords of men, with a mind full of oblation and devoted to the sacrifice — as a son speaks to his two fathers, so I address you who are like an envoy arousing two high-minded ones.
Agni has been kindled and blazes in our midst; even the borders of the darkness have become visible. The banner of Dawn in the east has been perceived — the daughter of heaven is being born in beauty.
The skilled invoker now follows you two, O Aśvins, the speakers of truth, with hymns as he raises his voice. Come hither along the ancient paths with your light-winning, wealth-laden chariot.
Now with yearning I call you two, O Aśvins, for help, when, at the pressing of the Soma, one desirous of wealth calls to you two who are sweet. May your strong horses bring you; drink the sweet draughts pressed here for us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Turn my eastward-directed, unfailing, wealth-seeking thought toward winning, O divine Aśvins. Help all the wise ones in the contest; grant us that, O lords of power, with your powers.
Help our thoughts, O Aśvins; may our seed among them be fruitful and shameless. Hastening to you in respect of our offspring and progeny, may we, rich in good gifts, come to the feast of the gods.
This treasure of sweetness, as in a former friendship, has been placed and given to us by you two. Come hither with a friendly mind and enjoy the oblation among the human peoples.
In one single draught, at the common yoke, your chariot goes around the seven streams; they do not tire, the vigorous ones yoked by the gods, those fleet ones who draw you at the pole.
Be inexhaustible to the generous ones who speed on with wealth to the gift of bounty, who press forward with true words to cross over kinship-obligations, mixing cattle-wealth with horse-wealth as their gifts.
Now hear my call, O two young ones; come, O Aśvins, on a path that brings refreshment. Bestow treasures and let the patrons grow old in honor; guard us ever with blessings.
Come with your bright, fair-horsed chariot, O wonder-working Aśvins, delighting in the hymns of one who longs for you; enjoy the oblations brought to you — come to us.
The intoxicating drinks have gone forth to you; come readily to enjoy my oblation; hear our invocations across the distance of the stranger's land.
Your swift-as-thought chariot sets out, O Aśvins, bearing a hundred aids across the realms of space — moving toward us, O you who have the Sun for your treasure.
When this pressing-stone, rising high, speaks for you the god-seekers, O Soma-presser, to you two — may the inspired singer turn to you with beautiful oblations.
Truly wondrous is your gift; keep the buffalo-drinker away from Atri — he who being dear to you places his trust in your protection.

title: Rigveda
text:
And that, O Aśvins, which was given to Cyavana as an oblation-gift approached you for protection — because you bestow special form and aid upon him.
And Bhujyu whom his companions, hard to live with, had abandoned in the midst of the sea — carry him out, O Aśvins, the one who is without a helper but longs for you.
Grant help even to the wolf that is in distress, and hear when Śaya calls upon you — you two who filled the barren cow with milk like water for a dry one with your powers, O Aśvins.
This singer wakes and praises with well-spoken hymns in the van of the Dawns, of good intention. May the inviolable cow enrich him with her milk; guard us ever with blessings.
Let your chariot come to us, O Aśvins — golden, filling the two worlds, drawn by bulls and horses; with its track of ghee, flashing with its wheel-rims, the lord of men who bears nourishment and wins prizes.
Spreading itself across the five regions, triple-thonged, moving with purpose, let it come harnessed; with which you two visit god-seeking peoples wherever you choose to direct your course, O Aśvins.
Come hither with your glorious fair horses, O wonder-workers; drink the honey-sweet treasure. Your chariot, moving with the wife beside it, drives back the ends of heaven with its wheel-tracks.
The Sun's daughter has chosen the glory of you two in the race; when you have aided the god-seeking one with your powers, your strength goes around the heat of the sun with your protection.
He who dresses at dawn as your charioteer — that chariot, as it is yoked, circles its track. With that, O Aśvins, at the shining forth of the Dawn for our wellbeing and ease, convey us to this sacrifice.
O two lords, thirsting like a buffalo-cow for lightning, come today to our pressing; for in many places men call upon you with their thoughts — may no other god-seekers constrain you away from us.

title: Rigveda
text:
You two lifted Bhujyu who had fallen into the sea, carrying him up from the flood with your boats that do not tire, that do not swerve, that do not sink — with your wondrous craft, O Aśvins, bearing him across.
Now hear my call, O two young ones; come, O Aśvins, on a path that brings refreshment. Bestow treasures and let the patrons grow old in honor; guard us ever with blessings.
Come to us, O Aśvins of universal bounty; that place has been proclaimed for you on the earth. Like a prize-winning horse with the dog on its back standing ready — when you two sit down as in a fixed station.
That goodwill most dear to you two follows close; the hot oblation is shared in the house of the mortal; he who fills the rivers to the seas for you, harnessing as if with well-yoked steeds — even the swift one.
The stations which you two Aśvins have established — on the great rivers of heaven, among the plants, among the peoples — sitting on the peak of the mountain, carry refreshment to the worshipping mortal.
The gods have delighted in the plants and waters — what the sages attain to when fit for yoking — you two have laid many treasures down for us, looking after the former ages in order.
Even though you have heard many a prayer of the sages, O Aśvins, you look upon them; come and bring the best to the people; may the goodwill most dear to you be ours.
Whichever sacrifice to you, O Nāsatyā, has oblations, with prayers composed and fit for the assembly — come near and bring the best to Vasiṣṭha; these prayers are sung for you two.
This meditation, this song, O Aśvins — delight in this eloquent praise, O mighty bulls; these prayers have come longing for you two; guard us ever with blessings.
Away from her sister Uṣas night retreats; the dark one yields the path to the ruddy Dawn. O Aśvins, rich in horses, rich in cattle, we call upon you — ward off the shaft from us by day and night.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come near, O Aśvins, to the mortal worshipper, bringing bounty on your chariot. Drive away from us weakness and disease; protect us sweetly by day and night.
May the well-wishers, the mighty ones, turn your chariot at the breaking of this last dawn; come, O Aśvins, bearing wealth on the rein-grasping chariot yoked with horses joined by holy order.
That chariot of yours, O lords of men, the bearer, three-seated and richly laden, that reaches at dawn — come to us, O Nāsatyas, upon it, for your all-nourishing car draws near to us.
You two freed Cyavana from old age, you transported to Pedu the swift horse; you rescued Atri from distress and darkness, and placed Jāhuṣa within the yielding earth.
This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins; be pleased with this praise, O mighty bulls. These prayers have come to you, yearning for you — do you ever protect us with blessings.
Come, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot rich in cattle, rich in horses, splendid with many lights. All the teams attend upon you, you two who shine beautifully with desirable radiance.
Come hither to us with the gods, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot together with Uṣas. For ancestral friendships between you and us endure — the bond is the same; know that bond.
The praises of the Aśvins have arisen; the kindred hymns and the divine Uṣas attend on Heaven and Earth. The inspired priest declares aloud toward you, O Nāsatyas, who dwell in the two worlds.
When the dawns shine forth, O Aśvins, the poets bring prayers forward to you; divine Savitṛ has raised his light on high, and the fires blaze greatly with the kindling.
Come, O Nāsatyas, from behind and from before; O Aśvins, come from below and from above; come from all directions with the wealth belonging to the five peoples — do you ever protect us with blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
We have crossed to the farther shore of this darkness, offering praise as we strive toward the gods. The hymn calls upon the Aśvins, of many wonders, most excellent, immortal from of old.
The dear human Hotṛ has sat down, O Nāsatyas — he who worships and glorifies you. Taste the sweet drink close at hand, O Aśvins; the oblation-offerer calls upon you at the assemblies.
May we have ample breadth of paths for the sacrifice; be pleased with this praise, O mighty bulls. Vasiṣṭha, singing your praises with hymns, has awakened like one sent swiftly to meet you.
May those two conveyors come to our folk — the slayers of demons, assembled, with strong hands. The exhilarating draughts have met together; do not disregard us — come with favour.
Come, O Nāsatyas, from behind and from before; O Aśvins, come from below and from above; come from all directions with the wealth belonging to the five peoples — do you ever protect us with blessings.
These morning invocations call upon you, O Aśvins. I summon you here for help, O you rich in mighty deeds, for you go to every dwelling.
You two, O lords, have granted wondrous nourishment; urge it on for him who speaks gracious words. Turn your chariot hither with one accord; drink the sweet Soma.
Come near, adorn yourselves, drink the sweet drink, O Aśvins. O mighty bulls, rich in desired wealth, drink the milked draught — do not disregard us, come.
The horses that swiftly carry you two toward the home of the worshipper — come with swift-going steeds, O divine Aśvins, O lords, eager for us.
Indeed, as the Aśvins go, the refreshing foods attend the generous patrons. Grant to the bountiful ones lasting glory and shelter — and to us, O Nāsatyas.
Those who have gone forward unhurt, like chariots, protectors of men — they have grown mighty through their own power, O lords, and they dwell in a beautiful dwelling.

title: Rigveda
text:
Uṣas has shone forth, born of heaven, come disclosing her greatness by holy order. She has driven away the hateful, unwelcome darkness; most like the Aṅgiras-priests, she has set the paths in motion.
Be wakeful for us today for great well-being, O Uṣas; reach forth for great good fortune. Place on us, O goddess, brilliant and glorious wealth — O human goddess among mortals, eager for renown.
These brilliant, immortal rays of visible Uṣas have come; generating divine ordinances, filling the atmosphere, they have spread across the sky.
This one, yoking her team from afar, at once encircles the five settlements. Looking upon the appointed ways of the peoples, she is the daughter of heaven, the mistress of the world.
The youthful bride of the sun, rich in prize horses, mistress of brilliant treasure and riches, praised by sages, O bountiful one — Uṣas shines forth, hymned by the bearers of oblation.
The ruddy, bright horses of the glittering Dawn were seen carrying Uṣas; she journeys in her shining chariot, all-adorned, bestowing treasure on the pious worshipper.
True among the true, great among the great, divine goddess among the adorable gods — breaking open the pens, giving gifts belonging to the cows, the cattle have lowed back in answer to Uṣas.
Now bestow on us, O Uṣas, a treasure rich in cattle, rich in heroes, rich in horses and much nourishment. Do not make our sacred grass a reproach among men — do you ever protect us with blessings.
The immortal, universal light has risen; divine Savitṛ, all-knowing, has ascended. By the will of the gods the eye was born — Uṣas has made all of the world visible.
The paths of the gods have appeared before me, unfailing, adorned with riches. The banner of Uṣas appeared in the east; she has come, facing toward us, over the dwellings.

title: Rigveda
text:
Many indeed were those days in the past at the earlier rising of the sun, from which Uṣas has wandered about like a lover — yet she is never seen striving to return.
Those ancient seers, righteous and wise, were feast-companions of the gods. Our fathers found the hidden light; with true incantations they brought forth the dawns.
Gathered together in the same pen they know one another and do not strive against each other — they do not transgress the ordinances of the gods, unfailing as they move with riches.
The Vasiṣṭhas, waking at dawn, praise thee with hymns, O auspicious one, having glorified thee. O Uṣas, leader of cattle, mistress of bounty, O nobly born, shine forth first, age gracefully.
This Uṣas, leader of bounty and gracious words, shining, is praised by the Vasiṣṭhas; bestowing on us long-famed wealth — do you ever protect us with blessings.
She has shone forth like a youthful girl, rousing all that lives to move. The fire has been kindled for the kindling of men; driving away the darkness, she has made the light.
Facing all, she has arisen in full breadth, wearing her gleaming robe and shining bright. Gold-coloured, fair to behold for the beautiful to look upon, the mother of kine, leader of days, she has shone.
Eye of the gods, auspicious, bearing the white horse of beautiful appearance — Uṣas was seen, made manifest by her rays, with brilliant gifts, shining over all the world.
Shining near your bounty, drive the foe afar; make for us a wide pasture free from fear. Drive away enmity, bring riches, urge your bounty, O bountiful one, toward the singer.
Shine upon us, O Uṣas, goddess, with your finest rays, extending our life. Bestowing on us refreshment, O all-choosing one, and a bounty rich in cattle, rich in horses, rich in chariots.
You whom the Vasiṣṭhas magnify, O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, nobly born, with their thoughts — do thou bestow upon us sublime and lofty wealth — do you ever protect us with blessings.

title: Rigveda
text:
The first banners have appeared; the anointing beams of this Dawn spread upward. O Uṣas, bring to us wealth on your great, luminous chariot drawn hitherward.
The kindled fire blazes in her honour; the inspired priests hymn her with their thoughts. Uṣas comes with light, the goddess, driving away all darkness and ill.
There, those shining dawns were seen in the east, stretching out their light. They brought forth the sun, the sacrifice, the fire; the hateful darkness has gone away to the west.
She, the bountiful daughter of heaven, has become visible; all behold the shining Uṣas. She has mounted the chariot, harnessed by its own power, which the well-yoked horses draw.
To you today, with good thoughts, may our bountiful patrons and we ourselves awaken. Rejoice in the shining Uṣases — do you ever protect us with blessings.
Uṣas has shone forth, opening the paths of the peoples, awakening the five human settlements. She has climbed the light with well-visible bulls; the sun has opened wide the two worlds with its gaze.
They adorn the nights at the ends of heaven; like harnessed folk the Uṣases strive onward. The cows for her turn the darkness round; she extends the light like Savitṛ's arms.
Uṣas has arisen, most Indra-like, most bountiful; she has brought forth glories for well-being. The divine daughter of heaven, most like the Aṅgiras-priests, apportions riches to the pious.
Grant us, O Uṣas, as much bounty as you have given to your singers when being praised. You who, at the bull's roar, opened wide the firm doors of the mountain.
Spurring god after god to grant bounty, sending forth gracious words toward us — shining forth, do thou set our thoughts toward winning gain — do you ever protect us with blessings.
The Vasiṣṭha priests, the inspired ones, first awakened Uṣas with their hymns and songs — she who turns the two realms on all sides and reveals all worlds.

title: Rigveda
text:
This very one, bestowing new life, hiding the darkness with her light — Uṣas has awakened. She goes in front, the youthful one, unabashed; she has made the sun, the sacrifice, the fire appear.
May the auspicious Uṣases always shine forth for us, rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in heroes. Milking ghee, satiated on every side — do you ever protect us with blessings.
She is seen coming forth, the Daughter of Heaven as she rises; she spreads the great waters wide for sight to behold, the gracious one makes light and dispels the darkness.
The Sun releases the ruddy cows together as he rises, bright like a burning star. At thy dawning, O Uṣas, and at the arising of the Sun, may we come together to share in our allotted portion.
We, alert and eager, have greeted thee, O Uṣas, Daughter of Heaven; who, all-triumphant, bringest many things worthy of desire — joy as a jewel to the worshipper.
She who, rising, with her greatness illumines all for sight, O Goddess, that heaven's brilliance may be seen — may we be sharers in her treasure, as sons are in their mother's.
Bring that wondrous, most far-famed bounty, O Uṣas; that portion for mortals which belongs to thee, O Daughter of Heaven — bestow it, and let us partake of it.
Fame, immortality, wealth of possessions, prizes rich in cattle — bestow these upon the liberal lords, upon us. May Uṣas, the rouser of the bountiful, rich in true speech, shine forth and drive away all foes.
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant great shelter to our people for the sacrifice. May we conquer in battles the obstinate foe who seeks to overcome him long-lauded in prayer.
One of you is called Samrāj, the other Svarāj; both are great — Indra and Varuṇa, great in wealth. All the gods in the highest heaven have joined together your strength and your might, O you two bulls.

title: Rigveda
text:
With your power you clove open the channels of the waters; you drove the Sun, the lord, aloft in the sky. O Indra and Varuṇa, in the exhilaration of this sage's soma, speed his unimpeded thoughts; let his prayers flow freely.
You alone are the bearers in battles and in wars; you two are wisely known at the impelling of prosperity. Lords of both kinds of wealth, you craftsmen — O Indra and Varuṇa, easy to invoke, we call upon you.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when you by your greatness made all these creatures of the universe — Mitra serves Varuṇa with security, and the other, the mighty one, goes in glory with the Maruts.
For Varuṇa's great tribute the splendour and fixed might which is his own are measured out. The one transcends the unrestrained assailant; with little he makes the other choose the many.
No anguish, no evil deeds, no torment from any quarter can reach that mortal, O Indra and Varuṇa, to whose sacrifice you two go and feast. No mortal's affliction can overtake him.
Come hither, O heroes, with divine protection; hear my call if you take pleasure in it. Grant us, O Indra and Varuṇa, that friendship of yours, or that alliance — your gracious favour.
Be our vanguard fighters in every contest, O Indra and Varuṇa, with the strength of your peoples. When men on both sides call upon you in the contest, in the battles for offspring and descendants.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us radiance and great far-spreading shelter. We meditate upon the unfailing light of Aditi that augments holy order, and upon the glorifying word of the god Savitṛ.
Gazing upon your alliance and seeking cows, the Pṛthupārśvas went eastward. Slay both the Dāsa and Ārya foes; protect Sudās, O Indra and Varuṇa, with your aid.
Where the banner-bearing warriors come together, where in the contest something dear is won, where the heaven-seeing worlds tremble with fear — there speak on our behalf, O Indra and Varuṇa.

title: Rigveda
text:
The brilliant ends of earth were seen together; the battle-cry rose to heaven, O Indra and Varuṇa. Enemies of the peoples have stood against me — come hither with protection, ye who hear our call.
O Indra and Varuṇa, winning an irresistible breakthrough with your weapons, protect Sudās. Hear the prayers of these men along with their oblations; true was the office of the Tṛtsus' priest.
The hostile enemies of the noble one press upon him with their spells, O Indra and Varuṇa. You two are kings of both kinds of wealth — therefore protect us in the supreme heaven.
Both parties called upon you in the contests — Indra and Varuṇa — for the winning of wealth. Where he was pressed hard by ten kings, protect Sudās together with the Tṛtsus.
Ten kings assembled, offering no sacrifice, yet could not vanquish Sudās, O Indra and Varuṇa. True was the praise of the table-companions among men; the gods were theirs at their invocations of the gods.
In the Battle of the Ten Kings, when all pressed round, Indra and Varuṇa aided Sudās. Where the Tṛtsus, white-robed and knotted-haired, devout in thought and rich in prayer, spread out with homage.
One of you smites the foes in battles; the other protects the sacred ordinances for ever. We invoke you both, O mighty bulls, with well-fashioned praises — grant us shelter, O Indra and Varuṇa.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us radiance and great far-spreading shelter. We meditate upon the unfailing light of Aditi that augments holy order, and upon the glorifying word of the god Savitṛ.
I would turn you two kings toward our sacrifice with oblations and acts of reverence, O Indra and Varuṇa. She who holds clarified butter in her two arms, manifold in form, courses around of her own accord.
Heaven quickens your great sovereignty, you who bind with bands without a cord. May we be turned aside from Varuṇa's wrath; may Indra make a wide space for us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Make our sacrifice beautiful in the assemblies, make our prayers celebrated among the patrons of worship. Let god-sped wealth come near us; lead us forward with your longed-for aids.
Grant to us, O Indra and Varuṇa, a wealth all-excellent, rich in substance, abounding in plenty. The Āditya destroys those who transgress his ordinances; the immeasurable hero shares out his goods.
This my hymn has reached Indra and Varuṇa; rushing swiftly it has helped in progeny and offspring. Possessed of good treasure may we come to the feast of the gods. Preserve us evermore with your blessings.
I purify for you both a demon-free prayer, pouring out soma for Indra and for Varuṇa. Like a goddess whose face is clarified butter — like Uṣas — may those two protect us on our path in the encounter.
They indeed compete at this invocation of the gods, those upon whose banners the lightning-bolts fall. Smite those enemies, O Indra and Varuṇa, with your arrows, scattering them in all directions.
Even the self-luminous divine Waters at their seats have held Indra and Varuṇa as their deity. The one sustains the peoples spread apart; the other smites foes that cannot be withstood.
Let him be a wise-minded, truth-knowing hotar, who O Ādityas, reverently approaches you with your strength. The one who has turned to you for aid with oblations — let him indeed be endowed with prosperity.
This my hymn has reached Indra and Varuṇa; rushing swiftly it has helped in progeny and offspring. Possessed of good treasure may we come to the feast of the gods. Preserve us evermore with your blessings.
The wise know well by his greatness — he who propped asunder the two great worlds, heaven and earth. He thrust high and aloft the lofty vault of heaven; he spread out the starry firmament on two sides, and the earth too.

title: Rigveda
text:
I shall commune with my own self about that — when shall I be within Varuṇa's grace? When will he, unangered, enjoy my oblation? When shall I, joyful, behold his mercy?
I ask what that sin is, O Varuṇa — longing to see, I come to question the wise. The seers have told me the same thing: 'Varuṇa himself is wrathful toward you.'
What was the chief transgression, O Varuṇa, that you wish to slay your praising friend? Declare that to me, O hard-to-gain, self-sustaining one; I shall come swiftly to propitiate you with homage, free from this.
Release us from the inherited sins of our fathers; release also those which we ourselves have committed in our own bodies. Release, O King, as a thief who has satisfied himself with cattle — release Vasiṣṭha as a calf from a rope.
It was not my own will, O Varuṇa; it was intoxication, dice, anger, thoughtlessness. The older one is present near to the younger; even sleep is a promoter of sin.
I shall do service to the bountiful one as a slave, sinless, to the god who is wroth. The noble god has enlightened the unperceiving; the wise one spurs on the inspired to wealth.
May this hymn of praise, O Varuṇa, self-sustaining one, abide well lodged within your heart. May there be welfare for us in repose, and welfare in action. Preserve us evermore with your blessings.
Varuṇa carved out paths for the Sun; he spread out the great flood of the rivers of the sea. Acting in accord with holy order, like a released racehorse, he made the great streams flow for the days.
The wind is your breath; it has renewed the realm. Like a restless beast pasturing on the meadow, these two great expanses, the earth and heaven, abide between — all your dear dwelling-places, O Varuṇa.
Varuṇa's keen-eyed spies look out from both the well-adorned worlds, heaven and earth. The holders of holy order, the seers wise in sacrifice, the far-sighted ones who speed thought forward — they behold.

title: Rigveda
text:
Varuṇa has spoken to me, the wise one; the inviolable cow bears thrice seven names. The knowing one shall not declare the hidden secrets of the track — teaching the inspired poet of the later age.
Three heavens are set within him; three earths, the upper ones arranged sixfold. The wise King Varuṇa has made this golden swing in the sky for splendour.
Varuṇa has stood over Sindhu like heaven, like a white drop, a mighty beast. Deep-voiced, he who measures out the realm, the king of all that exists, the lord of good protection.
He who shows mercy even to one who has sinned — may we be sinless before Varuṇa. Thriving in accord with the ordinances of Aditi, preserve us evermore with your blessings.
Purify and bring the most beloved prayer to Varuṇa, O Vasiṣṭha, to the bountiful one — he who makes the worshipful, the thousandfold blessed, the mighty bull turn toward us.
Having gone to his sight, I shall contemplate the face of Agni and of Varuṇa. When upon a rock the guardian of heaven's intoxicant would lead my form to see the radiance.
When Varuṇa and I shall embark upon the boat and drive it out to the middle of the ocean, when we shall roam upon the ridges of the waters — shall we then swing together on the swing for splendour?
Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha in the boat; by his great deeds he made him a seer, skilled in works. The inspired lord, on the bright days which the heavens have stretched out and which the dawns have stretched, glorified his praiser.
Where have those friendships of ours gone? We two used to keep companionship without hostility, as in former times. I have entered your great, thousanddoored, self-sustaining house, O Varuṇa.
He who is your eternal companion and dear one, O Varuṇa, yet commits transgressions against you — let us not, being sinful, enjoy your worship, O holy one; give shelter to the poet who praises you.

title: Rigveda
text:
May Varuṇa release from us the fetters while we dwell in these firm abodes. Winning the favour from the lap of Aditi, preserve us evermore with your blessings.
May I not go, O King Varuṇa, into the house made of clay. Have mercy, O thou of good dominion, have mercy.
When I go about trembling like an inflated bladder, O lord of the stone-pressing — have mercy, O thou of good dominion, have mercy.
Through lack of strength, O shining one, I have gone against your will in my wretchedness. Have mercy, O thou of good dominion, have mercy.
Thirst has found the singer standing in the middle of the waters. Have mercy, O thou of good dominion, have mercy.
Whatever transgression against the divine order we mortals commit among the divine people, O Varuṇa — whatever of your ordinances we have violated through ignorance — do not injure us for that sin, O God.
The pure soma-draughts, sweet and pressed by the adhvaryus, have been prepared heroically for you two. Come hither with your teams, O Vāyu; drink the pressed soma juice for exhilaration.
He who has made the oblation reach you the master, the pure soma, O pure-drinking Vāyu — you make that man praiseworthy among mortals; again and again a champion is born to him.
These two worlds, heaven and earth, were born for wealth; the divine Dhiṣaṇā sets the god for wealth. Then his own teams accompany Vāyu, and the white one, the holder of goods, in the distinction.
As Uṣas shines forth, pure on the bright days, the meditating ones have found the wide light. Even the cowpen the Uśijs have opened wide; for them the waters have flowed onward from day to day.
They, meditating with a truthful mind and yoked with their own will, drive onward. The refreshments accompany your chariot that carries heroes, O Indra and Vāyu, you two lords.
Those who are lords and who establish for us the sun with cows, horses, goods, and gold — may the wise lords prevail for Indra and Vāyu with a full span of life, with steeds and heroes in battles.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like coursing steeds seeking fame, the Vasiṣṭhas invoke Indra and Vāyu with fine praises. Striving for the prize, we call upon you for your own protection. Preserve us evermore with your blessings.
Were there indeed those blameless gods of old who waxed great by homage? They, for Vāyu's sake and for distressed Manu, made the Dawn depart by means of the Sun.
Like willing messengers, like unwounding guardians, the months are your paths, and many autumns have been. O Indra-Vāyu, this hymn of praise comes to you seeking your grace and new well-being.
The wise and radiant one, who increases wealth and whose lustre clings to rich food, accompanies the swift teams. For Vāyu's sake those men of one accord spread abroad, and performed all things for the welfare of their offspring.
So far as the vigour of the body, so far as the strength, so far as the men contemplating with vision — O pure drinkers Indra-Vāyu, drink the pure Soma pressed for us; be seated on this sacred grass.
Harnessing your desirable steeds, the swift teams, O Indra-Vāyu, come hither on one chariot. For this is the first portion of the mead offered to you; be satisfied and release your bounty upon us.
Whatever hundred, whatever thousand swift teams belonging to you, O Indra-Vāyu, all-desirable, attend you — with these most excellent ones come hither, O heroes, and drink of the mead that is offered.
We Vasiṣṭhas, like steeds craving renown, invoking Indra-Vāyu with well-wrought praises, seeking the contest, call you for protection. Do you always guard us with blessings.
Come, Vāyu, O pure drinker, adorn yourself for us — your thousand swift teams are all-desirable. To you, O god, I bring the invigorating intoxicating drink of which you hold the right of first draught.
The swift presser has stood forth at the sacrifices to press the Soma for Indra and Vāyu to drink. When the adhvaryus, devoted to the gods, bring forward with their acts the first portion of the mead for you two —

title: Rigveda
text:
With whatever swift teams you advance, O Vāyu, toward the worshipper for enjoyment in the house — yoke for us wealth rich in good food, yoke a hero, and cattle-wealth and horse-wealth as a gift.
O Vāyu, those who bring joy to Indra, ungodlike, ever goading the noble foemen — smiting the obstructions together with generous patrons, may we, having overcome foes in battle with men, prevail.
Come to our rite with your hundredfold swift teams, come to the sacrifice with your thousandfold. O Vāyu, rejoice at this pressing. Do you always guard us with blessings.
May Indra-Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, take pleasure today in this pure, newly-born hymn. For I invoke you both with full voice — you who are easy to call; do you two, most eager to grant, immediately bestow the prize.
You two have truly been prosperous, jointly waxing in strength, growing together in might. Ruling over abundant wealth and rich pasture, mix for us the mighty, impetuous prize.
When the eloquent, wise men went to the assembly of the prize-winners, seeking guidance through their prayers — like steeds straining toward the goal, those men call upon Indra-Agni.
The sage, seeking guidance through his hymns, implores the glorious wealth that falls to the first share. O Indra-Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fine bolt, advance us further with new gifts.
When the two great shining ones contend together, competing in the gain-of-heroes with self-radiant splendour — strike down the ungodly in the assembly together with the godly, as a body pressing the Soma.
Come to us now at this Soma-pressing for our well-being, O Indra-Agni. For you have always paid attention to us; may I win you ever and again through the prizes.
O Agni, kindled with this oblation and homage, speak to Mitra, to Varuṇa, to Indra. Whatever sin we have committed — forgive that well; may Aryaman and Aditi loosen that bond.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, through these swiftly performed rites, may we attain the prizes in concert with both of you. May Indra not pass us by, nor Viṣṇu, nor the Maruts. Do you always guard us with blessings.
This ancient praise-song to you two, O Indra-Agni, from this mind, has been born like rain from a cloud.
Hear the call of the singer, O Indra-Agni, take pleasure in the hymns. As lords, swell our prayers with your favour.
O Indra-Agni, do not deliver us, O heroes, to wickedness, nor to blame. Do not abandon us to reproach.
We raise up the great homage and the well-fashioned praise to Indra and Agni, seeking help through prayer and song.
For the eloquent men have ever thus invoked you two for help, in the press of battle, for the winning of the prize.
We who are eloquent, offering our libations, call upon you two with our hymns, seeking to win the sacrifice and the bounty.
Come to us with your protection, O Indra-Agni, overcomers of men. Let no evil-speaker have power over us.
Let no treachery of any hostile mortal injure us. O Indra-Agni, bestow shelter upon us.
The wealth rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses — that which we implore of you two, O Indra-Agni, may we win that.
When the men who worship with horses call on Indra-Agni at the pressing of the Soma —
Those two who are greatest slayers of Vṛtra — they, rejoiced even by the hymn, are worshipped with praises and with lauds.
Those two — let them strike down with their weapon the evil-speaking, ill-knowing, demon-possessed mortal; the greedy one — strike him down with your weapon; the flood-like one — strike him down with your weapon.
This Sarasvatī, the iron-built fortress, surges forward with her flood and nurturing stream. Pressing onwards like a charioteer she goes, surpassing in greatness all other rivers and streams.

title: Rigveda
text:
Sarasvatī alone has perceived among rivers — pure, flowing from the mountains to the sea; perceiving the wealth of the abundant world, she has yielded milk and ghee for Nahuṣa.
She has grown mightily among the women, a bull-calf, a bull among the sacred females. She bestows the prize-winning horse upon the generous patrons, and spreads herself wide for the winning.
And may that fair Sarasvatī, well-pleased, hearken to us at this sacrifice; coming with those who reverently bow their knees in homage, may she, even with wealth as her companion, be supreme among friends.
O Sarasvatī, as we pour oblations to you, be pleased with this hymn of praise offered from our homage. May we, established in your most beloved shelter, stand under you as under the shelter of a tree.
O Sarasvatī, this Vasiṣṭha has thrown open for you the two doors of Ṛta, O beautiful one. Increase the one who praises you; grant him prizes, O bright goddess. Do you always guard us with blessings.
I shall sing a great word of lordly power — O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Sarasvatī alone with well-wrought praises, with hymns to both worlds.
Since the Pūrus dwell in your two bright, mighty floods, O Sarasvatī — be our protectress, allied with the Maruts, and urge forward the bounty of the generous ones.
The auspicious Sarasvatī, wholly free from flaw, the prize-bearing, shall bring about what is auspicious. Being praised as Jamadagni praises, and lauded as Vasiṣṭha lauds.
Seeking wives, O first-born ones, seeking sons, O liberal givers — we invoke Sarasvat.
O Sarasvat, your waves that are sweet as honey and dripping with ghee — with these become our protector.
May we partake of the swollen breast of Sarasvat who is visible to all, receiving offspring and nourishment.
At the sacrifice, in the seat of men of heaven and earth, where the godly men rejoice — where the Soma-pressings are pressed for Indra, and the first nourishment and delight come —

title: Rigveda
text:
We choose the divine aids; may Bṛhaspati be our great ally and friend, that we may stand blameless before the bountiful one who gives to us from afar like a father.
Him, the eldest, the most pleasant lord of prayer, I praise with homage and oblations. May the great divine praise cleave to Indra, who is the king of the prayer that is god-made.
May Bṛhaspati, who is all-desirable and most dear, take his seat in our place. May he grant the desire of wealth with heroic offspring, and lead us safely past all unbroken dangers.
These immortals, ancient-born, have set up that song of praise dear to the immortal. We invoke Bṛhaspati, the pure-voiced, worthy of worship, lord of households, unwounded.
Vigorous, ruddy horses carry Bṛhaspati, drawing together. His assembly-place too, clothed in a form red as the sun, is deep-dark in its strength, like a cloud.
He is pure, hundred-winged, cleansing, swift with a golden axe, winning the light. Bṛhaspati of good appearance, noble, is most capable of bringing the libation to many friends.
The two divine worlds, heaven and earth, mothers of the god, have increased Bṛhaspati by their greatness. May the power of friends, fit for mastery, make the prayer easy to ford and easy to sound for the lord of prayer.
O Lord of Prayer, this well-wrought prayer-hymn has been fashioned for you and for bolt-wielding Indra. Strengthen our thoughts, seize the full minds, consume the noble man's hostile treasures.
O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra are lords of heavenly and earthly wealth. Bestow riches on the one who praises, even on the one who sings your glory. Do you always guard us with blessings.
O Adhvaryus, offer the red-pressed, milked stalk to the bull of the peoples. Indra comes nearer than the wild ox to the drinking-place, ever going and seeking the pressed Soma.

title: Rigveda
text:
Whatever fair food you have accepted from of old, day by day you carry off his draught. O Indra, enjoying it with heart and mind, and longing, protect the Soma-draughts set forth.
At your very birth you drank the Soma for strength; your mother has proclaimed your greatness. O Indra, you spread out the wide atmosphere, and in battle you made room for the gods.
When you made those who deemed themselves great fight each other, and we overcame them with our arms repeatedly — when you, O Indra, surrounded by heroes, fight against them — may we win through you that battle of good fame.
I will proclaim the former deeds of Indra, and the new ones that the bountiful one has performed. When he overcame the ungodly magical powers, then the Soma became his alone.
All this world around you that is rich in cattle — all that you see with the eye of the Sun — you alone are the master of the cows, O Indra. May we partake of your offered wealth.
O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra are lords of heavenly and earthly wealth. Bestow riches on the one who praises, even on the one who sings your glory. Do you always guard us with blessings.
Growing beyond measure with your body, none attain to your greatness. We know your two realms of space and of earth, O Viṣṇu, god — you know the highest.
Neither one being born nor one already born, O Viṣṇu, god, has attained the farthest limit of your greatness. You have propped up the lofty, vast vault of heaven, and you have established the eastern direction of the earth.
You two have truly been rich in nourishment and cattle, rich in good pasture, conferring gifts upon Manu. O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds, you have established the earth on all sides with your pillars.
You two made wide room for sacrifice, giving birth to the Sun, to Dawn, to Fire. O heroes, you smashed the sorceries of the Dāsa Vṛṣaśipra in the battles.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra-Viṣṇu, you smashed the ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara. Together you slew a hundred and a thousand warriors of the irresistible Asura.
This great wisdom, growing great with power, with wide strides — I have offered you this hymn at assemblies, O Viṣṇu. O Indra, swell our refreshments in the communities.
O Viṣṇu, I make the vaṣaṭ-call to your mouth — O Śipiviṣṭa, take pleasure in my oblation. May my praises and my hymns increase you. Do you always guard us with blessings.
Now the mortal who worships and wishes to gain — who has offered to Viṣṇu of the wide stride — he who with a wholehearted mind has worshipped and sought to please this manly one —
O Viṣṇu of swift course, grant us a goodwill that is universal, never-failing, and a prayer — so that we may have the abundant well-being, the horse-rich and greatly-glorious wealth.
Three times has this god strode across this earth of a hundredfold abundance by his greatness. Let Viṣṇu be mightier than the mighty; for the name of this ancient one is terrible.
This Viṣṇu strode across this earth to grant it as a field to Manu. His peoples stand firm and immoveable; he of noble birth has made a broad dwelling.
This your name, O Śipiviṣṭa — your noble name — I, knowing your manifestations, proclaim today. I praise you who are mighty, stronger than the strong, ruling over this realm in the far distance.
What, O Viṣṇu, should be concealed by you, when you declare, 'I am Śipiviṣṭa'? Do not hide this form from us — that form in which you appeared of altered shape in the battle.
O Viṣṇu, I make the vaṣaṭ-call to your mouth — O Śipiviṣṭa, take pleasure in my oblation. May my praises and my hymns increase you. Do you always guard us with blessings.
Speak forth the three voices, light-tipped, those that milk this sweet-milking udder — he who makes the calf, the germ of plants, roars aloud as a bull, born at once.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who nourishes the plants, who rules the waters, who is lord of all that moves, O god — may he grant us threefold shelter and comfort, and the three-turning light for our own satisfaction.
From you the barren becomes fruitful, and from you the fertile one — this one has shaped the body as he willed. The mother receives the father's milk; by that the father grows, by that the son grows.
In him all beings stand; the three heavens have flowed in three ways, and the waters flow — three vessels, ladle-like, drip the honey-mead around the mighty one.
May this word be inmost in the heart of Parjanya the self-ruler, may he take joy in it. May the rains bring well-being upon us; may the herbs be well-beaded and god-protected.
He is the seed-sower, the bull of all the eternal ones; in him rests the Self of the moving and the standing. May that Ṛta protect me for a hundred autumns. Do you always guard us with blessings.
Sing forth to Parjanya, son of heaven, the bountiful. May he seek out pasture for us.
Parjanya — who makes the germ of the plants, of the cows, of the mares, of women.
To him — pour into his mouth the most honey-sweet oblation. May he bring us the combined refreshment of Iḷā.
Lying still for a year like Brāhmaṇas observing their vow, the frogs have raised their voice set in motion by Parjanya.
When the heavenly waters came over him — like a dry bladder lying in a pool — the voice of the frogs, like the lowing of cattle and the lowing of cows with calves, comes together here.
When the rains came down upon them as they were longing and thirsty at the coming of the rainy season, one approaches the other who is speaking, as a son approaches his father, making the akhkhalī sound.
One grasps the other of the two when, rejoicing at the flowing of the waters — when the frog rained upon leaps about, the spotted one mingles its voice with the green one.

title: Rigveda
text:
When one of them speaks the voice of the other like a pupil practising — everything of them, when you speak well on the waters, is like a season of their prosperity.
One of them is cow-lowing, one is goat-lowing, one is spotted, and one is green. Bearing the same name though different in form, they have patterned their voice in many ways as they speak.
Like Brāhmaṇas at the all-night Soma-feast, speaking all around like a full lake — that day of the year has come round on which the frogs have entered the rainy season.
The Brāhmaṇas, Soma-drinkers, have raised their voice, performing the annual prayer. The sweating adhvaryus heating the cauldron appear — as if none are hidden.
They have guarded the divine ordinance of the twelve months; these men do not transgress the season. At the coming of the rainy season in the year, the heated caldrons obtain their discharge.
The cow-lowing one has given, the goat-lowing one has given, the spotted one has given, the green one has given us goods. The frogs who give hundreds of cows extend their life at the thousandfold pressing.
O Indra-Soma, scorch the demon, crush it, hurl down those that increase darkness, O mighty ones. Cast them away from us, burn them up — strike them, drive away, and utterly destroy the devourers.
O Indra-Soma, let a heated cooking-pot of fire pursue the evil-speaker, the sinful one. Place an inescapable hatred upon the hater of prayer, the flesh-eater, the one of terrible glance, the kimīdin.
O Indra-Soma, pierce the evil-doers into the cave, into the darkness which has no foothold. May not one of them emerge from there again — let that wrathful strength of yours accomplish this.
O Indra-Soma, hurl down the weapon from heaven, the crusher from the earth upon the evil-speaker. Hew out the solar bolt from the mountains with which you smite the demon that has waxed great.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra-Soma, hurl from heaven with your fire-heated stone-smiting weapons, with your burning, ageless weapons, pierce the devourers in the ribs — let them go to silence.
