O Indra-Soma, may this thought encompass you on all sides, like a girth around a prize horse. With this oblation I send forth to you both — quicken these prayers as a king of men.
Remember with your smiting courses — slay the deceitful demon, the destroyer. O Indra-Soma, let there be no easy path for the evil-doer who at any time would harm us treacherously.
He who assails me as I go with a simple mind, attacking me with false words — like waters clasped by a shining sieve, let his speech be empty, O Indra, let him who sits there be a speaker of nothing.
Those who scatter the praise of the simple man with tricks, and those who corrupt the good with their crooked ways — may Soma deliver them to the serpent, or place them in the lap of Nirṛti.
O Agni, whoever would injure the taste of our food, or of our horses, of our cattle, of our bodies — the traitor, the thief, the one who commits theft, a little let him come — let him be abandoned with body and descendants.
Let him be far off with body and descendants; let all three earths be below him. O gods, let the glory of him wither who would harm us by day and he who does so by night.
To a person of discernment, the two speeches — truth and untruth — contend. Of these two, whichever is the truth, whichever is the more straight — that Soma protects; he slays the false.
Soma does not advance the crooked man, nor the warrior who holds power falsely. He slays the demon; he slays the speaker of falsehood — both of them lie in the snare of Indra.
If I have been a worshipper of false gods, O Agni, or have prayed to the gods in vain — why, O Jātavedas, are you angry with us? Let the treacherous speakers accompany Nirṛti to destruction.

title: Rigveda
text:
May I die today if I am a sorcerer, or if I have scorched any man's life-breath. Let him be torn asunder by ten heroes who calls me falsely a sorcerer.
He who calls me a sorcerer, a wizard, and he who being an impure demon claims 'I am pure' — let Indra smite him with his great weapon; let him fall to the lowest place of all beings.
She who roams like an owl by night, hiding her body with treachery — let her fall into an endless pit. May the pressing stones strike the demons with their sounds.
Spread out, O Maruts, searching through the peoples — seize and grind to pieces the demons. Those who have become birds and fly by night, and those who have placed treachery in the divine sacrifice —
Hurl down the stone of heaven, O Indra, sharpened by Soma, O bountiful one, sharpen it well. From east, from west, from below, from above — smite the demons with the mountain.
These — look, they fly about, the dog-wolves, seeking to harm inviolable Indra, the harmers. The Mighty One is sharpening the weapon against the slanderers; now he will let fly his bolt against the sorcerers.
Indra became the destroyer of sorcerers, the supreme one for those who were stealing the oblations as they sought to please. The Mighty One, like an axe splitting a forest, goes forth cleaving to pieces the demons.
Slay the owl-sorcerer, the young-owl-sorcerer, slay the dog-sorcerer, the cuckoo-sorcerer. Slay the eagle-sorcerer, the vulture-sorcerer — O Indra, crush the demons, O stone-crusher.
Let no demon harm us; let the pair of kimīdins, those who belong to the sorcerers, drive us away. May the earth protect us from earth-dangers; may the atmosphere protect us from heavenly dangers.
O Indra, slay the male sorcerer and also the female who is striking repeatedly with her magic. Let those with bent necks, the foolish-godded ones, be crushed — may they not see the Sun rising.

title: Rigveda
text:
Look around, look about — O Indra and Soma, be vigilant. Hurl your weapon at the demons, the thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
Praise nothing else, O friends, and suffer no harm; be a praiser of Indra the bull, attending him at the pressing; again and again recite the lauds.
Like a bull who charges without bend, like an ox bearing the plough-yoke unwearied — he who dispels enmity, who wins all over, most munificent, the ally of both sides.
Though these many peoples here invoke you diversely for help, let this our prayer, O Indra, be yours; may it be your strengthening through all the days.
The inspired poets of the people, the bards of noble rank, spread their hymns to you, O Maghavan; advance upon the many-formed prize, bring the booty nearest to us for our aid.
Not even for a great price would I give you away, O wielder of the stone; not for a thousand, not for ten thousand, O thunderbolt-bearer, not for a hundred, O hundred-gifted one.
You are more to me than a father, than a brother who withholds; even my mother you and wealth gratify equally, O Vasu, for the sake of riches and bounty.
Where are you, where do you go? Your mind wanders to many places. You are roused, O warrior, O destroyer of citadels — the Gāyatrā metres have gone forth.
Sing the Gāyatrā hymn to him, to him who has been quickened, the fort-destroyer; with these very metres may the thunderer come to sit upon the barhis of Kāṇva and may he smash the forts.
Those steeds of yours that are in tens, those in hundreds, those in thousands, your bulls that run swiftly — with those come quickly to us.
Today I call forth for the Gāyatrā-trembling one the cow that yields savours; Indra is the good milch-cow, another, the food of broad stream, well fashioned.
When the sun urged on Etaśa the fleet, winged like the wind, and the hundred-powered Indra conveyed Kutsa the son of Arjuna, tracking the undefeated Gandharva.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who even without prayer, before the collarbone could be pierced, is a joiner of joints, the Maghavan of many treasures, who repairs what has gone wrong.
May we not be like strangers, O Indra, remote from you, like abandoned forests; hard to satisfy, we, the stone-wielder's people, thought of wealth.
We pondered, lacking swift horses and lacking fodder, O Vṛtra-slayer; but once with your great bounty, O hero, may we exult following your laud.
If Indra would hearken to our laud, may the swift soma-drops that have flowed through the filter gladden him, him who grows mighty for Tugrya's descendants.
Come today, urged on to this joint praise, come from your friend's side; may the praise of the bountiful ones go before you — for you I desire excellent laud.
The pressers press the soma with stones; rinse it in the waters; men have clothed it as with a robe of cowhide and have drawn it from the flanks.
Whether from the earth or from the broad sky's luminous realm above, grow great with your body through this hymn of mine; O wise one, fill what has been born.
Press out for Indra the most intoxicating, most excellent soma; may the mighty one satiate himself with it, with every thought urging it like a racer for the prize.
Let me not make you weary, O Indra, always begging with my songs over the soma; you who rage like a wild beast at the pressings — who would not beg the sovereign lord?
The fierce rapture impelled by exhilaration, with fierce might, the overcomer of all, the one shaken from ecstasy — for in rapture he gives to us.
The god grants many desirable things to the mortal who has offered; he gives to the one who presses soma and to one who praises — praised by all, unharmed in renown.
Come, O Indra, rejoice with your brilliant bounty, O god; fill your broad belly with the soma draughts together with your drinking companions, as a lake fills up.

title: Rigveda
text:
A thousand, a hundred, harnessed to your golden chariot — let the long-maned bays yoked by prayer, O Indra, bring you here to drink the soma.
On your golden chariot let the two tawny coursers with peacock-feathered tails and white backs convey you here for drinking the sweet exhilarating juice.
Drink of this, O hymn-lover, as the first drinker drinks the pressed soma; this offering of the refined, flavoursome juice is pleasant, fitted for exhilaration.
He who is alone in his wonder-deeds, great and fierce in his ordinances — may that broad-jawed one come; he will not stay behind; coming, he does not avoid the call.
You crushed with blows the roving fort of Śuṣṇa; you followed the light then, when you, O Indra, became one to be called upon in the second pressing also.
For me at sunrise, for me at midday of the sky, for me at the forward journey even in the dark season, O Vasu, have the lauds turned to you.
Praise, do praise — these are your most bountiful ones, O you of the patrons' gifts: Ninditāśva, Prапаthī, Paramajyā, Magha — thus, O Medhyātithi.
When in faith I mounted the chariot of Vananvat's horses, then is the wealth of the beautiful known to him who is the cattle-rich descendant of Yadu.
He who has bestowed upon me the bright bay horse together with golden trappings — may this chariot of Āsaṅga, resounding with good fortune, excel all things.
Then Plāyogi surpassed others; Āsaṅga, O Agni, with ten thousands; ten bright bulls he gave me, gleaming, they stood forth from the pond as if from a lake.
Before him is seen the broad thigh hanging down without bone; many a woman, beholding it, has said: 'You bear, O noble one, a splendid prize.'
This pressed soma-juice, O Vasu — drink of it; fill full your belly; we have poured it out for you without fear.
Shaken by men, pressed with stones, filtered through the wool of sheep, purified — like a horse washed in the rivers.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like barley sweetened with milk, we have prepared it for you, O Indra, at this joint celebration.
Indra alone is the soma-drinker; Indra alone drinks the pressed juice, the all-living; he stands between gods and mortals.
Neither the bright one, nor the evil-wisher, nor the satisfied can turn away the wide-ranging one, the good-hearted Indra.
When others hunt after him as a herd hunts a wild beast — with cows away from us — they approach him with milch-cows.
Let three soma-pressings of the god Indra be made, of him who drinks the pressed juice in his own dwelling.
Three vessels trickle down; the three bowls are well full, all upon the same support.
Pure you are, established in many places, mixed with milk in the middle, most exhilarating with curds — for the hero.
These sharp soma-draughts, O Indra, pressed here among us, bright, call for the admixture of milk.
Mix the admixture and the cake offering; O Indra, prepare this soma — for I hear that you are wealthy.
Having drunk in their hearts they fight, like madmen with spirituous drink; they shout like a naked udder.
The praiser of such a wealthy patron of prizes would himself be wealthy; go forward then, O bay-horsed one of renown.
Even a laud being recited — the unfriendly man of no gifts does not heed it; nor does he heed the Gāyatrā being sung.
O Indra, do not hand us over to the mocker, do not hand us over to the arrogant one; give of your bounty, O powerful one, with your powers.
We indeed, for this very purpose, the Kāṇvas your friends wishing you near, laud you with hymns.
Nothing else was gained in the newest works of the craftsman, O thunderer; it is your laud alone that has been desired.
The gods desire the one who presses soma; they do not long for sleep; the unwearied ones go to the feast of joy.
Come forth now with prizes; do not be wrathful toward us, like a great man with a young wife.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let not the ill-willed one do evil to us today at evening from afar, like an ill-favoured son-in-law.
For we know the bountiful good will and the three-fold-born mind of this heroic one.
Pour in with the Kāṇvas present — for we know nothing more glorious than the hundred-aided one of might.
Press for Indra, O presser, the excellent soma, for the hero, for the mighty; bring it for the manly one to drink.
He who is most knowing in unmoved exploits, who gives to the singers the horse-rich prize, to the praisers the prize rich in cattle.
Wondrous, ever more wondrous, O pressers, hasten with the intoxicating soma for the hero, for the champion.
The Vṛtra-slayer will drink the pressed soma; he will come, not distant from us; the hundred-aided one is restrained.
Let the two bays yoked by prayer convey here the bountiful, the friend renowned through hymns, him who delights in songs.
Sweet soma-draughts await you — come! Prepared soma-draughts await you — come! O broad-jawed, sage-like, mighty one, come here to this joint rejoicing.
And the praises that magnify you for great bounty and heroic might, O Indra — they magnify the doer of deeds.
The songs and lauds directed to you, O hymn-bearer — those altogether have taken on powers.
Thus he, roaring aloud, the prize-winner, the sole thunderbolt-holder, from of old unscathed, distributes.
Indra the Vṛtra-slayer with his right hand, the much-invoked, the much-praised — great through his great powers.
In him all peoples, and the bold deeds and the courses — they all indeed follow him, the gladdener, the generous.
He, Indra, has done all these things, he who is heard beyond all — the prize-bestower for the bountiful.
The bearer-forward of the prize-seeking chariot, whom he protects even from afar — the lord of wealth, he is the carrier.

title: Rigveda
text:
The inspirer who gains with swift horses, the hero who slays Vṛtra with his allies, the true protector of the one who serves.
Worship him, O Priyamedhas, worship Indra with a gathered mind; may he who is the true drinker of soma be here with the soma-draughts.
Sing, O Kāṇvas, of him who has song-fame, the lord of truth, eager for renown, far-stretching — the prize-winner.
He who even without a word of praise gave cattle to his friends, the mighty companion of men — those who have leaned their desire upon him.
Thus, O stone-wielder, you went to the devout Kāṇva Medhyātithi, having become a ram, going towards him.
Instruct Vibhindhu to give four times ten thousand and eight thousand besides.
And those two who grow with milk — may the Naptyas of Raṇa give no harm; we have invoked them for procreation.
Drink of the pressed, flavoured juice; rejoice, O Indra, in the cow-rich one; be our companion in joint rejoicing for our increase; may your thoughts protect us.
May we be in your favour, prize-winners; let not our foe overthrow us; protect us, O you of brilliant might, with your aids; guide us into your blessings.
May these words of mine magnify you, O lord of many goods; the purifying, bright, inspired ones have sung around you with their lauds.
This one, made powerful with a thousand sages, has spread like the ocean; true is that greatness of his — I extol his might, which reigns supreme among the inspired at the sacrifices.
Indra truly at the assembly of gods, Indra at the proceeding sacrifice, Indra we call in the battle for the gaining of the forest's prize, Indra for the winning of wealth.
Indra spread out the two worlds with his greatness and might; Indra made the sun shine; in Indra all living beings have found their order; in Indra the pressed soma-drops.
O Indra, the descendants of Āyu who drink first, the Ṛbhus together in accord have resounded with lauds; the Rudras praise the ancient one.

title: Rigveda
text:
By this has Indra grown strong in his bull-like might through the rapture of the pressed soma with Viṣṇu; today the descendants of Āyu praise that greatness of his as of old.
I seek from you that heroic strength, that prayer for the ancient design — with which you helped the Yatis and Bhṛgu when the prize was set, and with which you protected Praskaṇva.
With which you released the great waters into the ocean — that is your bull-like might, O Indra; that greatness of his is immediately unattainable, which the wide earth resounds with.
Be able for us, O Indra, since I seek from you the wealth and heroic strength; be able for the prize the first to be desired, be able for the laud, O ancient one.
Be able for us — for you protected our ancient understanding, O Indra, of those who desire the prize; be able as you protected Ruśama, Śyāvaka, Kṛpa, O Indra, and Svarṇara.
What mortal now, swifter than linseed plants, shall praise him newly? For those who sing his Indra-might and glory have never truly attained to his greatness.
When do those who praise and order the divine, when does the seer, what inspired one, convey it? When, O Maghavan Indra, do you come to the call of the soma-presser? When do you come to the praiser?
Up go these most honey-sweet words, the lauds are set in motion — the prize-winners with imperishable aids, like chariots rushing for the prize.
Like the Kāṇvas, like the Bhṛgus, like the suns, they have all attained to what has been obtained; the Āyus, the Priyamedhas, magnifying Indra with their lauds, have sung out.
Yoke your two bays, O Indra, best Vṛtra-slayer, from afar; come hither, O Maghavan, for the soma-drinking, O fierce one, come with your two tall steeds.
For these Kāṇvas have cried out to you with prayer, the inspired ones for the winning of the sacrifice; so you, O Maghavan Indra, O hymn-lover, hear our call like a beloved one.

title: Rigveda
text:
You drove Vṛtra out from the great bows, O Indra; you drove out the magic of Arbuda the beast; you drove out the cows from the mountain.
The fires blazed forth, the sun blazed forth, the Indra-belonging essence of soma blazed forth; you pressed down the great serpent from the air — that, O Indra, is your manly power.
Him whom Indra, the Maruts, Pākasthāman, Kaurayāṇa gave me — the most splendid of all in his own nature, running as if in heaven.
Pākasthāmā gave me Rohita, the well-yoked one filling the girth-strap — the awakener of riches.
For whom ten other carriers bear back the yoke-shaft — like a bird to the home of Tugrya.
The self of the father, the body is the garment, the strength-giving ointment — Rohita's fourth one, Pākasthāman, the Bhoja, the giver, I have spoken of.
Whether eastward, westward, northward or southward, O Indra, you are called by men — you are universally wide-spread, born for men, for the Ānavas you are abundant strength, for the Turvaśas.
Whether with Rumā, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, or Kṛpa you rejoice together, O Indra — the Kāṇvas, the bearers of lauds, draw you with their prayers; O Indra come.
As a wild bull thirsty makes its way to a waterless pool's edge, come quickly at our invitation, at the forward journey; among the Kāṇvas drink in full companionship.
May the soma-drops gladden you, O Maghavan Indra, for the giving of bounty to the presser; from there you drank soma pressed in the bowl — that greatest strength you have taken on.
He put forth strength with strength, broke anger with might; all your enemies, O young Indra, have bowed down like trees.
Like one accompanied by a thousand, he who has brought near praise of you the youthful warrior — he makes a son surpassing, with heroic strength; he prospers with words of homage.
Let us not fear, let us not toil, in your friendship, O fierce one; great and worthy of sight is your deed, O bull — may we see Turvaśa and Yadu.

title: Rigveda
text:
He roars following the left flank like a bull; the giver's gift does not wane; the milch-cows mixed with honey by the bees — come quickly, run, drink.
Your friend, O Indra, is rich in horses, rich in chariots, well-formed, rich in cattle; he accompanies the feast of meat always; the moon-bright one goes to the assembly.
Come like a thirsty antelope to the watering-place; drink the soma following the wish; having drunk, O Maghavan, day by day you take on the strongest might.
Make the soma flow, O Adhvaryu — Indra thirsts; now the two bull-strong bays have been yoked and the Vṛtra-slayer has come.
Even the worshipping man himself reckons where you satisfy yourself with soma; this food of yours, fit companion, well sprinkled — come for it, run, drink.
O Adhvaryus, standing in the chariot, press the soma for Indra; those pressing for the offering-performing sacrifice look toward the bright one above.
Both eager bull-strong bays will convey Indra to the waters; may the seven steeds lovely at the rite convey you hither at the pressing.
We choose Pūṣan for alliance, the lord of many goods; O mighty Indra, much-invoked, give of your bounty for our thought, for the strength to win wealth, O liberator.
Sharpen us like a razor on a whetstone, O liberator of riches; give to us — in you is that wealth of the morning cow, easily found, which you impel toward mortal man.
I reach out to you, O Pūṣan, to straighten myself; I reach out to the praiser, O shining one; I do not reach for what is remote — for that, O Vasu, I praise the Sāman of the Pajras.
Cattle have gone somewhere to the pasture, O shining immortal of permanent treasure; O Pūṣan, be our protector, be favorable, most bountiful for the winning of the prize.
Substantial bounty with a hundred horses at the heavenly attacks of Kuruṅga, in the gifts of the splendid, fortunate king — among the Turvaśas we have thought of it.

title: Rigveda
text:
Through the thoughts of the prize-winning Kāṇva and the heaven-assailing Priyamedhas, the seer drove off sixty thousand impeccable ones, drove off herds of cattle.
Even the trees have resounded at my approach; they allotted me cattle abundantly, they allotted me horses abundantly.
As if from afar, when truly the ruddy-hued one shone out, it spread its beam all across the universe.
O wonder-working Aśvins, you two accompany the Dawn with a manly, mind-yoked chariot of broad splendour.
O Vājinīvasū Aśvins, the lauds have faced toward you two; I, the messenger, have readied speech.
We Kāṇvas praise the Aśvins, who are dear to many for our aid, who delight many, who have many goods.
Most bountiful, most prize-winning, urging onward, lords of beauty — you will come to the house of the devout one.
For the god-devoted, devout one, sprinkle the cattle-pasture with good intelligence and irresistible help, with ghee.
Let our laud come running swiftly with swift eagles; come, O Aśvins, with your horses.
With those with which you two circle around the three remote realms, all the luminous spaces of heaven, and the three watches of night.
And for us the cow-rich refreshments and the gifts — O you who know the day, loosen the bonds on the path to the winning.
Bring to us, O Aśvins, wealth rich in cattle, rich in heroes, rich in good chariots — bring refreshments rich in horses.
Grown great, lords of beauty, wondrous ones with golden paths — drink the soma-sweetness.
O Vājinīvasū, to us and to the bountiful patrons of wide extent, bring shelter that cannot be deceived.
Do settle down the prayer of the people, come swiftly with the youngest speed; do not pause at another place.
Drink of this, you two Aśvins, of this pleasant intoxication, O attentive ones, of the honey bestowed.
Bring to us the wealth of hundreds, of thousands, of great abundance, all-nourishing.

title: Rigveda
text:
In many places indeed the wise men, the praisers, call upon you two, O heroes; come, O Aśvins, with the singers.
The people who have strewn the sacred grass, who bear oblations, who are prepared — they invoke you two, O Aśvins.
This laud of ours today is the most carrying and most intimate; may it be for you two, O Aśvins.
The leather bag of honey placed upon the chariot-seat — from that drink, O Aśvins.
With that, O Vājinīvasū, bring rich refreshments for our cattle, for our offspring, for our wellbeing, for our cow.
And the heavenly refreshments and the rivers — O you who know the day, you pour them down like opening a door.
When did Tugra's son find you two, O heroes, abandoned in the ocean, when your chariot flew to pieces?
You Nāsatyas honour again and again with aids Kāṇva, restored and settled in his house.
Come with those newer, excellent aids when I call upon you two, O Vṛṣaṇvasū Aśvins.
As you helped Kāṇva, Priyamedha who was nearby praised, Atri, Śiñjāra — so, O Aśvins.
As in the contest for the prize you helped Aṁśu among cows, Agastya — as Sobhari in the races.
To this extent, O Vṛṣaṇvasū Aśvins, or even more — while praising we seek your favour.
O Aśvins, you have mounted the chariot with golden seat, with golden reins, sky-touching.
Your pole is golden, the shaft is golden, the axle is golden; both wheels are golden.
With that, O Vājinīvasū, come to us from far away; come to this excellent praise of mine.
Bring from afar, O Aśvins, eating the many divine, immortal refreshments.
Come to us, O Aśvins, with glory, with renown, with riches; O Nāsatyas, you of many splendours.
Let the winged ones, the birds sprinkled with drops, convey you both here to the people whose rite is good.
Your chariot that rolls with the refreshment singing along — the wheel does not obstruct it.

title: Rigveda
text:
With a golden chariot, with swift-footed horses — O Nāsatyas, swift in thought.
You two refresh the wakeful wild beast, O Vṛṣaṇvasū; mix refreshment and wealth for us.
May you two Aśvins know the new acquisitions of mine, as when Kaśu the Caidya gave a hundred camels and ten thousand cattle.
He who has given me ten gold-gleaming kings — the peoples around him, the subjects of the Caidya, pressed down to the ground, wrapped in hides on all sides.
Let none travel this path along which the Cedis go; lest another patron of superior bounty be drawn away from the people.
Great is Indra who through might, like Parjanya swelling with rain, has been magnified through the lauds of Vatsa.
When the bearers, the inspired ones, carry the offspring of the Ṛta forward with the carrying of the Ṛta, who nourish the offspring of the Ṛta.
When the Kāṇvas fashioned Indra with their lauds as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the kindred declared the weapon.
To his wrath all peoples, all clans, have bowed, as rivers to the ocean.
This might of his was blazing when he rolled both together — Indra rolled the two worlds like a hide.
He split the head of the roaring Vṛtra with his hundred-jointed thunderbolt, with the bull-like weapon.
These thoughts at the head of the streams of the inspired we have praised forward, shining like the blaze of Agni.
When the thoughts that are in hiding blaze forth of their own accord, the Kāṇvas do so through the stream of the Ṛta.
May we attain to that, O Indra — the wealth rich in cattle, rich in horses; may we bring prayer forward for the ancient design.
I indeed have grasped the wisdom of the Ṛta from the father; I was born like the sun.
With ancient thought I adorn the hymns as Kāṇva does — with which Indra took on his energy.
The seers who have not praised you, O Indra, and those who have praised you — grow great for me, O well-praised one.

title: Rigveda
text:
When his wrath surged forward, breaking Vṛtra joint by joint, he set the waters moving toward the ocean.
You struck down the bullying Śuṣṇa with the thunderbolt, O Indra, against the Dasyu; for you, O bull, O fierce one, are famed as such.
The heavens have not encompassed Indra in his might, nor the mid-spaces the thunderbolt-holder, nor the earths.
He who lay blocking your great waters, O Indra, as they were being held firm — you thrust him down with your feet.
He who seized these two great worlds, both together — him, O Indra, you have hidden in darkness.
O Indra, the Yatis who have praised you, the Bhṛgus who have praised you — O fierce one, hear my call for me.
These spotted cows of yours, O Indra, milk out ghee and the admixture; these have swelled with the Ṛta.
Those springs, O Indra, like your own, have made the embryo — surrounding him like ordinance does the sun.
You alone, O lord of might, the Kāṇvas have magnified with laud; you the pressed soma-drops.
In your leadings, O Indra, O stone-wielder, is the proclamation; the sacrifice is one to be spread far.
Bring to us, O Indra, the great refreshment; break through like a fort rich in cattle; and offspring and heroic strength.
And that swiftness of horses, O Indra, which shone at the head of the Nahuṣa peoples.
Like the sun you stretch out to the nearby-visible fold; when you, O Indra, show us favour.
When indeed you, being fierce, rule over the settlements, O Indra — great, boundless in might.
To you, of wide stride, the peoples bearing oblations call for aid with soma-drops.
In the curve of the mountains, at the confluence of the rivers, the inspired one was born through insight.
From there he, perceiving, looks down upon the ocean on the slopes, from where the drinking of the inspired one surges.
From the ancient seed they see the daily light, when it is kindled above the sky.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Kāṇvas, O Indra, all magnify your thought, your manly power, and your bull-like strength, O mightiest one.
O Indra, be pleased with this excellent praise of mine; do protect me; and do increase my thought.
And we, devoted to prayer, O grown-great thunderbolt-holder, inspired ones, have fashioned this for life.
The Kāṇvas have sung toward Indra as waters rushing down a slope, the thought that eagerly desires him.
The lauds have magnified Indra as rivers magnify the ocean — him of indestructible wrath, him who does not age.
Come to us from afar with your two tawny, desired bays; drink this pressed soma, O Indra.
You alone, O best Vṛtra-slayer, the peoples who have strewn the sacred grass invoke for the winning of the prize.
Both worlds follow you like a wheel rolling behind Etaśa; the pressed soma-drops follow you.
Rejoice well, O manly shining one, O Indra, at Śaryaṇāvat; be exhilarated with the thought of Vivasvat.
Having grown great in the sky, the bull, the thunderer roared aloud — the Vṛtra-slayer, the greatest soma-drinker.
For you are the first-born seer, alone sovereign through might, O Indra, you eagerly seek wealth.
May a hundred tawny steeds, with white backs, drive toward our pressed soma, toward the offering.
This ancient thought swollen with sweetness and ghee — the Kāṇvas have magnified it with laud.
Of the great ones let a mortal choose Indra at the sacrifice; let one who would win choose Indra for his aid.
O much-praised one, the two bays praised by Priyamedha shall carry you hither for the soma-drinking.
From Tirindira I received a hundred, from Parśu a thousand — the bounties of the Yādavas.
Three hundred horses and ten thousand cattle they gave to the Pajra singer.
Kakuha has reached up to heaven, giving camels harnessed four together, making the Yādava people renowned.

title: Rigveda
text:
When, O Maruts, the inspired one let the Triṣṭubh impulse flow forth for you, you ruled throughout the mountains.
When, being fierce, O bright ones, you harnessed the course, the mountains bent down.
The roaring sons of Pṛśni rose up with the winds, they milked out the swelling refreshment.
The Maruts scatter the mist, they shake the mountains when they travel the course with the winds.
When for your march the mountain and the rivers have set themselves in order for the great burst of your energy.
You we invoke for aid at night, you during the day, you at the proceeding sacrifice.
The ruddy-hued, brilliant ones are set in motion with their courses — the roaring ones upon the ridge of heaven.
They release the ray with might, the path for the sun to travel; they have spread themselves out with their beams.
Hearken to this hymn of mine, O Maruts, to this laud, O Ṛbhukṣan; be pleased with this call of mine.
The Pṛśnis milked three lakes of honey for the thunderbolt-holder — the barrel-shaped overflowing spring.
O Maruts, when we invoke you seeking favour from heaven, then do come to us.
For you are good-givers, Rudras, in the house, O Ṛbhukṣans, and also wise ones in the exhilaration.
Set in motion for us from heaven, O Maruts, the wealth shaken with exhilaration, of great abundance, all-nourishing.
When, as if over the mountains, you bright ones harnessed the course, be exhilarated with the pressed soma-drops.
To this extent a mortal might beg the favour of these indestructible ones, with hymns.
They who blow upon both worlds like drops following the rains, milking the inexhaustible spring.
They rose up with their roarings, up with their chariots, up with their winds; up with their lauds, the sons of Pṛśni.
With which you helped Turvaśa and Yadu, with which you helped Kāṇva who wins prizes — may we meditate on that for wealth.

title: Rigveda
text:
These refreshments, O good-givers, swollen with ghee, have magnified the Kāṇva with their hymns.
Where now, O good-givers, do you rejoice with those who have strewn the sacred grass? What brahmin worships you?
For not before when, O Maruts of strewn sacred grass, with praises, have you quickened the troop through the Ṛta.
They have brought together the great waters, brought together the two earths, brought together the sun; they placed the thunderbolt together joint by joint.
They went through Vṛtra joint by joint, through the mountains without a king — acting out the bull-like manly power.
They followed the energy and the will of Trita as he fought; they followed Indra in the Vṛtra-contest.
Lightning-handed, heaven-assailing, with golden helmets on their heads, the bright ones adorned themselves for beauty.
When Uśanas came from afar, you two reached the hole of the bulls; heaven resounded with fear.
For the giving of the prize, O gods, come to us with golden-handed horses.
When the dappled mare, the fore-runner, the ruddy one, draws the chariot of these, the bright ones go loosing the waters.
At Suṣoma, at Śaryaṇāvat, at Ārjīka, at Pastyāvat, the heroes went along with their wheels.
When will you come, O Maruts, here to the inspired one calling, to him seeking your grace in his need?
Where now, where-beloved one, have you abandoned Indra? Who draws your friendship away from him?
With strength among us — we Kāṇvas praise Agni with the Maruts of thunderbolt hands, with golden roarings.
I would turn the sacrifice-loving bulls toward a newer well-being, the ones of brilliant prize.
Even mountains submit and bow down, those who think themselves ribbed peaks; even the highlands bend themselves.
They who move diagonally carry through the mid-air as they fly — givers of sustenance to the praiser.

title: Rigveda
text:
For Agni is the ancient knower; like the sun with its flame he is the metre; they have spread themselves out with their beams.
Come to us with all your aids, you two Aśvins; O wondrous ones of golden path, drink the soma-sweetness.
Come now, O Aśvins, with a chariot having the skin of the sun, O you who bend, of golden ornament, O poets, of deep understanding.
Come around from Nahuṣa, from the mid-air, with excellent lauds; drink, O Aśvins, the sweetness, the soma pressed at the pressing of the Kāṇvas.
Come to us from heaven, from the mid-air, O you who love what is below; the son of Kāṇva has pressed here the soma-sweetness for you.
Come to us within earshot, O Aśvins, for the soma-drinking; O svadhā, the magnifiers of the laud — the two poets go forward with their thoughts, O heroes.
For the seers who of old invoked you for aid, O heroes — come, O Aśvins, come; approach this excellent laud of mine.
Come to us from above the luminous realm of heaven, O you who find the sun; O you of calf-like wisdom, heard in the invocation through the lauds.
Why do others sit about us with lauds for the Aśvins? The son of Kāṇva, the seer Vatsa, has magnified you both with his songs.
The inspired one has called you both here with his lauds for aid, O Aśvins; you who are stainless, best Vṛtra-slayers — be our benefactors.
When the maiden mounted your chariot, O Vājinīvasū, you two Aśvins went forward to all the thoughts.
From there come with your thousandfold-adorned chariot, O Aśvins; Vatsa the poet-seer has declared the honey-sweet speech to you.
O you who greatly delight many, who have many goods, O you who carry thoughts of riches — may the two bearers, the Aśvins, sing toward this my laud.
Bestow on us all bounties, O Aśvins, without shame; do not let us who observe the seasons be put to shame, do not abandon us to blame.

title: Rigveda
text:
Whether you two Nāsatyas are in the distance or dwell above in the air — from there come with your thousandfold-adorned chariot, O Aśvins.
The seer who has magnified you both, O Nāsatyas, with his songs — for him set the thousandfold-adorned refreshment dripping with ghee.
Give to him the strength dripping with ghee, you two Aśvins; he who has praised you for your favour, seeking goods, O lords of the giving stream.
Come to us, O consumer of enemies, to this laud — O you who enjoy many things; grant these to us for beauty, O heroes, give them for our conquest.
The Priyamedhas have called you both with all aids; O Aśvins, ruling over the rites, at the calls of the journey.
Come to us as benefactors, O Aśvins, as you who bring well-being; Vatsa who admires you has magnified you with his thoughts and songs.
With those aids with which you helped Kāṇva Medhātithi, with which you helped Vaśa of ten herds, with which you helped Gośarya — with those help us, O heroes.
With those aids with which you, O heroes, helped Trasadasyu in the contest for the prize — with those help us well, O Aśvins, for the winning of the prize.
May the well-fashioned lauds, the hymns, magnify you both, O Aśvins; O best Vṛtra-slayers in many places — be those who are eagerly desired by many for us.
Three steps of the Aśvins are manifest; beyond is the hidden; the two poets through the paths of the Ṛta — before the living beings on this side.
Now the seer has arranged the laud of the Aśvins with a beautiful melody; may he pour the most honey-sweet soma into the heated vessel of the Atharvans.
Whatever heroic power is in the mid-air, whatever is in heaven, whatever follows the five peoples — that bestow on us, O Aśvins.
The inspired ones who have touched the wonders of you two, O Aśvins — take heed of the Kāṇva's words just so.

title: Rigveda
text:
This hot drink is poured around you both, O Aśvins, with the laud; this honey-sweet soma, O Vājinīvasū, with which you perceive the Vṛtra.
What you have done in the waters, in the forest lord, in the plants, O you of many wonders — with that enter into me, O Aśvins.
What you nourish, O Nāsatyas, or what you heal, O gods — this Vatsa does not find you through prayers, for you go to those who bear oblations.
Now the seer has arranged the laud of the Aśvins with a beautiful melody; may he pour the most honey-sweet soma into the heated vessel of the Atharvans.
Mount now the swift-wheeled chariot, O Aśvins; these lauds of mine have stirred toward you like a cloud.
If today we have stirred you, O Nāsatyas, with lauds, or with songs, O Aśvins — take heed of the Kāṇva's words.
What Kakṣīvant invoked of you, what the seer Vyaśva invoked, what Dīrghatamas invoked — what Pṛthī son of Vena invoked in his seat — just so, from that, O Aśvins, take heed.
Come as shelter-protectors and as protectors from beyond; be protectors of the world and of our bodies; travel as a path for our offspring and progeny.
When you two go with Indra in one chariot, O Aśvins, or when you two are with Vāyu as co-dwellers; when you are of like will with the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus; or when you stand in the strides of Viṣṇu.
If today I were to invoke you two Aśvins for the winning of the prize, for strength in the overwhelming battles — that is the best aid of the Aśvins.
Come now, O Aśvins; these offerings are prepared for you; these soma-draughts are here among the Turvaśas and Yadus, these among the Kāṇvas then for you.
Whatever remedy exists far off or nearby, O Nāsatyas — with that, O wise ones, give shelter to Vimada and to Vatsa.
The divine one has arisen; together with the speech of the gods I speak the Aśvins; the divine one has turned — the thought and the gift open out for mortals.

title: Rigveda
text:
Waken the Aśvins, O Dawn; waken, O great divine Sūnṛtā; waken the hotar of the sacrifice in succession; waken the great glory for exhilaration.
When you, O Dawn, go with your beam and shine together with the sun, then the chariot of the Aśvins turns in its course, worthy for men to drink.
When the soma-stalks, having been drunk, yield as cows with their udders, or when the songs have resounded forward, O Aśvins, in the manner of those seeking the divine.
Go forward for glory, go forward for might, go forward for the shelter that conquers men, go forward for skill — O wise Aśvins.
When now, O Aśvins, you two sit down with your thoughts in the father's seat, or with your favours worthy of laud.
Whether you two are in the long dwelling place, or in the shining realm of heaven, or in the ocean in the fashioned house — from there come, O Aśvins.
As you two mingled well with Manu's sacrifice — just so take heed of the Kāṇva's words; I invoke Bṛhaspati, all the gods, Indra and Viṣṇu, and the Aśvins, O swift-rushing ones.
These two Aśvins I now invoke, the wonderful deeds-doers, taken in grasp; whose friendship with us is foremost, attainable among the gods.
Those in whose presence the sacrifices of the sun-like patrons are foremost — those two, O wise ones, drink through your own powers the soma-sweetness at the sacrifice and the rite.
Whether today, O Aśvins, you are westward or eastward, O Vājinīvasū; whether among the Druhyus, the Anus, the Turvaśas, the Yadus — I call upon you; therefore come to me.
Whether you two fly through the mid-air, O you who enjoy many things, or whether you weave along both worlds — or whether you mount the chariot with your own powers — from there come, O Aśvins.
Thou, O Agni, art the guardian of sacred rites among mortals, O god; thou art to be praised at sacrifices.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou art praiseworthy at the assemblies, O conquering one; O Agni, thou art the charioteer of the ritual offerings.
So do thou, O Jātavedas, drive away from us the enemies, the godless malevolences, O Agni.
The sacrifice of a mortal foe, even though near at hand, thou dost not seek out, O Jātavedas.
We mortals contemplate thy many names, O immortal Jātavedas; we the inspired sages.
We inspired sages invoke with songs the inspired god Agni, we mortals for aid and protection.
May a devotee draw thy mind even from the most distant abode, O Agni, with a song longing for thee.
For thou art of like form in many places, lord over all peoples; we invoke thee in battles.
In battles we invoke Agni for protection, desiring prizes; him of brilliant bounty in contests.
For thou art the ancient one worthy of praise at the rites, and thou sittest as hotar both from of old and as the ever-new; satisfy thine own self, O Agni, and win good fortune for us.
That rapture most excellent at drinking soma which stirs in thee, O mightiest Indra, whereby thou smitest down the devourer — that we implore.
Whereby thou madest the Daśagva tremble, Adhrigu, the heaven-man; whereby thou didst protect the ocean — that we implore.
Whereby thou didst urge the great waters of Sindhu like chariots, to travel the path of Ṛta — that we implore.
This hymn of praise for thine invocation, like purified ghee, O wielder of the stone — whereby thou hast now grown in strength on this very day.
Be pleased with this, O lover of praise; it swells like the ocean; O Indra, thou hast grown with all thy aids.
The god who has been entreated by us from afar for friendship, spreading wide like rain from heaven, has grown.
His banners have grown, and the thunderbolt in his fists, when like the sun he caused the two worlds to grow.

title: Rigveda
text:
If, O great lord of the good, a thousand buffaloes have here been offered, then thy heroic power has greatly increased.
Indra burns down the afflicting one with the rays of the sun; like Agni in the forest, the victorious one has grown.
This timely meditation goes forth ever newer; worshipping thee, the much-beloved one, she has truly measured out.
The embryo of the sacrifice, the god-devoted one, purifies wisdom in succession; Indra has grown through the hymns of praise, he has truly measured out.
Indra has spread as the gaining of Mitra's prize, for the drinking of soma; like a cow lowing eastward for the presser, he has truly measured out.
Whom the inspired hymn-bearing Āyus have thoroughly delighted — he has swollen like ghee in the mouth, as is of Ṛta.
And Aditi, the self-sovereign, has generated a hymn of praise for Indra — of much proclamation as his aids, as is of Ṛta.
The bearers have chanted for protection, for praise; the two bay steeds of the god are not of diverse ordinances, as is of Ṛta.
When thou art exhilarated, O Indra, with Viṣṇu's soma, or with Trita Āptya's, or among the Maruts, together with the drops of soma —
Or when thou art exhilarated, O mighty one, in the distant realm, upon the ocean — delight in our pressed soma together with the drops.
Or when thou art the strengthener of the presser, of the sacrificer, O lord of the good, or in whose hymn thou dost delight — together with the drops of soma.
We would praise Indra, Indra, the god over each god for your aid; then for the conquering sacrifice they have attained fully.
With sacrifices the sacrifice-bearing one, with soma the most excellent soma-drinker — Indra they have magnified with priestly recitations; they have attained fully.
Great are his leadings forth, and many are his praises; all the good things have reached the worshipper fully.

title: Rigveda
text:
The gods placed Indra in the forefront to slay Vṛtra; the holy voices chanted Indra together for strength.
The great one with greatness — we with our hymns of praise, him who hears the invocation — we acclaim forward with songs for strength.
Whom neither the two worlds separated, nor the mid-air spaces, the thunderbolt-wielder — even from home his blazing radiance increases for strength.
When in battle-conflict the gods placed thee in the forefront, O Indra — then thy two beloved bays grew strong.
When thou didst slay with thy might Vṛtra who blocked the rivers, O thunderbolt-wielder — then thy two beloved bays grew strong.
When Viṣṇu strode out his three strides with might for thee, O Indra — then thy two beloved bays grew strong.
When thy two beloved bays have grown day by day — then all the worlds have been held in order by thee.
When the Marutic peoples have arranged themselves for thee, O Indra — then all the worlds have been held in order by thee.
When thou didst sustain yonder bright light, the sun, in the sky — then all the worlds have been held in order by thee.
This excellent praise of thine the inspired sage raises with meditations, nourishing a sister as with footsteps, before the rite.
When they have sounded together in unison in his beloved abode, at the navel of the sacrifice, the milch-cows, before the rite.
Bestow on us heroic power, good horses, and good cattle, O Indra — like the hotar for the first meditation, before the rite.
Indra purifies wisdom worthy of recitation at the pressed soma-drinks; he is known for his growing power, for he is great.
He who is great in the first heavenly space, in the abode of the gods — he who crosses well, who has the highest fame, who conquers in the waters.
Him I call for the winning of prizes, Indra, powerful, for the contest; be our nearest friend in thy grace, for growth.

title: Rigveda
text:
This gift of thine, O Indra, lover of praise, flows from the presser; delighting in his sacred grass thou shinest forth.
Now grant us that, O Indra, which we beg of thee who press the soma; bring us the bright wealth that wins the sun.
When the all-discerning praiser has lifted up his songs beyond the arrogant — he who is pleased mounts like a branch.
Like the ancient one, produce the songs; hear the call of the praiser; in each exhilaration thou hast grown for the well-doing one.
His joyful truths play, like waters flowing downhill; through this meditation who is called lord of heaven.
And he who is called lord, the sole sovereign of the settled peoples — with those who grow through homage, seeking aid, delight at the pressed soma.
Praise the famous, wise one, whose two bay horses are victorious, who go to the house of the worshipper, bowing down.
Hastening, O great-minded one, with horses of sprinkled forms — come to the sacrifice with swift ones; indeed it is well for thee.
O Indra, mightiest lord of the good, hold wealth among those who praise thee; undying fame rich in goods for the patrons.
I call thee at sunrise, I call thee at noon of day; be pleased, O Indra, come to us with thy steeds.
Come now, run forward, be exhilarated with the pressed soma mixed with milk; extend the ancient thread as it is known.
Whether thou art in the distant realm, whether in the near realm, O Vṛtra-slayer, or whether thou art near the soma in the ocean.
May our songs magnify Indra, may the pressed soma-drops magnify Indra; the oblation-bearing peoples have rejoiced in Indra.
Him indeed the inspired sages, seeking aid, with their downward-flowing aids — the settled peoples magnified Indra like branches.
At the three soma-vats the gods have fashioned the perceptible sacrifice; may our songs magnify him who ever grows.

title: Rigveda
text:
When the praiser devoted to thee has placed the recitations in proper order, he is called pure and purifying — that one is marvellous.
That great ancient thing of Rudra stirs in the primeval abodes, where the discerning ones have separately placed the mind.
If thou art near in friendship to me, protect this soma; whereby we have crossed beyond all enemies.
When, O Indra, lover of praise, will the praiser be most blessed? When wilt thou place us in wealth of cattle and horses?
And thy well-praised, virile two bay steeds draw thy chariot, the most exhilarating of him who knows no old age, whom we implore.
Him the much-praised, the mighty, we implore with ancient aids; may he sit down on the beloved sacred grass, and then a second time.
Grow well, O much-praised one, with aids praised by sages; kindle the swelling refreshment and turn it towards us.
O Indra, thou art near to the praiser standing thus, O wielder of the stone; from Ṛta I urge thy mind-yoked meditation.
Here yoke those two bay steeds who are gladdened together for the drinking of soma; O Indra, resound towards us with both thy riches.
May they resound towards us, thy Rudras who have obtained glory; and the Marut-attended peoples, with refreshment.
These rushings forward of his enjoy the foot-place that is in heaven; at the navel of the sacrifice they have put together as is known.
This one goes eastward before the rite for the far-seeing eye; he measures out the sacrifice in succession, the far-seer.
Virile is this thy chariot, O Indra, and virile too are thy two bay steeds; virile art thou, O lord of a hundred powers, virile is the invocation.
Virile is the pressing stone, virile the rapture, virile this soma now pressed; virile is the sacrifice which thou dost pervade, virile is the invocation.
As virile I invoke thee, the virile one, O thunderbolt-wielder, with brilliant aids; for thou hast desired the responsive praise — virile is the invocation.

title: Rigveda
text:
If I, O Indra, were as sole master of wealth as thou art, then my praiser would be a companion in cattle.
I would teach him and would give to the wise man, O lord of śacī; if I were master of cattle.
Thy joyful truth, O Indra, is like a milch-cow for the sacrificer who presses soma; she milks out cow and horse, full and swelling.
There is no turning away of thy bounty, O Indra — neither god nor mortal; when thou, being praised, art willing to give wealth.
The sacrifice magnified Indra when he rolled the earth apart, fashioning a support in the sky.
Of thee who hast grown, of thee who hast won all riches, we choose the protection, O Indra.
The bright lights overpassed the mid-air in the rapture of soma when Indra shattered Vala.
He drove the cows upward for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden in the cave; he thrust Vala towards him.
The bright lights of heaven have been made firm and established by Indra; the stable things he does not push away.
Like a wave of the waters exhilarating, the hymn of praise rushes swiftly towards Indra; thy raptures have shone forth.
For thou, O Indra, art the magnifier of hymns, the magnifier of recitations; and the well-doer for the praisers.
The two maned bay steeds carry Indra to the drinking of soma, to the sacrifice rich in bounty.
With the foam of the waters thou didst twist off the head of Namuci, O Indra, when thou didst conquer all adversaries.
Those who sought to escape by wiles, who sought to climb the sky, O Indra — thou didst shake down the Dasyus.
The assembly of those who press not soma, O Indra, thou hast scattered in all directions, becoming superior as soma-drinker.
Come here, harm him not, ye who go forward; pause not, O ye of equal wrath; even the firm things are bent.
He whose great double-strong power has upheld the two worlds — with his virility, mountains, plains, waters, and heaven.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou, the much-praised, dost reign alone; thou dost strike down the Vṛtras, O Indra, to attain conquering glories.
That rapture of thine we praise, the virile one, ever victorious in battles, also the world-maker, O stone-wielder, beautiful with bay steeds.
Whereby thou hast found the lights for Āyu and for Manu — delighting in his sacred grass thou shinest forth.
That same thing even today thy reciters praise as of old; conquer the waters whose lord is the rain-bull, day by day.
That great heroic power is thine, thine too is the impetus and the will; divine wisdom sharpens the desirable thunderbolt.
Heaven increases thy manliness, O Indra, earth increases thy fame; the waters and the mountains urge thee on.
Viṣṇu of great dwelling praises thee, Mitra praises thee, Varuṇa; the Marutic host is exhilarated after thee.
Thou art born the rain-bull, the most generous among peoples, O Indra; thou holdest all things of good offspring together.
Thou alone, O much-praised one, dost cut down the Vṛtras completely; no other power than Indra's is greater.
When thinking of thee, O Indra, many invoke thee for aid — conquer the sun here with our men.
Apt for our great dwelling, entering all forms — exhilarate Indra, lord of śacī, for victory.
The praiser proclaims forward the universal king of settled peoples, Indra, ever new with songs — the man, the man-conquering, the most generous.
In whom all recitations delight and all desire for fame — like the impetus of waters in the ocean.
Him I invite with excellent praise, the chiefest king, in the contest the wisdom-bearing great prize-winner for his gains.
Whose deep, full raptures are broad and rescuing — exhilarant in the winning of heroic prizes.
Him indeed they invoke as champion in the wealth-contests that are set out; those whose Indra it is, they conquer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Him indeed the settled peoples approach with swift acts and with deeds; this Indra is the maker of wide space.
Indra is brahman, Indra is the seer, Indra is many and much-invoked; great with great powers.
He is worthy of hymns, worthy of oblation, true, a warrior of many deeds; being alone he is all-conquering.
With arkas, with sāmans, with Gāyatrī verses, the settled peoples — the dwelling places magnify Indra.
The leader forward to better things, the maker of light in battles — the ever-victorious one who has conquered enemies in battle.
He the protector shall carry us across in safety — the much-invoked Indra — beyond all enemies.
So thou, O Indra, with prizes and with favour and with a good path — lead thou us to grace.
Come hither, for this soma is delicious to thee; O Indra, drink this; here is the sacred grass, my seat for thee.
Let the two maned bay steeds yoked by prayer carry thee, O Indra; hear our prayers.
We the prayer-bearers with our ally invoke thee, O Indra the soma-drinker, we who possess soma, we who press the soma.
Come to us who press soma, to our excellent praises; drink well of the soma-juice, O thou of mighty jaws.
I pour into thy two flanks; let it flow through the limbs; take the honey with thy tongue.
Let it be sweet at the meeting, honey-sweet for thy body; may soma be beneficent to thy heart.
This one, O all-discerning one, wrapping thee around like women — may the soma glide forth, O Indra.
Thick-necked, fat-bellied, well-armed in the exhilaration of the soma — Indra strikes down the Vṛtras.
O Indra, go thou in front, being master of all by thy might; O Vṛtra-slayer, smite down the Vṛtras.
Long be thy hook whereby thou dispensest wealth to the sacrificer who presses soma.
This soma, O Indra, is purified upon the sacred grass; come here, run to it, drink.

title: Rigveda
text:
O thou who art rich in śacī and honoured through śacī — this soma is pressed for thy delight, O Ākhaṇḍala, thou art invoked forward.
He who is thy descendant, O Śṛṅgavṛṣa, the great-grandson, the one who drinks from the kuṇḍa vessel — in him thou hast fixed the mind.
O lord of the homestead, the firm post, the common feast of those rich in soma — the drop that shatters the ever-enduring forts, Indra the friend of the sages.
Son of Pṛdāku, worthy of worship, seeking cows, being alone he exceeds the many; driving the impetuous horse with urgency, having seized the forts, he leads Indra to the drinking of soma.
Now indeed a mortal should beg the grace of these, the Ādityas' unrivalled favour in their power.
For the paths of the Ādityas are unobstructed; their guardians are undeceived, who strengthen good growth.
May Savitṛ, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us that wide shelter which we implore.
Come, O divine Aditi, with the gods, O thou of unharmed sustenance, with our patrons, O much-beloved one, with those of excellent shelter.
For those sons of Aditi know how to keep away enmities; they who are wide-wheeled, sinless, even from straits.
Aditi, without duplicity, shall protect our livestock by day; Aditi shall protect it by night; Aditi, who ever grows, shall protect us from distress.
And may that thought, Aditi, come to us by day with aid; may she make well-being and joy, and drive away failures.
And may those two divine physicians, the Aśvins, bring well-being to us; may they drive away affliction and failures from here.
May Agni with his fires bring well-being; may the sun warm us auspiciously; may the wind blow sinless and auspicious, driving away failures.
Drive away sickness, drive away failure, drive away ill-will; O Ādityas, keep us away from distress.
Drive the arrow away from us, O Ādityas, and also ill-will; make enmity go separately from us, O all-knowing ones.

title: Rigveda
text:
Grant us that shelter, O Ādityas, which releases; even the sinful from sin — O good givers.
Whoever among mortals seeks to harm us — let that man be harmed by his own people; may he be injured in his life.
Evil shall indeed befall that evilly-intending mortal, the enemy who approaches with deceit on our side.
O gods, ye are protectors of the simple; in your hearts ye know mortal man, both the deceitful and the non-deceitful, O Vasus.
We choose the shelter of the mountains and the aid of the waters; keep calamity far from us, O heaven and earth.
With your auspicious shelter, with your boat, O Vasus, carry us across all difficulties.
For a weak offspring indeed — grant us a longer life to live, O Ādityas of great greatness.
The sacrifice has been slighted among you, O Ādityas — be gracious; we are indeed close to you by kinship.
The great shelter of the Maruts, the divine protector, the Aśvins — we implore Mitra and Varuṇa for well-being.
Sinless, worthy of praise like a man, O Mitra, Aryaman, O Varuṇa — may the Maruts lead to us their triple shelter.
Though indeed we Manus are bound by death, O Ādityas — extend further our life to live.
Him praised upward, the heaven-man, the gods have set in motion the divine fire-messenger; they have harnessed the oblation to the gods.
O inspired sage, praise Agni of broad bounty, of brilliant flame, the controller; O Sobhari, in this soma-offering, forward the ancient one for the rite.
We have chosen thee, the most sacrificing, the divine immortal hotar among the gods — the one of good will in this sacrifice.
The son of strength, the much-blessed one, the well-shining Agni of best flame — may he win for us the grace of Mitra, of Varuṇa, of the waters, in heaven.
The mortal who has served Agni with fuel, with oblation, with sacred knowledge — who with homage conducts the rite well.

title: Rigveda
text:
His horses run swiftly as racers, his glory is most luminous; him no distress god-made from anywhere, nor man-made, shall reach.
May we be of good fire through your fires, O son of power, O lord of strengths; thou art of good heroic might, well-disposed to us.
Being praised, a welcome guest like Mitra, Agni is like a chariot to be known; in thee good prosperities exist, thou art king of riches.
That mortal who truly serves the rite, O Agni, is much-blessed, he is praiseworthy; through his meditations may he be a winner.
He for whose rite thou standest upright, the master of dwelling heroes — he achieves; he wins with swift horses, he with inspired men, he wins the deed with heroes.
He in whose house Agni would hold the form, the hymn, and the delight — or would pervade all the desirable oblations throughout the peoples.
Among the gifts of the inspired praiser, O son of power, O most swift one — make the word of one who knows above the mortal reach the gods, O Vasu.
Who serves Agni of good discernment with offerings of food, or with homage, or with song — him of swift flame.
The mortal who has served Aditi with kindling at night-time with his abodes — may he, much-blessed with meditations, cross over all peoples with glories as if with flood-waters.
Bring that glory, O Agni, which has overcome any devourer in the dwelling — the wrath of the people that is hard to deceive.
That whereby Varuṇa sees, Mitra and Aryaman, whereby the Nāsatyas and Bhaga — we would serve thee in that, with power most knowing the way, protected by Indra's nature.
Those indeed, O Agni, are of good thinking, O inspired one, who have placed thee, the man-watching one — the inspired ones, O god of good will.
They the altar, O much-blessed one, they the oblation — they have performed them in heaven; they have won great wealth with prizes, those who have laid their desire in thee.

title: Rigveda
text:
Auspicious to us is the invoked Agni, auspicious is the gift, O much-blessed one, auspicious is the rite; and auspicious are the praises.
Make thy mind auspicious in the slaying of the Vṛtra, whereby thou dost conquer in battles; stretch out the firm things of the many who are haughty — we would win with thy aids.
I praise with song him who is set in place by Manu, whom the gods have appointed as messenger and fire-envoy — the most sacrificing, the oblation-bearer.
To Agni of sharp jaws, the young one who shines, thou singest refreshment — he who fashions heroic might with joyful truths; Agni invoked with ghee.
When Agni, invoked with ghee, carries the splendour both upward and downward — like an Asura his shining garment.
He who has sent forth the oblations, established by Manu, with his sweet-scented divine mouth — he who properly conducts the rite seeks the desirable things, the divine immortal hotar.
If, O Agni, I were thee and thou wert me, the mortal — then I would be the great friend, the immortal; O son of power, invoked one.
I would not give thee over to reproach, O Vasu, nor to wickedness truly; may neither my praiser be transgressing nor ill-placed, O Agni, nor the evil one.
Like a well-tended son in his father's hall — may our oblation go forward to the gods.
With thy nearest aids I would follow thee with pleasure, O Vasu Agni; always a mortal of the god.
By thy will may I win, by thy gifts O Agni, by thy praises; thee indeed they call the wise guide, O Vasu; mine, O Agni, be exhilarated to give.
He stretches forward through thy aids, O Agni, those rich in heroism, those bearing prizes — whose friendship thou dost maintain.
Thy drop, dark-hued, bellowing in season, being kindled, is taken in the tip; thou art the beloved of the great dawns; thou dost reign in the abodes of nights.

title: Rigveda
text:
We Sobharis have come to him, the thousand-testicled one, of own conquest, for aid — to Trasadasyu the universal king.
Whose other fires, O Agni, dwell around like branches — the glories of inspired sages unite, magnifying thy dominions among the peoples.
The mortal whom you Ādityas, the non-deceitful, lead to the farther shore — O good givers, to the especial goods of the generous.
Ye are kings, conquering all settled peoples, dwelling among humans; may we be the charioteers of Ṛta, O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman.
Trasadasyu, son of Purukutsa, gave me fifty female slaves — the most generous, the noble one, the lord of the good.
And to me, from among the two beloved and the two weavers upon Tugvan, of three times seventy — may Śyāva be the leader, the good one, the lord of the liberal givers.
Come hither, harm not, ye who go forward; pause not, O ye of equal wrath; ye are the benders even of firm things.
With firm fellies, O Maruts, O Ṛbhu-lord, O Rudras of keen cutting — come to us today with refreshment, O ye much desired, O sons of Sobhari, to the sacrifice.
For we know the fierce impetus of the Rudriyas, the active Maruts, of Viṣṇu's rushing, of those who send rain.
They flew apart over the two islands; the two worlds, where evil omens abide, have yoked together; the bright-diademed ones drove the dry lands forward when ye, self-shining ones, shook.
Even the unshaken things in your course resound — the mountains and the lord of the forest; the earth trembles at your marches.
For your going, O Maruts, the great heaven above has lifted up; where the men, of arm-strength, point to their own bodies the vigorous forms.
In accordance with their self-power, the men carry great glory, those of fierce appearance, mighty, of rain-form, of unerring form.
The hymn of the Sobharīs is anointed with cows, in the chariot, in the golden sheath; those who are kinsmen of cattle, well-born, for refreshment and enjoyment — the great ones, touch us now.

title: Rigveda
text:
Bring forward your oblations to the manly triumphant ones, to the virile Marutic host — the oblations to him who moves with the rain-bull.
With the rain-steed, O Maruts, with the chariot of rain-form and rain-nave — like eagles among the winged ones, come freely, O men, for the enjoying of our oblations.
With the same anointing their golden ornaments shine brightly on their arms; the spears flash lightning.
Those fierce ones, virile, of fierce arms — none has stretched himself over their bodies; firm are the bows, weapons on your chariots; upon your battle-fronts are glories.
Whose fame, broad like a flood, the fierce name of the ever-present ones — one alone enjoys it, like ancestral strength of birds.
Worship those Maruts, praise them; for of those roaring ones — we cannot exhaust their gifts, so great are they, so great their greatness.
Blessed with good fortune is he who has been in your former aids, O Maruts, at the dawnings — or who is such now.
Or to whose oblations you, O prize-winning men, come for enjoying — may he attain your graces with glories and with winning of prizes, O ye who shake.
Just as the youthful sons of Rudra, of the divine powerful one, desire the sky — so may it be in that way.
Those Maruts, good givers, who are worthy and who roam in common with those who send rain — from here come to us also with a better heart; as young men grow ye strong.
With the newest song indeed, O Sobhari, praise the virile purifying ones with words; sing as one who ploughs like cattle.
Those who are victorious, who must be called upon like fist-fighters at the hotars in all battles — worship today with song the shining virile ones of highest fame, the Maruts.
Even the cows of equal wrath, O Maruts, are of one kin and one bond; the bulls lick one another in turn.
Even a mortal, O dancer-heroes of golden breasts, comes forward to brotherhood; step forth to us, O Maruts; for always your kinship is firm with us.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Maruts, bring to us the Marutic medicine, O good givers; ye are friends, ye are steeds.
Whereby ye protect Sindhu, whereby ye conquer, whereby ye serve Krivi — be of benefit to us with those auspicious aids, O ye of beneficent nature, O enemies of the hateful.
Whatever medicine is in Sindhu, in Asiknī, in the oceans, O Maruts of good sacred grass — whatever is in the mountains —
Seeing all, ye carry it in your bodies — speak to us of that; forgive the sin, O Maruts, of the afflicted one; restore for us what has gone astray.
We who seek thy aid, bearing no gift like others to an unrivalled [lord], invoke thee, O brilliant one, for the prize.
For thy aid in our work, the bold one who urged us on has approached thee, O young [lord]; for we friends have truly chosen thee, O Indra, as our constant protector.
Come hither, lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fields; these soma-drops [call thee]: drink the soma, O lord of soma.
We inspired poets, though without kinsmen of our own, have held fast thee, O Indra, who art rich in allies; come, O bull, with all thy abodes for the drinking of soma.
Settling as birds [settle] in the sweet, intoxicating, exhilarating [draught] mixed with milk, we praise thee eagerly, O Indra.
We speak to thee with homage and approach thee; why dost thou repeatedly shine elsewhere? Our desires are present, O bay-horsed Indra, we are here, thou art the giver; our prayers too are present.
We have now become new recipients of thy protection, O Indra; truly we lack nothing from thee, O stone-wielder; we have known [thy bounty] of old, in former times abundantly.
We know thy friendship and thy gifts of enjoyment, O hero; we seek those [gifts] from thee, O wielder of the vajra; and do thou whet us toward the same [battle], O lord of wealth, in the contest with cattle, O fair-lipped one.

title: Rigveda
text:
Him who formerly led us repeatedly to ever greater good, him I praise for you, O friends — Indra — for our protection.
Him of the bay horses, the true lord, who overpowers the peoples — for he is the one who rejoiced — the bountiful one bestows upon his praisers a hundredfold of cattle and horses.
With thee as our ally, O bull, we would indeed challenge the one who threatens [us], in the gathering of the people rich in cattle.
May we conquer in the contest, O much-invoked Indra, and overcome the deceivers; may we slay Vṛtra with our men, may we prosper; speed forth our thoughts, O Indra.
Without a brother's enmity, without a kinsman's [rivalry], O Indra, thou art from birth and from of old without an equal companion; yet thou seekest fellowship even in battle.
Thou dost not find a wealthy man for friendship; those of swift horses mock thee; but when thou makest a roar and stirrest everything together, then thou art called upon as a father.
May we not, like fools grown old at home, O Indra, be parted from the friendship of thee who art such; may we sit together when the soma is pressed.
May we not fall away from thy bounty, O giver of cattle, O Indra; may we not be deprived of thee; reach forward and bring [gifts] even from the firm [strongholds] of the stranger — thy gifts are not to be deceived.
Either Indra indeed gives this bounty, or the blessed Sarasvatī gives wealth; or thou, O brilliant one, [givest] to the worshipper.
The brilliant one alone is the true king; the others along the Sarasvatī are but petty kings; like Parjanya he has spread with his rain, giving thousands and ten-thousands.
I have called hither today that most wondrous chariot for our aid — the one which you two Aśvins, easily invoked and driving on a dread path, have set in place for Sūryā.
I call that chariot which goes before in life, easily invoked and much desired, foremost in prizes, which brought Bhujyu [to safety]; of good thoughts, without hatred toward Sobhari, and without reproach.

title: Rigveda
text:
Here, the two gods most often praised, the Aśvins, we draw hither with our homage fully toward us for aid — [you] who go to the house of the worshipper.
The rim of your chariot-wheel revolves [around]; the thong that urges you on stirs itself; may your benevolence, O lords of beauty, come to us as a cow [runs] to her calf.
The chariot which is yours, O Aśvins, of three joints and golden reins, the renowned one that adorns both heaven and earth — with that, O Nāsatyas, come hither.
Ministering [with gifts] to Manu, you two plough in heaven the ancient barley with a wolf [as your ploughshare]; the two of you, O lords of beauty, O Aśvins, we now praise with our prayers.
Come to us, O wealth-possessing lords of prizes, along the paths of Ṛta; with those [paths] by which, O bulls, you quicken Tṛkṣi and Trasadasyu to great dominion.
This soma, O men, O lords with strong bulls, has been pressed for you with the pressing-stones; come to drink the soma; drink it in the house of the worshipper.
Mount, O Aśvins, the golden-bodied chariot, O lords with strong bulls; harness the nourishing draughts [of refreshment].
With those [aids] by which you helped Paktha, with those by which [you helped] Adhrigu, with those by which [you helped] Babhru to be well-pleased — with those, O Aśvins, come quickly and swiftly to us, and heal whatever is afflicted.
Even now at this very moment of the day, O Aśvins, O lords who hold unswerving cattle, we call upon you — we who celebrate [you] with songs and praises.
Come with those [aids] to my all-containing, all-excellent call, O bulls, most bountiful and most praised of all, O men; with those by which you made Krivi to prosper — with those come hither.
Even now in these very days, I call upon those two praised Aśvins close [to me]; those two we implore also with our homage.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those two [are present] at dusk, those two at dawn, those two lords of beauty, those two who travel on a dread path; do not look beyond us, O lords of prizes, toward any mortal enemy — [you] two Rudras.
For the pleasant journey, [come] on a pleasant [chariot] at dawn, O Aśvins, or [come] as companions; I invoke [you], Sobhari, as a son [invokes] a father.
Swift as thought, O bulls, whose ecstasy is overwhelming, with your swiftly-moving aids — even from afar be present for our protection with your many former [gifts], O all-nourishing ones.
Come to us, O Aśvins, on the best path with horses, O men who drink the sweetest [draught]; [bring] cattle and gold, O wondrous ones.
In this your approach, O lords of prizes, possessing good ambrosia-glory, good heroic force, excellent desirable [gifts], unconquered and potent, may we establish all good things.
Praise and worship Jātavedas directly: the one whose smoke moves freely, whose flame is unconstrained.
With my song I praise Agni, the bond for all peoples and of all-embracing mind, and also [as] the swift one of chariots racing together.
The oblation-bearer who is a friend in distress, whose hymn-worthy impulses and nourishments are within his grasp — [such a one] finds wealth.
The flame of the blazing, ageless one has risen up, [the flame] of him of glowing jaws, of beautiful radiance, adorned by [his] host [of flames].
Rise up, O performer of right sacrifice, praised and glowing with divine beauty; look upon [us] with thy great radiance, O blazing one.
Come, O Agni, with well-composed praises, offering the oblations in continuous succession, as thou hast become the messenger and carrier of the offering.
I invoke for you the ancient Agni, the hotar of the peoples; I celebrate him with this voice, and for you I praise him.

title: Rigveda
text:
Him of wondrous purpose who is purified by [their] grace through sacrifices, well-established like Mitra among [his] people, the guardian of ṛta.
Those who follow ṛta have rejoiced with their song in the upholder of ṛta, the perfector of the sacrifice, at the place of homage.
Let our sacrifices go straight to him who is most Aṅgiras-like, who is the hotar most worthy of praise among the clans.
O Agni, those who kindle thee, thy ageless ones, [display] great brilliance; they are like stallions possessed of force and vigor.
So do thou, O lord of vigours, bestow upon us wealth with excellent heroic force; protect us, our offspring, our progeny, in battles.
When the lord of the clan, alert and well-pleased, is [present] among the people of Manu, Agni wards off all demons.
Hear, O Agni, my new hymn of praise, O hero, lord of the clan; burn down the deceitful demons with thy heat.
No mortal enemy shall have power over him through trickery — over the one who has served Agni with his gift of oblations.
The seer Vyaśva, who desired cattle, satisfied thee, O finder of wealth; for great riches we too would kindle thee.
Uśanā Kāvya established thee as hotar; [he established thee,] Jātavedas, who obtains [the sacrifice] for Manu.
All the gods in agreement have made thee their messenger; through [their] hearing, O god, thou hast become foremost and worthy of sacrifice.
A hero among mortals would indeed make this immortal one his messenger — the purifier who travels on the black track, [soaring] through the air.
Him we invoke with uplifted ladles: the brightly shining one of pure radiance, the ageless, ancient Agni of the clans, worthy of praise.
The mortal who has brought an oblation to him [Agni] with gifts of offering — he secures abundant nourishment and glory with heroic power.
The offering-ladle, full of the oblation, approaches with homage the foremost Jātavedas, Agni, the most ancient in sacrifices.

title: Rigveda
text:
With these, the greatest [thoughts], most bountiful, like those of Vyaśva, may we serve Agni, the one of pure radiance.
Sing now to the sky-traverser with hymns like those of Sthūrayūpa; O seer of the line of Vyaśva, [sing] to Agni the tamer [of foes].
The inspired poets implore the ancient Agni, the guest of men and son of the forest trees, for protection.
O Agni, sitting before all the great [gods] and before the human oblations, seat thyself upon the sacred grass with homage.
Win for us many desirable things; win for us wealth much longed-for, with excellent heroic force, with offspring, and with renown.
Thou art the best, O Agni; rouse the people to prosperity; bestow thy gift always and perpetually, O youngest [one], O lord of wealth.
Thou art indeed easy to call upon; grant us impulses rich in cattle; increase the winning of great wealth, O Agni.
O Agni, thou art glorious; bring hither Mitra and Varuṇa, the upholders of ṛta, the two sovereign lords of pure discernment.
Friends, let us recite the sacred word for Indra the vajra-bearer; I praise for you him who is foremost among men, the bold one.
For thou art renowned for might, the slayer of Vṛtra by thy slaying of Vṛtra; O hero, thou surpassest the generous with thy bounties.
While being praised, bring to us the wealth most brilliant in fame; for thou, O bay-horsed one, art the wealth-giver even in isolation.
Bring hither what is apart [from others] and what is dear [to us] among the [goods] of peoples, O Indra; being praised, bring [it] boldly, O bold one.
The hasty ones cannot restrain thy left hand nor thy right hand, O bay-horsed lord; no obstruction [holds thee back] in the quest for cattle.
I drive thee with my songs as [one drives] cattle toward the pen, O stone-wielder; fill full the desire and the mind of the praiser.

title: Rigveda
text:
With thy all-embracing mind, with our thought, O foremost slayer of Vṛtra, come here above us, O terrible leader, O lord of wealth.
May we know of thee, O slayer of Vṛtra, O hero, the latest [bounty] — of the wealth most to be desired, O much-invoked Indra, of the bounty.
O Indra, as it is — truly thy strength is unlimited, O manly one; thy gift for the worshipper is undiminished, O much-invoked one.
Rain down, O great lord, for great bounty, O most manly one; make [us] firm even in the firm [battle], O bountiful one, so that we may obtain thy gifts.
Now our hopes have gone nowhere but to thee, O stone-wielder; fulfil that for us, O bountiful one, with thy aids.
