Truly, O manly one, I find no other than thee for bounty, for wealth, for brilliance, and for might, O lover of praise.
Pour out the soma-drop for Indra; he drinks the sweet soma-honey; drive [us] forward with his bounty and his greatness.
I addressed the lord of the bay horses who mingles discernment [with action]: hear now the praise of him who sings of horses.
Truly, never in former times was one born more heroic than thee; none [is equal to thee] in wealth, nor in power, nor in the bestowing of gifts.
Pour forth something more intoxicating of the sweet mead, O adhvaryu; for thus is the ever-waxing hero praised.
O Indra, master of the bay horses, no one has reached thy ancient glory in might, nor in the giving of gifts.
Him, the lord of prizes, we call upon for you — we who seek fame — the one to be strengthened with unwearied sacrifices.
Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the man worthy of hymns, who alone overreaches all the peoples.
Speak the wondrous word to him who does not hoard cattle, who seeks cattle, who is heavenly — sweeter than ghee and sweeter than honey.
He whose heroic deeds are immeasurable, whose bounty is not to be encompassed — the gift of his right hand pervades all things like light.

title: Rigveda
text:
Praise Indra like Vyaśva: him of unwavering waves, the prize-winner, the controller, the noble one who bestows wealth upon the worshipper.
Even thus, O descendant of Vyaśva, praise him now for the tenth and ninth time: the one who knows well and is ever-active among those who move about.
For thou knowest the avoidance of calamities, O vajra-handed one, day by day — as the purifier [knows] the circuit of [his] steps.
Bring that, O Indra, for our gain, O most wondrous one; impel [us] to action; spur Kutsa twofold for his deeds.
We implore thee now with new [praise], O most wondrous one, for the gaining [of wealth]; so thou shalt overcome all hostile assaults upon us.
He who releases from hardship in the bear-[haunted realm], who [delivers] from danger in the seven rivers — O mighty-spirited one, we have bent down the weapon of the Dāsa.
As thou didst bring wealth to the excellent-song [singer] for the gaining [thereof], to the [descendants] of Vyaśva, O blessed one, O possessor of prize-winning steeds.
May the gift of the right hand of the noble one go to the soma-pressing descendants of Vyaśva — the abundant bounty, a hundredfold, a thousandfold.
When the sacrificer asks thee, led astray by a deceiver and a deceiving deed, [say:] this Vala, when laid open, stands [revealed] before the cow-rich [realm].
Those two of you, O gods worthy of sacrifice among the gods, O guardians of all, O upholders of ṛta and of pure discernment, I sacrifice to you.
Mitra and Varuṇa — their bond is like that of chariot-fellows — and he of good purpose; from of old well-born, [their] offspring, keepers of their vow.
The great Aditi, the mother of all knowledge and of divine power, the one abounding in ṛta, bore those two of boundless greatness.
The great Mitra and Varuṇa, the two sovereign lords, divine Asuras, upholders of ṛta, proclaim ṛta with a great voice.

title: Rigveda
text:
Grandsons of great might, sons of Dakṣa, of good purpose, givers of flowing [gifts], sitters upon the dwelling-place of nourishments.
You two have brought together the divine and earthly nourishments; may the cloud-bearing rains come to you.
They who look down from the great heaven as [a herdsman looks] over his herd — the two upholders of ṛta, the sovereign lords, devoted to homage.
The two upholders of ṛta, of good purpose, have sat down for sovereign rule; the keepers of their vow, the rulers, have attained dominion.
With glaring eye [they watch], more knowledgeable than even the eye itself [in finding] a path; unblinking and sharp-sighted, they have discerned everything.
And may the divine Aditi protect us and [may] the Nāsatyas [protect us]; may the Maruts of grown might protect us.
May those good givers protect our ship by day and by night; may we, unharmed, remain under [their] guard.
Unharmed, to thee, O Viṣṇu, O good giver, we address [our prayer]; hear, O self-moving river Sindhu, for [thy] ancient understanding.
We choose that most excellent, desirable [protection] which guards — what Mitra guards, what Varuṇa guards, what Aryamā guards.
And may the Sindhu of the waters grant us that; the Maruts, the Aśvins, Indra, Viṣṇu — all the generous ones in unison.
For those men who are eager [to please them] strike back the hostile designs of any whatsoever — [fierce] as the raging current strikes back — they are impetuous.
This one sovereign lord truly sees widely and abundantly; following his ordinances do we move.
We follow the ancient, well-known [ordinances] of the sovereign rule — the vows of Mitra and Varuṇa, heard far and wide.
He who has measured with his cord the boundaries of heaven and earth, who has filled both the world-halves with his greatness.
The sun has raised up the light in the shelter of heaven; like Agni bright, once kindled and invoked.

title: Rigveda
text:
He is lord of speech whose dwelling-place is vast, lord of the prize rich in cattle; he is the lord of the invigorating nourishment to give.
That sun I invoke before both world-halves, at evening and at morning; always shine upon us among the generous ones.
The gleaming [bull] on its path, the silver-bright on the golden [track] — may we obtain the yoked chariot in the good soma [pressing].
Those two who urge on [the steeds] of horses, [those who guide] the bay horses — and also the man-carrying [bay steeds] of [those] who act [heroically].
With gleaming reins and whips, with the freshest inspired thought, the two great prize-winning coursers are seated together.
I call your chariot for the common praise among the patrons; [you] of unweakened power, O bulls, O lords with strong bulls.
You two are the best for [him of] excellent soma-song, for great offspring, O Nāsatyas; come with your aids, O bulls, O lords with strong bulls.
We call upon you two today with our oblations, O lords of prizes; [you who] quicken the many impulses through the nights.
May your swiftest chariot come, O renowned Aśvins, O men; you appear at the praises of Tura for [his] glory.
Even while going astray, O Aśvins, you two would be well-disposed, O lords with strong bulls; for you two, O Rudras, carry [us] beyond our foes.
For you wonders travel continually around everything with swiftness; quickeners of thought, honey-bright, lords of beauty.
Come to us, O Aśvins, together with wealth that nourishes all, O bountiful ones with excellent heroic force, ever-steadfast.
Come toward me directly for this, O Indra and Nāsatyas; today, O gods, [come] to the gods as the most helpful companions.
For we call upon you two, seeking cattle-wealth like the [descendants] of Vyaśva; come hither, O inspired ones, with your benevolences.

title: Rigveda
text:
O seer, praise the Aśvins well; perchance [they] who drive by swiftly will hear the call — even from nearer than the Paṇis.
You men know the fame of the descendant of Vyaśva and know of this [hymn] of mine; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryamā [are] in accord.
O bulls, instruct me day by day in what has been given by you and what has been brought by you among the patrons.
He who is enveloped by your sacrifices like a bride clothed in garments — he who serves you two has caused beauty [to be made], O Aśvins.
He who perceives your most wide-ranging [bounty] worthy of men, to him, O Aśvins, come round on your course, eager for us.
Come to us well, O lords with strong bulls, on your course worthy of men; as if against traitors you have borne our sacrifice with your song.
The hymn of praise, the best bearer of your invocations, shall be the messenger calling [you], O men; let it belong to you two, O Aśvins.
Whether you two are in that ocean of heaven, or taking joy in [your] home with refreshments — hear, O immortal ones, this [hymn] of mine.
And this white-coursing [river], the best bearer among the rivers — the Sindhu with her golden track.
With this good fame, O Aśvins, with this white thought, you two who travel brightly shall carry [us].
Harness, O Vāyu, the chariot-supporters, yoke the nourishing ones, O lord of wealth; come and drink the sweet [soma] of ours; come to our soma-pressings.
Thy aids, O Vāyu, lord of ṛta, O wondrous son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose [for ourselves].
We, the people who have pressed the soma, brilliant [in song], implore the son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of wealth — Vāyu.
Come, O Vāyu, with auspicious [gifts] from heaven; carry well [the omen of] good horses; carry [us] with great, broad-winged [speed] in thy chariot.
Thee, the most easy to find a place with among the places of men, we invoke — like the pressing-stone, not [like one who rides] on the horse's back, with generosity.

title: Rigveda
text:
So do thou, O god Vāyu, in thy mind, rejoicing as the foremost one, grant us prizes; drive forward [our] thoughts.
Agni is appointed hotar in the recitation, the pressing-stones and sacred grass at the sacrifice; with my verse I approach the Maruts, the lord of the sacred word, the gods, the most excellent help.
Thou encompassest cattle, earth, forest trees, Dawn and Night, the plants; and may all of you, O Vasus, all-knowing, be the promoters of our thoughts.
Let our sacrifice go forward among the gods, the ancient one [proceeding] to Agni; [let it go] to Varuṇa the keeper of his vow among the Ādityas, and to the Maruts of all-pervading radiance.
For all of them, all-knowing and devouring enemies, truly existed for the growth of Manu; with uninjured guardianship, all-knowing, may they lead us to a safe shelter.
Come to us today, all of you with one mind, all in accord; with verse and song, O Maruts, O divine Aditi, [come] to our great domestic dwelling.
Come, O Maruts, toward the dear [offerings] and those of yours that are equine — the oblations, O Mitra; let Indra, Varuṇa, the swift men, the Ādityas, sit down on our sacred grass.
We, with strewn sacred grass, with offerings set in place, in succession, with pressed soma, O Varuṇa, we call upon you — with fires kindled as in the [time of] Manu.
Come forward, O Maruts, Viṣṇu, Aśvins, Pūṣan, with no niggardly thought; let Indra come first with his prize-winning [powers] — the bull whom I praise as the slayer of Vṛtra.
Protect us, O gods, free of malice, with unbroken shelter; for no sheltering [power], whether from far or near, even now subdues [the foe], O Vasus.
There is a community of kind with you, O gods who devour enemies; there is kinship; speak to us for our former well-being, quickly for a newer blessedness.
Now indeed I have sent forth homage to you and now [homage] for the obtaining of the good [gift] — I, who reverently approach you all-knowing ones, as if toward another.

title: Rigveda
text:
He, your Savitṛ, O best-guiding ones, has stood up high, most excellent; the two-footed [creatures] and the four-footed ones have come to rest, [and so have] the flying ones who seek their purpose.
Each god among you for protection, each god for favor — each god we call for the winning of prizes, celebrating [each one] with our divine thought.
For all the gods, with one mind, all together, were truly generous to Manu; may they today and tomorrow, in our want, in our need, be the finders of wide space for us.
I declare for you, O guileless ones, at the gathering of praises: no deception [afflicts] that mortal, O Varuṇa and Mitra, who has given devotion to your ordinances.
He who gives devotion to your favor extends his dwelling, [gaining] manifold impulses; he is born [abundantly] with offspring according to the law; uninjured, he prospers fully.
He finds [success] in battle without [harm], travels the roads by easy [paths] — him whom Aryamā, Mitra, and Varuṇa, generous and in accord, protect.
Even in the open field make for him an easy descent [from danger]; even in a narrow pass a good escape; even this thunderbolt that has missed its mark from this [foe] — let it vanish away.
What you, O dear-sovereignty ones, establish as ṛta when the sun rises, O all-knowing ones, and at sunset, at awakening, or at midday of the sky —
And whatever ṛta you Asuras direct toward [us] at the drawing near of gifts, what shelter you two determine for the worshipper — may we stand in the midst of that, O Vasus, all-knowing.
What good [thing] you, all-knowing, place for Manu at the rising of the sun, and at the coming of midday — [you bestow it] upon him who pours the oblation, the wise-minded.
That [bounty] of you sovereign rulers we choose like a son [chooses] what is much to be drunk; may we, O Ādityas, when we pour the oblation, attain that by which we may enjoy better things.

title: Rigveda
text:
The gods who, more than thirty-three, have sat on the sacred grass — they found [it], and also sat down in both [realms].
Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryamā — the fires of memorable generosity — accompanied by their spouses, summoned with the vaṣaṭ-call.
They are our guardians in the south, they in the north, they rightly here below and above — in front with all the folk.
As the gods wish, so indeed it shall be; no one diminishes that [will] of theirs; no mortal [is] without their bounty.
Of the seven [groups], seven are their spear-points, seven are their glories; seven are borne upon their splendors.
One [god] is tawny-brown and facing both ways, youthful; he anoints himself with gold.
One, the shining one, has sat down in the womb [of the altar], the wise one among the gods.
One holds the iron axe in his hand, the firm one among the gods.
One holds the vajra in his hand, laid ready; with it he strikes down the Vṛtras.
One holds the sharp weapon in his hand — the pure, terrible one, the healer with cool medicines.
One watches over the paths as a thief [watches]; he knows the treasures hidden [along the way].
One of wide stride has stepped out the three [steps] to where the gods rejoice.
Two travel with the birds, together with one; they dwell as if [going] abroad on a journey.
Two have made their seat the highest in heaven, the two sovereign rulers, at the pressing of ghee and soma.
Some, singing, comprehended the great Sāman; by it they made the sun to shine.
There is no one among you who is a small child, O gods, no one who is a mere boy; all of you are truly great.
Having been thus praised, you have been [revealed as] the devourers of enemies — you who are thirty-three, O gods of Manu, worthy of sacrifice.
Protect us, help us, and speak above us; do not lead us far away from the ancestral paths of Manu, to a remote distance.

title: Rigveda
text:
You gods who stand here, all of you, Vaiśvānara as well — grant to us shelter of broad extent, [shelter for] cattle and horses.
He who sacrifices — he alone truly sacrifices — who both presses the soma and cooks the oblation: such a man has found favour, like a priest, with Indra.
He who presents to Indra the sacrificial cake, the soma, and the milk-mixture — even from such distress does Śakra free him.
His chariot shall be resplendent, impelled by the gods, growing in strength, conquering all hostile forces.
In his house, Iḷā, rich in cattle, never failing, milks her udder day by day with progeny in abundance.
Those husband and wife who, of one mind, press the soma and hasten to the ritual — for them the gods are ever present with their milk-mixture.
Together they reach toward the sacrificial grass spread here to receive the prāśitra offering; they two are never wearied in the winning of prizes.
They do not conceal the benevolence of the gods nor do they withhold it; they seek to win great glory.
That pair, blessed with sons and daughters, enjoy full length of life — both of them adorned with gold.
They who enjoy the fire's oblation, who have accumulated wealth, honouring the immortal rightly — they milk the woolly udder together and render service among the gods.
We choose the shelter of the mountains and of the rivers, and the shelter of Viṣṇu who is ever present with us.
May Pūṣan come, and riches, and Bhaga — welfare most all-sustaining; may the wide road be for our wellbeing.
Aramati, ever undisturbed, fully in accord with the mind of the universal god — she is truly the faultless one among the Ādityas.
Even as Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa are our guardians, may the path of Ṛta be easy to travel.
With this hymn I praise Agni for you, the ancient god, foremost among the Vasus — as we worship him who is dear to many, who, like Mitra, accomplishes things in the field.

title: Rigveda
text:
Swiftly moves the chariot of him who has the gods with him, or the hero in whatever battles — the sacrificer who seeks to please the will of the gods surpasses those who do not sacrifice.
You do not suffer harm, O sacrificer; nor the soma-presser, nor the devout worshipper — the sacrificer who seeks to please the will of the gods surpasses those who do not sacrifice.
No one can harm him through deeds; no one has driven him away nor drives him away — the sacrificer who seeks to please the will of the gods surpasses those who do not sacrifice.
There shall be good heroic strength and that famed wealth of horses for him — the sacrificer who seeks to please the will of the gods surpasses those who do not sacrifice.
Proclaim, O Kaṇvas, in your song the deeds of Indra, the soma-drinker, in the exhilaration of the soma.
He who, fierce, releasing the waters, slew Sṛbinda who gave no gifts, Pipru, the Dāsa Ahīśuva.
O Indra, that manly feat belongs to you — that you pushed down the broad top, the height of Arbuda.
For you who are renowned I boldly call upon Indra — swift as Tūrṇāśa from the mountain-top — the well-jawed one, for his aid.
Exhilarated by the soma-draughts, you burst open the stall of cows and horses, O hero, like a fortress.
If you have delighted in my pressed soma or set your pleasure in my hymn, come from afar of your own accord.
Indeed we are your praisers, O Indra, who art praised with hymns; invigorate us, O soma-drinker.
Bring us nourishment, gladly sharing what is inexhaustible, O Maghavan — your wealth is abundant.
Make us also rich in cattle, rich in gold, and rich in horses; may we lay hold of Iḷā's blessings.
We call upon Bṛbaduktham, upon the Sṛprakarṇas, for aid, for the protection of him who acts rightly.
He who, even amid a battle, at once acts thus — the Vṛtra-slayer, Śatakratu, rich in goods, for his praisers.

title: Rigveda
text:
May even powerful Śakra be able, bringing gifts from the interior — Indra with all his aids.
Him who is the great sustainer of wealth, easy to cross, the friend of the soma-presser — sing to that Indra.
Him who is coming, greatly steadfast, winning glory in battles, ruling over abundance with his strength.
No one is the restrainer of his powers, of his true and gracious gifts; no one who says 'he will not give.'
There is now no debt owed by the brahmins who press soma and consume the oblation; the soma is not drunk unrewarded.
Sing of the wondrous one; recite hymns of the wondrous one; compose the prayer — it is for the wondrous one.
The wondrous one who goes unchecked shakes down hundreds and thousands — Indra the prize-winner, who increases the sacrificer.
Pass freely through the peoples according to your own will, following the invocations; O Indra, drink of the pressed juices.
Drink of those who follow their own will, and of him who is with Tugrya, and of this one too, O Indra, who is yours.
Come past him who presses soma in anger; come to the one who has well pressed near at hand; drink of this soma that has been given.
Go to the three distant regions, go beyond the five peoples — the hymn-speech has shone clearly upon Indra.
As the sun releases a ray, may my hymns reach you and guide you aright, as waters flow downward to their goal.
O Adhvaryu, pour the soma for the hero with prominent lips; bring it for him to drink of the pressed juice.
He who split the cloud-dam of the waters and released the rivers downward, who held back what was ripened in the cows.
He slew Vṛtra, Ṛcīṣama, Aurṇavābha, Ahīśuva; he struck Arbuda with frost.
Sing forth the god-given prayer to the fierce and inexorable one, the unconquerable, the all-subduing.
Indra, in the exhilaration of the soma-draught, takes note of all the ordinances among the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Here those two tawny steeds who rejoice together, golden-maned, carry him toward the oblation that is set forth.
O much-praised one, your two tawny steeds praised by Priyamedha shall carry you hitherward to drink the soma.
We indeed, having pressed soma, like waters with the kuśa-grass spread, O Vṛtra-slayer, sit around the streams of the purifying filter as your praisers.
The men sound forth praises of you at the soma-pressing, O Vasu, with uninterrupted hymns; when will you come thirstily to your home, to the pressed soma, O Indra, like a bull-elephant to its lair?
O bold one, boldly burst open the thousandfold prize for the Kaṇvas; O tawny-formed Maghavan, wide-seeing one, we desire quickly a prize rich in cattle.
Guard the exhilarating drink of the soma's essence for Indra, O Medhyātithi — he who is intermingled with his two tawny steeds, who is present at the pressing, the vajra-bearer, whose chariot is golden.
He who is well invoked, well rewarding, the lord who is praised for his good resolve, he who is the mine of thousands, who has a hundred gifts — Indra who is invoked as fort-splitter.
He who is bold, unimpeded, who rests his power upon his beard — Vibhūtadyumna, the one who shakes all, praised by many, in might like a bull by reason of his wisdom.
Who knows him drinking together at the soma-pressing? What body has he assumed? — He who shatters strongholds with his strength, intoxicated by the soma-draught, the jawed drinker.
You have taken up a far-ranging movement like a liberal bull-elephant; no one restrains you — come to the soma-pressing, you who move in greatness with your power.
He who, being fierce and not overcome, stands firm, prepared for battle — if Maghavan hears the call of the praiser, Indra would not tarry but would come.
Truly thus you are a bull; impelled by virile strength, unimpeded; a bull you are heard, O fierce one, even afar; a bull you are renowned here close at hand.

title: Rigveda
text:
Your reins are virile, virile the golden goad, virile the chariot, O Maghavan, virile your two tawny steeds — you yourself are a bull, O Śatakratu.
Let the virile presser press for you, O bull, O Ṛjīpin, bring hither; a bull stirs the bulls in the rivers for you, O steadfast one, master of the tawny steeds.
Come, O Indra, to drink the sweet soma-drink, O mightiest one — let Maghavan, of good resolve, hear these hymns and prayers directed toward him here.
Let the tawny steeds yoked to the car carry you hitherward to stand in the chariot; pass beyond the pressings of others, O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu.
Fix your mind upon our most intimate praise-hymn of today, O greatest of the great; may our pressings be most blissful for your exhilaration, O resplendent soma-drinker.
Truly that hero who brought us here — neither in your instruction nor in mine nor in another's does he take pleasure.
Even Indra himself has said this: the mind of a woman is not worthy of praise, and moreover her will is fickle.
Even the two that carry the chariot together, a pair shaken by intoxication — even so the bull's yoke is the upper one.
Look downward, not upward; draw your feet closer together; let not your hair-knots be seen — for you have become a woman-priest.
O Indra, come with your tawny steeds to the fine praise of Kaṇva — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
May the speaking pressing-stone here, resonant with the soma-sound, draw you — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Here the rim of these wheels does not rattle — the wolf shakes not the sheep — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
The Kaṇvas call you hither for protection, for the winning of prizes — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.

title: Rigveda
text:
I offer you, O bull, the first draught of the pressed juices — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come to us, possessed of power and wisdom, all-knowing, for our aid — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come to us, O greatly wise, O possessor of a thousand streams, O Śatāmagha — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
May the praiseworthy Hotṛ, established by Manu, carry you to the divine sphere — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Your two tawny steeds, shaken by exhilaration, shall carry you like a falcon on its wings — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come hither, O noble lord, come round about — svāhā! — to drink the soma — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come to us, O Upaśruti; take delight here in our hymns — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come well to us with matching pairs, O one whose horses are well gathered, with well-gathered gifts — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Come from the mountains, from the height above the ocean — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Burst open for us thousands of cattle-prizes and horse-prizes, O hero — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
Bring to us by thousands, by ten thousands, and by hundreds — commanded by yonder heaven, go to heaven, O nourisher by day.
When Indra and I have brought a thousand of the glowing-with-wealth, the mightiest of horse-prizes, the cattle-wealth.
Those that are chestnut-bright, swift as the wind, ruddy and light-footed — they shine like suns.
Among the gifts of Pārāvata, among the swift ones with rolling wheels, I stand in the middle of the forest.

title: Rigveda
text:
Together with Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, being present with them — together with Dawn, and with the Sun — drink the soma, O Aśvins.
Together with all intuitions, with the world, O prize-winners, with heaven, earth, and mountains being present — together with Dawn and with the Sun — drink the soma, O Aśvins.
Together with all the gods — three and eleven — with the Maruts here, with the Bhṛgus, being present — together with Dawn and with the Sun — drink the soma, O Aśvins.
Be pleased with the sacrifice, be aware of my invocation; come here, O both divine ones, to both pressings — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bring sustenance to us, O Aśvins.
Be pleased with the hymn as young men with maidens; come here, O both divine ones, to both pressings — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bring sustenance to us, O Aśvins.
Be pleased with the hymns, be pleased with the sacrifice; come here, O both divine ones, to both pressings — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bring sustenance to us, O Aśvins.
You two fly like golden falcons to the forest; you come to the pressed soma like two buffaloes — together with Dawn and with the Sun — come round three times, O Aśvins.
You two fly like swans, like those that traverse the path; you come to the pressed soma like two buffaloes — together with Dawn and with the Sun — come round three times, O Aśvins.
You two fly like two eagles for the offering of the oblation; you come to the pressed soma like two buffaloes — together with Dawn and with the Sun — come round three times, O Aśvins.
Drink and be sated, and come here; bestow progeny and bestow wealth — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bestow vigour upon us, O Aśvins.
Conquer and urge forward your praisers; bestow progeny and bestow wealth — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bestow vigour upon us, O Aśvins.

title: Rigveda
text:
Smite the enemies and restrain the friendly ones; bestow progeny and bestow wealth — together with Dawn and with the Sun — bestow vigour upon us, O Aśvins.
Together with Mitra-Varuṇa, together with Dharma, together with the Maruts, come you both to the call of the praiser — together with Dawn and with the Sun, come with the Ādityas, O Aśvins.
Together with the Aṅgirasas, together with Viṣṇu, together with the Maruts, come you both to the call of the praiser — together with Dawn and with the Sun, come with the Ādityas, O Aśvins.
Together with the Ṛbhus, O ye bulls, together with the prize-winners, with the Maruts, come you both to the call of the praiser — together with Dawn and with the Sun, come with the Ādityas, O Aśvins.
Quicken the prayer and quicken the inspired thoughts; smite the demons and drive away the diseases — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, come to the soma-presser.
Quicken the royal power and quicken the men; smite the demons and drive away the diseases — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, come to the soma-presser.
Quicken the milk-cows and quicken the clans; smite the demons and drive away the diseases — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, come to the soma-presser.
Hear the ancient praise of Śyāvāśva as he presses soma, O ye two who are shaken by exhilaration, as once you heard Atri — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, across the day.
Release streams of fine praises toward Śyāvāśva who presses soma, O ye two shaken by exhilaration — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, across the day.
Guide the reins of the sacrificial rites toward Śyāvāśva who presses soma, O ye two shaken by exhilaration — together with Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, across the day.
Turn the chariot hither, drink the sweet soma; come here, O Aśvins — I call upon you both with desire for aid; bestow treasures upon the worshipper.

title: Rigveda
text:
O ye heroes, when the reverential call is set forth at the sacrifice, to drink the soma-drink — come here, O Aśvins; I call upon you both with desire for aid; bestow treasures upon the worshipper.
Be sated, O divine pair, with the soma-draught prepared with svāhā — come here, O Aśvins; I call upon you both with desire for aid; bestow treasures upon the worshipper.
You are the protector of the soma-presser who has spread the sacred grass; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.
Help the praiser, O Maghavan, he who helps you; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.
With nourishment protect the gods; with strength protect yourself; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.
Begetter of heaven, begetter of the earth; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.
You are the begetter of horses, the begetter of cattle; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.
Make the hymn of the Atris great, O stone-armed one; drink the soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu — that share which all-conquering armies have preserved for you, striding widely, meeting in the waters — O Indra accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of the good.

title: Rigveda
text:
Hear thus Śyāvāśva pressing soma, as you heard Atri performing his deeds; you alone protected Trasadasyu, O hero-overpowering Indra, making the prayers grow.
Mightily have you protected this prayer in the slayings of Vṛtra; protect the soma-presser, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
Overpowering, fierce against the armies, against the deceivers, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
You reign as sole king over this world, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
You alone drive away both the moving and the stationary, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
You rule over security and over its means of attainment, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
You protect for the sake of dominion; it is you who protect, O lord of might, Indra, with all your aids; O Vṛtra-slayer, beyond reproach, O bearer of the vajra, drink of the midday soma-pressing.
Hear thus Śyāvāśva singing aloud, as you heard Atri performing his deeds; you alone protected Trasadasyu, O hero-overpowering Indra, making royal powers grow.
You two are indeed the ritual priests of the sacrifice, victorious in prize-winnings and in deeds — O Indrāgnī, be aware of this.
You two, hastening your chariot, are the slayers of Vṛtra and unconquered — O Indrāgnī, be aware of this.
This sweet, intoxicating drink the men have milked with the pressing-stones for you two — O Indrāgnī, be aware of this.

title: Rigveda
text:
Be pleased with the sacrifice for the attainment of desires, with the pressed soma — ye who are praised together — O Indrāgnī, come hither, O heroes.
Be pleased with these pressings by which you have been offered the oblations — O Indrāgnī, come hither, O heroes.
Be pleased with this my fine praise that moves in the Gāyatrī metre — O Indrāgnī, come hither, O heroes.
Come with the morning rites, with the gods, O ye two whose wealth is desirable — O Indrāgnī, to drink the soma.
Hear the invocation of Śyāvāśva who presses soma, and of the Atris — O Indrāgnī, to drink the soma.
Thus I have invoked you both for aid, just as the wise invoke you — O Indrāgnī, to drink the soma.
I choose the protection of Indrāgnī, who are accompanied by Sarasvatī — in whose honour the Gāyatrī is chanted.
I have praised Agni, worthy of hymns; Agni is to be praised and worshipped; may Agni anoint us among the gods — for the seer moves as messenger between both the assemblies. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
O Agni, set down upon our bodies with fresh speech the praise of these worshippers; set down upon the miserly the hostility of all — may the foe's hostilities depart from here, the witless one. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
O Agni, the prayers for you are poured as ghee upon the mouth; make those known among the gods — for you are the ancient, the beneficent messenger of Vivasvat. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Agni bestows sustenance just as the pitiful one supplicates; the oblation of nourishment of the Vasus, and happiness and welfare, he bestows for every divine invocation. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Agni perceived with the more powerful by wondrous deeds; he is the Hotṛ encompassed with gifts for all time, and he drives off the adversary. Let the others on the same side be confounded.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni is the birth-place of the gods; Agni knows the secret of mortals; Agni is the bestower of wealth; Agni, well-invoked, opens the doors with fresh oblation. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Agni dwells together with the gods; he is among the clans in the sacrificial assemblies; he joyfully nourishes the many poetic visions, everything, like the earth — the divine and sacrificeable one among the gods. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
That Agni who is Saptamānuṣa, who resides in all the rivers — to him we have come, the triple-stationed one, belonging to Mandhātṛ, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the ancient Agni at the sacrifices. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Agni, the seer, dwells upon the three triple-layered realms; the inspired messenger, perfectly formed, shall here worship and delight us with the three sets of eleven. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
You alone, O Agni, ancient one, rule over our life-forces, over wealth among the gods; the flowing waters with their own banks circle around you. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
O Indrāgnī, you two conquering heroes bestow riches upon us — wealth whereby even in the contests we might overcome what is firmly fixed and strong, as fire in the forest with the wind. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
We do not choose you two by exclusion — we indeed worship Indra, the mightiest, the hero among men; may he come to us at some time with his steed for the winning of prizes, may he come for the winning of sacrifice. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Those two, Indrāgnī, are settled in the middle of sustenance; those two seers with their poet-wisdom, when questioned, come together in friendship and together attain what is laid down, O heroes. Let the others on the same side be confounded.

title: Rigveda
text:
Praise Indrāgnī with song and hymn as Nabhāka did — those two in whose great lap this whole moving world, yonder heaven and earth, carry their treasure. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Send forth the prayers to Indrāgnī as Nabhāka did — those prayers that uncovered the ocean with seven foundations, with the oblique shore — Indra the ruler by his power. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Cut away as of old, deceive the Dāsa's swelling power as one lops a tree's branch; may we share out that accumulated wealth of his together with Indra. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
When these peoples call upon Indrāgnī with their lineages and hymns, may we, with our heroes, overcome those who battle against us and conquer those who would conquer us. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Those two that are white, rising upward from heaven, moving alongside the days — the rivers following the ordinance of Indrāgnī go along, those which they two released from their bond. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Many are your similar forms, O Indra, many too your praised deeds, O son of Hinva, O tawny-steeded one; may those who are the sources of heroic wealth now accomplish our inspired thoughts. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Whet him with fine praises — the resplendent champion worthy of hymns; and may he who by his strength shatters Śuṣṇa's eggs conquer the water-bearing streams. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Whet him who conducts the sacrifice well, the true champion, the seasonable one; and may he who shatters with unstoppable force the eggs of Śuṣṇa conquer the water-bearing streams. Let the others on the same side be confounded.
Thus to Indrāgnī in the manner of the Fathers, newly, as Mandhātṛ and the Aṅgirasas declared: protect us with threefold shelter — may we be lords of riches.

title: Rigveda
text:
Sing praise to him for our abundance — to Varuṇa, to the Maruts, to those who know most; who, as the herdsman keeps cattle, guards the thoughts of men. May the others perish all alike.
Praise him with harmonious song, with the hymns of the Fathers, with the praises of Nābhāka — who at the rising of the rivers stands as middle one with seven sisters. May the others perish all alike.
He has embraced the nights; by his māyā he has laid the dawns within; he is visible encompassing all. Three Dawns have grown great following his ordinance, his streams. May the others perish all alike.
He who sustains the summits, visible above the earth — the primal footstep of Varuṇa is his steed; for he is a shepherd, like a protector of the fold. May the others perish all alike.
He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret names of the dawn-cows — that seer nourishes manifold forms with his wisdom-songs, as the sky does. May the others perish all alike.
In him all poetic wisdom is lodged as in a hub; they serve Trita swiftly; as cows meet in the fold, he yoked the horses to the yoke. May the others perish all alike.
He who in those mantles reposes — all creatures are his; he has touched round about the dwellings of Varuṇa in the heavenly abode; all the gods follow his ordinance. May the others perish all alike.
He, the hidden ocean, swiftly ascends like the sky; when he laid the sacred formula in those waters; he spread his steps with flaming māyā, ascending the vault of heaven. May the others perish all alike.
His white, far-seeing ones have spread over the three earths; the upper realms have been filled thrice; he rules Varuṇa's fixed abode, sovereign over the seven. May the others perish all alike.
He who made the white ones with shining raiment and the dark ones to follow his ordinance; he measured out the primal domain; he who with his prop held apart the two worlds, sustaining the sky like an unborn one. May the others perish all alike.

title: Rigveda
text:
The mighty lord, all-knowing, propped up the sky, he measured out the breadth of the earth; he, the universal sovereign, has established all the worlds — all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.
Thus praise Varuṇa the lofty; with reverence worship the wise guardian of immortality; may he grant us threefold shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap.
O god Varuṇa, sharpen together the resolve and discernment of this suppliant's devotion; by that may we cross over all difficulties and mount a well-constructed ship.
O Aśvins, the pressing-stones have stirred toward you, the inspired seers with their hymns; O Nāsatyas, come for the drinking of soma. May the others perish all alike.
As Atri the inspired sage called to you both, O Aśvins, with his songs; O Nāsatyas, come for the drinking of soma. May the others perish all alike.
Thus I call to you both for aid, even as the wise have called; O Nāsatyas, come for the drinking of soma. May the others perish all alike.
These songs of praise go forth for the inspired and creative Agni, who is worshipped with unceasing sacrifices.
For you, O Jātavedas, wide-seeing one, who art delighted in return — O Agni, I fashion the beautiful praise-song.
Truly, O Agni, your sharp flames are like teeth; with them you devour the forests.
The tawny ones with banners of smoke, urged on by the wind toward the sky — the flames of Agni strive in all directions.
These flames of Agni, kindled and striving everywhere, were seen gathered together like the banners of the Dawns.
The dark regions tread his path at the advance of Jātavedas, when Agni spreads across the earth.
Making nourishment, Agni devours the plants yet does not diminish them, going again to the young shoots.
With his tongues he bows down, crackling and blazing with his flame; Agni shines in the forests.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, your dwelling is in the waters; you pervade the herbs; you are born again in the womb.
O Agni, that flame of yours blazes upward from the oblation of ghee when it is offered, licking at the mouth of the ladle.
With praises let us serve Agni, who is fed with bulls, fed with cows, whose back is the soma, the creative one.
And we implore you, O Agni, with homage, O Hotṛ, O most excellent in purpose, with kindling-sticks.
And you, O gleaming Agni who receivest offerings, we invoke as Bhṛgu did, as Manu did, as the Aṅgirases did.
For you, O Agni, inspired among the inspired, being true among the true, are kindled as friend by the friend.
So you, O Agni, give to the inspired, bountiful worshipper a thousandfold wealth, a vigour accompanied by heroes.
O Agni, brother, mighty one, with bay steeds, of pure ordinances — accept this hymn of mine.
And O Agni, may they who delight in my praise reach you, bellowing in response to the call, like cows to the cow-stall.
For you, O best of Aṅgirases, all the various fair abodes have been ordered, O Agni, to fulfil your desire.
The wise, the intelligent, the eloquent impel Agni with their thoughts, that he may take his seat at the meal.
Him — you, O Agni — powerful in courses, as they spread out the sacrifice, they laud, the carrier and the Hotṛ-priest.
For you are present everywhere, lord over all peoples; we call upon you in the battles.
Praise him — Agni who is invoked and blazes with the ghee-oblations; may he hear this our call.
Him, you — we call upon the listening Jātavedas, O Agni, who smites away our foes.
This wondrous king of peoples, overseer of the sacred laws — this Agni I praise; and may he hear.
Agni the all-invigorating, quivering like a vigorous youth — we speed him like a prize-winning steed.
O Agni, blazing with your sharp flame, smiting away the foes, burning the rākṣasas at all times.

title: Rigveda
text:
You whom people kindle as Manu did, O best of Aṅgirases — O Agni, that one attend to my words.
Whether you, O Agni, art born in the sky or born in the waters, O mighty one — we invoke you with our songs.
For you indeed these various peoples with all their fair dwellings impel nourishment for your eating.
May we, O Agni, O thou of good thoughts, beholding men, pass through all days, crossing difficult places.
Agni the joyful, beloved of many, swift, with purifying flame — him we implore with joyful hearts.
You, O Agni, luminously wealthy, sending forth rays like the sun, boldly strike down the darkness.
From you, O powerful Agni, we implore that gift which is inexhaustible; from you comes all desirable wealth.
Kindle Agni with fuel; with ghee rouse the guest; pour the oblations into him here.
O Agni, accept my hymn; grow with this meditation; delight in our sacred verses in return.
I place Agni as messenger in front; I invoke the bearer of oblations; may he seat the gods here.
O Agni, your lofty, gleaming flames of the kindled, burning one go forth brilliantly.
Let my ghee-laden ladle approach you, O beloved; O Agni, accept our oblations.
The joyful Hotṛ, the sacrificing priest, brilliant of light, luminously wealthy — Agni I praise; and may he hear.
The ancient, praiseworthy, beloved Agni, wise in intent, the glory of the sacrifices.
O best of Aṅgirases, accepting these oblations one after another, O Agni, lead the sacrifice rightly in due season.
Being kindled here, O brilliant-flaming, truthful one, bring hither, discerning, the divine company.
The inspired Hotṛ, unbeguiling, with banner of smoke, luminously wealthy — the banner of sacrifices we implore.
O Agni, protect us; O god, ward off those who would harm us; shatter enmity, O mighty one.
Agni, adorning his own body with ancient meditation, the seer has increased with the inspired hymn.

title: Rigveda
text:
I call hither the son of strength, Agni of purifying flame, to this sacrificial rite, this good sacrifice.
O Agni, great as Mitra, with your brilliant flame, take your seat on the sacred grass with the gods.
To that mortal who honours Agni, the god, at home in his own body — to him may he shine forth wealth.
Agni is the head, the peak of heaven; lord of the earth is he; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Agni, your pure, brilliant flames blaze upward; your lights, your rays go forth.
For you are lord of desirable gifts, O Agni, master of the sun; may I, your praiser, dwell in your shelter.
You, O Agni, the wise ones impel; they urge you on with their thoughts; may our songs make you grow.
The friendship of Agni — undeceiving, of inherent power, the messenger, ever praising — this we choose.
Agni is most pure in his ordinances, pure, inspired, pure, the seer; blazing pure when the oblation is poured.
And may my devotions, my songs, make you grow at all times, O Agni; be mindful of our friendship.
If I were you, O Agni, or if you were I — your prayers here would be fulfilled in truth.
For you are indeed wealth, lord of wealth, O Agni, luminously wealthy; may we abide in your good favour.
To you, O Agni, of firm ordinances, the bellowing songs go forth as rivers to the sea.
Youthful, lord of the clans, the seer, all-devouring, of manifold vibrations — Agni I adorn with my meditations.
We, on the chariot-road of sacrifices, would seek with praises Agni, the firm one with sharp teeth.
This singer here, O Agni, truly belongs to you; to him, O purifier, be gracious.
For you are wise, seated at the meal, ever watchful like the inspired sage; O Agni, you shine in the sky.
O Agni, O seer, O lord, prolong our life before the troubles come, before the insults come.
Those who kindle Agni and spread the sacred grass continually — Indra is their youthful companion.

title: Rigveda
text:
Lofty indeed is their fuel, great and far-praised the broad post — those whose youthful companion is Indra.
The hero, without fighting, drives back with warriors what is held back in battle — those whose youthful companion is Indra.
The Vṛtra-slayer took the club at birth; he asked his mother clearly: 'Who are the mighty? Who are those who hear?'
Speaking back to you with power, like a warrior at a mountain in the waters, he fights — whoever claims enmity against you.
And hear, O Maghavan: what one desires from you, that you have spoken; whatever you make firm, that is firm.
When Indra the battle-maker, seeking good horses, goes forth to battle — he is the greatest charioteer among charioteers.
Do you, O wielder of the vajra, dispel all attackers in every direction; be our most glorious protector.
May Indra place our chariot in front for victory, that which the deceivers cannot mislead.
May we turn aside your enemies; you are able, O Śakra, to give; may the gift be for us, Indra, rich in cattle.
Even when going slowly, O stone-wielder, they that carry horses, troops of a hundred, are eloquent, sinless.
For day by day thousands and hundreds of joyful words are bestowed upward upon the singers.
For we know you, O Indra, winner of wealth, splitting even the firm things asunder, as one who cleaves like Gaya.
May the Soma drops delight even the eloquent one, O seer, O bold one, when we implore the Paṇi away from you.
He who is ungenerous, who has seized the wealth that belongs to you for his own enjoyment — bring us his wealth.
These too perceive you, your Soma-pressing companions, O Indra, as prosperous ones regard cattle.
Even though you seem deaf to us, we call you here from afar for aid, you who have ears that hear.
If you should hear this call, this hard-to-ignore invocation, and act upon it — be our nearest intimate.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even if through confusion we who have come near you have fallen short — be the giver of cattle, O Indra; be mindful of us.
We have seized you as aged men seize a support, O lord of might; we desire you at the meeting-place.
Sing the praise-song to Indra, of many manly deeds, the warrior whom none resist in battle.
O bull, at the pressing of the pressed Soma, I pour it toward you for drinking; be sated, attain to full exhilaration.
Let not foolish, unhostile men deceive you, nor the mockers; win not those who hate the brahman.
Here may the cow-rich ones exhilarate you for great bounty; drink like a wild bull at a pool.
What the Vṛtra-slayer has obtained in the distant realm, ancient and new — proclaim those in the assemblies.
Indra drank the soma pressed from the water-vessel at the thousand-armed one's place; there he displayed his manly power.
That is true: among the Turvaśas and Yadus, knowing the invincible — he spread glory upon the Turvaṇa in calm.
The swift one of the peoples, the distributor of vigour rich in cattle — I have proclaimed him as the equal one.
Not to be turned away, like Ṛbhukṣan, in the praises, who increases the Tugryas — Indra when the soma is pressed together.
He who cleft open the broad mountain for Triśoka, to release passage for the cattle.
What you seize when you are heedless and exhilarated, what you are about to set in motion — do not do that, O Indra; be gracious.
Even a small deed from one such as you is heard throughout the earth; may your mind come to us, O Indra.
These fair praises would truly be yours, and your glories — when you, O Indra, art gracious to us.
Do not strike us down for a single offence, nor for two, nor for three; do not smite us, O hero, for the many.
For I am afraid of one such as you, the mighty, the overthrower, the wonderful one who bears up in the onslaught.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let not the friend find emptiness, nor the son, O abundant lord; may your mind turn back toward us.
Who then is the companion who, without quarrel, says a true word to his companion? Who now goes away from us?
In such manner, O bull, at the Soma pressing, going to and fro abundantly, not giving out — like a female gambler going downhill.
I grasp your two bay steeds yoked to your words, of beautiful chariot — when you give it to the brahmin-singers.
Shatter all enemies asunder, beat away the harassers, kill the scorners; bring hither that desirable wealth.
What is stored up, O Indra, in the firm one, in the solid, in the rock — bring hither that desirable wealth.
Whose great gift all mankind knows — bring hither that desirable wealth.
We belong to you, O Indra, O abundant lord, O leader — to you, the steady master of the bay steeds.
For we know you truly, O stone-wielder, as the giver of refreshments; we know you as the giver of riches.
Your greatness, O thou of hundredfold aid, O thou of hundredfold resolve, the singers celebrate with their songs.
Truly well-guided is that mortal whom the Maruts, whom Aryaman, whom blameless Mitra protect.
He who bears abundance of cattle, horses, and manly strength, spurred on by the Ādityas, flourishes always with riches longed for by many.
We implore that Indra for his gift — the powerful, the fearless; we implore the lord of riches.
In him are all aids, fearless together; let the coursers bring him hither, the abundant lord, the bay steeds, for joy at the pressed Soma.
That exhilaration of yours, O Indra, which is most excellent, most Vṛtra-slaying, whereby you seized the sun with men, which is hardest to withstand in battles —
He who is invincible, desired by all, worthy of fame, the conqueror in contests — that most powerful one, O lord, come to our pressings; may we reach the cow-rich fold.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even as before, O great and mighty one, be generous to us with cattle, with horses, with chariots.
O hero, I find no limit to your bounty at all; O Maghavan, even now, O stone-wielder, assist our devotions with prizes.
He who is lofty, the companion who makes things heard — he, much-praised, knows all births; all peoples in every age call upon Indra the mighty, with ladles extended.
May he be our protector in contests, the abundant lord, standing before us, the bountiful Vṛtra-slayer.
Sing with a great song, in the joys of soma, the hero of wide perception; Indra by name is famous, the mighty — even as the word.
Give wealth for the body, give goods, give the vigorous one in contests, O much-invoked one — give now, and therewith.
Ruling over all goods, even the form of him who has conquered — of the lamenting one — now beyond that.
Sufficient for your great desire, we praise the bountiful one, fit to come, fit to arrive; with sacrifices and songs of all people you seek to speed the Maruts — I sing you with a hymn of reverence.
Those who cause to fly with their courses along the ridges of the mountains — the sacrifice of the loudly-bellowing ones, the favour of the powerfully-roaring ones, forward at the rite.
Bring the shattering of ill-wills, O most powerful Indra; bring us riches befitting allies, impelling to the mind — the greatest, impelling to the mind.
Gain-winner, great gain-winner, O fierce, brilliant, most discerning, joyful one — the irresistible sovereign, he who conquers the conquerable, Bhujyu, the foremost in contests.
Let him come hither — the impious one who seized the pious man's filled store — even as Vaśa the horseman took it from him of wide fame, from Kānīta, at the breaking of dawn.
Sixty thousand horses, ten thousand as a seat, twenty hundred camels, ten hundred dark mares, ten hundred tawny-striped ones, ten thousand cattle.

title: Rigveda
text:
Ten dark, prosperous, generous-spirited, swift ones — they turned the wheel of the chariot at Mathrā.
The generous Kānīta of wide fame and rich bounty — giving a golden chariot, he became the most bountiful patron and gained the highest glory.
Come to us, O Vāyu, for our great extension, for vigour and strength; for we have done much for you to give — at once, for great giving.
He who with horses carries the dawns three times seven of seventy — with these Soma-pressing Soma drinks, O Soma-drinker, for giving, purified and bright-drinking.
He who delighted even this one by his own nature in brilliant giving — at the axle of Araṭva, for Nahuṣa, the good-actioned one, to the one of better deeds, the right-purposeful.
He who is self-ruling in the embodiment of praise, O Vāyu, bathed in ghee — urged by horses, urged by splendour, urged by the hunt, that which is swiftly advancing — this is now that.
And then the dear gift for the vigorous one — sixty thousand for a seat, of steeds, of the stallions.
Like cattle going to the herd they come to the gelded ones; the gelded ones come to me.
And then in Cārathe's troop he distributed a hundred camels; and also among the white ones twenty hundreds.
From the slave Balbūtha the inspired Tarukṣa received a hundred; these people, O Vāyu, rejoice, guarded by Indra they rejoice, guarded by the gods.
And that great woman who faces forward — the desire for horses, adorned with gold, is led away.
Great, O Varuṇa, O Mitra, is the protection of you great ones for the worshipper; he whom the Ādityas protect from betrayal — may misfortune not reach him. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
O gods, O Ādityas, know the removal of evils; as wings are above a bird, spread shelter over us. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
Spread that shelter over us, as wings over a bird you extend; all protective things, O all-knowing ones, we meditate upon. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.

title: Rigveda
text:
To whom the far-seeing ones have given home and life — these Ādityas rule the riches of all Manu's kin. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
May evils be warded away from us like a charioteer on difficult roads; may we be in the shelter of Indra and under the protection of the Ādityas. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
One who deviously takes away a man's gift given by you — O gods, the Ādityas have powerfully aimed at him. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
No sharp missile hits him, no heavy weapon strikes him — to whom the Ādityas of wide shelter have given protection. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
We rest on you, O gods, as warriors in armour; you protect us from great sin, you from small. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
Let Aditi protect us widely, let Aditi give shelter — the mother of opulent Mitra, of Aryaman, and of Varuṇa. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
Whatever shelter, refuge, good fortune, freedom from disease — whatever triple, protective power — that spread over us. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
O Ādityas, look down like spies from a bank; lead us along a good ford as of a horse, along an easy path. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
May welfare be here not for the fierce beast, not for the worn-out cow, not for the yoke-mate — but welfare for the cow and milch-cow, and for the hero who seeks fame. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
Whatever evil is manifest, whatever is hidden, O gods — all that place far from us upon Trita Āptya. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
Whatever ill-dream is among cattle, whatever among us, O daughter of the sky — carry that far away to Trita, to Āptya, O brilliant Dawn. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.

title: Rigveda
text:
Whether one makes a necklace or a garland, O daughter of the sky — all the ill-dream we hand over to Trita, to Āptya. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
That for the eater, that for the worker, that portion for the one who has approached — O Dawn, carry the ill-dream away to Trita and to Dvita. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
As we bring together a fragment, a hoof, a debt — so do we bring together all the ill-dream to Āptya. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
We have conquered today; we have prevailed; we have become sinless; O Dawn, from whatever ill-dream we feared — may it shine away. Sinless are your aids; good aids are your aids.
The wise one of good thoughts has tasted of the sweet drink's vigour, the drink of wide delight; him, calling honey, all the gods and mortals go about.
You have entered within and have become Aditi, warding off the wrath of the divine; O Indu, enjoying the friendship of Indra, may you prosper in riches as along the front of the chariot.
We have drunk Soma; we have become immortals; we have arrived at the light; we have found the gods. What now can hostility do to us, and what the malice of a mortal, O immortal one?
Be beneficial to us, O Indu, when drunk into the heart, O Soma, gracious to the son as a father; wise, of wide fame, as a friend to a friend — O Soma, extend our life to live.
These drops, when drunk, renowned, and widely protective, have bound the joints together as oxen a chariot; let them protect me from going astray, and let the Soma drops keep away fatigue.
Like Agni rubbed forth, kindle me up; make us see further; make us better; for then, O Soma, in your intoxication I think: go forward like a wealthy man toward abundance.
With eager mind may we partake of your pressed drink like the wealth of a father; O King Soma, extend our lives as the sun the days.

title: Rigveda
text:
O King Soma, be gracious to us in wellbeing; we are your worshippers — know that; your discernment and wrath are roused, O Indu; do not hand us over to the will of the Ārya foe.
For you, O Soma, are the guardian of our body; you have sat in every limb, beholding men; when we have transgressed your ordinances, be gracious to us, O god, O best friend, for the sake of wealth.
May I accompany the friendship of the soft-bellied one, the one drunk, O Hariyaśva, that does not injure me; this Soma that has been set down in me — I go extending life to Indra for it.
Those feeble ailments have departed; the diseases have been driven out; the darkness has shuddered away; Soma has mounted up into us through the heavens; we have come where life is extended.
That Indu which was drunk by the Fathers in their hearts — the immortal entered into mortals; to that Soma let us offer with oblation; may we be in his gracious favour, in his good will.
O Soma, communing with the Fathers, you have stretched yourself out along heaven and earth; to you, O Indu, let us offer with oblation; may we be lords of riches.
O gods who protect, proclaim to us: let not sleep overpower us, nor idle talk; may we, always beloved of Soma, with good heroes, speak in the assembly.
You, O Soma, give vigour from all sides; you who find the sun — enter into us, beholding men; O Indu, united with your aids, guard us from behind and also from in front.
Sing forward Indra of rich bounty as you know him — who as the bountiful one, abundant in wealth, provides for the singers as with a thousand.
Like an army of hundreds he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the worshipper; like streams from a mountain his gifts of the many-nourishing one swell.
The pressed Soma drops, the exhilarations, O Indra, O lover of song — like waters, O vajra-bearer, they fill your own dwelling, your lake, O hero, for your bounty.

title: Rigveda
text:
Drink the sinless, surpassing, eloquent one, the sweetest drink; so that when exhilarated you scatter gifts upon us boldly by your own nature, like a small one.
May our praise approach us, driven like a horse by the pressers; which the milch-cows make palatable for you, O self-ruling one, the gifts of Indra among the Kaṇvas.
We have approached with reverence the mighty hero, of widespread, inexhaustible wealth; O vajra-bearer, the devotions flow pouring like an udder at a well, O Indra.
Whatever is now, whatever is at the sacrifice, whatever on the earth — from there, O mighty one, come with swift steeds, with great thoughts, with powerful ones, to our sacrifice.
Your agile, swift bay steeds that flow forward like winds — with which you go around the offspring of Manu, with which you make all the sun visible.
For this much we implore you, O Indra, of favour rich in cattle — as, O Maghavan, you helped Medhyātithi, as you helped Nīpātithi in gaining wealth.
As you, O Maghavan, helped Kaṇva against Trasadasyu, as you helped Paktha at Daśavraja, as you helped Ṛjiśvan of Gośarya — O Indra, with cattle and gold.
Sing forth the famous, richly-bountiful Śakra for the sake of conquest; who lavishes desired wealth upon the Soma-presser and the praiser as with a thousand.
The missiles of this Indra are hundredfold, hard to withstand; his great impulsions — they swell like a bending mountain among the bountiful ones when the pressed drops have exhilarated him.
When the pressed Soma drops have exhilarated the dear one — O lord, the pressing is set as waters, like milch-cows to the worshipper.
The sinless one, who is called upon for aid — the streams of the sweet drink flow as devotions; O lord, the Soma drops, calling upon you, have set themselves among the praises.
When driving toward us, O Soma, at the good sacrifice, he is not slackened like a racing horse; the welcoming songs make palatable for you, O self-flavouring one, the invocation — you delight in it in the city.

title: Rigveda
text:
Proclaim the mighty hero, the discriminating one, grasping wealth, the abundant one of great bounty; O vajra-bearer, you have ever nourished the worshipper with wealth like an udder at a well.
Whatever is now in the far distance, or on earth, or in the sky — come, O Indra, yoking the bay steeds, with great thoughts, O lofty one, with lofty ones.
Your bay steeds, the charioteers, who do not stumble, who carry the vigour of the wind — with which you surround the Dasyu for Manuṣa with a roar, with which you go around the sun.
For this much, O lord, may we know you anew, O hero — as you helped Etaśa in the contested wealth, as you helped Vaśa at Daśavraja.
As you were present for Kaṇva at the sacrifice, the ceremony, at the long-guided rite, O home-friend; as you, O stone-wielder, shone forth at Gośarya — so be it for me, for the clan of golden glory.
As, O Indra, thou didst drink the pressed soma together with Manu Sāṁvaraṇa, O Maghavan, with Nīpātithi and Medhyātithi — those who bring increase, those who bring hearkening — so too now.
Pārṣadvāṇa caused Praskañva, who had lain down, the withered and emaciated man, to sit upright; the seer, aided by thee, O Indra, like a wolf to the Dasyu, gained thousands of cattle.
He who gains nothing whatsoever by his recitations, he who is stirred to verse — speak toward that Indra with a fresh thought, the one who suffers no harm, for the sake of bounty.
He for whom they have sung the hymn of seven heads, of triple substance, in the highest station — he has roared over all these worlds; thereby his manly vigour was born anew.
We call upon that Indra who is the giver of good things to us; for we know his latest favour — may we reach the cow-filled stall.
He to whom thou, O Vasu, dost extend thy giving, he obtains the fullness of wealth; thee, O Maghavan Indra, O lover of hymns, we who have pressed soma now invoke.

title: Rigveda
text:
You are never barren, O Indra; you do not abandon the worshipper. Step forth, O Maghavan, step forth again — then once more is the gift of the god sought.
He who pressed eagerly forward with might against Kriви, driving Śuṣṇa to his ruin with his blows, who propped up yonder sky while spreading it wide — thereby the earthly hero was born.
He whose is this whole world — the Ārya, the Dāsa, the guardian of treasures, the foe — even through the Ārya, through Ruśama, the wealth that resounds is driven toward thee.
The swift, inspired sages have sung the hymn that drips with honey and ghee; in us the wealth and the bull-like power have spread wide; in us the pressed soma-drops flow.
As, O Śakra, thou didst drink the pressed soma with Manu Vivasvat, as, O Indra, thou hast found pleasure in the metre at Trita's side — exhilarate thyself there.
At Pṛṣadhra's pressing, O Indra, with Mātariśvan, thou wast exhilarated; as with the soma at Daśaśipra's, at Daśoṇya's, at Syūmaraśman's side — thou art the straightener.
He who alone has upheld the recitations, who has boldly drunk the soma, for whom Viṣṇu strode his three strides in accordance with Mitra's ordinances.
Him in whose praises thou, O Indra, dost delight — thee, O prize-winner, O hundred-powered one — thee we invoke like cowherds milking a good milch-cow, we who are eager for renown.
He who is our giver is our father, mighty, fierce, the ruler of rulers; the fierce Maghavan of many treasures, ever moving — may he give to us cattle and horses.
He to whom thou, O Vasu, dost pour out thyself in giving, he sets wealth growing; we who desire goods invoke with praises Indra, the lord of goods, the hundred-powered.
Thou dost never fail: thou guardest both births. O fourth Āditya, thy mighty power has taken its stand at thy invocation, the immortal one in the sky.

title: Rigveda
text:
To whomsoever thou, O Maghavan Indra, O lover of hymns, dost impart thy giving for the worshipper — hear our songs and our excellent praise, O Vasu, as for Kaṇva, hear our call.
The ancient prayer has been praised; speak forth the sacred formula to Indra; the many great ones of Ṛta have sung in response; the wisdom of the praiser has been poured forth.
Indra shook together the great riches, shook together the two worlds, shook together also the sun; the bright, pure soma-draughts mixed with milk have rejoiced Indra together.
Thee, the highest of the bountiful ones and the greatest of the bulls, the most fort-breaking, O Maghavan Indra, the finder of cattle, the lord of wealth — thee we implore.
Who, growing great day by day, subdued Āyu, Kutsa, and Atithigva — thee, of the bay horses and the hundred powers, we invoke as we seek the prize.
Let the pressing-stones pour for us the essence of all the sweets — those soma-drops that have been pressed among distant peoples and those that have been pressed among the near ones.
Smite all enmities and drive them away; let all bring good things; even among the highest, thy inebriating soma-stalks rejoice thee, wherever thou art satiated with the soma.
Come here yet nearer, O Indra, with helps measured by wisdom; with the most beneficent conquests, with the most good, come with good sleeps, with good sleep-bringers.
Make the swift-racer, lord of the good, he who is seen by all peoples, share of offspring; speed them forward with thy powers who are thy reciters and who purify understanding in succession.
May we be of those most favourably disposed toward thee, for help in thy battles; we, having won, exult with the priestly calls and with invocations of the gods.
For I, O lord of the bay steeds, go with thy prayer eager for the prize, to the contest with ever-present helps; thee, even thee I urge, the eager seeker of horses, seeker of cattle, at the fore of the contests.

title: Rigveda
text:
This heroic power of thine the Kārus celebrate with songs; they who offer invocations have gone to the ghee-dripping strength; the singers of the family of Pūru have gained it with their devotions.
Those who by good work sought Indra for aid, at whose pressings thou dost exhilarate thyself — as thou wast exhilarated at Saṁvarta's, as at Kṛśa's — even so, O Indra, rejoice in us.
Come all of you, O gods, equally pleased, come near to us; let the Vasus and Rudras come to us for help; let the Maruts hear our call.
May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, the seven rivers strengthen my call; may the Waters, Vāta, the mountains, the forest lord, and Earth hear the invocation.
Whatever bounty is thine, O Indra, the very best of gifts, O most bountiful one — with that be aware of us, O thou who dost enjoy thy feast, for our increase, as our share, for giving, O Vṛtra-slayer.
O lord of the contest, lord of heroes, thou indeed wilt carry the prize to us, O wise one; having won through the priestly calls and through the divine repasts, they will be heard.
For there are the noble blessings of the people's life, O Indra; seek us out, O Maghavan, for our help close at hand; milk out the swelling refreshment.
May we honour thee, O Indra, with our praises; be thou ours, O hundred-powered one; pour out for Praskañva the great, abundant, dispersed, and shameless bounty.
I have beheld the many heroic deeds of Indra as he comes forward; thy bounty, O wolf to the Dasyu, is great.
A hundred white bulls shine in the sky like stars; they have propped up the sky with their greatness.
A hundred bamboo tubes, a hundred dogs, a hundred worn skins; for me a hundred bundles of balvaja-grass and four hundred reddish cows.
You are of the good gods' company, O descendants of Kāṇva, wandering each according to your nature; you move about like horses.

title: Rigveda
text:
And they have made resound the great fame of Sāptasa, the complete one; the dark-hued mare, outpacing the roads, could not be reached even by the eye.
For thee, O wolf to the Dasyu, the shameless bounty has been seen spread out; the power is broad as the sky.
Ten thousands of (cattle) have been given to me by Pautakrata, the wolf to the Dasyu.
A hundred asses for me, a hundred woollen (ewes), a hundred female slaves — beyond reckoning.
Moreover, distinguishable ones were led forward for Pūtakratā — like a troop of horses indeed.
Agni, the conveyor of oblations, the discerning one, became known; he of the good chariot — Agni blazed mightily with his bright flame; the sun shone in the sky, the sun shone bright.
You two gods, yoked by the ancient will to your mighty chariot, O adorable Nāsatyas, come hither with your powers; drink this, the third pressing.
The gods, the true ones, the three and thirty, have been seen before the truth of you two; enjoying our sacrifice and pressing, O Aśvins of blazing fire, drink the soma.
Praiseworthy is that work of yours, O Aśvins; the bull of sky and earth's expanse — a thousand praises and those in the contest for cattle — come to all of these to drink.
This is your appointed share, O adorable ones; come hither to these songs, O Nāsatyas; drink the sweet honey-soma among us; protect the offerer with your powers.
Him whom the priests, making manifold preparations, bearing this sacrifice in concert, for whom the instructed Brahmin was engaged — what indeed was the understanding of the sacrificer therein?
One indeed is Agni, kindled in many places; one is the Sun, who pervades all the world; one is Dawn that illumines all this — that one has verily become all this universe.
The luminous, the radiant, the three-wheeled, comfortable chariot, easy to sit in, much sought — she of brilliant gifts, she who was born at the yoking of it — that chariot I call for you two, beyond measure, to drink.

title: Rigveda
text:
These your apportioned shares flow forth for you two, O Indra and Varuṇa, at your great soma-pressings; at sacrifice after sacrifice, at the pressings, you are active; when you aid the sacrificer who presses soma.
The herbs that block and the waters have been laid ready; O Indra and Varuṇa, they have reached greatness; those two who flow at the end of the expanse of the path — of these two, no enemy, no ungodly one, escapes.
True is this, O Indra and Varuṇa: for the diminished Kṛśa the seven voices milk out a wave of your sweetness; with those, O lords of splendour, protect the worshipper who, undeceived, guards you with his thoughts.
The ghee-sprinkling, soma-born, swift-giving, seven sisters that are the seat of Ṛta — those that drip ghee for you two, O Indra and Varuṇa — with those bestow and give instruction to the sacrificer.
We have spoken the true great power of the mighty sense to the two brilliant ones for great good fortune; protect us well, O Indra and Varuṇa, you who are ghee-dripping, with three times seven, O lords of splendour.
O Indra and Varuṇa, what inspired wisdom, speech, thought, and sacred knowledge you gave to the seers at the beginning — those stations which the wise ones created, spreading the sacrifice with fervent devotion — those I have perceived.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow on the sacrificers an unhaughty benevolence and the flourishing of wealth; bestow offspring, nourishment, and prosperity on us; extend our lifespan for longevity.
Come, O Agni, with the fires; we choose thee as the Hotṛ-priest; let the well-extended oblation-bearing ladle anoint thee, the most adorable, to sit upon the barhis-grass.
For toward thee, O son of strength, O Aṅgiras, the ladles move in the sacrifice; we implore Agni the grandson of strength, of ghee-bright hair, the ancient one at sacrifices.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, thou art the sage, the ordainer, the Hotṛ, the purifier, worthy of worship; the joyful one, the most adorable at the ceremonies, worthy of praise by the inspired with bright hymns.
Bring hither the blameless gods, O youngest one, continually for the feast, to the longing ones; go to the well-placed offerings, O Vasu; be thou gladdened, stirred by the devotions.
Thou indeed art far-famed, O Agni, protector of Ṛta, the seer; thee, O kindled and blazing one, the inspired ordaining priests come to revere.
Blaze, O most blazing one; shine; grant comfort to the clan, O thou who art great for the praiser; may my patrons be in the shelter of the gods, conquerors of enemies, of good fire.
As, O Agni, thou dost consume on the ground the aged stubble grown thick, so burn, O thou of mighty alliance, whoever plots against us, whoever of evil mind desires to harm.
Do not deliver us to the mortal enemy, to the rakṣas-afflicted, to the evil-speaking one; protect us, O youngest one, with unfailing, crossing, auspicious guardians.
Protect us, O Agni, with one protection; protect us also with a second; protect us with three songs, O lord of vigour; protect us with four, O Vasu.
Protect us from every rākṣasa, from the ungenerous; ever help us in the contests; for thee, the nearest, we seek as our ally and kinsman for increase, through the divine companionship.
Bring to us, O Agni, the wealth that enhances vigour, O purifier, worthy of praise; O incomparable, grant us too the much-desired gift, the one of good guidance that is its own glory.
With which we may overcome the proud ones in battles, crossing the enemy's attacks — with that, O thou of mighty power, increase us with refreshment; incite the thoughts that find good things.
Sharpening himself like a bull, Agni waves his horns; his sharp jaws are not to be resisted; the offspring of strength, of good teeth, leaps up.

title: Rigveda
text:
There is no resisting thy jaws, O Agni, O bull, when thou spreadest wide; thou as our Hotṛ make our oblation well-offered; win for us many desirable things.
Thou dost lie in the forests, the child of two mothers; mortals kindle thee together; unwearied, thou dost carry the oblations, the oblation-maker, and then thou reignest among the gods.
The seven Hotṛ-priests praise thee, O Agni, thou who art easily released and shameless; thou dost split the rock with thy heat, with thy blazing; go forward, O Agni, beyond the peoples.
