We invoke for you Agni upon Agni, the irresistible, we who have strewn the barhis; Agni with offerings placed, at all times, the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples.
He follows your shelter with understanding, O Agni, discerningly, with good praises; with impelling zeal bring to us the prize of many forms, the nearest, for our aid.
O Agni, O praiser, thou art the lord of the settlement, the scorcher of the rākṣasas, O god; not having stayed away, thou art the great lord of the house, the guardian of the sky, who remains in the dwelling.
Let no rākṣasa enter us, O glowing Vasu; let not the sorcerers with their magic afflict us; drive far away the want beyond the extent of the pasture, drive away hunger, O Agni; repel those afflicted by rākṣasas.
May Indra hear this our twofold speech, turning hither; may the bountiful one, most mighty, come with intent toward soma-drinking, united in purpose.
Him, the self-resplendent, the bull, the two divine Wisdom-goddesses have fashioned for strength. Thou sittest foremost in the place of laudation; for thy mind is eager for soma.
Drink deep, O Indra of many gifts, of the pressed soma juice. For we know thee, O lord of bay steeds, as the ever-conquering in battles, the unassailable one who yet dares boldly.
Do not disappoint us, O bountiful one; so let it be, O Indra, according to thy will and wisdom. May we, hastening, win the prize through thy help, O thou of the full cheeks, O wielder of the bolt.

title: Rigveda
text:
Be able, O lord of power, O Indra, with all thy aids. For like Bhaga we follow after thee, the glorious, the finder of wealth, O hero.
Thou art the abundant source of horses, the great maker of cattle, a golden fountain, O god. None can diminish the gift that is in thee; whatever I ask for, bring that to me.
Come thou indeed hither to the swift steed, find the treasure for acquiring wealth. Bestow in abundance, O bountiful one, for the winning of cattle, O Indra, for the winning of horses.
Thou dost bestow for gift many thousands and hundreds of herds. We have celebrated the fort-breaker with inspired words, singing to Indra for his help.
Whether the unlearned or the learned man, O Indra, has tended thy word — he has rejoiced exceedingly through devotion to thee, O thou of a hundred powers, with the thought turned eastward, without harm.
If the fort-destroyer of mighty arms, the anointer of all, should hear my call — we who desire wealth invoke Indra the lord of wealth, the hundred-powered, with hymns of praise.
We hold no evil thoughts, nor are we niggardly, nor torpid; since we would make Indra the bull our companion at the pressing of the soma.
We have yoked the mighty, ever-conquering in battles, the debt-exacting, the indestructible. He knows even a wandering thing; the most skilled charioteer, the vigorous one whom he indeed reaches.
From that which we fear, O Indra, make us free from fear. Be able, O bountiful one; through thine own aids slay those who hate us, destroy our foes.
For thou, O lord of bounty, art the lord of mighty bounty for him who worships. We who have pressed soma invoke thee, that Indra the bountiful, beloved of hymns.
Indra, the spear-thrower, and the slayer of Vṛtra, the guardian from afar, is our most choiceworthy one. May he protect our last, may he protect our middle, may he guard us behind and before.

title: Rigveda
text:
Guard us, O Indra, from behind, from below, from above, and from before, everywhere. Put far from us the divine terror, put far from us the hostile missiles of the ungodly.
Today and today, tomorrow and tomorrow, O Indra, save us, and in the time beyond. Thou wilt protect all our singers, O lord of truth, through all the days, by day and by night.
The heroic breaker-of-foes, the bountiful, the greatly gifted, the battle-joiner for valour — thy two arms, O bull, O thou of a hundred powers, whereon the bolt is fixed, pour down strength.
Offer forward to him the praise-song which he desires. With hymns the soma-pressers increase Indra's mighty strength. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Unmatched and without equal, he alone among men is unwearying. He has grown exceedingly beyond all former things, surpassing all beings with his might. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Even with a hostile steed the swift-giving one succeeds. That heroic deed of thine, O Indra, is to be proclaimed as thou performest it. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Come, let us make for thee, O Indra, the prayer-offerings that increase thee, by which, O most mighty, thou art gladdened — here the glorious one wins glory. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Even of the bold thou makest the mind bold, O Indra, when thou art such. When served with the potent soma-juices and honored with reverences by those who adorn themselves with obeisance. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Ṛcīṣama looks down like a man looking on his flock. Pleased with the skill of the soma-presser, he makes a yoke-fellow his companion. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
All the gods, O Indra, gave thee heroic strength in accord with thy will. Thou hast become the lord and guardian of all, O thou much-praised. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
I laud that supreme power of thine, O Indra, for the obtaining of divine grace — when thou smitest Vṛtra with might, O lord of power. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Like one desiring a companion, making the human generations equal — Indra knows that consciousness, and then he is glorified. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Upward has thy power arisen, O Indra; upward thyself, upward thy will. Many praisers have increased greatly in thy protection, O bountiful one. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Let you and I be yoked together, O Vṛtra-slayer, for the gaining of prizes. Even like an adversary, O wielder of the bolt, he will think of us two, O hero. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Truly and not falsely do we praise that Indra. Great is his slaying-power against one who presses not soma; abundant are the lights for him who presses soma. Auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
He, the foremost of great ones, the shining one, has shone forth with his acts of will, through whose doors Manu the father has shone among the gods with wisdom.
The stones, whose backs are soma, have not sat upon the measure of heaven; the recitations and the prayers are to be proclaimed.
He, knowing, Indra drove away the cows for the Aṅgirases. I praise that heroic deed of his.
He, Indra, who in the ancient manner increases the seers, is the sustainer of speech. May he come favorably to our laud at the oblation here to help us.
And then, according to thy will, svāhā! — the worshippers of the chosen one, the chanters have sung the dog-sacrifice hymn, O Indra, for the giving of the cow-herd.
In Indra are all heroic deeds, those done and those yet to be done, he whom the singers know as the sacrifice.
When the peoples of the five tribes sent out shouts to Indra, he spread out with greatness the inspired utterances of the noble one's thought — that is his dwelling.

title: Rigveda
text:
And this praise-song of thine has been fashioned for those heroic deeds; thou didst drive forward the turning of the wheel.
In the scattering of this bull's generosity, he strode widely for life; like barley for cattle he takes it up.
Holding that, desiring help, with you as fathers of skill, may we be for the increase of the one accompanied by the Maruts.
Yes! We praise thee, O hero, with hymn-singing for the seasonable abode. May we conquer, O Indra, with thee as ally.
The Rudras, the great ones, the mountain-gods, united in harmony in the slaying of Vṛtra at the invocation of Bhara — upon him who praises and lauds, Pajra has been set; may the gods with Indra as chief protect us.
May the hymns exhilarate thee; bestow bounty, O wielder of the bolt. Strike down those who hate the sacred word.
With thy foot press down the Paṇis, the ungenerous ones. Thou art great; none whatsoever can stand against thee.
Thou, O Indra, art lord of those who press soma; thou art lord of those who press not. Thou art king of peoples.
Come, advance — thy dwelling is in heaven, resounding gloriously among the peoples. Thou fillest both the worlds.
Even that great cloud-mass, the mountain with its hundreds and thousands, thou hast shattered apart for the singers.
We indeed call upon thee when soma is pressed by day; we call upon thee by night. Fill our desire.
Where is that young bull with thick neck, unbowed? What priest worships him?
Whose pressing does the bull descend upon, well pleased? Who then truly approaches Indra?
Whose have thy gifts reached, O Vṛtra-slayer? Whose the heroic deeds? Who is closest in the hymn?
This soma of thine is pressed among humankind, among the Pūrus. Come to it, hasten forward, drink.
This soma is dear to thee at Śaryaṇāvat, on the banks of Suṣomā; at Ārjīkīyā it is the most intoxicating.

title: Rigveda
text:
That soma, lovely for great bounty, for intoxication, for exhilaration — come, O Indra, hasten and drink.
Whenever thou art called by men, O Indra, eastward, westward, northward, or southward — come quickly with thy swift steeds.
Or if thou art rejoicing at the outpouring of heaven, at the sun's gathering, or in the ocean of the soma-plant —
— thee, the great and wide, I call with hymns, like a cow for enjoying, O Indra, to drink the soma.
Let thy bay steeds, O Indra, O god, bearing thy greatness, carry thee in the chariot — they who bear thy might.
O Indra, I sing thee, I praise thee, the great one, the fierce, the maker of lordship. Come, drink our pressed soma.
We who have pressed soma, we who are devout, invoke thee. This is our sacred grass for thee to sit upon.
For although thou art common to all people forever, O Indra — thee, even thee, we invoke.
The men with the pressing stones have milked this sweet soma for thee. Pleased with it, O Indra, drink it.
Surveying all the wise nobles, come quickly to us. Bestow upon us great fame.
The giver to me of dappled mares, the king of golden women — may the bountiful one not be harmed, O gods.
Among the thousand dappled mares, on top — the brilliant, great and broad, pure golden gift, I take it.
The descendants of the hard-to-grasp, of the thousand-fold of good bounty — they made renown among the gods for me.
With songs I invoke for your aid Indra, the finder of wealth, amidst the pressing-stones, singing loudly at the sacrifice where soma has been pressed — I call him like a porter bearing a load.
Whom the unruly do not hold back, whom the firm-set men do not check in the joy of the well-cheeked one over the soma — who is a giver to the praising presser of the laudable oblation.
Who is capable, the anointer, the horse-like, or the golden young plant — he, Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, makes tremble the releasing of the enclosure of cattle.

title: Rigveda
text:
Even what is buried, much gathered together, he scatters as wealth for the worshipper. The bolt-wielder of fine cheeks, the bay-horsed — even that Indra does by his will as he wishes.
That which thou hast desired, O much-praised, even of old among men, O hero — that, O Indra, we bring together for thee: sacrifice, hymn, and swift speech.
Together in the soma-drinkings, O much-invoked, O bolt-wielder, for exhilaration, O heavenly-dwelling soma-drinker.
We fattened this bolt-wielder here just yesterday. For him then today bring the soma with equal measure; adorn him now, O glorified one.
Even a wolf, the ram's wool-puller, adorns himself at the gatherings. Being pleased with this our hymn of praise, come, O Indra, with shining intelligence.
What unfinished heroic deed of Indra's is there now? By what effort has the Vṛtra-slayer not been heard, from birth?
And what are the great unassailed powers of his? What has the Vṛtra-slayer left unspread? Indra conquers all the beka-nāṭas visible by day, and the Paṇis by wisdom.
For thee, O Indra, O Vṛtra-slayer, we most numerous ones bear the prayers, the unprecedented ones, O much-invoked, O bolt-wielder, like wages we bring them forward.
Many indeed are the desires of those calling upon thee with Indra's help, O great worker. Even across the pressings of the noble — come, O most wealthy one, O most mighty, hear my call.
We are truly among the inspired ones with thee, O Indra. For there is no other compassionate one than thee, O much-invoked, O bountiful one, none whatsoever.
Rescue us from this lack of wisdom, from hunger, from slander. With thine aid, with thy shining wisdom, sustain us, O most able one, knower of the way.
Let the soma be pressed for you, O Kalayas — do not fear. This one disperses away of himself; indeed he will go away of himself.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those sovereign Ādityas we shall beseech to come down here, the graciously kind ones, for our succor.
May Mitra bring us across difficulty, may Varuṇa and Aryaman — as the Ādityas know how.
For theirs is the wondrous, hymn-worthy protection for the worshipper, for him who has made himself ready before the Ādityas.
Great is your help, O great ones, O Varuṇa, O Mitra, O Aryaman — we choose your aids.
Keep us alive, O Ādityas, before the blow. Why are you named hearers-of-the-call?
Whatever protection is yours for the weary presser of soma, whatever shelter — with that speak over us.
There is, O gods, broad escape from distress; there is treasure for the sinless. O Ādityas, there is wonderful freedom from sin.
May this snare not fasten on us; may the great one loosen it around us. For Indra is the renowned, the powerful.
May the injury of enemies, of the wicked, not reach us, O you who are not eager for destruction. O gods, wipe us clean.
And thee too, O Aditi, I the great one approach calling upon thee, O goddess, for thy gracious mercy, for our succor.
Carry us across in poverty, O deep one, O mother of the fierce sons — from the one who would slay us. Let no harm come to our offspring.
O sinless, wide-ranging, wide-glowing one, for spreading out — make our offspring live.
They who are the heads of peoples, the undeceivable, self-glorious ones — they guard the sacred ordinances, being without treachery.
O Ādityas, free us from the mouth of wolves, as a bound thief, O Aditi.
Drive away from us this arrow, O Ādityas, drive away the evil thought. Let it go from us having slain no one.
For ever through your aids, O Ādityas, good givers, have we indeed enjoyed you before and now.
For the wise gods, even him who turns back in sin — the perpetual one — ye make to live.
This good fresh releasing, O Ādityas, which frees — O Aditi, as one bound from bondage.

title: Rigveda
text:
There is no crossing beyond that, O Ādityas, to leap across. Be gracious to us.
May the artificial dart of Vivasvat not strike us, O Ādityas, before old age.
Drive away hatred, drive away difficulty, O Ādityas, drive away what is tightly bound. Drive away in all directions the injury.
We turn thy chariot for thy aid, for favor; O greatly-active, O crusher of enemies, O Indra most mighty, O lord of the good.
O greatly vigorous, O greatly willing, O powerful one, in all thoughts thou hast spread wide with thy greatness.
By whose greatness the two great ones travel around the earth; whose hands bear the golden bolt.
The lord of all men, the lord of unbowed power, with these — I invoke with the aid of chariots, for the peoples.
For succor, the ever-growing one, him who rains heaven — men call upon him in many ways for his aid.
Ṛcīṣama is beyond measure — Indra the fierce, the greatly bountiful, the ruling one even of wealth.
Him, even him, I urge Indra for great bounty, for drinking — he who rules over the ancient praise-song, the dancer of peoples.
No mortal has obtained thy friendship, O most mighty. None has attained thy powers.
Aided by thee, with thee as ally, may we win great wealth in the waters, in the sun. May we conquer in battles, O wielder of the bolt.
That thee we approach with sacrifices; that thee with hymns, O most beloved of praises, O Indra — even as thou didst protect the man of many wiles in the contests.
Whose friendship is sweet, whose leading is sweet, O wielder of the bolt — whose sacrifice is to be stretched wide.
Make wide room for our body, wide room for our dwelling. Grant us wide room for living.
A wide path for men, wide for cattle, wide for the chariot — we think of the divine journey.
Beside me six pairs of men stand in the joy of soma — they are sweet-gifted ones.

title: Rigveda
text:
Two bright steeds Indra took and gave to the son of Ṛkṣa: the two bay horses of the horse-sacrifice.
Of good chariot for Atithigva, of good reins from Ṛkṣa — at the horse-sacrifice, of beautiful ornament.
Six horses for Atithigva, accompanied by Indra, with a bride, together with pure action, as a prize.
Among those bay horses he discerned the reddish one among the brilliant ones — one with good reins and a whip.
Among you, O prize-companions, no mortal who would seek to reproach can bear reproach.
He glorifies you — the refreshment of the triṣṭubh meter, for the soma-drop that gladdens heroes — with wisdom, with clever intelligence, for the winning of sacrificial food.
The bull of the swelling waters, the bull of the ever-moving ones — I aim at the lord of your unslayable cows.
Those dappled cows that pour out the sweet extract cook the soma for him at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
Sing forward to the cow-lord of the mountain, to Indra, as he knows it — the son of Truth, the lord of the true.
The bay steeds have been let loose; the reddish ones are on the sacred grass, where we call out to them together.
The cows milked the mixed drink of honey for Indra the bolt-wielder, when he found them in the hidden place.
When we two go up to the topmost abode of the sun, the house, and Indra — having drunk of the honey, may we two be together in the thrice-seven steps of the friend.
Sing, sing forward, O Priyamedhas, sing. Let the young sons also sing. Sing boldly as if to a citadel.
The lute sounds down, the lute of the go-dhā skin resounds all around, the tawny one leaps all around — the sacred word raised up for Indra.
When the desirable ones, the good milkers, fly hither without a kick — grasp the kicking soma for Indra to drink.
Indra drank, Agni drank, all the gods rejoiced. Varuṇa alone dwells here; the waters have hymned him as calves around a cow lowing together.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou art a good god, O Varuṇa, whose seven rivers flow along thy palate like through a hollow pipe.
He who drove the fleet ones, the well-yoked ones, toward the worshipper — the swift one is the leader; that indeed is the form of the supreme one who was released.
Indeed the mighty Indra has overpowered, has overcome all enemies. He split the young man's gruel as it was cooking, beyond the song.
Like a small boy, a young child, mounting a new chariot — he cooked the mighty wild buffalo for his father and mother, the one of wide-reaching power.
Come, O fine-cheeked lord of the household, mount the golden chariot. Then may we two be together with the heavenly, thousand-footed, reddish one that treads well and is without fault.
The reverential ones sit near him, the self-resplendent one. Even the purpose of his well-placed offering, which the comers turn back for giving.
Following the ancient dwelling of these Priyamedhas, the grass-strew preparers of well-laid offerings have partaken of the earlier guidance.
Him who is king of peoples, traveler with chariots, unchecked — the conqueror of all battles, the greatest, who is the Vṛtra-slayer — him I praise.
Adorn that Indra for aid, O thou of many slayings — in whose supporting pair of hands the bolt has been placed, the visible one, great as the sun in the sky.
None can reach by action the one who made the ever-growing — Indra, praised everywhere through sacrifices, the skillful, the indomitable, the boldly powerful.
The unconquerable, fierce, ever-conquering in battles — in whose birth the great, wide-coursing ones, the cows bellowed together; heaven and earth bellowed.
If there were a hundred heavens, O Indra, and a hundred earths — a thousand suns would not match thee, O bolt-wielder; the two worlds did not encompass the newborn one.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thou hast spread wide with the bullish greatness of virility, O bull, O most mighty, with all strength. Protect us, O bountiful one, in the cow-possessing enclosure, O wielder of the bolt, with wonderful aids.
No godless mortal of long life has obtained his refreshment. Even the swift one — he who has yoked the swift bay pair, Indra has yoked them.
That great, greatly invocable Indra, the ever-present for giving — who is invocable in the shallows, who in the forests, who is invocable in the contests.
Rouse us up indeed, O wealthy one, for the great bounty; touch us, O hero. Rouse us indeed, O bountiful one, for great generosity. Rouse us, O Indra, for great fame.
Thou, O Indra, dost satisfy us who seek truth, who speak thy praise. Dwell in our midst, O greatly heroic one; with thy blows cut down the Dāsa in the wide space.
The one of alien rites, the inhuman, the non-sacrificing, the ungodly — the mountain, the friend of the good, has shaken him down; the mountain has shaken the Dasyu down for easy slaying.
Do thou, O Indra, most mighty, grasp their hand for giving — like grains gathered up, do thou who art eager for us gather them together twice for us.
Friends, seek the wisdom — how shall we attain the purpose of Śara? The praise-song is for Bhoja the patron, the seer who is without shame.
Thou wilt be praised together with many seers spreading the sacred grass, since in this way Śara gave the calves one by one.
The bountiful Śauradeya, taking by the ear, brought the calf to us from the three — and the she-goat for the seer to sustain.
You, O Agni, guard us with your great powers from every hostile niggardness, and from the hatred of a mortal foe.
For no human wrath has power over you, O you who are dear by birth; you alone are the lord of the night.
So, O son of strength, O bright-flaming one, together with all the gods grant us wealth that is desirable in every way.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Agni, no niggards, no lack of riches, shall ever injure that mortal whom you protect — the one who has offered worship.
He whom you, O inspired Agni, impel toward wealth in the contest of sacrifice — he, under your protection, shall go among the cattle.
You, O Agni, bestow upon the mortal worshipper wealth rich in heroes; lead us forward toward better fortune.
Protect us! Do not deliver us, O Jātavedas, to the malicious one, to the mortal who is hard to satisfy.
O Agni, let no ungodly man cut off the bounty of the divine one; you are the ruler of riches.
Fill us with wealth, O son of strength, O great one, O friend and lord of riches, for those who sing your praise.
Let our hymns go forth to him of the flame-bright radiance, to the glorious one; let our sacrifices with obeisance go to the much-wealthy, much-praised one for our aid.
Agni, the son of strength, Jātavedas, giver of desirable gifts — he who has become immortal in twofold form among mortals, the gladdest Hotṛ in the settlement.
Agni for you at the divine worship; Agni at the advancing sacrifice; Agni first in sacred thoughts; Agni for the swift one; Agni for the accomplishment of the fields.
May Agni, who is lord of desirable things, grant us refreshments in his friendship; we ever beseech Agni for offspring and descendants — he who is the treasure-keeper of our persons.
Laud Agni of the flame-bright radiance with songs for our aid; men laud Agni for wealth — him who is much implored and far-famed; Agni for a splendid shelter.
We praise Agni to ward off from us hatred; we praise Agni to bestow on us weal and health; may he be invocable as a protector in all the settlements, the dwelling-place of the seers.
Prepare the oblation; the Adhvaryu shall come; he who knows shall seek again the rule of this rite.
The Hotṛ priest sits down upon the Manu's altar beside the keen soma-stalk, delighting in its companionship.

title: Rigveda
text:
They seek him, Rudra, in the community by thought transcending; they seize the grain with the tongue.
The bird-bearer mounted the forest whose sister bow has burned across; he struck the stone with his tongue.
The calf wandering and shining here finds no one to bind him; he seeks the mother of those who praise.
And truly of his the great, horse-rich, vast yoking — the bond of the chariot has been seen.
Seven milk one; two release five; at the ford of the river, in its sound.
Indra shook the vessel with the ten descendants of Vivasvat by the threefold whip of heaven.
Around the triple-seasoned sacrifice the ever-newer flame moves; the Hotṛ priests anoint with the sweet drink.
They pour oblation on him who accepts reverence, on the high-wheeled one moving all around, whose downward-hanging branches are inexhaustible.
The stones have poured out the honey into the lotus bowl, right at the overflow of the well.
The cows have come down toward the great well of the sacrifice that raps sweetly; both its ears are of gold.
Pour upon the pressed soma the splendour, the glory of both worlds; may the flavor receive the bull.
They recognized their own home, like calves with their mothers; they touched one another with their kindred.
Feeding at the jaws they make a foundation in the sky; homage to Indra and Agni — the heavenly light!
The stranger has milked the swelling refreshment, the vigor that goes in seven steps, with the seven rays of the sun.
The sun, urged on by Mitra and Varuṇa, has taken up the soma; that is the remedy for the sick.
And truly the track of the beloved one, his treasure-place — he spread it out around the sky with his tongue.
Rise up, O Aśvins, for the truthful one; harness your chariot, O Aśvins; may your help be nearby.
Come, O Aśvins, with a chariot swifter than the twinkling of an eye; may your help be nearby.

title: Rigveda
text:
Strew for Atri the hot vessel with cold, O Aśvins; may your help be nearby.
Where are you? Where have you gone? Where have you flown like hawks? May your help be nearby.
If today or at any time you would hear this call, may your help be nearby.
O Aśvins, most invoked at sacrificial journeys, I seek the nearest kinship with you; may your help be nearby.
You two, O Aśvins, make the house favorable for Atri; may your help be nearby.
You two have warmed Agni with heat; speak beautifully to Atri; may your help be nearby.
Saptavadhri with hope stretched out along the stream of Agni; may your help be nearby.
Come hither, you two possessors of wealth and bulls; hear this call of mine; may your help be nearby.
Why is this recited to you as if an ancient thing, as if by an aged man? May your help be nearby.
You two, O Aśvins, share the same kinship; your bond is equal; may your help be nearby.
Your chariot, O Aśvins, traverses the realms between the two worlds; may your help be nearby.
Come to us with thousands of cattle and horses; may your help be nearby.
Do not pass over us with thousands of cattle and horses; may your help be nearby.
Rosy-hued Dawn has appeared; the guardian of sacred order has made the light; may your help be nearby.
O Aśvins, may it shine clearly upon you like an axe upon a tree; may your help be nearby.
Like a fort, O bold one, burst it open — oppressed by the dark tribe; may your help be nearby.
Desiring victory, with hymns of might, I laud for you Agni as the guest of every people, the much-beloved, the one at your homestead.
Him whom the oblation-bearing peoples praise with eulogies, like a friend poured with ghee, like a pressing of the sacred drink.
Jātavedas the most praiseworthy, who with uplifted hand for the gods sent the oblations upward to the sky.

title: Rigveda
text:
We have come to the most Vṛtra-slaying, the eldest Agni of the Ānavas, in whose army Śrutarvā, the great Ārkṣa, prospers.
Jātavedas the immortal, visible through the darkness, worthy of invocation when ghee is poured — him we laud.
Whom these striving peoples worship with oblations, pouring libations with outstretched ladles — that Agni.
This newest thought for you, O Agni, has been placed from us; O joyful one, nobly born, of good will, O wise and wondrous guest.
May that prayer be for you, O Agni, most blissful, most pleasing, most dear; grow great by it, O well-praised one.
That prayer, resplendent with glories, would lay glory upon glory in the slaying of Vṛtra.
A horse, a cow, one who fills the chariot, the fierce one like Indra the lord of heroes — whose glorious deeds you excel, and the peoples count wondrous and wondrous.
He whom Gopavana called most pleasing with his song, O Agni, O Aṅgiras — that purifier, hear his call.
He whom the striving peoples worship for the winning of the prize — be alert for the slaying of Vṛtra.
I, invoking Śrutarvā the Ārkṣa who sends down the frenzy, touch the heads of the four who cut their hair like the troops of the shearers.
May the four swift fleet ones, the runners of the most mighty one with good chariot, carry me toward refreshment as a bird toward Tugriya.
Truly I have pointed you out by the great river Paruṣṇī; no mortal is mightier as a giver of horses than the most mighty one.
Yoke now the most god-summoning horses, O Agni, like a charioteer; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ on the seat.
And, O god more knowing, speak to us of the gods; make all desirable things real for us.
Truly when you, O youngest one, son of strength, were invoked, you became the guardian of sacred order, worthy of sacrifice.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold, hundredfold prize; the wise head of riches.

title: Rigveda
text:
Reverence him as the Ṛbhus revere the wheel-rim with joint invocations; O Aṅgiras, bring the sacrifice nearer.
To him now, the heaven-aiming one, with your speech of Virūpa as your constant means, urge forward an excellent praise for the bull.
With whose help, with the army of this Agni of far-seeing vision, shall we overcome the Paṇi in the cattle-raid?
May the clans of the gods not abandon us like cattle bathed in the rain abandon a lean man.
May the encircling hatred, the difficult hostile power of the whole, not smite us like a wave smites a boat.
The peoples, O god, chant homage to you for your might, O Agni; with your weapons crush the enemy.
May you not fail to press together for us wealth for the cow-quest, O Agni; you who make wide space, make wide space for us.
Do not turn away from us in this great prize-contest like one who bears a burden; win the prize all together, win the wealth.
May this evil portent follow another person away from us in fear, O Agni; increase our might, our powerful strength.
He whose Śamī tree the reverential ones, or that of the one of no evil sacrifice, has favored — Agni indeed increases him.
From over the farther boundary, cross over toward the nearer ones; protect those among whom I am.
For we have known you of old, O Agni, as the protection of a father; so now we crave your favor.
I now invoke this wily Indra who rules by might — him attended by the Maruts, whom one does not withhold.
This Indra, companion of the Maruts, split asunder the head of Vṛtra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
Indra, waxing great as companion of the Maruts, shook Vṛtra apart, releasing the waters toward the sea.
This is he by whom this sun was won, accompanied by the Maruts — by Indra — for drinking of the soma.
We invoke with songs Indra attended by the Maruts, the soma-possessing one, the mighty one, the widely extending one.

title: Rigveda
text:
With ancient prayer we invoke Indra accompanied by the Maruts for the drinking of this soma.
O Indra with your Maruts, O showerer of blessings, drink the soma, O hundredfold of will; you are much praised at this sacrifice.
For you, O Indra with the Maruts, the soma draughts are pressed, O stone-wielder; the singers of hymns call with heart's devotion.
Drink, O Indra, companion of the Maruts, the pressed soma at the divine impulses, sharpening the thunderbolt with might.
Rising up with might, having drunk, O Indra, your two jaws quivered from the soma pressed in the bowls.
Both worlds lamented after you as you strode forward, O Indra, when you became the slayer of the Dasyus.
I have measured out the body of the speech of eight feet and nine-syllabled, touching sacred order, from Indra.
Being born, the hundredfold-willed one at once asked his mother: Who are the fierce ones? Who have been heard of?
Then the power said to him: Aurṇavābha, the fearful one among serpents — let these be crushed, O son.
The Vṛtra-slayer cut all those asunder in the cavity like wheel-spokes with the wedge; waxing mighty, he became the Dasyu-slayer.
With a single countermeasure Indra drank simultaneously thirty lakes, to his very fill of the soma.
Indra crushed the Gandharva in the bottomless spaces and dusts, indeed for the benefit of the Brahmin seers.
Indra shot out from the mountains, held up the cooked rice-offering — the self-stretched bundle.
The arrow with a hundred holes, with a thousand feathers — it is the one you, O Indra, made your ally.
With that bring to the singers, to men and women to eat, O you who stand firm among the Ṛbhus, born at once.
These mighty deeds of yours have been accomplished; the greatest of all with abundance — you held them firm with the heart.
All these did Viṣṇu bring, the far-striding one, urged on — a hundred buffaloes, the milk-cooked rice-dish, the boar that Indra had taken away.

title: Rigveda
text:
Your fierce and well-wrought, fine bow, your trusty golden bundle — both your arms, fit for battle, well-adorned, grow great even from the supple, the supple-increasing.
O Indra, bring us a thousand puroḍāśa-cakes from the soma draught, and hundreds of cows, O hero.
Bring us adornment, a cow, a horse as additional adornment, together with a golden mind.
And bring us many ear-ornaments, O bold one; for you are heard, O lord of wealth.
No sycophant, O Indra, is yours, nor a good listener, nor a good giver; and no other sacrificer is like you, O hero.
Indra cannot be cut down, the mighty one cannot be overpowered; he hears and sees everything.
He, undeceived, takes note of the passion of mortals; he takes note of the blame before it comes.
Through his will alone the belly of the fleet one, the worshipper, is full — the Vṛtra-slayer, the soma-drinker.
In you, O Soma, are gathered the riches and all the good fortunes, well given and not turned away.
My desire that longs for barley, for cows, for gold — it is you it seeks; and the longing for horses seeks you.
O Indra, of you I have taken in my hand the gift with hope; whether of the day or of the gathered wealth, fill us, O Maghavan, with barley of the Kāśī land.
This Soma is the agent ungrasped, the all-conqueror, the one who breaks forth; a seer, an inspired one through his poetic power.
He clothes what is naked; he heals whatever is ailing; the blind man was made to see; the lame man was made to walk.
You, O Soma, are a wide-spreading shelter from those who cause bodily harm, from hostilities, from evils done by others.
You are the discerner, O Soma-bearer; by your might from heaven and earth you ward off even the hatred of evil.
If those who seek an object go toward their object, may the gift of the one who has given reach them; may the desire of the thirsty be fulfilled.

title: Rigveda
text:
Having found again what was lost of old, he set in motion the guardian of sacred order; he led life across what could not be crossed.
The kindly one who shows mercy, of undaunted will, unhindered — be for us, O Soma, a joy to the heart.
O Soma, do not terrify us together; do not scatter fear abroad, O king; do not smite our heart with your fierce energy.
When in my own station I observe the ill-intentions of the gods — O king, drive away the foes; O showerer, drive away the slanderers.
For there is no other bestower of grace more mighty, O hundredfold-willed one; you, O Indra, show us mercy.
You who have always unfalteringly protected us for the winning of the prize — you, O Indra, show us mercy.
What then? Are you the inspirer of the weak, who have stood by the soma-presser? Can you indeed be capable of helping us, O Indra?
O Indra, push our chariot forward even though it is behind, O stone-wielder; set it before me at the front.
Come now, why do you sit idle? Make our chariot first; the fame that strives for the prize shall be the highest.
Help our chariot that strives for the prize; it is easy for you — what lies beyond it? Make us truly victorious.
O Indra, be firm; you are our fort; auspicious comes to you the accomplished task; this thought is timely and potent.
May no reproach have a share in the vast goal, in the wealth laid up there; may the arm-spans be unobstructed.
The fourth sacrificial name — when you perform that, that is what we desire; and then the lord carries it forward like a friend.
The immortals have made you great; the one-day giver has gladdened the gods and also the goddesses; make therefore a praiseworthy offering to him — may he come swiftly in the morning, rich in thought and wealth.
Seize for us, O Indra, a splendid, bountiful prize with your great right hand.

title: Rigveda
text:
For we know you as one of mighty deeds, of mighty gifts, of mighty wealth, of mighty measure through your help.
Neither the gods nor mortal men, O hero, can hinder you when you are minded to give, terrible as a raging bull.
Come, let us now praise Indra, the self-sovereign lord of wealth; he will not fail us with his bounty.
He shall sing forth, he shall come near, he shall hear the Sāman being sung, he shall roar in response with his bounty.
Bring it to us with your right hand, touch it also with your left; O Indra, do not deprive us of wealth.
Step forward boldly, O bold one, and bring to us the treasure of him who has not pressed soma — him who is the more unworthy.
O Indra, whatever prize of yours is to be won through inspired poets — do win it well for us.
Your prizes, swift as the speed of a day, all-glittering, and the willing steeds — may they come quickly at our desire.
Run forward here, O Vṛtra-slayer, from far away and from near, to the pouring out of the sweet drink.
Come hither: the soma juices are strong and pressed, intoxicating; drink steadily as is your wont.
Exhilarate yourself with food; indeed it is fit for your desire and your mood; may it be good for your heart, O Indra.
Come, O you who have no foe, come hither; you are also invoked for the recitations in the highest luminous realm of heaven.
This soma, pressed for you with stones and strained through the cow-hairs for exhilaration, is called forth for you, O Indra.
O Indra, hear well my call; achieve the full drinking and satisfaction of our soma mixed with milk.
That soma, O Indra, which has been pressed for you in the bowls and the cups — you are the lord of it; drink of it.
The soma that gleams in the cups like the moon in the waters — you are the lord of it; drink of it.
That soma which the eagle bore to you with its foot through the realms of air, the untouched — you are the lord of it; drink of it.

title: Rigveda
text:
That great help of the gods — that we choose for ourselves, the aid of the mighty bulls on our behalf.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryamā always be our allies, and the wise ones who bring increase.
Bear us beyond the many widespread dangers as if across waters with ships; you are the charioteers of cosmic order.
May the excellent thing be ours, O Aryaman; excellent, O Varuṇa, worthy of praise — for it is the excellent that we choose.
For of the excellent are the wise, ruling, conquering Ādityas the lords; they do not lead to harm.
We, whether dwelling at home or going on the road, call upon you, O bountiful gods, for increase.
Watch over us, O Indra, watch over us, O Viṣṇu, as our kinsfolk; and so too the Maruts and the Aśvins.
The brotherhood of you bountiful ones — we take it up again together, even as in the mother's womb.
For you are the bountiful ones with Indra as your chief, you who shine upon us — even of you, therefore, I speak.
I praise your most beloved guest, dear as a friend, Agni the well-known, like a chariot.
The seer-like, wise one whom the gods thereafter placed a second time among mortals.
Protect, O youngest god, the men of the worshipper; hear our praises; guard his offspring and also yourself.
With what praise, O Agni Aṅgiras, O child of strength, shall I approach you, O god, to satisfy your will?
With what mind shall we serve the sacrifice, O son of strength? What shall I say? — this homage here.
So you shall win for us all good dwellings; our songs are full of prize-winning wealth.
Whose ample thoughts do you now quicken, O lord of the house? His hymns to you are cow-winning.
They adorn him, the wise one who goes before in the contests, the prize-winner in his own abodes.
He dwells among good, peaceful folk; none slays him, but he slays; the man of good heroes prospers, O Agni.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come both of you, O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, to my call, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Hear this my laud, O Aśvins; hear this my call, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
This Kṛṣṇa calls to you both, O Aśvins, O lords of fleet steeds, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Hear the call of the worshipper Kṛṣṇa as he praises, O heroes, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Bring the inviolable shelter to the inspired man who praises, O heroes, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Come to the house of the worshipper who praises you thus, O Aśvins, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Yoke the donkey to your firm-wheeled chariot, O you who possess bulls, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Come with the triple-poled, triple-fastened chariot, O Aśvins, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Now, O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, do the two of you promote my songs, for the drinking of the sweet soma.
Both of you, O wonder-workers, are healers, bringers of joy; both of you have responded to the words of our skill. Viśvaka calls you both for the protection of his body; do not forsake our friendship — release us.
How should a distracted man praise you both? Yet you have given him thought for the attainment of better things. Viśvaka calls you both for the protection of his body; do not forsake our friendship — release us.
You two, O givers of abundance, gave this Viṣṇāpva his increase for the attainment of better things. Viśvaka calls you both for the protection of his body; do not forsake our friendship — release us.
We call also that hero who wins wealth, who has soma-juice, though he be far away, for help; whose most sweet favour is like a father's care. Do not forsake our friendship — release us.
The god Savitā rested through cosmic order; the horn of cosmic order spread out broadly; order has overcome even the great ones who fight against it. Do not forsake our friendship — release us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Our glorious praise calls to you, O Aśvins, like a miller pouring — come hither; drink, O heroes beloved in heaven, of the sweet pressed juice, like two wild bulls at a pool.
Drink the hot sweet milk-drink, O Aśvins; sit upon the barhis, O heroes; gladdened in Manu's dwelling, sit down and bestow strength with your wisdom.
The Priyamedhas have called you both with all aids; come along the path to those who have prepared the barhis, to the sacrifice made pleasing in its heavenly aspirations.
Drink the sweet soma, O Aśvins; sit with good intention upon the barhis; growing strong through the excellent praise, come from heaven like two wild bulls to a pool.
Come now, O Aśvins, with your water-sprinkling steeds; O wonder-workers of the golden track, O lords of beauty, you who strengthen cosmic order — drink the soma.
For we inspired singers call you both for the winning of the prize; come, O charming wonder-workers of many wondrous deeds, O Aśvins skilled in prayer, come in obedience to our call.
We praise with our songs that wonder-worker of yours, who conquers in the onslaught, who rejoices in the wealth of soma-juice, even Indra — as cows lowing to their calf at their resting places.
We desire the heavenly, bountiful one, clothed with his powers like a mountain, the giver of abundant enjoyment, the flourishing prize of hundreds, of thousands, rich in cattle — come quickly.
Neither great mountains nor hard rocks can keep you back, O Indra; when you desire to give wealth to the praising singer of your praise, none can diminish that in you.
You are a warrior by wisdom, by might, and by wondrous power, surpassing all beings by your greatness; this hymn which the Gotamas have begotten turns to you for aid.
You have burst forth from the ends of heaven with your might; the earthly realm could not contain you, O Indra; you have grown according to your own nature.

title: Rigveda
text:
There is no hindrance to your bounty, O Maghavan, when you bestow gifts on the worshipper; be stirred by our laud, O most munificent one, for the winning of the prize.
Sing the great hymn to Indra, O Maruts, to the mightiest slayer of Vṛtra, through whom the strengtheners of cosmic order have generated light, the wakeful deity for the god.
He drove away the revilers, destroying those reviled; then Indra became resplendent. The gods, O Indra, with the host of Maruts, O you of great brilliance, yoked themselves to your friendship.
Sing forth to the great Indra, O Maruts, with your sacred formulas; the Vṛtra-slayer, the hundred-powered one, slays Vṛtra with the hundred-jointed bolt.
Bring forth with bold heart, O bold-minded one; may your glory be great; let the waters flow swiftly, like mothers — slay Vṛtra and win the light of heaven.
When you were born without precedent, O Maghavan, for the slaying of Vṛtra — thereby you spread out the earth; thereby you also propped up the sky.
From that the sacrifice was born for you, from that the hymn and the praise-shout; thereby you are the overcomer of all that has been born and all that shall be born.
You stirred the ripe in the unripe; you raised the sun in heaven; like the gharma-vessel heat it with your songs of praise — the great hymn pleasing to the hymn-lover.
May Indra prosper us in all our callings; may the Vṛtra-slayer, supreme in might, who delights in sacred verse, attend our prayers and pressings.
You are the first giver of bounties; you are the true maker of lordship; we choose for our ally the great might of the son who has exceeding glory.
Prayers that cannot be overcome are fashioned for you, O Indra, O lover of praise; accept these, O lord of bay horses — the songs, O Indra, which we have composed for you.
For you, O Maghavan, are true and unbowed, and you lay low many Vṛtras; therefore, O most mighty, O thunderbolt-handed one, turn abundant wealth toward the worshipper.

title: Rigveda
text:
You, O Indra, are glorious, the soma-drinker, O lord of strength; you alone slay the resistless Vṛtras, unconquered, upholding the people.
And you, the wise lord, we now implore as we would implore our share of bounty; your shelter, O Indra, is like a great hide for protection; may your blessings reach us.
A maiden, going to fetch water, found soma by a flowing stream; bearing it home she said: 'I will press thee for Indra, I will press thee for Śakra.'
O thou hero who goest shining from house to house — drink this soma pressed between the teeth, mingled with parched grain, mixed with gruel and sweet cakes, accompanied by lauds.
We do not tend thee out of regard, we do not pour thee away out of neglect; gently, ever so gently, O drop, flow round for Indra.
Will he be able? Will he accomplish it? Will he bring us into greater prosperity? Will women who hate their husbands meet together with Indra?
These three flat surfaces — make them grow, O Indra: the head of that bald man, the field yonder, and this my belly.
Both that field of ours, and this body of mine — and the head of that bald man — make all of them hairy.
In the nave of the chariot, in the nave of the cart, in the nave of the yoke, O Śatakratu — Indra, thou didst purify Apālā thrice, making her skin radiant as the sun.
Sing forth to Indra, the guardian of your soma-draught, the all-conquering, the Śatakratu, the most bounteous among men.
Him who is called by many, praised by many, celebrated in songs, ever-famed — call him 'Indra'!
Indra indeed is the giver of great prizes and of vigour to us; the mighty one stoops down to his knee.
With his beautiful jaw Indra has fully drunk from the inebriating soma-juice of Indu, of great power, of abounding stimulation — the soma mixed with barley.
Sing forth to that Indra for the drinking of soma; this indeed is his increase.

title: Rigveda
text:
Having drunk of his exhilarating draughts, a god through the power of the god, he becomes lord over all the worlds.
Him, the all-conquering one, whom you set in motion in all your songs — invite thou him to come hither for our aid.
The warrior ever unconquered, the soma-drinker never falling away, the man whose will none can check.
Grant us wealth, O Indra, thou who art very wise; O sage, help us at the decisive contest.
Come hither to us even from afar, O Indra, with a hundred prizes, with nourishment winning a thousand prizes.
Let us pursue the thoughts of the devout with our swift steeds, O Śakra, winner of kine; may we conquer in battles, O wielder of the bolt.
We, O Śatakratu, rejoice in thee with our lauds as cows in pastures.
For all that belongs to mortality is desirous of following, O Śatakratu; we have come to thee, O wielder of the bolt, with our hopes.
In thee, O son of strength, are concentrated the desires of those who slay Vṛtra; none surpasses thee, O Indra.
Do thou, O bull, assist us with thy most excellent, most terrible, most swift bounty; fill us with understanding and with abundance.
That rapture of thine which is now most glorious, O Indra, O Śatakratu — in that exhilaration be thou now exhilarated.
That rapture of thine which is most wonderfully famous, O Indra, which is most mighty for the slaying of Vṛtra, which is the greatest giver of vigour.
We know indeed that rapture of thine, O lord of the stone-bolt, given by thee thyself, O true soma-drinker, among all peoples, O wondrous one.
Let our praises surround the soma pressed for Indra's exhilaration; let the singers intone their hymn.
In whom all glories resound, the seven assemblies — we invoke Indra at the soma-pressing.
The gods stretched forth the conscious sacrifice at the three soma-bowls; let our praises magnify that.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let the soma-drops flow into thee as rivers into the ocean; none surpasses thee, O Indra.
Thou hast spread wide with thy greatness, O bull, the drinking of soma for the wakeful — that which is in thy belly, O Indra.
Let the soma be ready for thy belly, O Indra the Vṛtra-slayer; let the soma-drops be ready for thy seats.
The far-famed singer sings readiness for the horse, readiness for the cow, readiness for Indra's dwelling.
For thou art ever ready to grace our pressed somas, O Indra; thou art ready, O Śakra, for giving.
Even from afar may our praises reach thee, O lord of the stone-bolt; may we come to meet thee.
For thus thou art heroic, thus, O hero, thou art also firm; thus is thy mind apt for liberality.
Thus was thy gift established, O thou of great wealth, by all the ordaining powers; be thou still with me, O Indra.
Do not become sluggish like a brahmin, O lord of prizes; be exhilarated with the pressed soma mixed with milk.
Let not the sun outshine us, O Indra, as he traverses the rays of light; with thee as ally may we win that prize.
With thee, O Indra, as our ally, may we respond to our rivals; thou art ours and we are thine.
Thee indeed thy devotees follow as they roam, praising thee ever; thy friends the singers, O Indra.
Thou risest up indeed toward the far-famed, wealth-bestowing bull whose works are manly — thou goest to the shooter, O Sun.
He who broke ninety-nine fortresses with the strength of his arms, and with the power of the Vṛtra-slayer slew the serpent.
May that Indra be our auspicious friend, who milks for us abundance of horses, kine, and barley — like a cow with flowing streams.
Whatever exists today, O Vṛtra-slayer, since the sun rose over all — all that, O Indra, is in thy power.
Or if thou, O full-grown lord of the righteous, dost think 'I shall not die' — that too is truly thine.

title: Rigveda
text:
The soma pressings that are done in the distant region, the soma pressings done in the near region — to all of them, O Indra, thou goest.
We stimulate that Indra to slay the mighty Vṛtra; may he be the bull among bulls.
That Indra is fashioned for giving, he is the mightiest; he is devoted to exhilaration, glorious, renowned, devoted to soma.
Like a thunderbolt assembled by a hymn, together with his power, never giving way — the vigorous, unconquered one has grown strong.
Make for us easy passage even through difficulty, as thou art praised, O Indra, lover of hymns; thou art our desire, O Maghavan.
Thy self-rule, even the slightest command of which no god, no wretched man diminishes.
Then the two divine worlds, heaven and earth with beautiful jaws, serve thy irresistible might.
Thou hast sustained the bright milk in the dark cows and in the tawny ones, and in those of the Paruṣṇī river.
When all the gods stepped away from the serpent's flash of brilliance, they found the disease of the wild beast.
Then may there be protection for me; the Vṛtra-slayer has commanded manly valour; he who has no born enemy is unconquered.
I proclaim for you the most famous Vṛtra-slayer, the champion of men, for the attainment of great riches.
With this thought that seeks kine, O thou of many names, praised by many — by whatever soma thou hast appeared at each soma-feast.
May he be attentive to us — the Vṛtra-slayer, the lavish with libations; may Śakra hear our prayer.
With what aid dost thou exhilarate thyself toward us, O bull? With what dost thou bring abundance to the singers?
For whom does the bull, the Vṛtra-slayer, together with his team, rejoice at the pressing, the bull for the drinking of soma?
Come to us and, exhilarating thyself, be the bringer of thousandfold riches to the worshipper.

title: Rigveda
text:
These somas pressed with their consorts go eagerly to the enjoyment; the drinker of waters, Indra, comes to the purified drops.
The desired invocations, the augmenting ones, have been let loose toward Indra at the sacrifice; toward the final bath with vigour.
Here let those two revelling bay steeds with golden manes draw toward the oblation prepared for them.
For thee are these soma-drops pressed, the sacred grass is strewn, O all-illumining; bring Indra to the singers.
As he places in thee luminous power and distributes treasure to the worshipper — sing to Indra for the singers.
I place all the lauds in thy heroic power, O Śatakratu; be gracious to the singers, O Indra.
Bring us blessing after blessing, bring vigour, O Śatakratu — whensoever thou art gracious to us, O Indra.
Bring us all good things, O Śatakratu — whensoever thou art gracious to us, O Indra.
Thee only, O mightiest Vṛtra-slayer, do we who press the soma invoke — whensoever thou art gracious to us, O Indra.
Come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds, O lord of exhilarations; come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds.
He who is doubly the mightiest Vṛtra-slayer, Indra, the Śatakratu — come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds.
For thou, O Vṛtra-slayer, art the guardian of these somas — come to our pressed soma with thy bay steeds.
May Indra give us food, the ample, Ṛbhu-like wealth; may the prize-winner give us the prize.
The cow suckles the Maruts' fame-seeking mother of the wealthy; yoked are the two draught-horses of the chariots.
In whose lap all the gods sustain all their ordinances, the sun and moon for the beautiful sight.
That do all the noble ones ever call for us, the singers — O Maruts, for the drinking of soma.
This soma is pressed; the Maruts drink of it, and the self-ruling Aśvins also.

title: Rigveda
text:
Mitra and Aryaman and Varuṇa drink of the purified, swift soma that has three seats.
And now Indra too takes pleasure in this pressed soma mixed with milk, exhilarated like a morning hotar-priest.
How do the luminaries shine, like waters across the currents? They flow, those of purified power.
Which of the great gods' aids shall I choose today, and of the wondrous-radiant ones by their own power?
They who have spread out all earthly things and the luminous regions of the sky — O Maruts, for the drinking of soma.
Those pure-powered ones of heaven, O Maruts, I now invoke you — for the drinking of this soma.
Those who have propped apart the two worlds, the Maruts, I now invoke — for the drinking of this soma.
That troop of Maruts dwelling on the mountains, the bulls — I now invoke them for the drinking of this soma.
The hymns have come to thee like chariot-warriors at the soma-pressings, O lover of praises; they have lowed toward thee together, O Indra, as mothers toward a calf.
The bright pressed soma-drops have stirred thee, O Indra, lover of praises; drink now of this soma-juice, O Indra — it is established for thee in all things.
Drink the soma pressed for exhilaration, O Indra, brought by the eagle — for thou art the lord and king of all eternal peoples.
Hear the call of Tirascī, O Indra, who worships thee; fill him with wealth in heroes and kine — thou art great.
O Indra, he who has brought forth for thee the newest, most pleasing hymn — the thought full of understanding, the ancient one swelling with Order.
Let us now praise that Indra whom hymns and lauds have magnified; eager to win his many manly deeds, we celebrate him.
Come now, let us praise Indra the pure with a pure sāman-chant; let him who is magnified by pure lauds, the pure one, be gladdened by a pure invocation.

title: Rigveda
text:
Come to us as the pure Indra, O pure one, with pure aids; as the pure one establish wealth for us; as the pure, soma-loving one, be exhilarated.
Indra, pure, thou givest us wealth; pure, thou bestowest treasures on the worshipper; pure, thou smitest Vṛtras; pure, thou seekest to win the prize.
The sweet-sounding dawns of night stretched out their path for Indra; for him the seven mother-waters stood as rivers easy to ford, for men to cross over.
Though pierced through, the weapon of even a tottering one — thrice seven ridges of the mountains joined together — no god nor mortal could pass what the mighty bull accomplished.
Indra's bolt is of iron, plunging deep; in Indra's two arms is the greatest vigour; Indra's thoughts poured out from his head, they streamed forth, heard nearby.
I deem thee the most adorable of those who deserve worship; I deem thee the shaker of the unshakeable; I deem thee, O Indra, the banner of warriors; I deem thee the bull of mankind.
When thou dost take up in thy arms the bolt, the exhilaration-shedder, to slay the serpent — forth cried the mountains, forth the cows; the priests drew near to Indra.
Let us praise him who has produced all these beings inferior to himself; may we secure friendship with Indra through our songs; may we approach the bull with reverences.
All the gods who were thy friends abandoned thee as thou wert striving, driven by Vṛtra's roar; may thy friendship with the Maruts be established, O Indra, and then conquer all these hosts.
The thrice-sixty Maruts, grown mighty like heaps of dawn-cattle, adorable — we come to thee; make us partakers of thy share; with this oblation may we worship thy vigour.
Sharp is the Maruts' weapon, their army — who has dared to oppose thy thunderbolt, O Indra? The Asuras without weapons, the godless — with thy discus, shear them away, O Ṛjīṣin.

title: Rigveda
text:
Send forth a well-formed hymn to the great, mighty, most auspicious one, the possessor of cattle; direct many praises to Indra, the hymn-borne; may he perchance find something for his own being.
For the far-spreading laud-bearer, direct thy thought as one directs a raft to the far bank of rivers; touch with thy thought that being of the renowned and ever more beloved — may he perchance find it.
Discover what Indra has enjoyed; praise with a fine hymn, seek to win by reverence; approach with care, O singer — do not cry aloud; let thy voice be heard — may he perchance find it.
The dark drop descended and stood on the Aṁśumatī river, moving with ten thousands; Indra, the man-minded one, aided him who was blowing, and took away from him his slippery ones.
I saw the drop wandering at the meeting-point, in the bend of the Aṁśumatī river, standing like a dark cloud come down — I urge you on, O bulls, fighting in battle.
Then the drop, shining brightly, held its form in the lap of the Aṁśumatī; Indra allied with Bṛhaspati overcame the ungodly tribes that came against him.
Being born from the seven, thou becamest an enemy to those who had no enemy, O Indra; thou foundest heaven and earth that were hidden; thou didst establish battle for the worlds of the far-extending.
Thou boldly didst strike that unequalled strength with thy bolt, O wielder of the bolt; with thy weapons thou didst descend against Śuṣṇa; thou didst find the cows, O Indra, by thy power.
Thou, O bull of mankind, didst become the mighty smiter of Vṛtras; thou didst release the rivers that were dammed up; thou didst conquer the waters that had Dāsa lords.
He of good counsel who rejoices at the soma-pressings, whose anger is unbeaten, who is rich as a serpent — he alone, the manly doer of deeds, is the Vṛtra-slayer; otherwise they call him another.

title: Rigveda
text:
He is the Vṛtra-slaying Indra, the sustainer of men; him let us invoke as the worthy one with praise; he will be our protector, our Maghavan, our patron; he is the giver of vigour and fame.
That Vṛtra-slaying Indra, the Ṛbhukṣan, born at once, became the worthy one to be invoked; performing many manly deeds, like soma when drunk, worthy of invocation for friends.
The riches, the sun-wealth that thou didst bring away from the Asuras, O Indra — increase, O Maghavan, the wealth of this singer, and of those who have trimmed the sacred grass for thee.
The horse, the cow, the unfailing share that thou, O Indra, dost apportion — place it in the sacrificer who presses soma and gives the sacrificial fee; not in the miser.
He who, O Indra, sleeps out of season, the ungodly, the slumberer — let him perish by his own means; place his nourishing riches far away from there.
Whether thou, O Śakra, art in the distant region or in the near region, O Vṛtra-slayer — the soma-presser seeks thee hither from that distance with shining songs, O Indra, with hymns that reach the sky.
Whether thou art in the luminous realm of heaven, above the layer of the ocean, or in an earthly dwelling, O mightiest Vṛtra-slayer, or in the atmosphere — come hither.
Be thou exhilarated, O soma-drinker, at our soma-feasts, at our pressings, O lord of might; with thy bountiful gift, O truth-possessing Indra, with thy wealth abounding on all sides.
Turn not away from us, O Indra; be our companion in revelry; thou art our ally, thou art our kinsman — turn not away from us, O Indra.
Sit down here with us, O Indra, at the pressed soma to drink the sweetness; grant great aid to the singer, O Maghavan — with us, O Indra, at the pressed soma.
Neither the gods nor mortal men have ever equalled thee, O lord of the bolt; thou art the overpowerer of all creatures by thy might — neither the gods have equalled thee.

title: Rigveda
text:
Together they fashioned and begat Indra, the man most overpowering of all hosts, to be king — him most excellent in will, the bounteous, undying one, utterly fierce, most vigorous, mighty, and swift.
Together the singers chanted to Indra for the drinking of soma — the lord of the sun, who is established for his growth, firm in his vows, by his power and his aids.
The inspired singers, calling aloud, bow down with their gaze to the rim of the wheel and to the ram; your bright ones, free from enmity, swift in the ear — they come together with hymns.
I invoke again and again that Indra, the bounteous, the mighty, who holds irresistible strengths; most generous with hymns, may he, the adorable, turn back, and may the wielder of the bolt make for us all good paths to wealth.
Thou, O Indra, formerly didst know how to destroy these with thy might, O mightiest Śakra; from thee all the worlds tremble, O wielder of the bolt, and heaven and earth with fear.
May that Order, O heroic, wondrous Indra, protect me; like water, O wielder of the bolt, carry me over many difficulties; when wilt thou, O Indra, richly bestow on us the all-nourishing and desirable wealth, O king?
Sing a great sāman to Indra, to the inspired, to the great; to him who establishes Order, the wise, the praiseworthy.
Thou art the overpowerer, O Indra; thou didst make the sun to shine; thou art the all-maker, the all-deity, the great one.
Blazing with light thou didst reach the sun, the luminous realm of heaven; the gods arranged themselves for thy friendship, O Indra.
Come to us, O Indra, thou who art dear, the all-conqueror, unconcealed; like a mountain broad on all sides, lord of the sky.
For, O true soma-drinker, thou hast become the guardian of both worlds, heaven and earth; thou art the increaser of the soma-presser, lord of the sky.

title: Rigveda
text:
For thou art the breaker of eternal fortresses, O Indra; slayer of the Dāsa, increaser of Manu, lord of the sky.
Now indeed, O Indra, lover of praises, we release our great desires toward thee, as waters that rise upward.
Like water do the sacred verses magnify thee, O hero, with their streams — thee who hast grown great, O lord of the stone-bolt, day by day.
They yoke the two bay steeds of the swift one in the spacious chariot with wide yoke — the two Indra-bearing, speech-yoked ones.
Bring us, O Indra, fullness of might, manly vigour, O Śatakratu, wide-seeing; bring us a hero who withstands armies.
For thou hast become our father, O Vasu, thou hast become our mother, O Śatakratu; therefore we implore thy favour.
O strong one, O widely invoked, I call upon thee, the prize-winner, O Śatakratu; do thou grant us good heroic strength.
Thee indeed yesterday the eager men refreshed, O wielder of the bolt; so, O Indra, bearer of praises, hear here — come for the early-morning rite.
Be exhilarated, O fair-jawed one with the bay steeds; this we crave; the wise ones adorn thee; thy fames are supreme, worthy of lauds, at the soma-pressings, O Indra, lover of praises.
As they cling to the sun, eat from all of Indra's bounties; being born we have shone with vigour, at birth, steadfastly toward our share of good things.
Praise the giver of riches who never fails; auspicious are Indra's gifts; he does not neglect the wish of his worshipper, but urges his mind to giving.
Thou, O Indra, art beyond all rivals in onslaughts; thou art the destroyer of curses, the producer, the pervader; thou art swift against the one who attacks.
The two worlds followed after thy hastening might like two mothers after a child; all rivals are crushed by thy wrath when thou, O Indra, dost overwhelm Vṛtra.
From here, with his aid, invoke the unfailing, the unsent sender, the swift conqueror, the impeller, the foremost charioteer, the unassailable, the increaser of Tugrya's line.

title: Rigveda
text:
We invoke this same Indra for aid — the accomplisher of unaccomplished things, the force-created, the hundred-aided, the Śatakratu, the possessor of good things, swift as wealth.
I come before thee with my whole body; all the gods approach me from behind; when thou shalt assign me my share, then with me, O Indra, perform heroic deeds.
I offer thee a share of honey first; let the pressed soma be thy allotted portion; and thou shalt be my friend on the right side, and then let us smite many Vṛtras together.
Bring forth your laud, eager for the prize, to Indra the true — if truth there be; 'Indra does not exist,' said a certain one; 'who has seen him? Whom shall we praise?'
Here am I, O singer — look at me here; I surpass all beings with my greatness; the directions of Order cause me to grow; shattering, I shatter the worlds asunder.
When the Venas climbed up to meet me, me sitting alone on the back of the beloved one of Order — even my mind spoke back from the heart; the young friends cried out aloud.
All these things of thine are to be proclaimed at the soma-pressings, which thou, O Maghavan Indra, hast done for the soma-presser; the distant, abundantly-gathered wealth thou didst uncover for Śarabha, the kinsman of the seer.
Run forward now separately — let not him who has held you back stop you here; Indra has struck the bolt into the vital part of Vṛtra.
Swift as thought, advancing, he crossed the iron fortress; the fair-winged bird flew to heaven and brought the soma to the wielder of the bolt.
The bolt lies within the ocean, surrounded by water; the assembled ones, whose streams flow forward, bring tribute to him.
When Vāc speaks things that lack understanding — she who is the queen of the gods has sat down pleasing; she has milked four strengthening milkings; where then has her highest form gone?

title: Rigveda
text:
The gods brought forth the divine Vāc; all living beings speak her in manifold forms; may she, the cow Vāc, that milch-cow milking joy and strength, come to us with her excellent praise.
O friend Viṣṇu, stride out more widely; O heaven, give space for the bolt to prop itself; let us smite Vṛtra, let us release the rivers — let them flow forth at Indra's urging.
Rightly indeed has that mortal striven for the sake of the gods, who now has engaged Mitra and Varuṇa for his desire, for the bestowal of the oblation.
Mightiest in dominion, wide-seeing, those two lords, those two kings most famed of all — they travel, wondrous in their arm-power, together with the rays of the sun.
He who ran swiftly as your messenger, O Mitra and Varuṇa, the iron-headed one, swift in exhilaration.
He who delights neither in entreaty nor in being invoked again, nor in conversation — from that calamity guard us today; guard us with your arms.
Sing forth, O truth-possessing ones, the companionable praise to Mitra and to Aryaman; sing the sheltering, pleasing word of laud among the kings, to Varuṇa.
They impelled the ruddy, noble, excellent one — the single son of the three mothers; they, the immortal ones, behold undeceived the ordinances of mortals.
My words are raised up, most glorious in their working; come, both of you, Nāsatyas, together delighting, to accept the oblations.
When we call upon the demon-free gift of you two, O Vājinīvasus, come, O lords, prolonging the eastern invocation, praised by Jamadagni.
Come, O Vāyu, to our sacrifice that touches the sky, with good intentions; this bright one, being purified within above, is offered to you.
The adhvaryu goes by the straightest paths to receive the oblations; so now, O lord of the team, drink of both our peoples the pure soma mingled with milk.

title: Rigveda
text:
Verily great are you, O Sūrya; verily great are you, O Āditya; the greatness of you the great one is praised; truly, O god, you are great.
Verily great are you, O Sūrya, in renown; great, O god, are you in every way; mighty among the gods, you are the Asura, the purohita, the all-pervading, indestructible light.
This one, the ray-bearing one of downward form, fashioned after Rohiṇī — like a wondrous thing she is seen appearing, coming amid the ten arms.
Three offspring have passed beyond; other ones have entered on every side around the sun; the mighty one has stood within the worlds, the purified one has entered into the green.
She is the mother of the Rudras, the daughter of the Vasus, the sister of the Ādityas, the navel of immortality — I now proclaim this to the discerning people: do not slay the guiltless cow Aditi.
The cow, who knows speech and who utters speech, who is present with all insights, divine, who has gone around among the gods — let no mortal of small wit snatch her away.
You, O Agni, bestow great wealth on the worshipper, O god — you the seer, the householder, the ever-young.
So bring the gods to us along with their praise, O Agni, you who serve them well; bring them, O all-illumining one, that we may know.
With you indeed as our ally, the greatest impeller, O youngest one, we strive for the winning of the prize.
Like Aurva and Bhṛgu, like Apnavāna, I invoke the pure Agni, who has the ocean as his garment.
I invoke the power that sounds like wind, the seer that roars like Parjanya — Agni, who has the ocean as his garment.
As the invigorating impulse of Savitṛ, as the enjoyment of Bhaga, so I invoke him — Agni, who has the ocean as his garment.
Agni, who grows great through sacrifices, the most glorified of all — sing to his vigorous grandson.
Just as Tvaṣṭar comes to us, fashioning forms as things to be shaped — through the will of this glorious one.

title: Rigveda
text:
This Agni reigns over all glories among the gods; may he come to us with prizes.
Praise here among all the priests the most glorious, Agni, the foremost at the sacrifices.
The sharp one with purifying flame, the eldest who shines within the houses — of widest fame, he blazes.
Praise him, O sage, like a prize-winning steed, the vigorous one — like Mitra, who unites people.
The sister hymns, pointing out the oblation-maker, have stood before you at the face of Vāyu.
His three-layer strewn barhis stands without suture; even the waters have placed their foot on it.
The footstep of the bounteous god, with irresistible aids — auspicious is the sight, like the sun.
O Agni, blazing with your flame through the layers of ghee, O god — bring the gods hither and worship them.
The mothers gave birth to you, the seer; the gods, the Aṅgirases — to you the immortal conveyor of oblations.
You, the wise one, the most excellent, the desirable messenger, the conveyor of oblations — they have established you, O Agni the seer.
I have no milch-cow, no axe that bites wood; yet I bring you such an offering as this.
Whatever pieces of wood we lay down for you, O Agni — be pleased with them, O youngest one.
What the little tongue-flame devours, what the ant creeps along — let all of that be ghee for you.
The mortal who kindles Agni with his mind shall join his thought to insight; he kindles Agni with his illuminations.
He has appeared, the most knowing of ways, in whom they have placed their holy observances; may our hymns approach Agni, born to magnify the noble man.
Daivodāsa's fire goes toward the gods in its greatness like a divine gift; he has turned, following mother Earth, and stands upon the vault of heaven.
At whose deeds, as he performs his powerful works, the peoples tremble — worship Agni by yourselves with thoughts, as in a gain-bringing sacrifice for a thousand.

title: Rigveda
text:
The mortal whom you lead on to wealth, O Vasu, whoever has offered to you — that man by himself possesses a hero, O Agni, who recites the laud, a nourisher of thousands.
He breaks through even the hard place and wins the prize with his steed; he obtains imperishable renown; in you, ever among the gods, O Purūvasu, may we lay up all good things.
He who as hotr distributes all wealth, the charming one of the folk — as the first cups of the sweet drink go to him, so praises go forth to Agni.
Like a chariot horse with hymns the bountiful, god-loving ones groom him; O wondrous lord of the settlement, carry across to both progeny and offspring the wealth of the generous.
Sing forth to the most bounteous one, the upholder of truth, the great, the bright-flaming — you who stand in praise before Agni.
When kindled and invoked with oblations, the magnanimous one wins heroic renown; may his newest good will come toward us with prizes.
Praise the most beloved among dear things, the ever-present guest — Agni, the controller of chariots.
He who, praiseworthy, turns back toward good things whether praised or blamed — the one who would win the prize with insight: his billows in the deep channel are hard to cross.
May Agni, the wealth-bearing guest, this one widely praised, not be angry with us — he who is the good hotr, the auspicious sacrificer.
May those who address you, O Agni, O Vasu, with direct words through whatever ordinances, not be harmed; for even the poet implores you as messenger — he whose offerings are given, who sacrifices well.
Come, O Agni, with the Maruts as companions, with the Rudras, to drink the soma; rejoice, O bull of heaven, at Sobhari's excellent praise.
Flow, O Soma, with thy sweetest, most exhilarating stream; thou art pressed out for Indra to drink.
The slayer of Rākṣasas, beholder of all beings, settles upon the iron-firm birthplace, taking his seat in the wooden vessel.

title: Rigveda
text:
Be thou the greatest giver of freedom, the most bountiful, the most potent slayer of Vṛtra; convey to us the wealth of the munificent ones.
Flow forth with the Soma-juice to the feast of the great gods; flow forth for food and for renown.
To thee, O Indu, day by day we draw near with this purpose alone; our desires rest in thee.
The daughter of the Sun purifies thy flowing Soma with her eternal fleece, forever and ever.
Ten nimble fingers take hold of him, his sisters, at the proper celestial time — the ten divine maidens seize him.
The unmarried maidens urge him on; they blow into the resounding skin-bag — the honey that possesses three stations and is worthy of being held back.
The holy, unslayable milk-cows also mix him — this child, this Soma — for Indra to drink.
By these exhilarations of Soma, Indra strikes down all the Vṛtras; the hero bestows great gifts and wealth.
Flow forth swiftly, O Soma, thou who art the hero of the gods, past the filter; O Indu, O bull, enter into Indra.
Fill thyself full with the great food, O manly Indu, most abundantly glorious; take thy seat, thou who art firm by nature, upon thy birthplace.
The stream of the pressed one, the wise ordainer, has milked forth the beloved honey; clothed in the waters he stands, he of good resolution.
The great waters, the great rivers, flow after thee, the great one, when thou art about to clothe thyself with the cows' milk.
The ocean has cleansed itself in the waters; Soma, the support, the upholder of heaven, desiring us, flows through the filter.
The great tawny bull has cried aloud, beautiful as Mitra; he shines together with the Sun.
The praises, O Indu, of those who are busy working are polished bright for thee with power — those praises with which thou adornest thyself for intoxication.
We implore thee — thee who art impetuous for ecstasy, who art the maker of space; great are thy praises.

title: Rigveda
text:
Flow for us, O Indu, longing for Indra, with a stream of sweetness — as Parjanya laden with rain.
Thou art the winner of cows, O Indu, the winner of men, the winner of horses, the winner of food; thou art the primordial soul of the sacrifice.
This immortal god flies like a bird with wings; he settles upon the wooden vessels.
This god, fashioned by the inspired sage, runs past the crooked places; the Pavamāna is not to be deceived.
This god, the Pavamāna, is wiped clean by the inspired praisers, by those who live according to Ṛta; the tawny one is cleansed for the winning of prizes.
This Pavamāna, like a warrior hero advancing, strives to win all desirable things.
This god, the Pavamāna, moves like a chariot-warrior; he serves the generous patron; he makes the praiseful bard manifest.
This god, praised by the sages, plunges through the waters, bestowing treasures upon the pious worshipper.
This Pavamāna runs through heaven, passing through the realms of air with his stream, roaring aloud.
This Pavamāna has coursed through heaven, untouched, passing through the aerial realms; he is the lord of the proper rite.
