This god, pressed out of old for the gods, flows with his ancient birth through the filter, the tawny one.
This same one, of many ordinances, being born and generating nourishments, flows, when pressed, with his stream.
Both of old hast thou won, O Soma Pavamāna, and thou dost win great renown; so now make us more prosperous.
Of old hast thou won the light, of old the sun, and all good fortune, O Soma; so now make us more prosperous.
Of old hast thou won power and wisdom; slay the enemies, O Soma; so now make us more prosperous.
O ye purifiers, purify the Soma for Indra to drink; so now make us more prosperous.
Give us our share in the Sun, through thy wisdom, through thy help; so now make us more prosperous.

title: Rigveda
text:
Through thy wisdom, through thy aid, may we behold the Sun for a long time; so now make us more prosperous.
Flow forth, O Soma, well-armed, with wealth that is doubly great; so now make us more prosperous.
Flow forth, undiminished, having conquered wealth in battles; so now make us more prosperous.
The sacrifices have exalted thee, O Pavamāna, in thy distributive ordinance; so now make us more prosperous.
Bring to us, O Indu, brilliant wealth abounding in horses and full of all life; so now make us more prosperous.
Kindled, the lord of all quarters, Pavamāna reigns radiantly; the bull gladdens all, roaring aloud.
Tanūnapāt Pavamāna flows, sharpening his two horns, shining brilliantly through the atmosphere.
The Pavamāna who is worthy of invocation shines forth, luminous treasure, with streams of sweetness and with might.
Spreading the eastward-laid sacred grass with his might, the tawny Pavamāna, a god among gods, is invoked.
The divine golden doors swing open wide with a great sound, praised by the Pavamāna.
The two great ones, splendidly adorned with beauty — Night and Dawn, like two who do not see each other — Pavamāna desires them as a bull.
I invoke both the divine priests, beholders of men: Pavamāna and the bull Indra.
May Bhāratī of the Pavamāna, great Sarasvatī, and Iḷā — may the three fair-formed goddesses come to this our sacrifice.
I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the firstborn, the protector, the foremost mover; Indu is Indra, the bull, the tawny Pavamāna, Prajāpati.
O Pavamāna, anoint the lord of the forest with thy stream of sweetness — the thousand-branched, the green, the glittering, the golden one.
Come, all ye gods, to the Svāhā offering of the Pavamāna — Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Sūrya, Agni, and Indra together, in union.
Flow, O Soma, with thy gladdening stream, O bull, longing for the gods, desiring us through the woollen filters.

title: Rigveda
text:
Flow, O Indu, toward that exhilarating intoxication, crying 'Indra!'; flow toward the vigorous steeds.
Pressed out, flow, O Soma, through the filter toward that primordial exhilaration; flow toward food and renown.
The Soma-drops, the Indus, have flowed after their path like waters along a slope; purifying themselves, they have entered Indra.
Him whom the ten maidens wipe clean like a race-horse full of vigour — him who sports like a swift sheep in the forest.
Mingle the sap of that bull together with the cows' milk, when pressed, for the exhilaration and the delight of the gods; bring him.
A god flows by his stream for a god; when pressed, he flows for Indra, having swelled with his milk.
The soul of the sacrifice, pressed out, flows swiftly, well pressed; he preserves the ancient wisdom-poetry.
Thus purifying thyself, longing for Indra, O most exhilarating, for the delight — even in the secret place thou holdest the praises.
The Indu-drops, beautiful, have been set flowing along the path, along the ordinance of Ṛta, knowing the harnessing thereof.
The foremost stream of sweetness plunges through the great waters; he is worthy of praise among oblations, the best of oblations.
The foremost driver of words has roared like a bull in the forest; he is truly the one who pervades the proper rite with his seat.
When the seer, clothed in his poetic powers and in heroic might, flows around, the swift steed strives to win the sun.
Pavamāna settles upon the peoples who contend against him, like a king, when the ordaining priests set him in motion.
The beloved tawny one rests in the woollen filter, rests in the wooden vessels; the singing priest wins favour through his song of praise.
He who delights in Soma's ordinances goes together with his exhilaration to Vāyu, to Indra, to the Aśvins.

title: Rigveda
text:
Toward Mitra and Varuṇa, toward Bhaga, the waves of sweetness flow purifying, knowing his powers.
O Heaven and Earth, win for us wealth and the sweetness of Soma for the gaining of food-prizes — renown and all good things.
These Somas have flowed toward the beloved desire of Indra, increasing his heroic might.
They, the purifying ones who sit in the pressing vessels, going toward Vāyu, toward the Aśvins — may they grant us true heroic power.
O Soma, purifying thyself for the gift of Indra, stimulate his heart; take thy seat in the birthplace of Ṛta.
Ten nimble fingers cleanse thee; seven songs of praise urge thee on; after thee the inspired ones have rejoiced.
Thee, released for the exhilaration of the gods, O thou who dost spring over the filter — we clothe thee with the cows' milk.
Purifying himself, he, the ruddy tawny one, is clothed in garments in the bowls; he has wrapped himself about with the dairy-gifts.
Flow for us, O lord of bounty; slay all enemies; O Indu, enter into thy friend.
Flow from heaven as rain; lay glory upon the earth; establish our might, O Soma, in battles.
May we partake of thee, the beholder of men, drunk by Indra, the finder of the sun — of thy offspring and nourishment.
The beloved seer of heaven, placed amid the two young women's limbs, pressed out, goes forth — he of seer-wisdom.
Forth and forth, beloved of the guileless people who are worthy of praise and destined for a home — flow onward most pleasingly.
That pure son, born, has illumined both his mothers as they came into being — great is he, and they are the two great ones who prosper Ṛta.
He, sustained by seven songs of devotion, the guileless one has made the rivers rejoice — the rivers that have grown into the one eye.
They have placed Indu — the ever-present, unconquered, great, youthful one — within thy ordinance, O Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
The immortal bearer, ever-moving, looks upon the seven; the active one has gratified the divine ones.
Help us, O Soma, in our proper rites, O manly one; fight away the darknesses; smite them while purifying thyself.
Now, for the newest, most recent, well-spoken hymn, make smooth the paths; illuminate the brilliances as of old.
O Pavamāna, give us great fame, cows, and horses together with heroes; give us wisdom of old and the heavenly light of old.
Sounding forth like chariots, eager for glory like swift steeds, the Somas have stepped forth toward wealth.
Urged on like chariots, they have run forward upon the arms of the presser, like the loads of toiling men.
Like kings with their praises, the Somas anoint themselves with the cows' milk; like a sacrifice with the seven dispensers.
The pressed Indu-drops, pressed out, flow in a stream for exhilaration, with a mighty song.
Having drunk of Vivasvat's gift, they have given birth to the good fortune of the Dawns; the heroes spread the subtle one wide.
The singers, devoted men of the bull, open wide the ancient doors of inspired thoughts with the fiery glow of the bull.
The seven kindred priests, facing one another, sit; they fill the footstep of the one.
Hub to hub they joined together; even the eye accompanies the Sun; from the offspring of the seer they milk out the blessing.
With the eyes of the sun, the loved ones behold the seat of heaven set in secret by the adhvaryu priests.
Sing to him, O men, to the Pavamāna, to the drop Indu; he seeks to win the gods.
The Atharvans have blended milk with honey for you; the divine one, god-devoted, for the god.
Flow purified for our good, O king — welfare to the cow, welfare to the people, welfare to the steed, welfare to the herbs.
Sing a song to the tawny one, to the self-mighty, to the ruddy one that touches heaven — to Soma.

title: Rigveda
text:
Purify the pressed Soma with the stones shaken in the hands; run the sweet into the sweet.
Draw near reverently and be seated; press the Soma down and strain it; place the drop in Indra.
Flow purified, O Soma, slayer of foes, all-seeing, for the welfare of the cow, fulfilling the desires of the gods.
For Indra's drinking, for his rapture, you are poured around, O Soma — even the lord of the mind in the mind.
O Pavamāna, O Soma, pour upon us riches and heroic strength; O Indu, together with Indra be our companion.
The Soma-drops, the Indus, have flowed, pressed out, in the seat of Ṛta — for Indra, most rich in sweetness.
The inspired sages have sung toward him, as cows toward their calf, toward Indra for the drinking of the Soma.
The wise one, shaking rapture, dwells in the seat upon the wave of the river; Soma is established upon the Gaurī.
At the navel of the sky, all-seeing, he is magnified in the fleece of the sheep — Soma who is the wise-willed seer.
The Soma that is placed within the jars, set in the filter — Indu has embraced him all around.
Indu sends forth the voice above the expanse of the ocean, quickening the honey-dripping vessel.
The lord of the forest, ever-praised, the fulfiller within the inspired thoughts, urges on the generations of men.
Toward the beloved stations of the sky, Soma the seer flows impelling, with the stream of the inspired one.
O Pavamāna, hold fast for us the wealth of thousandfold splendour; O Indu, that which is self-sprung.
Soma flows purified, of a thousand streams, passing through the woolly filter, the appointed share of Vāyu and Indra.
Sing forth to the Pavamāna, to the inspired one, you who seek help — to him who is well-pressed for the delight of the gods.
The Somas of thousandfold brilliance flow for the winning of prize, being praised for the delight of the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
And flow for us for the winning of prize, with great refreshments; O Indu, with radiance and heroic strength.
Let those Indus, those gods, well-pressed, flow to us with thousandfold wealth and heroic strength.
Swift ones, driven like racing steeds by drivers, they have flowed for the winning of prize; the swift ones have spread the sheep's wool filter apart.
The bellowing Indu-drops flow toward him as milch-cows toward their calf; they have made their way to the arms.
O Pavamāna, exhilarating, beloved by Indra, roaring aloud — smite away all enemies.
The Pavamānas, gazing upon the light of heaven, driving off the niggards, take their seat in the womb of Ṛta.
The seer has rushed all around, established upon the wave of the river, bearing the prized thing much desired.
When the five troops of kindred, working with their hands, adorn the sustainer with their voice.
Then all the gods have rejoiced in the juice of this vigorous one when he is clothed with the milk-streams.
Cleansing himself, he flows forth, leaving behind the husks with his body; here he meets his mate in union.
He who, young and radiant, has cleansed himself among the daughters of Vivasvat, making the cows as a shining garment.
Passing over the two pressing-boards, going through obliquely, he goes with the slender stream for the cow-pastures; he raises the voice that is known.
The fingers have come together, purifying the lord of refreshment; they grasp the back of the swift racer.
Touching all the heavenly and earthly things, O Soma, come toward us bearing goods.
This hero goes by the slender stream of inspiration, with swift chariots, going to the appointed share of Indra.
This one is much meditated upon for the great gathering of the gods, where the immortals are seated.
This one, set in motion, is led through the bright path within, when the mighty ones urge him on.

title: Rigveda
text:
This bull of the herd, shaking his horns, whetted — bearing manly power with might.
This swift racer goes adorned with golden ornaments, with bright stalks, becoming the lord of the rivers.
This one, having gone past the knotty, clinging goods, goes down to the resting places.
The descendants of Āyu cleanse this one worthy of cleansing in the troughs, him who sets in motion the great refreshments.
And this one the ten fingers cleanse, and the seven devotions — he of his own weapons, most intoxicating.
Your pressers have sent forth the juice for rapturous exhilaration — Etaśa flies like a loosed arrow.
By the power of understanding, clothing himself in the waters with the Soma-plant that drives the chariot — we follow in the narrow ways of the cows.
Release the Soma that is unwet yet hard to pass through into the filter; purify it for Indra to drink.
By the will of the self-purifying one, Soma flows through the filter; by his power he has taken his seat in the common dwelling.
The Indus, the Somas, have let you flow, O Indra, with acts of homage — the active ones for great bestowal.
Flowing purified in imperishable form toward all splendours, he stands among the cows like a hero.
The stream of the pressed Soma, swollen like the crest of heaven, flows freely through the filter.
You, O Soma, streaming purified in the lifetimes of the all-wise, run through the fleece of the sheep.
Like rivers rushing downward, smashing obstacles, full-streaming, the swift Somas have flowed forth.
The pressed Indu-drops, like showers of rain upon the earth, have streamed toward Indra.
Soma, intoxicating and exhilarating, of surging waves, flows through the filter, god-seeking, shattering the Rākṣasas.
He runs into the jars, is poured all around through the filter, and grows great among the sacrifices with the lauds.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Soma, passing beyond the three shining realms, you shine as you mount the sky; urging the sun forward, you have set him in motion.
The inspired poets, the craftsmen, have sung toward him, the head of the sacrifice, placing the beloved one in the eye.
And you, the swift racer — inspired men, help-seeking, cleanse you with their devotions for the divine gathering.
Flow after the stream of honey; sharp, you have taken your seat in the common place, lovely, to be drunk for Ṛta.
Pressed and dwelling on the mountain, Soma has flowed through the filter all around; in raptures you are the giver of all.
You are the inspired one, you are the seer, the honey born from the Soma plant; in raptures you are the giver of all.
All the gods, of like enjoyment, have partaken of your drink; in raptures you are the giver of all.
You who have placed all desirable goods in your two hands; in raptures you are the giver of all.
You who milk these two great worlds together as a mother; in raptures you are the giver of all.
You who flow all around both worlds at once with prizes; in raptures you are the giver of all.
He, the vigorous one, flowing into the jars self-purified, has cried aloud; in raptures you are the giver of all.
O Soma, whatever brilliant wealth, worthy to be praised in hymns, celestial and earthly, may be — bring that to us as you flow purified.
For you two, O Indra and Soma, are lords of the light, lords of the cattle; ruling, do you two swell our inspirations.
The bull, flowing purified among the living, thundering upon the sacred grass, being the tawny one, has taken his seat in the womb.
The devotions have cried out over the seed of the bull — the mothers of the son, of the calf.
Did the purifying one place the embryo in those that desire the bull — those that milk the bright milk?

title: Rigveda
text:
Cast fear upon those who sit plotting against us, upon the enemies; O Pavamāna, find wealth for us.
O Soma, strike down the foe's virile power, strike down his vigour, strike down his strength — whether he is afar or near.
The seer flows through the fleece-filters for the delight of the gods, having overcome all rivals.
For he indeed impels toward the praisers the thousand-fold prize rich in cattle — the Pavamāna.
You touch all things with your consciousness and flow purified with inspired thought; O Soma, grant us fame.
Flow with great glory, with firm wealth for the bountiful ones; bring refreshment to the praisers.
You, O Soma, like a king of righteous vows, have entered the songs; O wondrous carrier, flowing purified.
He, the carrier, hard to pass in the waters, being cleansed in the hands — Soma takes his seat in the bowls.
Playful, bountiful like the active Makha, you go to the filter, O Soma, bestowing heroic strength upon the praiser.
These Soma-drops, the indu-streams, run swiftly on for Indra, exhilarating, intoxicating, finders of the heavenly light.
Pressing forward, conquering enemies, pressed for the liberal patron, finders of wide space, of themselves bestowing vigour upon the singer.
The indu-drops play freely and flow straight to the one gathering-place; they have streamed forth in the wave of the river (Sindhu).
These Pavamāna Soma-drops have attained all desirable things, like the seven bay horses harnessed to the chariot.
Place in this one, O indu-drops, the tawny (Soma) as a sign for Vena — he who is ungrudging toward us.
Like Ṛbhu fashioning a new chariot-wheel, place insight as a sign (for Vena); O bright ones, flow onward with the flood.
These very ones have bellowed forth; the swift ones have reached the goal; from his very being they have sent forth thought.

title: Rigveda
text:
These swift Soma-drops, swift as racing-chariots, strong, released in streams, have roared forth.
These are wide like the winds, like the rains of Parjanya, and freely roam like the sparks of Agni.
These purified, wise Soma-drops, mixed with curds of Dadhyañc, have penetrated through all sacred hymns with their stream of inspiration.
These cleansed immortal ones, having flowed on, have not grown weary; longing to worship, they illumine the paths of heaven.
These, striding apart, have pervaded the backs of the two worlds (heaven and earth), and have reached this highest realm.
They have reached the thread being woven most high, flowing downward along the slope — and this most exalted one too.
You, O Soma, have wrested treasures and cattle-wealth from the Paṇis; you have bellowed forth, stretching out the thread (of the sacrifice).
The swift Soma-drops have streamed forth with the flood of sweet exhilaration, pervading all the hymns of vision (kāvya).
The human worshippers of old have followed the newer path; for the sake of brightness they have generated the Sun.
O Pavamāna, bring for us the estate of the ungiven — the niggard's home; make our refreshments rich in offspring.
The Soma-drops, belonging to men, flow on with exhilarating intoxication, toward the honey-dripping cask.
Soma flows on, sustaining, bearing the Indra-potent juice, of excellent heroism, a guardian against curses.
For Indra, O Soma, you flow purified; joyous together with the gods, O indu, you desire to win the prize.
Drinking of this, (the Soma) of exhilarations, Indra smote the Vṛtras unopposed — he smote them and shall smite them now.
The Soma-drops, the Pavamāna indu-streams, have sprung forward swiftly; being mixed (with milk), they are cleansed in the waters.
The cows (of milk) have rushed forward, like waters flowing down the slope; being purified, they have reached Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Pavamāna, you rush forward as Soma for Indra to drink; you are led onward by the men (priests) along various (paths).
Flow purified, O Soma, gladdener of men, conquering all peoples — you who are the winner and worthy of rejoicing.
O indu, when pressed by the stones you run around the filter, you are (thereby made) fit for the seat of Indra.
Flow purified, O supreme Vṛtra-slayer, celebrated with hymns of praise — pure, purifying, and wondrous.
Soma is called pure and purifying in the sweetness of the pressed draught — the champion of the gods, destroyer of sinful speech.
Flow purified, O Hari (the tawny one), accomplishing skillful might, for the gods to drink — O exhilaration, (flow) for the Maruts and for Vāyu.
O Pavamāna, urged forward by sacred thought, crying out toward your resting place, enter into Vāyu by the law (dharman).
The vigorous seer shines beautifully together with the gods, beloved in his native seat — the Vṛtra-slayer, most sought by the gods.
Entering all forms, the desirable one goes, being purified, to where the immortals are seated.
The ruddy Soma, with the insight of a seer, flows purified, generating hymns for life, going to Indra.
Flow purified to us, O most intoxicating one, with your stream through the filter, O seer — and take your seat at the source of the hymn (arka).
Him, the powerful one, the inspired priests have cleansed upon the lap of Aditi, with fine and subtle thought.
The cows (of milk) have lowed toward him — the indu of a thousand streams, inexhaustible, the sustainer of heaven.
The inspired ones have extolled him — the Pavamāna, nourishing greatly upon the sky, the sustainer and abundant bestower.
They have extolled him with abundant devotion — he who dwells with Vivasvat (the Sun), the inviolable lord of the sacred word.
The kindred women (the fingers) urge him on with the pressing-stones upon the back of the (pressing-board) — the tawny, desirable one, the one of wide vision.

title: Rigveda
text:
The wise ones urge you forward, O Pavamāna strengthened by hymns, O indu, the exhilarating one for Indra.
This seer, praised with hymns, drips upon the filter; flowing purified, he drives away failings.
This one, winner of heavenly light, is poured around for Indra and for Vāyu, perfecting the rite with his power in the filter.
This one is led apart by men — Soma pressed forth, the bull, head of heaven, omniscient in the (sacred) forest growths.
This Pavamāna desiring cattle has bellowed forth, seeking gold; the indu, all-conquering, unvanquished.
This Pavamāna shines together with the Sun upon the sky; the exhilarating (drink) is intoxicating in the filter.
This vigorous, tawny bull has gushed down in the mid-air; the indu, flowing purified, goes to Indra.
This swift one, urged on by men, omniscient, lord of the mind, runs through the woollen filter.
This Soma, pressed for the gods, has flowed through the filter, entering all the (divine) abodes.
This immortal god beautifies himself in his native seat — the Vṛtra-slayer, most beloved of the gods.
This vigorous bull, crying loudly, restrained by the ten kindred (fingers), runs into the wooden vessels.
This Pavamāna, all-observing, has caused the Sun to shine, knowing all the (divine) abodes.
This vigorous, undeceivable Soma flows being purified — champion of the gods, destroyer of evil speech.
The streams of this vigorous, pressed (Soma) have flowed forth with might, shining for the gods in abundance.
The wise chanting-bards cleanse the swift horse (Soma), praising him with hymns — he who has generated light worthy of praise.
O Soma, those exploits of yours, O lord of abundant wealth who flowst purified, are truly victorious — increase the ocean that is worthy of praise.
Winning all riches, flow purified, O Soma, with your stream; drive away hatreds utterly.

title: Rigveda
text:
Protect us well from the evil spirit, from the noise of every (foe), from reproach wherever we may be released.
O indu, flow purified with your stream (bringing us) earthly and heavenly wealth; bring the resplendent vigour.
The streams of this vigorous one have flowed freely through the filter; flowing purified, he sends forth the sacred word.
The indu, urged forward by the pressers, being wiped clean, cries out — he stirs up the divine power of Indra.
Flow purified, O Soma, with your stream, bringing us vigour that conquers men, filled with heroes, greatly desired.
Soma Pavamāna has gushed forth, overflowing with his stream; he has settled into the wooden troughs.
In the waters they urge you forward with the pressing-stones, O most honey-sweet tawny one, O indu, for Indra to drink.
Press out the most honey-sweet Soma for Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt — the lovely, exhilarating one for his divine host.
The Soma juices, self-bright and purifying, have flowed forth; they create wealth endowed with consciousness.
Be, O Indu, above heaven and earth, increaser of splendour; be the lord of nourishing powers.
To you, O Soma, the winds blow most dear; to you the rivers stream; they increase your greatness.
Swell forth; let your virile power come together to you from all sides, O Soma; be present at the gathering of nourishment.
To you, O tawny one, the cows have milked butter and indestructible milk upon the highest ridge.
O Indu, lord of the world, you who are well-armed and ever-present — we desire your friendship.
The Soma juices, dripping with exhilaration, have flowed forth for our glory, for us the bountiful; the pressed drops have advanced to the assembly.
The maidens of Trita press the tawny one forward with the pressing-stones — the Indu for Indra to drink.
Like a swan upon the flock, he has filled all minds with desire; like a swift steed he is anointed with the milk-streams.

title: Rigveda
text:
You have illumined both worlds, O Soma; like a beast that has been sprinkled, you flow onward, settling into the womb of Ṛta.
The cows have lowed in response, as a young woman toward her beloved lover; they have reached the contest as if appointed.
Bestow upon us and upon the bountiful ones luminous glory, O Soma; bestow the winning of wisdom and of fame.
The wise Soma juices flow forward like waves of the waters, like buffaloes through forests.
The tawny, bright ones have streamed into the wooden vessels with the stream of Ṛta, carrying nourishment rich in cattle.
The pressed Soma juices flow for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts, and for Viṣṇu.
Three voices arise; the cows low, the milch-cows cry; the tawny Soma comes roaring along.
The sacred prayer-streams have sounded in answer, the mighty mothers of Ṛta; they cleanse the child of heaven.
Purify for us, O Soma, from every side the four oceans of wealth, thousandfold.
Pressed and urged forward, the Indu streams along with a continuous flow, breaking through firm obstacles with his might.
Pressed out, Soma streams for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts, and for Viṣṇu.
They press the Soma, the vigorous bull yoked with bull-like stones; with skillful effort they milk forth the milk.
He becomes the cleanser of Trita; he becomes the exhilarating drink for Indra; the tawny one is anointed with his bright forms.
The speckled mothers milk for him the summit of Ṛta — the dear and most beloved oblation.
These faultless hymns flow together toward him as he streams along; the roaring one has called out to the milk-cows.
Purify for us, O Pavamāna, with a stream of abundant wealth, whereby you would reveal light to us.
O Indu, set the ocean in motion; flow onward, shaker of all things, sustainer of riches for us by your might.

title: Rigveda
text:
With you as our hero, O heroic one, may we overcome those who attack us; flow toward us what is desirable.
The Indu, the inspired sage desiring to win nourishment, sends forward the prize — knowing the sacred ordinances and his weapons.
Him who sets speech in motion, we clothe with hymns as he purifies himself — Soma, the lord of the people's cattle.
All people have steadied themselves in the sacred vow of him who is the lord of Dharma, of him who purifies himself, the lord of abundant wealth.
He has been released like a racehorse; pressed out, he enters the filter of the two bowls; the prize-winning steed has stepped down upon the field.
You, O Soma, the ever-wakeful carrier, flow onward, most heroic among the gods, toward the vessel that drips with sweetness.
O Pavamāna, you the primeval one, illuminate the lights for us; impel us toward wisdom and discernment.
Adorning himself with those who live by Ṛta, being cleansed by the hands, he purifies himself in the imperishable wool-filter.
Let that Soma purify all heavenly, earthly, and atmospheric riches for the worshipper.
Desiring horses, desiring cattle, O Soma, desiring heroes — you ascend to the back of heaven, O lord of might.
This Soma, pressed and bull-like, streams through the filter for drinking, smiting the demons, eager for the gods.
The far-seeing tawny one, the steady one, streams through the filter, roaring toward his birthplace.
The prize-winning Pavamāna runs through the luminous realms of heaven, the slayer of demons, through the imperishable woolen strainer.
Purifying himself upon the ridge of Trita's realm, he illumined the sun together with his kinsmen.
That pressed, bull-like, unfailing Soma, slayer of Vṛtra, the finder of wide space, has rushed forward as if to win the prize.
That divine one, urged by the sage, runs toward the wooden vessels; the Indu flows toward Indra with his bounty.

title: Rigveda
text:
This indeed is that bull-like chariot which streams with the sheep's-wool strands, going to win the thousandfold prize.
The maidens of Trita urge this tawny one forward with the pressing-stones — the Indu for Indra to drink.
The ten tawny mares, eager for action, cleanse him — those by whom he shines for the exhilaration.
This one settles among human settlements like a falcon, going like a lover toward a woman.
This intoxicating juice, the child of heaven, gazes down, this Indu who has entered the woolen filter.
This pressed tawny one, the steady one, streams for drinking, calling out toward his dear birthplace.
Flow swiftly, O Soma, for him of great wisdom, around with your dear abode — where the gods declare you to be.
Adorning what is unadorned, dispensing refreshments to the people, flow around as the rain of heaven.
The pressed one moves through the filter, bearing brilliance with his might, all-seeing and illumining.
This is he who, swift of course, has flowed out through the filter from the heavens, like a wave of a river.
Shining forth from what is far away and also from what is near, the pressed one — the sweet drink is poured for Indra.
Those who face together have sounded in response; they urge the tawny one forward with the pressing-stones; settle in the womb of Ṛta.
Purifying himself, the all-beholding one has advanced against all enemies; with their sacred thoughts they adorn the inspired sage.
The ruddy, bull-like, pressed Soma mounts the birthplace; he goes to Indra; he settles in the firm abode.
Now, O Indu, O Soma, purify for us from every side a great and thousandfold wealth.
O Soma Pavamāna, O Indu, bring to us all glories; bring thousandfold refreshments.
Do you, as you purify yourself, bring to us wealth rich in valiant men for the singer; increase the hymns of the praiser.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indu, as you purify yourself, O Soma, bring us doubly-great wealth; O bull, O Indu, bring us what is worthy of praise.
They who, like impetuous cattle, have boldly stridden forth — the fierce, eager ones — smiting off the dark skin.
We meditate upon prosperous welfare, overcoming the hard-to-cross barrier, overpowering the Dasyu who observes no sacred rites.
The roar of the vigorous Pavamāna is heard like the sound of rain; the lightnings move about in the sky.
Flow in, purifying thyself, with great refreshment, O Indu — refreshment rich in cattle, rich in gold, rich in horses, rich in food, thou the pressed one.
Purify thyself, all-beholding one; fill the two great worlds — as Uṣas, as the Sun with rays.
Flow around us on all sides, O Soma, with a sheltering stream — even as a swiftly running juice flows through the firmament.
Generating the bright spaces of heaven, generating the Sun within the waters, the tawny one clothing himself with the cows and the waters.
This god, pressed out, purifies himself with a stream surpassing the other gods, with the ancient hymn of praise.
For him who is ever waxing strong, for the swift one, for the winning of prizes, the Somas of thousandfold splendour flow, purifying themselves.
Milking out the ancient milk, he pours himself around the filter; roaring, he has given birth to the gods.
Soma, self-purifying, flows toward all desirable things, toward the gods who magnify the sacred order.
Purify thyself, O Soma, pressed out with refreshment rich in cattle, rich in heroes, rich in horses, rich in food — with abundant refreshments.
Him who is polished with cows like a steed for exhilaration — the beloved one — we clothe with hymns.
All our songs, eager for favour, adorn him as of old — the drop, for Indra to drink.
The beloved Soma moves, self-purifying, adorned by the hymns of the inspired sage, of Medhyātithi.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Pavamāna, grant us wealth — beautiful wealth, O Soma, O Indu — of thousandfold brilliance.
The drop, like a prize-winning steed, neighing, pours itself through the filter — the pious one flowing out beyond.
Purify thyself for the winning of prizes, for the growth of the inspired singer who praises thee; O Soma, bestow heroic strength.
For us, O Indu, thou flowest forth bearing a wave toward the great web; thou, the eager one, strivest toward the gods.
Soma the seer, pleasing to the mind, directed by thought, is urged on from afar — with the stream of the inspired sage.
This watchful one, pressed out, goes into the filter; Soma, the all-beholding, moves onward among the gods.
Purify thyself for us, eager for food, fashioning the lovely sacrifice; thou seekest to illuminate the one who is rich in sacred grass.
Let that ever-growing Soma, whose heroes are inspired sages, reach to us among the gods for Bhaga and for Vāyu.
He who knows the will, who knows the way most excellently — do thou today, for our obtaining of wealth, win for us food and great glory.
Purify thyself, O soma drop, for gladdening delight — thou who seest mankind — for the enjoyment of the gods, for Indra to drink.
Flow toward us on thy embassy to Indra for his satisfaction; bring the best gift from the gods to thy friends.
And we anoint thee, the ruddy one, with cows for gladdening delight; throw open wide for us the doors to wealth.
The prize-winner has stepped forth beyond the filter like a chariot-horse on the march; the drop holds sway among the gods.
The friends together have sung aloud — the drop that plays in the wood like an unruly ram; they have praised Indu with their boat-song.
Purify thyself with that stream by which, when drunk, thou art seen in thy glory; O Indu, bring heroic strength to the singer.

title: Rigveda
text:
They have rushed forth for the enjoyment of the gods — like strong ones performing their task — flowing, strengthened by the mountain-stones.
The Indu-drops, adorned, like a maiden following her father, the Somas have been sent forth toward Vāyu.
These Soma-drops, these Indus, pressed out in the two bowls, full of refreshment, magnify Indra by their deeds.
O ye of skilful hands, run hither; seize the bright ones with the stirring-stick; blend the exhilarating juice with cows' milk.
Purify thyself, O conqueror of wealth, directing great bounty toward us; O Soma, knowing the path.
The ten fingers polish this worthy one, the self-purifying Pavamāna — the exhilarating intoxicant for Indra.
By this right action, Soma has grown great even beyond the great; gladdened, he roars like a bull.
His deeds accomplished, ready to be done, his Dasyu-smiting powers are awakened; the bold one metes out debts in recompense.
So Soma, the invigorating essence, becomes a thousandfold-conquering thunderbolt when his praise-hymn is born.
The seer himself, among those who dispense, seeks a gem for the inspired man — when the thoughts are polished well.
Thou art one who desires to win riches — as horses in contests of speed; thou art the victor in the battles of givers.
Thee — bearing manly powers, lovely, in the dwelling-places of the great heaven — we call upon with right action.
The bold one who draws all to himself, worthy of praise-hymns, the exhilarating rapture whose great vow is mighty — him who desires to break a hundred citadels.
From yonder place, the well-winged one, undisturbed, O Sukratu, has brought thee — the king of heaven — bringing wealth.
The hero has brought the guardian of the sacred order — the light of the sun, common to all to behold, swiftly passing through the region of the air.

title: Rigveda
text:
Then, urging on the Indra-faculty, he has attained to a greatness that is still greater; the all-beholding one who creates conquest.
Purify thyself, bringing rain for us, the wave of the waters from around heaven — bringing great refreshments free of disease.
Purify thyself with that stream by which the cattle have come hither — the kindred ones near to our house.
Flow with a stream of ghee, thou most beloved of the gods at sacrifices; purify thyself bringing rain to us.
For our strength, run through the imperishable filter with thy stream — for the gods shall surely hear.
Pavamāna has settled himself; he has kicked away the demons; he illumines his lights as of old.
Thy vigours rise up like the sound of a wave of the river; urge forward the rim of the wheel of the lute-player.
At thy impulse, the three spirited voices rise up — when thou goest to the sheepskin ridges of the straining-cloth.
On the woollen filter, with the pressing-stones, they urge on the beloved tawny one — the self-purifying Pavamāna who drips with sweetness.
Flow into the filter with thy stream, O most exhilarating one, O Seer; take thy seat in the womb of the hymn.
Purify thyself, O most exhilarating one, anointed with cows and with rays of light, O drop, for Indra to drink.
O Adhvaryu, release into the filter the Soma pressed with the stones; purify it for Indra to drink.
Press out the supreme elixir of heaven, this most honey-sweet Soma, for Indra the wielder of the vajra.
O Indu, the gods partake of that sweet drink of yours, of the sweet juice of you who flow in purification — the Maruts do so.
For you, O Soma, when pressed, invigorating, pour yourself for the exhilaration of the vehement one; O bull, be the aid of the singer of praise.
Flow onward, O all-discerning one, pressed, with a stream through the filter; flow onward toward strength and toward glory.

title: Rigveda
text:
May the heaven-dwelling bestower of wealth, through his inebriating liquor, bring us strength; pressed out, flow into the filter.
By the ancient paths of yours, beloved, through the sheep's-wool filter, may he of a thousand streams pass along in full body.
O Indu, like a cauldron rock it — rock that generous gift; rock it with your weapons, O bearer of weapons.
Press down, O Indu, the vigor of these peoples, O much-invoked one — of him who attacks us.
O Indu, flow in purification for us with a hundred aids — or a thousand — of the bright ones, O lavish bestower of riches.
Your powers have risen up, O stone-crusher, shattering the Rākṣasas; drive away those who are rivals.
This one has struck down with might at the chariot-encounter when the prize is at stake, to be praised with a fearless heart.
The sacred ordinances of this flowing Soma are not to be defied, not easily broken; break the one who contends against you.
They urge him on — the tawny one that sheds exhilaration, the prize-winning Indu flowing through the rivers — for Indra, the enrapturing one.
Following the ancient brightness of this one, the unfailing ones have milked out his bright milk — the seer who wins a thousand.
This one, like the sun, is visible all around; this one runs through the lakes, along the seven downward slopes to heaven.
This one, while flowing in purification, stands over all beings — Soma, the god, like the sun.
O Indu, flowing in purification, you course around us with cattle-rich prizes for the delight of the gods, O you who are eager for Indra.
O Soma, pour around us with your inebriating liquor — more and more nourishment, more and more abundance — and all good fortunes.
O Indu, according as your praise song rises, according as your inebriating juice has flowed forth — take your seat on the dear sacred grass.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Soma, flow in purification with your inebriating liquor, knowing where the cattle are and knowing where the horses are, with the swiftest days.
He who conquers and is not conquered, who slays the enemy fearlessly — flow in purification as the winner of thousands.
Soma, swift and eager for the gods, flows around the great Ṛta in the filter, smashing the Rākṣasas.
When Soma flows for the prize, his hundred streams are active, entering into friendship with Indra.
The ten maidens have cried out to you as to a lover, as young women do; you are polished, O Soma, for winning the prize.
O sweet Indu, flow around for Indra and for Viṣṇu; protect the men, the singers of praise, from distress.
Your unceasing streams flow onward like the rains from heaven, toward the thousand-fold prize.
Viewing all the beloved poetic powers, the tawny one flows on, thrusting forward his weapons.
He, being polished by the living beings, like a mighty king of good vows, settles like a falcon at the resting-place.
O Indu, flowing in purification, bring us all treasures from heaven and from upon the earth.
Swiftly he runs, that exhilarating one — the stream of the pressed inebriating juice; swiftly he runs, that exhilarating one.
He knows the morning cattle of treasures, the divine aid for mortal man; swiftly he runs, that exhilarating one.
From the two dusty, far-reaching ones we receive thousands; swiftly he runs, that exhilarating one.
From those two we receive by lineage thirty and also thousands; swiftly he runs, that exhilarating one.
Flow in purification, O Soma — winner of cattle, winner of horses, winner of all, winner in battle; bring a jewel together with offspring.
Flow in purification among the waters, O inviolable one; flow in purification among the plants; flow in purification among the divine intelligences.

title: Rigveda
text:
You, O Soma Pavamāna, cross over all difficulties; O seer, take your seat upon the sacred grass.
O Pavamāna, knower of the sun-realm, as you were born you became great; O Indu, you have prevailed over all.
Sing forth in the Gāyatrī meter — Pavamāna the all-surveying, Indu of a thousand eyes.
You, the thousand-eyed one, and moreover the one bearing a thousandfold — they have purified you through the filter.
Flowing in purification, having dripped through the filters, he runs toward the jars, entering into the heart of Indra.
O Soma, O all-surveying one, flow in purification auspiciously for Indra's bounty; bring seed together with offspring.
Flow around with this enjoyment, O Indu, who in thy raptures hast slain ninety-nine foes.
Forthwith, for Divodāsa who reflects even thus, thou didst smite Śambara; and Turvaśa, and Yadu.
Flow around us, O Indu, thou who knowest horses, with nourishment rich in kine, in gold, in steeds, thousandfold.
We choose the friendship of thee, Pavamāna, whose filter is sprinkled all about.
With those waves of thine, O Soma, that flow over the filter in a stream, be gracious unto us.
Do thou, purifying thyself, O Soma, bring to us wealth rich in hero-sons and food, thou who art lord of all.
Ten fingers cleanse this very Soma, the river-born, who has been viewed together with the Ādityas.
Pressed, he flows through the filter together with Indra, together with Vāyu, together with the rays of the Sun.
Flow for us, O sweet one, lovely for Bhaga, for Vāyu, for Pūṣan, for Mitra and Varuṇa.
The exalted birth of thy exhilarating juice is placed on high in heaven and on earth — mighty shelter, great glory.
Through this, O noble one, desiring to win all the glories of mankind, we praise thee.
Flow around, for us, for worshipful Indra, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts — thou who knowest wide space.

title: Rigveda
text:
The gods have come near to this Indu, the swift-moving one newly born, adorned and decked with cows.
May our hymns strengthen him — as mother cows lowing around their calf — him who gladdens Indra's heart.
Flow to us, O Soma, blissful for the cow; milk out for us fattening nourishment; increase the hymn-worthy ocean.
Pavamāna has generated the great Vaiśvānara light, wondrous like the thunder of heaven.
Thy juice, the exhilaration of thee Pavamāna, O King, unerring, flows forth through the woollen filter.
O Pavamāna, thy vigorous juice shines brilliantly — the universal light, the sun, to be seen.
With that excellent rapture of thine, O Soma, flow through thy juice, a friend to the gods, a slayer of the wicked.
Thou art the slayer of the hostile Vṛtra, the winner of prizes day after day; thou art the finder of cows and horses.
Be thou commingled, O tawny one, like cows with fair udders, sitting down like a hawk into the vessel.
Do thou flow pure, thou who hast aided Indra to slay Vṛtra who had covered the great waters.
Provided with good heroes, may we win wealth, O liberal Soma; purifying thyself, magnify our hymns.
May we, who gain under thy protection and shelter, be active and eager; O Soma, be wakeful in thy rites.
Soma flows, smiting away enemies, driving off the niggardly, going to Indra's place of purification.
Bring us great riches, O Pavamāna; smite our foes; O Indu, grant us glory rich in hero-sons.
Not even a hundred deceivers can obstruct the bounty thou willest to bestow, when purifying thyself thou art bountiful.
Flow pure, O Indu, pressed and virile; make us glorious among men; smite away all enemies.
In thy friendship, O Indu, in thy supreme splendour, may we overcome those who fight against us.
Thy terrible, sharp weapons that are for the harm of the oppressor — guard us with them wholly from those who blame us.

title: Rigveda
text:
These swift Indu-drops have been poured forth through the filter, going toward all prosperities.
Clearing away many evils, opening easy paths, the vigorous drops create good progeny for offspring and the coursing steed.
Making wide space for the cow, they flow toward excellent praise and toward Iḻā assembled together for us.
The stalk has been pressed for exhilaration; his vigour dwelling in the mountains and the waters — like a hawk he has settled in his seat.
The bright food, desired by the gods, purified in the waters, pressed by men — the cows make it savory with their milk.
Then, like those who urge a horse, they have adorned him for immortality, the juice of the sweet drink at the common festival.
Those honey-dripping streams of thine, O Indu, that have been poured forth for our help — with them thou hast settled on the filter.
He flows for Indra to drink, through the undying woollen hairs, settling into his vessel in the wood.
Do thou, O Indu, flow around, most sweet for the Aṅgirases, thou who knowest wide space — milk and ghee.
This Pavamāna, the all-seeing, placed here, grows wise; urged on, he impels the great watery ocean.
This vigorous Pavamāna, of vigorous vows, the destroyer of revilers, shall bestow riches on the worshipper.
Flow to us with thousandfold wealth, with cattle, with horses, with many splendours, much longed for.
This one is poured around, being well-cleansed by the living ones — far-ranging, of sage-wisdom.
He of a thousand streams, of a hundredfold gifts, the measurer of the firmament, the sage — this exhilaration flows for Indra.
Indu, born by the hymn, here praised, is placed for Indra — he fills the vessel as it were a dwelling-place.
Pavamāna Soma, pressed out by men, has run forth like a prize-winner, seating himself by his power in the bowls.

title: Rigveda
text:
They yoke him to travel in the triple-backed, triple-fellied chariot, with the seven thoughts of the seers.
Speed him, the pressers, the touch-prize swift one, the tawny vigorous one, for travel and for the prize.
Entering the vessel when pressed, flowing around all glories, he stands like a hero among the cows.
For thy exhilaration, O Indu, the living ones milk out the milk; the gods bring sweetness for the gods.
Release Soma into the filter for us, most honey-sweet, most renowned among the gods for the gods.
These Somas have been poured forth, praised with the stream of him most exhilarating, for great glory.
Toward the cow-wealth for enjoyment, toward manly powers, thou purifiest thyself and flowest; O ever-prize-winner, flow around.
And flow to us with all nourishments rich in cows, with sounds everywhere resounding, praised by Jamadagni.
Flow pure, O Soma, foremost of utterances, with variegated aids, encompassing all poetic wisdom.
Thou foremost of the oceanic waters, stirring the hymns, flow purified, O mover of the universe.
These worlds, O sage Soma, stand for thy greatness; toward thee flow the rivers.
Thy streams go forth unceasing like rains from heaven, over the bright strewn grass.
Purify for Indra this fierce Indu, the instrument of the mighty one, the lord, the bestower of boons.
Pavamāna, the true, the sage, Soma, has settled on the filter, bestowing heroic might upon the praiser.
Flow to us, O Soma, with thousandfold wealth and heroic strength; pour upon us glories.
Thou dost swell with food and vigour, most exhilarating for Indra; thou sittest down in the bowls.
Soma, pressed out for Indra, for Viṣṇu, flows into the vessel; may he be sweet for Vāyu.
These swift tawny Soma-drops have been poured, crossing over the crooked places by the stream of truth.

title: Rigveda
text:
They who increase Indra, the swift-moving ones, making all things noble, smiting away the niggardly.
The tawny Indus, pressed out, flowing toward their own domain, the drops of Soma go to Indra.
Flow with that stream by which thou didst make the sun to shine, urging on the human waters.
Pavamāna yoked the dapple steed upon Manu, to travel through the atmosphere.
Indu yoked also those ten tawny mares of the sun to travel, saying 'Indra'.
Pour around the pressed, exhilarating juice with hymns for Vāyu and Indra into the woollen strainers.
O Pavamāna Soma, find for us the irresistible wealth — that which is not to be consumed by the assailant.
Flow toward thousandfold wealth with cattle, with horses, toward the prize and glory.
Soma the god, like the sun, is purified by the stones when pressed, holding his juice in the vessel.
These bright, noble abodes have flowed with the stream of truth toward the prize rich in cattle.
Soma-drops pressed for Indra the thunderer, mixed with curd, have flowed beyond the filter.
Flow forth, O Soma most honey-sweet, through the filter toward wealth, O exhilaration most beloved by the gods.
The living ones cleanse him, the tawny prize-winning Indu, in the streams, the exhilarant for Indra.
Flow purified, O Soma, with gold, with horses, with heroes; bring us the prize rich in kine.
As one who wins prizes, pour the most honey-sweet one into the woollen strainers for Indra, around the prize.
The wise, seeking help, cleanse the sage, the one worthy of cleansing, with their thoughts; the vigorous one flows bellowing.
The inspired sages have sung together with thoughts and the stream of truth about the vigorous, swift-moving Soma.
Flow purified, O god-life-prolonger; let thy exhilaration go to Indra; mount upon Vāyu according to thy ordinance.
O Pavamāna Soma, thou dost pour out wealth worthy of renown; beloved, enter the ocean.

title: Rigveda
text:
Flowing, thou smitest enemies, O Soma the exhilarant who knowest purpose; push away the godless folk.
The Pavamāna Soma-drops, bright Indus, have been poured forth encompassing all poetic wisdom.
The swift, bright Pavamāna Indus have been poured forth, smiting away all adversaries.
The Pavamānas have been poured from heaven, from the atmosphere, from above the earth upon the ridge.
Purifying thyself, O Soma, with thy stream, O Indu, drive away all failures; slay the demons, O excellent in purpose.
Smiting the demons, O Soma, flow forth bellowing, with thy loftiest brilliant vigour.
Pour upon us riches heavenly and earthly, O Soma, O Indu — all desirable things.
Thou art a vigorous bull, O Soma, full of brilliance; O god, a bull of virile vows; a bull thou holdest thy ordinances.
Thy virile strength is the strength of a bull; virile is thy love, virile thy exhilaration — truly, O bull, thou art a bull indeed.
Like a neighing stallion, O vigorous Indu, join the cows to us, join the steeds; open wide the doors of wealth for us.
The vigorous, bright, swift Soma-drops have been poured forth striving for cattle and horses and heroes.
Adorning themselves, being cleansed by the life-giving forces of truth by the hands of men, they flow through the undying woollen filter.
May those Somas — heavenly, earthly, and atmospheric — flow purified bringing all wealth to the worshipper.
O all-knowing Pavamāna, thy streams have been poured forth like the rays of the sun.
Making a banner over the sky, thou flowest around all forms; O Soma, thou swellest as the ocean.
Being urged on, thou impellest the hymn, O Pavamāna, in the course of thy ordinance; like the sun-god thou hast stepped forth.
Indu, the wise, beloved of sages, has entered the filter, releasing the steed with his thought like a charioteer.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thy wave which, dear to gods, flows around through the filter, settling into the womb of truth.
Let that exhilaration, most beloved by the gods, flow to us through the filter, O Indu, for Indra to drink.
Flow for nourishment, O Indu, with thy stream, being cleansed by the wise; go with thy radiances to the cows.
Purifying thyself, O lover of song, create wide space and vigour for the people; O tawny one, releasing the mixed drink.
Purifying thyself for the delight of gods, go to Indra's place of purification, flashing with thy prize-winning steeds.
The swift Indus, being urged forward, sped toward the ocean, impelled by thought, poured forth.
The Indus, being well cleansed by the living ones, have freely gone to the ocean, entered the womb of truth.
Go around us, O thou who desirest us, with all riches by thy might; protect us with shelter rich in heroes.
The carrier-steed lows, as one who yokes himself with singers, when Soma is poured into the ocean.
When the swift one settles into the golden womb of truth, he abandons the unwise.
The wise ones, the discerning, follow the streams and sing beside them; the foolish are submerged.
O Indu, flow purified, most honey-sweet, for Indra with his Marut-host; settle in the womb of truth.
The inspired, wise, sapient ones adorn thee on all sides; the living ones cleanse thee together.
O sage, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, and the Maruts drink the juice of thee the Pavamāna.
Thou, O Soma, O Indu, purifying thyself, dost impel the wise speech of thousandfold bounty.
And bring to us, O Soma, O Indu, purifying thyself, the speech of thousandfold bounty, eager for sacrifice.
Purifying thyself, O Indu, beloved of these widely invoked peoples, enter the ocean.
With flashing, all-resounding radiance and with grace, the bright Soma-drops, blended with milk, shine forth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Urged on, guided by the urgers, the vigorous prize-winner has stepped toward the prize, the drops settling like eager ones.
O Soma, flowing separately for well-being, the sage who comes together from heaven, flow purified to be seen as the sun.
The dawn-rays, like sisters of the same kin, urge on the great Indu, their lord, the mighty ones delighting in greatness.
O Pavamāna, with brilliance upon brilliance, O god, enter all riches from the gods.
O Pavamāna, bring us excellent praise, service to the gods, rain; flow purified, concentrated, for nourishment.
For thou art a vigorous bull with thy radiance; thee the brilliant one we invoke, O Pavamāna, excellent in thought.
Flow purified with heroic strength, rejoicing, O thou whose weapons are good; come here, O Indu, come.
When thou art sprinkled around with the waters, being cleansed by the hands, thou attainest the common seat in the wood.
Sing forth to Pavamāna Soma, like Vyaśva, to the great one of a thousand eyes.
They urge on with the stones the honey-dripping, tawny Indu whose colour gleams, for Indra to drink.
We, having won all the riches of thee the vigorous prize-winner, choose thy friendship.
Flow purified, O vigorous bull, with thy stream, O exhilarant, for him with his Maruts, bearing all things with strength.
I urge thee on, O Pavamāna, the sustainer of the well, the beholder of heaven, the prize-winning one in the contests.
With this flowing, wise stream, O tawny one, flow purified; urge on the yoke-fellow in the prizes.
Flow to us, O Indu, with great nourishment, thou the all-beautiful; O Soma, thou who knowest the way to us.
The vessels have resounded, O Indu; with thy streams and strength, enter for Indra to drink.
He whose pungent, exhilarating juice they milk out with the stones — flow pure, thou destroyer of assailants.

title: Rigveda
text:
The King Pavamāna travels with his wisdom upon Manu, to journey through the atmosphere.
Bring to us, O Indu, the prosperity of a hundred cows, the possession of good horses; bring good fortune as an aid.
Bring to us, O Soma, pressed out for the delight of gods, strength and swiftness as form for brightness.
Flow, O Soma, most brilliant, roaring over the troughs, settling like a hawk into thy vessel.
Soma flows swiftly for Indra, for Vāyu, for Varuṇa, for the Maruts, for Viṣṇu.
Bestowing nourishment on our offspring, O Soma, from all sides, flow purified, thousandfold.
Those Soma-drops that are pressed in the distant region, those pressed in the near region, those pressed at the Śaryaṇāvat lake —
Those among the Ārjīkas, among the active ones, those in the midst of the homesteads, or those among the five peoples —
May those Indu-drops, the divine, when pressed, flow purified for us with rain from heaven and with heroic strength.
The lovely tawny one flows purified, praised by Jamadagni, being urged on upon the cow's skin.
The bright, life-giving drops, urged on like steeds, being mingled, cleanse themselves in the waters.
The powers present in the pressed draughts urge thee on for the service of the gods; flow purified with this radiance.
Today we choose thy power that brings happiness, the carrier that is guarded, the much-longed-for one.
The joyful, the excellent, the inspired, the wise, the guarded, the much-longed-for one we choose.
Wealth, clear consciousness, O excellent in purpose, within our own persons — the guarded, much-longed-for one we choose.
Flow purified, O thou who art seen by all, encompassing all poetic wisdom; thou art a friend to be praised by friends.
By those two dwelling-places of thine that stand facing, O Pavamāna, O Soma, thou reignest over the universe.

title: Rigveda
text:
Around thy dwelling-places, O Soma thou art from all sides, O Pavamāna, O sage, with the seasons.
Flow purified, generating nourishments, encompassing all desirable things; be a friend to friends as an aid.
Thy bright rays spread the filter on the back of heaven, O Soma, with thy dwelling-places.
These seven rivers flow at thy command, O Soma; the milch-cows run to thee.
Go forth, O Soma, with thy stream, pressed and exhilarating for Indra, bearing imperishable glory.
The seven sister-streams have rung out together for thee with thoughts that urge thee, the inspired one born of Vivasvat.
The assembled ones cleanse thee together on the swift woollen strainer as thou art rubbed in the wood, O singer.
O sage, O prize-winner Pavamāna, thy currents have been poured, like steeds eager for glory.
Toward the honey-dripping vessel the prayers have bellowed out; the drops were poured into the undying woollen filter.
Toward the ocean the Indu-drops, like milch-cows going home, have entered the womb of truth.
For us, O Indu, in the great exhilaration, the waters flow like rivers when thou wilt clothe thyself with the rays of cattle.
We, longing to serve in this thy friendship, aided by thee, O Indu, desire thy companionship.
Flow purified for the winning of cattle, O great Soma, O thou seen by heroes; enter the belly of Indra.
Thou art great, O Soma, foremost among the mighty, O Indu, the most powerful; being a fighter thou hast conquered ever and again.
He who is mightier even than the mighty, more heroic even than heroes, more bountiful even than the greatly giving.
Thou, O Soma, art that sun for winning progeny and persons; we choose thee for friendship, we choose thee for fellowship.
O Agni, flowing pure, bestow upon us lives and vigour and nourishment; repel misfortune far from us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni is the seer, Pavamāna, the household priest of the five peoples; we implore him who grants great wealth.
O Agni, flow purified, O excellent worker; bestow upon us brightness and heroic strength, placing wealth and prosperity in me.
Pavamāna flows over all foes toward excellent praise, like the sun, beautiful to all.
He, the Indu, being well-cleansed by the living ones, lavish of oblations, devoted to offering, the swift, the clear-sighted.
Pavamāna has generated the great truth, the bright light; he has struck down the black darknesses.
From Pavamāna the striking tawny one, brilliant swift streams have been poured, gleaming with swift radiance.
Pavamāna is the best charioteer, most beautifully praised by the bright ones, tawny and brilliant, having the Marut hosts.
Pavamāna has pervaded with his rays, most winning of prizes, bestowing heroic might upon the praiser.
The pressed Indu, the axle, has flowed beyond the undying filter; Indu, purifying himself, goes to Indra.
This Soma sports upon the skin of the cows with the stones, calling upon Indra for exhilaration.
With that bright milk of thine, O Pavamāna, brought from heaven, be gracious to us that we may live.
Thou, O Soma, art the sustainer, joyful, most mighty at the sacrifice; flow purified, thou who givest wealth freely.
Thou, pressed out, gladdening men, most swift-running, most exhilarating, art the wise one for Indra with thy food.
Thou, well-pressed by the stones, flow forth bellowing with thy loftiest brilliant vigour.
Indu, being urged on, flows through the undying woollen strainers; the tawny one has bellowed for the prize.
O Indu, thou flowest through the wool, through glories, through prosperities; O Soma, through prizes rich in cattle.
Bring to us, O Indu, O Soma, wealth of a hundred kinds rich in kine and horses, thousandfold.

title: Rigveda
text:
The swift Pavamāna Indus, through the filter, have reached Indra with their courses.
The eminent Soma-juice, Indu the ancient, flows purified for Indra; life flows for the living.
The dawn-rays urge on the honey-dripping Pavamāna; they have sung together with their hymn.
May Pūṣan, the protector with his goat-team, at every journey, partake of the Soma-drink among our maidens.
This Soma flows like ghee, sweet, for Rudra with his braided hair; may he partake among our maidens.
This pressed juice of thine, O radiant one, flows purified like ghee; may he partake among our maidens.
Thou art the source of the utterances of the seers; flow, O Soma, with thy stream; among the gods thou art the bestower of treasure.
He runs into the vessels, like a hawk cleaving through the armour, bellowing over the troughs.
Around and forth thy juice, O Soma, pressed out, has been released into the vessel; like a hawk that is rubbed clean, he flows.
Flow purified, O Soma, gladdening, most honey-sweet, for Indra.
They have been poured for the delight of gods, striving for prizes like chariots.
Those pressed drops, most exhilarating, bright, have been poured for Vāyu.
Struck by the pressing-stone, praised on all sides, O Soma, thou goest to the filter, bestowing heroic might upon the praiser.
This one, struck and praised on all sides, plunges through the filter, the demon-slayer through the undying woollen strainer.
Whatever fear finds me here, whether near or far, O Pavamāna, strike that away.
May that Pavamāna, the all-seeing, today purify us with the filter; he who is the Potṛ-priest, may he purify us.
With that filter of thine, O Agni, which is spread within thy flame, with that brahman-prayer purify us.
With that filter of thine, O Agni, that is bright as flame, purify us; with thy sacred stimulations purify us.

title: Rigveda
text:
O god Savitṛ, with both the filter and the divine impulse, purify me on all sides.
O god Savitṛ, purify us with thy three highest Soma-dwelling-places; O Agni, purify us with thy powers.
May the divine folk purify me; may the Vasus purify me with thought; O all ye gods, purify me; O Jātavedas, purify me.
Swell forth, flow forth, O Soma, with all thy shoots; thou art the highest oblation for the gods.
We have come to the dear, glittering youth who grows great with oblations, bearing him reverence.
The axe of the Alāyya has perished — cleanse away that, O divine Soma; even the rat's mischief, O divine Soma.
Whoever reads through the Pāvamānī hymns — the juice assembled by the seers — all of it he eats purified and made savory by Mātariśvan.
Whoever reads through the Pāvamānī hymns — the juice assembled by the seers — for him Sarasvatī milks out milk, clarified butter, and honeyed water.
Toward the god, the honey-laden Indu-drops have hissed forth; the cows have come to us like milch-cows; seated on the sacred grass, endowed with utterance, the dawn-cows have set in order the filtered stream with their udders as its lustrous garment.
He, bellowing, cried out over the former ones; mounting up, the tawny one sounding sweet loosens himself; moving around through the filter, covering vast extents, the god lays down the shaft-wounds and chooses the best.
He who measures out, though twin-born, the exhilaration when the two flow together, swelling with milk that grows together and is imperishable — he who knows widely the two great, boundless firmaments, striding forward, has taken up the imperishable vigour.
He, roaming between the two mothers, making the waters prize-winning, the wise one swells his track by his own power; the stalk adorned with grain, directed by men, reaches together with his own kindred and guards the head.

title: Rigveda
text:
With energy and thought the sage is born, the embryo of truth placed beyond the twins; though both being young, they first knew each other — the birth hidden in the secret place is not this one uplifted here.
The wise ones have recognised the form of the joyful one, when the falcon brought the food from afar; him they cleanse — the stalk that grows well in the rivers, that is eager and hymn-worthy, moving around.
The ten maidens cleanse thee, O Soma, pressed out, set in place by seers with their thoughts and insights, both with woollen strainers and with divine invocations; directed by men, thou shalt burst forth the prize for the winning.
The sacred utterances have sung beside Soma who moves around pervasively, well-seated and fitting to be borne — he who with his stream, his honey-sweet wave from heaven, the immortal one rich in wealth, sets the hymn in motion.
This Soma sets the whole firmament in motion from heaven, purifying himself, he settles in the vessels; pressed and cleansed with waters, cows, and stones, the Indu purifying himself shall find wide space and the beloved.
Even thus, O Soma, as thou art poured around, flow purified, bestowing most wonderful vigour upon us; without hostility may we invoke Heaven and Earth; O gods, bestow upon us wealth with heroic sons.
As an arrow is set to the bow, as a calf is loosed to the mother's udder, so thought is set in place; like a wide-flowing one it is milked when it comes at the beginning; in his rites Soma too is set in motion.
To it thought is mingled, the sweet drink is poured, the joyful, life-giving one is set in motion from within the seat; Pavamāna the continuous one, the honey-sweet drop like one who crushes the host, flows around the strainer.
He who seeks his bride flows purified over the skin of the sheep; the granddaughters of Aditi loosen themselves when truth is set in motion; the tawny worshipful one has strode forward; the exhilaration, contained and whetting his manly power, shines like a great bull.

title: Rigveda
text:
The bull lows; the milch-cows go toward him; the divine females of the god approach his place of purification; Soma has stepped over the white undying woollen strainer, wrapping himself around it like a garment being washed.
With his unspotted, gleaming garment, the immortal tawny one, displaying his lustrous robe, wraps himself around; the back of heaven, prepared as a strewing for his bright garment, is the misty bottom of the bowls.
Like rays of the sun, the exhilarating, well-running drops move in company about the stretched thread; the swift currents flow around it — without Indra, not a single ordinance is purified.
Like swift ones in the descent of a river, the exhilarations poured by the bull from the deep have entered their path; be there welfare for us in the dwelling of bipeds and quadrupeds; O Soma, may prizes and cultivated fields stand firm for us.
Flow to us with wealth, with gold, with horses, with cattle, with grain, with heroic strength; for you are indeed, O Soma, my fathers — the heads of heaven, come forth bestowing vigour.
These Pavamāna Soma-drops, when pressed, have gone like chariots toward Indra for the winning; they pass beyond the woollen filter, the tawny ones abandoning the covering go toward the rain.
O Indu, flow purified for great Indra, bountiful, blameless, devouring rivals; bring shining riches for the praiser; O gods, may Heaven and Earth protect us.
Thrice the seven milch-cows milked for him the true mixed drink in the primeval sky; he made the other four worlds beautiful as his lustrous garment when he grew great through the laws of truth.
He who begs for the beautiful immortality has split apart both heavens with his poetic power; he wraps himself around the sharpest waters with bounty — when they know the dwelling of the divine one by his fame.

title: Rigveda
text:
May his tokens be immortal, undeceivable, following along both births; with which they purify both manly power and the divine, and with their thoughts they have grasped the king thereafter.
Being cleansed by ten well-working ones, he runs forward, accompanying them among the middle mothers at the first station; he who has drunk of the beautiful immortality, the hero-seer, surveys both the wide expanses.
Being well-cleansed for Indra's power and for nourishment, he, placed in his seat, rejoices toward both ends of Heaven and Earth; the vigorous bull with his vigour drives away evil thoughts, directing them apart like a bowman driving forth his arrows.
He, the bright one, going without seeing his two mothers, roars as he goes like the sound of the Maruts; knowing the truth, what was at first the sunlit way, the one of excellent purpose has chosen it for his own glory.
The terrible bull roars with his strength, sharpening his two horns, the clear-sighted tawny one; Soma the well-made sits down in his seat — the cow-skin becomes his bright garment, the woollen fleece his lustrous vesture.
The pure one, purifying his spotless body, the tawny one has run down upon the ridge of the fleece; beloved by Mitra, Varuṇa, and Vāyu, the threefold sweet drink is made by the well-working ones.
Flow pure, O Soma, for the delight of gods, O vigorous bull; enter the soma-vessel that is the heart of Indra; before adversity presses upon us carry us across the evil; for the knower of the field declares the directions to him who asks.
Like a harnessed steed flow toward the prize, O Indu; flow purified into the belly of Indra; like a ship carry us across the flood, O knowing one; like a hero fighting, strike down those who blame us.
Forth to the right the mighty one is set free, going to the seat; the ever-wakeful one wards off the demons, the haters. The tawny one makes his couch upon the sky, upon the milk; he lays sacred prayer in the two bowls for adornment.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like a ploughman's team he goes forward bellowing; he strips away that dark color, his own. He casts off his fleece and goes to the father's pure realm; he adorns his body with the streaming robe of cleansing.
Pressed by the stones, he flows pure from the two arms; he shows his manly power, he trembles with inspired thought in the sky. He rejoices, he attains, he accomplishes with song; he purifies himself in the waters, he makes offering around about.
They pour him round about, that child of heaven, nurtured by the mountain, son of strength, the sweetness, the guardian of the mansion; in whom the cows, at the well-fed udder, anoint his first portion on his head with their abundant streams.
The ten sisters, in the lap of Aditi, have together harnessed him as a chariot from the two sides without flaw. He wins near, he reaches the secret place of the cow — that station which the inspired ones brought forth for him.
Like a falcon he approaches the golden womb, the dwelling made by wisdom, the divine seat. They set in motion the beloved one on the sacred grass with song; like a horse he comes to the gods — the one worthy of worship.
Forth, fully revealed, the tawny sage of heaven, the bull of triple ridges, has gone and won the cows. The impulse with a thousand paths, going forward beyond, shines bright over all the dawns like a chanting singer.
He makes his form dazzling — his hue, wherever he lay hidden, drives away the scorners when gathered. With his own power he goes through the waters to the divine folk; together he attains with good praise, together with the foremost cows.
Like a bull going round herds he has bellowed out; he has taken on the brilliances of the sun. The divine fair-winged one looks down upon the earth; Soma beholds all beings round about with wisdom.

title: Rigveda
text:
They cleanse the tawny one; like the ruddy one he is yoked; Soma is anointed in the jar together with the milch-cows. He raises his voice, he is urged by inspired thought — how beloved he is, the widely praised one, to some!
Together many inspired ones declare when they have milked Soma into the belly of Indra. When skilled-handed men cleanse the desirable honey with the ten that share one nest.
Not lingering, he goes beyond toward the cows, across the cry of the dear daughter of the sun. The Vinaṅgṛsa brought favor along to him; he dwells together with the sisters, the paired kindred ones.
Shaken by men, pressed by stones, beloved on the sacred grass, the lord of the cows, from of old, the drop, moving in season, rich in plenteousness, accomplishing the sacrifice of Manu — O Soma, pure by inspiration, you flow, O Indra, for you.
Urged by the arms of men, poured out in a stream, O Soma, you flow for Indra in proper order, O Indra, for you. You have filled the rites; together with the unslain ones at the ceremony, the tawny one with inspired thoughts has settled, like a bird, upon the two bowls.
The inspired, active seers milk the roaring, inexhaustible, wise stalk. Together the inspired thoughts and the cows go, harnessed, in the birthplace of Truth, returning again to their seat.
The foundation of the earth, the support of the great sky, sprinkled within the flood of the waters, within the rivers — Indra's bolt, the bull of wide-spreading wealth: Soma, the gladdening one, flows sweet to the heart.
Flow then round about the earthly realm, giving delight to the singer and to the one who shakes you, O wise one! Let us not be excluded from wealth that touches the divine seat; may we clothe ourselves in plentiful, golden riches.
Come, O Indu, give us a hundred-fold gift of horses, a thousandfold gift, rich in cattle and gold. Approach us with great and bountiful refreshments; for the praise, O Pavamāna, come to us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Together they have roared at the sides of the swelling drop; the naves of Truth have come together in its womb. He, the Asura, has grasped the three heads at their joint; the ships of Truth have ferried across the well-made deed.
Fully together, the great bulls roared in unison; on the wave of the river the inspired ones made the reeds tremble. Generating with streams of honey the very song, they have made grow Indra's dear body.
Those possessed of the purifying sieve sit round about the speech; the ancient father guards their vow. Varuṇa has set himself across the great ocean; only the steadfast ones have found their grip on the foundations.
Together they have roared down to you at the thousandfold stream, the honey-tongued ones who do not cease, on the vault of heaven. His spies, the vigorous ones, do not shut their eyes; step by step there are noose-bearing guards.
Those who have roared together toward father and mother, blazing with sacred verse, burning up the lawless — they blow away by their power the dark skin, hateful to Indra, from all around the expanse of heaven.
Those who have roared together from of old by measure, the thought-movers of the vehement one, drivers of song — those with nostrils stopped, the deaf ones, have laughed; the evil-doers do not cross the path of Truth.
In the far-stretched, thousandfold filter, the seers, the inspired ones, purify the speech. The spies of these, Rudras, swift and unharmful, beautifully moving, fair to see, watching over men.
The guardian of Truth, the one of good resolve, not to be deceived, has placed the three filters in his heart within. Knowing, he looks upon all beings; he pierces the lawless, the ungratified, into the pit.
The thread of Truth is stretched out in the filter, at the tip of Varuṇa's tongue, by his wisdom. Even the steadfast ones strive to attain it — there the one without mastery falls down into the pit.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like a newborn child he has roared out in the wood, when the tawny swift one seeks to win the sun. He follows after with the seed of heaven, growing with milk; we implore him, of good will, for broad-spreading shelter.
He who is the pillar and foundation of heaven, self-stretched, the filled stalk that goes round about on every side — he will worship the two great worlds covered all around; the wise one has held together in the pair, the refreshments.
Great is the well-made somalike sweetness, the wide pasture-land of Aditi, where Truth is reached. He who rules the rain from here, the tawny bull, the leader of the waters from here — the one fortified from here, worthy of the hymn.
The self-containing cloud is milked of its ghee and milk; the navel of Truth, the immortal one, is born. The like-minded, the bountiful ones, gratify him; men of good will shower down their gift upon him.
The stalk has cried out, accompanied by the wave; it swells the divine skin for Manu. It places the embryo in the lap of Aditi, through which we sustain our offspring and our progeny.
Those unceasing streams at the thousandfold flow — may they be rich in offspring in the third realm. The four navels fixed below the sky carry the oblation, the immortal, the ghee-dripping ones.
He makes a white form when he sets out to win it; Soma, the rain-giving Asura, knows the fullness. With wisdom he accompanies effort, so that he speaks forth; he bursts the cloud-barrel of the sky that swells above.
Then the swift one, victor, has stepped into the white bowl anointed with cows, in the dark soil. Those who desire the gods have urged him forward with their minds, for Kakṣīvat of the hundred winters, with the cows.
O Soma mixed with the waters, your juice runs through the sheep's-wool filter, O Pavamāna. When cleansed by the seers, make yourself most gladdening and sweet for Indra to drink, O Pavamāna.

title: Rigveda
text:
The swift one, dear-impelled, flows forth through the beloved names in which he grows. The great one has mounted the wide chariot of the great sun, going in all directions, the far-seeing one.
The tongue of Truth flows with sweet, beloved honey; the lord of this thought is the speaker, not to be deceived. The son places the secret name, the third, upon the shining realm of heaven.
