Thee, whom men surround as cows approach a warm stall, O youngest one, thou art the messenger between the gods and mortals; thou roamest in between as the great one, through the shining realm.
As a mother cherishes her noble child and makes him thrive, tending him carefully, thou descendest swiftly from the bow, O eager one, and streakest forth like a loosened animal.
We are foolish and do not know, O wise Agni; thou thyself knowest thy own greatness well. He lies concealed, yet roams, eating with his tongue, and licks the young woman, being the lord of the folk.
He is born ever-new among the ancient ones; he stands in the forest grey-haired, smoke-bannered. Like a bull whose thirst is unquenched he moves forward; him whom men of one mind lead on.
Like thieves who hazard their bodies, the two who roam through the forest, have clothed themselves with ten ropes. Here, O Agni, is a newer hymn for thee; yoke thy chariot as it were with gleaming limbs.
May this prayer and this reverence and this song be ever a source of increase to thee, O Jātavedas. Guard for us, O Agni, our children and offspring; protect our bodies without ceasing.
The one ocean, foundation of riches, with many births, surveys us from our hearts. He clings to the udder in the lap of the hidden waters; the station of the bird is set in the midst of the fountain.
Clad in the same abode, the bulls have come together with the mares. The poets guard the station of Holy Order; they have placed the hidden names beyond.

title: Rigveda
text:
The two, possessed of holy order and of magic power, hold together; having met, they begat the child and nourish it — unwinding with the mind even the thread of the moving and the stationary, the navel of all the world.
For the tracks of Holy Order attend upon the well-born one, upon the impulses that have come long ago, for vigor. Wearing their garment, the two worlds when praised increase together with ghee, with food, with sweetnesses.
Eager, knowing, he has loudly called the seven ruddy sisters and raised them up with honey to be seen. He who was born of old, spanning the mid-air, seeking, found the hiding-place of Pūṣan.
The poets fashioned seven boundaries; to one of these alone the wicked one approached. Standing in the nest of the highest of Āyu, at the branching of the paths, on the firm foundations.
Both the Non-existent and the Existent are in the highest firmament, in the birth of Dakṣa, in the lap of Aditi. Agni indeed is our firstborn of Holy Order, the bull and the cow in an earlier age of existence.
This is he in whose shelter and with whose aid the praiser kindles the fire and wins his wish. He who, surrounded, goes about the seers with his greatest radiances, the far-shining one.
He who, far-shining, shines with his radiances, Agni, with the gods, keeper of holy order, unceasing, he who has won friendship from his friends, not turning aside, like a swift steed.
He who commands all divine refreshment, who commands all life at the brightening of Dawn — in whose fire, all-sustaining, Ariṣṭaratha sets the oblations in mind, with his praises.
Increased by praises, delighting in the hymns, swift-flying he goes toward the gods. That joyful Hotṛ with his ladle, most skilled in sacrifice, Agni who mingles with them, draws the gods near.
Glorify with songs and reverences that gleaming Agni who trembles like Indra, whom the inspired seers praise with their thoughts — Jātavedas, wielder of the oblation-ladle, who bears the burden.

title: Rigveda
text:
In whom all good things have assembled, as horses with swift steeds in the race — turn hither to us, O Agni, the aids that are most like those of Indra.
For indeed, O Agni, by thy greatness, sitting present, straightway when born thou wert fit to be invoked. The gods followed thy will in that; the primal helpers then grew strong.
Grant us, O Agni, welfare from sky and earth; grant us all life for the act of worship, O god. May we attend upon thy discernments, O wonder-worker; protect us, O god, with your broad protections.
These thoughts, O Agni, born for thee, praise the bounty with cows and horses. When a mortal follows after thy gift, O Vasu, bearing thy praises, O well-born one.
I think of Agni as a father, I think of Agni as a kinsman, I think of Agni as ever a brother and friend. I worship the face of great Agni — bright, adorable, dwelling in the sun in the sky.
Efficacious prayers that gain spoils are ours, O Agni, for him whom thou protectest at home, O everlasting Hotṛ. That keeper of holy order, red-horsed, rich in rain, may he have good fortune through his days and nights.
With day-gifts set, like a friend useful for service, the ancient ritual priest, the lusty lover of the rite — the descendants of Āyu with their arms generated Agni and seated him as Hotṛ among the peoples.
Sacrifice thou thyself to the gods in heaven, O god; what can the simple-minded, thoughtless one accomplish for thee? As thou hast sacrificed to the gods in the seasons, O god, so sacrifice, O well-born one, for thyself.
Be our protector, O Agni, and our guardian; be our strengthener of vigor and our nourisher. And grant us the gift of oblation-bearing, O greatly good one; protect us and our bodies without ceasing.
Agni moves forward with his great banner; the bull roars filling the two worlds. He has reached even the highest limits of the sky; the great one has grown mighty in the lap of the waters.

title: Rigveda
text:
The crested bull, as the embryo, rejoiced; the calf, never resting, powerful, cried aloud. He, performing deeds surpassing those of the gods, goes first to his own abodes.
He who has seized upon the head of his two parents — at the rite the flood of the sun has been laid down. On his flight, the ruddy mares rooted in horses delight in the womb of holy order, in their own forms.
For, O Vasu, thou goest to the front of each dawn; thou wast the far-shining presence of the two Yamas. Thou settest seven stations for holy order, engendering Mitra for thine own self.
Thou hast become the eye of the great Ṛta, the guardian; thou hast become Varuṇa when thou seekest holy order. Thou hast become the Son of the Waters, O Jātavedas; thou hast become the messenger of him whose oblation thou dost favor.
Thou hast become the leader of the sacrifice and of the expanse, where thou art present with thy benevolent teams. Thou hast set thy head in heaven, winning the sun; O Agni, thou hast made thy tongue the bearer of the oblation.
Trita, within the cave, by the will of this one, seeking the intelligence, the tracks of the far Father, being helped, in the lap of his two parents, calling upon his kin, goes to fetch weapons.
Knowing the paternal weapons, spurred by Indra, the Waters' son fought against the enemy. Having slain the three-headed one of the seven rays, Trita released even the cattle of Tvaṣṭṛ's son.
Much did Indra surpass the rising might; the lord of the good overwhelmed the proud one. Even of Tvaṣṭṛ's son Viśvarūpa, while seizing his cattle, he cut away the three heads.
O Waters, you are truly sources of well-being; grant us strength and vigor for great joy and to behold the great.
Of your most auspicious essence grant us a share here, like eager mothers.
Let us hasten to you, for whose abode you quicken us; O Waters, generate us.

title: Rigveda
text:
May the divine Waters be auspicious for our protection, for our drinking; may they flow on us for well-being and happiness.
Ruling over precious things, presiding over men — I ask the Waters for healing.
Within the waters Soma has declared to me all remedies, and Agni, who brings welfare to all.
O Waters, provide the healing balm, the protection for my body, so that I may long look upon the sun.
O Waters, carry away whatever evil is in me, whatever wrong I may have done, or whatever curse or falsehood.
I have gone today with the Waters; we have mingled with their essence. O Agni, rich in milk, come hither; unite me with splendor.
Yamī speaks: I would surely turn a friend toward friendship, though he has passed over many floods. The ordainer should establish us as the grandson's line of the Father, thinking of further offspring upon the earth.
Yama speaks: Thy friend does not wish for this friendship — that she who is of the same sign should become of a different form. The heroic sons of the great Asura, who uphold the sky, look out over the wide world.
Yamī speaks: Indeed the immortals desire this, that progeny of this one mortal might arise. Let thy mind be set in my mind; a husband should enter the body of his wife.
Yama speaks: What we have not done before, how should we do it now? We who speak of holy order — should we speak falsehood? Gandharva is in the waters and the watery maiden — she is our highest tie of kinship, she is our utmost bond.
Yamī speaks: Surely the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ the all-shaped, will make us husband and wife in the womb. None violates his ordinances; both Earth and Heaven know of this for us.
Yama speaks: Who knows of the first day? Who has seen it? Who would proclaim it here? Great is the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa. What would you say, O Yamī, to men with impunity?

title: Rigveda
text:
Yamī speaks: The longing for Yama has come upon Yamī, to lie together in the same womb. As a wife opens her body to her husband — I would spread apart like the wheels of a chariot.
Yama speaks: These spies of the gods who wander here do not stand still, they do not close their eyes. Go quickly elsewhere, Yamī, not to me; spread apart with him like the wheels of a chariot.
Yamī speaks: With nights and with days she should serve him; let the eye of the sun open again and again. May Yamī, twin-born, related as kin to Yama, bear what is non-kin between Heaven and Earth.
Yama speaks: Later ages shall come when those of the same kin will do what is not kin. O fortunate one, stretch out thy arm to the bull; seek thyself another husband, not me.
Yamī speaks: What use is a brother if she remains without refuge? What use is a sister when Nirṛti comes upon her? Smitten by longing I speak out much of this: unite thy body with my body.
Yama speaks: I shall not unite my body with thy body. They call it evil when a man goes to his sister. Arrange for thyself pleasures with another, not me; thy brother, O fortunate one, does not desire this.
Yamī speaks: Alas, alas, O Yama — we have not found out either thy mind or thy heart. Surely some other woman clasps thee as it were a girth on a yoked horse, as a creeper embraces a tree.
Yama speaks: Let another clasp thee, Yamī, and let another clasp him as a creeper clasps a tree. Seek his mind, or let him seek thine; make a good compact together.
The bull-like one has milked out the milk-giving draughts of heaven for the bull-like one; the swift, inviolable son of Aditi. He knows all things even as Varuṇa knows through insight — let him, worthy of worship, perform sacrifice at the proper seasons.
May the Gandharva's consort and the water-maiden [Apsarās] guard my mind amid the roar of the stream. May Aditi establish us in the midst of the desired [realm]; our eldest brother, the foremost, shall proclaim it.

title: Rigveda
text:
Verily, glorious, splendid and luminous was the dawn that shone for Manu, rich in light. When the eager ones, following the will of the willing one, brought forth Agni as hotar for the assembly.
Then the falcon, impelled [by the gods], brought hither that far-reaching, all-seeing drop [of Soma] to the sacrifice. When the Āryan clans chose the wondrous Agni as their hotar, then was wisdom born.
Thou art ever joyful, O Agni, and flourishest like barley; the pious man's sacrifice proceeds well through thy priestly invocations. When the inspired sage, after his toil, brings thee the hymn-worthy praise, thou approachest [him] with abundant food-prizes won.
The lover stirs up the two parents [Heaven and Earth] and desires to offer to Bhaga; the beloved one hastens, longing in his heart. The carrier [Agni] speaks, the active one is alert; the mighty asura [Agni] grows strong, trembling with inspired thought.
That mortal, O Agni, son of strength, who wins thy benevolence — he is heard beyond all others. Bearing food and borne along on horses, he, brilliant and mighty, adorns his days.
When, O Agni, this divine assembly gathers among the gods, worthy of worship, O worshipful one — and when thou distributest the treasures according to thy nature — may our share here be rich in wealth.
Hear us, O Agni, in the assembly, in the gathering-place; yoke thy chariot swift as the immortal. Bring hither to us Heaven and Earth, divine children; may thou never depart from the gods' company here.
Heaven and Earth, the primal pair, are renowned through Order [ṛta] and are truthful of speech. When the god [Agni], making mortals ready for sacrifice, sat down as hotar, proceeding forward, guarding his own vital force.
The god who surpasses the gods through Order — first knowing all, bear our oblation. Smoke-bannered, blazing bright with fuel, the joyful hotar, eternal, most skilled in speech and sacrifice.

title: Rigveda
text:
The divine immortal [Agni] is the self-yoker; when born from the cow [fire-sticks], they sustained the two broad [worlds]. All the gods followed after that sacrificial formula of thine when the bright [cow of heaven] milked out the divine ghee.
I praise you two, O ghee-streaming waters, for your increase; O Heaven and Earth, O Rodasī — hear me. In the days when the heavens brought the vital breath's dispensation, may the two parents [Heaven and Earth] sharpen us here with sweetness.
What has our king taken? In what have we transgressed his ordinance? Who knows fully? Even Mitra, though invoked, [may be] cheated among gods — yet may the call go forth; there still is prize-wealth.
Here let him reconsider the name of the immortal [Agni] — that which, of equal mark, takes manifold forms. He who meditates well on Yama's [order] — protect him, O tall Agni, without ceasing in vigilance.
In whom the gods rejoice at the assembly, holding [their seats] in the dwelling of Vivasvat — in the sun they placed the light; in the moon the nights; the two luminaries circle unceasingly.
In that hidden thought wherein the gods wander together — we, for our part, know it not. May Mitra here [declare us] sinless, and Aditi; may divine Savitṛ speak to Varuṇa on our behalf.
Hear us, O Agni, in the assembly, in the gathering-place; yoke thy chariot swift as the immortal. Bring hither to us Heaven and Earth, divine children; may thou never depart from the gods' company here.
I yoke you two with the ancient sacred word, with reverences; may the hymn go forth like the sage's [chant] along its path. May all the sons of the immortal hear, even those who have taken up their stations in the divine realms.
When you two came forth as the two striving [like a pair of twins], men devoted to the gods brought oblations to you. Take your own place, you who know it well — be a good seat for Indu [Soma] among us.

title: Rigveda
text:
I have mounted the five-footed [gāyatrī]; I follow the four-footed [triṣṭubh] according to sacred law. By the syllable I measure this [speech]; at the navel of Order [ṛta] I purify it together.
For the gods he [Yama] chose death; for progeny he did not choose immortality. They made Bṛhaspati the sacrificial ṛṣi; Yama yielded up his beloved body [to death].
The seven [streams] flow for the young Marut-accompanied one; the sons, for the father, have set Order [ṛta] in motion. Both [Heaven and Earth] reign over both aspects [of existence]; both strive and both nourish all.
Honour with oblation Yama, the king, son of Vivasvat — who has gone forth along the mighty slopes, and has explored the path for many, the gathering-place of peoples.
Yama first discovered the way for us; this pasture cannot be taken away. Where our ancient Fathers went forth, there, born along that same path, all beings follow their own paths.
Mātali grew strong with the Kavyas; Yama with the Aṅgirases; Bṛhaspati with those who chant the Ṛk. Those whom the gods exalted and those who exalted the gods — some rejoice with svāhā, others with svadhā.
Come, O Yama, sit upon this sacred grass together with the Aṅgiras Fathers, in accord with them. May the seer-proclaimed mantras bring thee hither; with this oblation, O king, be gladdened.
Come hither, O Yama, with the Aṅgirases worthy of worship, of varied forms; rejoice here. I call Vivasvat, thy father — having sat down on the sacred grass at this sacrifice.
The Aṅgirases are our Fathers — the nine-fold, the Atharvans, the Bhṛgus, the Soma-drinkers. May we abide in the good favour of those worthy of sacrifice, in their auspicious benevolence.
Go forth, go forth on the ancient paths along which our ancient Fathers departed. There thou shalt behold the two kings rejoicing in the oblation — Yama and the god Varuṇa.

title: Rigveda
text:
Unite with the Fathers, unite with Yama and with [the reward of] sacrifices performed and pious works, in the highest heaven. Leaving behind all imperfection, return again to home; unite with thy body, radiant.
Depart, withdraw, and disperse from this [place] — the Fathers have made this world for him. With days, with waters, with nights illuminated — Yama bestows a resting-place upon him.
Run past the two dogs of Saramā, the four-eyed, brindled ones, by the good path. Then approach the gracious Fathers who feast together with Yama in joy.
Thy two dogs, O Yama — the guardians, four-eyed, watchers of the road, observers of men — commit this man to their keeping, O king; grant him welfare and freedom from disease.
Wide-nostrilled, life-drinking, fig-tree-coloured, the two messengers of Yama roam among men. May those two grant us today here to see the sun again — may they restore vital breath and blessings.
Press Soma for Yama, pour the oblation for Yama. The sacrifice goes to Yama, well-prepared, with Agni as its messenger.
Pour the ghee-rich oblation for Yama and step forward. May he bring us [the blessing] among the gods — long life for us to live.
Pour the sweetest oblation-offering for Yama the king. This homage [goes] to the ancient ṛṣis, the first-born, the first path-makers.
By the three Soma-pressings he [Yama] flies [encompasses] the six wide [worlds]; one alone is the Vast. Triṣṭubh, Gāyatrī — all the metres are established in Yama.
Let the lower Fathers rise up, and the higher, and the middle Soma-drinking Fathers. Those who have gone to life, the harmless, knowing Order — may those Fathers aid us at our invocations.
Let there be homage today to the Fathers, those who departed first and those who departed later. Those settled in the earthly realm of dust, or those now among well-ordered communities.

title: Rigveda
text:
I have found the gracious Fathers, and Viṣṇu's grandson and his stride. Those who sit upon the sacred grass, who share by svadhā in the pressed [Soma] — may they come most swiftly here.
O Fathers seated on the sacred grass, come hither to us with your help; enjoy these oblations we have made for you. Come with the most blessed aid; then grant us health and freedom from affliction.
The Soma-drinking Fathers have been called upon, at the dear sacred-grass resting places. Let them come, let them hear here; let them speak and protect us.
Bending the right knee, sitting down, praise this sacrifice, all of you. O Fathers, harm us not for any sin that we, being but men, may have committed against you.
Sitting in the lap of the ruddy [dawn clouds], bestow wealth upon the mortal who gives. O Fathers, pass on to his sons the riches that are his; establish here for him vigour and strength.
Those ancient Soma-drinking Fathers of ours, the most excellent, who followed the Soma-drinking [rite] — may Yama, rejoicing with them, eat the oblations at his pleasure, himself eager with the eager ones.
Those who thirsted [for the divine], striving toward the gods, knowing the priestly arts, shaping hymns of praise with [sacred] songs — O Agni, come hither with the gracious [Fathers], with the true, wise, cauldron-seated Fathers.
Those who are true, eaters of oblation, drinkers of oblation, riding the same chariot with Indra and the gods — O Agni, come with a thousand praised by the gods, with the later and the earlier Fathers seated at the cauldron.
O Fathers tasted by Agni, come hither; well-guided, take your seats at each seat. Eat the oblations offered on the sacred grass; then bestow upon us wealth with all heroes.
Thou, O Agni, invoked as Jātavedas, having made the oblations fragrant, didst carry them [to the Fathers]. Thou gavest [them] to the Fathers by the svadhā [call]; they ate — do thou, O god, eat the presented oblations.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those Fathers who are here and those who are not here, those whom we know and those whom we do not know — thou, O Jātavedas, knowest how many they are; enjoy the well-performed sacrifice with the svadhā-offerings.
Those [Fathers] burned by Agni, those not burned by Agni, who rejoice in the midst of heaven with the svadhā oblation — with those, O self-ruling one, fashion this vital dispensation for the body according to [thy] will.
O Agni, do not burn him entirely, do not scorch him; do not consume his skin nor his body. When thou hast made him done [cooked], O Jātavedas, then send him forth to the Fathers.
When thou hast made him done, O Jātavedas, then hand him over all around to the Fathers. When he goes forth by this dispensation of vital breath, then he becomes subject to the will of the gods.
May his eye go to the Sun, his breath to the Wind; let him go to the sky and to the earth according to cosmic law. Or go to the waters, if it be fitting for thee there — abide in the plants with [thy remaining] body-parts.
The unborn portion — consume it with thy heat; let thy glow heat it, let thy flame heat it. Those auspicious forms of thine, O Jātavedas — with those carry him to the world of the pious.
O Agni, release him back again to the Fathers — he who, offered to thee, wanders with svadhā-offerings. Clothed in life, may the remainder [of his vital parts] come near; may [he] unite with his body, O Jātavedas.
That which a black bird has pecked at thee, or an ant, a serpent, or a wild beast — may Agni make all that wholly free of ill, and Soma who has entered into the Brāhmaṇas.
Wrap thyself around with a coat of mail from Agni; cover thyself all over with fat and marrow. Lest the bold one [Agni], fiercely blazing, seizing and meaning to burn thee, encircle thee.
O Agni, do not tip over this cup; it is dear to the gods and to the Soma-drinkers. This is the cup from which the gods drink — in it the immortal gods take delight.

title: Rigveda
text:
I send the flesh-eating Agni far away; let him go to the realm of Yama, carrying the impurity. But let this other Agni, Jātavedas, carry the oblation to the gods here, knowing well [his task].
That Agni who, flesh-eating, has entered your house — beholding this other Jātavedas — that god I carry away for the Fathers' sacrifice; may he drive the cauldron in the highest dwelling.
May the Agni who carries the flesh, who worships the Fathers, the increasers of Order — may he announce the oblations forthwith, both to the gods and to the Fathers.
Desiring [this], we place thee [on the altar]; desiring [this], we kindle thee. Desiring it, bring the desiring Fathers hither to eat the oblation.
Him whom thou, O Agni, hast fully burned — do thou extinguish him again. Let young dūrvā grass and the spreading vyalkaśā plant spring up here.
O cool one, O cooling one; O refreshing one, O refresher — by the frog-spell [or: O Maṇḍūkā], rejoice and gladden this Agni well.
Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the bridal for his daughter; at that, all this universe comes together. The mother of Yama, the great wife of Vivasvat, disappeared when she was being carried [in the bridal procession].
They concealed the immortal [Saraṇyū] from mortals; having made a woman of like appearance, they gave her to Vivasvat. Then what there was [of her] she bore to the two Aśvins; Saraṇyū abandoned the two twin children.
May Pūṣan, knowing the way, drive thee forth from here — the guardian of the world, whose cattle are never lost. May he hand thee over to those Fathers, and Agni to those gods who know well [their duty].
Universal Life [Āyur] shall guard thee on every side; may Pūṣan guard thee before on the forward path. Where the pious sit, where they have gone — there may the god Savitṛ establish thee.
Pūṣan knows all these quarters [of the sky]; may he lead us by the most fearless [path]. The giver of blessings, radiant, all-heroic, never stumbling, knowing well, let him go before.

title: Rigveda
text:
Pūṣan was born on the forward path of paths, on the forward path of heaven, on the forward path of earth. Moving toward both most beloved resting-places — coming and going — he travels knowing [the way].
The god-loving call upon Sarasvatī; at the sacrifice as it extends they [call upon] Sarasvatī. The pious invoked Sarasvatī — may Sarasvatī bestow the prize upon the worshipper.
O Sarasvatī, thou who hast ridden on the same chariot, O goddess, rejoicing with the Fathers by the svadhā-offerings — seated on this sacred grass, be gladdened; bestow upon us vigour free from disease.
That Sarasvatī whom the Fathers call upon, approaching the sacrifice from the south — the share of Iḻā [worship] worth a thousand — bestow prosperity of wealth upon the sacrificers.
May the Waters, our mothers, cleanse us; may the ghee-purifying ones purify us with ghee. For the divine [Waters] carry away all impurity — I rise up from them purified and clean.
The drop [of Soma] flowed forth following the first days, and this womb, and the one that was before. I pour the drop that flows along following the common womb — the seven hotars following.
Whatever drop of thine spills, whatever shoot falls from the arms, from the lap of the vessel-goddesses [dhiṣaṇā], or from the adhvaryu priests, or from the purifying filter — that I pour for thee, called forth with mind and vaṣaṭ.
Whatever drop of thine has spilled, whatever shoot fell down or away from the ladle — may this god Bṛhaspati pour it together for bounty.
The plants are full of sap; let my speech be full of sap. Let the sap of the waters be full of sap — with that, purify me together.
O Death, depart by thine own other path that is different from the gods' road. I speak to thee who hast eyes and ears: do not harm our offspring and do not injure our heroes.

title: Rigveda
text:
Having come here wiping away the footprint of Death, establishing a longer span of life, growing prosperous with progeny and wealth — pure, cleansed, be ye worthy of sacrifice.
These living ones have turned away from the dead; our invocation of the gods this day has been auspicious. We have gone forth to the dance and to laughter, establishing a longer, further span of life.
I set this enclosing barrier for the living — may none of them proceed to that farther goal. Let them live a hundred autumns many-branching; may they hold Death within, as by a mountain.
As the days come in succession one after another, as the seasons go well in their proper order, as the later [season] does not abandon the earlier — so, O Creator [Dhātṛ], fashion for these ones their lifespans.
Climb up to old age, choosing [long] life; go in order, striving, you who stand [here]. May Tvaṣṭṛ, well-born, of like mind, fashion for you here a long life to live.
These women here, not widows, blessed with good husbands — let them enter [the house] with collyrium and ghee. Tearless, free from affliction, adorned with fine jewels, let the wives first mount the [bridal] seat.
Rise up, O woman, to the world of the living; come, approach this one who lies here, lifeless. Thou hast fulfilled completely here the wifely state of him, thy husband, who took thy hand and desired thee.
Taking the bow from the hand of the dead man — for our lordship, brilliance, and strength — right here thou [shalt be] and here we, rich in heroes, shall conquer all enemies and those who hate us.
Creep to thy mother, this Earth, the wide-spreading, pleasant-abiding Earth. Young maiden, soft as wool, may she, who gives on the right side, protect thee from the lap of Nirṛti.
Heave thyself up, O Earth; oppress him not. Be easy of access, easy to pass by, for him. As a mother wraps her son in her robe, so cover him, O Earth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let the earth, heaving up, stand firm; let [the pillars] be propped up for a thousand [years]. Let those houses drip with ghee; let them be a refuge for him here for all days.
I prop up the earth from thee [the corpse], placing this clod upon it; may I not be harmed. Let the Fathers hold fast this pillar; here may Yama fashion thee a seat.
In the westward days they [the funeral priests] have laid me aside like a leaf. I have seized westward speech, as one seizes a horse by a rein.
Turn back, do not go away; let the prosperous [cattle] cling to us. O Agni and Soma, ye who restore wealth — hold fast riches among us.
Turn them back again, bring them back and settle them here. May Indra restrain them; may Agni drive them hither.
May these turn back again; may they thrive here with their herdsmen. O Agni, hold [them] fast right here; let the riches remain right here.
That [power] of leading forth, of bringing down, of agreement, of going away — the turning back, the returning — I call upon whoever is the guardian [of that power].
He who raised the dispersing, he who raised the going-away — may the guardian of the turning back and the returning now turn back.
Turn back, cause to turn back; O Indra, give us back our cows again. May we enjoy [them] while they are alive.
I set [this charm] around you on every side with vigour, with ghee, with milk. Whatsoever gods are worthy of worship — may they join riches together with us.
O Turning-back, cause to turn; O Returning, cause to return. From the four quarters of the earth — from those, turn them [the cattle] back.
Breathe upon us blessings of mind.
I praise Agni, youngest of those who enjoy [oblations], the friendly, hard-to-restrain one by [thy] command. In whose ordinance the bright cows [rays] attend the udder of their mother [the sky].

title: Rigveda
text:
Him whom the two lips nurture, shining with splendour as his banner — he blazes, bestowing brilliance in rows.
The lord goes forward on the path of the clans when he has reached the ends of heaven — the seer blazing through the clouds.
Enjoying the oblations of man, he has stood upright, mighty at the sacrifice — measuring out the seat, he goes forward.
For he is the abode [of safety], the oblation, the sacrifice; by his hearkening [command] goes the path. The gods [seek] Agni with his chopper [vāśī].
I desire to serve [him] through the sacrifice of well-done worship — Agni of primal bliss. They call him the son of the rock, the living one [Āyu].
Whatever men come toward us from every side — may they all be good to us, magnifying Agni with oblation.
His course is black, white, ruddy; the tawny, the shining red, the glorious [are his colours]. The Creator [Janitā] has begotten him of golden form.
Thus has Vimada [expressed] this insight for thee, O Agni, O son of vigour, in concord with the immortals. Seeking good favour, may he bring hither by song [the gifts of] food, vigour, good dwelling — thou who hast illumined all.
With our own songs of praise we choose thee, Agni, as Hotṛ for the sacrifice spread with sacred grass. In the exhilaration of your Soma, radiant and pure-flaming, thou art eager to speak forth.
Thee, verily, do thy own devotees adorn—those rich in horses. The oblation-ladle seeks thee, O Agni; in the Soma's rapture the forceful offering seeks thee, and thou art eager to speak forth.
In thee the ordinances rest, like ones pouring with their ladles. Dark forms and bright forms—in the Soma's rapture thou assumest all splendours, and thou art eager to speak forth.
Whatever wealth thou, O Agni, mighty one, immortal, thinkest of—bring that wondrous treasure to us at the sacrifices for the winning of strength. In the Soma's rapture thou art eager to speak forth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni was born through Atharvan and found all the inspired poems. He became the messenger of Vivasvat—beloved of Yama, the desirable one—in the Soma's exhilaration eager to speak forth.
Thee, O Agni, they praise at sacrifices performed in order at the rite. Thou grantest all desirable treasures to the worshipper—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.
Thee, as the beautiful sacrificial priest, O Agni, they have set in the ritual—the bright-faced one of Manu. Most brilliant and most watchful with thine eyes—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.
O Agni, with thy bright flame thou spreadest wide and mightily. Roaring like a bull thou art exuberant; in the Soma's rapture thou layest seed in kindred women, eager to speak forth.
Where is famed Indra heard? Among which people today is he known, like Mitra? Whether it is in the dwelling of seers, or in a hidden place, where hast thou laboured with thy hymn?
Here, renowned among us, shall Indra be praised today—the wielder of the vajra, who consumes the sacrificial food; who, like Mitra, has spread his fame unceasingly among peoples.
He who is lord of great, unceasing strength, who multiplies great manly power—the bearer of the bold vajra, who cherishes (his devotees) as a father a dear son.
Harnessing the swift horses of the wind, O divine Vajra-wielder, releasing them along the shining path, urging them onward—thou art to be praised on the way.
Thou comest with those swift horses of the wind, which carry thee onward of their own accord—horses whose charioteer no god or mortal, no one at all, can discern.
And then, going forth, Uśanā asks you two: 'For what purpose do you not come home?' You have come from afar—from heaven and from earth—to the mortal.
Come, O Indra, to taste our uplifted hymn. This we implore of thee—that thou hadst smitten the non-human Śuṣṇa.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Dasyu is without rites, without mind, of alien vows, non-human, who assails us. O slayer of enemies, strike down the weapon of that Dāsa with a crushing blow.
Thou, O Indra the hero, with heroes, and those upheld by thee with strength—in many places thy gifts are glorified as the earth-regions rejoice.
Thou, O hero Vajra-bearer, hast incited those men to battle against Vṛtra—in the hidden realm of the inspired seers, of the star-empowered peoples.
Swift are thy gifts, O Indra; they who seize them are fittingly enjoyers, O hero Vajra-bearer—all that thou didst crush of Śuṣṇa's creation with thy companions.
May they not wander away, O Indra, hero—let good succours be ours! May we, we ourselves, dwell in their protection and in thy grace, O Vajra-bearer.
May those truly unharmful (cows) of thine be ours, O Indra, with their touch. May we know the enjoyment of those milk-cows, O Vajra-bearer.
When the handless, footless earth swelled up through the deeds of those worthy of knowledge—thou didst strike down Śuṣṇa in a rightward circuit, for the sake of all living beings.
Drink, drink, O Indra hero, the Soma—may it not harm thee, thou who possessest wealth, full of riches! And protect the liberal worshipper who sings thy praise, and grant us great and glorious wealth.
We worship Indra who holds the vajra in his right hand, the charioteer of the bay steeds—those that take varied courses. He who shook his beard upward, who distributes bounty, parting (the foe) with his armies, with his gifts.
His two bay horses, found in the forest as wealth—may Indra the bountiful, slayer of Vṛtra, be rich in gifts! Ṛbhu, Vāja, Ṛbhukṣan—he masters strength; I even diminish the very name of the Dāsa.
When he holds his golden vajra, then the bountiful, long-renowned Indra mounts the chariot drawn by those bay horses through (the realms of) the pious—Indra, lord of food and far-famed spoil.

title: Rigveda
text:
So indeed is this rain of his own herd—Indra bedews his golden beard; he comes down to the fair dwelling, and at the pressed Soma he shakes (all things) like the wind shaking a forest.
He who with his voice out-spoke the hostile voices, who slew many thousands of ill-fortuned foes—these several acts of his manly strength do we proclaim, he who has increased his might as a father (the strength of) a son.
Vimada and his companions generated for thee, O Indra, this unprecedented and manifold hymn of praise for the great giver. For we know the feast of this mighty one—what offering we shall make as herdsmen bring the cattle.
May none sever these friendships of thine and ours, O Indra, and of the seer Vimada! For we know thy fore-thought, O god, as one knows a kinsman—may thy friendships with us be gracious.
O Indra, drink this honey-sweet Soma pressed in the cup. Bestow upon us thousandfold wealth—in the exhilaration of the Soma-draught, O thou of many gifts, eager to speak forth.
Thee we approach with sacrifices, hymns, and oblations, O lord of power—lord of mighty deeds. Bestow on us the choicest gift—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.
Thou who art lord of desirable things, the inciter of the feeble—O Indra, protector of praisers—in the Soma's rapture guard us from adversaries and from distress, eager to speak forth.
You two mighty ones, possessed of māyā—the Aśvins—rubbed out the fire together; when praised by Vimada, the Nāsatyas rubbed it out (from the kindling-sticks).
All the gods mourned as the Aśvins' wives departed. The gods said to the Nāsatyas: 'Bring them back again!'
Honey-sweet be my going forth, honey-sweet my return. O gods, through divine grace make that (journey) sweet for us—you two (Aśvins).
Breathe into us an auspicious mind, O Soma, skill and understanding. So then, in friendship with thee, through thy Soma-draught, in the rapture of the juice, may our prayers resound like cows in the pasture, eager to speak forth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thy heart-touching (inspirations), O Soma, rest in all thy dwellings. And then my desires—in the Soma's rapture they spread wide, seeking riches, eager to speak forth.
And thy ordinances, O Soma, I do not transgress in foolishness. Then, as a father to a son—in the Soma's rapture be gracious to us even against the weapon (of death), eager to speak forth.
Together do the inspired thoughts advance, like streams into the lowlands. O Soma, sustain our power of action for life—in the Soma's rapture, holding them up like the cups, eager to speak forth.
With thy powers, O Soma, those who desire thee have opened (the enclosures). The wise of the Gṛtsa clan, (endowed) with thy strength—in the Soma's rapture (they win) a cow-filled and horse-filled pen, eager to speak forth.
Thou guardest our cattle, O Soma, the moving world spread in many places. Thou bringest together for life—in the Soma's rapture, beholding all beings, eager to speak forth.
Be thou our all-round guardian, O Soma, inviolable king. Drive away all blemishes—in the Soma's rapture, O king, let no slanderer have power over us, eager to speak forth.
Thou, O Soma of good purpose, watch over us for the bestowal of strength. Knowing the field better than Manu—in the Soma's rapture guard us from treachery and distress, eager to speak forth.
Be thou, O Indu, greatest slayer of Vṛtra, a gracious friend to us—when men invoke thee in battle—in the Soma's rapture, as they fight for the gaining of offspring, eager to speak forth.
This swift intoxication grows dear to Indra. This great (Soma) increases the inspired thought of Kakṣīvat the seer—in the Soma's rapture eager to speak forth.
This Soma sends forth cattle-rich prizes for the inspired worshipper. This (Soma) wins the choicest gift for seven (sages)—in the Soma's rapture it saves both the blind man and the lame, eager to speak forth.

title: Rigveda
text:
Forward, indeed, go the longed-for prayers toward the Niyuts. Forward—may Pūṣan of the Niyut-chariot, the wondrous, the great one, help (us)!
Whose great power coming from the wind this people (praises)—may the inspired poet win him through (his) thoughts; he is known for excellent hymns.
He knows excellent praises—Pūṣan the bull, like the Soma-drop; he sprinkles the eager one; like the pen (full of cattle) he sprinkles (gifts).
We shall honour thee, O god Pūṣan, as ours—for the perfecting of (our) thoughts and as the incessant helper of inspired seers.
He is the counterpart of sacrifices, the impeller of horse-drawn chariots. He is the seer set in place by Manu, the companion who drives away (evil) from the inspired poet.
He is the lord of her who is anxious and of the bright one and of brightness—the weaver of garments; he cleansed the garments of sheep.
He is the mighty one, lord of prizes, the mighty companion of abundance. He who is golden-bright shook out his beard freely—he who is inviolable.
The goats have turned to the yoke of thy chariot, O Pūṣan—the companion of everyone who seeks, born long ago, never displaced.
May Pūṣan the great one help our chariot with his strength. May he increase our prizes and hear this our invocation.
Let it be so for me, O praiser—the impulse is firm—that I should bestow (gifts) on the Soma-presser, the sacrificer. I am the giver without desire for return, the smiter; I crush the mighty one who perverts truth and seeks crookedness.
If I were to lead out (my forces) to battle against the Devayū-enemies who had been swelling in body—let me cook a fat bull for thee here at home; let me pour out the potent Soma fifteen times.
I do not know him who boasts that he has slain those who do not honour the gods in battle. When my fierce chariot proclaims the battle, then indeed do the bulls speak out in my praise.

title: Rigveda
text:
When I was among unknown peoples, all the bountiful ones were on my side. I shall defeat the proud one dwelling in comfort at home—I shall push him from the mountain, having seized him by the foot.
Neither the peoples stop me nor the mountains, when I set my mind (to something). At the sound of my voice the frightened one with the small ears trembles; even so through the days the wren trembles.
They shall see here those cooked-flesh eaters bereft of Indra, cut off from arms, flying from the arrow—or those who have blamed a bold companion; the wheel-rims shall surely roll over them.
Thou wast born, thou grewest, life came to thee—the former may see (this), the later will see (this). Two wheel-pieces encompass him who has not yet been, who has entered the farther side of this expanse.
The cows of the lord were set loose and ate the barley; I saw them roaming, herded together. The calls of the lord came from all sides to gather them—how many of them will the master of his own house be pleased with?
When we, the eaters of barley among peoples—I myself an eater of barley within the broad expanse—here the yoked (one) sought to unyoke, then the unwilling one the eager one harnessed.
And then thou shalt deem my word true—what (wealth) of two-footed and four-footed I shall bring together. If any man here contests with woman the manly one—the unwarlike shall be divided; I know (how to deal with) him.
One whose daughter was born wheelless—who, knowing this, should think lightly of her as blind? Which of the two releases the ram for her—he who would take her away or he who would choose her?
How dear is the young woman to the wooing young man when she is well-pleased with the wonderful gift! The bride is auspicious when she is beautiful—she herself wins a friend even among the people.

title: Rigveda
text:
One awoke from his feet, eats facing forward; with his head he placed a covering against his head. Sitting, he diminishes the lap of the upright one; going downward he follows the supine earth.
A tall (tree) without shade, without leaf, has stood still; the loosened embryo eats the mother. Licking another's calf, she has lowed—where has the cow placed her udder?
Seven heroes rose up from below; those eight from above came together. Nine mighty ones came from behind; ten from in front spread across the back of the rock.
One reddish-brown one among ten—the same—they urge him toward the rite for crossing over. The mother carries the well-placed embryo in her womb, soothing him as he turns about.
The heroes cooked the fat ram; the dice were cast along the day. Two of them, with purifying strainers, move in the great waters purifying them.
They who were crying out went off in all directions; the half cooks (the share) — the half that does not side (with anyone). This god Savitṛ has told me this: 'He who eats from the wooden vessel will thrive on ghee-food.'
I saw the village being carried away from afar, moving along by its own power without wheels. The lord constantly goes forward through the generations; even now the fresh one, renewing his generative vigour.
These two cows of mine are yoked to Pramara—push them not away, make (me) glad again and again! Even the waters lose their power before him; the sun has eclipsed and the hawk has swooped down.
This vajra that is manifold, unfolded from the great fullness below the sun—beyond that there is yet another renown; the steadfast ones, growing old, cross to that.
The cow lows, tied to each tree; thence the man-eating bird shall fly forth. Then let all this world be afraid and let (the reward) be given to the Soma-presser and to the seer (who praises) Indra.

title: Rigveda
text:
The first (ones) stood at the gods' measure; from that point of cutting the later ones rose up. Three scorch the watery earth; two carry the dung-heap croaking (like frogs).
Know both her life and his—do not hide such a thing as this in battle. He makes the light manifest, he conceals his nakedness; he who has appeared is not freed from his adornment.
Any other enemy who comes—but today my father-in-law has not come. Let him eat the grain-cakes and drink the Soma; when well fed let him go home again.
Bellowing, the sharp-horned bull has stood at the top, at the breadth of the earth. I protect him in all the enclosures—him who fills my flanks with pressed Soma.
For thee, O Indra, with the pressing stone they press the exhilarating Soma-draughts quickly; thou drinkest them. They cook bulls for thee; thou eatest from them—thou who art nourished with food when called upon, O bountiful one.
Understand this well for me, O singer—rivers flow against the current as a curse! The jackal has eaten the lion facing him; the jackal has driven the boar out of the thicket.
How shall I understand this—the insight of the wise Gṛtsa concerning thy mighty thought? Do thou, knowing (all), speak to us in order—what, O bountiful one, thou drivest as thy pleasant half (of our share).
For thus they increase me, the mighty one—even my higher course is the great (course) of heaven. I smite many thousands simultaneously, for my father begot me without an enemy.
For thus the gods, O Indra, have begotten me—the mighty, the fierce, the manly one at every deed. Exhilarated, I slew Vṛtra with the vajra; I opened the pen (of cows) with my greatness for the worshipper.
The gods came bearing their axes; cutting through forests they came against the enclosed settlements. They place the woodpile upon (the altar's) chest—where the moisture is, they burn along with that.

title: Rigveda
text:
The hare swallowed the razor point-first; I split the rock from afar with a clod. I shall subdue even the great one for the weak; the calf, striving, weaves (about) the full-grown bull.
The eagle thus grips the prey with its talon—checked, like a lion held at the trap. The thirsty buffalo too, though restrained—the lizard has drawn this noose for him.
For those who feed on the Brāhmaṇa's food by drinking it against him—the lizard has drawn this snare. They eat the freely-loosed bulls, (yet) sharpening the limbs' own strength.
These have prospered through their labours who urged forward the Soma (for bodily) strength with their hymns. Speak to us in man-like fashion—approach us with prizes! As a hero thou placest thy fame, thy name, in heaven.
As the fire deposited in the forest resplendent—the pure hymn of praise has been aroused for you two, O sustainers. He for whom Indra, the most manly of men, the heroic one, the night-passing Hotṛ among many lineages—
Beyond this dawn and the next may we be in the manliness of the most manly among men. Triśoka drove a hundred men after (the battle)—the chariot that (aided) Kutsa achieved victory.
Which of thy pleasurable exhilarations has arisen, O Indra? Rush forth, fierce one, against the doors (of thy strongholds) with (our) hymns! What oblation may bring thee close to us? May I be able to approach thee with food to (offer) the highest gift.
What splendour dost thou, O Indra, make for such men? By what thought dost thou come to us? Like Mitra, true and far-striding, in the presence of food, of all (the foods)—as the inspired prayers shall be.
The sun urges (them) to the goal, like (a boat) to the farther shore—those who have gone like mothers (come) to his desire. And the many hymns addressed to thee, O Indra nobly born—men who praise thee receive (their reward) with foods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Immense indeed for thy mother, O Indra, are heaven by grandeur and earth by wisdom. For thy choice, may the ghee-mixed Soma-pressings be sweet for thee to drink—the honied draughts.
They poured out for him the vessel full of sweet Soma—for Indra, for he is the truly bountiful. He has grown great in the breadth of the earth, in his will, in manly power and virility.
Indra has spread out the battle-hosts with his own might; many (allies) endeavour for friendship with him. Stand firm in the battles as on a chariot—him whom thou urgest on with (thy) auspicious benevolence.
Let the path go forth to the gods for the Brahman priest, toward the waters—like the impulse of the mind. Render up the great sustenance of Mitra and Varuṇa in beautifully constructed prayer to the far-spreading one.
O Adhvaryus bearing oblations—eager ones approaching the invoked (Waters), eager (themselves)—what the red eagle beholds descending—draw that wave to yourselves today, O dexterous ones.
O Adhvaryus, go toward the ocean; worship Apāṁ Napāt (Child of the Waters) with your oblation. He will give you today a pure wave—press for him the honey-sweet Soma.
He who shines without fuel within the waters—whom the inspired priests praise at the rites—O Apāṁ Napāt, give the honey-sweet waters by which Indra has grown to might.
O Adhvaryu, go toward those waters by which Soma is pleased and exhilarated, like a young man (pleased) with beautiful maidens. May the water purify what thou shalt have poured in, together with the herbs.
Thus indeed do the young women bow to the young man, when the eager one comes to the eager ones. They understand one another with mind, they have discerned (each other)—the Adhvaryus and the divine Dhiṣaṇā-waters.
For him who made a world-space out of your enclosures, who freed you from the great curse—for him, for Indra, send forward the honey-sweet wave, the god-exhilarating one, O Waters.

title: Rigveda
text:
Send forward for him the honey-sweet wave—the embryo who is the spring of sweetness for you, O rivers. O rich Waters, praised at the rites with ghee-backed offerings—hear my call.
O rivers, send that exhilarating wave fit for Indra's drinking—him who stirs both (worlds). (Send) the intoxication-shedding, Uśanā-born, cloud-born one circling around the three-threaded, mobile spring.
Rolling onward in two streams, now fighting over the cattle like warriors heading for the stall—O seer, revere the waters, the mothers and mistresses of the world, those who increase together, those who share the same womb.
Help our rite with your divine worship; help the sacred prayer for winning of wealth. At the yoking of ṛta release your udder—O Waters, be quick-hearing, attentive to us.
O rich Waters, you dwell on riches; you bear the auspicious will and immortality. You are the wives of him whose offspring is excellent—may Sarasvatī grant strength to him who praises this.
When the Waters were seen coming, bearing ghee, milks, and honey, agreeing with the Adhvaryus in mind—bringing the well-pressed Soma for Indra—
These rich Waters bringing living riches have come. O Adhvaryus, friends, make them sit down! Seat these Soma-bearing ones on the sacred grass, in agreement with Apāṁ Napāt.
The eager Waters have come; they have sat down here on the sacred grass at the rite, seeking the gods. O Adhvaryus, press the Soma for Indra—your divine worship has become efficacious.
May the praise of the gods, the adorable one with all swift helpers, come to us for our protection. Through them may we become good companions, crossing over all adversities.
A mortal may well desire wealth; let him move along the path of Ṛta with reverence. Let him also speak in accord with his own understanding; with his mind let him grasp the superior discernment.

title: Rigveda
text:
The prayer has been set in place; the portions have been released; the waves approach the wondrous one as at a sacred ford. We have attained the vigour of blessedness; we have become those who know the immortals.
The house-lord who is perpetually brilliant, the home-companion for whom the god Savitṛ has given birth — may Bhaga anoint his face with cattle, may he be pleasing and auspicious to him.
May this earth be as it is at dawns, when the mighty ones come together with strength. Seeking this praise of the singer, may the strengthening prizes come to us full of blessing.
Of him has this benevolence spread wide; the ancient cow became multitudinous. His companions, in the womb of the mighty lord, are borne along equally in the same vessel.
What was the wood, what indeed was the tree from which they fashioned Heaven and Earth? The two, ageless in their standing-place, with their helpers here, have aged through the many former dawns.
There is nothing greater than this, nothing else beyond it; the strong bull bears Heaven and Earth. He who has self-power makes the pure skin, when the bay horses carry the Sun.
Like a roof he passes over the wide earth; like mist the wind blows apart the multitude. There where Mitra and Varuṇa, the instigator, like Agni in the forest, have released their flame.
When the barren one suddenly gave birth, being impelled, making the trembling into steadiness, self-guarding — when the son was born before his parents, the cow devoured the pestle when she was asked about it.
They also call Kaṇva the son of Nṛṣad, and the dark horse Śyāva took the wealth. The bright one swelled out the udder for Kṛṣṇa; here none has pressed upon Ṛta for him.
Come forth, O seekers of the prayer-holder, choosing excellent things; sit down favourably upon the choicest things. Indra delights in both of ours — what he awakens of the Soma juice.

title: Rigveda
text:
O Indra, praised by many, you traverse the celestial luminous realms and the earthly ones with the dust. Those who carry you repeatedly to the sacrifices — let the eloquent ones who fall short win you over.
That which is more beautiful than the beautiful form delights me — when the son takes on the knowledge of his parents. The wife who carries her husband with voice full of goodness: the auspicious wedding adorned with a male child.
That dwelling-place shines beautifully — when the cows like milk-cows point toward the wedding. When the mother of the counsellor anciently shines for the herd, the people of the seven-fold song indeed.
The step of the god-loving one has spread forth surpassing; the mighty one travels alone with the Rudras. For the givers among those immortals, or for old age, pour honey around for the helpers.
The guardian of the vows of the gods declared to me the one that is placed and hidden in the waters. Indra, being wise, has indeed beheld you; instructed by him, O Agni, I have come.
The one who knows not the field questioned the one who knows the field; he proceeds, instructed by the field-knower. This indeed is the auspiciousness of instruction — and he finds the stream of the straight paths.
Today it has breathed without thinking; covered by these days, it drank from the mother's udder. Old age came upon this youthful one; unangered, the good one became of pleasant disposition.
Let us do these auspicious things, O vessel; O Kuruśravaṇa, the gift of bounties. Let giving indeed be yours, O Generous One; and may this Soma which I bear in my heart be yours.
The inciters of the people have yoked me; I carry Pūṣan between them. Then all the gods protected me; the cry arose: 'One who commands ill has come.'
The ribs scorch me on all sides like rival wives. Poverty, nakedness presses me down; thought flutters about like a bird weary of its course.

title: Rigveda
text:
The middlemen eat up the praises like mice their phalluses, O Śatakratu. Just once, O bountiful Indra, be merciful to us; thereafter be like a father to us.
I choose Kuruśravaṇa, the king, the descendant of Trasadasyu — most bounteous of those who are priests of the sacred song, the seer.
Whose three bay horses carry me rightly on his chariot — I would praise him of the thousand sacrificial gifts.
Whose words are very sweet, of the most famous father, like a joyful field to one who has praised.
Come here, O Upamaśravas, grandson of Mitrātithi. I am the praiser of your father.
Whether I were lord of immortals or of mortals — may the bounteous one live for me indeed.
Not even one of a hundred lives beyond the law of the gods; in such wise the yoke-companion has turned away.
The big ones born in a gust of wind, rolling in the hollow, exhilarate me as I shake. Like the draught of Soma from mount Mujāvat, the vibhīdaka tree, the wakeful one, has drawn me to itself.
She never harmed me, never became angry at me; she was kind to my friends and to me. For the sake of one die, of a single stake, I have driven away my devoted wife.
My mother-in-law hates me; my wife pushes me away; the afflicted one finds no one to take pity on him. Like an old horse put up for sale, I find no use of the gambler.
Others fondle his wife, in the case of him for whose stake the prize die has been greedy. Father, mother, brothers say of him: 'We do not know him; take this bound man away.'
When I resolve that I will not play with them, I am left behind by my departing companions. The brown ones, cast down, have uttered speech — I go to their meeting-place like a strumpet.
The gambler goes to the assembly hall, asking himself 'Will I win?', his body aglow. The dice cross his desire in the opposite direction, giving to his adversary the winnings.

title: Rigveda
text:
The dice indeed are hooked, pricking, deceitful, torturing, scorching. They give gifts like a boy; they strike again and again, smeared with honey, they destroy the gambler.
Their group of fifty-three plays like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true. They bow not even to the wrath of the fierce one; even a king does homage to these dice.
Rolling downward they spring upward; handless, they overpower the one with hands. Heavenly coals cast into the hollow, though cold, they burn the heart through.
The gambler's abandoned wife burns with grief; the mother grieves for her son wandering — who knows where? In debt, afraid, craving money, he goes at night to the houses of others.
It pained him to see the woman — the wives of others and the well-found source — the gambler; he yoked the tawny horses in the morning, and fell as an outcast at the fire's edge.
To him who is the general of your great host, who became the first king of the band — to him I render; I do not hold back the wealth. I speak this truth: I offer ten times toward the east.
Do not play with dice; till the soil instead; delight in your property, thinking it much. There are the cattle, O gambler, there is your wife — this the noble Savitṛ shows me as the right path.
Make friendship with us, verily have mercy on us; do not move against us boldly in terrible fashion. Let your wrath subside now, let the enmity enter; let another now be in the thrall of the tawny dice.
Those fires accompanied by Indra awakened, bearing light at the dawning of the Dawns. May great Heaven and Earth be awake, and the Waters — today we choose the protection of the gods.
We choose the protection of Heaven and Earth; the mothers, the rivers, the mountains of Śaryaṇāvat. We implore the sinlessness of the Sun, of the Dawn; may the pressed Soma make us auspicious today.

title: Rigveda
text:
May Heaven and Earth, the great mothers, protect us today, sinless ones, for our wellbeing. May the Dawn, as she shines out, drive away evil — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
May this first Dawn of ours, rich in gods, shine forth richly for the winners of wealth, richly. We set the wrath of the evil adversary far away — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
She who flows forth with the rays of the Sun, bearing light at the dawning of the Dawns — may she shine today for our glory — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
May disease-free dawns come unto us; may the fires rise high with light. May the Aśvins yoke their swift chariot — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
O Savitṛ, impel today for us the best, most excellent share, for you are the giver of treasure. I call upon Dhiṣaṇā the mother of riches — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
May that proclamation of Ṛta fill me — what we thought of as belonging to the gods among humans. With all the Dawns the Sun surely rises — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
Without enmity today, upon the strewing of the sacred grass, in the yoking of the pressing stones, we perfect the prayer. You stand firm in the shelter of the Ādityas — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
Upon our sacred grass in the great joint-joy of heaven, I invoke the gods — set the seven priests in place. Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga for conquest — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
Come, O Ādityas, for our complete welfare; protect our sacrifice with one accord, for our growth. Bṛhaspati, Pūṣan, the Aśvins, Bhaga — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.
Grant us, O gods, O Ādityas, this excellent proclamation — shelter well-supported, fit for lords. For cattle, for offspring, for progeny to live — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

title: Rigveda
text:
All the Maruts today, with all their aids; may all the fires be kindled. May all the gods come to us with protection; may all riches, all vigour be ours.
Whom the gods aid in the winning of prizes, whom they protect, whom they fill and save from distress — he who in your herd knows no fear: may we be swift for the feast of the gods.
Dawn and Night, the great, well-adorned pair; Heaven and Earth; Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — I invoke Indra, the Maruts, the mountains, the Waters, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and Heaven.
May Heaven and Earth, the wise, possessing Ṛta, protect us from distress and harm. May evil-intentioned Nirṛti not rule us — today we choose the protection of the gods.
May Aditi, mother of the wealthy Mitra and Varuṇa, protect us from all distress. May we attain the light that resembles the sun, free from wolves — today we choose the protection of the gods.
Let the speaking pressing stone drive away the demons, evil dreams, Nirṛti, all devouring things. May we attain the shelter of the Āditya, of the Maruts — today we choose the protection of the gods.
Let Indra sit upon the sacred grass; let Iḷā swell; let Bṛhaspati praise with hymns and lauds. We set in our heart the thought well-perceived, to live — today we choose the protection of the gods.
O Aśvins, make our sacrifice sky-touching, swift-coursing, with goodwill for the quest — the oblation with eastward ray, offered with ghee — today we choose the protection of the gods.
I call upon the Marutas host, easy to call, purifying, noble, beneficent, for friendship. We set in our heart the swelling of riches, for good fame — today we choose the protection of the gods.
We bring the invigorating Soma of the waters, fit for the gods, easy to invoke, the glory of the sacrifice. We control the bright-rayed, Indra-meant Soma — today we choose the protection of the gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
May we win that through excellent winning with our winnings — we, living, with living sons, sinless. Let those who hate sacred knowledge bear their sin in every direction — today we choose the protection of the gods.
You who are among Manu's gods of sacrifice, listen — what we implore of you, O gods, give that. A victorious resolve, riches, heroic fame — today we choose the protection of the gods.
Today we choose the great protection of the great gods, of the vast unchallenged ones. So that we may reach wealth born of vigour — today we choose the protection of the gods.
In the great shelter of Agni blazing, sinless in Mitra and Varuṇa for welfare — may we be in the best impulsion of Savitṛ — today we choose the protection of the gods.
All the gods who are in the vow of Savitṛ of true might, in the vow of Mitra, of Varuṇa — may they bestow on us auspiciousness with heroes, with cattle, with substance and brilliant wealth.
Savitṛ from the west, Savitṛ from the east, Savitṛ from the north, Savitṛ from below — may Savitṛ impel us toward complete welfare; may Savitṛ grant us long life.
Reverence to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, to the great god — attend to that Ṛta. Proclaim the far-seeing, divine-born banner, the son of Heaven, the Sun.
May that truthful utterance guard me on all sides, there where the days are stretched out and the Heavens. Everything else that moves enters into rest; the Sun goes forth every day, every day.
No godless one abides before you from days of old, when you career with winged steeds. One realm follows in the east; you go upward, O Sūrya, with another light.
With that light with which you thrust away darkness, O Sūrya, and raise up the whole world with your beam — with that, drive away from us all weakness, all that is unfit for offering, all disease, all evil dreams.

title: Rigveda
text:
Sent by all, you guard the law without anger; you rise by your own power. Whatever resolve we make today calling upon you, O Sūrya, may the gods approve that resolve of ours.
May Heaven and Earth, the Waters, Indra, the Maruts hear this call of our voice. May we not be empty in the sight of Sūrya; living, may we attain an auspicious old age.
Always, of glad heart, with good sight, with progeny, free from disease, sinless — may we see you rising, O Sūrya of friendly greatness, day by day, living long.
You who bear the great light, the discerning one, the radiant delight of every eye — as you mount around the great expanse, may we see you, O Sūrya, living.
By whose banner all beings go forth, and by whose nights they enter into rest — with sinlessness, O golden-haired Sūrya, day by day rise for us more and more enriching.
Be auspicious to us with your light, auspicious to us with the day, auspicious with your beam, auspicious with your cold, auspicious with your warmth. As it may be auspicious on the way and auspicious in the house — O Sūrya, grant us brilliant wealth.
O gods, extend shelter to both our births — to the two-footed and to the four-footed. May he eat, drink, be invigorated, be satisfied — place that healing and welfare free from harm in us.
Whatever offense toward the gods we have made with the tongue, or through the impulse of mind, O Vasus — the hostile one who wishes ill upon us, place that sin upon him.
In this glorious, energetic battle-shout, help us, O Indra, for conquest — where the cattle-winning missiles fly in all directions against the brave men, in the bold raids.
Uncover for us in the dwelling a wealth full of grain, of cattle, worthy of fame, O Indra. May we be the allies of you who are victorious, O Mighty One — O Vasu, do as we desire.
Whether the Dāsa or the Ārya who, O much-praised Indra, plans to fight against us the godless — may your enemies be easy to overcome with us; may we, with you, win them in battle.

title: Rigveda
text:
He who is to be invoked with few gifts and he who is with many, who clears a wide path in the man-conquering fray — we turn today toward that famous winning hero, we turn Indra toward us for aid.
For I have heard you, O Indra, as self-choosing, unstoppable, O bull, spurring on the weak. Free yourself from Kutsa; come here — why would one like you remain bound by the testicles?
That circuit-running, well-turning chariot of yours, O Aśvins, called upon with oblation from evening to dawn, most frequent — this of yours we also invoke by the easy-to-call name as a son calls his father.
Set in motion kindly truths; swell up our prayers; stir up full minds — this we desire. Make our portion glorious, O Aśvins, and grant us lovely Soma among the bounteous.
Though the lot be ageing in the house, you two become its helpers; of one who is decaying, of one who is nearly lost. Even of the blind, O Nāsatyas, and of the emaciated — you two are called the healers even of the broken.
You fashioned Cyavana, old as an ancient chariot, into a young man again for movement. You carried Tugra's son across from the waters — all these deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the pressings.
I will declare your ancient heroic deeds to the people; you have also been healers, producers of bliss. We now invoke these two of yours, fresh, for our protection — may this worshipper place faith in you, O Nāsatyas, as a friend.
This is my call to you — hear me, O Aśvins; teach me like parents teach a son. Friendless, ignorant, unfitted of birth, of wrong understanding — before that reproach, rescue me.
You two brought the bride of Purumitra to Vimada in your chariot, the lovely one. You two heeded the call of Vadhrīmatī; you two granted good birth to Puraṁdhī.
For the inspired one who had come to old age, you two made youthful vigour again. You two raised Vandana up from the Ṛśyad; you two straightway made Viśpalā able to go.

title: Rigveda
text:
You two, O mighty Aśvins, raised up Rebha who lay hidden, as if dead. You two made Atri, enclosed in the pit and scorched, find comfort — for Saptavadhri you two did the same.
You two gave to Pedu, O Aśvins, a white horse with nine times nine prizes — ever-active, companion-scattering — like Bhaga, a prize invoked by men, a producer of bliss.
Not from anywhere does distress reach him, O Aditi, nor does evil or any fear — the one whom you Aśvins, easy to call, of fierce course, make to go before the chariot together with his wife.
Come with that chariot, swifter than thought, which the Ṛbhus fashioned for you, O Aśvins — at whose yoking the daughter of Heaven is born, both days of Vivasvat being auspicious.
Come along that path, victorious over the mountain; you swelled the milk-cow for Śayu, O Aśvins. Even the quail from the jaw of the wolf — you two with your powers released her who had been swallowed.
This praise for you, O Aśvins, we have made; we have fashioned it as the Bhṛgus fashion a chariot. We have polished it as a young man polishes his bride, holding it constantly as a son and child.
Where, O heroes, who adorns your bright chariot as it comes for your blessing? I prepare with thought the early-travelling, far-reaching one, carried from dwelling to dwelling, folk to folk.
Where were you at evening, O Aśvins, where at dawn? Where do you make your approach? Where do you dwell? Who invites you to rest, as a widow invites a brother-in-law, as a young woman invites a young man to her seat?
In the morning you delight like an old woman of the Kāpī clan; from dwelling to dwelling, O adorable ones, you go to the house. Whose wonderworkers do you become, O heroes, or as king's sons do you go to whose pressings?
Like two wild bulls, hunted by hunters, we call upon you two at evening and dawn with oblation. You bring the priestly office, performed in season, to those men who offer — to the people, O lords of beauty.

title: Rigveda
text:
Ghoṣā seeking you, O Aśvins, the king's daughter, said — I ask you, O heroes: be present for me by day, and be present at night; grant me the ability to win a husband with horses and a chariot.
You two are the seers, O Aśvins, concerning the chariot; like Kutsa the singer you two seek the folk. Swiftly at your mouths, O Aśvins, bear honey, like an adorned maiden.
You two rescued Bhujyu, O Aśvins, you two rescued Vaśa, you two came to Śiñjāra through Uśanā. The bounteous ones sit around your companionship; I long for your goodwill, your protection.
You two rescue the emaciated, O Aśvins, you two the lying sick, you two the worshipper and the widow. From the winning prizes you open for the Aśvins the thundering fold of seven mouths.
The maiden was born; the boy flies away; he strikes the plants beautifully along their magic power. For him the rivers flow as into a hollow; for this day his flight comes into being.
Weeping for the living one, they part at the sacrifice; the men have contemplated the long continuation. Those who have assembled this loveliness for the fathers, the women embrace bliss for their husbands.
We do not know that — tell us indeed — when the young man dwells in the womb of the young woman. We desire, O Aśvins, to go to the house of that beloved potent bull, the seed-sower.
May your benevolence come, O Aśvins rich in prizes; desires have settled in our hearts. Become guardians as a pair, O lords of beauty — may we attain the dear houses of Aryaman.
You two, gladdened in the house of Manu, place wealth together with heroes for him who would praise. The ford is made, the good drinking place, O lords of beauty; strike down the evil mind that stands on the path.
Where today, O wonderful Aśvins, lords of beauty, among which peoples do you two delight? Who has guided them? To whose house have they gone — the inspired singer's or the sacrificer's?

title: Rigveda
text:
With well-fashioned hymns we call at the break of dawn that same much-invoked, laudable, three-wheeled chariot that comes to every soma-pressing — the wide-ranging, assembly-worthy car of the Aśvins.
O Nāsatyas, ye two mount the chariot that is yoked at dawn, that goes forth at dawn, that carries sweet gifts. With it ye visit the sacrificing clans, O heroes; even the poet's sacrifice which has its Hotṛ — ye, O Aśvins.
Whether ye come to the Adhvaryu who holds sweets in his dexterous hand, or to the Āgnīdhra who is of firm skill and devoted to the house, or to the soma-pressings of the inspired priest — come thence, O Aśvins, to drink the honey-offering.
Like a bowman shooting his arrow farther and farther, bring forward the hymn of praise for him as if adorning him. O inspired singers, with your voice surpass the voice of the stranger; O singer, appease Indra who is swift to respond.
Assist your friend with the milk-gift; O singer, rouse the eager Indra. Stir the hero to bestow his wealth, as one shakes a full vessel brimming over with riches.
What then, O Maghavan, do they call thee the liberal giver? Sharpen me — I hear that thou art sharp already. May my prayer be rich in bounty, O Śakra; bring us, O Indra, a fortune rich in goods.
People who have gathered in places of real conflict call on thee, O Indra, in battle. There the man who has oblations makes a comrade; the hero desires no friendship with one who does not press soma.
For him who presses the sharp soma-juices for Indra with oblations, bestowing abundant flowing wealth — for such a one, at the early hour of day, [Indra] slays Vṛtra and crushes the nimble foes with his well-wrought weapon.
In Indra in whom we have placed our hope, who the Bounteous One has fixed his desire upon us — may even the distant foe tremble before him; may the peoples bow down their glories to him.

title: Rigveda
text:
Drive far away the hostile obstructor, O mighty one, O much-invoked; with that power keep him at a distance. Bestow on us, O Indra, riches with barley and with cattle; make our prayer prize-winning for the singer.
When the sharp, copious soma-draughts pressed at the bull-pressings have entered Indra within — the Bounteous One never restrains his gift; to the presser he brings abundant wealth.
One also wins a great stake by playing better at dice — when the dog-slaying gambler picks out the winning throw at the right moment. One who is devoted to the gods and does not withhold his wealth — him the self-powerful one unites with riches.
With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.
My thoughts, all finding the sun, all yearning, together sang forth toward Indra. They embrace [him] as wives embrace their husband — the Bountiful One, pure as a young man, for our aid.
Indeed my mind does not turn away from thee — upon thee alone do I fix my desire, O much-invoked. O wondrous Indra, sit down upon the sacred grass as a king; let there be a good draught for thee at this soma.
Indra is the dispeller of both folly and of hunger; he, the Bountiful One, is master of riches and of goods. To him the seven rivers on their downward slope increase the strength of the mighty bull.
Like birds settling on a fair-leafed tree, the gladdening soma-draughts settled upon Indra, dwelling in the soma-vessels. Shining forth on their band with might, he found the sun, the noble light for Manu.

title: Rigveda
text:
As a dog-slaying gambler picks out the winning throw in the game — thus [was] the conquest when the Bountiful One won the sun. No other could match that heroic deed of thine, O Maghavan — neither one of old nor one of recent times.
The Bountiful One has lain around every clan; the bull has made the song of the peoples glisten. He at whose soma-pressings Śakra takes delight — that one conquers with the sharp soma-draughts those who attack.
When the soma-juices flowed together toward Indra like waters to a river, like channels to a lake, the inspired poets strengthen his greatness at his seat, like rain [strengthens] barley with its heavenly gift.
Like an angry bull he swept into the dust-clouds — he who made these waters subservient to noble masters. He, the Bountiful One, found the light for the swift-giving presser, for the oblation-offering Manu.
Let the axe rise together with the light; may it be a good milch-cow of truth as in ancient times. May the bright red one shine forth with his radiance, pure as the sun; may the lord of the good blaze with brilliant light.
With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.
Let Indra, the good lord, come for our exhilaration — he who is mighty, ever hastening by his sacred ordinance, swelling with overwhelming might, surpassing all resistances with his boundless, great virile power.
Thy chariot is well-poised, thy two bay horses well-reined; the bolt is fixed in thy fist, O lord of men. Come quickly, O king, by the good path hither — we would strengthen the virile powers thou hast drunk in.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let the Indra-bearers — the fierce, mighty, powerful ones — bring hither the lord of men, the bolt-armed, terrible one, the waxing bull of true force, to rejoice together here with us.
