Thus, O lord of the press-vat, O like-minded one, thou art the bull in the steadfast pillar of strength. Exert thy power, take it into thyself, so that thou mayest be lord for the growth of those who drink of the soma.
Come to us, for riches may come our way — I have praised a self-willed gift; come, O soma-drinker, hither. Thou art the master; sit here upon the sacred grass. Thy vessels are inviolable by thy sacred order.
The earliest invocations of the gods, going separately, achieved renown hard to surpass. Those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship — those wavy fools descended only into the current itself.
Thus let the others — whose horses have been yoked in a faulty manner — be turned away and be hard to milk. Those who thus are ahead and ready for giving, where there are many marks of enjoyment.
He held up the trembling hills and open plains; heaven roared and the middle regions were stirred. He propped apart the two concordant spheres of thought; drunk with exhilaration, the bull recites the sacred verses.
I bear for thee this well-crafted goad with which thou forcest open, O Maghavan, thou who breakest with hooves. At this pressing let it be thy home — be wakeful at the desired soma-pressing, O Maghavan, as one worthy of the share.
With cattle may we overcome the niggardly one who is hard to approach, and with barley overcome all hunger, O much-invoked. May we, with kings, be first to win riches, with our own community winning.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind and from above, from below, and from the evil-doer. May Indra in front and from the midst of us, as friend to friends, make wide space for us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni was born first from heaven; secondly Jātavedas was born from us. Thirdly, [he was born] in the waters, he of manly wisdom, inexhaustible — the wise man, kindling him, worships him.
O Agni, we know thy three forms in their threefold nature; we know thy dwelling-places borne in many places. We know thy supreme name which is hidden; we know the spring from which thou hast come forth.
O Agni, the manliness-minded one kindled thee in the sea, in the waters within; the man-seeing one [kindled thee] at the udder of heaven. Standing in the third realm, in the lap of the waters, the great ones increased thee.
Agni cried out like thundering heaven; licking the plants, he scorched the earth. Just born, kindled, he gazed all around; blazing within, he lit up both worlds with his radiance.
He is the noble giver of good things, the foundation of riches, the inspirer of those who contemplate, the guardian of soma. The good son of strength, the king in the waters, blazes forth at the front of the dawns, being kindled.
The flag of all things, the embryo of the world — being born, he filled both world-halves. He even clove the firm rock as he went forth, when the five peoples worshipped Agni.
Eager, purifying, incessant, of good wisdom — Agni, the immortal, was implanted among mortals. Carrying it, he sends the ruddy smoke upward, reaching to the sky with his brilliant flame.
The golden ornament, seen afar, blazed wide; shining with glory, his life is hard to endure. Agni became immortal with his forms, when heaven, of good seed, begat him.
He who makes for thee today, O Agni of auspicious flame, a ghee-laden sacrificial cake, O god — lead him onward to better and better fortune; grant him the divine favour, O youngest one.
O Agni, give him a share in the [wealth won through] glorious praise; give him a share at each recitation of lauds. He becomes dear to Sūrya, dear to Agni; let him burst forth with what is born, burst forth with successive generations.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thee, O Agni, the sacrificers have held as all desirable goods through the days. Seeking riches together with thee, the eager worshippers have opened up the cow-pen.
Agni Vaiśvānara, the guardian of soma, beloved of men, has been praised by the seers. With benevolence may we call on Heaven and Earth; O gods, grant us riches together with good heroes.
The great Hotṛ priest, born like the cloud-born one, the man-seated one, has settled in the lap of the waters. He who was made the firm-upheld one — he, protecting the body, as the guide of riches for the worshipper, branches forth.
Worshipping him in the dwelling-place of the waters, they followed [him] by his tracks like a lost animal. The wise Bhṛgus, seeking with reverence, found him who was lurking in the secret place.
Trita, eagerly seeking, found him abundantly at the top of the inexhaustible Vaibhūvasa. Born to growth in the houses, the young one becomes the navel of the shining realm.
The eager ones have set up with their reverences the gladdening Hotṛ, the forward-leading priest, the guide of rites; they made the purifying, oblation-carrying Arāti into the priest of the clans, establishing him among humans.
The great one arose victorious, the far-inspiring one, who destroys fortresses, though without intellect of his own — those guiding the embryo of the forests have placed the inspired thought; golden-bearded, swift as a horse, rich in wealth he blazes.
Trita, supporting [himself] in the dwelling-places, enveloped, settled inward in the womb. Taking from there, the house-master of the clans is led without restraint to men with his holding of the law.
His unaging flames are the oarsmen of the house; the purifying fires blaze with luminous smoke. White-gleaming, surging, active, dwelling in the forest — like soma-draughts, like winds they move.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni carries forth the trembling flame with his tongue; with his mind he carries forth the marks of the earth. They who are purifying — the Āyavas set up the gladdening Hotṛ, the most worthy of worship, as most fit for sacrifice.
The Agni whom Heaven and Earth brought forth, whom the Waters, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the Bhṛgus brought forth with their powers — Mātariśvan first made the adorable one to be praised; the gods fashioned him as the adorable one for Manu.
Thee whom the gods established as oblation-carrier, the adorable one desired by many humans — thee, O Agni, as thou goest, thou givest sustenance to the praising one; moving god-ward, thou dost bring together many glories.
We, desiring wealth, have grasped thy right hand, O Indra, O lord of riches. For we know thee as the bull-hero, the guardian of the cows — give us a brilliant, virile wealth.
Give us a brilliant, virile wealth — well-weaponed, well-housed, well-guided, four-oceaned, the steadfast foundation of riches — active, praiseworthy, of many gifts.
O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — well-brahmanic, accompanied by the gods, great, wide, deep, of broad base, of renowned wisdom, terrible, overwhelming adversaries.
O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — ever prize-winning, inspiredly heroic, overcoming, touching riches, swelling with growth, of good skill, truly slaying the Dasyus, breaking through the fortresses.
O Indra, give us a brilliant, virile wealth — rich in horses, furnished with chariots, rich in heroes, of a thousand, a hundred contests, of auspicious vow, inspiredly heroic, winning the sun.
The prayer goes forth toward Bṛhaspati of the seven tones, the one whose thought is true, of good wisdom — he who is of the Aṅgiras clan, approachable with reverence — may he give us a brilliant, virile wealth.

title: Rigveda
text:
My lauds, imploring, moving as my messengers, seeking good favour, travel toward Indra — touching the heart, being spoken with the mind; may he give us a brilliant, virile wealth.
What I seek from thee, O Indra, grant us that — the great, unequalled dwelling for the peoples. Let Heaven and Earth speak in agreement with this; give us a brilliant, virile wealth.
I was the first lord of riches; I win wealth perpetually. Living creatures call on me as on a father; I apportion enjoyment to the pious worshipper.
I, Indra, having raised the obstruction and nurtured the Atharvan, produced the cows upon the serpent for Trita. I seize the manly power away from the Dasyus; teaching the cow-pen, [I give] to Dadhīca and Mātariśvan.
For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron bolt; in me the gods have bent their will. My face is hard to endure like that of the sun; people approach me with what has been done and what is to be done.
I sharpen this cattle-winning, horse-winning animal — the one rich in food, golden, with an arrow-swift [movement] — many thousands [I give] to the worshipper, when the soma-draughts with their lauds have gladdened me.
I, Indra, have never lost the prize; I have never yielded to death at any time. Press soma and ask me for riches; O Pūrus, do not fall into ruin in my friendship.
I smote one by one these two who were ever hostile, who armed the bolt against Indra in battle. Those who were calling out I struck down with my blow; speaking firm [words], those who did not bow I made to bow.
I alone am prepared to face one; what then can two, or three, do? I strike many back like heaps of chaff on a threshing floor. Why do my foes who are without Indra blame me?
I extricated Atithigva from the Guṅgus; I sustained nourishment like a Vṛtra-slayer among the clans. When [battle raged] around Parṇayaghna and around Karañja — there I was heard in the great Vṛtra-slaying.

title: Rigveda
text:
Namī Sāpya has come forward to my aid for nourishment and enjoyment; establish friendship twofold through the pursuit of cattle. When I enkindled the lightning in battles for him, then I made him worthy of praise and of laud.
Soma has been seen within this [one], half of it; as guardian he makes half manifest. Wishing to battle the bull with the sharp horn, [the demon] stood waiting for treachery, bound deeply within.
Of the Ādityas, of the Vasus, of the Rudras, I as god do not diminish the ordinance of the gods. They have fashioned me for auspicious power — unconquered, uncast down, invincible.
I give the ancient good to the singer; I make the prayer that is my own growth. I became the impeller of the sacrificer; I am the witness of the non-sacrificer in every contest.
They have made me Indra by name as the divine power; the beings of heaven, of earth, and of the waters [know me thus]. I hold the two bay stallions, swift of diverse courses; I boldly take up the bolt for might.
With my blows I shattered the mantle for the sage; I assisted Kutsa with these aids. I am the slayer of Śuṣṇa, the restraining weapon — one who never gave the noble name to the Dasyu.
Like a father I subdued the Vetasus for conquest; I subdued Tugra and Smadibha for Kutsa. I became the king of the sacrificer when I press forward in battle against the dear untouchable enemy.
I subdued the deer-slayer Mṛgaya for Śrutarvaṇa, who hurled himself [against me] without even following a sign. I made the obedient Veśa for Āyu; I subdued the hexapod Padgṛbhi for Savya.
I am the one who crushed the Dāsa Navavāstava with the great chariot, shattering him like Vṛtra, the Vṛtra-slaying smasher — him who was growing and spreading continuously, who had made a glittering place at the far end of the realm.
I go around the sun with my swift [horses], the Pra-Etaśas, being carried with might. When the human champion called me the shining, clearly victorious one — with my blows I made a Dāsa of the villain.

title: Rigveda
text:
I, the slayer of seven, mightier than Nahuṣa, caused Turvaśa and Yadu to be heard by my power. I, with might overpowering might, caused to decrease nine and ninety of the weakened ones, subduing the others.
I, the bull, the fast-moving one, held the seven streams as ploughs upon the earth. I, of excellent resolve, cross through the floods; I found through battle the way to the sun for Manu, for the sacrifice.
I held therein what even the god Tvaṣṭṛ could not hold as shining — the desirable, mixed soma with the honey of honey in the udders of cows, in their bellies, the Śvātra soma.
Thus Indra, whose bounty is true, has encompassed the gods and men with his impulse, the Bountiful One. All these feats of thine, O lord of the bay steeds, O mighty one — swift heroes of their own renown declare them.
Sing forth with laud to the great one who exhilarates himself with the soma-drink, to the all-human, the all-being Indra — whose fair-jawed might, whose great glory and manly power the two worlds serve.
He truly, the manly Indra, mighty through friendship, ever-active, praised, exhilarates himself for the pious man. In all charges, in prize-winning actions, at Vṛtra, in the waters, thou rejoicest, O hero, O lord of the good.
Who are thy men, O Indra, who desire thy bounty? Who would honor thy auspicious shared goodwill? Who would urge thee for prize and for lordly power? Who [would urge thee] in the waters, in fair regions, in virile might?
Thou hast become great through the sacred formulation, O Indra; thou hast become the one worthy of worship at all soma-pressings. Thou hast become the impeller of men in every contest; the foremost prayer, O one seen by all.
Who then is greater than thee who lovest the sacrifice? The peoples know thy great protection. Mayest thou be truly unaging and growing, winning all these soma-pressings, O industrious one.

title: Rigveda
text:
Win all these soma-pressings by thine own power, O Son of Strength, thou who holdest them. For thy choosing, the vessel [is set], by the sacred ordinance perpetuated; the sacrifice, the sacred formula, the brahman speech held upraised.
The inspired ones who are made brahmanic by thee are present at the pressing — for giving of riches and of goods. May they go forth on the path of thy goodwill through mind, in the exhilaration of the pressed soma-drink.
Great and thick was that membrane — great it was — wrapped in which you entered the waters. One god alone, O Agni Jātavedas, saw all your bodies manifested in many forms.
Who saw me? Which was that god who beheld my bodies manifested in many forms? Where dwell, O Mitra and Varuṇa, all the divine fuel-faggots of Agni that lead to the gods?
We sought you, O Jātavedas, hidden in many forms, entered, O Agni, into the waters, into the plants. Yama revealed you, O Citrabhānu, as you shone forth glowing from the ten kindling-woods.
I came here, O Varuṇa, fleeing from the office of Hotṛ, lest the gods should harness me to that task. My bodies entered in many places — of that matter I, Agni, was unaware.
Come! Manu, pious and desirous of sacrifice, is ready; thou dwellest in the darkness, O Agni. Make the paths easy that lead to the gods; willingly convey the oblations.
The earlier brothers of Agni perished following this same course like a charioteer on the road. Therefore, O Varuṇa, I came far away in fear, trembling like a gayal from the bowstring of the archer.
We shall grant you ageless life, O Agni, so that, O Jātavedas, harnessed, you shall not be harmed. Then joyfully you shall carry the share of the oblation to the gods, O noble-born.
Give me the prayājas and the anuyājas alone as my exclusive, vigorous share of the oblation — ghee, and the essence of waters and plants. And may Agni's life be long, O gods.

title: Rigveda
text:
Yours alone shall be the prayājas and the anuyājas as vigorous shares of the oblation. Let this entire sacrifice be yours, O Agni; let the four quarters bow down to you.
All you gods, instruct me how I, chosen as Hotṛ by Manu, shall sit and perform the rite. Tell me what the share-apportionment is to you, by what path I may bring the oblations to you.
I, the mightier Hotṛ, took my seat; all the gods and Maruts urge me on. Day after day the Adhvaryu rite is yours, O Aśvins; the Brahman becomes the kindling-wood and the offering is yours.
This one who is the Hotṛ — who then is he of Yama? Whom do they adorn when the gods anoint? Day after day, month after month he is born anew — the gods have appointed him carrier of oblations.
Me the gods appointed carrier of oblations, though long hidden, wandering through many difficulties. Agni, knowing all, shall order our sacrifice — of five courses, threefold, and sevenfold in thread.
I shall worship immortality and heroic strength for you so that I may make wide space for you, O gods. I shall place Indra's thunderbolt in his arms; then shall he conquer all these hosts.
Three hundreds and three thousands — thirty and nine gods together — attended to Agni; they sprinkled him with ghee, spread the sacred grass for him, and then installed him as Hotṛ.
He whom we sought in our mind has come — knowing the sacrifice, wise, the many-jointed, the discerning. He, mightier in worship, shall sacrifice for us at the divine assembly; let him take his seat as our closest, foremost.
The Hotṛ has taken his seat, the worthier one; he beholds the well-set offerings. Come! let us worship the gods worthy of worship; let us praise with ghee those who merit praise.
He made our divine communion excellent today; we have found the hidden tongue of the sacrifice. He has come bearing life, clad in fragrance; he made our invocation of the gods auspicious today.

title: Rigveda
text:
Let me today utter first that speech by which the gods overpowered the Asuras. O eaters of vigour, and you who are worthy of sacrifice — ye five peoples, delight in my Hotṛ-call.
Let the five peoples delight in my Hotṛ-call — those born of cattle and those worthy of sacrifice. May the Earth protect us from earthly distress; may the Atmosphere protect us from what comes from heaven.
Spinning the thread, follow the gleam of the sky's expanse; protect the luminous paths made by the mind. Weave, without breaks, the waters that have been sung; be Manu, beget the divine people.
Tie the axle-pins and fasten them, O ye who have soma; trim the reins and adorn them. Drive from both sides the eight-yoked chariot whereby the gods drove toward the beloved.
The stony river flows — grasp one another, rise up, cross over, O friends! Here let us leave behind those who were unfit; we shall cross over toward the blessings, toward the prizes.
Tvaṣṭṛ knows the wisdom — the most artful of craftsmen — bearing the vessels, most comforting, fit for the gods to drink from. He now sharpens the iron axe with which the Etaśa-horse, Lord of Prayer, shall cut.
Now, O sages who are being perfected, sharpen yourselves with the chisels with which you work for immortality. Knowing, cut out the hidden tracks by which the gods attained immortality.
They placed in the womb of the woman the calf, hidden with secret mind and tongue. He who is well-disposed, ever seeking union, reaches victory — the worshipper wins it alone.
Well do we proclaim that glory of yours, O Maghavan, in your greatness — when both the frightened worlds called upon you. You protected the gods, overpowered the Dāsa with your force; for that offspring you trained, O Indra.
When you went about growing in your own body, declaring your powers, O Indra, among the peoples — may it not be that the battles they speak of come to nothing; you have not yet ceased to know the enemy.

title: Rigveda
text:
Who of the earlier sages before us ever reached the full measure of your greatness — you who together generated both your mother and your father from your own body?
Your four mighty names, belonging to the bull, are inviolable. Only you, O Maghavan, know them all, those names by which you performed your deeds.
You alone hold all the riches — those that are manifest and those that are hidden. Do not, O Maghavan, disappoint my desire; you, Indra, are the knower and you are the giver.
He who placed light within light, who mingled sweetnesses with sweetness — to that dear Indra this praise, this mighty utterance, was spoken from the brahman-made high hymn.
Far away is that hidden name, in remote regions — the name by which both the frightened ones, growing old, called upon you. You propped up both earth and sky together, O Maghavan, blazing with power, protecting your brother's sons.
Great is that hidden name, widely touching all, by which what was and what shall be comes to be. The ancient, born light that is dear to him — the dear five entered into union.
He filled both the worlds and the middle space; the five gods he filled seasonally, seven by seven. With thirty-four he views them in manifold forms, by a light of uniform appearance and varied ordinance.
When you, Dawn, first shone forth among the radiant ones, you generated nourishment from nourishment. What is the lesser kinship, what the higher? Great, for the great one, is that single Asura-power.
The wandering moon, sleeping at the assembly of many, though young, was devoured by the grey one. Behold the divine mystery in its greatness — he who died today was alive yesterday.
By his own might, the reddish fair-winged hero, great, brave, forever unassailable — whatever he perceives, that truly is not fruitless; he is winner and giver of desirable wealth.

title: Rigveda
text:
With these he received his bull-powers and manly vigour, wherewith the Vajra-bearer anointed himself for the slaying of Vṛtra. Those gods who were born through the greatness of deeds being performed — they performed their acts according to Ṛta.
Generating deeds in union, all-powerful, slayer of the wicked, all-minded, overpowering the strong — having drunk the Soma, growing great from the sky, the hero drove out the Dasyus from battle.
This one is yours, and yet another is beyond — enter union with the third light. At the gathering-in be lovely in body; be dear to the gods in the highest birthplace.
She who leads your body, O Vājin, may she grant us beauty, shelter to you. Untroubled, for upholding the great gods, measure out your own light as in the sky.
You are the swift horse, fleet by means of the fleet; well-sped, you delight in the hymn of praise; well-sped, you go to heaven. Well-sped, follow the primeval truths of dharma; well-sped among the gods, well-sped along the path.
Not even the Fathers could control the greatness of these; the gods placed their will in the gods. What they covered and what they set ablaze entered back again into their bodies.
With their powers they circled all the expanse of the sky, measuring the primeval, immeasurable stations. They held all the worlds within their bodies; they stretched them out manifoldly among the offspring.
The sons established the Asura, the finder of heaven, in two ways by the third deed. The Fathers, together with the fathers' world, stretched the thread of their own offspring through the lower ones.
As a ship crosses the flood, the quarters of the earth — by blessings may we pass beyond all difficulties. The one of great praise, through his greatness, established his offspring in the lower and even in the higher regions.

title: Rigveda
text:
May we not stray from the path, may we not stray from the sacrifice, O Indra, we who have pressed the Soma. May the ill-wishers not stand among us.
That thread which perfects the sacrifice, stretched out among the gods — may we attain it, duly offered.
Now we call upon the mind — with the Nārāśaṁsa-Soma, and with the praises of the Pitṛs.
May your mind return again — for will, for discernment, for living, and long to behold the Sun.
May the Fathers restore our mind; may the divine company give it back. May we be joined with the living host.
We, O Soma, in your covenant, bearing the mind in our bodies — may we, endowed with offspring, be joined together.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to Yama Vaivasvata — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the sky, to the earth — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the four-cornered earth — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the four quarters — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the ocean, the flood — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the bright rays, to the heights — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the waters, to the plants — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the Sun, to the Dawn — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the great mountains — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

title: Rigveda
text:
That mind of yours which has gone far away to this entire universe — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to the farthest of the far regions — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
That mind of yours which has gone far away to what has been and what shall be — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.
Lengthen out your life further, newer and newer — like a good charioteer with an able-willed chariot. Then, O Cyavana, rise up to your great purpose; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.
With a hymn we shall win wealth, a treasure of food; we shall win splendid fame in many ways. May all these things rejoice our singer; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.
May we become the chief with manly powers — as the sky does not injure the earth, nor the mountains the plains. May our singer know all these things for us; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.
O Soma, do not hand us over to death; may we still see the sun rising. May old age appointed by the gods be friendly to us; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.
O Asunīti, hold the mind within us; for living, extend our life well. Grant us the sight of the sun; with ghee do you strengthen your body.
O Asunīti, give back sight to us; give back breath, give enjoyment here to us. May we long see the sun rising; O Anumati, be gracious to us, bring us well-being.
May the Earth give back our life-breath; may the divine Sky give it back; may the Atmosphere give it back. May Soma give our body back; may Pūṣan give back the well-being that is on the path.
Blessed be both worlds for the good-kinsman — the two young mothers of Ṛta. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.

title: Rigveda
text:
In pairs and in triplets the healing remedies move down from heaven; some roam the earth one by one. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.
O Indra, set in motion the ox who drew the cart for the queen of the Uśīnaras. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.
We have approached the man of dazzling appearance, praised among the Māhīnas — bearing reverence, we have come.
Incomparable, piercing, fierce, the chariot that follows the course — may we share in the true lord of the chariot.
He who stood over men like a buffalo, furnished with a sharp-pointed weapon — and also one with a blunted weapon in battle.
He in whose covenant Ikṣvāku, rich in wealth, prospers and thrives — like the five peoples in the sky.
O Indra, sustain Kṣatrāsamāti in his chariots, foremost among the foremost — to be seen like the sun in the sky.
You yoke the two red horses from the clan of Agastya. O King, you have overcome all the Paṇis who gave no gifts.
Here is your mother, here is your father, here the living one has come. Here is your restoration, O Subandhu — come out, come forth.
As they bind a yoke with a threefold tie for its support — so has he held your mind fast, for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.
As this great Earth holds these forest trees in place — so has he held your mind fast, for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.
From Yama Vaivasvata I have brought back the mind of Subandhu — for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.
Downward the wind blows, downward the sun burns; downward the cow gives her milk — may your disease go downward.
This hand of mine is full of fortune; this hand is even more fortunate. This hand contains all medicines; this hand is the gentle healing touch.

title: Rigveda
text:
This praise-hymn truly Rudraic, rich in laud, was found through insight and power in the midst of battle; when his parents, most bountiful, were creating, may he lead the group, may he smite and summon the seven priests.
He, striving to win a gift worthy of gratitude — Cyavana — measured out the altar with skilled hands; he the foremost in sweet speech, pressing ever onward, poured forth semen as a flood of water flowing.
Like the mind, sharp in those invocations — you two inspired ones, swiftly moving, win by your power; he who, mighty in strength, with his shafts laid blood upon his arm's direction and smote it.
When the dark one settled among the ruddy cows, I call upon you, O Aśvins, grandsons of Heaven; come to my sacrifice, come to my food, you who have won your way, guiding without forgetfulness.
He whose heroic deed was set in motion and accomplished — the manly one thrust it away; he draws back again what was carried away from the maiden, borne along from his daughter, he the unhurt one.
When in the midst there arose what had to be done in the encounter — the father making love to the young woman — the two, parting asunder, let fall a little seed; it was poured upon the back, in the womb of the one who had done well.
When the father, mounting his own daughter, united with her on the ground and poured forth his seed — the gods, deep in thought, generated the sacred hymn and fashioned Vāstoṣpati, the guardian of vows.
He, like a bull, shot forth foam in the contest; he who was poor in wisdom went away from there; the right hand turned back running like a foot — those speckled ones did not seize them for me.
Like a swift carrier eagerly approaching the offspring, like a naked one approaching the udder of fire; he who wins the fuel and wins also the prize — that supporter was born with force, ever youthful.

title: Rigveda
text:
Quickly the Navagvas came to friendship with the maiden, speaking truth and reaching the right season; those of double strength who came to the herdsman — without the right fee — sought to milk the unyielding one.
The yet newer friendship of the maiden, like a gift and like seed, hastening toward truth; when they sacrificed to your pure treasure — to the milk of the cow that gives all fullness.
When the cattle awaken separated in the rear — so says the speaker, he who is generous — the craftsmen, faultless, seek the substance of riches and pervade all wealth close by.
Those who sit around came to that very thing — sitting in many places, seeking to overcome Nārṣada; the unhurt one opened what was knotted of Śuṣṇa, finding what lay hidden of the many-fathered one.
Bhar-gas — 'the Radiance' — so the gods call him; like the sun, those who have taken seat in the triple resting-place; Agni too they call Jātavedas — hear us, O Hotṛ, priest of truth, O priest who never fails.
And those two Rudraic, radiant ones, the Nāsatyas — O Indra — I wish to worship for gladness; like Manu, generous to the one whose grass is strewn, joyful, with offerings set in place, they are worshipped among the folk.
This king, when praised, is a worshipful creator; the inspired one crosses the waters by his own dam; he made Kakṣīvant tremble, he who is Agni, swift and hurling like the rim of a wheel on a racehorse.
He the twice-bound, the Vaitaraṇa, the sacrificer — that the cow of all fullness and the horse may be milked; when he unites with lauds Mitra and Varuṇa, with the highest protections of Aryaman.
Bound to that, the sage in heaven establishes thought; Nābhānediṣṭha speaks forth, piercing deep — that is our navel, and the highest also; I was that, how many soever times in the past.
This is my navel, here is my seat; these are my gods, I am here entire; twice-born, firstborn of truth — this cow yielded her milk as she came into being.

title: Rigveda
text:
Then the charming, tireless, far-shining one will flow down; he who turns in two directions, conquering the woods — when the row of teeth rises like a child newly grown, the mother swiftly brings forth the hard, swelling member.
Then the cows followed the likeness of the maiden after someone who had fallen asleep; hear us, you of good treasure — you who have grown by the swift gifts of him who slays horses.
Now do you, O Indra, know us, O lord of men, thunderbolt-armed, for great wealth; protect us and guard our liberal lords in your faultless, golden assistance.
And when the two kings in the contest for cattle — Saraṇyu swift-moving and Jaranya toward the singer — the most inspired was dearest among them; he will carry them forward and lead them across.
Now indeed in the prosperity of his conquering wealth we praise freely — that we seek even now; Saraṇyu's son, the horse, and the inspired one are both fighters for fame.
If for your two's friendship — for our band of heroes — the reverential praise-hymn has found favor; in whom from all sides the converging songs unite, may the path, ancient as ever, be given for truth's song.
He, praised with waters, is truly god-possessed; of good alliance, with reverence and well-spoken hymns, he grows with lauds and words — for now indeed he travels along the milk-stream of the dawn cow.
Be you then, O great adorable gods, of one accord for our aid; you who lead prizes hither from afar, you who are the wise, clear-sighted discerners.
Those who, consecrated by sacrifice and the sacrificial gift, won the friendship of Indra and immortality — to them, O Āṅgirasas, may good fortune come; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.
Those fathers who drove forth the cow-rich treasure, who with truth broke open the Vala cave in the circling year — long life be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.

title: Rigveda
text:
Those who by truth raised the sun up into heaven, who spread wide the earth, the mother — good offspring be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.
This navel-born one speaks sweetly in your home — O sons of gods, O seers, hear this; excellent Brahmanhood be yours, O Āṅgirasas; O wise ones, receive the gift of Manu.
Of varied forms are these seers, of deep inspiration — the Āṅgirasas who are his sons were born from Agni himself.
Those who were born around Agni, of varied forms born from Heaven — Navagva and Daśagva, most Āṅgirasa, together are generous among the gods.
With Indra as their ally, the inspired singers drove out the cow-and-horse-full pen; the eight-eared ones who gave me a thousand made glory among the gods.
Let this Manu now spring forth and grow like a sprouting shoot — he who straightway is generous with a thousand and a hundred horses for the gift.
No one reaches it — like the ridge of heaven, untouchable; the bounty of Sāvarṇi has spread wide like a river.
And the Dāsas who dwell around, well-directed and girt with cattle — Yadu and Turvaśa too have honored me.
The village leader who gives thousands — may Manu not be harmed; may his bounty come forth along with the sun; may the gods extend the life of Sāvarṇi in whom, untired, we shall win the prize.
Those gods who shine forth from the distance, kin to the waters, dear to Manu, of Vivasvat's lineage, who sit upon the sacrificial grass of Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa — may they speak on our behalf.
All your names, O gods, are worthy of reverence and praise, and worthy of sacrifice; those of you born from Aditi, from the waters, from the earth — may they hear my call here.
Those for whom the mother pours sweet milk as first-flow — Aditi, the heaven, she whose lap is the rock; those mighty with hymns, bull-strong, sleep-bringing Ādityas — rejoice with them for our well-being.

title: Rigveda
text:
They watch over men, they are unwinking, worthy of honor; the great gods have attained immortality; their chariots are of light, their magic conquers winter, sinless — they dwell on heaven's height for our well-being.
The universal rulers who grow well, who have come to the sacrifice, who unconfounded have their dwelling in heaven — revere them with reverence and excellent lauds, the great Ādityas and Aditi, for our well-being.
Who among you fulfills the praise that you delight in, O All Gods, wherever you stand among men? Who makes the sacrifice ready for you, mighty-born, who will lead us beyond danger for our well-being?
Those to whom Manu first offered the priestly call, with kindled fire, in mind, with the seven priests — may those Ādityas grant fearless shelter; make easy our paths, the paths of well-being.
Those who are lords of the world, the wise, the thinkers of all that is fixed and all that moves — may those gods save us today from guilt done and undone, for our well-being.
In battles we call upon Indra, easy to invoke, the deliverer from distress, doer of good, the divine person; Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa for winning, Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, the Maruts — for our well-being.
Let us mount the good-shielding earth, faultless heaven, Aditi the good-sheltering, good-leading divine ship with good oars, sinless and never sinking, for our well-being.
O all adorable ones, speak out for our aid; protect us from the ill-road and from what assaults us; with your true invocation of gods we call you — O gods who hear, come to our protection and well-being.
Drive away disease, all evil, the unoffered, ill-will, the hard-to-understand, of the malicious one; O gods, keep enmity far from us; grant us wide shelter for our well-being.
Unharmed, that mortal thrives in everything and multiplies with offspring beyond law; he whom the Ādityas lead with good guidance past all evils — for well-being.

title: Rigveda
text:
He whom the gods protect in the winning of the prize, whom the Maruts, slayers of heroes, protect when prizes are set — on that chariot, going forth at dawn, O Indra, ever victorious, never harmed, let us mount — for well-being.
Blessing on our roads and on the desert ways, blessing in the waters, in the fortified sun-filled place; blessing on us in the births of sons, in the womb — Maruts, grant us blessing and wealth.
Blessing, indeed the best as she travels onward, she who brings treasure-wealth, who moves toward the good — may she protect us at home and abroad; may she be the self-entering one, guarded by the gods.
Thus the son of Plāti, the thoughtful one, has magnified you all, O Ādityas, O Aditi; you lordly men — the divine race has been praised by the immortal with his song.
In the procession of which of the gods shall we think of a welcome name among those who hear? Who will be merciful? Which one will bring us joy? Which one will return to us with his aid?
The purposes stir the purposes, the thoughts in the hearts; the longing ones desire and fly in all directions — no mercifulness is found other than in these; on the gods my desires have been set.
With song I honor manly Pūṣan, the unhideable, Agni kindled by the gods; Sūrya and Māsa, the Moon, Yama in heaven, Trita, Vāyu, Uṣas, Aktu, and the Aśvins.
How does the seer, mighty in strength, with what song, with excellent praises magnify Bṛhaspati? May Aja Ekapāda, with those whose calls are good and whose hymns are apt, and Ahir Budhnya hear the oblation.
In the law of the birth of Dakṣa and Aditi, you seek to favor the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa; Aryaman of unblocked paths and many chariots — the seven-priest, of varied forms in the births.
May those swift, contest-hearing ones, all the prize-bearing, carefully moving ones, hear our call; they who by themselves, like a thousand-winning sacrifice, carry off great wealth in the battles.

title: Rigveda
text:
Magnify with praises Vāyu, who yokes his chariot, and Pūraṃdhi, seek the friendship of Pūṣan; for they accompany the will of the divine Savitṛ in his impulse, companions together, of one mind.
The thrice-seven rivers, the great waters, for our aid; the forest lords, the mountains, Agni — we call; Kṛśānu, the archers, Tiṣya in his seat, Rudra among the Rudras, the Rudraic one, we invoke.
May Sarasvatī, Sarayu, and Sindhu with their waves — the great ones, the nourishing rivers — come with aid; O divine waters, O mothers who give good pleasure, sing to us your milk rich as ghee and sweet as honey.
May the mother Bṛhadivā hear us, and Tvaṣṭṛ as father with the gods and the birth-goddesses; Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, Rathaspati, Bhaga, the joyful hymn — may the praise of the self-offering one protect us.
The sight of him is joyful, like a nourishing dwelling; blessed is the praise-song of Rudrāṇī and the Maruts; may we be renowned with cattle among the folk, always, O gods, let us be joined with refreshment.
The vision that you, O Maruts, O Indra, O gods, O Varuṇa, O Mitra — that you have given me: nourish it like a cow with milk; will you indeed carry my songs upon your chariot?
Will you, O Maruts, again somehow become aware of this our same-born kinship? There where we first meet at the navel-point — there may Aditi establish our bond of brotherhood.
For they — the two great mothers Heaven and Earth, the divine goddesses, worshipped by the gods from the beginning — both bear both, with their wealth-bearing ones; they pour manifold seed along with the fathers.
That priestly office spreads and wins all desirable things; Bṛhaspati and Aramati, the more wonderful; where the pressing stone is called the great honey-presser, the wise men have rejoiced with their thoughts.
Thus the seer, mighty in strength, knower of truth, seeking wealth, desiring riches — with his lauds and thoughts here the inspired one nourished the heavenly birth of the homestead.

title: Rigveda
text:
Thus the son of Plāti, the thoughtful one, has magnified you all, O Ādityas, O Aditi; you lordly men — the divine race has been praised by the immortal with his song.
Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Vāyu, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī — of one accord; the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the great sun, Soma, Rudra, Aditi, and Brahmaṇaspati.
Indra and Agni, lords of the good in the slaying of Vṛtra, mutually impelling each other, dwelling in the same abode; they filled great mid-air with their might; Soma, gleaming with ghee, stirring forth greatness.
By the greatness of those great and unhurt ones, knowers of truth, who increase the truth, I urge forth these praises; they who have the streaming wave and marvellous bounty — may they, good allies, grant us greatness.
Heaven-bright, the mid-spaces, the shining realms, the Heaven and Earth — they prop up the earth with their might; like the nourishing ones, magnifying, of good gifts, the gods, the sages, are praised for Manu.
Seek to please Mitra and give to Varuṇa — those two universal kings who do not fail in mind; whose great abode shines by law, of both of whom both world-halves are encompassed, never lowly.
The cow who circles the prepared track, giving milk, obedient to her vow, never failing — she who speaks out, shall give to the one who gives to Varuṇa, shall give to the gods with the offering, to Vivasvat.
Those who dwell in heaven, whose tongue is fire, who increase truth, who sit contemplating the womb of truth; having propped up the sky they created the waters with might, and having generated the sacrifice they wiped themselves clean.
The two parents who guard on every side, the ancient and primeval ones, dwelling together in the womb of truth — Heaven and Earth, sharing the vow of Varuṇa, swell out ghee-rich milk for the great bull.

title: Rigveda
text:
Parjanya and Vāta, the two bulls full of rain; Indra and Vāyu, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — we call the gods, the Ādityas, and Aditi; those of the earth, those of heaven, those in the waters.
Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, the Ṛbhus who make glad, the two divine priests, Uṣas — for our well-being; Bṛhaspati, who devours Vṛtra, the wise one; Soma, Indra's own — these too we seek as prize-winners.
They generated the Brahman, the cow, the horse, the herbs, the forest trees, the earth, the mountains, the waters; raising the sun in heaven, the good-giving ones, releasing the noble vows upon the earth.
You freed Bhujyu from distress, O Aśvins; you quickened the dark son of Vadhrimatī; you brought a bride to Vimada, the love-passionate one; you two released Viṣṇāpva, the all-bodied.
Pāvīravī, the thunder, one-footed Aja, the support of heaven, Sindhu, the waters, those of the sea — may all the gods hear my words, and Sarasvatī together with her thoughts, the full-gifted one.
All the gods, with full thoughts and full gifts, Manu's adorable ones, immortal, knowers of truth; the ones who grant, who approach, who know the sun's realm — may they delight in the solar songs, in the Brahman, in the well-spoken hymn.
Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have spread over all the worlds; may they grant us today the widely-proclaimed; always protect us with blessings.
I call upon the gods of great glory for our well-being, makers of light, wise in the sacrifice; those who have grown exceedingly, all-knowing, with Indra as their chief, immortal, who increase the truth.
Impelled by Indra, guided by Varuṇa, those who have attained a share of the light of the sun — in the company of the Maruts, in the fortified place, let us think devotion; may the sages, not being stingy, generate the sacrifice.
May Indra with the Vasus guard our home; may Aditi with the Ādityas grant us shelter; may the divine Rudra with the Rudras be gracious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the goddesses quicken us to well-being.

title: Rigveda
text:
Aditi, Heaven and Earth, the great truth, Indra and Viṣṇu, the Maruts, the great sun — we call the Ādityan gods for aid, the Vasus, the Rudras, and Savitṛ of wonderful deeds.
Sarasvan with his thoughts, Varuṇa who holds to his vow, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Mahiman, Vāyu, the Aśvins — makers of Brahman, immortal, all-knowing — may they grant us triple-walled shelter from distress.
Manly be the sacrifice, let the adorable ones be powerful bulls; bull-like are the gods, bull-like the oblation-makers; manly are Heaven and Earth, the guardians of truth; the bull is Parjanya and manly are those who praise the bull.
I call upon Agni and Soma, the mighty bulls, much praised, mighty bulls, for the winning of the prize; those two who have been worshipped as bulls by the worship of the gods — may they grant us triple shelter.
Firm in their vow, lordly, performing the sacrifice, of great luster, the glory of the rites; fire-offering, winning truth, without treachery — they released the waters at the conquest of Vṛtra.
Heaven and Earth, generating in accord with their vows, water, herbs, the sacrificial forest plants — they filled the mid-air and the sun for aid; the gods wiped themselves clean upon the willing body.
The Ṛbhus, supporters of heaven, skilled-handed; Vāta and Parjanya of the great bull's thunder — may the waters and the herbs extend our songs; may Bhaga, Rāti, and the prize-bearers come to my call.
Ocean, the rivers, the dust-realm of mid-air; one-footed Aja, the rumbling wave — may Ahir Budhnya hear my words, and all the gods, and my sages.
May we be your Manus for the feast of the gods; lead our sacrifice forward on the good path; O Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, good-giving ones — quicken these Brahman-words as they are being recited.
The two divine priests — first among the household priests — I follow the path of truth rightly; I seek the lord of the field, the neighbor-god; all the immortal gods who do not fail.

title: Rigveda
text:
The Vasiṣṭhas have spoken the word like a father, praising the gods like seers for our well-being; coming as desired like pleased kinsmen — O gods, shake down wealth upon us.
Vasiṣṭha has praised the immortal gods who have spread over all the worlds; may they grant us today the widely-proclaimed; always protect us with blessings.
Our father found this vision of seven heads, born from truth, the vast one; truly the universal Ayāsya generated the fourth — reciting the laud for Indra.
Reciting truth, thinking straight — the sons of heaven, the heroes of Asura; the Āṅgirasas, bearing the inspired seat, thought on the first abode of the sacrifice.
Like swans with chattering companions, loosening the rocky fetters — Bṛhaspati, roaring forth, drove the cows and sent them away; the knowing one sang out loud.
Down from two and beyond the third — the cows standing hidden in the bondage of falsehood; Bṛhaspati seeking light in the darkness drove the dawns upward, for he opened all three.
Splitting apart the eastward-lying city, he cut off three together from the ocean; Bṛhaspati found the Dawn, the Sun, the cow, and the hymn — thundering as the sky.
Indra split open Vala, the guardian of the milch cows, like an elephant with his roar; seeking the rich mixture with his sweat-smeared limbs, he made the Paṇi weep and seized the cows.
He, with his true, shining companions, burst asunder the bow-stringed one with prize-seeking; Brahmaṇaspati distributed the wealth with bulls and boars who sweat with heat.
They, with truthful minds, seeking the lord of cattle, set the cows in motion with their thoughts; Bṛhaspati, and those who drink away blame of one another, released the dawn cows with their own yokings.
Magnifying him with auspicious thoughts — him who roars like a lion in his seat — may we rejoice after Bṛhaspati, the mighty bull, the victorious, in every battle and contest.

title: Rigveda
text:
When he won the prize of all forms and climbed to heaven, to the upper dwellings — magnifying Bṛhaspati, the bull, though separated, they bore the light in their mouths.
Make true the blessing with your life-giving ones, for you protect even the singer with your own forces; may all the enemies be thrust to the rear — hear this, O Heaven and Earth, you who are all-pervading.
Indra with his might shattered the head of great Arbuda of the great wave; he slew the serpent and released the seven rivers — may Heaven and Earth together with the gods protect us.
Like birds protecting their watering place, babbling like the sound of a thunder-cloud — the mountain-leaping waves in joy roared forth to Bṛhaspati with their songs.
The Āṅgirasa, reaching his goal with the cows, led forth as Bhaga leads Aryaman; like Mitra he anoints the lord and lady among the folk — O Bṛhaspati, urge on the swift ones in the contest.
Going straight, like guests arriving, vigorous, desirable, beautifully golden, of blameless form — Bṛhaspati sifted the cows out from the mountains as if threshing grain from the straw.
Sprinkling the womb of honey and truth, the hymn hurled like a meteor from heaven; Bṛhaspati, lifting the cows from the rock, split the earth's skin as with water.
With light he drove darkness from the midair as wind drives moss from the water; Bṛhaspati, having stroked the cloud of Vala, brought in the cows like the wind brings a cloud.
When Bṛhaspati broke the vitality of the abusive Vala with fire-heated hymns — as a tongue laps up what surrounds the teeth — he revealed the hidden stores of the dawn cows.
Bṛhaspati knew the hidden name of those sun-cows in their dwelling in the secret place; like breaking the egg of a bird, he drove the dawn cows up from the mountain by himself.
He saw honey encased in stone, like a low fish lodged in water; Bṛhaspati tore that out as a cup from a tree, cleaving it with a roar.

title: Rigveda
text:
He found the Uṣases, he found the sun, he found Agni; he pushed back the darkness with the hymn; Bṛhaspati tore out the marrow of Vala who was cow-bodied, as one does from a joint.
As frost strips leaves from forests, Vala wept for his cows taken by Bṛhaspati; what was done could not be undone, done irrevocably — as the sun and moon rise alternating from each other.
Like decorating a dark horse with ornamental stones, the fathers decorated heaven with the stars; they set darkness in the night, light in the day — Bṛhaspati clove the rock and found the cows.
We have done this reverence to him who echoes like a thundercloud, who follows after the many; Bṛhaspati — may he set life-power for us with cattle, with horses, with heroes, with men.
Blessed is the sight of Agni Vādhrya-aśva, beautiful his leadership, his coming pleasant; when the Sumitras kindle him at the head of the folk, fed with ghee, he shines and blazes forth.
Ghee is the growth of Agni Vādhrya-aśva, ghee is his food, ghee is his nourishment; fed with ghee he spreads out widely — the oblation of clarified butter glows like the sun.
That face of yours, O Agni, that Manu kindled, that Sumitrā kindled — may this now be newer; shine brilliantly, take delight in the songs, win the prize, and establish glory here.
That you whom Vādhrya-aśva, the praised one, first kindled, O Agni — may he now take delight in this; be our protector and body-guard; protect the gift that this here is for you from us.
Be glorious and be a herdsman for Vādhrya-aśva; may the ill-will of men not pass beyond you; bold as a hero, moving on, the Sumitrā — now I shall proclaim the name of Vādhrya-aśva.
You gathered the level and mountain treasures; you conquered the Dāsa hosts and the Ārya foes; bold as a hero, moving men — do you, O Agni, overwhelm those who make battle against us.

title: Rigveda
text:
Of far-stretching flame, of great udder is this Agni; with a thousand stars, with a hundred paths, skillful; brilliant among the brilliant, tended by men, he shines among the Sumitras who seek the gods.
In you, O Jātavedas, a well-milking cow pours freely, the inexhaustible, of all fullness; O Agni, you are kindled by men of good gifts, by the Sumitras who seek the gods.
Even the immortal gods, O Jātavedas, proclaimed the greatness of Vādhrya-aśva; when human folk came to consult you, you conquered with the men who magnified you.
Like a father bearing a son upon his lap, Vādhrya-aśva has tended you, O Agni; taking pleasure in his fuel — the youngest one — you overcame those who had grown weak, even the earlier ones.
Always Agni has overcome the enemies of Vādhrya-aśva with men who press Soma; you burned the common meeting-place, O bright-shining one; you struck down even the growing one who had grown weak.
This Agni of Vādhrya-aśva, the Vṛtra-slayer, kindled of old, to be invoked with reverence — may he stand over our non-kinsmen and kinsmen alike; overwhelm those who are hostile, O Vādhrya-aśva.
O Agni, take pleasure in this my fuel at Iḷā's place, delight in the ghee-laden offering; on the heights of the earth, in the clear days, rise up straight for the worship of the gods, O wise one.
May Narāśaṃsa, first-farer of the gods, come here with his all-formed horses; let the most divine among the divine ones, along the path of truth with reverence, drip the sacrificial offering for the gods.
Most frequently do those men who hold the oblation beseech Agni for the embassy; with swiftest horses, with well-rolling chariot, bring hither the gods; sit down here as Hotṛ.
Let the god-beloved sacred grass be spread out crosswise, long and fragrant for us; with an unhostile mind, O god, worship with the barhis the willing gods with Indra as their chief.

title: Rigveda
text:
Touch the higher ridge of heaven, or spread out with the full measure of the earth; O eager divine doors, with greatness through the great ones, support the divine chariot of the chariot-lover.
The two divine daughters of heaven, of beautiful craft — Dawn and Night — let them sit down in their place; may the gods, eager and willing, sit in your wide, blessed lap, O you two.
The pressing stone stands upright, the great fire is kindled, in the dear abodes in Aditi's lap; the two household priests, the seasonal sacrificers in this sacrifice — may the more knowing ones gain wealth through worship.
O three goddesses — Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Mahī — take your seat on this best-of-barhis which we have made comfortable; may the divine Iḷā, with ghee-steps, take pleasure in the sacrifice set right as Manu's, with well-placed oblations.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, when you attained charm, when you became a companion of the Āṅgirasas — knowing that, approach the path of the gods; eager, O giver of wealth, of good treasure, do you worship.
O Lord of the Forest, bound with the cord, knowing — bring hither along the path of the gods; may the god make the oblations sweet; may Heaven and Earth protect my call.
O Agni, bring Varuṇa for our worship, and Indra from the sky, the Maruts from mid-air; may all the adorable ones take their seat on the barhis — Svāhā! May the immortal gods rejoice.
O Bṛhaspati, that first beginning of Vāc — when they set forth, giving names — that which was their best, that which was pure and free from blemish: it was hidden in them and revealed through love.
Sifting the flour as with a sieve — therein the wise ones fashioned Speech with their mind. Friends discerned their friendships there; good fortune was sealed within their speech.
By sacrifice they traced the track of Speech; they found her entered and dwelling among the seers. Fetching her, they distributed her in many places; the seven chanters glorify her together.

title: Rigveda
text:
Yet one man, though seeing, does not see Speech; another, though hearing, does not hear her. But to this one she reveals her body, as a loving wife, beautifully robed, reveals herself to her husband.
They say of one who is a friend: he has drunk the draft of friendship, yet even in the contests they do not incite him. He wanders on fruitlessly, through delusion — having heard Speech that is barren and flowerless.
He who has abandoned a friend who knows his way — he has no share whatsoever in Speech. What he hears, he hears in vain; he has not found the path to what is well done.
Friends with eyes, friends with ears — they proved unequal in the contests of the mind. Some reached up to the shoulder, others to the chest; as those who have bathed in a lake, they have been seen there.
When the brāhmaṇas as friends celebrate together, in the flashes of thought fashioned within the heart — there some have fallen away from the knowable; the would-be-Brahman wanderers go about still among them.
These who move neither hither nor beyond, who are neither brāhmaṇas nor pressers of Soma — they, having come to Speech by a sinful path, spin the thread of weavers, unknowingly.
All friends rejoice in the one who has come gloriously, who overcomes assemblies; he who removes guilt and procures food is well fitted for the contest — for such is their helper.
One dwells in the prosperity of the hymns having nourished it; another sings the gāyatra verse in the śakvarī chants; one proclaims the knowledge of Brahman that was born; yet another measures out the measure of the sacrifice.
Let us now proclaim with praise the generations of the gods, so that one may behold them in a later age when the hymns are being recited.
Brahmaṇaspati blew these together as a smith blows the bellows: in the earliest age of the gods, Being was born from Non-Being.

title: Rigveda
text:
In the first age of the gods, Being was born from Non-Being. After that the regions were born; and after that, from Uttānapāda.
Earth was born from Uttānapāda; from the earth the quarters were born. From Aditi, Dakṣa was born; and from Dakṣa, Aditi.
For Aditi was born, O Dakṣa — she who is your daughter. After her were born the gods, the blessed ones, who have immortality as their bond.
When the gods, all banding together, stood fast in the ocean — then a piercing dust, as though from those who dance, arose from them.
When, like ascetics striving in discipline, the gods swelled the worlds — then from the ocean they drew forth the hidden sun.
Aditi had eight sons born from her body. She approached the gods with seven; but Mārtāṇḍa she cast away.
With seven sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age. But for birth and death she brought Mārtāṇḍa back again.
He was born mighty for strength, for swiftness — gladdening, most vigorous, of great self-pride. Even the Maruts increased Indra when his most bounteous mother bore the hero.
The dappled ones, fixed in the midst of trickery, increased Indra with manifold praise. Like ones enclosed, those embryos arose from darkness and from pre-dawn with a great stride.
Mighty are your feet when you go striding forward; the prizes grew — even those that were here. You, Indra, subdued a thousand wolves in their lairs; you would have turned the Aśvins to your side.
With equal swiftness you come to the sacrifice; you bring the Nāsatyas to friendship. You hold the prayer of treasure, O Indra; the heroic Aśvins gave their bounties.
Rejoicing from the law for the sake of progeny, Indra with his swift friends aimed at the goal. By these powers he came upon the Dasyu; he scattered the dark ones like drops of dew, dispersing the darknesses.
Even though of the same name, the smiters fell before him; Indra drove them back as Dawns drive away the night. You came with your noble willing friends; and together, standing firm, you smote what was dear to the heart.

title: Rigveda
text:
You slew Namuci who lusted for sacrifice, making the Dasyu powerless before the seer. You made smooth paths for Manu, like roads well-anointed leading to the gods.
You filled all these with your fame; you hold them, ruling, Indra, in your hand. The gods exult with you in your strength; you made trees spring up from their roots above.
The wheel that is fixed in the waters — may it pour sweet honey for him. The udder spread upon the earth — the milk you have placed in the cows, in the plants.
When they say 'He came from the horse' — and yet I think him born of strength; he came from fury and stood in the houses. The source from which Indra was born, that he himself knows.
The fair-winged birds — the seers Priyamedhas — alighted upon Indra, calling upon him. Roll away the darkness, fill up our sight; release us like treasures that have been bound.
Whether one has worshipped among the Vasus by thought or sacrifices of the two worlds — or those whose swift steeds are rich with spoils in battle, or those who have given renown to the well-renowned Vaṇu.
The call of these reaches the Asura in the sky; with fame-seeking mind they touch the earth. Beholding where the gods would make good fortune, as Heaven with its own clouds.
This song of the immortals — in its entirety — for those who yearn for the jewel; perfecting thought and sacrifice, may they grant us unceasing wealth.
These sons of Indra praised that act — those who would reach the cow-rich pen. Those who milked the great, mighty one, with many sons, with a thousand streams.
By power make Indra ready for our help — the unbowed one who subdues his foes; the Ṛbhukṣin, the bounteous one, of beautiful praise, the bearer of the manly bolt, rich in nourishment.
What Indra, the all-conquering, the slayer of Vṛtra, has desired most — he has filled up his names. The mighty lord of prevailing strength has been perceived; may he do what we desire to be done.

title: Rigveda
text:
The bard shall proclaim your highest greatness, O Waters, in the house of Vivasvat. Seven by seven they have moved in three ways; the Sindhu surpasses the swiftly flowing rivers in power.
Varuṇa dug out the paths for you to run, O Sindhu, when you charged toward the prizes. You go over the earth upon a sloping back; when you move at the head of these, the moving ones.
Your roar stretches up above the earth to heaven; you raise up boundless vigor with your brightness. As the rains thunder forth from the cloud, so the Sindhu bellows as it goes, like a bull.
They rush toward you, O Sindhu, like lowing mothers to their calf, like milch cows with their milk. As a king going to battle leads his forces, so you move at the forefront of the rushing streams.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī — come together with my hymn! O Paruṣṇī, Asiknī, Marudvṛdhā, Vitastā, Ārjīkīyā — hear it! O Suṣomā!
First with the Tṛṣṭāmā you go united; joined with the Rasā and the white Śvetī. You, O Sindhu, travel in the same chariot with the Kubhā, the Gomatī, the Krumu, the Mehatnu.
Rushing straight, white, mighty — it bears the realms around the courses. The Sindhu, undeceived, best of workers among rivers — like a beautiful mare with a wondrous body to behold.
The Sindhu is rich in good horses, in good chariots, in fine garments; golden, well-formed, rich in prizes. Woolen, youthful, endowed with gifts — the fortunate one wears the garment of honey-growth.
The Sindhu has yoked an easy, horse-drawn chariot; with it she shall win the prize in this contest. Great indeed is the greatness to be praised of this inviolable, self-glorious, all-pervading one.
At the breaking of the strengths I reach you; anoint Indra and the Maruts with the two worlds. May both the days attend upon us together, seat by seat opening outward to give us room.

title: Rigveda
text:
Press that best Soma-pressing; the pressing-stone is not to be touched lightly by the presser as a horse by the hand. For a noble man who finds manly power that overcomes — he wins even great wealth when he conquers the chariot.
That is indeed his pressing's opening flood, as once it found a way for Manu. They have delighted in the Tvāṣṭra Soma-pressing — in the cow-colored, horse-stripping rite — in the sacrifices, the skilled sacrificers.
Drive away the Rākṣasas, the evildoers; prop up Nirṛti, drive away ill-will. Press out for us all-heroic wealth; O press-stones, carry the divine-seeking praise-song.
More powerful even than those from heaven; broader even than the all-pervading; swifter in the Soma-ladle even than Vāyu; sing of those who prepare food more perfectly than Agni.
May they — the press-stones, glorious and inspired by inspired Speech — press out the Soma for our glory. Where the men milk the desirable sweetness, calling out together, pressing against each other.
The chariot-borne stones press the Soma; they milk out the juice of it for the cow-seeking ones. They milk the udder to fill the vessels; the men purify the oblations with their mouths.
You men have become excellent craftsmen, you O press-stones who press Soma for Indra. Gift upon gift in your divine abode; wealth upon wealth to you who press upon the earthly.
As cloud-drops sprinkle wealth with speech, as knowledgeable sacrifices with oblations — you who deserve a brāhmaṇa-hymn like that of the Maruts' troop: I have praised the host of them; you shine with them.
The young men adorned themselves with bright ornaments for glory, like those of the Maruts beyond the many nights. These sons of Heaven have not grown old; these Ādityas have grown great like eagles.
They who, by their own greatness, have surpassed heaven and earth as the sun surpasses the clouds; vigorous as heroes worthy of praise, devouring their enemies, young men desiring the sky.

title: Rigveda
text:
At your foundations, as in the flow of waters, the great earth does not totter, does not slip. This all-nourishing sacrifice is here toward you; come hither, like those pressing forward together.
You, harnessed in the shafts with reins as drivers, luminous with your brilliance at the dawning; like self-glorying eagles devouring enemies, like travelers who have rushed forth, sprinkling everywhere.
When you carry yourselves forward from afar, O Maruts, lords of the great treasure-store — knowing the wealth of blessings, O Vasus, drive far away all enmity, even from a distance.
He who has offered up in sacrifice what stands in the place of the ceremony, offering to the Maruts as a man should — may he enjoy splendid nourishment with good heroes; may he be in the protection of the gods.
For they are worthy of sacrifice in sacrifices, sheltering ones, most beneficent by the name of Āditya. May they protect us, swift as chariots in thought, delighting in the great journey and the ceremony.
Like inspired sages with their hymns, self-meditating; like the god-seeking with their sacrifices, well-awake; like brilliant kings fair to behold; like guiltless young men among the peoples.
Like Agni with his blazing splendor, gold-breasted; like the winds, self-yoked, bringing help in a single day; like the elders who know well, of good guidance; like the Soma-draughts bestowing shelter for one who goes the right way.
Like roaring winds they move and hasten; like the tongues of fires, shining out; like armored warriors, energetic; like the praises of the Ancestors, those of liberal gifts.
Like the spokes of chariots, sharing one nave; like conquering heroes desiring the sky; like worthy young men sprinkling the oblation, singing forth like those of excellent praise.
Like the eldest, the swift horses, like the charioteers who desire, of liberal gifts; like waters rushing on with downward and with upward floods; all-formed, like the Aṅgirases with their Sāman chants.

title: Rigveda
text:
Like the press-stones, the enlightened ones, whose mother is the Sindhu, always crushing; like rocks that shatter at all times; like playful young ones of good mothers; like a great host in their march and their blazing.
Like the banners of the Dawns, beautiful at the ceremony, adorned with bright ornaments, they shone; like the swift rivers with flashing spears, they measured out the distances as from far away.
O gods, make us fortunate, of good treasure — us, the praisers; O Maruts, who have increased; go forth upon the praise and upon the friendship — for from of old your jewel-gifts are set aside for us.
I beheld the greatness of this great Immortal one among the mortal peoples. The two jaws — separated and yet brought together — the insatiate eater devours abundantly.
His head hidden in the cave, his two eyes apart — the insatiate one devours the forests with his tongue. The foods are carried to him with feet; those with upraised hands bow down in worship before the peoples.
Seeking the deeper secret of the mother, he crept over the broad ways like a child among plants. Blazing, he found the ripe grain within; licking, the trickster was in the mother's lap.
This truth I declare to you both, O Heaven and Earth: the embryo devours the mothers at birth. I, mortal, have not fully understood the god — but Agni himself is the far-seer, the wise one.
He who brings food and oblation eagerly to him, who pours ghee upon him and flourishes — for him, Agni, you look out with a thousand eyes; you face all ways toward him.
What forsaking sin have you committed among the gods, O Agni? — I ask you now as one who does not know. Playing and not playing, the tawny one to eat — eating, he cut joint by joint like a sword through a cow.
The forest-born one has yoked his swift horses in different directions, grasped with reins on both sides. Mitra, well-born, looks on with the Vasus; growing with his joints, he has swelled together.

title: Rigveda
text:
Agni gives the prize-bringing seven-horsed (team); Agni gives a famous hero, firm in action. Agni moves through the two worlds, uniting them; Agni gives the woman of heroic womb, rich in understanding.
May the kindling of Agni's work be auspicious; Agni has entered the great two worlds. Agni impelled the one in battles; Agni splits asunder the many Vṛtras.
Agni protected the ear of the old man; Agni burned up the Jarūtha from the waters. Agni saved Atri within the burning heat; Agni released Nṛmedha together with his offspring.
Agni gives wealth shaped with heroes; Agni gives the seer who wins thousands. Agni has spread the oblation in heaven; the stations of Agni are carried in many places.
The seers invoke Agni with their hymns; men pressed in need invoke Agni on their journey. Birds flying in mid-air invoke Agni; Agni moves around the thousands of cattle.
The human peoples invoke Agni; those of Manu and Nahuṣa born everywhere invoke Agni. Agni holds the Gāndharvī path of the law; the pasture of Agni is established in the ghee.
The Ṛbhus fashioned a prayer for Agni; we have proclaimed great Agni with beautiful praise. O Agni, most youthful, protect the singer; O Agni, win for us great wealth by sacrifice.
He who sacrificed all these worlds — the seer-priest, our father — sat down as Hotṛ. Seeking wealth with his blessing, he first carved out the lower realms and entered into them.
What was the base, the point of support? What was the timber? How did it stand? From what did Viśvakarmā, the all-seeing, bring forth the earth and unfold the sky with his greatness?
He whose eyes are everywhere, whose face is everywhere, whose arms are everywhere, whose feet are everywhere — he, the one god, forging together heaven and earth with his hands and wings.
What was the forest, what was the tree from which they fashioned heaven and earth? Sages enquire with the mind: upon what did he stand when he upheld the worlds?

title: Rigveda
text:
Your highest abodes, O Viśvakarman, your lowest, and your middle ones as well — instruct your friends in the oblation, O Lord of self-nourishment; waxing great, sacrifice your own self.
O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice earth and heaven yourself. Let other people about us be confounded; here let our munificent patron be the wise lord.
Today in the contest we call upon the Lord of Speech, Viśvakarman, swift as thought, for our aid. May he, of perfect deeds, well-being to all, be pleased with all our invocations and come to our help.
The wise Father, father of the eye, gave being by his mind to these two bowing ones and kindled them with ghee. When the eastern ends were made firm, then only did heaven and earth spread out.
Viśvakarman, of surpassing mind, far-ranging, the ordainer and disposer, the highest, the all-seeing — their offerings and desires exhilarate together where they speak of the seven seers beyond the One.
He who is our father, our begetter and ordainer, who knows all the abodes and all the worlds, who alone assigns the names of the gods — to him the other beings come with their inquiry.
To him the ancient seer-praisers, like heralds, sacrificed wealth together — those who sat in the unformed and formed realm of mid-air, who fashioned all these beings here.
Beyond the heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and asuras — what was that first embryo the waters held, where all the gods gazed together?
That first embryo the waters held, where all the gods came together — it is set, the One, in the navel of the Unborn, in whom all worlds stand.
You do not know him who generated all these things — something else has come between you. Shrouded in mist, chanting emptily, those who delight in life and only proclaim hymns go their way.
O Manyu, who aided you — the bolt, the arrow — nourishes continuous might through the whole world. With you as ally, O strength-given, violent, mighty one, may we overpower both Dāsa and Ārya.

title: Rigveda
text:
Manyu is Indra, Manyu himself is the god; Manyu is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa, and Jātavedas. The human peoples worship Manyu. Protect us, O Manyu, united with your ardour.
Come here, O Manyu, mightier than the mighty; with ardour as your ally, smite down our foes. Slayer of enemies, slayer of Vṛtra, slayer of Dasyus — bring all riches to us.
For you, O Manyu, are vigour that overpowers; you are self-existent ardour, subduer of enemies; all-seeing, forceful, victorious — place your strength in us for the battles.
Portionless, I am left out, O keen-minded one — because of the intent of you, the mighty. I, O Manyu, the will-less man, have failed you; come with your own body to grant strength.
I am here before you — come to me, facing me, O overpowering sustainer of all. O Manyu, wielder of the bolt, turn toward me; let us smite the Dasyus together and know yourselves allied.
Come here and stand to my right, and then together we will crush many foes. I pour for you the sweetest libation, the first drop — let us two drink together in silence.
O Manyu, mounting the chariot together with you, exhilarated and emboldened, the Marut-companied warriors — men of fire-like form, whetting their weapons, arrows keen — let them surge forth.
Like fire, O Manyu, when kindled, overpower; be our army-leader, O overpowering one, when invoked. After slaying the enemies, divide the booty; measuring out your strength, drive away the battles.
Overpower, O Manyu, the enemy assailing us; breaking, crushing, destroying, go forth against the foes. Your fierce strength has truly advanced; you, the sole-born, bring the dependent into your power.
You alone, O Manyu, are invoked by many; inspire every clan for battle. Unscathed, with you as ally, we raise the resounding battle-cry for victory.
Grant us victory, irresistible like Indra; be our overlord here, O Manyu. We recite your dear name, O overpowering one; we know the source from which you arose.

title: Rigveda
text:
Born together with dominion, O bolt-like arrow, you bear a higher overpowering strength. O Manyu, by your will be united with us; O much-invoked, join us for the great prize.
May Varuṇa and Manyu give us both kinds of wealth, amassed and gathered together. The enemies, defeated, their hearts filled with fear, let them slink away and vanish.
By truth the earth is upheld; by the sun the sky is upheld. By ṛta the Ādityas stand firm; Soma is established in heaven.
By Soma are the Ādityas mighty; by Soma the great earth stands; and in the lap of these stars here Soma is placed.
He who drinks the pressed herb thinks he has drunk Soma. The Soma that the Brāhmaṇas know — of that no one actually partakes.
Shielded by covering guards, O Soma, protected by great enclosures, you stand listening to the pressing-stones; no earthly being consumes you.
When the gods drink you fully, O god, from that you are replenished again. Vāyu is the guardian of Soma; the moon is the form of the common one.
The Raibhī song was the accompanying gift, the Nārāśaṁsī the one that confers upon her; for Sūryā the beautiful raiment has come, adorned and completed in the hymn.
Thought was her pillow, sight was her collyrium; heaven and earth were the casket when Sūryā went to her husband.
The hymns of praise were the poles of the canopy; the metre was the bridal headgear with dangling ornaments; for Sūryā the Aśvins were the suitors; Agni was the foremost leader.
Soma became the wooer; the Aśvins were the two suitors. When Sūryā declared herself willing in her heart, Savitṛ gave her to a husband.
Her mind was the cart, the sky was the canopy; the two white bullocks were yoked when Sūryā went to her new home.
The two cows yoked by Ṛk and Sāman are your sāman-players; your two ears were the wheels; in heaven the path moves to and fro.

title: Rigveda
text:
Your two pure wheels move freely; the axle was the in-breath. Sūryā mounted the mind-made cart, going forth to her husband.
The bridal procession of Sūryā went forth, which Savitṛ released. When the Maghā asterisms come, the cows are slaughtered; when the Arjunī stars come, she is driven around.
When you two Aśvins came inquiring, bringing Sūryā's wedding-procession on the three-wheeled car, all the gods acknowledged that — Pūṣan, the son, chose you two as fathers.
When you two Lords of Beauty came to woo Sūryā — where was the one wheel of yours, and where did you two stand for the guide to the way?
O Sūryā, the Brāhmaṇas know your two wheels according to the season. But that one hidden wheel — only the truly wise know that.
To Sūryā, to the gods, to Mitra and to Varuṇa — to those who know all existing things — I have made this obeisance.
These two children play and go around the sacrifice by their magic, moving forward and back. One surveys all the worlds; the other, ordained the seasons, is born again.
Ever new he is born again; he becomes the signal of the days, going to the fore of the dawns. Coming on, he distributes the portion to the gods — the moon stretches out long life.
